He's a really passionate about the subject, but he doesn't care about returning grades unless you personally approach him either through email or see him at his office... but even then it's a hit or miss. He posted up one exam grade throughout the whole semester (out of 4) and he's ALWAYS late to class. His lectures were interesting though.

It is incredibly annoying and insulting to show up for a class, and the professor does not show up until 15 minutes after class starts, and this happens every time including exams. Anderson does not post grades and does not respond to e-mails and shows up late for everything. The class is an interesting subject, which is the one reason I liked it.

He is fascinating and makes the class interesting. We even discussed Charlie Sheen and whether or not he was bi polar! Great class, but he is late and does not give out grades. Currently, there is only one grade up when there should be three.

Fantastic instructor in regards to teaching the criteria of Abnormal Psychology.  However, he failed to return grades, though you can attend his office hours and ask, though he may not have all the grades.  I got an A easily and never knew my grade until finding out I got an A when official grades were released.  TRUE!

Amazing teacher. Highly recommended. He makes the class interesting and fun. He has a few downfalls, he is late to class, never graded anything, and was rarely around during his office hours. He is very insightful and helped me decide on my major. Read the book and split up the chapters. You'll definitely get an A or a B.

He is one of the gems that UMBC has been keeping since long who wants students to learn and to enjoy the course. Yes, he doesn't give grades back but he gives answers right after the exam to see how you have done. I'd say please be little more organized so you won't have to run back and forth. Also, I found it very rude to be late for every lecture

DOES NOT GIVE BACK A SINGLE GRADE!!!! U WILL HAVE TO GUESS WHAT YOUR GRADE IS. On another note I thought he was very interesting. Lectures outline info to study in the book. Easy Tests. Always makes up excuses was to why he doesnt have the grades. I WENT TO HIS OFFICE 3 TIMES AND STILL HE HAD NO GRADES JUST EXCUSES. NO MORALITY OR ETHICS FOR STUDEN
Late to EVERY class inc. exams. Does not hand back ANY grades OR calculate grades before the end of the semester.

Very interesting class, definitely knows what he's talking about and is extremely clear on what subjects he'll test you on. However, he does not hand back grades. After exams he does allow you to see an answer key, but you can only get an estimate to your grade. If you attend lectures and/or read the book, you will get no lower than a B.

So far my absolute favorite professor. He makes you actually care about the topic, and the lectures are always interesting. Class discussions are consistently insightful. My one problem, however; he's not good with giving back grades. But the good absolutely outweighs the bad.

Good teacher but very disorganized and cannot seem to get grades back and doesn't seem like he cares at all.  I'm afraid I won't ever be told what my grade is though I'm positive I will do well because I'm intelligent.  Shows up late sometimes and doesn't give a crap lol.

I have taken 385, 380, and 345 with Dr. Anderson and have thoroughly enjoyed all of these classes. His weakness is in organization and grading promptly, but if you go in during his office hours, he'll let you know how you're doing. He is helpful, enthusiastic and takes a genuine interest in his students' success.  Definitely recommend Dr. A.

He was some what interesting at times he is NOT a teacher I recommend. He was late to class, only gave us 1 grade back ALL semester (which was our 1st exam), he got off topic very easily by students, this class had similar content to his others, & he said he would give study guides before exams, did once and the others times were day/hours before

Prof Anderson is a very interesting and enjoyable lecturer....however, and this is a huge HOWEVER, he is horrible at getting grades back.  tried to go see him to get my grades and he always has an excuse as to why they aren't done or why he can't see me at that moment....great professor but this makes me give him a B-
Awesome, cute professor for an older guy. Charismatic, wants everyone to do well, and answers questions well. Usually late for class and often ends early. Would absolutely take again.
Great professor! He is clearly interested in what he is teachng and keeps the students interested.

Definitely one of the BEST professors I've had--the guy is GREAT! He has a very large knowledge base and seems to know a lot about everything--meaning, you can learn a lot from him. This class did not require much studying and exams were moderately easy. I HIGHLY recommend taking any course taught by Anderson!

THis teacher is awesome. He is totally passionate about his classes and will go out of his way to help you out. His classes are not hard you just have to pay attention and take good notes. He will have items from lecture on the test. I will def be taking him again.

Very engaging professor, I'm an engineer auditing the class because my wife is in it. He is very interested in his topic and has a lot of clinical experience. He's very interested in training students to go out and fix the problems of society. Easy to get in touch with if you just drop by his office. Very considerate of students' situations.

I have taken PSYC 342, 385, 380 with him. Great Professor! He is very enthusiastic and a great lecturer. He really cares about what he does! I am trying to take another class he teaches next semester!
You should take all is classes if you are interested in psychology.

he is a creeper, nice though.  his tests are pretty easy and the 1 page papers are just give away points. he isnt that good about getting grades back for exams, but i would suggest this class for an easy A. the subject is pretty interesting too
Will definetely hit on you if you are at least a semi-attractive female. Very Sleezy

I had him for psychology of aggression and antisocial behavior, he is really animated and interested in what he teaches, so it is a great class to take.  He also tries to involve everyone, and has a lot of real life stories and is really funny too, I highly recommend him.

His classes are VERY interesting and  fun.It is sufficient to only study the notes. But PLEASE make sure you check your grades and keep track of it. I got an A in the class, but he gave me an F. He was a big procastinator in changing it (it took him 9 months).And I wasn't the first person to experience this

Lots of experience teaching and practicing psychology, he's definitely worth taking.  The material is very interesting, and the tests aren't difficult if you paid attention in class.  However, he often teaches out of the textbook, and you won't see your grade until grade reports are out.  He's also sometimes disorganized, but overall good.
good

Dr. Anderson is the best! I had no interest in PSYC prior to attending this course and now I plan on minoring in it! Contrary to other's comments, I never felt like he talked down to the class. He really brings the subject matter to life and is a genuine and courteous person.  Do the online labs, take good notes, read the book and you'll get an A.

Lectures were fun, but the tests are ridiculoulsy hard! does not curve the grade at all. i actually read the bookk and barely made C's. but the online labs help boost your grade. pay attention during lectures and take good notes. thats the key.
Very easy teacher, all you have to do is take the online quizzes show up for class and take your exams. I barely went to the class and still got a B.

Exams were fair and relatively easy, as long as you take good notes and briefly scan the chapters.  However, he's rather bad with telling you what grade you have in class.  Still, I enjoy him enough that I will be taking his aggression class next semester.

Irresponsible in terms of giving back papers, always seems to be talking about sex no matter *what* class he's teaching. How does sex relate to our aggression class? Heard you have to flirt to get an A- not sure what I'll end up with then, since I haven't even talked to the guy. Mandatory attendence, avoid if you like to keep track of grades.
Anderson is a Really good teacher. Class was fun and notes that he gives you in class ARE seen and used in his exams. He is also cute ..you know ..for his age and being a professor.

Online exams are easy. Doesn't grade you're exams until the very end of semester so you won't know your grade until it shows on your transcript. Makes attendance mandatory and covers everything the book does.

Anderson is funny and interesting. Class Attendance is counted as part of the grade. His labs and quizes are all on Blackboard, very easy to do. His tests are somewhat hard, most importantly he put stuff that he talked about or graphs that he drew in class on the test. So go to class! Besides that it was a fun class!
Ok professor...told me I had one of the best grades in the class but i ended up with a C. Fun lectures though!

Great professor--keeps it interesting and engages you which you'll like if you're a psyc major. However he feeds off the classes energy so a boring class can make it less fun. Speak up in his class!! Took abnormal with him too and it was great.
He is a very intelligent man and quite capable teacher.  I really enjoyed his class and his fun sense of humor.

Nice, funny occasionally. Gave "pop" quizzes randomly. They were 3 questions, you could use your notes and even if you got them wrong you still got points for being in class. Going to class is worth it.

No matter what the lecture is about he always finds a way to come back to the point that size doesn't matter b/c of blah blah blah...  This dude really needs quit speaking about how he's anatomically challenged!

Good professor. Sometimes really boring. Came late to every class. I did really bad on some of the exams but got a B in the class. Passes around a sign in sheet but you really don't need to be there. As long as you read the book your set. Online exams are EASY.

attendence is mandatory but easy class and boring lectures. exams are somewhat hard. prof arrives late to almost every class and is not helpful he didn't even posted anything on blackboard until end of the semester and doesn't reply to e-mails

Nice teacher. Lectures didn't really help with the exams. Exams weren't very hard. Class was not really mandatory, passed around a sign in sheet. Understanding and not difficult person. I missed the online tests, and he let me take them after the due date. I thought I got a D on most of the exams, but I got a B in the class...didn't really make sen

Good teacher, nice guy. Class attendance is not mandatory, but he does send around a sign in sheet. Funny, down to earth, answers each and every hand. There are three-four exams (including final), all go over basic stuff.

Ha, cannot believe this guy. He thinks everyone he is teaching is an idiot, and goes over the most basic things. Secondly, there are blaring gaps in scientific logic in his lectures. A specially shocking moment was when he acutually suggested that the conscience might be located on the shoulder (seriously). He also promoted Jungian theories. Omg...

really really really interesting teacher.  he kept the class awake even later in the evening.  i have taken 2 classes with him and i plan on taking another before i graduate because he can make any class interesting.

good teacher. i took abnormal psych with this guy and he knows what he's talking about and he makes the class very fun, interactive, and interesting. he might be little bit hard to get in touch with but he's very kind and nice.

Attendence was required and he was always late to class even though the class use to start at 2:30. Does not response to e-mails. His teaching style was okay but the tests were really hard. If you are taking psycology for the first time i would suggest avoid him. Take someone else
Would not help when you need it.  Does not respond back to emails if they require him to do any work at all. Does not do his own grading and will not review when asked. Not a good instructor.

If you read the chapters and show up to class half of the time, you'd have to be brain dead to get less than a C. I barely put any time into this class, and I got an easy A. Also the professor is interesting, uses his experience to guide lecture, and he lets the discussion take tangents if people show an interest.
No Comments

This was honestly the biggest waste of time in my life. He takes attendence which is the only reason I even came to class. Seriously, bring a book. You'll learn more from the computer labs and text than you will from him. Just write down what he puts on the board and study. His tests aren't too easy, but easy enough.
No Comments

Science majors: don't take his classes, they are boring as heck. By brain was about to melt, I wouldn't have survived if I didn't have novels to secretly read during class. Takes attendance so have to come to class. No one found out ANYTHING about their grade till the report card. I think he never grades anything, just rolls a dice.

I've taken Anderson twice now, and both times he has been nothing short of amazing. He's brings his experience to the course and shares stories instead of blindly reading from the text. It is important to go to class because the lecture info is featured on the test, but it is usually worth your while since he is interesting.

This is the best professor I ever had!! Lots of fun, lectures are very interesting and his exam are not that hard!  Make sure you go to his lectures and take notes.  One downside is he is always late to class.  But thats the only one.

Easier than a middle school health class. He is unknowledgeable, and tells you stuff you knew since age 2 (in fancy words). ALWAYS LATE TO CLASS (at least 15 mins daily). The class is at 1 pm, so I have no idea what makes him so late. Bring work from other classes, and take him if you have a heavy load, because you can ignore his class easily.

Most people on this page right, tests not extremely easy with short answers you must study some, but it is by far my easiest class. Dr. Anderson very nice but where are our grades and why he always late?

This class is obscenely easy. He hasn't told us any of our grades so far this year, and he's always really really late to class, especially on exam days (15- 20 mins late). But the exams are easy, and even if you barely read the book you should get an A. Take him if you have a heavy course load.

He basically reads the book to you so most of the time you don't have to listen. He is terrible on giving back grades. It is almost the end of the semester now and he hasn't told us our grades yet. He's nice as a person, but as a professor he's not so hot. He needs to get with Blackboard.

i loved taking Dr. Anderson's class! the material is very interesting and he lectures really well. just take notes and read the text a bit before exams and you'll do fine. if you ever need any help with the material, he is very helpful and approachable. overall a great class and great prof!! * he has been really late with exam grades this semester.

He's a terrific teacher. He interacts with students well and always asks for student input. He does his best to make the material understandable and does it well. He knows what he is talking about and is quite funny. If you go to lectures, you should be fine, and the readings are not that bad. Negative? Giving grades back on time, but good overall.

I actually mean to give him a poor rating, but he saitsfies the criteria for this website. If you want to take his class, REMEBER TO BRING WORK FROM OTHER CLASSES. Class is worthless and easy. It's like kindergarten. I felt like my brain was going to melt in that class. Once we learnt what the word "affect" meant, and he spent 15 mintes on it.
No Comments
he's one of the good ones. take a class of his if you can. make sure you go attendance is a must but you won't mind sitting through his lectures. plus if he knows your name and face your good.
No Comments
No Comments
Cool guy, good teacher, a bit picky on attendance but attendance helps get better grades.  Flexible with handing in assignments late, but DO NOT forget to sign in each day.

Dr. Anderson is a excellent teacher.  He makes lectures interesting.  His tests are mostly multiple choice and straight from the lecture and partly from the book.  I took two classes with him and had no complaints.

I would not take another class with him. He is funny and nice however his tests are hard and a good portion of your grade counts on your test scores. He is not leanent and is also picky on attendance.

Dr. Anderson is a great professor.  He brings his job as a clinician into the classroom while describing mental disorders.  His tests are very straight-forward from book and lecture.  Must take notes during lecture and go to class in order to pass test, and also because he takes attendance.  Overall, easy A if you go to class and read.
i loved his class. its a must for anyone even if your not a psych major. ill be taking more from him i enjoyed it so much.

I took psych 285 as a gfr, therefore I am a non-majour attempting to finish the elective to graduate.  He makes the material clear and interesting.  His exams are not overly difficult, usually quite fair, however make sure you read the text.  Overall one of the better professors that I have had.
You have to take a class with him, he is fun and laid back and straight to the point. All you need is class notes and he gives examples from his work that help out a lot. Easy on the eyes too ;-)
Dr. Anderson is the best professor I have ever had! Very understanding, laid back. Exams are straight-forward as long as you go to class.. definately would recommend! :)

If you must take PSYC 100, take it with Dr. Anderson.  He's a fun guy, but is very disorganized.  We went most of the semester without syllabi.  Exams are usually straight forward, but expect to put in a tiny bit more than minimal amount of studying.  Good class.
Great teacher. He's what got me into psych. Really easy to follow, and knows what he's talking about.
great teacher, loved him!!

Dr. Anderson is the best psyc teacher I have taken.  His lectures are interesting and he makes class fun.  If you take notes and skim the book you should have no problem.  The only thing bad is he replies to emails very slow if not at all.

He is not an easy teacher, you need to take notes in class and pay attention as well as read the book in order to do well on the exams. But he's got a good humour and most of the time, interresting lectures. He takes atendance every day (10% of grade)

Great lectures! Make sure you do the readings for the exams though. He sometimes asks specific questions from the readings- but overall, if you do the reading and go to class you can learn a lot and do well in the class.

awesome guy!!practicing clinician that brings his street smartness into the class.sometimes a talking Hallmark card, but you leave the classroom with the feeling that you learnt something about human psychology + stays with you after taking the class

The absolute BEST teacher every.  He can make even boring things interesting.  I've had him 3 semesters now (200, 285, 380) and I'm going to miss him next semester.  If you can take any class with him, DO IT!
No Comments
No Comments
Great teacher!! He gives interesting and informative lectures.
He's done it all. He teaches, he practices, and he used to teach kindergarten!!

Chris Brandt is a friendly and approachable professor who creates a comfortable learning environment. His TA, Chelsea Taylor, was reliable and helpful. He uses in-class assignments to reinforce key concepts, and his open-book exams encourage understanding over memorization. He explains material clearly and keeps the class organized. Very helpful!!

This class was not only very interesting, but also very fun and informative. The professor makes it clear what the deadlines are, but is very flexible and understanding if you give him your time and information. Assignments and homework are easy, just don't do it last minute. Great professor 5/5!!
Such an easy course! Great professor.

Professor Brandt is such a sweet guy! He cares about you outside of classes. Lots of reading, with weekly assessments and assignments. Weekly chapter readings and once a week meetings online. One exam, which is the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Brandt is a really nice and caring professor. The homeworks are pretty easy as long as you read the text book. Every class day you are required to submit the in class assignment by 11:59 (I recommend joining the meets because sometimes he gives out the answers). Highly recommend taking this class.

Super fun and nice professor! Makes lectures interesting. Most of the work is homework with clear cut deadlines, so as long as you work ahead and communicate any issues you may have, you will be fine!

He is a gem! All work is on you since it's online, but he is always there to help. Keeping up with reading, notes, and assignments will make this class a joy and stress-free. He made lectures the highlight of my week, effortlessly explaining concepts. He taught me so much about myself and others, and I'd retake this course every semester!

Amazing Professor. He's so wonderful and kind. Love his teaching style. There are a lot of assignments, so time management is your best friend. There are 13 SmartBook chapters each with assignments and assessments (39 in total). There are 13 in-class assignments, one mini-project, and one Final Exam.

Very kind and soft spoken. He's clearly passionate about what he teaches and he makes the class as enjoyable as he can. He often shares personal anecdotes. Assignments homeworks, and exams are quite easy, just pay attention to the material and you'll be fine. Not lenient on deadlines, but the work isn't difficult so just do it. He's wonderful!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Easy going. Easy homework and assessments. Go to class you can skip 3 in class assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: If you don't like McGraw Hill online textbooks, don't take this class. If you do like them, you're in luck, because that's where most of your time will be spent for readings and assignments. Lots of memorizing terms and stages. Lectures are a bit boring but he spices it up with personal stories sometimes. Receptive to questions.

Please take him! He is such a funny, nice, and kind professor. I wish he taught more classes. He just goes through slides and he asks us questions and we all get into a conversation about it. It's a very easy class and he's such a chill professor. Weekly assignments on Connect. He is not lenient on deadlines, so make sure to complete on time!

he's genuinely so funny, always cracking jokes during class and is great to be around. when asking questions he's very receptive and explains it so that you get a good understanding of course material. would 100% take again and totally recommend.

Professor Brown was actually very easy going and cracked jokes throughout the class. He always told a very little story before starting class and was honestly such an easy class to take. Just do your ALEKS and practice quizzes and you'll be fine. I would 100% take his class again. I appreciate him because his class gave me little to no stress.

Professor Brown is the best! He explains everything so clear so it makes learning easier. As someone who's TERRIBLE at math I've learned a lot from professor Brown. He is very helpful and I'm thankful that I took his class. I would 100% recommend taking his class!

Professor Brown was one of the best- so supportive and had a great sense of humor I laughed myself into an A all math teachers are NOT the same.. I appreciated his efforts to help me succeed in a subject I struggle with

Ronnie is a really good professor, as someone who struggles with math, he teaches everything very well and breaks everything down to where it is comprehendible. His quizzes, exams, and homework are all very easy and relate back to the lectures. He is also hilarious and makes lectures engaging.

he is a chill guy, I finally wasn't completely horrible at math cuz he actually covered the topics, only complaint is that when he cancelled a class he didn't change the timeline to fit so the Aleks assignments were quizzing me on stuff I hadn't learned yet,  bummer, so maybe he is a bit of an airhead

Professor Ronnie is such a great professor for Math 104. One of my favorite. His lectures are clear, easy to follow. He's funny and keeps the class engaging. The workload is reasonable with 7 quizzes (you can drop two) the quizzes are very easy if you attend lectures. Two exams and final. There will be homework but it's online. Highly recommend!

I had professor Brown for math 104 and he was great. Very straight going while still having fun and being humorous and cared for his students. His quizzes are easy if you pay attention in class and hardly ever gives out homework.
very chill

Class is easy if you keep up with homework and quizzes and understand the textbook concepts. There's a quiz and homework almost every week, so stay on top of it to avoid dropping below a B. The professor is interactive and caring but can be strict at times. Exams are weighted a hefty amount, so make sure to understand the topics well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: hard, can come off passive aggressive but all in all does actually care for students' futures, a little so much so that hes a stickler when it comes to grades, curving, ai. when it comes down to it, if you put your best foot forward, he'll meet you where you are, still a very demanding and heavy class.

FYI on the previous review: He DID curve everyone's exam 1 grades AND dropped quizzes so everyone passed with a minimum B. He's tough on homework and work ethic in general but he is fair and he is understanding. He will work with you if things go sideways and gives you plenty of chances to get back up. For ref, I got a low D in the 1st exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is really really great! The most engaging IS professor I have taken at UMBC. He really genuinely cares about student success and makes a great effort to get to know every student individually despite it being a larger class. Super accommodating, but still encourages everyone to be on top of their work. Highly recommend.
Great professor with very clear study guides. I enjoyed his lectures and would 100% take this class again if I could.

New IS Professor for UMBC, has been great so far, he's a good lecturer and has some energy. Flexible, but has a higher set standard, which makes the class difficulty a bit higher than another professor, but its not really outside of expectation for a college class. Good overall, easy to talk to, good overall for his first class as a Professor.

Professor Beverley is a great Prof, he made IS 310 much easier to understand with clear explanations and a supportive approach. He was friendly, patient, and always willing to help. His passion for teaching created a positive learning environment. Highly recommend

She's hands down the best and easiest professor you can take. If you need your GEP credit 1000% take her. Course consist of 3 exams (gives the EXACT exam questions the day before), 8 random quizzes (1 question on each quiz, questions like "whos your favorite superhero"). Attendance kinda matters since u need the quizzes. overall ez class, take her.

She's a very sweet old lady and genuinely cares about her students. Definitely attend her lectures they can feel a bit slow if you're not into philosophy, but she's kind, She posts exam questions beforehand, holds review sessions, and gives about 10 super easy quizzes all semester sometimes even fun ones like What's your favorite cartoon?
Super nice and makes the test easy to understand. She loves her job and tries to make the class fun and easy.

I enjoyed how chill and stress free her lectures were. There was no homework, class days for exam reviews, and quizzes were extremely simple. She is super calm and lectures are fairly organized, the content is all laid out on slides but she tends to revisit the same content multiple times. Kinda challenging but it's not normally an issue.
Super easy class. She gives exam questions the class before exam day.

Slides posted on blackboard, lectures ok but I don't think anyone ever went to class cuz she would go over the exam QandA the class before the exam, and there would be a video on blackboard of the review so students could reference it. Basically a free class. She's also really nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was a great professor. The class was an easy 100%. You could skip every class except for the one class before the exam and pass with 100% because she gives you the answers to the T the class period before. Amazing and easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very easy class, goes over all answers before exams. Show up to class during review sessions and you will get an A.
Very chill and laid back professor, goes over all answers before an exam, just show up and you'll get an A.

I loved having Amy for philosophy, she is one of the best profs at UMBC! She puts a lot of subtle humor into her lectures and assignments are incredibly easy if you just show up to class. Awesome class and would absolutely take again.

Ms. Payne is a UMBC gem. I've never felt so relieved or glad to have taken a college class before. She really cares about her students and this class is so easy to pass, as long as you show up. Even if the room is "dry", she will still try to inject humor so the lecture isn't boring. Although easy, the class discussions were a blessing to the mind.

Dr. Payne is one of my favorite teaches til this day. Her quizzes are all written but they are short and you are able to watch her past lectures on her Youtube channel to help. She gives us like 3-5 days to do the tests but it'll probably only take you like 10 minutes max. This class is a must take if you go to UMBC.

Professor Payne is awesome! Shes funny, and actually teaches you the material that she puts on the exam. Before tests, she goes over what questions will be on the test. Also, her attendance isnt mandatory.

The easiest class I've ever taken. Easier than any high school class I took. She makes it easy and digestible and gives exam questions and answers before the exam. You have to put in considerable effort to pass with less than an A. Not only this she's a great person, very knowledgeable, and is there for you if you need it (academically) :)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Her classes are very interesting!

Take Professor Payne if you want to take PHIL100! She is very laid back and gives very few assignments, and she is not a tough grader. Professor Payne genuinely wants you to learn and doesn't want you to stress about her class. Highly recommend!

Her class was pretty simple. She has readings but you don't have to read them to understand what she's talking about. We have weekly 'quizzes' that are easy as long as you partially listen and extremely easy if you take notes As long as you show up and engage in her content a little, the class won't be a problem.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Her lectures might put you to sleep sometimes but if you listen a little bit you can pass the occasional quiz. Also the exams are essay based and she gives you the answers the class before. Literally just memorize it and you should get an easy A. The final paper is not that difficult. One of the easiest courses you will ever take at UMBC

one of the easiest professors at UMBC. Gave us the answers to the exam questions the class before the exam. If you didn't want to go to class, she said "just say your dog ate your keys and its fine." Along with the class being easy, she is actually a really great person and she is so funny. if you participate she'll love you, but sleeping is fine 2

She is a very sweet and funny teacher. The lectures are a little boring but it is very easy to get a 100% on all three exams (which are essays she gives you the answer to the class prior). 3 essay exams and a final research paper that is not very difficult. Class is very easy and do-able. There are quizzes once a week or every other week, easy.

She was pretty good. She seemed a bit disorganized and like she didn't plan much ahead of time, but her lectures were still interesting. She's funny and definitely adds some of her humor to the lectures. Not the best prof at UMBC, but definitely not the worst.

This class seem like an easy A but the professor has a harsh, high pressure teaching style and frequently puts students on the spot with little time to respond. If your answer isn't what he expects, he can be openly rude which creates a very uncomfortable classroom environment. Emails are rarely answered, making it difficult to get clarification.
Mean professor, will put you on the spot and call you out if you don't know a certain answer.
Great class! Dr. B. Teaches history different from other professors. More important stuff going on today and stuff. Movies too
Cool class. We went over stuff I never had in other classes. Take home exams were pretty easy. Would take it again!
Pretty easy class and easy “A.” Talked about readings which were cool. Frankenstein, 1984, Dune. Highly recommend for those who want WI.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr B is great. I was a bit skeptical of his use of history to describe disease but it made what would have been a boring class okay. Will definitely take him again.
Great class. It wasn't the sort of name and date things we did more discussions. Got cool at the end. Midterm and finals were most of the grade
Cool class. Pretty easy workload based on group projects. Generous grader if you show up and participate.
Not your typical history class. Fun discussions and we even watched documentaries. Looking forward to my next PBHL with Dr B

Dr. B. was great. I've never taken a history class at UMBC. We didnt do like names and dates or anything. instead we just sort of talked about biger ideas in history and how things relate to the present. Some students had trouble with the readings and Dr. B. shortened the work and assignment and even assigned us a documentary to watch instead.

Cool stuff and a fun teacher. Who knew the history of public health could be exciting (yawn, right?). A few of the other students didnt read so that occationally brough things down here and there. lookin forward to taking him in 340 next semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. B is great! I highly recommend this class to STEM students. We did a lot of deep thinking about the sciences and read some cool sci-fi books like flowers for algernon and 1984. Really like Frankenstein. It was a bit awkward at times tho as a few of the students didnt read the book but pretended to. All in all lots of fun. See you in teh spring!

great class. i loved all the history stuff dr. b. put in the lectures. fgave so much extra credit that I don't have to take the final. highly recommend. i woudl take him again next semester but i don't need those courses to graduate.

Cool class. Lots of reading. I was cool though. Stuff like Frankenstein and 1984. Pretty kind and chill professor too. I ended up with so much extra credit that I just kind of showed up for the last few weeks nand didn't have to do any homework. Highly recomment
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very good at facilitating discussion about the multitude of readings across the semester. Not good at all in terms of posting clear instructions for assignments in a timely manner, and there were multiple occasions where he would wait to upload a discussion post until Saturday (due Sunday). Group/final project was poorly-explained but great.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Openly rude to students during class discussions when given an answer he thinks is wrong or doesn't understand. Will not excuse absences for any reason besides jury duty. Does not communicate instructions clearly or let students know when expectations have changed. Difficult to approach due to both his attitude and lack of communication (ironic)

More of an internship than a lecture. we mostly did group projects and stuff in class. one downside, the text book wasn't used very much and I could have used that cash for something else. Still a lot of fun. taking again next semester for a history course.

I had Dr B. in another course this semester. Both were cool but both had a lot of reading. In this one though we read classics like Frankenstein and 1984 so it was pretty fun. I liked the books more than I thought I would. Friends in other schools had courses like this and read more. I think some of the other rating just didn't want to read?

If you want to read and talk about some big ideas this is the class for you. I've had other history classes and it was a lot less reading than those but it was more than we usually do in public health. He tried really hard to bring everyone along and gave lots of extra credit. I'm pretty sure I'm getting an A as I have a 110% going into the final
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment:
Lots of Blackboard discussions and LOTS (3-4 books and other things) of reading as well. Actual classes are mostly discussion, and he expects you to show up and participate. 

Group project was hard. Posted guidelines less than a week before the presentation date, with almost no detail for what he actually was looking for.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: He is an absolutely terrible professor. You'd think an online public health history class would be easy, but it's not. He assigns too many readings and expects you to interpret them exactly his way. He's rude, condescending, and never replies to emails. Even real excuses count as absences. Grades harshly and barely gives A's. Avoid this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Not the best PBHL professor, he makes things too difficult and he is very degrading.

I wanted to take this class for fun because, I wanted to learn more about the history in Public Health, but he made the class extremely difficult and unenjoyable, maybe he should think about teaching graduate level students instead of undergrads
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I did not learn much from this class, He makes the class really difficult, randomly picks on you, if you don't know the answer he will give you a zero, answer the questions correctly and in 5sec or you won't pass this class. no recordings, no notes, etc. he won't even repeat questions because "it is a waste of everyone time" Don't take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He gives us 5 second to answer the prompt and if you don't there goes your participation points. He said that If we get a B that means that we are doing good and he usually doesn't give A's out. He said he doesn't care if you get hit by a bus. The only way to get an excused absence is if you have jury duty. DO NOT TAKE HIM!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Overall my experience with this professor was horrible. He was incredibly inflexible when it came to any absence including excused absences. He was constantly belittling and talking down to his students. He requires a ridiculous amount of reading for each class. He talks extremely fast and refuses to post notes or PowerPoints. Avoid if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He makes the class far more difficult than it has to be, with too many restrictions that are generally really strict, and the exam and quizzes are written (essay format) on the blue book.

A great class but quite different than my other courses (mainly bio and public health). Each we read a chapter from a book on a different part of us history of public health. There was alot of reading but only a midterm and final to worry about although he graded attendance and how much you talk. I am planning to take him again in the spring.

This is a very reading heavy class. Sometimes 30 plus pages due a week and he expects extensive notes and understanding of the material. Overall, he is rude and does not treat students with care and respect, often telling us that we are too dumb to have our own ideas. The class was interesting but he was not.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A fun class. We kind of bounced around philosophy, sociology, and history. It was sort of your typical 100 level class but with a bit more writing (it was a WI course so that's to be expected). Attendance (and cameras on) is mandatory but there's lots of extra credit if you miss a class. Would DEF take again. (Dr. B. is kind of dorky but funny).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Taking the summer class right now. Class is MUCH more fun than I thought. Lots of guest lecturers and conversations. With the extra credit I'm going into the last day with an average over 100%. He's a bit passionate and goes off on subjects a bit but its entertaining to watch.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A kind and understanding professor. Another reviewer that said he gives 0's for absences--not true, but his "attendance policy" gets confusing. If ur absent, Dr. B. gives the whole class a chance at extra credit. Doesn't care if ur absent. If you want a teacher going over the top to make sure you get an "A," this is the one for you.

Rate My Professor really failed me with this one. Dr. Bonneau does not excuse absences for sickness or religious holidays (attendance points taken off). He expects a specific format for projects/papers but does not provide you with any kind of guidelines until days before due date. So disappointed by the lack of understanding in this professor.

I took the Human Context of Science and Technology with Dr. B this semester. It wasn't like any course I've taken at UMBC but that was okay. We had discussions about crazy stuff like Frankenstein, Forsensic Science, and CRISPR. I think I did well becuase I answered questions. He grades on participation. Good guest lecturers too, esp for bio majors.

My favorite class of the semester (Im bio). It was a bit more work than I expected from a 100 level class, but it covered my WI requirement. Also, Dr. B. was really into the subjects and made the subjects easier to understand. There was no final paper. e just did a presentation with our group. (Blah... group work). The guest lectures were cool foo.

While he is a good professor and cares about his work, I found the class boring. I don't believe we needed to meet for the class which lasted 2 and a half hours with no breaks on many occasions. I personally did not learn anything and could have done all the work on my own without meeting with the professor weekly.

I took this class to check off my WI requirement but am starting to like it. We have some pretty entertaining discussions and write up two quick one page papers per week. One is a paragraph long and another two paragraphs long. Lots of EXTRA CREDIT, too (We are about 2/3rds of the way through and I have a 115% average). Funny guy, too
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: A great class. A fun mix of movies and reading. Well, a LOT of reading, but it was a summer class. Dr. B. managed to mix up things with guest lecturers and debates. I took the class for the WI requirement but am interested in the HCST minor.

Class was a "capstone" course for seniors in History and the HCST program and revolved around a long research paper. Was a bit nervous about that but Dr. B. put me (and the other PBHL students) at ease and worked with us individually. Also, REALLY liked the weekly discussions about current issues in public health seen through historical examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took the class to check off my WI req. Class was an intense winter class and online, but discussions were cool and he was pretty fair in his expectations. Got us thinking about ethics and stuff going on in the world. Guest speaker was pretty great too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I'm a math major and took the class to fulfill a prerequisite. I didn't expect the history of science to be interesting, but Dr. B. is an entertaining lecturer (and could be a stand up comic if he tires of teaching). We read a lot more than I'm used to (but I suppose that's normal for history courses). Essay exams. Would definitely take him again.

Second time taking Bonneau. Watch out because he is not always clear on his expectations for assignments, but don't be afraid to ask questions. Be prepared to read and write a lot. We read 3 small books this semester on top of having small bi-weekly assignments and a research paper. Bonneau is a really nice professor though and easy to work with.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Bonneau is great! I'm not sure what one of the previous raters was talking about, it was great when he sometimes moved classes online, and doing readings is just part of being in a history class... But he's a great professor! I'm taking his class again this coming fall!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: A fun research-oriented class. We saw a project though from start to finish. The group work wasn't half as bad as I've seen it in other classes and I enjoyed the readings.

Took this course to fulfill a req (not a hist major) and loved it. Great lectures and fun activities. Not sure what the person below meant--wasn't a hybrid class but did have online activities? Some reading but Dr. B. is good about giving students his time and there are plenty of opportunities for extra credit. Will be taking him again in the Fall!

Does not post lectures online, and forces students to come to class claiming there could be a quiz any day.  The random switch to hybrid halfway through the semester did not help the class.  Gives out more work (reading and assignments) than what should be given for a 100 level course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great class so far.

Easily my favorite class at UMBC. The lecture were interesting (especially the Art History stuff) and the discussions were super relevant to everything going on today (epidemics, grief, etc). A few of use weren't sure were ready to be "live" again after Covid but Dr. B. was kind and patient. Wish I was a history not a bio major!

if you do not like participating in group discussions, AVOID THIS CLASS! All assignments were sent through email. grades were always put in late or incorrectly. he rambled too long during class, often going over class time, then would yell at us for not participating. no exams but many essays (easy though). no homework. lots of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Bonneau's requirements were really straightforward. You turn in responses to works of art were along with responses to readings. They're very short in length and you don't even have to do one each week. His lectures are really important to attend, but he makes the lectures interesting and fun. 10/10 Great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's not a bad professor but the class is pretty rigorous in terms of writing (it is a WI) but he is a reasonable grader and gives you room for creativity and improvement. You do have to pay attention and do multiple readings which are not too bad. One thing I was not a fan of was the wait time in emails and how hard it is to contact him sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A great class with a fun instructor. The quantitative stuff was a bit intimidating at first but blended well with the larger research and left everyone better historians for the trouble. Going to put Dr. Bonneau on my thesis committee right away.
A genuinely caring professor who cares deeply about his home discipline (history). Lectures were entertaining, even over Zoom, and paired well with the readings. Would ABSOLUTELY take Dr. B. again.

Good professor. Was more lenient (probably because of COVID) and so he dropped a few assignments for everyone. Gives extra credit and has opportunities for students to go the extra mile. Participation is part of your grade, so you need to show up and ask questions/give answers. Overall a fun and understanding professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Bonneau is an amazing professor with great lectures. Attendance & participation are a large part of the grade. At least one of an art reaction and reading reaction every unit, each 400-500 words. There is a group project where you lead a discussion based on lecture. Final project is a 10 min presentation & 3-4k word paper. Great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: What a time for a class on the history of pandemics. Professor B was great. I loved how he brought together art and science to understand the subject matter. Just be prepared to talk in class--he seems to want to hear as much from you as you do from him!

Hes a great person! Although the books are mandatory, he makes sure you learn in every way possible so you can get a better understanding of it. My grade was only low due the writing intensive during the time of the pandemic. If you love writing/science, the class is for you!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Class was super entertaining. Make sure you do all the readings and essays. If you do a quality job on homework and show up to class you will get an A. Easy class but requires a lot of time outside of class. Professor Bonneau is super accessible and he will respond to emails right away. Great class, would definitely take this professor again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This could have been a boring class (the history of ancient and medieval science doesn't scream "fun"), but the prof was really into it and made it interesting. I especially liked how he paid attention to the class performance/comprehension and reduced readings if we needed to slow down and get through tough sections. Highly recommended.
So entertaining you forget that youre in class

Don't waste your time! Not only hard to understand, but handwriting is illegible during lectures. Tests and quizzes are based largely on the lectures, but class notes are not published on Blackboard. Subject is not difficult, but you have to teach yourself. Brags that half the class will either fail or drop out before end of semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Baek is fantastic at engaging with students through humor and being welcoming. I personally liked this class.

Class could be easy if the professor was clear and engaging. Lectures were beyond boring and I learned more from youtube than the actual lectures. Also never communciated with the TA so grading was horrible and discussion had no value.

Not a fan of his teaching. He is hard to understand and his notes are bad. But he is accessible via email and office hours. I recommend using the library study tools. Exams were p easy, and short. Homework was worth 20% of grade and was super easy. This class is definitely passable. But be weary of missing class bc his notes suck.

PLEASE DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. Expect to fail because his lectures make no sense and asking questions is of no help either. The TA assigned is no help either. Please for the love of your GPA and money beware of this Professor Baek. Please ask around to see what professor is better and it will be worth the effort.

Very dry lectures that were hard to follow and often weren't even applicable to the hw. However, he would prepare us well for the quizzes and the hw's being a large part of the grade made things much easier. Don't expect to learn much, but it's very passable. I don't recc taking it if you don't have to take it tho

Never before have I met a more arrogant, inconsiderate professor. 85% of the stuff we went over in class had nothing to do with the quizzes/exams. He was a terrible lecturer. He would put ppl on the spot then laugh when we were confused (which was all the time). Gave out nearly no partial credit on the exam. Avoid if you can.

VERY demotivating unsure what he wants from us. Unsure if we just want to challenge us or wants us to learn. Lecture is not helpful, just practice problems by yourself for tests. Everything's from lecture but students are still struggling. Students can still do well when professors are being kind. Being harsh doesn't always make a good result

reviews.comment: I enjoyed the lectures, he works through a good amount of examples in class which helps a lot. He responds fast to emails outside of class and never made me feel stupid for asking questions. Tough grader on exams but the exams are not difficult. The homework was not that difficult either just tedious at some points.

His lectures are very dry, seem so uninterested. He has a think thick accent which makes it very hard to understand. He skims through practice problems and sometimes won't finish example problems because the 
rest should be "easy". Doesn't provide a formula sheet for at least the first exam from what I remember, other professors provide them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Has a thick accent; lectures were hard to understand. Textbook was unhelpful. Homework was graded for accuracy, but you can look up the answers online and don't have to show your work. Quizzes weren't too hard but the tests were. I have no idea how I got an A in this class- he must have curved the final grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I am enjoying this course so far.

- The lethargic manner of speaking by which this professor delivers his lectures will struggle to capture your attention.
- Exams demand cramming a copious quantity of information into your head in a relatively short time prior to test-taking in order to obtain an adequate score for them.
- Professor provides scarce amounts of hands-on material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you have questions during the exam, even if it is about his wording, he wont answer anything. Chicken scratch over powerpoint. Received first exam back w/over 20 people staying after class to discuss. Got answer right on many questions, majority of points taken off. When asking him, he said he "would take more points off if he could've". Avoid.
dropped the first week..
good
He was passionate about the subject and taught it well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Homework assignments are difficult but are graded by completion. Quizzes are typically very easy if you have a basic understanding of the concepts covered. Class participation is graded on a poll posted at some point during the lecture. Grading policy is fairly lax with partial credit if you show your work.
Excellent professor! The content was interesting and I gained new information to learn. The grading is very efficient and quick.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Inspirational--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Textbook is a better teacher than he is, and the textbook isn't even a good one. Lectures are difficult to understand. The worst part: No transparency or clarity with grades. Deducts massive amounts of points from exams with no explanation for anything. Exams covered content he said wouldn't be covered. By far the worst prof I've had at UMBC.
The critiques below are way too harsh. He really knows the material clearly very smart and willing to go over material again.

If you have another class that is on top of his office hours, good luck passing he doesnt help beyond that. Although the prerequisite says you dont need to know R programming, you definitely do! He is a harsh grader who doesnt give personal feedback since you can find it in the book. Expect to learn better on your own then with this professor.
His lectures will not help you at all, terrible professor. Does not give any examples of R code during his lectures. Overall the worst professor I've ever had. Do not recommend.

It was his first time teaching stat 355, it wasn't the best his voice makes me want to take a nap. just thinking about it makes me tired. I suggest you take someone else, he is a nice professor and will help you out. But if you don't have time then don't take him. Your exams are your only grade for the most part, no extra credit unless "pop" quiz.

R is a hard language to learn, but he is really understanding and helpful. There is a lot of opportunity for bonus points. Also, there's pop quizzes in class, usually in groups. For the most part they're ok especially if your group is good. Sometimes at the end of the semester he'll give you the quiz credit just for actually showing up to class.

nice guy, lectures are HEAVY on notes so if you like notes you'll do good. i had gripes with the amount of reading quizzes for a calc class but apparently thats just how it works usually, nothing to do with dean himself

Take Dean if you can, he's the GOAT. I never went to lecture because he posted all of his notes and they were straightforward. The discussion quizzes help you not fall behind. His exam review he uploads is basically the exam but with different numbers. Thanks for making what I've heard to be a tough course an easy A+ and great learning experience!

He's the best math professor to take if you have the option, his extra credit on exams are very clutch, just try not to stay behind and do practice quizes/exams (they are the same as the exams but with different problems but same concept) and youll pass easily. He grades very leniently and wants everyone to pass

Provided very clear and accessible information for everything you need to know about the course. Lectures were intuitive and informational. If you do all the homework and discussions, most of the questions on the test are repurposed from those assignments. Manageable workload, studying material is plentiful. Overall amazing prof
didn't go to lectures, only discussions. Use practice exams to study, they are the same problems, just different numbers. dont miss any homeworks and study for your quizzes.

Great professor, especially considering the content density of Calc 2. Makes lectures comprehensible and digestible. Reasonable exams. He is no-nonsense and gets straight to the point. Blackboard is very organized with several resources for studying. Calc 2 is a difficult course, but he definitely makes it bearable.

This class is very by-the-book. Prof. Dean goes very quickly, and the class follows naturally, making it hard to catch up if you get lost. Also, he's very strict with grading. I had a 103 fever and had to sit for an exam with a box of tissues. His office hours WILL NOT help you, as his explanations are "That's just how the process is ".

I have some complaints about his TA's, but Professor Dean himself is very kind and shows a clear understanding of the material in his lectures. The homework consists of reading quizzes and homework that have clear due dates, as well as a quiz every week in our discussion. I'd highly suggest doing the practice exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures felt like we were just trying to get through the material vs. trying to really get it. However, Dean is clear, concise. Class went over a lot, which sucks because it's at night. Weekly quizzes. 3 exams, best 8 quizzes. Final is cumulative.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Dean is amazing. Hand-writes all his lecture notes & posts them immediately after. Provides practice midterm exams which are very similar to the actual exams. I went to his office hours almost weekly, and he cares about helping students understand calc 2 concepts. He does go over a few minutes in lecture often though.

Dean's lectures are beneficial because he excels at explaining concepts in class and posts his notes online. Also, his practice exams help a ton for the midterms in the course. Overall, great professor.

Teaches clearly and straight forward. No calculators at UMBC so it makes the math problems simple. 

Drops lowest quiz grades, replaces lowest exam grade with final and grades exams generously with extra points available.

Just study the practice exams and quizzes, extremely similar to the ones they test on to get a high grade.
Math 150 might be the easiest class I've taken thus far. The quizzes, group quizzes, and exams are so straightforward. Dean is a good professor with understandable and well-paced lectures.

The course itself is really easy, but his teaching method doesn't work for everyone. Really nice guy and funny at times, not a tough grader but his teaching style feels rather repetitive at times as though he's just saying things and not actually explaining them. Also, very lecture heavy but he provides resources to learn outside of class.

Prof Dean is amazing. Very easy to understand and all of his tests are basically identical to the practice tests he gives you. He writes his own notes at the start of each lecture so it is very easy to stay with him while he talks. Overall he made precalc very easy and I will be taking him again for calc 2.

2 weekly quizzes: 1 group (T.A.s give answers), 1 solo (same test). 20 min before solo, content reviewed. The lowest 3 groups & solo quizzes dropped. 4 easy exams; 3 have practice exams, actual exam changes numbers from practice. 
No time-wasting Qs in class. Ask vital Qs to proceed; others after class.

Long Lectures.

TAKE NOTES OR YOU WILL FAIL

Lecture can be a bit confusing but overall a good professor. I went to tutoring for extra help and that helped a lot with exam review to. The Practice exams are really similar to the actual exams so make sure you know the material!

If you are going to take Math150 MAKE SURE YOU TAKE PROFESSOR DEAN. I've always thought I was bad a math so going into this class I was nervous, but professor dean actually teaches you rather than just solving problems from a slideshow (targeted lol!) Just read and show up and you will be ok!
He's great practice exams are similar to the real exam so you should be fine.

Professor Dean goes through things a little quickly, and it seems hard to get a question in, but you can tell he cares. He is very polite and responds to emails quickly. The class is very formulaic, so once you get into a pattern that works for you, you should be comfortable for the rest of the semester. There's a lot of quizzes (two per week).

Notes are so good because he writes literally everything down, illustrates concepts clearly and USES HIS ERASER TO CORRECT NOTES because he's a perfectionist, so you can study on your own just with those notes.
lots of extra credit built into exams, final grade replaces another exam if it's higher than that midterm, gives a lot of partial credit.

Don't listen to anybody who says the lectures are "boring". They don't know what they are talking about. It's a math class and it's gonna be boring, but Dean helps you understand. 

Gives good notes and is always able to help if you don't understand. Idk about others, but he gave me an extension for a quiz when I asked.

Dean is an okay professor. He lectures constantly, but I managed to keep up. Pay attention and take notes. Weekly homework is good for practice. Discussions are crucial for tests/quizzes, but with a good TA, you'll be fine. You can't cheat; exams and the final will cook u, so lock in.

TA graded unfairly and when i talked to him about it he didnt seem to care that much but his exams made up for it. Actually go to lecture because even if you half pay attention it will help alot with the final which is kinda rough

Legendary professor. He explains concepts so well. The class was a breeze. The exams were hilariously easy. They were basically the practice exams he gave but the numbers were switched up. The quizzes are also easy. Homework is assigned every week and they can range from 10-20 problems but it isn't too bad. Overall, incredibly easy class.

Solid. The only word to describe him. Every quiz has a corresponding practice quiz that's clear and extremely efficient in preparing you for exams and quizzes. He made Calculus II feel like the easiest college course Ive ever taken. 10% extra credit available on exams, extremely lenient grading, he wants to see you do well in this course; it shows.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, really wants you to learn. Grades the exams really easily too.
Brian is the best professor out there for math. People coming into Calc may find that he goes fast in his lectures, but he posts his notes online and is super lenient on grading for the exams.
Good professor, easy tests, but boring

If you don't take Calc 2 with Prof Dean, you are doing yourself a disservice. His class is amazing, exams are very simple, and--if you study diligently--you can find yourself getting an A. He never throws trick questions or something not following the format of his practice exam, etc. I did much better in Calc 2 than Calc 1 because of Prof Dean.

Took this Spring 2024. He was a good lecturer, but sometimes he'll introduce a new concept quickly and rush through problems with it. While he was willing to help after class, he was sometimes a bit harsh to students who'd ask questions during lectures. However, I still believe he did a great job overall. Just attend lectures, and do the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Knowledgeable but does bad job at material. Lectures are really boring and he would often get annoyed when a student asked a question. He also strictly follows the syllabus, no subject to change about it. I don't think he is that awful of a professor but I would also cry in the middle of his lectures because his course load was super overwhelming.

Absolutely phenomenal professor, in my opinion he is the pinnacle of what a professor should be. Respectable, helpful, makes it clear what he expects and fair. Outside of attending lectures, if you review the practice exams and go to the discussions to review that weeks quiz topic, you will breeze through the class. No tricks, thats all u gotta do.

I took Dean last semester for Calc 2 and he does everything he can to make sure you pass. The practice exams are almost the exact same as the ones you take and while he may be super by the book (I stopped attending lecture after maybe a week), he's infinitely better than the other calc 2 professor (tighe). Do not take her, take Doctah Dean.

Best prof ever for MATH 152, if you have to take MATH 152, take it with Dean over Tighe, explains everything straight in lecture, makes harder concepts easier to understand by breaking them down.
5/5

He is passionate about biology and very happy to help students during his office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The only thing going for Dr. Lohr is that he is very approachable. Otherwise his lectures were kind of boring, though the concepts were fairly clear. The exams which counted for 60% of the grade, had almost nothing to do with the lectures. Each exam felt like Trivial Pursuit. the homework was virtually nonexistent but the discussions were horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Lohr is a great professor, extremely knowlegable and gives very interesting lectures. He is however a really tough grader, my class had a 60% average for the first exam and the top grade for class presentations was a 95% (no 100%). This aside, I do not at all regret taking his class as I have learned so much more than any other bio courses.

Dr Lohr made it remarkably easy to pay attention during his classes. He's an excellent teacher, gives fantastic explanations and encourages discussion. Outside of class hours he remained approachable and patient. He designed assignments to test our understanding and communication in a wide range of relevant topics.

His lectures are well prepared and he is one of the knowledgeable professors Ive had at UMBC. I recommend listen to his lectures in class and try to understand and if you can record and listen to take notes later it would be really good. His tests are not easy, but if you study well and understand, A is not that hard. I recommend him as a logical p

Dr. Lohr is very knowledgeable, and his lectures are crystal clear. However, he covers material at lightening speeds, so be sure to record every lecture. The tests he gives don't test on the important concepts and tend to ask for unimportant details of the text. Also he LOVES asking questions on hormones.

This guy is really knowledgeable and he is very clear when describing concepts and answering questions.  Unfortunately, his voice kind of drones and puts me to sleep.  His exams are a little difficult, but fair and there is still a large curve.
He alright. He is the only teacher for 305 who is articulate. What he says in class is mostly from the book but he goes by pretty fast. Gentle and mostly expressionless. Easy on the eyes though! :)

Dr. Bass is a wonderful lecturer and is always open to questions during and after class. RealChem (used for HW and readings) is not the best platform and frustrating to use, but her actual Blackboard course is very well structured. It is easy to fall behind, but she has many opportunities to catch up and clearly cares about student success.

Incredible information accessibility for the course. REAL Chem is a pain to use at times but manageable. Lectures are consistently too fast to take notes effectively, but as long as you review you will be fine. Tons of out of class opportunities, very friendly professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Chem is very challenging but Dr. Bass does her best to break down complex topics. Her lectures are clear and provide helpful examples, and are thorough without dragging on too long. 

Attendance is not mandatory but gives bonus points (and I'd highly recommend attending). I found the workload of this class to be the most difficult aspect.
dont take lots of work
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: she teaches the content more confusing than it needs to be

She's a really good professor. Always answers her emails, her lectures are very good, they give bonus points if you answer pollev questions in lectures, exams are straightforward and REAL chem is super helpful. I reccomend her and would take her class again!

Honestly, Bass wasn't a horrible teacher at all; Chem is just beyond difficult. For a class like this, a more engaging teacher would've been great, but Bass's voice is enchanted with some sort of sleep spell so that wasn't helpful. However, she always made herself availible outside of class, offered plenty of extra credit, and gave us resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Chemistry is a hard course on its own so I think that a lot of students blame her for that. HOWEVER Dr. Bass is always willing to help and has great lectures - you just need to come prepared and not be lazy. She teaches in a way that carries off the readings and homework which is super helpful - she tells you exactly what you need to do to succeed
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: dr bass is amazing

lecture attendance was extra cred with pollev. lectures were kinda rushed and not the most helpful. realchem textbook/hw was SO annoying. posted multiple old practice exams for every exam except final. second exam brought me to a B. go to SI PASS/other tutoring, helped more than the lectures. loads of extra cred opportunities.
Great professor, you can tell she puts a lot of time and effort into every aspect of the class. The subject is naturally content heavy, so put the hours in outside of class and you'll do just fine.

everything was fine until the final. we were only given 50 minutes to answer all 40 questions which i think was not enough time. i felt so pressured and rushed on most of them and couldn't even go back and check my answers. i also didn't get to answer like the last 5-10 questions even tho i knew how to do them bc of the time;(

For preface, I took CHEM101 last sem w/Carpenter and failed so I had to retake it this sem w/Bass and I gotta say she is SO MUCH better than Carpenter. I'm honestly confused by the bad reviews from this sem bc she's genuinely so lenient, like she gave us sm bonus/extra credit opportunities through PollE, tokens, etc., which Carpenter doesn't do.

If you are a bad test taker you may fail this course. The exams are 60 percent of your grade even if you do well on discussions and homework it's unlikely you will pass. I don't even blame Professor Bass because she is a nice instructor but chem is inherently difficult.
Trust me, it gets worse. Her lecture is bad, and she doesn't know how to teach.
Boring boring boring boring boring, takes all the fun out of chemistry, but keeps all the hard stuff. Nothing is fun about this class, just question after question.

Amazing professor. She was very clear in her lectures, and the tests/homework were over material taught in class. The slides and blackboard course materials were helpful and accessible. Very friendly environment and she is very easy to talk to when needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Bass is a decent professor given a poor curriculum. However, her teaching style is overly fast-paced and lacks depth for true understanding. This course is essentially self-paced due to the heavy reliance on readings and homework assignments from the online textbook, while her lectures are just summarized slides from that same textbook.

Bass is super nice and genuine. She doesn't just read off slides, she explains well, with examples. Reading content isn't too heavy, but lots of assignments each week. Her exams were pretty good: they reflected question styles from assignments. Same with the final which is external: her assignments, notes and exams set you up well for the final.

This class is unnecessarily hard for a chemistry 101 class, even when it is required for most majors and your grade is mainly dependent on exams Just know that this class is a lot of self studying and lectures she just reads off the screen.There are extra credit opportunities for 5% bonuses on exams, but doesn't really help since exams are tough.

Bass is a good teacher! Very well-made slides and great explanations. There is a fair amount of homework, but it's not hard so long as you pay attention in class. Pretty generous with extra credit and exams are manageable with studying! If you put in the time and effort you will do well. She provides tons of resources and opportunities to succeed!

Bass is a good teacher! Very well-made slides and great explanations. There is a fair amount of homework, but it's not hard so long as you pay attention in class. Pretty generous with extra credit! and exams are manageable with studying. If you put in the time and effort you will do well. She provides tons of resources and opportunities to succeed!

She puts thought and care into her lectures, and knows the subject very well. There's so many resources to help you- videos, practice problems, office hours, please utilize all of it. She will gladly explain things if you have questions. Anyone can pass this class if they just stay on top of things.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Bass more than Carpenter because of her genuine care and love for chemistry. But, it is hard to do well in this class unless you self-study and enjoy math, because this course is extremely math-heavy. The quizzes are just like the practice problems she gives out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Bass is great as she takes the time to explain during lecture and will address individual questions. The course is more of the issue. HW and reading quizzes due 3x a week for each. The exams are generally fair and there is extra credit offered but it takes hours to complete. Would recommend to go to Bass over Carpenter for lectures.

Attendance is mandatory because we do polling questions in class that count towards your final grade. There is a bit of work (smth due everyday) but a lot of resources to practice the concepts are provided which are super helpful! She also gives the opportunity of a 5% bonus on each exam if students complete the extra credit assignments :)

Gives way too much homework, flipped classroom approach, her lectures usually consist of her reading off of copy-pasted textbook slides and practice problems that are unnecessarily hard (and grades those problems for accuracy).

Please do not sign up for this professor. She gives absolutely no resources to complete her math heavy work other than these stupid and useless TA's.
