The best professor I have ever had. She has memorized the entire contents of the books she teaches from and is very understanding. If you do not do well in her course it is entirely your fault. She's very curvy and gives plenty of extra credit

She is a great professor. Her exams are straight forward. Gives good examples in class and gives plenty of extra credit on exams. She curves the final grade of an individual based on performance and effort. If you fail, you didn't try. It's a 300 level course, you have to try. Easy A if you try.

She's a great professor. A little naive at times as she discussed students grades in class for those who failed. However, she is such a great professor and her instructions are quite clear. In my academic pursuit this is the third statistics course I've taken and she is by far been the easiest of the instructors to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is very rude and unwelcoming.  Rarely responds to emails or replies back,  3 tests were MC with some extra credit (over 50 questions), 1 test was Free response and the final is free response. You will need to attend class to pass. Aplia HWs had over 50-75 questions as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had at UMBC. She's clearly knowledgeable and explains things very well, and she clearly cares for her students. Attendance isn't technically counted, but she makes a clear point that you should attend all of them that you can; the tests are modeled after what she goes over. She also gives ample extra credit.

Dasgupta is smart, but she teaches ECON  102 like it is a 400 level class and not a 100 level. She expects you to know the material as well as her by the exams and if you don't you'll probably get a C at best.  If you and I get the same answer but yours is more detailed, you'll get more credit on the exams. She doesnt answer emails for office hours

Great teacher! Must show up to class to understand material.  Make sure to do all of hw because it's worth a lot. Quizzes and exams can be tricky so make sure to practice a lot at home. She gives extra to make sure to take advantage of it.  She can be unclear at times so make sure you ask her questions.  No formula sheet is allowed on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Dasgupta runs a quality class. Attending class is a must if you want an A. She is very knowledgeable and answers every question we ask clearly. LITERALLY tells you what to do on the exam for an A. Only issue is she writes on a chalkboard so reading the board can be hard, but will read it out loud for you if need be. Would def take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Best teacher I've had so far at UMBC. She's extremely nice and helpful. She writes her lecture on the board, which is very engaging. I enjoy every minute of her lecture. Offer extra credits if you do well on her exams and quizzes. Come to class and study, ask for help then you'll absolutely pass the class.
I am very disappointed with this class.  I expected a phenomenal teacher based on the reviews but what the teacher is like is so far from that.

her reviews are so unfair because she is such a sweet lady and she cares about her students. She is honestly one of the best professors i've had. Her exams are easy and she gives plenty of extra credits so its impossible to fail.

Not a good teacher. She is focused on looking smart instead of having a thorough discussion with students. I also found her to be very unapproachable.  She never smiled or looked comforting to students. She instead was always stern and was never welcoming. Take the class with another teacher. At least you will have a comfortable environment.

Not a good professor. If you missed class, good luck getting the notes because she hand writes the lecture on a blackboard and won't upload it online. Even if you were in class, good luck getting the notes down, her lecture notes are very unorganized and difficult to follow
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tough grader: Will not curve grades and scores Get Ready To Read: The FYS I took was about Poverty but was heavily focused on ECON Participation Matters: Accused some students of skipping when they didn't  In short - heavy Indian accent, wants to prove how knowledgable she is, and not recommended.  I dropped this class after a month in.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Avoid her for summer stat 351! Hard as hell! Her exams aren't easy and she doesn't give extra credit like in the regular semester on tests

A horrible professor. She is knowledgable but extremely haughty and only trying to prove how brilliant she is. Not a good professor. Her teaching style is uninteresting and demeaning. Avoid her at all costs. I would never recommend her to any student. Save your grade. Exams are very tough.

Dasgupta is very clear and fair. She spends the entire time hand-writing notes (rather than using PowerPoint) which makes the lecture more engaging and interesting.  The fact that she has the book memorized is impressive.  All exam questions are available at the beginning of the semester so there is no reason to not know/understand the answers.

She goes at a fast pace, but doesn't assign homework. She will have handouts online with 300+ multiple choice questions for each chapter or two. THESE ARE YOUR LIFELINE. She pulls exam questions straight from these packets so READ THEM ALL. There is also a lot of extra credit (I ended with a 135% in the class). Do NOT skip her class she will know!

Great professor. If you attend most of the lecture there's a great chance you'll get an A.  I had a C and D on two tests but still ended up gettin an A in that class. She'll call you out if you skip too many classes.

She's a brilliant lecturer with a really really good memory. Even in a lecture hall of 150 students, if you missed a day, she'll know. If you never show up, she DEFINITELY knows. She doesn't use powerpoints just what's in her head, because she can lecture 100% without them. Book not required hw is online (just get access code). Overall so easy.

Super easy professor. If you don't go to class just find someone else who does and get the notes. Not much homework, just a few exams. Most of the exams had questions that we practically did in class. Don't worry about the term paper, it's a joke. Took her for 408 as well, same thing.

One of the Best. She is very clear and is very efficient in teaching the material. If you have any questions about the material she will help you clarify, only if you ask her during class or right after because she does not reply to your emails. Lots of extra credit on her quizzes. 5-6 quizzes and a final and she usually drops the lowest one.

She is the best professor at UMBC. Just study the handouts and you'll pass the class with ease. The class is very straightforward. Professor Dasgupta writes everything on the board as she has memorized the whole book. We rarely used the book in class, so I don't think it is necessary to buy one.

Dasgupta is my favorite professor at UMBC. Very clear, very thorough, and as long as you study her handouts, you'll ace the tests. She cares about the amount of effort you contribute (I missed a final because of an unexcused medical emergency and still landed a C). She gives you very clear instruction. Just go to class!
just one word : AWESOME. she is one of the best prof at UMBC, .take her ! but you need to show up to class, she knows who is there and who is not.

I really enjoyed Professor Dasgupta's class. Yes, she does have an accent but she talks very clearly so that you are able to completely understand her. Her class is all lecture but she engages you and relates the material to real life situations. Also she gives extra credit on all tests and the questions and powerpoints are online beforehand.

you need to show up to class and participate in order to get extra credit. her class is extremely difficult as she touches on matters that may not even relate to the subject. if you are in class and remembers your name she will give you plenty of EC. i did terrible on most of my tests, did extremely well on my paper and homework and still got a A.

She makes NO time what-so-ever for students. Makes other students tutor you if you don't understand. Answers no emails, whether you need a meeting or have a question. No other grades besides tests. She has no reasoning behind the grades she gives. Her accent is strong and you can't read her notes. She never makes jokes and she's very intimidating.

Tests are straight from the study guides, so make sure you study those. Go to class! She knows who is there and who is no, and she will definitely call you out. Study hard and you'll end up with an A or B
Absolutely one of the best professors I've had at this school. Makes econ interesting for any major and the professor has a sense of humor. If you take econ make sure to take it with this professor!

WONDERFUL TEACHER! COME TO CLASS! She has the book memorized, and puts it all on the board every class as notes. Most all tests are multiple choice, and come straight from practice tests she posts online. TAKE HER! She did move fast towards the end of the year, but raise your hand and she'll clarify anything. Accent is a little thick.

This professor is great for Macroeconomics. I highly recommend her. You cannot lose points for skipping class, although she will put an alert on BB if you do (harmless). She follows the book, but she teaches with graphs (easy to understand) much more than words. 7 exams for your entire grade, no HW, only grades 6 best exams, and does curve

TERRIBLE! Avoid her at all costs. She was very knowledgeable about the course, however, it didn't translate well to the class. She would ramble about topics and if we didn't understand she would make the explanation confusing and leave use even more confused. Her notes were also messy. WORST CLASS I'VE EVER TAKEN, WORST TEACHER I'VE EVER HAD.

Dr. Dasgupta is a sweet lady. She's a clear lecturer. Use the study guides she posts online! They look very much like the in-class quizzes. She gives many opportunities for extra credit on the quizzes. Overall, the class was reasonable.

One of the best teachers I have ever had.  Show up to class everyday and she will know you, even if you never participate and sit in the back, it really it quite amazing.  She loves students who come to class.  Also, exams are straightforward and easy if you show up to class.  She even has a sense of humor!  She's a gem of a teacher.
She is a true teacher.  You can tell she enjoys statistics.  She is very effective at helping you understand, and she wants you to do well.  One of the best professors I've ever had.
Excellent professor, attend classes, take notes and DO THE HOMEWORK!!! She is very helpful and willing to assist you so long as she sees you are a serious student

VERYY GOOD TEACHER!!! Make sure you attend class and take good notes. Look over the study guides as soon as they are posted. She is a very effective teacher and her lectures are interesting :) You will clearly know what is expected of you in her class.

Love her! You're really missing out if you take anyone else for Macro! Her lectures and exams are straightforward and you always know what she expects from you. Beware! She will know if you come to class or not, and attendance is a grade. Regardless, missing a couple days will not count against you.

HEY YOU!! YES YOU..LISTEN TO ME. She is one of the best professors I've ever come across. You may hear otherwise but don't believe the lies! Lots of extra credit opportunities. Just come to class, do the practice problems, and the class should be a breeze. If you don't understand, ask and go to discussion to get more clarity! God Bless you!

She's a pretty clear professor. tells you what you need to know for the exams. her tests are based off the study guides so look them over. She says the final is based from study guides but instead it seemed like it was written in another language. Very misleading. Overall easy to get a B.

She has an accent but takes great care to make sure she is understood by everyone.  She knows the material like the back of her hand.  Overall great professor.  WARNING - 90% OF FINAL GRADE BASED ON EXAMS.  If you are a bad test taker, not recommended you take her.
She's a great professor that will try to help you understand the course. Her quizzes and exams has a curve and it is really easy to get at least a B if you attend her class and take notes.

Dasgupta is an amazing professor. Make sure you do her review exams that she post on blackboard because she uses the same questions for the exam. Also attend class so she knows your face for the 10% class participation grade.

GREAT. Professor, she is very very good at explaining concepts in class and cares about student learning she is nice and helpful, One of the best professors at UMBC. Most material is taught in class and little outside reading or preperation is really unecessary. If your looking to take Macro take it with DASGUPTA. period.

awesome prof. read the text, and TAKE THE ONLINE REVIEW TEST. some of the questions are verbatim on her tests. make sure you show up to class once n a while too because at the end of the year you get graded on whether she can recognize you or not.

I LOVED HER. if you need to take econ 102, then take it with her! i hated econ 101 nd i thought that this class would be a drag too but it was reallllyy good. for any of her exams, make SURE you review the sample questions she provides for every chap (even if you skim and understand the concepts you should fine). Easy A!

She makes you do work, but it's helpful.  No homework (besides 4 projects), and the lowest quiz is dropped.  She even dropped our lowest Midterm.  Her primary concern in the students learning.  You won't find a better teacher.

She was fantastic! I was terrified about statistics, but she made everything so clear and recognized if you were attending class regularly. I would recommend her to anyone willing to put in the effort to show up to class.

She is the best! Explains everthing VERY clearly, no hw, just take notes in class and read some. If you attend class and take all her notes, easy A.  She provides a ton of extra credit on tests.  Only assignments are 5 tests, the lowest of which you can drop.  Great teacher
VERY EASY... LOTS OF EXTRA CERDIT POINTS... MUST READ THE FORMULA EQUATION IN THE BOOK.. NO HOMEWORK... SHE TEACHES U TO UNDERSTAND... GOING TO CLASS IS MANDATORY....
Best Econ teacher out there... just read the handout she gives on BB... that sets you up for the tests... easy A i got so for
whats all the hype about her?? how about democracy when it comes to determining the exam date! mmm! perfect for procrastinators who wish for a miracle!

Understands that we're all not little Einsteins so offers extra credit worth almost half of each exam. This means you can literally get 50% and still get a 100% on the test. TA is always available and also very clear and thorough. Not a math person but still excelled in this class. TAKE HER IF YOU CAN. Actually makes Stat half way interesting.

Very helpful to those who want help. read the book before class, or right after to make sure u understand. She will answer any questions u want to go over in the book. doesn't respond to email, but when u come to class she'll answer your question. doesn't take attendance but even in a lecture hall, she STILL knows who's there and who isn't.

Prof. Dasgupta's lectures are very clear and she gives many opportunities to get extra credit; she genuinely wants students to do well and makes the class easy to do well in so long as you go to class and make the effort to understand the material.

Took her 2 years ago, but I still remember her lectures.  She is caring(very), but extremely strict.  All the material she teaches in class will be crystal clear ( in terms of understanding).  Book is not needed to learn the material, just used for examples.  Just show up on class and you'll receive an A/B for sure

She is very nice to the ones who come to class and pay attention. She only taught half of the class, which could be a problem for those going to upper level classes and she added a standardized test into our grades, which was a bit unfair. But overall she cares about what she teaches and the class is easy. All exams have extra credit.

Not very impressive. We covered less than a half of the book. She wasted a lot of time on a dumb kid who was constantly arguing with her, stupid show off--he had no clue. She is good at explaining, but she is very forgetful, repeats herself a lot and uses filler words--not easy on the ears.  She is worth about half of the money.

the class itself was not that bad although it was ridiculous that we had to take TUCE, and she told us about it like 2 months b4 her final... I like her teaching style; i can see how passionate it is. take her if you like econ or want to get an easy A w/out doing a lot of work... it doesn't mean u dun have to study... just try a lit' then u'll get

I'm not sure what all the hype is about her. I don't think she's all that great. I think she's kind of "show offy" when she teaches. She recites long equations and tries to teach calculus in a 101 class. Exams come from the handouts, but the short answers are kind of difficult. I wasn't all that impressed.

Prof Dasgupta is very knowledgeable and helpful.this semester she did something new.instead of giving quizes in class,she posted them online,they were averagely about 80 questions multiple choice online. very time consuming. she makes sure her students understand the material. very nice prof.thinks of her students as her own kids. nice prof!
She's really nice and cares about her students. Her accent is perfectly understandable as well.
Awesome and easy professor. Honestly, if you go to class, pay attention, and do the review sheets, there is no way you can badly in her class. She is really funny and extremely knowledgeable.

I thought Dr. Carrol was pretty good for 101 but Dasgupta is miles ahead in quality. That is to say that Dasgupta is one of the best professors I've had and she's pretty admirable too considering the volume of her work. Come to class, browse the chapters, ace the tests.
this teacher is the best ever at UMBC.....u must take a class with her....she is so nice and beside she knows what she's taking about....

This prof is one of best I ever had at UMBC. Sure she does has a strong authority teaching style but is extremely helpful and has a funny sense of humor....ALthough class attendence is not required, you should always show up for class all the time and do all work if you want a easy A. Its really a easy A if you do all the work!
Stats can be hard, but she makes it easy. Getting an A in her class is easy. Infact, if you fail her class you should change your major

She was very detailed in her lectures. She covered just about everything in the textbook very clearly. Her exams and quizzes were very straightforward. She also has a very bright personality that makes her approachable and she's more than willing to help you out if you have a problem.
Tries to help the class whenever possible with grading adjustments such as extra credit and dropping lower grades.  She has an accent, but it isn't difficult to understand her.
very easy class, just go over the handouts and memorize the questions. sometimes she puts things not on the handout but something she taught in class so you should sometimes go to class.

While she does present the material in a fairly straight-forward manner, she has a very hostile means of teaching.  Ex: when handing back exams will make rude comments to the student who do poorly in front of the class.  Your grade will consist of 2 midterms, 4 quizzes (lowest dropped), projects, and the final.  Exams and quizzes focus on problems

Easy teacher but you HAVE to study all the 300 pages worth of material in order to pass the exams. Have to go to class too!!! She calls you out hardcore in front of the whole class if you dont show up.

Had her for stat351, one of easiest teachers ever.  I didnt buy the book but took really good notes and I got an A.  She gave extra credit on our last quiz, test and even the final, to help those out that werent doing that well.  I highly recommend taking her class you will not regret it.

Very Very easy. A TON of extra credit. Even without it, an easy A. I didn't like her teaching style though. If you read the book and don't come to class, you can still get an easy A. Coming to class is not mandatory. However, if you don't show up regularly she'll ask you why you don't come in front of everyone.
she is very rude if she doesnt like you and its very hard to keep track of how you are doing int he class.. be wary
She is an incredible teacher, she truly makes sure that everyone understands the material and teaches in such a way that you will absolutely understand it. Best teacher i've had yet.

Great teacher! Teaching method is absolutely wonderful. Reviews previous days lessons at beginning of class and explains everything thoroughly. Accent is easy to understand after a few minutes. Clarifies exactly what will be on test and makes tests easier than they could be. The discussoin class is especially helpfull/ a good review for tests.

She's one of the best teachers, teaching wise.  I took this class and her econ class and if you go to class you don't even have to buy the book b/c she teaches so well. She never gave me crap for not going to class, she'll just ask you why you didn't come if your one of those people who always come.  No homework easy tests, she want you to succeed.

Be aware, she has changed the structure of the exams as of fall 2005, she doesn't use the packets nearly as much as before, she has free response so actually have to learn compared to just being able to memorize the answers from the packets, no longer a guaranteed A as in other semesters

shes okay, becareful tho always show up for class and always bring your book otherwise shell call u by name and ask you y u dont have ti or y u werent there. will also constantly as "is that okay?" and just nod and agree else shes a decent teacher, not hard and grades are clear

this class was rediculously easy. all exams are questions from packets she hands out. if you're class is really big she won't do an essay q either. my only problem is that the class was hard to follow because of her broken english but if you want a good grade this class is it. don't buy book.

i don't know wat the other person is talkin about....she is the BEST teacher ever. says "is it clear" alot and wears the same 3 outfits over and over, and has an indian accent, but still underdstandable, but does that really matter...wat matters is that she makes sure u understand everything and is very reasonable and her exams are easy. Easy A.

the nicest teacher ever. U will easily get an A if u even try a little bit. "is it clear". haha...u just have to get used to that :) don't buy the book for this class..u won't use it..just study the packets and attend class.
SHE IS A WONDERFUL TEACHER... yeah she has broken english but you can still understand her. Test are easy and studying old exams helps ALOT! Take her if you want an A or B.

The tests are all from the packets. THE TESTS ARE ALL FROM THE PACKETS! What more could you want??!! The packets have answers on the back. She explains everything obsessively (just prepare yourself to say "yes" repeatedly to her "Is it clear"). Sit back and relax...understand and do the packets, and get an A. She drops the two lowest exams as well.

Extremely easy class when I took it (Fall 2003) but I hear it has gotten harder. We had 6 MC/T&F exams that were directly from the study guide, which she gave us the answers to, and she dropped the lowest 2, how much more could she do to hand us an A! Dasgupta is one of the nicest teachers at UMBC, she makes sure students understand, appropachable.

The best teacher I have ever had my entire school life.  She is very helpful and make sure every student understands the topic.  Best of all, she has sense of humor.  If I will be a teacher, I would try hard to be like her.  Got C on her class.

This class really isn't that bad if you have a little tolerance.  Yes she repeatedly askes if things are clear, but would you rather things be unclear and the professor just move on?  Exams come straight from the packets she hands out, never touched the book.

Too many haters on this site.  Dasgupta is wonderful! Repetitive- but wonderful.  She likes to make sure everything is clear for her students, and is reasonable with dropping grades/ curving.  I had her for econ 101 and stat 351( a boring class no matter who teaches it) and highly recommend her.

I can't stand the ways she emphasize on asking the class if what she says is clear. I hate how she makes it quite intimidating about exams coming up. I don't think her exams are easy. Multiple choices aren't my thing. take at your risk.
worst teacher ever!
Shes nice but her voice is so annoying it makes me want to stab myself. If I hear "is it clear" one more time I'll go nuts.

Also had her for Stat 351.  One of the worst teachers I've ever had.  Sooooo boring.  Repeats herself over and over again in broken english.  So boring I couldn't go to class for fear of hurting myself. If you can stand the boredom it's easy because you don't learn anything all semester. Not helpful

Dr. Dasgupta is an incredibly nice and caring professor. She wants her students to suceed and does everything she can to enable us to do well. The class is pretty easy, if you study the packets she hands out you are guarenteed to ace the exams.
realy a nice teacher...perfect understanding of her subject.will do anythin to help her students..subject was difficult but her understanding will help you out.great teacher..take her
very good econ class, great teacher, she really helps u out. if u know your calculus u should get an A. but if u dont u might have to settle for a B.
Awesome Teacher!

Covers material thouroughly and straight out of the book.  Exams are easy - questions come from the book as well.  Class projects use excel and take minimal time. Nice lady, really cares about her students.
Great teacher.  Take her if you get the chance
Really cares about students.
She is very concise.  Her expectations are clear.  She is super nice and makes sure that everybody is following what she is teaching.
Great teacher.  Very helpful and makes the class and tests easy.  Knows her subject.

Energetic, articulate lecturer. Demonstrated concepts and common misunderstandings in a Python REPL. High-quality, in-depth slides that can be used in place of the lecture if necessary. Built an alternate submission platform to save his students from the borderline-unusable "GL" server -- initially blocked by the dept (Fall '26) but now in use.
shoutout dr donahue, he's so nice and clearly passionate about comp sci. only comp lecture at this school i feel like actually helped me in the subject. i wish i attended more often tbh

Class is in Python as of 2025 fall

Homework is almost weekly, you have to solve 5 coding problems for homeworks
every 2 weeks or so you will have a project due instead of homework, projects obviously take a bit longer
Exams are kind of annoying but they are fair (final is 20% of the grade)

Shane himself is a great teacher, 100% recommend

Amazing professor for CS. All his lectures are fun and engaging and really makes coding easy to get into if you've never coded before or are new to Python. Coding on paper on exams sucks, but it's not his decision to do this.

This class is pretty easy. Shane wants to help students outside of class. Lectures are confusing + fast if you're new to CS though. Attendance not mandatory so I'd suggest watching youtube to learn. Exams are very similar to practice. Go to tutoring for help if needed, they can help you out. Easy class overall

Professor Donahue is really funny and his lectures can be engaging because of that. However, his teaching style wasn't for me - he goes through things REALLY quickly. All of the grading is done by TA's, along with the discussion period, which can be hit or miss (my TA was not good).

At first I only swapped to his class because it fit my schedule better, but I think that was the best decision I made for taking 201. His lectures were so easy to listen to, and he made the concepts fun by referencing video games and writing funny code to explain concepts. He was very approachable as well after class. Overall, great professor.
Such a cool professor!!! Writes code live time and asks questions to make sure we know how to actually make stuff. plus he is funny and knowledgeable and very helpful even outside the lectures :)))

Some people read power points, others truly show their passion to others and inspire, Shane is the latter. An inspiration for myself and in my eyes the ideal of what it means to be an educator. Puts in time, uncalled for to revamp old material and provides clear instruction and support for all students.  He is a cornerstone for UMBC's CS department

Mr. Donahue is a chill guy who knows his stuff when it comes to computer science. Some of the lectures went by fast, but the slides are accessible and have the coding examples from class. Mr. Donahue often asked if people had any questions about the material and would explain concepts clearly. I would 100% recommend taking this class.

Donahue is passionate about comp sci and presents the material in an easily understandable style. He links his slides on Blackboard and always encourages students to ask questions. He responds to emails quickly and is friendly, funny, and polite. He actually cares about his students. You're doing yourself a favor if you take this class with him!

Shane is awesome. He clearly understands the content and can teach it very well. He is not PowerPoint reader, he shows examples and asks the class many questions throughout his demonstrations. He makes every class interactive and fun. Just paying attention and putting the work in outside of class is enough for 201. Shane just makes it easier.

Professor Donahue was excellent! The lectures were engaging and he would always try to link the content to the real world. He was easy to access and provided amazing help with whatever topics I was struggling with. In addition, he would sprinkle amazing advice and sources in his lectures that go beyond the classroom.

He's a safe bet. Shane is a pretty good lecturer. Nerdy best describes him. Approachable, pretty nice, explains things in a way you can understand. Beginner friendly: There's no embarrassment from asking what something means. Responded to emails in good time. TA's do most of the grading. Explains by live-coding, uploads his "slides" online.

Shane definitely cares about his students. Don't be afraid to ask him questions about project/homework (didn't have time to go to office hours, but was still very helpful through email). He might go too fast in lectures for some people, but free feel to speak up and ask questions.

He is very funny. He does seem to go by fast so sometimes it was hard for me to keep up but he is willing to answer questions. In fact, after explaining a concept, he always asks everyone if they have any questions. Hamilton is a bit more thorough in terms of explaining but Shane does a great job too.

He's a morally good person who sincerely cares about his students. He's more than willing to answer questions about the material or the homework during his office hours or through email. There will be a lot of live coding in his lecture which is necessary to understand the lesson if experience in coding is not established prior to the course.

His lectures were very good. and you can tell he actually cared about what he was teaching. Hamiliton is the professor who created all the exams and assignments, so he had little to do with that. I took this class with Hamiliton before and got a C but retaking it with Shane was much better. Also, he responds to his emails very quickly.

Probably the most incomprehensible professor I've ever taken, and when writing on the chalkboard his handwriting is still somewhat shaky. Lecture slides aren't his, and was missing some of what was on HW / half of what was on midterm. Reading textbook is necessary to do good on assignments. Do not take Phatak if you want to learn anything.

Lowkey, half the time I don't know what he is talking about. You are better off just taking it with a different professor or just self studying with the lecture slides or textbook than showing up to his class.

Very confusing. Lectures are useless if you don't have some exposure to digital electronics already. I stopped going because he just rambles for a while and it's very difficult to understand him. He seems like a nice guy, just a terrible professor. Labs feel almost entirely separate from the lectures. If you want to learn avoid Phatak.
The professor does not know how to lecture well, so I stopped showing up. Assignments are often unclear and feedback is minimal. Just watch Neso Academy on Youtube and attend labs and you'll pass.

Horrible professor. Doesn't know how to teach. Awful at answering questions as he just reiterates what he just lectured. He even seemed to get annoyed when people didn't understand him. Online resources were infinitely more useful than this professor. The TA taught the labs better than prof taught the lecture material. Take another prof if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: terrible, terrible professor. dont take. he bad. no teach. no help. took him spring21 sem. lectures + lab not in sync. don't take with phatak no matter what. u wont learn a single thing.

Not a fun class. As a person Dr. Phatak seems very genuine and is very smart. I don't feel like this translates as a professor. Lectures are all over the place, tangents go on and on, and the class walks away more confused than at the beginning of lecture. Reading the sections of the book that he covers in class is really all you need.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had him for 212 and 411. By far the worst CMPE professor I've had. The fact that he is a nice guy doesn't make up for his rambling and incoherent lectures. Would sometimes spend the entire period ranting about something he read in the paper w/o even touching our course material. You'll get an A as long as you show up, but you won't learn anything.

Phatak, while he seems sweet is really difficult to have as a professor. He has a THICCC accent. Throughout the entire course I was confused and I did "well". It was an awful experience and many of the people chose to drop CMPE and go to CMCS instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly, he's a really sweet guy. Not as bad as everyone puts him. You might not learn anything from his lectures, but reading the textbook would do just fine. He tries to make lecture entertaining and you'll guarantee pass his class.

Dr. Phatak enertained the class and ensure questions were answered. Sometimes he could be condenscedning but he overall cared for his students. All you have to do is show up to class and try your best and you will pass the class. Dr. Phatak understands classes are difficult and works with you to make sure you understand the material.

Grade depends on labs, 2 midterms, final. Allows cheat sheets. Heavy accent, goes on tangents. Remembers names, likes to call on people. He will tell exam material in class & review sessions. Talk to the TAs in discussions! Go to labs! Exam avg in 30s, 3-4 problems, more complicated than examples he'll do. B/c curve, I needed 25% overall for a B
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Avoid him at any cost. Take it later with Yonis or Smith. You will not understand a single word in this class. Even thought you need at least B to pass, you will earn B or A depending on the fliping coin that he used. You will not learn -> do not be dump proud about your B or A that you got it, harder things are coming in upper level classes

His lectures are confusing and unclear. He speaks extremely fast, making it hard to understand him. When he learns a student's name, he calls them out, randomly selecting them to answer questions that no one knows the answer to. His test averages hover somewhere around a 30%, which he claims is intentional. Keep in mind 212 is a gateway for COMPE.

his accent is difficult at best. His lectures are bland and he crams a ton of information into them. the grading is basically arbitrary, you will fail his exams. i haven't gotten above a 35% but I'm still going to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Like everyone else said, its basically a guaranteed B if you do labs and homework.  Tests can have a ridiculous curve depending on how everyone else does (ie 30% B). If you just wanna pass take it with him, if you want to understand the material you're better off reading on your own and talking to TAs
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Extremely arbitrary grader. If you show up to exams and labs, you are guaranteed to get a B. There is no question about it. The exams are extremely difficult, but he claims to curve the exams. In reality he doesn't curve the exams, but you will still end up with a B. If you want an A sit in the front row and ask questions. The lectures are useless.

Where to begin? He gives grades by flipping a coin. I landed on the 'B' side and I could get past that easily. However, when I showed up in CMPE310 after 212, I was so far behind because he didn't teach us a single thing. He also didn't really care about us too much because he's a research prof and we aren't research so we aren't worth his time.

Try to avoid. Nice. HARD to undrstnd. Cares abt students so ask Qs in office hrs. Read txtbk b4 class if u wnt to follow lecture at all.  Exams: test creative thinking not just undrstnding of material, designing circuits so practice that in txtbk, sometimes open notes computer, similar to past yrs Tlk to him to get at least a B. Aprox40pt curve.
Awful, he gets his information from the various tv channels he seems to be watching over the weekend.

He is a good professor. Really hard exams but he gives a huge curve. Go to class(though it is not mandatory), participate(He likes participation),Read the book yourself(it helps a lot after his lectures). If you try hard, and he sees it, you're probably guaranteed and B.

I have taken two classes (Bs in both) with him and he is probably my favorite professor here.  Sometimes difficult to understad but extremely helpful.  If you look at class as nothing more than a means to a letter grade he might frustrate you; the classes are well-made to really emphasize learning over mindless formula-following or regurgitation.
He's pretty helpful. His exams are very tough but he helps you out on the grade, just go to class and talk to him a bit you'll be okay.

I had heard bad things coming into the course, & at first I didn't like him so much, but after I got used to the way he speaks I found that he was an excellent professor.  I got a B without opening my textbook a single time outside of exams (VERY good exam-style), & I would have gotten an A if I had done more of the labs.  I'd write more butnoroom

EXACTLY like everyone else has said. A HORRIBLE lecturer. Mumbles a lot. When asked a question, incapable of succinctly answering + often goes off on irrelevant tangents. His (Indian?) accent doesn't help matters. You will learn NOTHING unless u do LOTS of independent reading. TA's Shiva + Lottich r a boon. Couldnt have gotten a "B" w/o them.

Phatak knows this material extremely well, but his lectures are almost useless except for him dropping exam hints.  Despite this he is very willing to help outside of class.  Exams are very hard but he gives lots of credit for basic understanding.  Class is curved heavily, so do labs and homework, and make a good overall effort and a B will follow.

Phatak understands the material, but doesn't know how to teach it very well. His lectures are very muddled. His tests are very hard, but he curves them very heavily, and most people end up with a B in the class if they put some effort into the class.

Doesn't seem competent enough to teach the class.  He takes way too long to explain things and afterwards people still don't understand.  He's pretty funny every now and then, but it doesn't excuse his poor teaching method.

For Chem102, exam sample questions are locked behind practice assignments that are due 2-3x/week. Carpenter will act passive agressive if the majority dont do practice. You won't survive the class if you dont always practice. Always being at lectures gives 2% bonus for exams. If you fail 1-2 exams, you might pass at the end so don't worry.
Do not take if mech e major she is very stingy with due dates and assignments. Practice exam is nothing like actual exam
She is a Great Professor, but honestly she makes the class a little harder than it has to be. She is very Passionate tho which is very nice and she tries her best to make all students succeed

She's honestly really annoying. She thinks everybody's main priority is chemistry or something. She's super demanding and passive aggressive towards students in lecture , there's a lot of hw, and the discussions are graded off accuracy so there's not a lot of room to make mistakes if you care about your GPA.

She really cares about her students learning, and wants to be sure that they care about and understand what they are doing. She's an amazing teacher and if you put effort into any of her classes, you will be happy that you had her.

Take CHEM 101 at a different institute, the two professors are not good. They don't teach, you end up teaching yourself. You're even given an AI professor instead. The exams are nothing like the practice quizzes, and the questions feel unfamiliar because she doesn't want “pattern recognition.”

Dr. Carpenter is a great professor. From the moment you step into lecture you can tell she is passionate and loves her job. If you want to do well in the course, it's very straightforward - pay attention to everything that is posted on Blackboard, take advantage of the insane amount of resources posted. The textbook is online and interactive.

Her exams are very wordy at times and can trip you up. This was my 2nd time taking this class & I had to seriously apply myself to pass. The workload can be very overwhelming to freshmen; I'm a junior and had a hard time. She's pretty funny but moves through the class so, so fast that if you fall behind a little, you spend so long making up for it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
I wished for existence to cease just because of the professor and the course.
Go to the CC, never set foot at UMBC for CHEM, never, this is the greatest sin of my life.

Participation in lectures is mandatory and graded. The lectures themselves are really fast-paced because you're expected to read the material beforehand. It's really easy to fall behind because they're are pretty much assignments/ readings every day. The slides are really helpful, and a lot of practice work is given for you to be successful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Carpenter as a person, but I think she goes too fast when reviewing certain concepts and it makes it very difficult to understand. The whole class feels rushed, and we tend to move on and add too much too early. I dislike RealChem, but I know some people enjoy it very much. Overall, I did not really enjoy this class, which is a shame.

The class isn't an easy one, but she puts in a lot of effort to make her students understand. Her slideshows are VERY helpful, I reccommend taking notes off the presentations over RealChem to save some time. Show up to class --> 3% curve on all the exams. She truly cares about her students, and it's clear she's very passionate about the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Awesome professor. The material requires WORK outside class, but it is manageable. Her slides are VERY helpful for exams, and the curve is STRONG. Just study the slides, don't fall behind, and go to lecture as much as you can.

Enthusiastic lecturer, straight forward exams, and if you put effort into the class (show up to lectures, do the token activities etc) she will match it with extra credit and curves. Chem 102 definitely isn't easy specially over the summer with lab, but I felt that she helped make it very manageable for us all. Just make sure you put in the effort!

Dr. C is an amazing professor, the course is tough but she does her best to make the information easy to digest.  Possibly one of the nicest and most understanding professors I 100% recommend her to anyone having to take Chem 102!

Dr. Carpenter is a great professor but the material can be difficult bc it's fast-paced!! Her slides help w the exams a lot. In 102 there's a lot of overlapping material between the exams so you have to retain previous units. The final is written by ACS. The HWs and readings aren't hard just understanding the material in time for weekly discussions

Dr. Carpenter is a very caring and energetic professor. Her lectures were amazing and she really knows how to break down concepts. She is very accessible after class and she genuinely wants to see her students succeed and is TRULY passionate about chemistry and helping students learn. All her exams were helpful for the ACS final.

Dr.Carpenter is pretty understanding and offers lots of extra credit through homework and exploration assignments.There are 4 exams total, and she adds an extra 5% to your lowest exam score, which helps.But the exams especially the ACS final, can be very different from what we learned in class.Our regular exams don't fully prepare us for the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I had Carpenter for 101 and 102. Made a B in both. She makes fair exams, everything you need to know is on her ppt slides w/ practice, gives practice exams before real exams & gives good extra credit in 102. Bonus 2% on final grade, final was adjusted, bonus point on some exams, extra 5% on highest exam grade. Put in the effort! It's not an easy A.

Professor Carpenter was a great beginner friendly professor for those who need a refresher on Chemistry or haven't taken chem before. I would highly recommend watching some beginner chemistry 101 videos and just getting prepared before taking the class as it does have some new and difficult material and the class moves quickly so go to tutoring!

She wasn't terrible, and the class wasn't too hard, but the professors made it harder than it needed to be. Lots of homework on program with many glitches (realchem), exams were disjointed from what was taught in class. Exams were significantly harder than any of the materials she provided in class. She does post past exams, though, which helps.

She's nice but I don't like her teaching method. Her lectures are not helpful at all because all she does is just read off of her slides. I know some people who didn't even go to her lectures and just reviewed her slides, which are posted online, on their own. If anything, I learned more through RealChem which is an online textbook that we used.
As long as you show up to class and pay attention with some late nights up before exams you should be fine.

Enthusiastic and wants students to succeed. It's important that you understand the material and its applications since the practice questions in lecture are key to passing exams. Make sure you are able to do them on your own and get an AI to generate similar problems for you and you'll be good. You will not pass if you wait the week before to study

Very chill lectures, notes posted online. Sometimes lectures a tad fast and there's a decent amt of online work, but thats it. The questions on exams are pretty chill if you have a general understanding of the concepts and are good at mcq.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The professor is good when it comes to lectures but it's easy to understand if you do the reading & homework prior to the lecture. She gave an extra credit opportunity & a curve. Reading amount is intense, but not hard if you keep up. Overall she's a good prof. & the class isn't difficult if you put in the effort(the occasional late night studying)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
pretty hard class for an intro course, very doable as long as u put in the effort (which I didnt really do but I recommend doing that if u want an A). 

final is not made by profs, it is an ACS exam so I recommend using the official practice book (can be found for free online as well) for that from the beginning of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: They redid 101 for Fall 2024. Lectures were very helpful and slides made sense. Plenty of opportunities to practice in class. Good personality which makes all the difference. But it is easy to lose track of due dates, since everything is on a separate site. If you miss a due date, there is 0way to take it since it locks. Just need to pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Horrible would recommend taking the course at community college if possible. They make the 101 class hard asf for no reason. If you are not a science-type major like me, DO NOT TAKE CHEM or tbh any science here!!

An enthusiastic professor, who is willing to take the time to provide content related resources to help her students succeed. Lectures are just a slideshow of the assigned chapters in the textbook, so they can feel redundant to attend, but with practice questions provided in these lectures, it can make for solid review.

The class was quite tough and had a HUGE homework load and Dr. Carpenter sometimes moves through lectures quite fast but she goes out of her way to provide resources to help students succeed, including extremely good lecture videos, reading guides, and practice assignments. (I suggest making notes on the videos before class to ask questions.)
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good at teaching and knowledgable but she lectures quite fast and it's hard to retain anything unless you actually do the reading beforehand. Need to read the textbook because the slides from class are not enough. The exams are okay, but you have to really know what you're doing to do well. Gives a lot of resources and opportunities for help.

Tara can be intense, but her high standards really pay off. Stay on top of the material and utilize resources like unstuckstudy ai, and you'll likely do well. The workload is manageable if you put in the effort.

I took this class in the summer and it was definitely hard, but the homework helped a lot in understanding the material. I also feel like she rushed a bit in her lectures but that was understandable, being a summer class. I still really enjoyed the class though, it was obvious she loves chemistry and wants her students to as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She's a very good teacher and her lectures are easy to follow along with since she is so dynamic. There is a lot of homework and practice problems, but I feel like those are necessary in order to grasp the concepts taught. The exams can vary in difficulty but tend to be pretty difficult so you have to study the material well.

Professor Carpenter is a great professor, she is very tough on rules and grading, but when you are teaching 250+ students at a time you have to be. As long as you attend the lectures, pay attention, and submit your assignments on time, you'll be fine in her courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: While I have Professor Bass over her as an overall chemistry professor, Dr. Carpenter is more than capable of teaching. Even though you might receive a slick comment from her, do not be afraid to ask questions because chem 102 content is a significantly more challenging course than 101. UTILIZE SI PASS AND EXTRA CREDIT.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Even as someone who did well in the class, many things could have been done better. Random topics from one slide will be featured on three exam questions, and other things she stresses to study will be mysteriously absent. She can be demeaning when she responds to questions or criticisms, I recommend SI Pass or TA's for advice heavily over her.

Although she is a nice person, i don't really like the way she teaches. I learn absolutely nothing from lectures and I just go there for attendance. I've barely been passing chem 101/102 w a C/C+. It is a very difficult course, I'd rather take it at a community college and earn an A than deal with this type of stress.

Dr. Carpenter is someone who doesn't put up with nonsense, and I love her for that. Even though it may seem scary, her demanding your full attention pays off tenfold and she absolutely wants every student to succeed. She'll respond to every email and almost nothing will stop her from holding office hours. She's a very smart and kind professor.

The worst professor I have been with so far. She couldn't teach well, nor match what she teaches with the Exams. Trying what you have learned is so hard. The other helping resources she keeps on mentioning are completely useless. I reached out to tutors, si session, youtube videos & the textbook, but all was useless.

Your performance in a class with Carpenter will depend on your interest in Chem and quality of prereqs. If you have a solid understanding and interest, you'll do well because there's a lot of practice. If you took 101 at a CC or AP, you'll likely struggle since carpenter doesn't review anything because "you learned that in 101", when many did not.

Dr. Carpenter is a great professor, I wish she was here the full semester though because it really would have helped me more with the final few units w titration. Extra credit was added once more after exam 2, though I think it would've helped me personally more if it was before exam 2. Overall this class is not difficult at all, so don't worry.

Carpenter gets a bad rap but honestly, as long as you show up to lecture as best you can, attend Discussion, practice using the Blackboard practice and review the practice exams, you'll atleast notch a B. Exams make a huge chunk of your grade though! The people who complain are mostly those who treat it like highschool (freshmen)

Def would suggest to take at a community college. There's alot of work and she doesn't even give students enough time in order to do it. Class is very exam heavy and even if you get a 100% on everything else you will most likely end up with a D. The exam are very and when i say very VERY! difficult. Would not take again and literally changed my maj

I notice that a lot of people hate on Tara due to their poor performance in both chem 1 and 2, but I truly would put a lot of that blame on the individual. Her exams can be hard, but she genuinely tries her best with extra credit and assisting us, a lot of people just choose to do less than the bare minimum and then blame her for their poor grade.

Tara is my worst chemistry professor, the load is so heavy and she is not trying to make it easy for us. We are failing and she says "I don't know what to do you guys anymore since all of you get good grades on poll but fail the exams".
I advise taking the course outside at any other community college instead of attending with her.
her lectures are not helpful at all. you will learn something in the reading quiz the night before which is completely different from the lecture the next day

Unenrolled because class does not set you up for success. If you struggle with chemistry I would recommend submitting a verification of transferability form and taking your chem requirements at your nearest community college. Get a C or better at community college - it fulfills chem requirement, grade will not count towards GPA, and it is cheaper.

Carpenter was okay. The way she taught during lecture felt rushed and harder to understand than Bass's lectures. The course itself is doable but requires a lot of work outside of class. Exams are fair but the final is difficult because the Profs dont make it. Do not slack off on regular exams. The final is worth more of your grade and it's harder!

Dr. Carpenter is an overall ok professor but rushes through lectures/explanations. For this being CHEM101, you are expected to have a fair amount of background chemistry knowledge. It is extremely easy to get lost or fall behind. Be prepared to spend at least 30-40 hours a week doing chemistry. Assignment, quiz, and homework heavy. Difficult exams!
She's amazing! Her lectures are always so fun and she's always very energetic and passionate! Make sure that you don't skip lectures though because you can easily get lost. CHEM101 is a heavy class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: CHEM 102 can be hard if it doesn't click, and Dr. Carpenter doesn't make it any easier. She provides ample material for self-practice. But if you don't understand smth she will most likely say you should have learned it in 101, and will not explain it further (even if the whole class has the same issue). If confused go to youtube, not her.

I do not even understand how she is still working. Would openly flirt with certain male students during lecture (?!?!), did not make it a point to know me or remember my name, would actively condescend anyone who dared ask a question during lecture, and would explain concepts in the most backwards and confusing way. YouTube helped some.

I honestly do not understand how this teacher got her credentials. Explains Chem in the most confusing way possible. If you're taking her class, make sure to watch lots of youtube videos on the course content or else you will fail

This class was very time-consuming, I would spend hours on end on blackboard practices and Aktiv practice to really understand and excel in the math and just enough to get an A. Professor would go over in class how to do them and do polling questions which were helpful but tests were not easy unless you put in the time and work for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Midterms weren't hard as long as you came to class and did the practices outside of class. Final was really really hard, but she curved nearly 10% on it and lowered the grade needed to get the next letter grade (so for example a C was a 67 or smth.) A bit petty as a professor but her method of 100s of homework really do help you learn the material.

Didn't find this class too hard, just do blackboard practices along the way. Didn't like how discouraging she was, literally laughing when we got a question wrong + expecting us to do bad. Her explanations were overcomplicated to the point where I had to tune her out in class. Exams 1-3 are exactly like BB, find a ACS source to practice for final.

The midterms weren't terrible. But then we had the final using ACS questions. I'd highly recommend just buying the study guide because none of the previous exams or even homework can prepare you for the way that the final words its questions. 70% of the class earned a D or lower on the final. Use that information as you will.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: hard class, but ended w/ A through hard work. IF YOU DON'T FULLY UNDERSTAND SOMETHING, DON'T MAKE THE MISTAKE OF ASSUMING IT WON'T BE ON THE EXAM. no curves at all. to do well, do the optional Blackboard practices + Aktiv follow-ups. didn't like carpenter's attitude toward people asking questions tho - actin like ppl know should know already :-/
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: good lecturer but sometimes over explains concepts. definitely do the optional practice on blackboard. there are homework assignments almost every night or every other day on aktiv that open three days prior to the deadline. hard course so def practice- 70% is from 3 exam and final, 15% homework, and 15% discussion.

The attendance wasn't mandatory, but I'd highly recommend going to class, so you can get extra grade for participation. Space practice was REALLY annoying, but do it! It will do A LOT to help your grade because its 30% of the entire course.

Yes there's homework and pre-class assignments, but they're 40% of the grade. I'd rather have that than 85% of the grade being tests. She was nice as a professor, though she doesn't actually teach much in class. Instead she uses polling which can be a time-waster since only a few questions are covered in one class. But she gave a 1% bonus for it

Professor Carpenter is a great person overall but the course itself is really overwhelming. You will have about 10+ assignments per week and it's legit nonstop till the final week of classes. And the final exam had a lot of information that the class never even went over so prepare staying up extremely late doing Unit modules and Spaced Practices.
Okay teacher. Would not round my grade to an A when I was .02% off the A. She also sang songs during lecture? That was kinda odd.

Homework was awful. I spent every day crying because there were assignments due at 8 AM every day and then due at 11:59 PM every night, including weekends. Horrible. Would never traumatize myself like this again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: No idea how ANYONE likes this woman. It's extremely difficult to communicate w/ her. I feel like this class was supposed to be easier but instead I felt myself constantly being overwhelmed by the daily HW assignments, including the ones due on weekends. She lacks clarity as well. I'd write an entire thesis on how awful she made this course for me.

I had prof.carpenter in spring 2021 online. She created the spaced learning for our class and it did wonders. I would not have passed without it. I was really scared of her in the beginning, but she really cares for her students and wants the best. Do your homework, watch the lectures, read the book, and most importantly practice and you will be ok

Realize it(homework website) is a blessing and a curse at the same time. Assignments are every day, sometimes up to three a day. The weekend assignments are the most annoying. She changed her syllabus a few times to accommodate students which I liked and genuinely care about students' performance. If you put in the work an A is very attainable.

Get ready for minimum 30 mins - 1 hr homework every single night including weekends. If you email her she will either not respond or give you a very condescending response. There is no extra credit or make up assignments but assignments are repeatable so keep going until you get an A on every homework and you'll do fine.

Way too many assignments. Some days we had 2-3 in addition to them also being every day. Carpenter was rude when you emailed her questions about the homework or the exams so don't bother with that. God forbid I try and email my professor! She changed the syllabus multiple times and is so proud of her teaching methods when they taught me nothing :)

She is an amazing professor that cares. If you follow clear direction an A is definitely possible!! She gives A LOT of opportunities to improve your grade in any way possible. The only issue I had was the weekend homeworks. It got annoying having to do chem everyday, but its definitely worth it for the A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Honestly, I thought the course was HORRIBLE at first, but the everyday assignments really do help you learn. Dr. Carpenter is truly caring and has mastered the concept of learning and awarding good grades based on LEARNING. I wish there weren't as many weekend assignments and I wish she didn't change the syllabus so many times, but it was all good.

Dr. Carpenter is one of the best professors at UMBC. Be prepared to do a lot of homework. There will be homework due everyday, called Spaced practice. While it is a pain, it is really helpful and exam questions look similar to those on the homework. One of the kindest professors on campus and will go above and beyond for students.

Was a pretty easy class honestly, tons of homework. People like to do stuff on the weekends and we had homework on the weekends so that was something but if you don't do anything on the weekends, its not that bad at all as each hw should only take you 30 minutes.

Professor Carpenter has this philosophy where if we keep doing the same units over and over, it will be burned into our heads, which is good learning. The only thing is she makes us have homework due everyday including weekends, and they are only accessible 2 days out of the due date. Its tedious and some units are long. Only 2 exams, thats nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Avg homework (hw) has 11-17 questions with about 3-5min/problem. Max time is about 1.2hrs/hw IF you understand the content. Min time is ~15-30min. Some days will have 3 hw assignments. This not including required learning module (30min-3hrs).
She genuinely cares. The weekend homework was annoying, but at the end of the day, it helps you learn the material. Just wish it wasn't as exhausting but if you do the homework its an easy A.

Like others have said: very controversial this semester. Some hated her; some enjoyed it. Daily assignments that lead up to bigger quizzes. I felt prepared enough with the amount of hwk that I didn't need extra help. I really enjoyed her way of teaching. Online unit modules were easy to follow most of the time. Not an easy A, but not too hard.

If you take this class, get ready to do homework every night, including on the weekends. Two exams - the midterm and the final. The midterm was units 1-11, the final is units 12-27 which I'm grateful for, but there's homework due during the week of the final still. Lectures aren't mandatory and you can learn of what you need from homework. Beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Tbh I know alot of people complain about this class but it isn't too bad. However we do get assignments almost to every night, but it really is just homework, 2 exams, and discussion which isn't too bad. Homework is quick if you just read the textbook.

HORRIBLE. DO NOT TAKE CHEM WITH HER. SHE PUT ROACHES IN MY DORM. She's my 10th, 11th, 12th, and 13th reason Astaghfirallah. Her "system" of teaching is horrific and has given me PTSD. You have assignments due every single day including weekends, sometimes up to 3 assignments in a day. Would rate a -100000/10. Save yourself and your sanity.
She is my 13th reason
