Not an easy class. The tests varied with difficulty but there was always some very tricky questions. These questions required comprehension skills from the test-taker that I just don't think is necessary in a 101 class. However, I do feel that I learned the book pretty well. Paying attention to detail is crucial. Be sure to do book problems!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Getting an A was very difficult because her test questions are tricky. Read the questions very carefully. Do readings before class. Pay attention to the little details in the textbook because they'll show up on tests, like paramagnetic vs. diamagnetic.  She does care about this class a lot and knows what she's doing, but you'll have to work a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: If you pay attention in lectures, and  take notes from the book, you should be fine. However, take the rating below me into account. Even though this is a weed-out  class, I had to put in a ridiculous amount of work to get an A. I took 17 credits and this class required more work and was more difficult than the rest of them combined.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This was not an easy class at all. No matter how much you study, her exams are difficult. I studied every ounce of energy and barely managed to pass. The questions in her exams are not based on what she teaches. Material is very concept heavy, you must know the concepts inside and out. Worst professor I have ever come across.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She expects you to read the textbook to cover most concepts, and in class you'll practice them. Like others here mentioned the exams are tough(got a 5 on AP Chem but haven't managed to get above a 90% on the non ACS exams. Just make sure you read the book, go to office hours if you don't understand something and read questions carefully.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This teacher makes class harder than it really needs to be. If you read your book before class and pay attention you can do well in class but the exams are ridiculously hard. The final exam is a standardized exam by the ACS and students do way better on it than they do on any of the other exams which proves that they are way too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Exams are extremely hard for a 101 course. She will throw 2 million curveballs at you. If you feel like you're prepared for an exam, just know that you're not.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: so, yes this is a weed out course but she makes this class way harder than it has to be. If the class average is a D on every exam every year it might not be the students... be prepared to study hours for the exam just for the wording of the questions to trip you up. Only thing that taught me was ALEKS

Dr. Carpenter is very nice and enthusiastic. She gives students resources to pass the classes (recommended problems, SI/PASS, etc.) and it is up to students to seek help if needed. However, you really need to work hard in this class to pass. Reading, going to class, and putting effort into class are required if you want to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The average for exams in my class was a high D. If you are not so strong in math, be prepared to suffer a little bit. As a student who took AB calc in high school, I was pretty proficient in math and this helped me in the course. SI PASS (supplemental instruction helped me a lot, as did doing additional and recommended problems (these are key!!).
I LOVE HER!!!!!! You can't lay back and expect A of course duh

Dr. Carpenter is a great professor, if you don't mind feeling like you've got the test in the bag, and then 1thousands of curveballs are thrown your way. Every exam was much more difficult then all of the practice exams provided. There were clearly questions written to mislead everyone. 90% of the people I know in her class are failing due to exams

Carpenter is a crazy person.  She is mean and shouldn't teach this class because I don't think she even knows what she is talking about because she doesn't explain anything.  Do not take this class. You will cry all the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Carpenter is nice and she's very good at giving a fun and knowledgeable lecture, but her tests are way too difficult for a 101 class. As a person I think she's nice and a little intimidating but her tests messed me up and made me  question if I could handle my major.

Doctor Carpenter is very bright and intelligent, but she's one of those teachers that you either love or hate. Her exams are unnecessarily difficult (tricky questions). Also, you don't "learn" much in class at all; you teach yourself by reading the book, and you're quizzed in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Literally the worst professor I've ever taken in my whole life.  Honestly, the only thing you can do is go to all the tutoring sessions you can and spend hours trying to learn this stuff.  Each test is worth roughly 15% of your whole grade. And you have 4 tests altogether not including the final (which is also 15% of your grade).

Easy A for me, as I took AP Chem. I did see a lot of other students struggle, however, and all her test averages hover around 60%. She doesn't explain things very well in class, but will explain better during office hours or 1 on 1. She also is kind of condescending to kids who are learning this for the first time and thus lack basic understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: A lot of people don't like Dr. Carpenter but I really found her to be very intelligent and wonderful professor. She is excellent at explaining concepts. This class is very intense and DO THE RECOMMENDED PROBLEMS! THEY ARE NOT RECOMMENDED BUT NECESSARY! If you try and take your time to learn the material you will succeed. Final is ACS standardized.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Reading the textbook and practically memorizing all of it is mandatory or you won't pass the class. The exam averages were always a failing grade and she doesn't curve exams. I ended up dropping this class and changing my entire major because of how difficult it became. Be prepared to work long hours on homework!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Had her for 101 and 102, DO THE READING, her reading guides will be your friend. I took AP in high school so her course was quite easy for me, but I do admit, at times she is not the best at explaining herself. Great person overall, always willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Carpentar is a very difficult professor. Basically make sure you are only taking 1-2 classes the semester you take chem 101, YOU NEED TO FOCUS ALLLLLL of your attention on that class!!
Very tough class, emphasizes learning and not memorizing. Skip class and miss out on points that youll desperately need in the end. Beware of this professor.
Can be nice sometimes but is very blasé and dismissive towards people who don't go to her office hours. Lectures are not very informative, would recommend going to tutoring center.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is the absolute worst. Everything on her exams were not even on the study material that she gives out. Basically, her tests are based purely on luck. Don't even bother studying because she has no idea whats shes doing especially for a 101 course. Too bad this school can only afford 1 chem professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She'll test us on things uncovered by lectured. Three topics on an exam weren't even mentioned in class let alone covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Carpenter takes excessive pride in her chemistry ability. She told the students at  her office hours how she bombed out of every subject except chemistry while in school. As a result she makes the class far more difficult than a 101 class should be. sadly she is the only lower level chem professor. This made me change majors.

The absolute worst teacher I have ever had. She was extremely unhelpful in terms of teaching and this is basically an entirely self taught course. She goes extremely quickly and hoards you with clicker questions so be prepared. Seeing her during her office hours did not help me much and she wasn't very polite to us when she was in a bad mood.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I had her for both 101 and 102. I disliked her very much both times. I think the whole flipped classroom is not meant for a freshmen/beginner level course. Her exams were tough for a 101/102 course and she was of no help inside or outside the lecture. The whole chem 101/102 is a weed out for all the stem majors. Must work very hard to earn ur grade

She is not such a bad instructor as some of my colleagues believe.  She is in fact very helpful when you approach her for help.  I found her to be quite clear as well in classroom. Agree she could have been a little easier when it comes to grading, but what else you expect in a chemistry course?
Great but Tough Professor!
greeeeeeat + VERY HOT

She's not terrible. She's a tough grader, has awful tests, and doesn't tell you much in lecture. The hardest problem with her class is the sheer number of grades that she crushes you under and the stupid grading criterion.  Her lectures are just practice problems. She doesn't really "teach" anything.

I did work a lot for this class in the beginning of the year, but once I found my way of studying I did't study too much. The main thing is that different people have different ways of studying for this class. A lot of people come into this class expecting that its like high school, but it is not. What I noticed is that this is the regular.

If you're taking this class really get ready to put forth effort specially freshmen. A lot of the material is self-taught and lecture is solely used just to clarify some information. If you don't understand the material in lecture then office hours become very helpful. Always do end of chapter problems most of the test questions come from there.

She doesn't teach. You have to read the book and teach yourself. Class consists of a bunch of clicker questions based off what we read, no lecture. And she barely even goes over the clicker questions. Sometimes she is very rude. I definitely don't recommend her. Very disappointed.

She makes the test exceptionally hard and she doesn't usually go over the contents in class. You need to set your own time to go over it. In class, it's usually just group questions. And lots of reading quizzes

Dr. Carpenter explained things very well and answered as many questions possible during class. She provided us with many resources such as practice exams, practice problems, and office hours. However, I felt that her exams were unfair and had many trick questions. She only curved the class by 3%. You need to put in the effort or you won't succeed.

She gets a bad rep but honestly she provides her students with many ways to prepare for her exams including practice tests, practice problems, and there are usually sessions held by the TAs.  An A in this class isn't difficult in this class if you use all the resources you are given.  I think she is very clear when explaining concepts within chem.

I took this class as a Freshman (took Chemistry AP but did not take the AP test). My advice would be to read the book thoroughly. She assigns chapters to read before class, so that you are familiar with the material as she explains it. Make sure to do this, and do not fall behind. If you follow this task, you should receive an A on every test.

I actually loved Dr. Carpenter. She was so helpful! I ended getting a D on the first exam and A's on the others! She gives so many resources to help you. I think I'm going to end up with an 88 though, however, I do think there is a slight curve. Study from the book, and read before lecture!

Tests can be tough, if you don't study. There are so many ways to practice ahead of time (practice tests, review questions, reviewing ALEKS), make use of them and you can pass. If you took AP chem in high school, this is all review and you should be fine. Don't skip class because of clicker questions. Study/read and you can get an A, no problem.

Tara Carpenter is almost the most stereotypical professor in terms of professionalism and attitude. She almost takes it personal when the class does poorly, and will vocalize. She can have an attitude, but most of the time if people shut up, she lectures... However you must teach yourself, class is for practice and reading quizzes.

She is the only option for CHEM 101 so just brace yourself and use ALL of your resources. Go to the RLC for tutoring and reviews before tests & make sure to go to her office hours. Reviewing everyday is key to passing.

She's a pretty good professor. I took AP chemistry and this class very easy for me. I, however, did have to study minimally. She does offer many resources to help you get an A, just make good use of them. Don't miss class. Don't miss discovery. Exams are a little tricky, make sure to read and re-read the question.

This professor does not help at all. I recommend getting the textbook because you will be doing a lot of self-teaching for this course and her CHEM102 course. Her tests are the spawn of Satan. Her lectures are 0% helpful. She gets frustrated easily when you go to ask for help and don't understand the concept immediately. Good luck, you'll need it.

This was the worst class I have ever taken at UMBC. When you ask her questions she can be extremely condescending. If you've never taken chemistry before good luck. She makes this way harder than it needs to be. This class jeopordized my standing in other subjects as well because it takes up so much time to study for.  Don't take if she's teaching!

Carpenter teaches every single Chem101 class. This class is made unnecessarily difficult and the amount of work/studying required is not proportional to other 100 level classes. This is because Chem 101 is a weed out class for STEM majors. If you can avoid taking carpenter for 101 or transfer in credits, you would be wise to do so. It sucks.
Took her for chem 101 and chem 102 and 102 was way easier. She uses them as weed out courses

Dr. Carpenter is a very good teacher; she says very early that you should do more practice problems, and begin studying early. THIS IS TRUE! If you don't, you will not get the grade you were hoping for. However, the tests are very tough for ALL the Chem classes. They have multi-conceptual questions. They make you think. You gotta work for it!
Great teacher but you must work hard to get an A. You must reach success at success at success.

Dr Carpenter is a fantastic teacher. She explains things in ways understandable to students, is approachable, and genuinely would get to know every student if she could, even in her 600 person lectures. Her exams are tough, but reasonable.

She's a good chemistry teacher. I came it knowing basically nothing about chemistry and as long as you do the end of chapter problems along with the reading like she recommends you'll do fine. Don't underestimate the class though. It is challenging
She makes you work for that A, but it will be worth getting to know her

Dr. Carpenter seems really nice at first but after the first exam you soon realize that she makes this class much harder than it needs to be. There will be a lot of work and it is extremely difficult if you don't already have a good chemistry background. This class is self teach. Sadly she is the only chem 101 professor so be prepared to struggle.

She is hardworking, dedicated professor.  She is not too easy but is fair. Managing hundreds of students each semester is not an easy task. She immensely deserves the teaching award!  I am proud that I took a course from an award-winning professor!
Congratulations, Professor Carpenter, for winning the Outstanding Faculty Award from the Alumni Association!  Well-deserved Recognition!!
I took her CHEM 101 and 102 classes in the 20132014 school year. She's a great teacher but she does NOT just hand you all the information you need! You must study on your own to do well!

Great professor. However the work needed  to pass is horrifying. There is this online homework called ALEX which can take hours to complete, the homework is also due 3 times a week. Discovery is a nightmare, but these things have nothing to do with Carpenter. Take her if you want to learn, but do not think it will be easy.

I found her to be rude and also made the class way harder than it needed to be. I avoided approaching her for extra help because when I did, she was sassy and made me feel worse for performing poorly. Exams were very tough if you have a weak background in chemistry. Reading, note taking, and practice were all essential.

Took her for 101 and 102. It was not easy. Ended up with a B in 102 because I ended up working harder in 102. Study and find a way for you to learn the material. The exams are manageable if you study hard enough and learn the basic concepts. Go to office hours if necessary. Small curve depending on how the exam averages were.

She was hard, no question about it. However, if you study then you will be fine. I did not study and failed some of the exams. There is a small curve depending on the average exam scores. Discovery was a pain.

A lot of people on this site say a lot of had stuff about her, but she offers LOTS of opportunities to get better. For one, she has virtual office hours twice a week, and also on days before exams. She also offers surveys, for extra credit, and she gives free points out a lot. Her lectures are very helpful. Before class, read the chapter though.

I got an A in her class but I think that's because I had a pretty solid chemistry background. I agree with most of the feedback. Makes it hard to answer easy questions. Too much work for an intro class. Chemistry can be intimidating, she only makes it worse.

She makes the class tough for the sole purpose of giving legitimacy to her subject - intro chem. There is no reason for this course to be as tough as she makes it. I'm not really sure what her objective is. The averages for the exams is around 70%.   Lets not get ahead of ourselves. We are talking about intro chemistry.   I think it's ego.

If you do the work you're asked to do and read the text book on your own to learn the material, then practice in class, you will do well in this class. If you're a freshman, be aware that a lot of college classes require A LOT of work outside of class. This class asks you to learn the basics on your own then learn problem solving in class.

If you read the textbook, take notes, and do practice problems, you'll be fine. Dr. Carpenter is super helpful; she literally tells you everything you need to do to get an A, you just have to do it. She's very helpful; she has office hours and virtual office hours every night before exams. She's sincere and rly does try to get u to pass her class.

. I was a chem tutor in high school and NEVER struggled but this class was absolute hell. You have to devote hours upon hours to the work. Like online hw before class, quizzes every class, practice problems after class, discovery for 2 hours etc. I went to office hours and tutoring and studied constantly and still failed along with 20% of the class
She's very nice and very clear!

This is a tough class, not going to lie.  However, Dr. Carpenter tells students from day one that the course is going to be tough.  You really have to devote a lot of study time for this class.  One thing that is an absolute must, MAKE FRIENDS IN CLASS. Discussion is allowed with clicker questions, and it's so easy to ask a friend for help.

The class got difficult very quickly. You're going to do well if you devote a lot of time to this class and pay attention AND MAKE FRIENDS. I can't stress this enough, do not try to go at it alone, especially for the clicker questions. Carpenter is always open to help, but can be intimidating.

I took AP Chemistry and scored a four on my AP Test during my senior year of high school. So I had already had a good exposure to the subject, but I found the class was a good review of the foundations of chemistry. As a fall semester freshman, it was definitely a good choice to retake to lighten my semester and boost my chemistry confidence.

Chem is a tough subject. I wish she would explain things more. The exams were crazy hard never got higher than a C on them. Average was between 60-72% Thank god she doesn't make final exam anymore its department based now.

Don't let other reviews fool you, this class is not extremely challenging but you must be dedicated and take a lot of time to understand the material. The tests are very tricky. When Carpenter says "know the exceptions" she means it, that's exactly what she tests. With effort, you can get a B but it takes a little more for an A. Carpenter is cool.

Need to read the book and do online homework and come to lecture and study like crazy. The whole lecture is clicker questions- she barely teaches. She is very dedicated to the class, though, and will answer questions on blackboard or in office hours. Very tricky questions. You'll need to work a lot for this class.

This class may be what is wrong with UMBC and college. This class made me: 1. Want to give up my dream 2. Want to transfer *She does not teach it is all clicker qs. *She is unapproachable and only answers you in office hours *she does not explain in class * tests are hard for no reason * class consumes life. Say bye to sunlight

SO she's fair, it's not a B.S class and you should go to a majority of classes as, in my semester (2014), she had quizzes in each unless she announced there wasn't. You have to go to discovery, which is group work, for 2 hours or you get penalized. Test are tough average of averages was about 68-72% .

This is a weedout class, for sure. Dr. Carpenter has done her best to make sure that year after year freshmen in STEM get introduced to the college experience. Her course is tough, not gonna sugarcoat it. READ. Study in groups. Do lots of problems. She's going to try and trick you, so you gotta think.  102 is even toughertrickier.
If you don't need to take Chem 101 -- don't.
the material is usually close to understandable, but the questions on the test are at a  more difficult and require a higher level applied thinking

If you read the book then the homework and clicker questions are easy. Class isn't actually mandatory but if you don't want to fail it is. Exams are much harder than the practice exams and is a lot of self learning.
Definitely one of the best professors at UMBC. Excellent lecturer

She's a tough prof. Her class is less teaching and more quiz questions based on homework and the reading assignments. This is more about self learning, than anything, however, she offers many outlets to get help and on a personal level she is fun and will help if asked.

Your grade is essentially based on the tests, and the tests make you think. She provides practice exams for all of the tests, but if you study just the practice exams you're not going to pass the test. Chem 101 and 102 are tough classes and you need to put the time in to read and understand the concepts. Not a horrible class and grading is fair.

DO NOT LISTEN TO THE HORRIBLE REVIEWS. Seriously. I was afraid to even take chem bc of what people said & waited a year longer to take it, but she is an AWESOME chem teacher. I never understood chem well, but with her class, I actually enjoy it now! GO TO CLASS & READ. Anyone saying it's "so hard" is not trying hard enough, studying, or reading.

Dr. Carpenter is definitely one of the best professors at UMBC! She is very approachable and does everything she can for her students. Her exams are tough but if you do exactly what she says you will do well in the course. She honestly made me love chemistry and her teaching style is probably the best possible way to learn it!
it's a pretty hard class, but if you pay attention in class the clicker questions are really helpful. Plus she has office hours multiple times a week and online office hours twice a week.

Carpenter is an awesome person. She is funny and loves to tell you Friday features. But, she is incredibly hard. The tests are ridiculously hard. You will need to spend every moment studying for her exams. This course consumes you. Don't be fooled by her nice personality, this instructor gave me hell.

CHEM 102 is a tough course, and you will have to study unless you're a Chemistry wizard. Carpenter is good at explaining things, but more often than not class is just clicker questions. I wish she had lectured more, but she does have office hours and seems to care about her students. I got a B in the course with some studying and an AP background.

Is a ok teacher all around. She is nice enough, but doesn't really explain concepts that well. Her clickers are graded on correctness so attendance is pretty much mandatory. Her tests are extremely difficult and she doesn't post an explanation key for them either, just an answer key so you dont really know why you got a question wrong.

Same rules as CHEM 101 apply. DO NOT FALL BEHIND. 2 or more hours of study each day. Read material & do learnsmart/quiz b4 class. GO TO CLASS. Do practice problems after class. USE THE PRACTICE WORKBOOK. Practice exams are helpful. End of chapter problems not so much. Final is cumulative, not as hard as her exams. Buy the ACS workbook & do it.

Read b4 class. DO learnsmart for class. GO TO CLASS. Do practice problems after class. You'll need all the points you can get. Do ALL learnsmart & quizzes. Exams are hard. Final is cumulative. Buy the practice workbook. It will save your life; do every single page & problem in it. If you can, get exams from previous students. DO NOT FALL BEHIND.

Great proffessor. Does so much to help students learn the material. How many proffessors holds weekly online Office Hours online at 8pm during the week and on sundays in addition to in person Office Hours?Her exam & clicker questions can be tricky, but it's so you understand the material. You get the grade you deserve with her, and there is a curve
Please explain in the class

She expects you to know everything prior to class. Unless you've taken AP with good understanding, you are screwed. 20% of the class failed 101 and more people are failing 102. she is approachable outside of class but she does not teach. you have to do a lot of self teaching.

Read the book, do the hw, don't skip class and do the end of chapter problems. The class is easy if you simply focus and put forth time and effort. 102 has more math, but I preferred it because by doing a bunch of end of chapter problems her exams don't seem bad at all. You can get an A if you make this class a priority. Plus, she's very helpful!

Take advantage of her virtual office hours! Meet with her one on one and she will tell you exactly what you need to do to do well. I failed exams but after I met with her one on one, I got A's. She's VERY approachable! Her clicker questions are great preparation for her exams. She really does want her students to pass. Best professor ever!

had her for chem 101 and i barely passed that (solid 65%. now for chem102...good god. first exam i got a 45% on. i studied daily (3-4hrs a day) for a month before that exam. she doesnt teach. she just uses the clicker the whole time and expects you to know the section in a day. practice exams are easy but the actual exam is 6x that difficulty.

She is the worst professor ever. I felt like no matter how hard I studied I never got higher than a D on her exams. She expects you to know everything and looks at you like you are dumb if you ask a chem 101 related question! DO NOT TAKE.

Horrible prof. She expects you to know everything before class so that she can hack your brain to bits with clicker questions.  If you think the clicker questions are bad, wait until the exams.  She gets angry really easily and doesn't lecture.  Sometimes she brings her darling children to class and spends the whole time telling them to shut up.

Don't take this class with Carpenter unless you have taken AP Chemistry or have a lot knowledge about Chem already. I walked in not having taken Chem for about 4 years and I had a bad time. Jeez, what an awful professor.  Nothing but clicker question after clicker question. Good luck if you take it with her.

Carpenter was a great professor. Whoever tried hard would easily get an A. She is very clear with EVERYTHING and is very willing to help.  Her office hours in person and online were dedicated to students. She is so accommodating and obviously cares about her students. She is fair and so were her exams. Nothing on the exam wasn't covered in class.

genuinely concerned about students, clears up small details in basics of chem, establishes the reasons behind steps of problems, distinguishes diff between similar words, clear in what she expects, extends office hours, very responsive to emails...only explaining when majority wrong = EFFECTIVE use of time..strugglers should've gone to office hours

I wouldn't consider her an "easy" teacher. She expects you to do a lot of work on your own, but you leave with a well-rounded knowledge of the subject. She is approachable and is willing to help if needed. She actually made me interested in chemistry enough to change my major. You actually have to try in this class, so be prepared.
Extremely challenging exams.  Probably my least favorite professor but unfortunately the only one for chem 101 and 102.

AWful teacher, spent almost no time teaching the subject and clarifying the things that needed to be clarified and just threw clicker questions at us, rarely explaining the answers to them. Only good thing about her is she gives lots of extra credit, but it doesn't help much

She's not a mean professor if you talk to her. In lecture, which is only short, she tends to run past topics spends time doing clicker problems. With that said, it is important to come to class prepared. Do the end-of-chapter problems! They are the best tool for the quizzes (some are directly used) and help with Exams.
She was nice, but when it came to helping during clicker questions, if you are apart of the minority that got the question wrong, you are completely out of luck, and will be left behind.
Dr. Carpenter is a horrible teacher. She is a nice person but don't expect her to ACTUALLY teach unless majority students get a clicker question wrong. Her exams are pretty hard and confusing.

The class overall is a mix between easy and bad. Unless you read the textbook, constantly go over practice problems and attend the office hours then you will have a hard time passing the class. I received a C in the class but I feel as if I could have doe better overall.

Try to get past exams from older students. She is helpful as long as you approach first and ask, but don't expect help to be given. I took AP chemistry in high school, so it wasn't as hard as I thought it would be, but I saw my friends fail. There is a really slight curve (max 3%). Don't count on it. Study for your tests and don't miss class.

In order to do well in this class, you have to put in effort. Read the textbook, go to office hours, review clicker questions, and do practice problems. The first two exams are HARD. Don't be disappointed if you fail - there is often a slight curve in grades at the end of the semester.

I never took AP Chem, so the class was different than high school honors Chem. I got a B, without really putting my all. But if you try your best and stay on top of things, then it is very likely you will get an A. I failed 2 exams but managed to get a low B.

Dr. Carpenter gets a lot of flak from people in her class who come thinking it is going to be easy and who refuse to work when they find out otherwise. She is very good teacher. She is thorough in lectures, she is committed to her student's success, and she just enjoys the subject. Chem 101/102 are weed out classes, so be prepared. This is college.
She gets your hopes up and then crushes them.  Don't get too excited when you see your exams.

She's an awesome person, but not the best teacher. She doesn't really lecture. She'll go over a few key points and do a few examples, then dedicate the rest of class to clicker q's. She only goes over a q only if a majority get's it wrong. Be prepared to read and take good notes, b/c you're basically teaching yourself. Tests are difficult too.

Dr. Carpenter is the classic intro level college professor; one that weeds out all the people who aren't interested in science. Personally, I felt like her policies were very overbearing and lecture was not very helpful, especially for 102. DO NOT TAKE HER CHEM 101/102 UNLESS YOU HAVE TO.

Her tests arent that hard, but she expects so much and teaches so little. If you are good at chemistry and can work on you own, you will do fine. If you struggle at the concepts that are intuitive to most people, then it will be harder since thats what she doesnt teach. I went to her office hours once and she yelled at me instead of helping me.

FYI, Huge Steelers Fan ! Her office door says Steelers Fans welcome ! Great teacher and a nice person.

Dr. Carpenter is generally useless as a teacher. She is the worst professor I have ever had. She doesn't teach at all, she just puts up practice problems in class for you to do. You have to teach yourself all the material to do well in this class. There are 4 exams with a FR section. The exams are fairly hard as well.

Hard class, great professor

Great teacher, but her exams are  difficult. If you put a lot of effort in this class and follow her guidelines she gives in the beginning of the semester you should be able to get an A.

Carp is the best. I enjoyed her sass/sarcasm all semester and will miss it. Follow her schedule, read BEFORE class and at least do the section review problems. One sentence: Carps is the best! If you follow her proven and tested guideline of reading before each class you'll rock CHEM 102 like a sire. Just like for CHEM 101, Dr. Carpenter is a good teacher.  However, the material in this course is harder than CHEM 101 so you have to put more time and effort into the class to get the A.

Dr. Carpenter is a really good teacher.  She does expect that you read the material prior to class but then expands on the topic in class.  Her tests are somewhat challenging, but if you put the work in and go to class it's definitely possible to get an A.
basically you are teaching yourself in this class by reading the book, lectures are helpful sometimes, and the last test and final are impossibly hard

I wish I knew how hard of a professor she is before taking the course, first course at UMBC and I would have read the entire textbook in the summer if I know how hard she was. She is a very sophisticated and smart professor.. however she should not be teaching at a college. she should be more of a  researcher than a teacher. very hard to follow her and one of worst teacher i had.

Dr. Carpenter is a brilliant lecturer. Problem: she doesn't lecture enough. Class mostly consisted of us just doing clicker questions. As I had only taken high school GT Chemistry before this class, I had to work very hard in this class. She is enthusiastic about teaching and wants students who are enthusiastic about learning. I skipped a bunch of classes and did fine with my soph HS chem knowledge. She is smart but did not take time in class to teach. If they were to fire her and just have us read out of the book I would have learned exactly the same as her being there. Very good at teaching. She really knows her stuff and cares about the success of her students. She is very tough but if you put in the work it is possible to do well. Definitely different from high school chemistry (depending on where you went of course). It was a wake-up for me. Everything is very fast-paced. Fantastic teach she sweats you but completely worth it

She's hard. But such a good professor with a real desire for you to learn. Expect to study and work hard and you will excel. She is totally fair and reasonable. I really like her class.

She is amazing

SOOOOOOOOOOOO HARD. Not too much work. Ok at teaching.

Dr. Carpenter is a very good professor with a great sense of humor.  Her lectures can get boring at times since she is reading straight from the power point slides, but they are worth going to. DO THE HOMEWORK PROBLEMS and read from your text book before class and you will be fine.

Awesome teacher in every way. She's funny and knowledgeable about all concepts we cover in 101. I got a 100% on wiley plus, its a free 10% of your grade. Also her exams were very easy if you can get over the fact that she tries to trick you in every problem. Oh, forgot to mention she's hott!

she aight, it all comes down to you and what you put into the class. She curves well, and willing to help if you go to her office hours. she is an awesome teacher! I had her for chem 101 and chem 102 and she was extremely helpful, if u asked! slide shows are very helpful and do the practice problems from the book!

she is good but sometimes she words the questions weird.
tries to be cute..unsuccessful. seems nice but when speaking to her one on one is very rude and mean. has tricky tests. discussions are the longest two hours of your life

very hard! Must study hard to pass class.

everything comes from the problem sets, pay attention because she is a tricky lady (VERY TRICKY), the second exam is the hardest

Truly abysmal as a teacher, doesn't know how to teach. Lecture slides are most vague, have stupid things written on them-page "257" title. She tries to cover alot but does a half assed job of it by going extremely fast and not emphasising KEY details.  Nobody understands anything, nobody raises their hands or participates in class LOL!)

She is a great professor, but a horrible teacher.  Don't expect to actually be able to understand the information from lectures (which are straight from the book). Examples are helpful, discussion is not! Use her office hours...she'll be more apt to curve your grade up if she knows your face. 2 things to expect: low exam grades, big curve.

People underrate her entirely. Excellent professor. Has printed slides so easy to follow lecture. To ensure a good grade do the recommended problems! The practice exams can also be very helpful! Showing up to class is not useless, since she does give out exam hints and so forth. So definately get her as your professor!

Ok... all I'm gonna say is...CHANGE THE DISCUSSION GRADING SYSTEM! It does NOT work and it is flat out stupid. The TAs are worthless and don't know what they're doing. As for the lectures, you're better off skipping them and just reading the sections in the textbook. The lecture actually lowers your IQ for the exam. That's why everyone fails.
there are alot of tiles in the lecture hall she teaches

3rd class chemist. jabs all day (and nobody wants to participates). only good thing = doesn't make you memorize the table. don't attend lectures & lecture slides. exams = extremely difficult & from the book. Don’t attend lecture, don’t read the slides. just read the book, then you won’t massacred like the masses who study lectures and get 45’s
fun class, great teacher!!!! Cares about her students.
Professor Carpenter is very helpful, the class is fairly easy.

Not approachable.Will not answer questions she considers "last week questions."Bad online quizzes, there have been instances when the whole class had to take a quiz again.Yes, 350+ plus people.She put up a review-exam up online, and many answers in the answer key were wrong! Brutal exams containing undisclosed and untaught questions. Avoid her...
Low class averages on tests, but the curve will save you at the end.  Just study your butt off for those tests.  She is a very good teacher, especially considering the enormous size of the class.

Chipper, nice pretty cool until test time. rediculous exams and the class depends on them but there is also a rediculous curve, i got a c with a 42 on the final and 45 average on exams, every class is different though, having a baby now so wont be back for a while who knows how she'll change  powerpoints to the max hard class but often mandatory

Hard class, but if you go to class and study, you should be fine.  Class averages tend to be in the 50s, so even though you might have lower scores than you're used to, you'll probabaly get an A.  Carpenter's demos are pretty good-they all involve fire.

Dr.Carpenter is very nice, her exans is really hard and need to study so hrad but it is not impossible. She would be more helpful if the semester was longer. I think the big problem is short time. THe subject is easy if every one read the book.
No Comments

If you have never taken chemistry before, you might be in trouble. This class is not hard if you keep up, it requires a lot of work. I got an A, but you must go to class, read BEFORE you go to class, do the homework and do the chapter studyguides on e-grade. She is a great teacher, but the test are tricky but this is how the MCAT will be, not easy.

shes always well-prepared and very knowledgable in chem. shes funny and likes telling stories to give everyone a break from the notes. her tests are very difficult and you need to be very prepared for them. we like her

Carpenter is a great person, but not a great professor. She honestly does try to teach the material and make it clear, but her lectures are often so basic that the test comes along and takes you by surprise. i feel that her lectures do nothing to prepare you for the exams. to succeed, be sure to print her lecture slides and to study for the exams o

Dr. Carpenter is very nice and you will learn a lot if you pay attention to lectures and do the practice problems. Tests are difficult and you need to study and work hard. She's not the teacher for you if you don't like reading from lecture slides. But she's pretty good.

I think she is a good professor but she needs to make her exams just as she teaches. Her exams are bit more difficult than the way she teaches and the sample questions that she gives us to look over. I don't like that aspect. However, she's very clear, answers questions when asked, and knows what she is doing.

The class starts out very easy but dont be lulled into a false sense of security. exam 2 is very difficult so study very hard or dont study at all because she drops one exam grade. the quizzes are online and hence open book but they are not easy so use your book and your friends. attend the lectures: u will learn alot. shez not very bad once u get

She isn't quite as bad as she seems.  Her slides are a good outline, but you need to read the book as well.  The exams are very difficult and she doesnt prepare you very well for them.  Overall, she is a decent teacher but the subject is a hard one.
her slides doenst help, hard exam..read the textbook instead of attending lectures.
It is meant to be a weeder course... She taught the calculations fairly well, but most of her theory, especially the questions, was worded very poorly.

very hard exams...not at all comformatble in answering questions...tries to avoid answering questions and says "we will cover in the next lecture...hold on to your thought" ..very unconformatble with her knowlwedege  of chemistry...doesnt want to answer questions...doesnt go over any major problems...unless the day before the exams....avoid if u ca

Since I did well on the first exam, I don't really have any complaints.  I normally hold conversations with her about the Pittsburgh Steelers doing mediocre this year before and after the lectures.  The class does require a lot of work.  Do the homework problems!  And don't fall behind either!
No Comments
Do the homework, go to the lectures, print out the slides, study, take the easy online quizes and you'll do fine.

HORRIBLE! Ever had a flu and been vomiting? It was a better experience than going to class. Got nothing out of class; read the book and still did horrible on tests which were very difficult. Quizzes were easy.
Straight forward in class, but everything else goes to shambles.  Maybe Math 151 should be the required class before Chem 101.  but she is nice and the slides don't help.
No Comments
She is really nice

Bad, bad teacher, who has a serious communication problem. She spends the class reading slides, and the slides are taken from the textbook. YOU WILL ONLY PASS THIS CLASS IF YOU PAY FULL ATTENTION TO THE HOMEWORK. Ignore what she says, do the homework and understand it. Self-teach-class all the way. The TA (Marple) basically taught me everything.

in my opinion she was fine-chem 101 is meant to be tough. her explanations of concepts weren't always so clear, but she encouraged questions-plus she makes herself pretty available for questions out of class. her exams are really tough and she puts in a lot of very involved calculations for the exam time. she's not trying to fail you.

Let's face it- Chem 101 is a tough course from any teacher. Dr. Carpenter is just as good a teacher as any. She would re-explain things when asked. Some of her test questions are a bit unclear- read them carefully. My advice: complete and understand the homework probs and use the solutions manual and you will be ok.

Funny...I got an A in this class. Tutoring and curving saved me. This class weeds people out! Don't rely on lectures; DO THE HOMEWORK. The answer guide: practically essential for passing. And Carpenter? I once said hello directly to her, and she ignored me in total disrespect. Don't fall for her false kindness; skepticism will save your grade!
the class was really tough and she had talked about a curve which never happened.

Bad bad teacher. Start teaching yourself everything at the beginning of the class and don't slack off. Also, her slides are worlthless. Forget about asking for help during class, she'll just make up an excuse about posting the problem on blackboard. Horrible class.

This class is the hardest class I have had and it is not even an upper level course! She thinks she is helping with the group work but the problems on the test are different. I hope I pass but if not I wont be taking it with her again.

Lectures sometimes seemed unprepared - the exams are incredibly difficult - the class had a 50% average on the second one.  The middle third of the semester seemed to be the hardest - I don't know if this was her fault or not.
Straight forward class, difficult assesments.  If you test well you should be alright.  Pay attention, and actually go to lecture.  Nice to look at atleast

She is very enthusiastic about the subject and tries to relay her excitment to us, but it doesn't work.  Her lectures are boring and not very helpful. I think she's good at the subject but not at teaching it.  Homework gets you through the quizes but tests are unreasonably hard.
very good and informative

The only, ONLY way to survive this class is to TEACH YOURSELF. Forget about the slides. Forget about coming to this class, actually, it'll just confuse you and put you to sleep. She's too new to know how to teach and you'll fail if you rely on her. Curves = yes. Get the book and sit down with it.

Dr.Carpenter is a nice person, and she is always ready to help you, but infortunately she does not know how to teach. Her lectures are very confusing and boring and they are straight from the book. I managed to get a B, but i put way too much effort on it. BOTTOM LINE DON"T TAKE WITH HER.

Horrid teacher. I hope you've taken this class before, cause if you haven't, i suggest studying for three weeks prior to the exam. i'm completely relying on ap chem and teaching myself. write fast, she speeds thru slides. quizzes in discussion every week, even on the week of an exam. She can't teach

Toughest class I ever took. Lectures are pretty boring, straight out of the book. Tests are darn near impossible...curve was a 50% to get a C. That's an awful lot of curve, but a lot of people would have failed without it.

She is new and does pretty good for a new professor. Its so much easier to skip lectures and teach urself everything from the text but she kinda helps... *kinda* Grades are curved alot ...but also cuz they needa be, the exams are very hard ..class averages are never above a 60. def. a weed out cours

Dr. Carpenter tries really hard to teach and genuinely wants everyone to do well (she curves the grades so much that you can get an A with 80% in the class). Dr. carperter tries but fails miserably in her attempt to teach.  She attempts to be funny, but it all ends up in a disappointment.  Her powerpoint slider finger can outshoot Eastwood, and her tests totally ruins student's life.  As a teacher, i give her props 4 trying, but please don't try!

This professor tries to help, but alas, she fails horribly as a new teacher.  I'ld like to give her another chance, but fraknly i don't think the result would be any different.  Her lack of clarification show on the subject is her worse flaw, next to her speedy powerpoint flipping finger and more.

She tried very hard to make sure people understood. She curved grades ridiculously so people could pass with a C (60-76=C)and people should be glad they had her instead of some other porfessors who would have just let them fail. She made a difficult subject manageable but u still have to study hard
She's just out to get people!
she trys reall hard to teach but lectures are a waste. exams are ridicously hard.. to the point of impossible. she is a really nice person who trys to help but it usally doesnt work
She really cares about teaching and making sure you know what you're doing. Not that bad of a class, considering how tough chemistry is here. I totally recommend her.

If you don't read the book, go to class.  She just puts up slides that are pictures from the book.  And if you expect to see how the math problems are done,  you better not blink, she goes over them very quickly.

Ahahahahahah!!!!  Carpenter..  Professor..  Hahaha..  sorry.. that's just funny to me.

a difficult class that all science-related majors must take. i won't lie that carpenter TRIED HARD to teach us, well, but didn't work. eventually, stopped going to her class because her lectures only made me more confused about the subject. if possible, try to avoid carpenter AND lacourse.

Not helpful at all, lectures are pointless.  I'm doing well in the class only because I took AP Chem last year and am retaking this class just to get a better background.  I learn more from just reading the book than anything I learned in lectures which is not much

I tally agreed the last comment.She is not helpful at all.She likes to shows up in the middle of the class discussion and says that we have to build up the class average.I guess that she doesnot want to be looked so bad as a professor.The way that she teaches does not seem to be professional.

her lectures are really annoying, i like to show up late and sit in the front row.  over half the class fails each exam.  She is a first year teacher so i guess we should cut her some slack. she loves to show up in the middle of discussion sessions and exams just to tell you how bad u r doing
She tries to be fun, but she could not. She is not a good chem professor. She can't teach, because her lecture doesn't help you to understand; it's all from the book.

I want to start off by saying this is a HARD course.  She is NOT a bad instructor.  She is NOT an easy instructor, this class is supposed to be difficult.  I would recommend taking with her because she WANTS to teach, and is there for the students--NOT for the research; she expects you to succeed.

I've never enjoyed a class more! I learned so many valuable skills and the discussions were absolutely the best part of this class. Dr. Kate is super understanding and supportive and genuinely wants to help you succeed. Your participation matters more than anything else so if you're passionate about social issues then this is the class for you!

I had her for the Humanities Scholar class. If you're an incoming freshman planning on joining the scholars program, you will LOVE Dr. Kate! She is so genuine, down to earth, and hands down the best professor I had this semester. Graded work is mostly response papers to articles that we read for the week, which were all (imo) so so interesting!
Dr. Kate is a phenomenal teacher! She is well read and respected. She is flexible with deadlines as long as you communicate with her. Lots of reading.
I freaking love Dr.Drabinski... my goat

Literally one of the most inspirational and kind people I've ever met. Dr. Kate takes such an incredibly personal interest in every student, and will do anything to help you succeed regardless of your situation. Classes were so fun and I learned so much from discussions. I absolutely adore Dr. Kate!

If you don't take this professor you are making a mistake!!! If you read the class description for GWST 200 and find it interesting YOU WILL LOVE THIS COURSE. Dr. Kate made my semester amazing and she made me excited to come to class. Coursework is very manageable and you get to do a fun project about an activism topic you care about.

Dr. Kate is an amazing professor who creates a welcoming environment in the classroom. She's very accessible outside of class and understand that we are human (and is therefore flexible w/ deadlines, within reason). This was not the first time I've taken one of her courses and it definitely will not be the last. I could not recommend her more.

Dr. Kate honestly cares about all her students. She wants to hear your opinions and is flexible with extensions and making sure people are getting the grades they want. She's a super easy A and she's the sweetest.

Dr. Kate is amazing, she is extremely knowledgeable on the topics of gender and sexuality studies and is able to explain the topics very well. The class is reading heavy but there are no tests or quizzes, and instead is mostly discussion based. Dr. Kate is also very understanding of absences and late work, and very supportive of her students.

Dr. Kate is a wonderful professor!! She really gets to know all students on a more personal level and facilitates really interesting discussions during class that keep everyone engaged. 

This course was very much a reading + discussion based class. Be prepared to do lots of reading!
My favorite professor on campus. This class you learn so much just by showing up. Light workload and she will give you extensions when needed. She is just so funny and caring.

Dr. Kate is amazing!! This was my highest level class, but literally my easiest. There's a few difficult readings, but going over it in class made it a lot easier to understand. Discussions in class were very interesting and easy to participate in! Dr. Kate is very funny but also approaches everything in a very respectful way. Great professor!!

Amazing professor!!! Would 100% take this class again. Had one short paper due at the start of the week and blog posts/comments twice a month. Really worth it for an upper level course and learned a lot.

Last fall, I enrolled in her GWST220 course and absolutely loved all of her lectures; she made things approachable and had you consider diverse LGBTQ+ views. She has a weekly discussion for the articles you read, and she makes them manageable; she even gives extra credit, extensions on unit papers, and no tests. NL

Convinced Dr. Kate is the best professor ever. There's a reason she has these reviews and everyone is saying they would take her again--she is passionate, smart, funny, engaging, and above all truly cares about and makes an effort to show that she understands her students' needs and concerns. Her love for the subject matter shines through. :)

Dr. Kate is one of the kindest Professors you will find. Is happy to give extensions on course work, course work is quite minimal, and you get out of the class what you put into it. There is no mandatory attendance, and the class is discussion based, so its lots of students sharing thoughts on assigned readings. Blog posts are cool, and easy final.

Dr. Kate is my favorite professor at UMBC. She's knowledgeable, an effective teacher, and flexible when it comes to deadlines. Her lectures are some of the most thought provoking I have ever attended. I find myself looking forward to classes with her because I know they will always be interested.

She is amazing!! Took her class Fall 2020 and I learned so many new, interesting things. Just need to show that you did the reading and understood the material in the weekly one page response papers. There were three exams and you have two weeks to write them.

I took GWST210 over the winter so my experience may be a little different than most, but Dr. Kate was extremely understanding and easy to get along with. The material covered was easy to understand and she was very clear with her expectations. Mostly graded on unit papers but very easy to complete if youve been paying attention
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Kate is such a great professor. Her obvious care for each of her students comes through in her teaching, and she will genuinely try to form a personal relationship with you, which I appreciated. Realizes that life happens outside of class, and only concrete HW is readings and a page of response on them, besides a few project updates.

Dr Kate is the BEST prof I ever taken at UMBC. She is very understanding of student issues, and is willing to help. Her class is engaging, and teaches important concepts. If you go to class and participate/take notes, you will get an A. She wants everyone to pass.

This is one of the most eye-opening classes I've take in college so far. Dr. Kate is hilarious and very passionate about the subject. She's also extremely understanding when it comes to things like absences and deadline extensions. You're mostly graded on unit essays, which are largely dependent on the readings you do throughout the semester.

Dr. Kate is an amazing professor! Her classes are very relaxed and she makes the content very interesting. She is super understanding of students lives and makes sure everyone is on track for success. There are only about 4 papers and a group project but with the notes from class and the readings, they are easy A's as long as you take notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I was new to UMBC (transfer) and felt so at home in her class that I changed my major to GWST (she's also my advisor now because of it!) The most caring professor I've ever encountered. I can't wait to take her more now due to my major switch! (There is no assigned textbook for this class but there IS readings which I really recommend reading)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: This is an excellent course to take and an incredible professor. Dr. Kate is hilarious, teaches with enthusiasm and really grabs your attention in class. While attendance wasn't graded, it is recommended to do well on exams. Be prepared to read a lot, too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Kate is a very caring professor and is generous with due dates and extra credit opportunities, she wants you to get an A if you come to class! There are many readings throughout this course but she has a discussion on them in class (so you don't really have to read all of them). The course material is also very interesting, but be open-minded!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Gives good feedback--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Kate is absolutely amazing!!! She is caring, genuine, and so so funny!  There are few assignments and not too much reading is required. But when there is a reading assignment, just do it.  (She sees it as a bit disrespectful if you don't.)  She also presents two group projects.  Super great class and amazing lectures! Plus, no exams! Yay!!

Great professor! Hilarious, caring, and understanding. The readings are cool but if you don't do them you'll be fine, as she explains them at the beginning of class. Really interesting subject material and expect fun, discussion based lecture classes. One group project but it's not too difficult. Would love to take another class with her.
My favorite professor always and forever.  Dr. Kate is knowledgeable, hilarious, and makes every lecture interesting.

Dr. Kate's class is so interesting. Attendance is not really mandatory but the content is so interesting and the lectures are important, especially if you slack on the readings. Participation is easy and helps you get a good grade. Three easy online "exams" and one group project but if you keep an open mind and discuss in class, you'll be okay.

I think this in-person class is one of the best ways to learn ASL!! You'll catch on quick and start having conversations with your peers early on. There's a good bit of homework, but it's manageable. However, there's lots of technical stuff you can get points off on, and you'll probably have to redo a lot of assignments. Classes are fun though!
Professor frame is a good asl professor. As long as you attend the classes, do the assignments and turn them in on time you'll do good in the class!

Professor Frame is awesome! He is hilarious and a great teacher. He is patient if you don't know what you're trying to sign.  There is a LOT of work if you take the hybrid 201, but you don't have to come to class (however I highly suggest you do, there are fun games and it's really good practice).

Very blunt and responds late to emails, class materials are extremely disorganized, no clear feedback nor clear directions. The instructional lessons and homeworks take more time than all of my STEM classes combined. He also made us redo all of our homeworks one week because of a mistake on his behalf. Do not take the hybrid version of this class!

Daniel may be the greatest Deaf ASL teacher that UMBC has ever had. He created a brilliant online platform that makes life easier for students who don't have to attend ASL 201 class, as attendance is not mandatory. Students who attend all the classes will receive a 5% bonus. I have always attended his class, and there are a lot of fun activities!

Professor Frame is a wonderful ASL professor!! I highly suggest that you take his class for ASL if you're considering learning sign language. WARNING  he does sign a little fast sometimes, but he repeats what he is signing if you ask him.  Professor frame is funny as well!

He really cares about teaching, is very friendly, and is absolutely hilarious. Once we could hardly focus because we were laughing so hard. He teaches in a way that shows that he wants us to understand, and is always willing to explain for students who are confused. He has a dynamic and energetic teaching style and encourages student participation.

Very funny guy, he uses a lot of humor in his lessons and his in person classes. Class is asynchronous with one optional lecture once a week. Class is EXTREMELY TIME CONSUMING, you will spend hours on doing the instructional lessons and homework assignments, prob more than you will for a lot of stem classes
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Frame was excellent! He really engages with students and is so passionate about teaching ASL. Going to class is extremely important (he excuses one absence then takes 5% off the overall grade each one after that). He is one of the best and funniest professors, makes coming to class fun. Kind of a tough grader but instruction is very clear
He didn't grade my final grade properly, forces you to buy over $130 worth of textbook materials that you can't find anywhere else. Not lenient whatsoever.

If you can keep up with his signs early on, this class is a breeze. He's very funny and spends a good amount of time visually acting out terms to the class to help you remember different words. The online homework is really easy too. You must come to class though or you will fall behind.

You pretty much get what you put into this class. If you try and stay on top of your work, you can easily get through the class with an A or B. The mistake I kept making was not checking the rubric. If you follow it exactly, you're almost guarenteed an A. He is a very kind and nice teacher but will not let you get away with being lazy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Loved this class so much, I HIGHLY recommend this professor. He is super funny and engaging. Very light work outside of class. Learned so much from him and truly enjoyed it!
Professor Frame is an amazing teacher. Expection are clear and what is taught is what is tested on. He made learning ASL feel less intimidating.

I took span102 with her in the winter semester, its an alright class, it sets you up for 201 really well however you do find yourself cramming as much as you can in the few weeks, the group projects were easy and the homework was just busy work, overall it was an alright class

Dr. Rodriguez makes learning Spanish easy. Works very well with students. As long as you participate and show you are trying, you will have no problem with this class. Unlike other Spanish professors that make it a weed out class, she keeps the hw and projects simple.

Prof Rodriguez one of the most understanding professors out there. While it says there are two lectures per week, its actually one lecture and the second is an asynchronous recording due on Sunday. There is work due every week, but its pretty easy. Very understanding when it comes to late work, just don't make it a habit.

Prof Rodriguez is an amazing gal! She takes a while to get to emails, but other than the lack of good communication, the class and work is very easy, especially being online. I took this to help prepare me for SPAN201, so hopefully I pass that class next semester!

If you are taking Span 101, TAKE HER. She is the best teacher ever. She understands students' lives. Her exams are really easy. Joining class is mandatory, however, if you submit the activity without joining she still would mark you present. Her grading is easy and convenient. Her papers are also very easy if you put a little effort. great teacher.

Shes a really good teacher. I felt like I understood the language because of the pace she taught it at. Has a very good and involved teaching style as well. I feel like she was very understanding of my struggles with my disabilities and for that I really appreciate her. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I came into Spanish this semester soooo bad at spanish, I thought I'd never be able to pass or learn a language, It's very hard for someone like me who sucks at foreign languages, but she makes the class easy to understand, it takes a few weeks I think to really get the basics.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Schultz is honestly a really cool professor and the class is enjoyable. Get ready to read multiple things a week for this class, submit like 2-3 documents and some discussion boards. The content is really interesting in the readings and lectures and there is a TON of extra credit. 4 exams + a final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very time consuming--all the course content is in the readings given for the 50something assignments given throughout the week. However, the content is quite interesting. Exams were closed note and a little difficult, but graded on a curve. Videos shown in class are often on the exams. Would take again.

A lot of hmwk assignments answering questions after reading/watching various mediums. Books & a lot of studies/videos are old. Small group exercises; no presentations, papers, research assignments. Exams are based on learning objectives. Attend class before & after the exams & take notes! Prof is light-hearted, funny, good guy. Good 4 SW/PSYC peeps

Dr. Schultz is my MAN. not only did he make this class super fun & interesting, but he is very kind & always available to help you via email. We had worksheets due (tue/fri) by 8 pm for completion. Don't wait until the last second b/c some worksheets can be long, but they're helpful for studying for the exam. I've enjoyed this class so much. 100/10

With the online structure, we had a once a week class, and then we had work due every Thursday, Saturday, and Monday at 8pm. Having it due at 8pm was rough because it's rather "early", but the work wasn't necessarily hard. It was a lot of homework, BUT the homework was very helpful and we could study all the homeworkswe did for a unit for exams.

It was disappointing since I had heard great things about this professor but after switching the class online, the exams changed. There's not a lot of workload in the class overall but he seems to be nitpicky on exam responses after going from multiple choices to free responses.

Lots of worksheets but based off of completion and answer keys posted after the due date. You make your own study guide by doing the worksheets. Overall great professor! Exams are not bad at all as long as you at least review worksheet material
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Lectures were interesting, but attendance isn't mandatory if you don't feel like going. The only thing is that example questions from class would show up on exams. Exams were very easy if you memorize all the wksts and he gives a generous curve along with extra credit for the class. He does give a lot of worksheets for homework, though.

Overall great teacher. Material is interesting and the worksheets are graded mainly on completion. He also cares a lot about students and encourages discussion. My one qualm is that the exams could have very specific questions based off lectures, so take very thorough notes and go to every lecture or else you won't do well on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher!! For is class Child Development, There's a lot of online work you have to do, it's not hard just very time consuming. there are 4 exams in the semester plus the final. The tests are easy if you show up to class and take notes and if you study the worksheets from the videos. He also provides practice quizzes for the exams. No paper

reviews.comment: His assignments are due at 8 pm like why. I hated this class it was so stressful.

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. For a 200 level course it is extremely hard. He assigns multiple online worksheets (with 50 questions) worth only 1 point.
