reviews.comment: The homework assignments ARE the exams. Studied for exams an hour or 2 before it the entire semester and am finishing with an A. Interesting class, but everything you learn is really from the homework reading and videos, not so much Professor Schultz. Many chances for easy extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is a pretty good professor and the class offers a lot of discussions. Gives study guides for exams and everything just needs to be memorized. Lots of worksheets needed to be done and sometimes can be time-consuming. Not a hard class but be sure to do the discussion board and you can get extra credit. Also a cute/goofy professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class is a hybrid course, so all of the work is done online. Coming to class ins't necessary. There is absolutely no way you can fail this class if you do the homework. The exam is literally questions pulled from the homework and video worksheets. He also gives us a study guide of EXACTLY what is going to be on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Schultz is a great guy and a great professor. I had him for a winter course so there was a lot of required work that needed to be done in a short time frame, however, with some planning it was manageable. The tests are based on both the readings and what ever he focuses on in class will be what is emphasized on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Had him for winter class. But he was a good teacher but gave so much work that most of us couldnt even finish it. So much reading and bought a book and read three chapters in it. His test are based off readings and what he says in class so you have to attend. I wouldnt take him again honestly, but gave extra credit but it was only worth one point
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He comes off at times as frazzled. There are things on the test that were not in the million and ten worksheets. This class was all taught via the worksheets and very little was said in lecture. When reviewing after the test the entire class had to prove that we hadn't covered the material for him to consider making it extra credit. take @ own risk

Took this class over the summer. Worksheets are graded for completion and gives us the information through his lectures so don't miss class. He makes his lectures fun and loves what he teaches. Easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Schultz is very friendly. The exams are fair; you  basically make your own study guide by doing hw. Enjoyed the class
Very good professor and interesting topics. I loved this class. Getting A is not hard at all

Class was easy enough until you get to the tests. Tests are unbelievably picky. Many questions tested whether you could remember the smallest detail, for example the year of a court course. He is a nice enough professor but his tests are impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Gives exact details about information found on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This course was a hybrid so get ready to answer a bunch of question sheets that include thousands of questions about the chapter or videos. Going to class was basically pointless and you learn nothing new. Basically you learn all of the content online.

This class is all book work 48 -65 q's with videos. You can't do other class work bc of his class. Only takes questions of those students  that are right in front. He will circumvent a question or out right ignore it if he feels its not worth answering. Neither the prof. or the teachers aid Lisa will answer course content questions. DON'T TAKE!!!!

Get ready to read.  I have studied hard for his tests but you have to make sure you read everything in those chapters because some of the answers from the book are apparently wrong.  He can also be hard to understand at times and jumps from one subject to another. He is all over the place.  Not good at going over the questions in the worksheets.

Really great teacher. Had him for 200 and 342 and he was great with both. Very passionate about the classes and makes sure everyone understands everything. Tests are just what he says and he is very understanding. Worth taking his class!

I took this class over the summer, once a week for 6 weeks. It was fun, lecture can be kind of boring. Textbook was easy to read. Alt of videos to watch at home but the worksheets were easy. Tests were not to bad, but you still need to study for them. I would recommend the class

This section happened to be a hybrid course. It was great only meeting once a week and he makes it very clear what will be on the test and what will not. The lectures required to watch on your own can be somewhat lengthy though.
Easy A, make sure to go to class, and at least skim the readings.

Definitely a good speaker, very interested in class material. There are lots of extra credit opportunities, usually for participating in grad students' psych studies. Online quizzes for every two chapters, open book and you get to retake one exam at the end of the semester. Really generous in those aspects I think, great class!

Dr. Schultz is a good professor.  He expects you to read the book in great detail, no nook or cranny should be missed.  He is incredibly knowledgeable and you can tell his desire to see his students succeed is genuine. He doesn't hold your hand but gives plenty of extra credit chances. Read the book, go to class and study hard; that's how you pass.

He expects you to know what you are talking about in class. You do this by reading the book, taking notes from his lectures, and preparing well for quizzes. He cares, and will consistently ask you for feedback. If you don't do well in his class, it is because you didn't study.

This course was a bit challenging. The exams are hard but you can retake one at the end of the semester. The class was boring, I had a hard time staying awake. It is possible to pass this class, but you have to work for it. Not your typical easy course.

He may be a nice person, but that has nothing to do with class.  You really have to read everything and go to class.  You won't learn anything, except for details you will never need to know for later in life.  There is a GROUP PAPER, that counts for about 25% of your grade, and he picks your groups!  So be smart and take this class with Anderson.

Schultz is the man.  He always helps out his students and is an all around good dude.  I would recommend him to anyone.  Im a engineering major and I still enjoyed the class.  Just read the book and you will be fine.

Definitely one of my favorite professors!  He does his best to keep class interesting, and speaks from experience.  His quizzes check for whether you've read the book rather than testing subject material, but the exams are purely on what you need to know.  He's a totally relaxed guy and does his best to help you without making class stupidly easy.

Professor Schultz is a good professor with a very slight sense of humor.  His lectures are pretty boring at times but they are worth going to because some of the test questions come from them.  Read the book and take the easy points on the reading quizzes.

Dr. Schultz rocks! He's funny and keeps class interesting. Quizzes once a week on chapters but only on the superficial stuff, nothing that would be on the real test. Tests are multiple choice and he drops questions or makes the extra credit if they seem confusing. Take this class for gen. reqs, you wont regret it.
Funny. Very fair and will knock exam questions off as extra credit if they were confusing or if he didn't teach the material well enough.

Dr. Schultz is a pretty good teacher.He is definitly not the easiest, but his quizes are straight out of the book..it's amazing how easy his quizes are.i got a C on every exam because i slept or didn't go to class but read the book, the girl nxt to me got a c without reading the book but going to class. cool guy, played basketball with him too

Prof Schultz is a practicing clinician and his stories are based on his experience, so take him seriously. The class isnt made to be easy,you do have to study. Attend the lectures and keep up on the work and it will do you good in the long run if your a psych major.

Great professor. Very funny and interesting. As long as you go to class, read the chapters, and study you should get an A. Weekly quizzes based on textbook readings; very easy though. Exams not easy, not you will do okay as long as you study.

Somewhat helpful, however, if U R late to class for 10-15 mins on an exam day (and not your fault due to traffic), he will not let you take the test, unless you look dangerously enough so that he thinks u'll kick his ass right there and then. A bit annoying and HE WILL MAKE YOU READ THE ENTIRE BOOK! TRUST ME!  AVOID THIS GUY! Worst teacher I've had

He is a good professor, class is never really boring, he likes to tell jokes when hes waiting for the projector to warm up. He seems to be dedicated to his field. Quizes and exams are easy, and tons of extra credit!! he also, gives you a list of topics and sections in the book that will be covered in the exams. awesome!
watch out for this guy.. he'll make empty threats for no reason whatsoever.
Would reccommend him highly.

So easy to get an A in this class if you read and come to class ready to participate. Group paper that is annoying but oh well. Easy quizzes. Tells us exactly what will be on the exams. Have to read a lot though, but interesting stuff.

whoever said he is a horrible professor has not had dr. provine. schultz is the man! he gives tons of extra credit and is so easy to talk to. he'll keep you interested (usually) and occasionally make jokes or tell funny stories. he's awesome!

Definitely recommend Dr. Schultz. There are quizzes every Monday on the reading but they are easy and if you read it is impossible to fail. The exams are not bad, mostly from the book and a few things from class. One big group paper but if you have a decent group it's not hard. Changes what things are worth to help grades go up. Easy to talk to.

As a physics major taking 14 credits of difficult classes, this class was a great part of my week. Just by reading the chapters and listening in class you can easily get an A. Didn't have to study or take notes at all. Somehow, though, the class tended to average like 25% lower than I did on exams, which is strange.

Nice guy, blah professor. Quiz every Monday on the reading but not actually about Psychology. Exams cover actual knowledge but questions tend to be vague and unclear. They make you assume a lot but he wont explain futher if you ask him. Tends to go off of tangents and stories. Material comes from the text so attendance is pretty pointless.

I thought this calss was beyond easy.  The quizzes are a nothing, i got 100s on all of them and the tests are on a lot of material but they are usually 50 questions for four chapters so its never real in depth questions and he gives a review that tells you wether or not each section of the book will be on the test.  gives occassional in class E.C.

A nice guy, but a HORRIBLE professor. Quizzes are easy, tests not so much but still doable. Attendance is pointless because all the test material comes from the book. Many questions on irrelevant info. Does NOT like to help students. I decided against adding psych as a double major because of this man. Try to avoid.

I feel as though he's a good person but an OK teacher, DO NOT be fooled by the easiness of his quizzes- his tests are WAY harder!! Tells you exactly whats on each test but questions are obscure...I'm in his class now we have one test left and I can honestly say I've read all 15 chapters of the textbook... and his final will cover ALL 15 :(

i did well in all my classes except for this one. the quizes every monday were easy, but they weren't worth anything. the exams are 4 chapters for each and are EXTREMELY hard. the questions are tricky and unclear. the final is on 15 chapters! i approached him for help on my grade and he was no help.

Easy class. Just pay attention for the most part in lectures and read the book. He gives quizzes most Mondays to check if you read, which are easy, they refer to examples. And the tests aren't bad at all if you read the sections before.

HE GIVES OUT QUIZZES WHICH ARE WORTH 10% OF UR GRADE EVERY MONDAY WHICH ARE EASY.  HE GIVES OUT 4 EXAMS THAT ARE HARD AFTER EVERY 4 CHAPTERS YOU COVER.  HE IS NOT LEANENT FOR****!! AND DOES NOT WORK W/ STUDENTS.  NO, I DO NOT RECOMMEND HIM.-CHILD DEV. CLASS

This class is mindlessly easy. If you do badly on a test don't worry, he'll curve it. Unless you do really badly, then you didn't read or study. Just read the book for the quizzes (every Monday) and study the review pages online. I stayed for a full class maybe 7 times the whole semester, didn't listen at all, and got an A.
Great professor! Class is easy if you read the book and pay attention to his powerpoint slides. He's really nice and gives extra credit throughout the semester. I would take him again!
He is great! He makes the class get interactive, and grades fairly.

Was my easiest class this semester-easier than my pass/fail class.  All you have to do is go to class and read the book.  No extra studying required.  Dr. Schultz is really nice, but sometimes can be boring.

super cute and fun to listen to. really loves what hes teaching. quizes easy if you read tests easy if you read and go to class 50% of the time. most comes out of book probably only 5 questions from class. but he makes it a lot of fun!

A wonderful teacher. If you read the text and study for the exams a little bit (he gives you a handout of EVERY section in the textbook and whether or not it will be on the exam) you should do fine. He will discount exam questions if more than 50% of the class gets it wrong. He's fair and passionate about the subject.  Take his class!

I loved Dr. Schultz. The quizzes were definatley easy, if you read the book. The exams were easy, if you read the book and came to class. I just made notecards for everything and pulled at 98% on the final. He is super nice, recommend this guy!

Quizzes every week, read ALL of the text . Read 50% of it grade = 50% read 90% grade=90%. His class is really 2 classes. One is the Lecture where you can discuss the lecture, the other is the text book, which he WONT go over except as a quiz question.You will need to study both for the exams, IMO this should be a 5 credit course not 3, or fire him.
Don't expect an easy 'A'.  weekly quizzes are easy but exams are difficult.  He won't round your 89.9 to an A.  But he is a cutie in that akward professor way.
Really easy quizes, but EXTREMLY hard tests.  Dont take him unless you want to study for hours and be disappointed with your grades.

Probably the worst prof for this class. EVER.  I thought it would be really interesting, and somehow he found a way to make something cool - violence - into a boring developmental account.  He also expected you to know irrelevent details and percentages on exams.  Do NOT take this class unless you take it with Anderson.

He is really nice and he has a great attitude when teaching.  Yes his quizes are easy but, his tests are hard. He does curve the tests a little because of questions know one got right. He really tests a lot on the material in the book. So the class requires a lot of reading.

Very friendly, but his final was absolutely impossible. He expected you to know exact details of certain things, that were not easily recalled. Study hard and do the reading...you'll be fine. If you're not a psych major, don't take him. I was really interested in the class before, and it wasn't anything like I expected.
I thought he was very fair. Weekly quizzes were extremely easy. If you keep up with the readings, go to class, and do the study guide, it should be an A, atleast a B.

Ok, you guys are all wrong.  Schultz is not easy and does not curve, I was very excited about taking his class and I am doing poorly even though I spend hours studying and reading! Questions are obscure. . .be careful when taking Schultz
Easy, just read, he tells you what sections to study for the exams
Not an easy class..if you get a 89.99 you get a B...This guy doesn curve at all and questions are sometimes obscure...Take someone else if you dont want your feelings hurt at the end of the semester.

BEST psych teacher ever!! he is the nicest and teaches very easily.  really easy to understand what he's saying and answers everyone's Q clearly.  weekly easy easy quizzes on chapter readings and 4 exams + final which are pretty easy too.  he lets u know exactly what to study.  TAKE HIS CLASS!
very cool guy. he's helpful and makes the class interesting but its not an easy A. be prepared to read and study but its enjoyable
Dr. Schultz is definitely the coolest prof I've had so far! He hands out what you need to study and he is always using himself as an example. He is the best psych professor ever!!

whoever put that Dr. S is hard must have never attended class or read anything at all. I did the minimum amount of reading and managed A's and B's on all of the tests- If you go to class and just do some reading youll be fine- an awesome guy!

This person who said that this course is hard is wrong... I have a high A with not too much effort. Dr. Schultz curves all tests A LOT just read what he tells you to read.. Dr. Schultz is AWESOME and very nice and helpful.. Plus he's really hot!! Take it!

He's a new teacher,so he might have been easier last sem, this sem hes not. He is a very nice teacher, but hes very hard. Be prepared to study and read ALOT,because his exam questions are not always easy to read, but only some Q's gets dropped.NOT EASY A!
He may be new to UMBC but he's an excellent professor.  Very nice and helpful.  Just wish he taught more classes so I could have him again.
he's such a great teacher (aka Dr. Smily)- take his class, its fun, interesting, and he's willing to help anyone about anything- he makes ME want to be a professor!

I broke my foot before starting his class over the summer and submitted the documents with doctors notes, asked him for accommodations for one singular part of the class that requires you attend an event outside of class and record a video on it, due to my injury i knew i was unable to do so, he told me to just drop the class with no lenience!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Hardest college class I've ever taken. Weekly quizzes felt super hard and required 2+ pages of writing every time. However, if you actually want to learn things in a class, he's the best lecturer I've ever taken. If you take notes in class, you'll get a B even if you don't read much.  If you don't read the final will be awful, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The coursework he gives can be intimidating, but the key to success is to read the lectures he posts and study in advance for the quizzes. He wants to help and is very open to online meetings to sort things out. Basically just don't procrastinate and read a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This guy will fail you after confusing you. He gives in class instructions that is different from what is on the syllabus and goes back and forth with syllabus instructions. He won't tell you what your grade is and he doesn't make the class available on Blackboard. He yells when lecturing and says he's not yelling, just avoid him by all cost.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: he don't tell you this but he wants you to find the similarities and differences between the two readings. idk why he couldn't just tell this straight up. MOST OF UR GRADE IS QUIZZES. don't matter how much effort you put into the irl video project or the discussions. 50% of ur grade is 4 MC quizzes, so a lot of effort in other stuff ain't worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His course schedule is a mess. I had to email & ask when some things were due because they weren't listed in Blackboard or the syllabus. There wasn't a proper calendar. He expects too much of his students - namely, asks them to purchase a printer, to print out ALL of the readings, for your computer to be plugged into ethernet (mine can't do that).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class was filled with extremely long readings every week that were brutal. Very challenging quizzes and tests. If you're filling a GEN Ed requirement I highly recommend avoiding this class.

Simply put, this professor does not teach. Yeah it's an asynchronous class, but he's never accessible, was very rude when I tried to email, lectures are ridden with fixable errors, the readings are unnecessarily long and sometimes weren't really on the topic of culture and politics. They were interesting, yes, but more suited for another class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Even after reading all the readings and doing the discussion posts, I was unable to get beyond a C on the quizzes, bring my grade down substantially.

Prof Dasgupta is one of the most inspirational professors here at UMBC SG. His POLI205 course was super informative, fun & exiting. We were graded by a few assignments, and had weekly podcast listening/google from HW to his "I Hate Politics" podcast which is so interesting to learn about our local politics here at MOCO. He's great take this course!

Classes are about equally challenging at all course levels, can be jarring at the start of the 200 level but on the more manageable side of the course selection at the 300/400 level. The readings can be complicated but will rarely leave you bored, there's a good mix of easy articles as well. Lots of discussions and assignments are very open ended.

Gives you multiple 40 page readings a week & makes you do 5 discussions a week according to the readings & then there is a weekly quiz based on the readings too which barely go with the readings. hell make up his own questions with his own intricate right answers, where there could be 3 possible choices but 1 that is totally correct. Uncooperative

He doesn't teach the class, he sends out a weekly 5-page text document (which frequently had multiple spelling and grammar errors) that serves as the "lecture," and assigns anywhere from 60 to 150 pages of readings every week. I never once even heard his voice as there was no class component. Grade is based on weekly discussion board participation

He is a great person and He REALLLLYYY knows his political science. He is very good but in my perspective I learn best when a proffessor gives us notes through lecture and he mostly just talks and talks about the topic we disscuss. Its kind of hard to keep up becuase he doesnt break it down or writes it down to better understand.

This professor is not the greatest. If you have to take the class don't do it online. Every day I have to write a 600 word summary, participate in the discussion 3 times, read about 100 pages of articles, and answer reading questions. He does not provide lecture videos and just a 3 page document. Additionally, the quizzes are super hard and timed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Incredibly rude and unapproachable. Unhelpful when asking questions and doesn't take the time to understand what you're asking about. Don't become a professor if you don't want to teach - its that simple. He's impatient and expects an unrealistic amount of work from students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dasgupta is not a good professor. His weekly reading requirements consist of very long, dense academic studies that are of little value. His tests are necessarily difficult, and he provides terrible feedback. He takes little to no interest in his students and is unwilling to assist with questions or concerns. please avoid this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Assigns reading that is way too difficult for a 200 level class or non poli-sci major. The readings have so many references to concepts and authors that will just not make sense to you if you haven't taken any other poli-sci classes. Readings are long, difficult to understand, and  I worked harder in this class than in my 300 level classes. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: It seems other students get the wrong idea of this knowledgeable man. Professor Dasgupta cares and if you actually approach him with questions and concerns, he is willing to give all the time it takes for you to understand the material. He has a big heart and truly cares as long as you also care.

He expects insights gleaned from the readings that he may not have considered. That's a level of insight that is subjective. I emailed him a more appropriate response and asked if it was acceptable and it still was not.  I foresaw this class being an issue and dropped, most people get Cs and I'm not ready to work so hard for a C.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you're a fool like i am, you would read this post and severely underestimate the amount of work that this class is. If i were you, i would avoid taking this class under any circumstance. There is hundreds of pages of reading per week as well as a interview compilation video you need to shoot in four weeks. If you work a part time,forget passing.

You certainly have to read the material. If you do the readings and watch the films you'll do well. Of course, the assignments need to be completed as well. The professor is fair and is more than willing to give his time if you're confused.

Absolutely WORST course experience at UMBC and I'm two weeks away from graduation. The quiz questions were unclear and terminology inconsistent. Wayyy too many readings and doesn't even address them all in lectures. Saw on myedu that 59% of his students receive a C! I would avoid this professor like the plague.

This professor makes it very hard to earn your grade. The course was completely online and the amount of reading was extensive and very challenging. there are projects to do and many submissions online to make. The quizzes are somewhat easy however they have some confusing questions. Having said all that... I will say I learned a lot!

The readings are very difficult for a 170 level class, and then if your discussion board posts about the readings aren't great, he gives you rude comments. The quizzes are incredibly hard, and the grade distributions for the whole class reflect that.

This class was challenging and I barely got a B. There are mandatory discussion board post, 4 or 5 a week. He grades easy on those but the quizzes are challenging. Had to re read readings, which were really long in order to get a C and up on quizzes. Also there is a assignment where you have to record a protest, tricky!. Good Luck!!!

He is extremely awful teacher. Beware of his online courses as the quizzes are extremely difficult. He gives his own material to read every week which are impossible to digest, have to read multiple times. Sometimes, he does not answer emails and rude in his comments about the discussion posts. Super conservative person. Do not take his class!

I took the 4 week online summer course. I understood this course would be challenging, however I did not expect a 100 level course to be this deep in concepts considering I am a senior. The reading is heavy and close to impossible with a part time job. The 4 quizzes are only 15 multiple choice ?s & answers are very similar/tricky. Be very careful.
He is hard to understand, really thick accent. He rumbles A LOT, but he tries to be helpful. I just don't think he is. Read the book = A in the course. I skimmed the book and half id the lectures.

This professor is really makes you work. We had to read 4, 20-40 page, articles weekly and post on blackboard 5 times a week at the very least. Has 4 quizzes are very tricky. I took the class in the summer and def would not recommend it. So far he doesn't give extra credit easily and no curve thus far either.

Professor is super nice and cool guy. Class was difficult and a lot of material, but shouldn't be hard to get at least a B if you do extra credit opportunities he gives and show up to class. I didn't read the textbook once and almost got an A

Exams and study guides are 78% of the course, already pretty rough for students who aren't the best test takers, but he does drop one at the end of the course. Boring lectures so there's really nothing to do, (no homework besides videos due at he end of the semester).

Bro made me want to rip my hair out. He overcomplicates EVERYTHING. You ask a simple question and he just confuses you more. He makes you do a study guide and grades it but you have to email him seprately to find out what you got wrong and need to study. Whats the point of a study guide if you cant even study from it. HATED this class dont take it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fall 2025 | As a first time professor, Dr. Strobach's class was more in-depth than a lot of intro courses, which I loved. He's receptive to student feedback, made exams easier, & cut content as the semester progressed. The content itself isn't difficult. Highly recommend if you're interested in geography. Not recommended if you just want an easy A.

The exams make up most of your grade, which are difficult. It was his first time teaching, and he had a monotone voice that was not engaging. He was very knowledgeable, but not the best professor as his teaching style wasnt my favorite. The exams were based on the lecture slides, which were always jam-packed with information for an intro class.

This is Professor Strobach's first time teaching however I do think he could do a few things to improve. He is very very passionate and obviously smart in his field, yet I think he could make the exams a lot less confusing. I also feel that he could explain topics a lot better than he has in the class.

Professor Strobach is clearly passionate about his field and is an expert. However, as this was his first time teaching, a lot of the class was TOO much- especially for an intro class. The exam questions are confusing and extensive, covering a lot in a short period. Strobach was willing to change styles to help students, but it didn't work for me
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I personally really enjoyed having Professor Strobach. There is a lot of interesting material that he goes very in depth about, and he clearly knows what he is teaching. I would only say that the most crucial information of the course lies in the lectures; if you pay attention and study hard for exams, you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I'm not sure about my grade yet, but Dr. Strobach did well for a first-time professor. He's funny, detailed, and very supportive. My only concern is the exams; “confusing” is probably the best word. He tries to rephrase questions in a way that ends up being unclear. I really enjoyed the class, but those exams… I don't know, man ToT

He's a new professor and trying his best though his class is very test heavy and it goes into great depth with the topics covered. Expect to study a lot and if you are not disciplined I would not recommend this class.

Professor Strobach is a very clear teacher who communicates well. His lectures and power points are very in depth and detailed and he always posts the slides the day before class so that you can access them when you need. The class itself is pretty test heavy with a lot of content, so make sure that you actually study and prepare! Don't wing it.

Not sure why there are a lot of negative reviews. I do agree that she can improve on grading with time and replying to emails more often, but other than that I've enjoyed her personality and classes. I took 309 and currently 311 with her, 312 next. She is really understanding and easy to talk to.

I think these reviews/rating is inaccurate, this is my second class with Dr. Evans, Her deadlines are extremely lenient and she always so considerate of students. You just need to show up, participate and do the work on time.

Avoid this professor at all costs. Severe time management problems and grading, while very late, was very unforgiving with no feedback whatsoever. Emails sent to the professor asking for help were completely ignored or unhelpful. The class itself was disorganized, with much time spent on tangents that had absolutely nothing to do with the class.

This professor struggles with time management and grading assignments in a timely manner. When students reach out for help, emails often go unanswered or responses are vague and unhelpful. Assignments were dropped due to being behind, which limited learning, and the course felt disorganized with little meaningful instruction blamed not having a TA

She never graded the assignments until the end of the semester, everytime you emailed her, never replied. She just talk and talks at class sometimes stuff that doesn't concern us.We get behind a lot, the worst class.

If you are interested in taking her course in PSYCH 312, please DO NOT REGISTER FOR HER CLASS. The teacher assistant grades everyone work and takes days off during the semester when the class needs her.

She gives terrible feedback takes way too long to grade, like how are you going to be slow and give zero feedback? When I asked for more thorough feedback and quicker grading she threatened to report me for plagiarism all because I forgot to include one source in my reference list. Unhelpful and incredibly discouraging

Perhaps Dr. Evans is respected in her field but as a professor there is a lot to be desired. Delayed grading, lack of encouraging or useful feedback. Uses degradation and threats of reprimand as ways to ensure compliance. This was a miserable experience and hope Dr. Evans finds her true calling.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a good teacher, terrible at explaining topics, getting in contact with her is impossible, takes forever to grade, assigns very important and time consuming assignments that take about a week to complete to be done in only 3 days, and she will give poor directions for assignments and be confused how you didn't do well on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor ever!

The professor is irresponsible in her scheduling and takes time off too many times. The grading is done by her teacher assistant so beware. The work is very diffcult and demanding, if you take this class keep up. A research paper is due at the end of the semester (heads up 9-12 pgs).

Very rude and unprofessional. Enforces strict policies but cancels class often for personal trips. Hard to reach, unpleasant in class, and grades harshly. Even if you attend and do your work, she's not reasonable. Avoid taking her if possible it's a frustrating experience overall. Mind you, the class it's self is not hard it's just her.

The single worst professor I've ever had. Snarky, lazy, strict, and unhelpful. Cancelled the third week of classes to go to Disney, and stopped lecturing altogether 3 weeks before the end of the semester. Doesn't accept doctor's notes and has a strict late work policy despite frequently being late herself. Finals week is hectic and exams are tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Leaves zero useful feedback. I am a 4.0 student who apparently can't even conduct a proper reference page in her class.

The course material isn't difficult but there are SO MANY modules that are just a repeat of lecture. Part of the group work grade is on how other members rate you, so it's out of your control. She gets off topic a lot when lecturing. There is a sign in sheet every class and it counts towards your total grade. Not difficult but VERY annoying.

Dr. E was a wonderful professor. I found her explanations of difficult content very helpful, and I understood concepts that I had not before because of her. She is very approachable and will hear you out if you disagree with one of her answers. She sticks to her syllabus, which is really helpful for staying organized and on top of everything.
Dr. E is super caring and really wants her students to succeed. She is engaging and enthusiastic about teaching. Overall a great teacher.
Very slow to grade

This teacher is awful! Grades were weeks late for assignments so there was no feedback before doing the next assignment. When asking questions for clarification responses were quick but snarky and unhelpful. The entire class she would be eating, working out, or have distractions like her dog whining. Lecture was boring and lacked valuable info.
Not good. the worst psych professor you could have

She actively seems to want students not to succeed. This semester with her has been detrimental to my emotional and mental well-being. She is disorganized, clueless, expects students to be understanding to her numerous missed classes & mess ups but doesn't try to be understanding to their circumstances AT ALL. A wolf in sheep's clothing. AVOID HER!

"My sincere apologies" is her go to phrase. Unorganized, passive, and careless. Her lectures are boring and her knowledge is limited. She canceled classes many times. Although she does bare minimum as a teacher, she is such a tough grader. She might seem nice but she is really not! Not good in communication either.  Avoid her!

I've never had an experience with a class like I had with Evans. Please avoid taking her if you care about your gpa. She is very stingy with grading and doesn't grade assignment rights away (You'd have to wait a week or two). She never gave us access to the final assignments until the end of the semester,which we now have to cram in a couple weeks.

Worst professor I have ever had. She gets extremely passive aggressive. She is obnoxiously slow with grading, troublesome when assignments build off of each other. When this was pointed out, she got more passive aggressive and didnt attempt to be understanding. She offers feedback for the paper but does not give it. She overexplains simple things.
He is way too petty and stingy with grading. You can literally follow every single criteria, yet never get full credit on an assignment. Avoid!
Avoid taking. Takes too long to enter in grades.
This was a hybrid class, but I never went. All the work is easy to do, just tedious and plenty. Had to write two papers, but those were simple to do. Overall, an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Nice and personable. During the semester she seemed to have a lot going on in her life which is unfortunate but she seemed to be very unorganized and even unaware of what was going on in her own course. Thankfully, the work was pretty easy and she has very helpful and detailed lecture slides, so detailed you do not even need to come to class.

Dr. Evans is a great person but she is an unorganized professor. Grading is consistently late. I reached out for help on final project, she told me the semester was over (2 days before the project was due). I just got half credit for a homework assignment bc the directions were wrong (the day before the semester is over). Frustrating.
One of the best instructors I had at UMBC. Dr. E is caring ad amazing. She will do the best she can to make her students succeed and she is very accessible outside of the class.

Dr. Evans is super chillll. She really works with everyone to make sure they really understand the material. Material over all is easy as long as u understand basic statistics. Students who didnt understand stat continued to hold the class back (even though stat is a prerequisite). Highly recommend dr. Evans shes it guys she is it.

Great professor in my opinion. If you pay attention in class and take notes, you will do fine in this class. His lectures are awesome and super entertaining. He doesn't take attendance, but enforces this by giving pop quizzes. To pass those, you need to be in lectures and listen. If you do this, this is a really fun class with a awesome professor.

professor ealick is very funny and nice towards his students. he does not take attendance, but will give pop quizzes every now and then, which are a bit difficult if u don't attend lectures. grade is based on those pop quizzes + a few papers. he is a very slow grader, but is fair and makes up for it by extending deadlines. very understanding!

had this prof for PHIL100, PHIL380, and PHIL478; besides being a very slow grader at times and only basing grades off a small handful of assignments, the assignments are relatively straightforward if you put in any effort and he's very funny and very nice with students

The professor has a great sense of humor and connects concepts to real life. While grading can be tough, attending lectures and using tools like unstuck AI for study prep makes the class manageable. Worth taking if you enjoy writing.

He wasn't a bad professor he just takes way too long to grade. He gives random pop quizzes so look over notes before every class. I got a B because I did bad on all the quizzes but I got As on all the essays which were really easy. Not too much work and overall an easy class.

Amazing lectures!! Made the class participate in a way that caused students to challenge previous beliefs. Every class was interesting. While attendance isn't mandatory, skipping can result in quizzes being more difficult.

Professor Ealick is my favorite professor in college. His lectures were interesting and engaging, I felt that I learned a lot and also there was very little work. He does not take attendance but he does give very easy pop quizzes which are instead of attendance. I also take scientific reasoning online with him and that is great as well.

He is very engaging when he lectures and his class was by far one of my favorites this semester. He is a bit slow on grading but he is very lenient. Hands down one of the easiest classes i've taken, just make sure to go to his lectures because the pop quizzes are based around his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He hates all forms of technology and will snap if he sees any. His lectures were okay and the workload was quite easy, but you will get almost 0 to no grades back before the end of the semester. If you do all ur work early you can get it out of the way. He cares abt what he's lecturing and doesn't seem mean or condescending.

I found the lectures super engaging and the concepts interesting. Sometimes his comments would be jarring, but they're meant to stop students from spacing-out, I think. Super slow grader, incredibly so. But he is aware of this and gives extensions. Knock out the 4 essays in the beginning, show up for pop quizzes, and it'll be your easiest class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: First PHIL class I've taken, but was still able to understand the material and engage in class. It's part lecture, part discussion. Read the material and be ready to make comments/ask questions in class. Loved how he added humor and made the class laid back.

Professor Ealick's class was not hard. He's not a hard grader, but his ways of teaching may be old school. Unknown amount of quizzes, and 3 very easy papers no exams. Will not allow make-ups unless you provide a sick note or something of the sort. He's kind and funny during lecture. Important to pay attention and do the readings for your papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took Greg Ealick for Philosophy of Mind, and this class was very interesting for me. I believe upper-level philosophy courses in general require a fair level of interest in the material, but Greg Ealick does a great job of getting the class's attention through humor and an obvious breadth of knowledge of the material. He can come off as arrogant.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof. Ealick is genuinely one of my fave professors I've had at UMBC. He's super funny and a very entertaining lecturer. He takes a while getting grades back, but is lenient on deadlines for papers, and often pushes back due dates. If I have room for an AH elective in my schedule, he'll be one one of the top picks.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Ealick is a great professor and is very good at what he does. He is very understanding and gives great feedback, I would totally recommend taking this class because it was very enjoyable. Be aware that there is a lot of reading and note taking for this class. The assignments are fairly easy and he is very fair when grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: There are three papers, weekly quizzes and discussion posts that you have to do for this class. Overall I think it's a pretty easy class and Professor Ealick gives good metaphors and stories to help explain the concepts being taught. He cares about his students and is accessible outside of class!

He is really funny and a great teacher. I enjoyed how he connected the topics to daily life and other funny similarities. He is a very lenient grader and as long as you are listening to what is going on in class, you can do great on the quizzes and assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Ealick's lectures are amazing. This course was the most interesting I encountered, and prof makes the content engaging. Must blog 5 times per week, biweekly quizzes, and 4 papers. Prof's only flaw is that he doesn't grade!!!! The agony of waiting until finals week to receive grades was unacceptable. Beware unless confident in writing!

Great professor would 100% recommend! He made lectures fun and engaging. This class was very enjoyable to take but if you don't like writing it may not be the best fit. Besides that he is super understanding and tries his best to grade papers in a somewhat timely manner so that you know how you're doing in the course and what to do to improve.

His class was lecture heavy and there was around 15+ pages of reading to do before each class. The readings were often confusing but weren't really necessary until you do the unit quiz and essay. His lectures were boring but if you participate it's fine. He is an easy grader and is lenient in working with individual students. Overall a chill prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Absolutely hated this class. It's good if you like logic, bad if you like language, even though it's called Philosophy of Language. His sense of humor is degrading to students and makes you feel bad for asking questions over email. In person is fine, though. He grades rather high while having confusing quizzes that cover things not in the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: He was fine. Nothing great. Some positives- It is a fairly average class, not much work. His humor is great, always enjoyed the actual lecture. Negatives- Grading, just as others say. There is not a great indication of how to actually study. There is no book, only readings and class notes. He doesn't write notes, you write what he is speaking.

Professor Ealick was hilarious. He plays off the energy from the class. He tries to balance the sophistication of the material with modern references mixing with some profanity and edginess. His end of the class paper is really when you can meet with him outside of class and discover that he truly cares about each students learning.

This class takes more work than you would think. He grades the essays very hard and the pop quizzes include very specific questions from lectures. He promises to have assignments graded time and time again and ends up grading them last minute. Not a fan.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: horrible. take phil100, not 152, if you want an easy arts credit. just oof.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tough grader. But he expects students to be understanding when he doesn't return half of the grades until the end of the semester. This leaves students stuck if they do not like a grade they received, because they have no more opportunities to make changes and bring their grade up.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lecture heavy, good attendance and detailed note taking are mandatory to do well on the weekly quizzes. Points are deducted for the most frivolous of reasons, and his TA's are very slow at grading and updating BB. There are three essays and you get to choose which topic to write about, but the final essay is worth the most points.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Get ready for pop quizzes and be specific while answering the pop quizes as he takes points off unfairly. I took his class thinking to boost my GPA because it was 100 level class but it was lot harder than any programming class I took here at UMBC. Avoid him at any cost.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I'm in my final year at UMBC and Ealick is the worst professor I've had. His pop quizzes are unfair, he uses profanity far too often, and he was rude to students. He snapped at people for simple questions and accused me of plagiarism with no evidence. It's a shame because the material was interesting and he often gave good lectures. Don't take him.

Not an easy A for a 100 Lvl class. Class itself is easy, but grading is arbitrary, with few assignments. Got points taken off final paper for things he didn't mention in instructions. He was mad when I pointed them out. Got points back, but I had to argue and he was toxic about it the whole time. Disappointed, because he was a funny guy. Not worth.

Cool dude; really chill and funny and makes lectures really interesting and you're sure not to doze off. Make sure you do well on the weekly quizzes; there mostly just a few questions on the definitions of the topics covered in class. For essays, make sure to back up your claim and be detailed and straightforward.

You have to go to every class because he lectures without the use of powerpoint or the board, so you have to pay attention. However, that is easy to do because he keeps the lecture interesting and engaging with his stories, amazing humor, and examples. Take lecture notes and you'll do fine on any quiz and exam. He grades fairly and is accessible.

I think hes pretty unprofessional. Not only are his jokes kinda really rude sometimes, but he also just creeps me out. He always wears jeans that he lets sag low and hes also always got sweat stains on his chest even if its 50 degrees out. Definitely wouldnt feel comfortable going to his office hours. Other than that, the class was fine.

He's very knowledgeable and does great at lecturing, but if you need a visual to learn, you're not going to get it. Personally, I don't like him too much, I think he has a bit of an ego, but he's certainly not a bad guy. He's a tough grader, make sure you have all the info you need but not TOO much or he'll complain about that too.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Terrible at getting grades back, never writes anything on the board so lectures are confusing sometimes, tough grader Too hard and too much stress for an intro class, I would not take this again ever
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ealick is great and makes class fun. He gives lectures from his head instead of presenting slides so writing down important info is on you. The class itself was great and very interesting; I would strongly recommend it. The discussion section is with a TA where you take a quiz each week. Other than that there is two short papers and one long.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Sometimes the lectures were boring, sometimes not! Taking Prof. Ealick again this coming spring. My main issue was the TAs graded our work, and one TA graded much harder than the other. I felt as if there wasn't much communication between the professor and the TAs.

The class had about 20 people in it. You have to delve deep into the readings. Coursework was graded consistently, the criteria is basically that you demonstrate you understand the material for a B, and an A means you demonstrate a philosophical jump onto deeper analysis. Loved the class. He is not intimidating, you just cant BS him.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Ealick is a charismatic individual. He makes lots of jokes, yet some come off as needlessly edgy or crude. Nonetheless, he is very passionate about the material. If you show up and do the readings, you can pass easily. Strict on grading, and exams would have no scores higher than a 92 but none lower than a 70. Randomly gives quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I loved his class, he's a great funny guy. Go to lecture, listen and take notes and you'll get an A

Aside from the interesting material, this class was awful. The professor is rather arrogant and is terrible about posting grades when he says he will. I still haven't gotten back my last exam despite him saying that he'd have it up over 2 weeks ago. He's passionate about philosophy but his snapping at students and lack of returning emails ruined it
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Ealick is genuinely knowledgable about philosophy. He jumps around a bit when giving lectures, but overall wants to make sure his students understand the material. This class is worth taking, but make sure to read over your notes before each class. Ealick is unfair in terms of pop quizzes and if you aren't prepared, it'll knock your grade
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Ealick is really funny and his lectures are interesting. He's disorganized, but he makes up for it in lecture. There are quizzes in discussion, 2 short papers, and 1 long final paper. Never go on your phone or interrupt him (especially when he's about to get to the point). Still participate and ask questions; he's interested in everyone's thoughts.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Seems like a cool professor at first, but was not accessible outside of class at all. His instructions for the assignments are "intentionally vague", but he clearly has a specific expectation of what he wants you to write for the assignments, even though he does not explain them at all. Be careful. I had a pretty bad experience with him.
2 exams and 1 paper. Read the articles and he will discuss them in class. He was slow to grade the exam and paper, but he was fair grader.

This is my first semester at UMBC, and prof. Ealick is one of my favorites! His lectures are always very interesting; never a dull moment. There are easy weekly quizzes in discussion, 2 short writing assignments, and 1 final paper. BE-FRIEND THE TA to get a good grade. His class sparked an interest in philosophy in me that I never thought I had.
Homework was often interesting.  Fair.  Maybe a little flighty but knowledgeable.

Your grade consists of weekly reading quizzes, 2 short writing projects, and 1 longer final paper.  The workload itself isn't difficult.  What is difficult is that there is little clarity on what we are being graded on in our papers.   I think As on papers are hard to come by in this class.

He is smart, funny, easy going, and hippie-like. He is one of my favorite professors that I have had since starting school. He's also really laid back. He doesn't or rarely ever writes anything on the board so you'll have to listen to him carefully when taking notes.  He also doesn't structure his lecture to a tee but that's fine. Awesome class :)

For all of you out there that want an easy A for a humanity, don't take him. He isn't clear about what is need to get an A and didn't pass back the last test (there are 3) or the final paper. Didn't feel like arguing over my grades with him but will never think about taking another class with him. He's a really smart guy though.

If you take Phil 150, the morality class, BEFRIEND THE TA! Heshe will grade all your quizzes, papers, and even the final paper. The TA control's your grade! You can show up and listen to the amusing lectures, but reading the book before the quiz may be fine as well. Overall easy class- do the work and have TA make corrections and you'll get an A.

Pretty simple clear cut class. For 150, Contemporary Moral Issues, you show up to lecture, take some light notes and do readings for homework (10 pagesweek, interesting to me). Quizzes are short and simple. I think he lectures well and is pretty funnyinteresting.  For 152, Intro to Moral Theory, same stuff basically. I enjoyed the class overall

Professor Ealick's course is mainly Socratic and the discussions are interesting. However, Ealick himself is not very helpful and is often rude and unsympathetic when approached with questions or concerns. He was not very helpful, and was quite intimidating. I found myself worried to ask questions out of fear that he would be rude to me.
Awesome class to take, lots of fun, not too hard.

Attendance isn't mandatory, but he flips a coin at the beginning of every class to tell if we will have a quiz based on reading- so you have to go to class. He clearly likes the subject, but I found him rude and unhelpful. He made you feel dumb for asking questions. I don't recommend him at all. I really disliked him! Hard grader, too!

Funny guy and knows his stuff. But when it comes to grading things he gets lazy, which has its pros and cons. He wasn't clear on the final paper which was a pain to deal with, and is easily irritated when you ask him to repeat something.

The funniest professor I've ever had. His humor is a bit dark, but it's not too bad. I would retake his class if I didn't have to pay for it. DO NOT BE LATE TO CLASS. I had a quiz every Friday during discussion, so it wasn't random. I really didn't read a whole lot from the book, but sometimes the quizzes were on the readings.

Interesting man.  Class was interesting but do not play with your phone, computer, etc. in class, and DO NOT fall asleep. He will get mad. Also, takes a long time to grade assignments and curses regularly in class.

This class was really boring. Attendance is not mandatory but he flips a coin every class to see if you have a quiz so you pretty much have to go. Not very helpful and didn't repeat if you missed something. I would recommend taking PHIL100 with Jim Thomas. If his class is already full, wait a semester!

By far the worst professor I have ever had. He was very unwilling to help students when they asked for assistance and his examples were extremely disturbing and inappropriate. Extremely sarcastic and automatically assumed that if a student did not understand something it was because they did not do the readings.
Very interesting class and lectures.

To be honest, I was looking forward to this class and thought it would be an easy "A" but it wasn't. You actually have to work hard. He lectures the whole entire time and most of the time, it's difficult to pay attention or stay awake. He doesn't grade anything. That's what the TAs are for and they kinda suck. Not the best professor. Try to avoid.

Ealick has no idea what he is doing. Most of his lectures are just random information thrown at you with no focus or direction related to the material. Honestly, how do you know what you're going to be tested on if the lectures aren't clear. Not an easy A. Avoid.

Very knowledgeable man. Requires 3 short papers (3-4 pages), and 1 final paper (6-10 pages). If you are a philosophy major and have written philosophical papers before, take his 454 course; easy 'A'. If not, it will be a struggle, but a solid 'B' is reasonable. He talks the entire time, so staying awake is a struggle. Assigns interesting readings.

Not a very good philosophy teacher at all. When he lectures he goes very fast. If you ask him to repeat something he can't remember what he just said. Must read textbook and take notes in class as best as you can.

As a nonphil major, I only take this class for my gen ed credits. Its not that bad of a class. You must go to class and take good notes and don't fall asleep while I do sometimes...Exams are not that hard. Read some of the book, the most useful material are class notes.
Nice guy but definitively didnt sense the energy or humor mentioned in all the previous feedback. Dry chuckles at most and potential quiz for every class.

He's such a stranger person. Some people found his lectures funny but I thought some of the stuff he mentioned was messed up and inappropriate even for college kids. Every class he flipped a coin on whether there would be a quiz so you have to keep up with the readings and go to class. I thought it would be an easy class but it wasnt

Excellent. He is hilarious, just pay attention. His exams are easy, just take a while. Everyone gets a low A or a high B on the exams, the key is to do well on the quizzes. He curves your grade up if he thinks you deserve it, so participate. He is awesome, just go to class and you have an A.

Awesome teacher, just be sure to be involved in discussion (which is often hilarious).  He presents the material clearly and is straightforward, just take notes when you aren't laughing at his crazy jokes.

He is fantastic! Totally hilarious, very helpful, write down everything he says and you'll  fine. Although, you can tell he gets annoyed when people aren't getting him and they keep making stupid examples but as long as its not you it's pretty funny.
Great Guy, Great Professor.
Ealick is the man. However, I would recommend going to each lecture and taking good notes. dont bother reading the text book

I did not use the textbook, waste of 80 bucks. He covers everything during lecture so just take notes and you ll be fine. He helps with the papers during office hour and the TA was really helpful. This was one of my favorite classes. I mean, the lecture is actually very thought provoking and exciting.

I LOVED Phil of Bio with Prof. Ealick. He is, by far, one of the most knowledgable profs. I have had, and is very well read. His lectures can be a bit circular though, and he doesn't make any notes on the board, so learn to take notes FAST! He grades VERY harshly, so be prepared to work at your essays. Very approachable.

Ever since I have been at UMBC, I prefer Ealick's class more than any other professors within the Philosophy department. During Ealick's lecture, his material is easy to understand, cleverly humorous, and just downright charismatic where you just cannot wait to go to his next lecture. Outside of class, he's AWESOME. He is willing to help anytime!

Ealick is an awesome professor! He is hilarious and he makes the class really fun and interesting. There is a textbook, but he knows that most people don't read it, and you could get by just going to lectures and taking some notes. Attendance isn't mandatory. And there are pop quizzes, but he almost always drops hints the class before the quiz.

Extremely interesting as a person and as a teacher.  His lectures are a bit unfocused, and he suffers fools a little too leniently, but that's forgivable.  Has obviously read widely in the relevant literature, and knows the terrain backward and forward.  Very funny guy, as well.  Recommended, if you can deal with the lack of overall organization.
Awesome professor. made the concepts very easy to understand if you attend lectures and pay attention. He's hilarious which made the lectures fun to go to. Best class I've taken thus far

I took the Philosophy of Science Fiction this summer and it was a really great class.  Prof. Ealick gives good, everyday examples to explain philosophical concepts.  I would recommend taking Ealick's class if you have the opportunity.
Ealick really made philosophy easy to understand - at least the parts that he covered in lectures.  If you attend the lectures and take good notes, you will do well in Ealick's classes.

this class is not 'mandatory', but there are a few surprise quizzes & yes go to class. mostly lecture. he is a VERY funny teacher that likes to use sarcasm, but in the most positive way. I had a hard time understanding the material because I'm not a philosophy major. He is approachable :)

Do not buy the book. I wasted money on it. Never used it. Just listen to his lectures. Hard part is lectures can be boring. The quizzes he gives are on the lectures. Everything is free response. I think it is impossible to get an A in his class. Tried my hardest ended up with a high B. I hear Jim Thomas is way cooler.

This review will sound conflicting: The class material and his lectures are interesting(if you are a philosophy student), however, he is the laziest professor I have ran into. He does not have a set rubric for papers, and he arbitrarily throws in grades on papers. If the class is graded on papers, dont even think about an A.

I thought the class would be easy and somewhat interesting. But he pretty much sucks. The class is boring and you leanr nothing. I don't pay much attention and you could still get by. There are some pop quizzes but he tells you when they are. There pretty easy. Tests are easy as well if you prepare. He is unprofessional. Doesn't give  note at all!!
loved him as a teacher, i actually LIKED waking up to go to this class... best teacher, made me interested in philosophy

Take Notes. There is a quiz once a week about what was gone over  in lecture (reading the book can be subsituted for class depending on the TA you get), two short essays you need to write and one long essay. None of the essays have set due dates and you can write about a variety of subjects discussed in class. He's very interested in philosophy.
An overall great teacher!  Incredibly interesting, clear to understand, and knowledgeable in the material covered.  Highly recommended.

I came in ready for some fundamentalist beyond reach or insane liberal.  Ealick kept a tight grasp on the class, which was amazing.  The focus wasn't the inflammatory topics or opinions, but the formal logic and rhetorical skill behind the argumentation presented.  Provides a good preview of what other phil classes will expect.

Great professor. Taught epistemology from a modern viewpoint so the material was somewhat unfamiliar and more difficult. Grades based on three short (4-page) papers and a 10-15 pager. His comments are very helpful. Very helpful professor in general. Class is all discussion of material from the readings, so definitely read ahead to do well.

He has pop quizzes that are very confusing and he grades them very hard. But he makes it obvious when the pop-quizzes are. You REALLY have to work HARD for his class. I am an engineering major and i signed up "thinking" Phil 100 would be easy but it really isn't. On top of all my coursework PHIL 100 also was there to make things much harder.

I didn't really like this class. I mean, I thought the debates on the subjects (abortion, euthanasia, capital punishment) were interesting, but I felt he just shot down anything anyone (philosophers in the book and students, alike) said about the topics. I thought he could be funny, but, honestly, I just thought of him as a huge elitist.

He's a nice guy with a lot of fun in him but he doesn't like psychology much (my major...) so don't mention it.  His tests and paper can sneak up on you but they are ultimately fair and he is relatively understanding.  Keep up with the book.  This is not a guaranteed easy class, period.
Great and interesting teacher. Everything you need to know for the exams he says in lecture, so come to class always and take notes. He's very helpful and tries to explain things clearly.

the material was boring, but he did his best to make it more interesting. exams were all essay format so you must know how to write effectively, he can be a bit picky about wording. show up to class, the book isn't that helpful so getting the notes is a must!
Brilliant man! Thanx for the knowledge. You will love his yipee boots
good teach. delivers material well. May the gnomes be with you GE

Excellent teacher! If you go to class and take notes you will be fine. He is really helpful and you will never be bored in class. He gives great examples and makes sure you undersatnd the material. Loved him!
Has great examples and stories to back everything up, makes all concepts crystal clear.  He is the stereotypical awesome "Dead Poet Society" cool college professor, and thats a good thing.

Ealick is one of the most interesting professors you will ever have. When he gets excited he talks like Macho Man Randy Savage. "Snap into a Slim Jim!" If that isn't convincing enough he kind of looks like a pirate. You should definitely take class with this guy.

Best teacher I've had at UMBC thus far. Very logical, organized in lecture but also engaging. I learned a lot and the work load was not bad at all; he gives very fair quizzes and tests. Great class, great teacher: definitely recommend.
He's a good teacher and makes the class interesting.  He practically teaches right out of the book.  I regret spending that $60.

He's an excellent teacher who always has an intersting little tangent to tell the class to keep them engaged. Is very reasonable in grading, and doesn't make tests that try to trick you. If you want to be intelectually stimulated, take have this teacher.
No Comments
He is great.  One of the smartest people I've ever met.  Just ask him about debate stories.  Expect to learn a lot.

A really great professor, he manages to engage the class in interesting information and ideas.  He's willingly to help you out if you have any questions at all, and is very down-to-Earth, in and out of the classroom.  Very good at getting the class thinking about things while leaving it open for input from him and other people.

DON'T take her class unless you're prepared for constant stress, frustration, and a genuinely miserable experience. She shows little to no concern for her students' success. Overall, an incredibly disappointing and exhausting experience. If you have any choice at all avoid her class. Instead, I highly recommend Dr. Hughes who is outstanding.

Nursing school was easier than her classes. If you can take Dr. Hughes, do it. She does not care about your time nor well being. Don't waste your time trying to talk with her either, she does not care.

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HER unless you want a mental problem. she don't provide powerpoint. Test are heavily graded.

This course completely ruined me. She yelled at me for not understanding content one time! The other bio department professors talk bad behind her back and she grades papers subjectively! I lost many friends and dropped clubs because of how deep in depression i was due to this class. Her humor is a bit dark but she is extremely smart. you'll learn.

0 powerpoints. 0 grades posted online. 0 support. you will feel extremely isolated from your friends and family. the majority of your grade relies on your exams & quizzes, which has little to no multiple choice. pick a religion and pray honestly. on the bright side, she answers emails quick!

reviews.comment: Nah don't...

I could not have had a more positive experience with Dr. Fleischmann. I first met her on an airplane and somehow a conversation started where we figured out that she is going to be professor in the future. She is so sweet, but her class is difficult. I absolutely worked by butt off for my A, but it was worth every second for the knowledge I gained.

There is way too much hearsay about this professor. She is the most supportive, sweet, and caring professor I have taken thus far. Yes her class is difficult and she was a difficult grader. However, her students will go on to know A&P like the back of their hand, as they should if they want to be healthcare professionals.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very sweet, caring, and intelligent professor teaching a hard class. Knows what she's talking about and will go above and beyond to help, you just need to show her that you're putting in the effort. No online slides or grades posted does suck, but she replies very quickly to questions about content and grades. You'll be prepared for nursing school

You will have to study a lot but she is a great prof, so sweet, nice and passionate about the class! There are a lot of exams and quizzes, but if you come to every class, take good notes and study, you will be fine! She tells you everything you need to know in lecture. Lab is tougher but she is still a great prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her ONLY grades are test and quizzes! She lectures without any PowerPoints. Nothing is in BB including grades. I took Dr. Hughes' class and the difference of teaching is amazing! I noticed this most in lab since Fleishmann basically has you learn all lab material on your own with no guidance, Hughes will explain every detail till you understand!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you don't pay attention or attend lectures you will fail. She doesn't cover everything in the book, only certain topics. She really cares about you and your schedule. She can be scary but is actually super nice and fun to talk to. Class isn't hard if you pay attention and just study your notes.

Pros: Clear with what she's testing in lecture, accessible outside of class, responds quickly to emails, grades fairly, knows what she's teaching, supportive as long as you show dedication 

Cons: doesn't post grades on blackboard, no lecture slides, lab material doesn't align with lecture sometimes

Overall she's a good professor in a hard class

reviews.comment: For your mental health DO NOT DO IT. I read the reviews thinking I would be different as I get straight A's every semester even in Orgo and this was worse. DO NOT TAKE HER

She does give a lot of tests and quizzes, but if you take the lab at the same time it actually makes it easier because a lot of them are repeats. She does give a ton of detailed information in her lectures, but if you attend every lecture, take good notes, study hard, and ask questions when needed, you will be just fine. She is a very sweet lady.

reviews.comment: Dr. Fleischmann's lab was pretty disorganized and old-school. She lays out anatomical structures and has her students look at them for the entire 3 hours of lab with lectures on the side. Practicals are insanely difficult, but I'd say the quizzes are pretty fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: her lecture exams are very clear cut with what she goes over in lecture. she doesnt try to pull any tricks and if you truly study itll be reflected in your grade. lab on the other hand feels much harder and disorganized. it can easily feel like ur constantly falling behind, but hey pre nursing

Although she expects a lot out of us, the class is doable IF you put in the work. It is not easy in the slightest and if given the chance I would've taken Hughes but one thing about her is you WILL be prepared for nursing school. Her lectures are thorough but lab is very disorganized and most of it needs to be self taught. Know your limits...

must memorize everything to have a chance at passing tests, does not believe in tech so you MUST show up to class, PICKY GRADER, no sympathy for students failing. if you are in this class, its bc you have no choice so try to not take it w other hard classes bc all your time will be spent studying here

Nursing cohort students, I strongly consider taking AP1 over the summer after fresh. year and AP2 during the fall soph. year with Dr. Hughes. Prof. F was honestly the worst teacher I've EVER had. Honestly the worst professor I have ever had in my life. She's so picky with her answers and even if you get the question partially right you will get a zero for that question. Its clear that switching online due to covid was difficult for everyone, which really shows from looking at past reviews of Dr. F. reviews.comment: Dr. Fleischmann is an amazing professor, and if you are genuinely interested in a career in healthcare, her A+P classes are worth it. Ive learned so much!

Dr. Fleischmann is an amazing but extremely difficult professor. She knows A&P like the back of her hand. Expect at least one quiz or exam every week, especially if taken with the lab. reviews.comment: She is very smart and a great teacher but she throws out a lot of content at you that you need to memorize. reviews.comment: She knows her stuff, but is in no way lenient about grading. She throws as much material as she can at you and makes the class far more difficult than it needs to be. She could really be a great professor if she provided more resources such as videos, labeling packets, and review sheets that could help with go along with her cluttered lectures.

Dr. Fleischmann is tough but if you show up to every class, pay attention, take notes, and study hard, you will get an A. Everything she says during lecture is fair game but questions on tests can be found in your notes word for word. She is funny but also serious. Dr. Fleischmann is one of the best professors I have ever had. Highly recommend.

reviews.comment: Awesome professor you just have to work super hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Hard class BUT I learned a ton.
