reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Fleischmann is an awesome teacher. She is very knowledgable about A&P material and super enthusiastic as well, which makes her lectures interesting. She tries very hard to get to know her students well especially if you are in the lab. Look over notes and diagrams from the lectures to prepare for quizzes/tests.

Prepare to study! She tells you everything you need to know for all the tests and quizzes given during lecture. Be prepares for fill in the blanks & free response questions. She is willing to answer any & all questions, Do not be afraid to ask! She seems intimidating at first but she is really passionate about anatomy. Take good notes & read!

Everyone told me not to take her, but I had no choice. She is definitely tough. If you don't attend class and take notes, it will guarantee you a failing grade. The first exam is the hardest because it's very different. There are generally three parts: Matching (large word bank), multiple-choice, and a lot of short answer (be VERY specific).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Honestly if you're looking for an easy A, take Hughes. She will make you work hard for your grade. Very detail oriented (especially for exams and quizzes). Exams were half written which were very difficult unless you studied a lot, even then she will be very nit picky. I recommend recording her lectures. Expect a quiz every week. And STUDY.

she is an awesome professor because you can tell that she is very passionate about what she teaches. during labs, she will come around and quiz you on small things so you can understand better. go to lectures and take notes meticulously. a lot of the things she tests are from her lectures. even the smallest details. understand each concepts

Professor Fleischmann is extremely knowledgable in A&P and really loves what she is doing. She's very willing to help and wants to get to know her students, even though she has hundreds of them. You definitely need to study hard, and you never get a break from studying for her class. Wish that I had more time to study for her class last semester

Very passionate about A&P. Do not understand material, get help ASAP all the content builds on itself. Her personality gives an off putting  vibe but if you show up to her office hours she's willing to help 100%. Will MAKE YOU WORK for grade.  MUST STUDY to pass, quizzes are somewhat easier, tests ARE TOUGH. VERY PARTICULAR GRADER.

She is a great lecturer and professor. However, she tests very specifically. Her exams are given in all forms (multiple choice, short answer, T/F, etc.) so you must study well. As long as you attend class, take notes, and put the time and effort to study, it is possible to do very well in the class. I learned so much to take with me in this class.

This class is hard, but a good grade is possible if you study really hard. Plan ahead and put the majority of your study time into this class. She is very nice and willing to help, but you have to put in effort yourself. She is one of the best professors I've had. B's are easily attainable if you study.
Marks down wrong for each and everything. Avoid if possible.
Terrible

Professor Fleischmann is a great lecturer - I didn't read anything out of the textbook after exam 1 and did fine. However, this is not an easy class. She's a tough grader and will mark you wrong for almost anything. Exams and quizzes are very difficult. Way harder than I expected for a 200 level class. I would say try to take it w/ Leupen instead.

Awesome lady! So enthusiastic about teaching and the content of the course. Very clear on what you need to know for exams. Used the book minimally, just to look over diagrams shown in class. Study her lecture notes and make flashcards. FLASHCARDS ARE YOUR BEST FRIEND. Especially for the bones and muscles!

I love love LOVE Dr. Fleischmann. She is enthusiastic and quirky, as well as very knowledgeable about anatomy. It's A & P, so people who wine about it being hard are lame, of course it's hard.You don't actually have to read the chapters to do well, but study any figures she shows you, & go to class. I will seriously miss her next semester

She's a great teacher and you end up learning so much from her. She's a fair person and her exams/quizzes aren't so bad IF you study. If you don't read, attend lecture, and study...you're screwed. You're lucky to pass. Only complaint is that she has favorites and it really shows--i hate that about her. She's kind of intimidating but she's not bad.
DO NOT get on her bad side.

Dr. Fleischmann is a very enthusiastic and passionate professor. She often relates the subject matter to the lifestyles of her students as examples throughout the course, which can make a difficult concept easier to grasp. Her exams are straightforward and are heavily weighted towards the notes given in class. I recommend making flashcards :)

I recommend taking one other class at most, reading the textbook & paying attention in class. I liked her teaching b/c she's really enthusiastic & seems to know the material very well, but in person, she might seem a little rude. Overall, I think this is one of my best classes.

She is FAIR. If you study for all the exams and NOT Cram, then its an easy A. My favorite subject is Anatomy and Physiology so I enjoyed it and wouldnt have wanted to take it with any other professor! But I do wish she curved a little..b/c i did cram for some of my exams..:( 88% is a B...
She's a tough teacher but a damn good one.

This teacher is enthusiastic about anatomy and teaches it well. But she has drawbacks in the way she talks to people one on one. I have seen on mutiple instances where she mocks people if she thinks the question was bad. Handwriting is worse than the doctors that I intern for which is saying alot. Expect to learn most of the things on your own.

Had her for both bio 251, 252. She's an amazing professor, clear on what we should learn, and she breaks it down so it is simpler. She will answer your questions, but only if they are relevant to subject matter. Study hard because there is a LOT of material. If you slack, you are screwed. An A is absolutely possible.

One of the best professors I've had. Lets you know right off the bat that you have to study A LOT! the material is basically all memorization if you're good at that you'll do great in this class. Make sure you start studying day 1 of class and don't stop till final. Great class A's just require lots of study time.
You will either be a favorite or not. If you are not a favorite you better make this class your life!

If you have to take this class make sure you do not take any more difficult classes it requires alot of time. I recommend taking the class somewhere else. Do not even try to ask questions either in class or outside of class b/c you will get a sarastic response!!

very good professor. hard course but an A is definitely possible. my suggestion is to take it during a full semester (fall/spring), and not summer or winter because it is a LOT to memorize and learn and you need time. study hard!
great professor, very clear. study hard for the bone/muscle tests. fair unit exams. the subject is difficult- you must study..cannot blame Fleischmann if you don't study hard enough and don't do well

not someone you want to go to if you have a question about your grade. i liked her though, her lectures were clear and her tests didn't have hidden tricks. make sure to keep track of your own grade because she refuses to learn to use blackboard, but overall a good teacher
If you go talk to her about your grade she will accuse you of not studying. Avoid her at all costs!!
Take the class somewhere else!! It will save you alot of sleepless nights.
She is the worst teacher I have ever had at UMBC. She critizes students and acts like she's GOD. Her class is BS!

The class is EXTREMELY hard. You WILL fail if you don't put work in. She is rude to some people and def. has favortie students. I talked to her once and she immediatley accused me of not studying. She is enthusiastic and funny at times, but intimidating to. She wasn't in my lab class which I liked becuase i'd be scared havign her there. I dont like

Great teacher, she loves the material, she loves the lecture, ans she almost always lets out early. She is extremely helpful outside of class, and she explains everything very clearly. couldn't have passed it with out her.

She is very enthusiastic about anatomy topics which rubs off on you during class. Go to all of her lectures and read the textbook if you need further clarification. Quizzes are mainly based on the lectures and end of chapter quizzes in the textbook. But read the book for the exams since they cover more in depth material.

Prof. Fleischmann is THE BEST professor in the bio department.  I had her for both 251 and 252  she is funny, enthusiastic, and very approachable. The course is terribly difficult, but she does a great job of explaining it, and exams are fair if you study. I took the class for nursing school, and I am completely prepared for my nursing courses.

LOVE HER! she's def one of the best lecturers i've ever had! really wants all her students to do well and you know she enjoys teaching the subject. her lectures are interesting and the labs are very hands-on. go to class, take notes, and go to open labs!
Great professor who wants her students to do well. Subject is hard, but she will help you at any cost! Likes to get to know her students and is very straight up about what she expects.

really good professor.  extremely challenging material, but she can explain it in a way to make you understand.  if you still dont get it she will go over it again and again untill you understand.  she wants her students to do well
Dr. Fleischmann is an awesome teacher and very helpful.  Anatomy is a hard subject, but she was very nice and always willing to take the time to make you understand the material.
No Comments

Definitely the best professor I've had @ UMBC.  The content is enormous, holds students responsible for EVERYTHING.  Material may seem rushed but do text review questions and you will do well on quizzes and exams.  Exams are fair, but very difficult if you don't know your stuff! DON'T SKIP A CLASS!  Approachable, helpful, enthusiastic.

the best teacher i've had in college. gets to know her students and will go out of her way to help anyone. class is very interesting, although challenging. the material is explained clearly and she lets you know what she expects. she's really funny too

Amazing teacher. She is extremely excited and enthusiatic about the material. Also she is always willing to meet with students for help. Quizes are straight from the notes however, exams are hard. You must read and understand the material in the book. I loved this class!!!
Good teacher but test are very hard and she does not let you know what will be covered on them.

very good teacher, passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. very willing to help students outside of class. before each exam she lets you know ALL of the material that you will be tested on. gives good clues on what to focus on extra while studying

reviews.comment:
Estabrook is a good and passionate professor, if you like the subject, she is good.

If taking for Elective credits, it has a fairly large amount of work for a 100 level, and has mandatory attendance, still not a bad option.

reviews.comment: Professor Estabrook is friendly and upbeat. Her lectures are easy to understand and her slides are very helpful. Her study guides are fantastic for preparing students for the three exams. Sometimes, her classes run a few minutes past the end time. The weekly homework assignments are easy but quite tedious as she has students handwrite them.

Class is pretty easy, she basically tells us exactly what topics are going to be on exam. Homework is ridiculous though, as it takes hours to hand write each week (not allowed to type) which is a complete waste of time.
Professor Estabrook was very well-rounded, giving good lectures and giving content outside of lectures that wasn't required but helped with homework, tests, etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Estabrook is a great professor. Class is made up of 3 exams, and there's 12 homework assignments. Attendance is mandatory, with 3 "sick days" allowed in the semester. Don't email her outside class hours, if you need anything ask a TA (if applicable) or go to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, clear in understanding, and is very passionate about what she is teaching. I would say the workload of the homework is a bit heavy and the homework takes around 3-4 hours to complete since it is handwritten. Very interesting class and insightful in general, but if you are just taking it for the credit do be ready for some work.

I honestly wish I could take every social work class with Dr. Evans. She is very straightforward with her grading criteria and breaks down a difficult semester-long assignment into shorter, more digestible parts. She gives good feedback and genuinely wants her students to succeed.
She gives assignments which encourage critical thinking amongst her students and which come in handy when they eventually become social workers

Dr. Evans is a really great, passionate professor. I enjoy her class and find it to be very manageable. She provides you with clear rubrics for papers and gives good feedback on your policy essay. The class consists of 2 papers and weekly quizzes along with some randomly sprinkled assignments. Her class is definitely one of my favorites.

This course is a lot of work, but Dr. Evans does a great job of working with you! You can tell she cares about her students and attempts to keep everyone engaged during lectures. Be prepared to write a lot, but its doable, and she gives you good feedback on your bill analysis. She also has opportunities for extra credit.

Good mix of lecture, video, class/small group discussion. Each week there is a decent amount of support material to read, watch, or listen to, and you should always count on having to report out on it in class discussions. This was one of the best classes I've ever taken. Papers spaced out well, but the standards are high, so use the time wisely.

Prof Evans is great, she's very kind and supportive and is passionate about social work. I enjoy going to her class, she is lenient about personal circumstances and cares about her students. I took the class for a GEP but it became my favorite class. She will also occasionally bring treats for the class too, which is pretty cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lots of students struggle with this class. It very well may be the toughest in the SW dept. Dr. Evans does take her job seriously, that is true. The work SWers do when we graduate is serious and having a prof that pushes us and makes us better prepared for that work is important. She will help you if you ask for it and gives lots of feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The worst professor I have had by far. I think she assigns work out of pure enjoyment. If you can avoid her at all cost.
Lectures didnt have useful information needed to pass the quizzes/exams. Needs improvement on lectures. Asks for student feedback but does nothing with it. Not helpful towards class content concerns.
Dr. Evans is an amazing teacher. Her SOWK-360 is pretty writing intensive, but her guidelines are clear and she is a fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Took Prof. Enis for CMSC 203 as well as CMSC 202. Great lecturer, goes beyond reading off the slides. Caring and reachable outside of class. Exams can be heavy (in terms of how much they weigh on your grade for both courses). He seems to be a by-the rules kind of guy which I can only knock him for because he didn't round my 89.4% up to an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took him for CMSC203 last semester and loved it! He was amazing at teaching the content and really engaged with his students. Overall I definitely would take a class with him again.

I took Mr. Enis for CMSC 426 and absolutely loved it! He cares about computer security, and it shows in his engaging and original lectures. He makes each concept relatable and easy to understand with examples both real and imaginary. He responds quickly to messages and is always ready to help with the homework. I highly recommend him for 426!
Engaging lectures and seems to care about every student.

Teachers such as Enis are the backbone of UMBC's CS department. Coherent, passionate, and relatable. One of my favorite lectures on the campus. Clearly breaks down concepts and engages the class to ensure understanding and is readily available to provide support both in term of class and career. This man should be considered for a tenure track.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Super easy professor, the tests were just like the homeworks. Only like 1 hw set a week and they're usually pretty chill. Lecture notes are online too, skipped like a month of class and still got over 100 final avg cuz the final exam had extra credit.

I highly recommend Professor Enis; he is a really kind individual who genuinely wants you to learn. He is a very relaxed prof; as long as you have a genuine want to study, he will help you. He is also friendly and knows his stuff. He's just very courteous.   And don't be afraid to approach and communicate to him if you need assistance.
Amazing Professor, explains things super well and makes the exam similar to the practice ones. Super chill dude and really helps their students

Enis is a great teacher. He is new which means he is flexible and understanding to students. I took him for CMSC 203 so I have no clue how he will do for CMSC 202 but I would trust him. He is very gracious with grading and his true intentions in the class are to help students as much as possible. I would definitely recommend having him for CMSC 203

Good at explaining the topics and Very helpful. Fun lectures, attendance is not mandatory but I would suggest you to go anyway. One of the best professors out there, I definitely recommend him to anyone taking this course.

Dr. Lasson is kind and forthcoming but his lectures are very slow-paced.  Sometimes, he does not even finish the lecture and then does not post the slides either, which is stressful.  Make sure you read the books and go to office hours!  Very few "low stakes" assignments so mostly essay and exam heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Lasson is your typical boomer who believes all classes have to be in person, even when it's just a lecture. When he found out other professors were doing their courses hybrid or online, he forced them all to come back in person. It's not like we're doing labs in any of these classes; they're all just about HR. This man is stuck in the 1900s.

Dr. Lasson is an expert in his field and it is evident in his teaching. His exams are application based so they require you to have knowledge of the course and require lots of writing as they are not just multiple choice exams. To put it simply, if you want to learn the field: take Dr. Lasson - If you want an easy A: do not take Dr. Lasson.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I didn't dislike his class but I felt like we were beneath him a little. Like I was in a class with 80 students rather than 20. Other teachers I felt more respected as a professional with work experience and meaningful contributions rather than just naother student

I really don't understand people hate on him. I took pre-calc my senior year and it didn't even help me much for this course. I swear math 155 is the easiest math I've ever taken in my life on god. Its actually just 70% algebra, and 30% calculus. Fortney quite literally made this class a piece of cake, and deserves a lot more praise in my opinion.

Professor Fortney has a complex over his students. He will berate a student for forgetting an old rule from algebra or making a mistake when factoring. And proceed to teach from his notes and make dozens of mistakes, confusing the entire class. He also is obsessed with fear mongering his students about material.

The homeworks are very long and tedious. Pay attention to the lectures. He posts them online as well. Exams/quizzes are similar to problems done in class and on the homework. Overall the class is very doable

Professor Fortney would often claim he has "made this class as easy as possible" and I believe that is half true. He is very straightforward with the topics and does examples in class that are very similar to worksheets and quizzes. Previously taking a calculus course is a MAJOR advantage in this class. But, no study guides/preparation for tests.

Exam heavy. You pretty much have quizzes and worksheets every week but they dont stand a chance against the exams. Very strict grading on the exams, you could get everything correct on them and you could still get a 85% on it if the work is not shown in the way he wants it. Class is what you make of it but its hard. Prof is nice but not helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I will be honest with you guys. If you struggle with math, don't take this professor. He doesn't let students know what will be on the quiz. The worst part about all this is he doesn't give points for showing work, meaning you only get points for each question if you have the answer correct.

If i were you I would just find a different professor to take this class. You can do well on homeworks, quizzes and worksheets and still fail from the tests alone. Multiple choice q's are worth half the points and you have to show work to get credit with no possibility of partial credit (wth?!). The exams are very flawed. Listen to the reviews!!!

The professor is rigorous; he does not know how to teach, and even his notes are wrong during the lecture. This is a no-calculator math class. The Exams make or break your grades, regardless of what you get on quizzes or worksheets—no study guide besides him having a quick overview of what you are expected to know during lectures.

He did not give us any resources, practice exams, etc. anything to use to prep for exams. All we had were our notes. The homework is too complicated. He only gives us the lecture time (50 min) which is not enough time for exams.

If you have a background in pre calc or any calc class, you'll be just fine. If not, then you might struggle a little bit, in class he doesn't fully go over certain topics but if you approach him during office hours about any questions/concerns he was always generally pretty kind. Be sure to review graded tests, he gets things wrong sometimes.

If you have a pretty strong math background this class will be easy. I got a C in AP calc in high school and easily got an A in this class. I think he explains the material well during lectures and if you know what you're doing, you will understand it. A lot of people fail this class but don't let that scare you, it's pretty easy.

He's average at teaching and sometimes he'll be too lazy to teach a certain part of a topic but still put it on the upcoming quiz. The TA for the class will take off points for any little thing and his help during quizzes are scams, he'll say its okay then mark it wrong later. Jon also will let his TA's make mistakes on grading and not correct it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor is a good teacher as his lectures are easy to understand and helpful if you go for office hours.
no partial credit on exam at all

He's a really nice guy, but I can see how he's not everyone's cup of tea. HW and quizzes alternate weekly, with 3 exams per semester. MATH215 is a weird course, and even he admits it's not his favorite to teach. You don't really get too in depth with any one technique, so if you struggle with one week, the other week is a new topic all together.

I had to retake this class. Its not easy, but if you study and practice the problems from notes and old exams, you'll be fine. You need to put a lot of time into this class. I took him online the 2nd time, and it was better than spring. Even though it was rushed, I still took time to study his class outside his online lectures (final was in person)

Fortney was a good prof if you acc attend lecture, quizzes and exams were very easy if you understood the material in class. He is willing to help you understand as long as you put in the effort. The TAs were a bit confusing but the SIPASS was good. For the most part the class is an easy A if you do the bare minimum that's required.

Nice and approachable guy but not the most organized. Quizzes don't always reflect what's on the class schedule, so be prepared. Exams are okay if you lock in; review packets and Organic Chem Tutor is a must though.

The hardest part about this class was understanding the material because it's challenging if you don't love math like me. However, Professor Fortney's lectures and slides really helped. Prioritizing those will definitely help you with the exams and quizzes during the discussion. He's very wholesome and funny at times.

He can't work his iPad, he's not transparent at all about what's on exams, quizzes, and homework, you can't call how he'll grade work on tests, he skims through notes, and attendance is required. 
Even with studying and previous Calc experience, it'll be extremely difficult to pass. Go to tutoring and hope for a good TA.

This man cannot work an iPad for his life. He doesn't explain concepts well and gets confused when students do poorly on worksheets, quizzes, or exams. He smiles creepily and is hard to access outside of class. He made attendance mandatory midway through the course because students were skipping lecture. Pray for a good TA.

extra credit? NOPE!
cancels lectures/attendance because he doesnt know how to work an ipad? YES!
isn't transparent with students regarding what will be on exams or quizzes? YES!
insanely late emails? YES!
smiles creepily at you? YES!
Be wary hes a newer teacher to this school but cmon, if I had one piece of advice take the other professor. srsly

if you arent locked in from day one then youre cooked. okay guy but even worse prof, he wont teach certain things but put them on exams?? he doesnt even teach, he explains things like hes trying to jog ur memory but theres nothing to remember because ur here to learn? i gotta retake cause i need a C or better but i couldnt change profs :(

Review packets didn't always match up with the test materials. Discussion is way easier then the actual class. If you have a good TA you will be fine. You have to study to pass this class. He would skip parts of the packet he would use for lecture. A lot of online homework that didn't really match with the class.

Used material from prior institutions requiring calculators (which are prohibited). Partial credit grading felt arbitrary. Struggled with his iPad too often. Spent ¼ of lecture urging attendance or returning tests. Required discussions weren't helpful. Seemed impatient at times. Homework was graded for both online and submitted written assignments.

nice person, not that great of a professor but has potential if he figures out how to use his iPad and apple pencil correctly and acc covers a good amount of the material in the classes. only went to a few classes, discussions are mandatory not becuz attendance is taken but becuz thats when u submit and receive hw and take quizzes.

The material for this class can definitely be easy for some and hard for others depending on what kind of math is easier for you. Professor Fortney is fairly good at explaining the material clearly and seems to care about his students. He is nice and approachable, however the course itself is not structured well, but that's not his fault.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is unapproachable, rude, and dismissive in emails. He rarely replies, assigns zeroes without reason, and doesn't give credit for showing math processes. He refuses to make helpful reviews, uses irrelevant finance problems in notes, and mocks students for pointing out inconsistencies. His strictness and attitude hindered my learning.

He's great person, but not a great professor. This is a business calculus, but he doesn't go over business questions and has them on quizzes/exams. No matter how much studying I did I averaged a 70% on the quizzes and had low grades on the exams. You either get it or you don't, he's not a big help. SI pass taught me more than he has.

The class is not hard! It is very lecture heavy and requires some reading. The lectures are not very engaging since they consist mostly of reading off of slides which are already posted for students online. Time management was a little rough, and lectures would be rushed many times so that's when reading the textbook can be helpful

Dr. Etopio was great. Lots of work outside of class and it is IMPARITIVE that you do it ON TIME if you want any chance at passing. The work isn't necessarily hard, it's just time consuming so start as early as possible for everything. Overall, really nice professor, she's really understanding and is genuinely a nice person to talk to.

She's a very good professor. She really keeps track of participation so it is very much necessary. You cannot get full points if you use your phone in class, and you have to raise your hand to ask/answer questions. If you do that, and keep up with the work, it's a great class. She makes it engaging, and enjoyable. She's also very nice
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I was really worried about the participation since it counts for points and she really keeps track of it but honestly, it was fine and kept me engaged. The content was really interesting, and Dr. E was very engaging with the class. Dr. E was very straightforward with expectations and deadlines. Follow the syllabus, and you'll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class is pretty straightforward. Took it as a gened. Lectures are boring and hard to follow, but slides are posted on Bb so its cool.
She was organized, clear with expectations, and her lectures were engaging and easy to follow.
I especially appreciated her humor and personality. I left the class feeling that I truly learned something meaningful.

Dr. Etopio was an outstanding professor and far exceeded my expectations. I was initially hesitant to take her course because of negative online reviews, but after completing it in Summer 2025, I honestly do not understand the low ratings. Her course was well-structured, with clear expectations, and her lectures were engaging and easy to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is so organized and caring. She literally put a suggested schedule for homework/reading/exams on her syllabus (the syllabus is helpful). All work is online; grading is quick, and exams are easy if you study and attend class. She's strict about attendance. Lectures were boring sometimes but digestible.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The way some of these reviews sound you'd think Dr. Etopio will break into your house and eat your puppy. maybe it's bc I had her for psych100 but she's pretty good! she goes over lectures pretty clearly and is open to questions (even if they're stupid questions :P), sometimes she skips a few slides that show up on exams but they're posted on bb

DONT TAKE HER CLASS. dont do it. I wish I had listened to my friend. Learned nothing, all this professor cares about are grades. I got awful grades on the online quizzes which some of the questions were stupid. I thought I had done well and answered all the questions correctly, but no, I got a 50% Why? Who knows? Because I can never see the results
Honestly the worst professor at UMBC. If you are an ineffective teacher you are an ineffective member of a university faculty. I might as well have thrown my money down a well.

Honestly, this professor's teaching really held me back. She's super strict for no good reason and not very friendly. The worst part is she won't let us see quiz reviews or old material, so how am I supposed to study and learn? She also doesn't give back tests, which is crazy. I can't even check my mistakes.

This "professor" is a roadblock to education. She actively undermines the learning process by denying access to quiz reviews and previous unit material, making it impossible to learn from mistakes. Refusing to hand back test results is either incompetence or pure academic sabotage. If you are serious about your education, run. She is also rude.
She is NOT a good professor. That'sall im gonna say. 67

I enjoy her lectures but she spends too much time glazing topics that she likes and rushes some lectures. You can easily get an A if you average Bs on the exams and score well on the homework which is generally easy. If you find the exams difficult, definitely read the textbooks, but you can get away without reading.

clear bias of topics, completely tossed the neuroscience/biological crap out to take up 2 lectures talking about social psych because its her fav... tests include stuff not taught that I only knew cuz its my major, attendance policy is horrible and unforgiving, how is it my fault if the wifi is bad? most people ik failed consistently on tests
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Would be better if she didn't use inquisitive for homework.

Overall, Etopio was a great professor. She taught the material well and wants you to the understand concepts. She gives lots of extra credit too. Attendance AND participation is very mandatory. Show you are mentally and physically present. Her grading is very picky and quite strict but she does give great feedback to tell you what you did wrong.

I truly believe that whoever doesn't like Dr. E just doesn't like to participate in class. Classes are incredibly engaging and she truly cares about your learning. Her syllabus and assignment instructions are very straight forward. If you go to class and do the readings and assignments you won't need to study extra for anything. She is great!

Dr. Etopio might be the worst professor I've ever had. Gave me 50% on multiple homeworks where we had to pick a concept from the chapter and made me come to office hours just to tell me she was looking for me to pick a definition and explain it (which were different instructions). Also marks off 4.7% of your grade for each class missed. Insanity!

I'd run as far away from this professor. She's extremely arrogant and gets off on being a control freak. There has to be an internal and underlying issue as to why she acts the way she acts. If you're a quiet student, she will publicly shame you for being shy and mask it as her trying to “help you build a skill”. I guess it's free exposure therapy.

She always comes off as condescending to the class and backs it up by saying “I'm not trying to be rude”. She does this so often that it goes against the fact that she supposedly isn't trying to be rude. Watches like a hawk to take down participation and will complain over mundane things. Her teaching style overall is buns and would not recommend.

The lectures were very interesting and the course schedule was very straightforward. Lectures are based on the readings so be ready to read. The average chapter length is 20 pages so pace yourself. If you read, you will be fine on quizzes and summaries. (Short one-paragraph summaries). Make sure to participate and show up to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Etopio teaches extremely interesting classes and has clear grading criteria. Though she can be inflexible about participation, it really is easy to simply show up and participate twice during class (not required to do this every day). What you get out of this class is what you put in, and I promise if you actively engage you will get an easy A.

Dr. E is one of (if not) the most unexciting and unapproachable professors. She excessively prioritizes participation, attendance, and writing, despite not being a writing intensive course. I have never been more frustrated after a class than in her's. I learned nothing of importance from these classes. I highly recommend not taking her classes.

Class is based on showing up and participating. If you are a student who has any health or conflicting schedules, I suggest you DO NOT take this because SHE WILL MAKE IT DIFFICULT FOR YOU. Grades HARSH, though she seems more critical of your writing skills than your ACTUAL assignment. I'm confused, Is this a focused PSYC course or an ENGL course???

Attendance over knowledge of crucial psychological principles misrepresents who truly understands the material.

Professor Etopio includes useless rubrics, even when followed, so pay attention to her instructions.

I was looking forward to taking psych of motivation this semester, but it's been one of the most unmotivating experiences in my life.

Prioritization of participation over assignments shows a disregard for her students' genuine understanding of content. She is extremely inflexible and expects assignments to be completed in a manner that only she would produce and not by her students' own minds. She has disregarded her own grading criteria when grading assignments.

Overall this class is okay, however things are graded pretty harshly in general. Participation its mandatory to earn points which is a bit pressuring for students who have a hard time participating in class. She is also a pretty harsh grader for reflections, but the learning content is very valuable. The professor she is always smiling and nice.

Barely passed b/c I refused to give in to her participation requirements - they are? Speak 2x every class + points deducted for being late. This type of part. shouldn't matter at this level especially when I aced the material. Easy class but she takes herself way too seriously. I'm proof you can pass despite her saying you won't without speaking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I would like to start out by saying Dr. E is a caring person and makes herself very accessible for help outside of class. However, she is a very tough grader with standards that are difficult to understand. Although I enjoyed her class, I don't think I would take her again because I felt more focused on meeting her homework standards than learning.

The grading criteria is excessively stringent and unnecessary, implying a seemingly deliberate intention to harm students. The classes lack engagement and are limited to mere textbook reading. Additionally, there is a consistent demand for reactions and quizzes prior to each class, which feels burdensome.


I do not encourage this instructure.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This was one of my favorite classes! No textbook but there are outside readings that are necessary. There are no long papers to turn in and participation is a big part of your grade. She's a fun professor and if you do your weekly homework (which is pretty quick/easy) and add to class discussion, you'll get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. E is an amazing professor! She has clear grading criteria, offers great feedback, and is very helpful even outside of class. Her lectures are actually engaging, and they don't feel as heavy or boring as the other lecture classes I have taken. She is so caring and understanding as long as you communicate with her!

Dr. E sets very clear expectations at the beginning of the semester. If you are willing to meet these, the class will be very easy. Most weeks consisted of one or two readings, typically around 10 pages each, and a quiz. The two "big" projects in the class took a maximum of an hour to complete and these take the place of the final exam!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Fun class! No textbook or exams, simply read the assigned readings, summarize it before class, take a short quiz, and then talk about what you learned in class. Participation matters and counts towards your grade. There were a few other assignments but they were all simple enough and she was always willing to help outside of class.

Loved having Dr. E as my professor this fall! Other people who have comments to say about her teaching and how she grades things clearly don't understand how college works. Every professor is different! She gives you points just for asking questions, she is accessible outside of class, and she is very helpful. She is passionate about what she does

Dr. Aubrey Etopio is a good instructor, but an unnecessarily tough grader.  It is difficult to grasp what she wants which seems very subjective. Would-be simple assignments are tougher than necessary.  I would definitely not select this instructor for future classes. There is definitely an underlying issue with control with this individual.

Passionate about the subject. Participation is mandatory and you can get it by raising your hand or going to office hours. Grading criteria very clear. No standard midterm or final, instead you have lots of smaller assignments. Flexible if you communicate with her in a timely way. Keeps things engaging with Kahoots and group discussions.

I loved working with Dr. E! She encouraged group discussion and would give great feedback to students on assignments. I felt I really understood the content more so than I would in just a lecture heavy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Learned more from the readings than Aubrey. Isn't lenient at all. Gets off by having power and control. Grades based off participation and attendance. Doesn't give clear feedback. Reports you for plagiarism if you don't quote/cite everything on discussion posts. Cares more about following directions than the actual work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had her for PSYCH 311 and she's very stern, discussions were due at 2pm on the dot which was really frustrating. She sorta gives out a good amount of extra credit but she's a harsh grader and you have to ask her to go over stuff. Thank god we didn't have a final and the class wasn't hard but it's a lot of reading & has unnecessary stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Asynchronous but easy
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Totally asynchronous but wasn't marked as one when you register. Got harder as the course went on and the 4 review sessions consisted of a kahoot that didn't help you to study for the exam at all. Was a T/TH course but had exams open only on M or W for 14 hours. psyc 100 has the potential to be super interesting but you're basically on your own

A bit of busy work, but lots of extra credit opportunities to help you out. She is always willing to help you out and explain anything that may be unclear, so if you have a question, please ask! She is always smiling and making sure that we have fun while we are learning, and always tries to find relatable examples when explaining new terms.

This professor is absolutely terrible at explaining things. She didn't even bother explaining our biggest assignment of the semester (230 pts) which left us all confused on how to complete it. When we complained to the psych dept, they said it was our fault for not asking; we did, several times. Add to that her charging $25 for discussions. Don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: A very clear syllabus. The assignments are a bit time consuming but are fairly easy. NO EXAMS. Discussion heavy classes that use packback which is $25. Participation is required but it is only asking or answering questions. Very willing to accommodate to help the students. Overall an easy class but a bit a busy work.

This course was taught perfectly for a research methods class, you mostly work independently on modules then take a small quiz, NO EXAMS! And attendance was only mandatory some days in which is clearly laid out on syllabus for due dates and days that is mandatory. The lectures were used to clarify any confusion and discuss the modules done. Loved!

Do not take!! She makes you pay for a third party service that is literally blackboard!! In a pandemic where no one has extra money. Doesn't explain anything well, way to much work, lots of quizzes. It's hours of reading, and she makes everyone put their cameras on.

Etopio's syllabus is 18 pages long. Eighteen. That alone should tell you what kind of professor she is. We're graded on things you don't normally get graded on, we're forced to pay for things we don't need to pay for, and she explains everything in the most confusing way possible. The other 311 prof requires lockdown browser, sooo, crap, or crap?
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. E requires "packback" for discussion, which costs $25, despite having Blackboard Collaborate, which is free. In the middle of a pandemic, with historic unemployment rates, she voluntarily chose to use something that charges us, instead of using something UMBC provides us for free. teaches junk, expects you to learn everything on your own, lectures are actually meaningless cant ask for help because he wants you to figure it out on your own, or he says to google it, trash class trash software trash labs

Professor Falco is very intelligent and wants to help his students succeed, but he has no tolerance for incorrect answers/discussions. He is quick to tell you if you are wrong, very abrupt about it and does not believe that he can ever be wrong. I will not be taking a class with him again.

Brilliant professor who has no time for idiocy or laziness. If you can't follow direction or if you aren't interested in being a diligent student, don't take the class. An amazing professor. Yes, he rambles, yes, he sometimes gets sidetracked, but that is irrelevant in light of his erudite scholarly status and amazing intelligence. Plus he is COOL and has a ton of life experience. The BEST Prof. I've ever had!

Falco went on tangents more often than he discussed the subject material. Probably one of the best professors I've ever taken. He is not easy at all but he's fun and interesting. All you have to do is show a little interest and participate in discussion and he'll give you a lot of leeway. Take him!

Awesome teacher, goes on awesome tangents, but gives no homework, takehome exams, and will only cover what we want to cover book wise.  We may be behind schedule but it does not matter because everything is interesting.  Did I mention he gives out paper extensions like it does not matter.

Despite his nerdy "Woody Allen" appearance and voice, the man is as intense as a laser beam. He's brilliant, exacting, fierce, and absolutely dedicated to his studies. I LOVE professor falco. this is the third class ive had with him and i think hes fantastic. his exams are definetely not impossible, if you do the reading and attend class. hes extrememely helpful if you need it and he is VERY knowledgeable definetely take a class with him. it's totally worth it!
Funny and engaging. Enjoyable class.

Great guy, great sense of humor!  Hardest professor I've ever had, but I learned so much in his class.  Just keep up with the readings and write down every word he says in lectures.  Don't let him scare you; I highly recommend him!

Falco is an excellent teacher! I don't understand why he has poor ratings. He's funny, engaging, knows his stuff, and is helpful outside of class. Study for exams, but they're fair. he is really well read and is so much fun in class and he is really helpful on papers. I would not be afraid to take a course with him if I were you

Did not learn that much in the first week. The 6 hours of lecture that he gives,  I can learn it on YouTube for only 20 minutes.  Do not take his class, if you want to fail. I had great math teachers in the past, this one in particular was not.
My favorite professor at UMBC. Really passionate about the material. Pretty difficult, good preparation for grad school.

He thinks that just because you may read the chapter before the lecture, that you are supposed to be an expert on it and know all the material.  The same goes for his quizzesexams.  He will give out quizzes and exams after a lecture on a completely new section, or give quizzesexams on sections we havent turned in the HW for.  Grades hard too.

Are you taking this crazy insane guy class? You will hate yourself for your decision. He seems care his students but NO. Very poor professor.  It is difficult to understand what he's saying, very boring and difficult to pay attention to. Exams were incredibly difficult.  Avoid if possible.

Honestly the worst teacher I've ever had. He likes to give homework on sections that he's only covered partially. The worst professor I have ever met, do not waste your time to sit in his class, poor English and teaching skill, he did drive you crazy. Awful teacher, so boring students didn't want to attend class, tough grader, and didn't follow schedule on syllabus at all, tests were weeks after the date, didn't teach very well and expected the class to know everything

good teacher,goes through book and keeps the problems simple to make sure you know concepts.  I take calc 3 for engineering but i don't like it. Does not provoke profound thought. Doesn't encourage positive mental health. When she stopped lecturing for a part of the year (so another professor could pick it up) everyone clapped knowing she was leaving -- she really is that bad.  She claims she answers students' questions, but in reality I question if she understand the content.

Doesn't answer questions and not very helpful. Her tests are much easier than Sokolove's, but still can be tricky. Lectures seem to last forever and time just doesn't pass in that class. However, there are curves for a majority of the categories graded, so that is nice. Pay attention in class/read/study the study questions hard and you should be ok

She is the worst professor I have ever had.  She doesn't respond to emails and if she does, she is literally no help.  She doesn't do anything in class except annoy you. If you want to ask her a question, her response is always "that's a question for a different type of biologist."  she's just rude and doesn't care about the students at all.

Her version of lecture is literally going over several diagrams in the textbook. Rarely is anything described in detail ( if ever). If you have to take this class at umbc, make sure you meticulously read and teach yourself the concepts. You won't learn them in lecture, that's for sure.

She's a difficult teacher. It's kind of hard to get help because she won't give you the answer. Some of the TA's won't answer your questions either. If you get lucky, you will have a TA who is really there to help. Read the textbook. Find someone who knows the material very well.

Walking textbook. If it weren't for the clicker questions, I wouldn't go. Her lectures are a boring assortment of text taken literally out of the book and she reads right off of her slides. My advice is to check Masteringbiology constantly and read the book. If you read the book, you can just answer the first clicker question and then take a nap.

Feeser is a brilliant lecturer but overall, her teaching style is not great. When you ask her a question, she will tell you to "ask your teammates" who are just as clueless as you. She is also not very fair; she posted 5 online quizzes about 40 hours before it was due and didn't email the class to let them know. A lot of students lots points.

She taught 303 this summer and it was better than the spring class with Witworth. We were in teams and could be called on at any time to answer questions, as a team or individually. We also did a lot of in-class assignments, which was kind of annoying, mainly because we did no have a lot of time to do them, but they also helped learn the material.

The class itself is not the most exciting, but it would have been helpful if Dr. Feeser was more present during the labs to explain what we were doing and why. It kinda reminded me of Gen Chem labs...

Lectures were uninteresting to me, and ultimately did not reflect the content on the exam she wrote - even the study questions did not help me. You have to *really* understand the concepts beyond the study questions. The whole class was a self teaching experience for me. Very professional though, and answered emails quickly.

Clickers are pretty basic questions that don't really match up with the difficulty level of her exams. Her exams are like hard because the questions can be specific and vague. You can't study from old exams or study question like Sokolove's test. She's very serious about exams and does not directly answer questions during lectures.

The exams are tough only if you don't read the book and break down the choices. Lectures are long but she covers everything that we need to know and what is on the exam. She doesn't give answers outright, but does give us hints so we can figure it out on our own. She responds to questions on the online discussion board.

She took over for Sokolov during the second half of the semester. She completely changed the way he ran the class.  She didn't discuss the new expectations or what material she would be putting on exams. None of the TAs and SI leaders knew what to expect either. She's very serious and unapproachable, and doesn't answer questions about exam content.

Gud at lectures. Gud thngs end ther. Condscending if u ask clarfyng qustion. I did ok on anouncd asigmnts, but pop quiz r inaccessible 4 ppl w lrning dsabilities. Mssed 1 of em staying home 4 mntl hlth reasns, nd wld've rched out 2 see if there was anythng I could do, but unwelcoming attitude discouraged me from askng. If u ADHD lik me, not rcomend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He always reads things off of slides. Lectures are boring. Attendance is mandatory and affects your grade. He'd ask everyone to participate in groups to answer questions based on the assigned readings. You should always do readings before lectures. Your grade also relies a lot on pop quizzes. Exams r easy if you study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: interesting class, i learned a good bit, but its ridiculously reading heavy. he'll make the whole class read a 50 page chapter on 2 days notice and get mad that no ones read it. that being said if you usually test well you'll have a good grade. only multiple choice exams from what i remember. you do kinda get the feeling he hates the class too tho
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Incredibly tough grader, likes to pull pop quizzes on days where he knows attendance will be low (first class after break, first class out of syllabus week etc.) Be prepared to teach yourself the content, he will be little help. Rude to people who ask questions, doesn't post material in a timely manner if at all.

This guy grades tests like I slimed his wife. He has personal issues with students. NEVER take his class. He cares too much about participation and will be passive aggressive and condescending and will single you out if you do not participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
For your sake, please listen to me and avoid him.
Extremely harsh grading. Everything is based around a few exams, pop quizzes, and write-ups. Comes across as very passive aggressive and will try to calls people out during discussions. This introductory course is worse than many (if not all) of the 300 level courses I have taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Try to take this class with some other professor. He knows a lot and looks really passionate about sociology but he doesn't have ability to incite the same passion nor is he great at passing the knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very good professor. Content was clear and digestible with very straightforward tests. Great person as well.
You can tell he's passionate and his grading standards are straightforward, but he is a harsh grader and the pop quizzes were every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very tough greater and a little hard for me to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Content is interesting and you can tell he's passionate about sociology. Isn't afraid to call out students that aren't paying attention though. Also comes off as condescending at times when responding to questions. Overall he isn't the worst but I'd choose another professor over him.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: HUGE ego and overall an unenjoyable person. Splits lecture hall into discussion groups, and forces you to participate in discussion and if he notices you not talking to others he'll walk over to you and make a scene in front of the whole lecture hall. had a pop quiz the day before thanksgiving break started, half the students had already gone home.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Zainiddinov "encourages" group discussions and class discussions, yet can be passive aggressive and sometimes will choose the person beside someone who raised their hand to speak. I used to speak a bit at the start of the semester but he'd repeatedly choose someone beside me to explain my thoughts so I just stopped.

Strenuous, stressful course-load and class environment. I do think she means well, but I have never felt more overwhelmed by a class in my life. Not an ideal class for beginners or slow learners. Also, she requires you to have your camera on for online lectures while her own camera is off?
If you miss one question on one assignment she takes half of your points. Gives a lot of homework and is very strict. This class is stressful, if you are a beginner do not take her class.

This had to be the most stressful class I've ever been in; the constant shouting and overall distrust the professor had in students left me walking on eggshells. During my midterm, I suffered a panic attack and cried so hard in the bathroom that I vomited. The overwhelming humiliation and stress of being in this class has left me with nightmares.

LOTS OF HOMEWORK. Other than that, the feedback for your Spanish she gives during class is very good as long as you keep up with the loads of homework you will be doing. Quizzes are all online and the tests were pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Now while this class was a bit more rigorous than some of my others, and the Professor was stern with us, I believe she means well and intends for her students to succeed. Will this course be heavy in term of work? Yes! If you study, reach out for help you'll live!
Horrendous. Does not make her expectations clear and is very confrontational with students. Expects far too much, especially for an introductory course and is awful at giving feedback.

The amount of work given out for a beginner level class is ridiculous. You have to make sure you stay on top of ALL of your work or you will get marked absent. Late work is not accepted at all and you are given course work on holidays. You are expected to learn Spanish in an impossible amount of time. The language credit at UMBC is a joke.

Holy, avoid this woman if you can. She will take the concept absences and turn them completely against you, even though you can be present in class. On some assignments you receive a ZERO if you miss a question or a section REGARDLESS of how much of the assignment you completed, and you're reported for cheating? She will chastise you constantly.

I don't have anything personal against the teacher, but her teaching style is not ideal, and does a lot of correcting in class. Conversifis are pretty stressful for me and wasn't comfortable for me to talk to random people in a language I have no experience with. For a 101 class theres a lot of expectation, would not take her again.

Professor Gomez truly doesnt have bad intentions, however if youre a freshman or your course load is large be careful taking this class. Any not turned in work=absence. Long winded homework, and the final project youre expected to do a full presentation in spanish without looking at notes. So take this class with a grain of salt.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: She is the worst language teacher at UMBC. Her instructions are never clear and her class is far to difficult for a "beginner" course. She wants us to learn the material in a week and expects everyone to be fast learners. I never understood why she thinks that learning a language can be an easy process that we would have conjugations down in a week
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Gomez is an very nice person and I believe her intentions are pure, but she falls short on many aspects of teaching. Her course is very difficult for a 101 class. She expects you to know the material very quickly and wants you to have full blown conversations. Just take another language...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is the absolutely worst professor I have ever had. I suggest if there is another teacher take them instead. She is beyond unreasonable, she's the type of teacher to assign something to you and not understand herself and the call you out for not understanding. UMBC should do a better job in auditing their professors.

She expects us to make our whole life around her class. For example if you work on the weekend as almost every college student does, it will not work with her class as we have projects, quizzes, coversifis due all in one week. And for conversifi we have to spend so much money or spend alot of time to get a token which rarely happens. DO NOT TAKE.

Professor Gomez is a tough professor, I won't lie about that. There are a lot of assignments due in a week and it is expected you keep up on them but you know about them far in advance. Attendance was HW, participation, and the discussion board after class. She corrects you out loud yes, but it is to help you learn. You will learn a lot from her!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Quite literally the worst professor this entire country has ever seen. I wanted to blow my head off every MWF sitting in a 50 minute class. Her attendance policy is quite the worst, have 9 absences and your grade drops by an entire letter grade, this may seem bad until you see that causes an "absence" , eg. not doing 1/1000 weekly assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Avoid her if you can. She expects constant in class participation for attendance but will yell at you if your Spanish is not perfect. Will change guidelines for assignments often, sometimes hours before said assignment is due. Lots of work and very condescending.

Awful class. Shes gives way to much qork for a beginner class, expects you to know everything, and changes rubrics/grading criteria last minute or after the assignment has already been turned in. You cant get anything wrong or she will call you out in front of the entire class and is so condescending.

DO NOT TAKE HER CLASSES. After having dealt with a semester of her buffoonery I cannot fathom how she is still trusted as an educator. She expects every student to have mastered the content PRIOR to lecturing rather than actually teaching us. The amount of work she assigns, attendance policy, attitude towards students and so much more. Good luck.

The study plan each week can be extensive on top of other work so there is lots of homework/studying. Professor Gomez is always available by email and willing to let you make up on work you may have missed but only under certain circumstances.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Gomez makes her expectations very clear from the beginning. She is very accessible and responds to emails very quickly. She expects a lot but does her best to accommodate students with extenuating life circumstances that may get in the way of their education. I recommend anyone to take this class but be prepared to work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I transferred to UMBC and noted the language requirement. But Professor Rubio has been the worst professor I've ever seen. She makes up reasons to mark you absent from class, even if you sit through her entire lecture. For a 101 class, she expects you to know so much in just 1-day intervals! I couldn't imagine taking her again. Avoid it honestly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Gomez-Rubio was completely unprepared, posed assignments with less than 24 hours notice for completion, expected classes on national holidays to be made up, and extremely impatient. She counts people absent for tons of reasons out of the student's control, and drops a letter grade for absences that she creates.

Professor Gomez is one of the best teachers I had at UMBC. She is indeed a tough grader, however, if you do all the assigned work and you participate during class it will make everything easier. She is always willing to meet with students whenever they have questions or concerns.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Profe Gomez-Rubio is such a great help when learning a foreign language. She expects vocabulary to be at least somewhat memorized before class, then in class she focuses on conjugating and using vocabulary in practical examples. The Conversifi section of the course is intimidating at first, but I never had a bad experience with any of the coaches.

Professor Gomez has really thorough slides that are on Blackboard & gone over in class. The weekly Study Plans helps a lot too. Orals are via Conversifi so we get to practice with someone in a Hispanic country through video call. If you really want to learn Spanish, take her class. She cares a lot & is very helpful and generous with her students.
Worst teacher ever taken. Very rude. Not flexible whatsoever. Very unrealistic.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: DO NOT take her if you want to pass your class. Her carelessness regarding grading resulted the difference between a letter grade for me.

If you take 102, be prepared to work like never before. Tremendous amount of online homework with short period of time, writing, conversation with spanish speakers, exams. But dont be scared, just study hard and do all those on time, you be alright.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Tough grader even for winter classes, and I know spanish

Spanish at UMBC is demanding but it is expected. The assignments were awkward, such as video-chatting with a native Spanish speaker and the exams can be tough if you don't study. Professor Gomez is sweet but she can be abrasive. Study hard and attend every class and you can definitely pass. She is very lenient on grades at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: First, do yourself the favor and DO NOT take Spanish with her. She is unreasonable for a 101 level class and expects you to know 200 material pretty fast. Test are hard and all free answer, so you have to know your stuff. Attendance is basically mandatory and you work with a partner also very class. Also required to do assignments due on weekends.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She wasnt particularly hard, but I did not enjoy her class. She doesnt have a very organize system of learning and everything is basically work from the textbook. Theres so much partner work and its basically what you do all class.

Only 4 extra credit opportunities always on Wednesdays. Attendance is mandatory, online homework is super easy and you can do as much as you wants as early as you want. She expects you to learn the material outside of class and come in and review it in class. Must be prepared for the journals with the pre-writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Her class is easy if you do your work. I spent an hour or two a week doing the homework and reviewing the vocabulary. I see why people complain about her, but they complain because they don't want to work for a grade. Not how college works.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I have taken 300's classes that are easier than Professor Gomez class. She makes the class unnecessary hard for no real benefit. Unless you're looking for a really hard and challenging Spanish class, don't take her.

Is not clear while lecturing. Goes over material once and if you ask a question or if you dont understand, she acts irritated. I have learned more from the book and internet videos than I have from her. Her English isn't great, which makes understanding her answers difficult. In short, SHE DOES NOT MAKE SENSE.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She doesn't really teach.  Profe Gomez just hands out a bunch of pieces of classwork and makes you do them without ever teaching the content. Plus, you cannot use the book either. This leaves you constantly confused. Also, she is a very subjective grader. Honestly I have learned nearly nothing in this class, which is far from the standard at UMBC.

Please do not take her class. She has terrible English, doesn't teach, changes due dates, grades harshly, and is just generally a horrible professor. She makes the course so much more difficult and confusing than it needs to be.
- Attendance was taken every class - Attendance and Participation was 10% of the grade   - Participation is required.

She is plain and simply a bad teacher. I absolutely would avoid taking spanish with this woman. I explained to her I was confused and having trouble and she told me to drop the class. Do not take class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Gomez is really dub honestly. This class is literally an extension of 102, so if you took that you know EXACTLY what you expect. Same kind of lectures, group/ partner work, unnecessary homework, etc. But you can get away with anything with Gomez and she always makes you dance to Pitbull or something so good luck with that...

I LOVE Profesora Maria! She's hilarious, plus really wants you to leave her class with the fundamentals and cares if you actually learn. I took her class at AACC, and literally wanted to follow her to UMBC! She's great! Buy and READ your text, pay attention and participate in class. STUDY the material when she gives it and you'll surely get an A!

Took her class at AACC- Absolutely loved Profesora Maria. She is absolutely hilarious and really tries to make learning another language easy and fun.  She is a tough grader, but only because she expects you to really try in her course. If I decide to continue Spanish, I will definitely be taking her again!

She's got a lot of personality! Be prepared for lots of homework, and be sure to participate. Not uncommon for several important assignments to be due at once, and deadlines can be pretty random change without much notice. She's usually very sweet and funny, but rarely might jump down your throat  for little reason. Also, she makes you dance!

I could have gotten an A had I turned one of my homework in on time. She's ok though. Has an accent but we could all basically understand her. Has these discussion boards though where you have to work in groups and those SUCK. Exams  are straight forward. Show up to class and you'll get a C, do the discussion boards and score ok on exams its a B.

Profesora Gomez definitely expects a lot out of her students, and I worked a lot harder in this class than I expected to. She can definitely be hard to understand at times but is happy to answer questions. Sort of crazy but in a good way- she keeps things interesting. She even tried to make everyone dance during the final!

Took this class as a condensed summer class. If you really study, it's not difficult. Profesora is as helpful as a person can be. She is a native speaker and does have an accent, but if you PAY ATTENTION she is very easy to understand. We had some HW before going over the topic in class which meant more effort to read the book and figure it out.

Hands down, the BEST Spanish teacher I have ever had! Lots of class activities and partner work. She is very good with introducing new concepts and gives a lot of hand outs for practice.We review before EVERY quiz and exams are super easy. Lots of online work involved, but if you show up every day, participate, and do the work, you will have an A:)

Profesora Gomez is a great teacher. She expects a lot from you. One thing others did not note was that she is told to give assignments and projects by the MLL department. It is not her choice. As long as you do the assignments in the manner she requests and show up to every class, you will be fine. I have a 97%. Work hard and you will be rewarded.

Profesora Gomez is hard on those when it comes to late work, missing a class, and when you need information relayed to you cause of it. DONT MISS CLASS. She explains everything thoroughly and the class in general isnt that hard. But there is a lot of tedious work you need to do. its not hard its TEDIOUS

Maria Gomez-Rubio expects you to work and work HARD. The department wants you to do a lot in a 201 course but Gomez-Rubio does nothing to help except pile on more work. She was great and really funny the first day and then awful the rest of the semester. She has a good heart, but I would highly recommend that you avoid her at any cost possible.

Unrealistic expectations and course load.Try hard for a C, probably get a D. Told class she will fail people that dont understand even if you try. Youre here to teach not threaten. Fix the problem dont just fail people because your entire department is inept. Got a B –I tried so hard I struggled in my real major classes and didnt have time for them
Worst Spanish Professor EVER. Spends tons of times to speak herself about trivial things. NOT TEACHES. Unfair grader. Explains NOT clearly. DO NOT TAKE HER.

Worst class I have ever taken. I hope you're not planning on taking ANY other classes along with Spanish 201. She barely understands English and assigns more homework and activities than some of the upper level BIO or PSYCH courses I have taken. She has no concept of what a reasonable course load should look like relative to the level of the class.
Terrible teacher and very hard to understand. Avoid this class.

She is very nice and makes the class exciting. She's funny and optimistic but she does expect a lot from you. She gives out A LOT of work mainly becuase she wants you to take the class seriously. Do the work and participate and you will be fine.

Professor Gomez is great! She really cares about her students, and you have to do a lot of work. Learning another language is tough, and Professor Gomez made Spanish very exciting. TAKE HER COURSE if you really want to learn Spanish. Take someone else if you are only looking for an underserved A. You have to earn your grade is her class.

There's a LOT of work assigned in this class, but DONT WORRY it's still pretty easy. She explains and sometimes even has the entire class go through it. It's a pretty nice class and sometimes she is funny. I'd recommend. All the Spanish teachers in this school have been a blast!

I really enjoyed having senora Gomez as my spanish profesor! She is a very sweet lady if you work hard in her class. Attendance is VERY important. I took this class only for the GEP requirement. There is a lot of work and projects to do, but if you try your best she will likely give you a good grade.

I have never written reviews for an instructor in my four years of college, but I feel it's my obligation to warn students about her. In short, disorganized and a poor English speaker. Communication is difficult, and she IS NOT willing to work with students that struggle with the language. If at all possible avoid this professors classes.

There is a lot of busy work in this class, but it's meant to help you understand the material. There is a bit of a language barrier, but she is sweet and helpful and definitely wants to see all of her students pass. Make sure to attend class and participate.

She is a very good professor and an incredible person.  Talk to her outside of class because she has an amazing journey to where she is now.  The class has a LOT assigned material and you will not pass if you miss too many classes (but thats MLL policy).  She wants you to do well and will help you even when it is not convinient for her.

Always very nice and energetic. Honestly, it's not that much work. A good amount ends up counting as extra credit. If you are an active participator, she will be more likely to let you turn things in late/accept extra absences (and really, just raise your hand 3-5 times a class to answer questions). She's really a sweetheart and wants you to pass.
