reviews.comment: Dr. Vetter begins this class by sharing you will sign a contract for the grade you want (so weird) I signed the B. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Dr. Vetter is a nice person but she does not teach this class well. It is an excessive amount of work, unorganized and unprepared in class. Don't waste your time with this class. Find a better professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Vetter seems nice when you first meet her but she is incredibly difficult to deal with and grades based on a convoluted and confusing system. She also failed to respect my university-approved disability accommodations, claiming that the way her class is set up already accounts for them, but this is not true. She is one of the worst professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: never knew how to run discussions, either contributing way too much or way too little and was really inflexible and somewhat passive aggressive over email when trying to sort out technical issues; the content itself was interesting though, so if you enjoy political philosophy then still worth considering this class

I'm shocked by these reviews. I loved her class and I loved her! Although the texts were a bit difficult to understand bc of how old the texts were, her presentations/lectures clearly explained them. Her quizzes were quick and easy and she gives you 2 chances for each. Exams are just past exam questions. Try your best and you will do just fine!

As opposed to lectures, she'd assign us two or three videos that would sometimes go up to an hour and a half long (each!) that I had to watch on 2x speed because of slow she'd speak. The audio on them was also terribly quiet, her quizzes were often confusing and she took ages to grade anything (we didn't have any grades in for the several weeks)

Dr. Vetters grading is bizarre, she is typically very unprepared, and assigns a lot of work. She only gives full credit on assignments that go 'above and beyond,' took 9 weeks to submit any grades for a weekly assignment, and in the last 2 weeks of class we had due 2 12 slide voicethreads, an 8 page and a 5 page paper.

I agree with the views of Professor Vetter. She is not very good with technology. Her quizzes are very confusing. Her lecture videos are boring and long, but helpful. However, her audio is terrible. She responds to emails late and waits until after the semester to grade everything. To those who'll be taking her class, I wish you the best of luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Confusing class because Prof Vetter is not very tech savvy. She forgets to upload assignments and then is confused. She also takes forever to grade so you will not know your grade until after the semester. She uploads videos explaining the readings but her monotone voice makes it a very hard watch. She is nice but her teaching style is boring.

A lot of readings; all the lectures are pre-recorded. The volume is horrible, and she yawns through them constantly. Quizzes associated with every reading/lecture; question wording is not very clear. Three VoiceThreads; feedback is right before due dates and vague. Responds to emails late, very few announcements. Do in-person or not at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: To start off she is really disappointing. When to try to ask for help on an assignment all she has to say is "We're all doing the best we can" and makes random jokes "Hehehe". Can't believe she assigned a whole project of 8 pages on top of a final exam essay (2 pages) that includes a voice thread all during finals week. Dont take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was time consuming for an asynchronous class. We had to watch videos and it was always very difficult to hear what she said and the quizzes we were given would be worded so strangely and would confuse everyone. We had VoiceThread activities and a lot of the feedback we got was very vague. The final exam MC part are old quiz questions

The reviews here are TRUE. She grades very late and responds to emails late. Not sure what she does in her free time but it isn't grading. She is assigning a whole analysis project ON TOP OF A FINAL EXAM THAT VERY WEEK. She posts assignments late minute. There are weekly writing prompts and lectures due each week. Won't take her again ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: A lot of reading and her video lectures go in circles like theorists do, extensive weekly journals. Boring and very discussion heavy. you get points for everything and the exams are extremely demanding, she asks for a lot of precision which is extremely difficult considering how abstracts the theories are. Tends to push her own narrative at times.

She is an ok professor, her recorded lectures are boring and lengthy. The quizzes are a bit hard since there is only one right answer. I'm taking her again because her exams are online so it saves the anxiety. She responds to emails late and her teaching is inconsistent. Wish there was a better professor in this department but I don't know any.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Vetter is a great as a person going to her office hours will help a lot. My class was not in person. most of the work was at my own pace. The issue is that I didnt know my final grade until the end of the year when final grades were posted. I was worried because I was right the boarder between and A and a B so deal with that at your risk.

The class is good to take if you are a Poli Sci major. However, the readings and the lectures were so vague and hard to understand. The quizzes style: are all good answers but there is ONE best answer. there would be assign. due the same week. felt like a 300/400 lev.course. thought I was doing good in this course. there goes the dean's list.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The course was asynchronous and the pre-recorded lectures were very helpful but she constantly yawned in them which was distracting. The weekly quizzes were way more difficult than they could have been and I would suggest watching lectures before reading as the language is very difficult. You will need the textbook to pass the course.

Dr Vetter is a really caring person who will bend over backwards to help students. If you try to do the few readings she assigns a week, do the minimal assignment requirements per week and at least try to keep notes going throughout the semester you'll be prepared for exams. Easy grader if you prepare to put in minimal effort. Easy A.

Im actually sad to give her this rating because she's a nice person and the subject matter was interesting. But she was so disorganized and inefficient. Posted assignments at an untimely basis. Her exams are ridiculous: timed long essays and a 10 page paper due at the same time. So much reading. Never responds to emails. Grades very late.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The readings are really long & difficult so you're better off just watching the lectures instead where she guides you through them, the lectures are dense but extremely helpful. Her powerpoints are disorganized though so you NEED to use the reading guide and fill it out with detailed notes throughout the lecture-exams are heavily based off of them.

Honestly I was really disappointed with this class. Prof Vetter is kind and knowledgable but her midterm and final were so hard and she assigned a 10 pg paper on top of the final with barely any heads up. Our discussions were short and we always ran out of time. You teach yourself most of the material.. wouldn't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Nice professor but she talks extremely quiet and is nearly impossible to understand during lectures. Unnecessary amount of reading assigned each week and the assignments are often posted late. The readings are difficult to understand and very boring to follow. Exams are online but questions are timed and very lengthy. Not worth the headache.

This professor was a bit all over the place for me. She was very disorganized with her notes as she would put random key words all over the board with no explanation. The textbook is a definite must have. The way to get through this class is taking notes on literally everything she says in class, even if you didnt read. All the exams are online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Nice woman but probably didn't have much business teaching this class at least. Basically every class was a structure-less lecture. She would have a power-point up but it was just small little notes only she would understand to guide her through her "lecture". The TA Gracie Bradford was much more knowledgeable. Everyone learns from the textbook.

Great discussions of different political theorists. Application papers (graded for completion only) make you think about each reading to formulate your thoughts on each author. Unit papers let you choose the theorist you want to write about. Final paper totally open ended - you choose the topic AND relevant theorists.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lisa Vetter is by far the best professor I have ever had. She encourages discussion and is totally open to listening to you as long as you can back up your points. This is a great starting point for anyone who wants to learn more about Political Philosophy.

Small class, made for great discussions. Highly interactive, participation important. Projects tie theories to actual issues. Variety of authors who often disagree presents multiple points of view. Learned a lot! Great prof.

The theories may be old but you learn to apply them to modern day issues - that's the basis for her graded group application activities and the FINAL EXAM. 3 unit exams deal with the theories only. No papers to write, but a 5-minute reaction writing every class. Is there to help - but YOU have to ASK. Lectures interesting & fun, but can run long.

She is funny, witty and a wonderful woman. She's great teacher and I would take another class with her. This class isn't tough but it's not the easiest either. Reading is essential because she assigns a quiz (online) for each new philosopher.  Lectures are useful especially when it comes time to her tests which are okay. Do you work and you'll pass

I had Dr. Lane in fall '25 and I loved his lectures! I took his class for the gen-ed credit and because I was very interested in the course (compsci major lol). Def look over the powerpoints, all of the test questions come from that and the group wksts. The extra credit was very generous and helps a bunch if you get points off on tests/wksts. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS UNLESS YOU MUST. Professor Lane assumes every student is as insanely interested in the content of the course as he is and creates his exams as such. Participating in class basically guarantees you a C but prepare to fail every exam unless you spend an obscene amount of time reading the textbook and preparing for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I took professor Lanes ARCH 200 class and I liked it. While I barely got by with a C, the class is interesting and professor Lane is a nice, smart guy. He jokes around a bit in class and is an overall pretty decent professor. He is kinda strict on grading and his lectures are dense. The class itself is hard, so I think his rating is a littleee low.

GOAT, so passionate bro, love him, wish I could go to Greece with him for the digs and I'm not even doing anything for archaeology, art, or culture like that bro... he is genuinely the goat idk what to tell you
I lowkey didn't do the readings and still did amazing cuz his lectures are so interesting, go to his class bro, he is just the best

I took this class as a gen ed and had absolutely no interest in the topic. Prof understands that most students feel the same way in this class and adds a lot of humor to lectures. He is very approachable and even 2 years after I took the class we still say hi and chat when we cross paths. Only complaint is that his handwriting is difficult to read.

Overall, decent guy. He Makes the class fun due to his high energy and enthusiasm for his work. HOWEVER, get ready to read, in ARCH 100 there are so many terms you need to memorize in order to be successful. He provides enough resources for Exams but no study guide... rather you must look over past PowerPoints.

unless you like reading, hard tests, and critical thinking, do NOT take this class. he's an absolute a-hole to his students and answers questions with a question. stopped reading stuff after week 2 because I was in 3 other classes and still passed with an A (barely). he's a tough grader and just likes to hear himself talk. awful do not take
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This course is ideal for archaeology majors. The energetic professor loves teaching Greek and genuinely wants students to succeed. While passing the class isn't hard, many fail. Instead of curving grades, he assigns extra work to balance scores. If you need a culture credit, consider another course. But if you like challenges this class is perfect.

I found his class very interesting, and it's one of the classes where you can really tell the Professor is enthusiastic about their field. I took this class for the culture credit, but it's not a good choice if you're looking for an easy A. 
We had about one homework per week, and the final paper is a easy way to bring your grade up at the end.

A lot of people may have not liked this class, but I enjoyed it. The lectures had a lot of information, but Mr. Lane highlighted the important stuff and even had slides with main idea questions and vocabulary, both of which I used to study for exams. It also helped that for each exam, we got to use an index card as a cheat sheet.

The exams can be tough, it was especially tough for me since I'm bad with memorizing information like this however just like all classes you get better after the first exam if you study back on them and use your cheat sheet that he lets you use to your advantage. His final cumulative exam was extremely easy which bumped up my grade from a C to B.

This class is not an easy gen ed to take for your arts and humanities credit. Do not take if you want it just for a credit. You have to study and memorize slides and understand the content. He is also a yapper he yaps a lot. Tests are hard. very hard. Also there's homework every week. You can't miss a class at all.

I will say this once, and once only. If you choose to take this class… you better be super smart and able to retain A LOT of information because the lectures and material that is required is insanely challenging. As someone who does great in classes like this, this was by far one of, if not the hardest class i've ever taken. proceed with caution.

I see a lot of reviews complaining about this class's difficulty as a 100lvl. To pass this class you literally just need to listen and do brief readings. Most of the material needed for tests is *very* clearly labeled on lecture slides. He constantly tells you in lecture if something will be important for exams. Just don't try to cram.

Dr Lane is great guy y but as a teacher he is the worst, he is so trapped in his own bubble he does not understand the burden he puts on his students in his world this is the only class were taking his course load is egregious and test are impossible anyone saying this class is for majors is wrong i'm a major and the others  with me are struggling

If you really read these ratings, they are mostly about his PERSONALITY and not his TEACHING style. This class is meant for ancient studies majors and not just for an easy A, there are easier culture credits you can take. The course name/ work is very misleading and nothing like what you think. Please take my warning.

Nice person, NOT a good professor! Test are extremely difficult and he always rambles while you're taking exams which is annoying and if you're thinking of taking this class as a Arts and Humanities requirement, DON'T. It WILL tank your grade. Only thing good was that homework assignments were graded on completion. Attendance was required.

Fantastic Professor, lots of energy, good at teaching, however the tests are HARD, for a 100 class the difficulty is high, and requires lots of studying and memorizing. If you want to take this class for your GPA I wouldn't suggest it, but you will enjoy the professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr.Lane is an amazing professor. I sat in the front, recorded every lecture, did all the homework, took detailed notes, and still failed. . Dr.Lane is extremely kind and intelligent and the fact that I failed says more about me then him. I will say, it is the hardest class I've ever taken and it is a 100 level. I will be retaking this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor, extremely enthusiastic, flexible and all around great lecture. Professor taught material well and demonstrated knowledge of material.
For a 100 level course, it is WAY too hard. Extremely passive agressive person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Lane is an amazing professor! He's really fun to talk to and is incredibly smart and well-spoken. He's always very passionate when teaching but be sure to memorize for tests and pay attention during lectures or you may miss something. Offers extra credit opportunities and makes you earn your grade. Would def take again.

Professor Lane is a very knowledgeable professor. He's very passionate about archaeology and is very lax. I would say that this course isn't geared well toward people not majoring in Archaeology. It definitely takes some prior knowledge and/or heavy research and studying to completely understand everything. Attending lectures is the most important.

He's a great teacher, easygoing, funny, and wicked smart. Best professor I expect to have. This course is an information load that includes a lot of work and memorization. Stay on top of the lecture material, do the homeworks thoroughly and review them well before tests. Tough course, but with hard work you'll do fine.

You can tell he cares, but he gives a lot lot LOT of homework and classwork. Your homework are the answers to quizzes, but doesn't give personal feedback nor direct feedback. The info he does give is in riddles and not very useful. MAKE SURE YOU BUY THE BOOK! Overall, he cares, but doesn't have my style of learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Prof. Lane is great! He will make you work for your grade, and expect a lot of readings and weekly lectures. Attendance is also mandatory but he is really flexible and willing to work with you as long as you talk to him. Would take again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Lane makes archaeology fun and interesting. I am an engineering major who usually has professors with very minimal verbal communication skills so he was a breath of fresh air. He obviously cares about his students and emphasizes the important material. Overall I was excited to attend lectures, even in pandemic end-times. :)

I needed an elective as I am a MechE major. Loved Prof. Lane as a person! But he was a terrible lecturer. He often went on tangents explaining his experience in X country, the tests were INSANE. If you are NOT A HISTORY PERSON DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. The class is scrambled and you wont pass if you skip lecture. Take a SOCY or something else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! Super kind and funny, really knowledgeable and passionate about his field of study. Only 1 4-5 page essay. Takes attendance and there are classwork grades, so come to class. Gives really helpful study guides before exams, fill them out and study them and you'll be good

He's a really cool guy who's very knowledgable in his field. It didn't feel like a 100 level course at times because of the material/concepts but he color codes what you need to know for the test and his study guides are really helpful. A challenging class but if you come to class and take notes on the lecture you will be fine!

His power points are worthless. There is not enough information on them to help you study for the exams. However, he is a very nice guy and he tries to make his class as exciting as possible but its hard to because pottery is not an exciting topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Lane as a person. As a prof, he caters to future archeologists and grades toughly due to that. He gives extra credit and wants his students to do well, but his tests are a bear. Scour your textbook and notes to memorize details and even then knowing all the info to get an A might be difficult. Take him if you want to be an archeologist.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Pros: Ivy league quality. Cons: Ivy league difficulty.

Prof. Lane is an amazing lecturer. Class is mandatory because he does group work and you get the credit by being there, not by completing the work. His powerpoints and the stuff he puts online are basically the tests, he color codes what is important. Easy A if you study and pay attention. He is just a classy guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Intro to archeology. Fantastic lectures, didn't really use the book. Come to lecture & listen or take notes. Test questions underlined in powerpoints and posted online. Very approachable and friendly with students. Had a crush, sat in the front, listened to everything, would have been an easy A if I hadn't forgotten about a test.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: As long as you keep up with posted readings for discussion and use your book to study you'll be fine. Dr. Lane can be intimidating since he seems to know everything there is to know, but he grades pretty generously. Take advantage of activities outside of class as well as his office hours. You'll learn a lot. And he's a great connection to have.

I absolutely loved this class. Attendance isn't mandatory but he's a great lecturer. If you don't attend you're just making the class that much more difficult for yourself. I never read the book, but if you pay attention to lecture and review the powerpoints he posts you'll excel. I only got a B because I forgot about a test and didn't review.

Michael Lane is very good at projecting his voice( to the point where he doesn't even use a mic ), he makes jokes, and even though he knows students won't respond, he is always happily exclaiming good afternoon when he enters the lecture hall. He is willing to help any who approach, and is overall very friendly. Would take his class again.

Dr. Lane is extremely well spoken , and his lectures are absolutely necessary for whatever course you're taking. Enthusiastic and helpful, Dr. Lane gives extremely helpful resources in order to pass his tests and assignments. Would not recommend for non-majors, unless you are good at memorization.

great instructor if your major is archaeology, but he is extremely enthusiastic about the topic and gives wayyyyyy too much work if you're just taking it for your general art credit. wouldn't recommend taking this

He's a good professor. He's very into what he does. His tests are very difficult. He even admitted this to the class after the semester was over, and admitted that the grading data was similar to an upper level class. He promptly curved the class. He's tough, lots of reading, but good.

Dr. Lanes Arch 100 class is one of the tougher 100 level course because of the amount of memorization and detail on the test. If you, at the very least, skim the reading, go over his PowerPoint notes and glance over his optional reading questions, you can easily pass his tests. If you expect this class to be a breeze, you are sadly mistaken.
Great teacher. Really loves what he teaches. Projects his voice loud and clear. Don't take this class for a gen ed because his test are extremely difficult.

Dr. Lane is a very knowledgeable professor. However, his lectures are extremely overly-complicated and can really disinterest you real quickly. If you have interest in Archaeology, then this is the class for you, otherwise, find a different class for Arts & Humanities or you will hate this class to death. Lots of random information thrown at you.

I honestly do not know HOW he has such a high rating. Maybe he's a better professor in his upper level classes, but he expects WAY too much out of a 100-level course. He expects you to remember every tiny detail that comes out of his mouth - it's more of a HISTORY course than an archaeology course. Do yourself a favor and don't take ARCH100.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS if you want an easy A for a general requirement. He expects you to memorize the slightest details of what he says in class. He gives study guides, but they are very vague considering the amount of details he expects you to memorize for the test. I wasted so much time studying for this class which isn't even part of my major.

Although this course had a lot of memorization and note taking, Professor Lane was so sweet! He is very caring towards his students and wants everyone to do well! Don't take this class if you don't want to work, however it's very easy to pass if you try!

Dr Lane is a fantastic lecturer and a great teacher for UMBC to have. He is passionate in his archaeology and very professional. I went to his office hours before every test, and he helped me clarify ideas. He was everything you can ask for from a professor. The class Arch 100 itself is a memory test, be aware!

Professor Lane is an awesome professor! However, his tests and the class itself is very hard. You must go to class and pay attention and take notes on everything he says to do well. Tests are all short answer, no multiple choice. Lane is very knowledgeable and interesting!

I loved him! He was very knowledgable and seemed passionate about what he was teaching. He gave extra points on the tests to help improve grades, and he always made study guides. I found the classes interesting even though he sometimes spoke a little too quickly. Overall, I thought he was a reasonable professor.

Professor Lane is extremely knowledgeable.  He throws a lot of information at you in class, but it's not too hard to keep up with if you take notes and pay attention.  He is EXTREMELY helpful during his office hours and wants to see you succeed. He even gave me an essay question that would be on the test, just because I came to his office for help.
Professor Lane is awesome, he is extremely knowledable in his craft and will give you alot of good bar travia too but he expects alot so don't be that guy.

Professor Lane is extremely knowledgeable and helpful.  He's charismatic and wants the students to do well, but he also expects you to put effort into class too.  You can't get by without taking notes in this class, or you will fail, though if you can't find something in your notes or his powerpoints, he's very helpful during office hours.

Hands down the most charismatic professor at this school. In his class, no cell phones are present; 50 people crammed into a room are spellbound by his flawless diction and well prepared lectures. Dr Lane has been to all of the locations of Greek lore, and his no nonsense style of teaching ensures an effective learning environment. Also gnarly tats

Hard professor, but knowledgeable. Do not take this class if you want an easy A, though an A can be achieved with hard effort. Some material is interesting, some is very dry. Nice guy, but hard tests. His study guides are sometimes not so consistent with his tests, and he has a love for details, so you have to memorize to the heart. Use the guides.

Not the sort of intro class I had in mind. Very detailed and the tests are incredibly hard, he talks down to you because he's an archaeologist and you're not. Do yourself a favor a skip this class if you don't have hours and hours to study for an INTRO class...so annoying.

This is not an easy A class. The material is very hard to understand. He goes over the material too quickly in class. Gives a study guide before the exam. Do the study guide and you will get a B on the exam. He expects the student to write in excessive details on the exam for the essay questions.However, he is very helpful if you are having trouble
Not easy, difficult to concentrate in class because of the rambling. From now on always check ratemyprofessor.com to get the best professors.

Professor Lane was a great professor but the material is a little dry. He provides study guides that are basically the test. The one problem is he expects certain things in each exam answer. So if you miss one part that the question really didn't ask, you will lose some points. Still was a slightly interesting  class.

He gives you everything you need, exams come from questions on handouts, which he gives answers to in lecture. He does go off on a lot of linguistic tangents, but some of them are interesting. Study a little and get an A, or do nothing (but whine and complain) like the others and get a B. The one textbook is painful to read, art book is good.
He's hard to follow and talks too fast. Its hard to take notes. Class is boring.
he gives the hand-outs of the powerpoints so the students could take notes as he goes through the slides in class. the class is boring but the professor is nice not to mention pretty cute.

If you don't attend the lectures it's your funeral. Conceptual focus, memorization heavy, some short algebraic proofs expected. Tough tests and quizzes just from how much is on them -- even when I didn't get stuck I never had time to go back and check my answers. Illuminated lin alg for me, but I found it hard to keep up. Rounded me up to an A.

He expects you to watch MULTIPLE 70+ min lecture videos before class and then proceeds to yap during his supposed "lectures". He doesn't give you time to process what he's teaching or break it down for you in class, he runs through practice problems at lightning speed and says "good enough." No practice exams, it's just you and the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: unreasonably difficult exams not like the quizzes. Very unpredictable. got a 94 on his first midterm. then studied 12+ hours for the second one. I'm PRAYING I got a 65. Only reason I'm not dropping is bc I had lenient TA quiz graders. and I did well on the first exam. Completely ruined my chance for an A. Might even get a C.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: My dog would have taught calc 3 better than him. If you need practice exam to study there none as the only thing is the textbook and his lecture. His exam are multi choice but no partial credit and there hard as he LOVE put in trig in. Did I also mention he love his own voice. Before the exam he yap for 10-20 min and the question are long too.
Just no a good professor

I can't stress enough how misleading the very small pool of reviews are. I assume there are only this many because everyone else who might've left one refused at the thought of seeing his name alone. Take any other professor, only then can you "visualize" a decent lecture and course.

Words don't describe how bad he is when people say 0 practice, literally 0 practice. Like, I kid you not, it's like learning to swim and the instructor says, "Dude, just read how to swim." Like, did I not pay you to teach that????
So slow think's he's funny and kind of mean.
Worst experience of my life

I've never seen a more disorganized professor. Practice exams Nope. Practice quizzes Nope. Decent lecture notes Absolutely not. He posts videos, not even lecture notes.

You will be examined and quizzed on the book, not his teachings, because he doesn't even no what he's doing; he's just talking, and he loves his own voice.

I had never taken a college math class before since I was in my first semester, and this was not the easiest class to start with. Muscedere spends a lot of time on some things and not enough on others and it makes for confusion, but as long as you study and work ahead of the class in the text book, you will understand his lectures.

Pretty good professor for a pretty hard class. Exams are ~1/2 multiple choice, so credit is all or nothing for that section. TA's were very helpful. Best way to study for exams is doing the recommend textbook practice problems. Lectures can be kinda fast paced, but uploads video lectures where he goes slower and more in-depth. STUDY!Calc 3 is hard

If you're not a good test-taker I would avoid this class, tests & quizzes are about 80% of your grade. Prof Muscedere is good, but he often runs through practice problems and just says "good enough". The TA's are somewhat helpful, but get ready to learn a lot of the material outside of class. If you're good at math you might be fine.

Do NOT take this prof, or this class at UMBC. You will fight for your life just to get a 70% in the class. Half the class is currently failing (exam 3 is coming up soon), and everyone is teaching themselves. TA's are trying to salvage the situation but prof does not heed their recommendations. This 4 credit class turned into 8 credits of work.

Fantastic guy, and extremely passionate about what he teaches. He wants you to succeed. His lectures are fast-paced and it can be easy to fall behind, but if you put in the work and go to class, you should be fine. If you have a good TA, they'll be a lifesaver. Check WebAssign weekly; he sometimes forgets to put the homework on Blackboard.

I think he's a nice/funny professor but I just couldn't learn from him. He would fly by lectures pretty fast and he won't even take the time to explain it. I heard more than half of the students withdrew from his class because everyone was failing. I would not recommend taking him if math isn't your strong suit.

He isn't hard, I just couldn't learn from him. Nice guy, but I was thoroughly confused. Pay attention to and practice class problems because they'll show up on quizzes and tests. DO THE PREREQ EXAM because it's basically free points. He changes grading in favor of students and will feed you out of his hand. I just didn't understand his lectures.

Doesn't lecture that well and the study material he provides was never of any help, ever. I was practically teaching myself the concepts the entire semester. Also had hour long video lectures in addition to the in person lectures that he wanted you to watch.
My main concern with him is that he does not respond to him emails. He barely gives you anything to help you study. You might as well learn the material on your own.

He seemed like a nice guy that tried to relate to the class and keep it upbeat but I found the lectures did not teach the material as he just went over example problems and skipped a lot of them. The discussion sections required with the class were the most helpful to me as long as you have a good TA. I would say he was average compared to others.

Was already going to leave a good review before I missed my final and he was gracious enough to let me make it up. Tough class but if you read and put the work in beforehand, lectures are very helpful/engaging & you get out what you put in. Hard teacher but I have a ton of respect for him, would absolutely take him again. Made me enjoy math again

Great guy, friendly and willing to help you if necessary. Also lenient with grading if you talk to him about it. The learning curve gets a little steep midway through but he's willing to help if necessary. Highly recommend, but lord is the homework an incarnation from hell. You will never experience a class with homework as awful as this one's.
kNOWLEDGEABLE BUT TOUGH TO UNDERSTANDE

Amazing Breadth of information, and shows how powerful Linear Algebra is. He emphasizes from the beginning that He wants you to pass. Please, take him up on that offer. His Quizzes are great, exams more than fair. and all he asks is that you attend class. Be a good student do your homework and come to class and you will pass with flying colors.

Very friendly and teaches the material in a very clear manner. Explains what will be on the quizzes and exams and guides you through the questions after passing them out. That being said, his homework is straight from the textbook and is incredibly frustrating and time consuming, especially with problems having you jump to older sections.
If you show up to class, do the work you'll get an A. He helps students with assignments too. Easy A for me.

I took math 155 in the summer. I have difficulty in math classes and  I  usually end up with D or F.  Because  the class was taught during the summer, materials were taught a bit fast pace. Make sure you study, do your homework and ask questions, go to tutors then you should be fine. Today, I am happy/proud to say that I passed the class.

100% great guy, who will do his best to make sure you pass. He get so excited about the subject and really engages the class. Stayed after class for hours to tutor students who still wanted help. He understands the textbook isn't very helpful, and he helps a lot on quizzes. BEWARE: He assigns more homework than you've ever known.

Nice introductory course. Eight lectures based on very thorough notes which are helpful to refer to after class. Homework assignments based off lecture are fair and reinforce concepts. Helpful professor, readily answers student questions and grades fairly. Great course, I recommend it to any math major!
If you attend class he really does his best to make sure you pass.
He is simply the worst I've ever had.  Take Riley instead if you must take 106
Good teacher, tough class
Very lenient and understanding. Corny at times but still fun. Helps you on quizzes and tests. He wants "all his students to pass his class".

Overall a very challenging class but learned a lot.  A bit fast paced, and had to race thru quizes/exams in order to complete on time, at the same time getting bogged down in row reduction.  Learn to do it FAST and ACCURATE.  Not sure about some previous comments.. grad students??  Reviews were interesting, but similar problems really not on exams.

Hard Class but Good professor. I think he can do much better on handling the material that is provided so he can avoid the want to be smart grad students. I believe they are the once who make the class harder. As far as for the professor, he is good and very helpful. His final is basically similar to previous cls exams but long.G2 his review sessio

Class is set up for you to do well.  If you do the homework and actually digest the work, you'll be fine in the class.  Helped out with grades as he wants you to do well.  Funny guy, enjoyable to go to class.

A good teacher, can help if you ask. Gives a lot of extra credit. The class is hard. The test average was around 44. but if you study hard, or at least do better than others, you will be rewarded. Got an A!!!

Muscedere is a great guy and always willing to help a student during his time before class. The class is hard and you will need to put in the effort to do well. HW was a lot, exams were OK and quizzes were not too bad. He does tend to fly through the material fairly quickly but his PowerPoints help reinforce that. Be repaired to put some time in!!

he is a great teacher. A little bit hard, but at the end curves according to student's standing in the class. SO you may do not very good, but later you will get an A or B. Always helps if you ask. Hard work is rewarded.

Muscedere is an interesting man, weird but interesting, he tries to help his students as best as he can but the class is still very hard. The average is like a 65, exams are tough, quizzes are bogus but overall he is a nice guy, but being a nice guy doesn't help you pass the class.
UGH... AVOID HIM. He's helpful... but can't teach.
No Comments

Teaches the class like everyone is a graduate student in Mathematics and expects people to understand it as fast as he can teach it.  Does not give clear lectures, only rewrites on the board what is in the textbook.  Even with a curve at the end half the class failed.  Unless you want to learn the information on your own avoid him.
Avoiding this guy is the key to passing Math251. DO NOT TAKE.

The instructor is suppose to do the exams him self and give the students three times the time it took him. The final was long and I am sure if given to any instructor who was not part of the creation it would take them more that 40 minutes to do the exam. The final exam consisted of 12 full problems with sub parts. Get ready for Flux calculations.
No Comments

Amazing teacher, he actually cares about his students and he really tries hard to get across extremely difficult concepts.  And there is apparently an adjusted grading scale that isn't on the syllabus, so if you think you're failing, you're probably not.

I've never gotten lower than an A in any math class I've ever taken... and because of this guys final exam, I will probably get a C. Most professors allow you to have an equation sheet for exams and this guy doesn't, so unless you want to memorize like 50 equations for 1 test avoid this guy.

Hmm.I think when u are at this level of math, the stuff is not easy at all.This professor i think has done an excellent job in trying to explain mind blowing concepts. He was always avaiable for help before and after class. Homework was lengthy but exam questions were similar to homework. One of the best professor for MAth 251 if u want to learn.

ok.. Muscedere is a special teacher. Everything he teaches is STRAIGHT out of the book ( same numbers, same examples..) and the way he teaches is not the best. The only way to pass this class with an A is to get the old exams!!!! trust me on that..

I always tried to get help and he told me he dint have office hours but apparently he did. He was a good teacher but his grading is very questionable and really punishes you even if you understand the concepts or even get teh answers right. I ended up with a B because the curve saved me.

He's tough, that is for sure. HOWEVER, he is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is fair and actually cares about the students. He WANTS you to learn, which is a very fare thing for professors. His homeworks are a bit lengthy...but, you will never be surprised on exams. He makes sure you have the knowledge you will actually need.

Some of the grading methods were questionable, like a small detail being worth a large percentage of the problem value. There were only 2 quizzes all semester, wish there were a few more to get a feel for the material and for preperation for exams. The teacher was really interested in the material, but seemed to focus on theEEparts attheendofclass

overall he is a nice guy.  even though his lectures are straight from the book, he adds in a few extra helpful notes once in a while.  the high intensity of the exams was not expected at first due to the laid back nature of the class lectures.  he is very generous with the curve.

Mr. Muscedere genuinely cares about his students and their success in his class. His main downfall was his negative self-talk, which started on the very first day. When he talks bad about himself he looses the respect of his students. I would give him a C+. If he didn’t talk bad about himself so much, I’d give him a B+.

He's a good professor.  Explains much better than most math professors.  He is extremely helpful.  He wants his students to succeed and understand the material.  His exam reviews are really helpful.  The material was very difficult, he really takes the time and tries to make it clear to everyone - most math professors don't do this.
over all, hes a pretty good teacher, he knows what is to be taught and what students have to learn. he tells exactly what question will be on the exam. funny guy too lol

He was an excellent professor and did a wonderful job. Whenever anyone needs help he is always available and makes a conscious effort to help the students pass. He practically gives everyone the exam and quiz questions prior to the dates and is just a great professor all around.

Would not recommend taking him.  Reads stright from the book, which anyone can do by themselves.  His lectures are absoulutly no help whatsoever.  He "tell's" you what's on exams, which can focus study time, but has extremely questionable grading.  Get a different proffessor or wait to take the class if you can!!!

boring to sit through, but it's just the subject. He teaches out of the book making it easier to do the homework problems he assigns us. He tells you what's on the exam so if u study u'll get a decent grade. Nice guy... not a bad class

seems like a nice guy but isnt a good teacher. reads word for word from the book. helpful reviews yet his grading is very questionable... you may get the right answer but if u dont do it exactly as they do in the book, he wont understand and therefore you are wrong. be prepared to teach urself the material b/c he simply recites the book to u.

Look..the bottom line is that he wants you to know Calc 3! Dont expect to memorize things and fly through the class. He is a GREAT person with positive intentions. I never liked him until I visited his office hours after failing 3 exams due to my own problems. He curves remakably b/c I have a C. Dont take this class unless ur ready to learn Calc 3!
this guy is a moron.  he knows less than you do about calc.  without the textbook he is lost and hopeless. exams are intense.
He's a good guy, tests are easy and he spells out exactly whats going to be on them. Lectures aren't the best, and hw is alittle long, but overall not bad.

rookie teacher. does evrything str8 outof the book. first exam is hell. rest get better only b/c evry1 fails the 1st 1 and for rest of the exams he tells u exactly wats on it. DO NOT miss the review sessions. I got an A, i thougt i had a C...curves big time (he has to, otherwise evry1 would fail.Be prepared 2 READ the book on u'r own. good luck
Horrible. Everything everyone above has said is true. I dropped the class for the exact same reasons. He is a horrific teacher. Don't take him; If you are taking him, Drop the class now!!!
No Comments
Nice guy, very friendly. Lectures are a litte boring, but he'll answer anything you ask him. Will tell you exactly what you need to know for tests. Not my first choice, but not too bad.
tests are nightmares, not a bad guy though
He is pretty frenetic for the first month or so. After the first mid-term he tones it down a lot. Ends up being pretty good.
I ended up with a B in his class. He's very downgrading and reads slides word for word with no examples.

If you have him drop him. THis is not only a very hard math class, but very useless to take with him. He reads straight from the book, which is horrible, and his test are crazy. Not to mention he is the worst personality professor i have ever had.
He must be the worst teacher...ever.  If you already added this, drop it before it's too late.  I cannot stress to you how bad of a teacher he is.

Horrible teacher, I had to drop this class because it was so difficult, homework is very easy as is everything in class then come the tests and quizzes that completly screw you. The class average was in the mid 60's when I dropped.

horrible... condescending and rude, thinks everything should be "obvious", says "See? That's easy, right!?" when it isn't. Quizzes/Tests 10x harder than homework. Expects mastery of calculus concepts.  My Class Avg = 64%

Horrible horrible teacher.  Completely unclear, even for someone who's always liked math.  Homework and quiz questions much harder than what we learned in class.  May as well just read the book...and even that isn't great...

Her lectures were easy and interesting at most times. She is very passionate with what she teaches, and It made the class much more enjoyable! She is super super friendly, and is overall a really well rounded professor. Class/lab assignments aren't hard or super time consuming and there are only two exams (midterm and final).

Really easy class, take this class for easy science lab credit. Professor McAllister does go off topic in some lectures but overall really nice and kind, no textbooks so exams are solely on lectures and labs. Labs also is fun, for lab reports just follow the guidelines and you should get a decent grade on it.

I love when professors care about teaching and want their students to learn. She is so passionate about what she does, and that always makes me want to put even more effort into any class. The class itself was pretty easy, and it was nice to see how much she cared about the material and the students.

Professor McAllister is very passionate and cares about her students. The class itself is easy; certain components (mainly the labs) are somewhat tedious but not hard. A great choice for a GEP course.

Good prof. Theres a lot of extra credit that no matter how you score on the midterm or final you should be at a A or a B. You are graded on attendance & participation so make sure to show up but besides that the class is easy. Their is a lot of work, but easy enough for a A so just pay attention.

Professor McAllister really does care for all her students and is insanely sweet; very understanding of circumstances and in any case, offers lots of extra credit opportunities. She's super passionate about what she teaches, and is also passionate on getting to know her students well. Please take her class!

Very passionate about the class even relating material to her own experiences. She truly wishes students to understand the fundamentals of science so even if they don't major in it they can still be educated enough to ask questions and understand others view points.

Class is easy overall. Professor is very passionate about what she teaches. Just go to lectures and study and the exams will be fine. Gives extra credit opportunities and participation points in class. Labs were not too hard and feedback is given on assignments

Lectures were very informative. Extra credit was a great boost to my grade. The workload was not crazy and most of the labs were quite simple. As long as you do the work before it is due and attend lecture, this class should be an easy A.
shes rly sweet .exams are hard study lectures. atendence is optional
shes so sweet. exams are hard so study and go to labs!!!!!!

I adore this professor so much! Her lectures are very reminiscent of secondary school lectures, which I really enjoyed. Has a great sense of humor and often told her own stories that connected back to the topic. Grading can be a bit tough, but she follows the rubric strictly on lab reports. Labs required groups, so be ready to work with others.
She is an extremely nice professor who is clearly passionate about teaching and the subjects she covers. Would highly recommend taking a course from her, whether it's required or not.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This was my second time taking Professor McAllister and I just adore her. She's so caring, funny, and genuine. She really wants her students to pass and she gives us so many opportunities for points. I skipped her final exam and still had an A. My favorite professor thus far.

A very nice and enthusiastic professor! Please do extra credit, it will save you and boost your grade in the end!! The only thing I would complain about is the amount of work that is expected to be completed by non-science majors. It's a lot. The assignments aren't difficult, but they're tedious.
Amazing Prof, she cares about her student and want everyone to succeed

Professor McAllister is enthusiastic & she made the class enjoyable. Come to class because she takes attendance most days. There are three exams and a final and she drops the lowest exam, one quiz every week, and two projects (one group, one individual). The class is an easy A if you come to class, and read the slides. Also, no need to buy the book
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor McAllister, is very enthusiastic about the topics that she teaches. But be prepared for the exams bc sometimes she doesn't give study guides, also go to class or you'll miss out on important information that could potentially be on the exam. She genuinely wants you to succeed, in her class. She is very accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is very passionate about what she does and you can appreciate that. She puts a lot of effort into her classes and her course doesn't feel like other typical college courses. Great professor overall and wants you to do well.

Overall an easy class if you go to lecture. Professor McAllister is very passionate about topics in class and cares about students. I struggled a bit with exams but did well on quizzes so good grade overall. Mainly a note taking class with one group project and one individual project. Attendance matters so go to lecture!

This professor is good overall! She does try her best to explain everything BUT SHE IS VERY TOUGH GRADER FOR JUST WATER SCI.I had done my best to the lab reports and still got below grade and my group members somehow got better grade despite the fact our lab reports were similar when they gave us back to look at the grade we received.

This professor, is wonderful/ amazing. She is very enthusiastic about environmental science! Be prepared to read because she does have sometimes very long google slides. Also don't just use the slides to study for exams use the text book and case studies she gives you to prepare for exams. She is also very accessible outside the classroom.

I'm not sure why her rating is high.Teaching wise she is a horrible teacher. Do not get me wrong she is a nice person but she can not teach nor does she teach on a college level. Her exams are hard to pass b/c her teaching is NOT on the same level. She needs to teach like that. There are 3 labs reports, 2 exams, weekly journal and extra credits.

This class is an easy A if you are good with time management. Bit strict with lab reports but work on it ahead of time, and you'll get a A or B. Lots of extra credit, so go to the lectures and look out for announcements! The exams are a harder than what the content seems. If you use Quizlet and study a week before the exam, you will be just fine!
she was average tbh not that understanding when it came to the fact that i literally couldn't take the final because i was flying out of the country

She is a wonderful professor, I attended like 2 of her lectures and they were informative, but I stopped going because the content is easy enough that I could do without. Do powerpoint to pdf, summarize pdf, memorize. Did great on both exams. The most tiring part of this class is showing up to lab and doing the 3 lab reports.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: genuinely loves teaching and wants everyone to succeed. she understands that ppl take the class to meet their GEP, so she's very lenient on due dates and lab reports. class is not hard just alot of busy work. Lab reports are easy but can take some time. gives lots of extra credit. Exams are easy and come from her ppt.
great professor! you get what you put in

Professor McAllister is one of the best professors at UMBC! She is so sweet and genuinely cares about students. This course isn't difficult at all, it is just a lot of work. Do all of the extra credit, and it will be a buffer for your exam scores. PLEASE attend her lectures; they are not only interesting but can give extra credit and test answers!

This is more of a rating for the SCI 100 class in general. IT IS RIDICULOUS. This class had the most work out of all my classes and it's a LEVEL 100 GEN ED. Nancy is OVERLY enthusiastic. She consistently forgets that if we are in this class - We are not science majors, and we are taking this class because we are forced to, not because we care.

Very well paced class! Only a chapter or so per week, textbook chapters are short and digestible. The topic can be depressing at times, but the professor's such a kind, warm, and enthusiastic teacher that it makes it a lot easier to take, especially when she often emphasizes more hopeful developments in environmental science. The perfect teacher.

Great professor. Personally very uninterested in science but I still enjoyed her lectures because she was so engaged and  kind. You can tell she really cares about the material and wants her students to be successful. Didn't have to take the final exam because I was happy with my other exam grades. Definitely recommend.

LOVED this professor! So enthusiastic about the subject and so caring for students! Lectures were so fun and engaging. Must participate for points. There are weekly quizzes (but 1 is dropped), 3 exams (there is also a final that is optional and cumulative, but can be substituted for lowest exam grade), and 2 projects. Really easy A, take her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She really cares about the students and will give you every opportunity to pass the class. Just show up to class to get points and read the textbooks since the quizzes and exams are based on that. She also makes the final an optional exam if you complete the first 3 exams and you are satisfied with your grade.

She is incredibly quick and thorough when responding to emails and is a very kind professor. Much of the tests and quizzes will be on material straight from the textbook but her power points during lecture help to break that down for you.

I took this class thinking it was an easy A and not really caring about the class. And now, thanks to Prof. McAllister's enthusiasm for the course, I'm getting a minor in GES. She's hands down the best Professor I've ever had at UMBC. The textbook helps with the quizzes that are every week. Exams and the two projects were pretty easy as well.
Great Professor. Do the work and you pass it's as easy as that.

McAllister is a great professor, she really cares about her students and is very enthusiastic when it comes to teaching the material. You need to read the textbook and her exams are like the quizzes and study guide. Take GES120 with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: she really cares about this topic, and you can tell. She's the best professor I have this year.

Easy class with an optional final and great lectures. As long as you pay attention youre good to go on exams. The textbook isnt really needed for passing. Some questions are pulled from lectures and guest lecturers. All multiple choice so even if you dont remember its usually pretty easy to guess.

Really great professor and enjoyable lecturer. Many opportunities for extra credit, few and relatively easy assignments. Exams will test you on reading and lecture;y you don't have to read the book to pass, but you have to read if you really want a secure A in the class and pass the exams. Syllabus, grading, and schedule are clear and organized.

Hands down fantastic professor. Easy course if you attend class and take good notes. Her grading criteria are very clear and she offers extra credit opportunities. In addition, the final is optional so if you do well, you do not need to take it. I highly recommend this for a science w/o lab requirement or just for fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Overall, Ms. McAllister is a great professor, always willing to help students or give extra resources when needed. The only thing is that the tests are very difficult so be prepared to know all your material and work for that A. If is not an easy class, so if you don't want to put in the work for the class you won't be successful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Mcallister is a good teacher. She makes her requirements very clear and allows you to take an optional final if you aren't satisfied with your grade. She is very nice and understanding.

Go to class, there are participation points. Read the textbook, take good notes from them, material is on the quizzes and tests. Don't bother with handwriting her lectures, take a laptop with you. Projects and quizzes are easy. Quizzes and exams are from her lectures and the textbook. 3 exams and optional final. She is  passionate about the subject
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: You can earn points for attendance.  One test is dropped so if you have an A in the class by the end of the semester you don't have to take the final.  She makes the information interesting.  Manages a huge class well.  Fair and personable.

Very passionate and has field experience. Lectures are fun and informative. Don't have to go to class, but the extra credit is worth it. Optional final, if you did well on the 3 exams, you can choose not to go. I highly recommend taking her class. Easy projects

Ms. McAllister is excellent! She explains exactly what you need to know in order to get A's on your tests. She's super nice, and very passionate. GO TO CLASS!!! The extra points are worth it, and trust me: you need the info. If you don't believe me, consider this: I got A's on the two tests I attended all classes, for, but a C on the one I did not.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. McAllister is extremely passionate about Env Science. She's knowledgeable, eager to help, and available by email easily. 3 exams, 2 easy projects, online quizzes. Study from book for exams. Come to class 4 highlights. Don't blow off going to class b/c she gives participation credit. Great course for a science non lab credit. Recommended highly.
great professor
Easiest class in all of UMBC. If it's a potential elective requirement of you just need to fill 3 credits with the most stressless class ever? Take this class

Going to this class at 7:10 pm is pretty brutal because of how boring it is, but it will let out at least an hour early every time. In class, you just watch videos or read a text, then go home and write a couple paragraphs about it. Sometimes she takes attendance for a grade. Small projects that are easy. Add this to your schedule for an easy A.

Perfect class to add to your schedule if you are looking for an easy A. Attendance is not mandatory, but sometimes she takes attendance, which is graded. Group work is in most classes, and these projects make up most of your grade. Easy final case study.

Tax is not scary with Medicus! Few assignments that are all easy A's! Going to class felt like a waste of time, but sometimes she takes attendance, and it hurts your grade severely if you are not there for it. The class let out early every time. One easy project. Overall, if you are looking for a light class with minimal effort, this is the one.

Class is one of the easiest that you can take on campus! everything is opinionated so there is not a real wrong answer. Great weekly discussions based off of the topics that you go over.  A weekly homework assignment and one final paper at the end of the semester.

She's a great professor with engaging lectures. Even though attendance isn't mandatory, her classes are genuinely enjoyable especially if you enjoy participating in discussions. 

You have 1-2 paragraph essays due at the end of each week and try to attend class because there is group activity on a random day. no final, no exams, just essays

I have taken her twice. She is a good professor that seems to care about her students. She might seem harsh at the start but once test role around you realize she is a kind person. She wants students to succeed, but wants them to put the work in. You are likely to pass her class if you stick through it.
She is a great and funny professor, I would recommend her for IS317.

Professor Medicus is my least favorite professor. While this course was an easy A, during lectures she would not answer questions and would be passive-aggressive. Homework would be unannounced, and not enough time would be given for exams. If you are looking for an easy A, take Medicus. If you would like to learn, I cannot recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Hands down this is probably the worst online class I've ever taken. Lectures consist of her reading off the slides. Group work is randomly given out, and you better hope she even posts the problems. 90% of test questions have zero relation to the homework.
If you do not enjoy accounting and/or don't like teaching yourself, do NOT take this class.

First week in, the class is purely online, thru Blackboard Collaborate. She reads the content on slides. A lot of idle time of just empty staring, and not really tech savvy unfortunately, a lot of time is wasted and not really learning anything, just feels like a robot spitting facts.

Great person, not a great professor.

Easy A. There were only a couple homework assignments and 2 take home exams, that's it. Lectures are extremely tedious and I never saw her take attendance. Assignments are based mostly on opinion and backing your reasoning.

She is a wonderful professor. Very chill and you do end up learning a lot of information by just listening to her speak. She plays a lot of videos to help with the topics. Just ask questions and answer hers and it's an easy A class but if you don't engage with her you will have a harder time. Great Professor 10/10

She basically read the slides even though she said she wouldn't. I once asked for help on hw I did to get ahead and all she said was we'll learn about it next week but I needed help because the question was worded weird. I also did the review too fast for her liking and she took off 25% and dropped my final grade to 89%
Very chill, easy going professor. Lots of group work, 2 take home exams and a project. I had her for MGMT 385, same exact structure. Show up to class, participate and u will easily get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Nice professor. There are 3 exams, and the lowest exam is dropped, and a final exam. There is homework through accounting lab and a final review guide which is graded for completion. She goes through PowerPoints quickly during the lectures so make sure you ask questions and also read the chapter in the book to better understand the concepts.

For her class, you will have three exams and a final. She is a nice person, but not an effective teacher. She goes over materials super fast and is not very good at explaining. Be prepared to become an independent learner.

Literally learned nothing from this course but it was extremely easy to get an A. She is caring and will work with you. Lectures are boring and it seems as though she does not prepare at all. If you are looking to boost your grade and need this credit take it with Medicus!

Professor Medicus is a super nice person. Someone that you can tell has a genuinely kind soul. That being said, Ive learned NOTHING from her class. Her lectures are extremely unorganized and lack meaning. I often ask myself in class, what are we talking about?? Super easy a, but if you enjoy learning I wouldnt recommend.
lots of group work, mundane lectures but respectable, nice, and fair professor

3 Exams (lowest one dropped), gives random extra credit, attendance req., gives a final review packet (worth 15% of grade, based on completion). Overall an easy class , not a fan of her class reverse setting with the whole group work. If you study the check-list of end chapters and the review packet answers she gives you'll be set to pass.

Nice lady. She cares for her students, always ready to help. The class has 3 online take-home exams (drops the lowest one) and a common final. Attendance is mandatory. She gives worksheet to work in groups. There are online HW. She reads from the slides, so lectures can be boring and hard to understand sometimes. Take her if you want to get an A.

Professor Medicus is a adjunct professor. She lectures at the beginning of the week then gives out work the end of the week. She often just sits in the front of class staring at her phone or computer. She doesn't do a good job of ensuring student understanding. She is rarely available outside of class. Her lectured are just reading powerpoints.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: very nice professor and very easy going. take her class for mgmt 385 and you will learn alot about ethics. easy A. take home exams and there is only 2

She is a interesting professor who is baffled by her own planning of lectures. An example, hands out a single worksheet to be done in 3-4 lectures while for those exact ones shes on her phone. Acts like she knows what shes doing toward the end of each class but honestly doesnt know what the next lecture going to be. Lets you redo exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: In my experience with Accounting professors at UMBC, she is one of the better ones. She encourages asking questions and I feel like doing questions in groups helps us understand better. Yes, she just reads off the slides but which accounting professor doesn't? Choose her and get your good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Medicus is one of the best professors you can have at UMBC. She's caring, thoughtful, and always happy to help. You should have no problems passing (most get As and Bs) as long as you come to class and participate in the group activities and group project. You must take her!

Hands out doobie points that decides whether she will curve your final grade or not. All exams are online (except final) and she doesn't hand out homework every week like other professors. Classes are an even mix between her lecturing and group work. Allows us to work out problems in class together instead of listening to her talk all the time.
NO exams. Just 2 papers and that's it.

Professor Medicus is a very good accounting professor.  She's actively participating in the field, which means she is able to give you the book version and the real-life version.  The only detriment is the department-mandated grade threshold on the final exam to pass the course, but that's not her fault.  Great prof, looking forward to 122.

Professor Medicus really makes accounting interesting! She also has her CPA so she teaches you what the book says and what really happens in real accounting life. You do the homework, take the 2 online exams, and attend class everyday then you'll do well. Unfortunately, the final exam is by the department and you must get a 50% to pass the class

Attend every class. Do every homework. Ace the two exams. Study study and study. Ask questions. Look at YouTube tutorials. Note each formula as you progress through the course, will be helpful for the final exam. She is an amazing professor and she really cares about her students. Definitely recommended.

Lots of online hw which was easy, 2 online exams that were also kind of easy, and extra credit is offered to cushion your grade. She goes extremely fast during class and reads off PPTs. The final review packet really helps you understand (or memorize) the material to pass the hard final. Just do the HW, study the review materials, and you'll pass!

Medicus was an ok professor. I had her for ECON 121 and again for ECON 122. She only reads off the slides and makes you do pointless group work. Tests are online and easy. But if you fail the final you fail the class. Like someone else said if you want to learn something don't take her, but if you want an easy A go for it.
BEST I'VE EVER MEET

Accounting is not an easy subject but she has a positive attitude that is encouraging. She speeds through powerpoints created by the book publisher. READ THE BOOK before every class! Group work was extremely helpful. As an adjunct, she does not have scheduled office hours but is willing to arrange meetings before and after class.
Boring class, but goes extremely easy on tests. Take this if you want an easy Accounting class. She's also a very sweet grandmotherly-type woman.

Easily one of the better accounting instructors. The class isn't difficult and the group work helps, but she flies through the lecture when working out problems. Attendance isn't mandatory, but helps w/ final grade. You must pass final with >50% in order to pass the class. Homework & exams are online and require an accounting lab subscription.

Had her for accounting 2 over the summer. Overall, an easy class. Tests are online and she gives you 4 hours to complete them (you can start and stop as many times as you want). The final study guide really helps for the departmental final.

The whole class she reads off of powerpoints and makes you do useless group work, all assignments are on online. It doesnt matter if you have a A in the class, if you fail the final you fail the class "/

Useless professor. Just straight powerpoint reading. Had her for accounting 122 and got an A in that class also. If you want an easy A, sign up for Medicus, but if you want to learn I would avoid her. The auditing class has take home exams (the only time I used my book), a group presentation, and a few homeworks but she never collected them.

She is very helpful and tries to work with every student. The course is not easy so studying is key. Having most of the course online helps keep your grade a float but the final is a doozy. Good luck!

Really good teacher that cares about her students. The exams are hard but if you come to class and study you will be fine. The departmental final is super hard, but it's not her fault. Does multiple examples in class while going thought the chapter. Probably one of the best professors at umbc.

Shes a great professor for someone starting out acctng class. 2 exams plus a hard departmental finals. exams are easy. come to class, you'll do fine. grp work and exercises is a must to master the exams!
She clearly knows the material very well. Easy class IF you read ahead of time plus do the homework. Her exams are ok, departmental final is hard!

Knows material, but ineffective teaching it - textbook replaces rapid-fire and unhelpful PowerPoint lectures. On-line work tedious and picky with answers. Shouts while teaching as if in lecture hall; irritating. No good 121 instructors exist; sadly, she's a better instructor than most. Depend on textbook for final exam. Offers extra credit - DO IT.
Attendance is mandatory for a class that could be entirely online.  Group work is pointless and exams are terrible preparation for the accounting final.

attendance mandatory. Doesn't give out much online homework. Group work on random days. She teaches by basically going over powerpoint and doing some problems in class. Exams aren't too bad, just study. Her exams don't really compare to the departmental final which is a lot harder so be prepared for that.

Make sure you read the book, because that will help you understand what she's talking about more. She talks from powerpoints most days, which is not helpful. Her tests are multiple choice and fill in the blank. The second one is harder and the final is ridiculously hard, so study. Idk if theres a better prof for acct 1 but if there is, take them

She basically teaches straight from the book and you do problems out of it sometimes in groups. Group isn't bad, actually helps more than she does. She reads off a powerpoint with is useless. Make sure you bring the book to every class, and she takes attendance which you'll need for participation credit.
All the tests are multiple choice so it makes it harder (but curves).

If you want to know the material, she is NOT an effective teacher.  The class is boring, because personally, powerpoint is not the way to teach it.  She is a passive teacher, who appears as if she is only there because it pays the bills.  If you just want an A, she is the one.  Her tests are so easy, they are stupid- but the common final is not!
Half the class is her quickly going over powerpoint slides and the other half doing problems from the book. She takes attendance, but offers extra credit and curves exams.
Very flexible. I love her. I've had her for 2 classes.

Really nice prof. But all over the place. Not clear in her teaching if accounting isn't your thing. 2nd exam she had to curve 15 points because most of the class failed it. Then gave 30 points extra credit assignment extremely difficult to help offset the grade. If Acct isn't ur thing, take with another prof.
great teacher!
Cool Professor, exams are easy, but she goes through the powerpoint really fast

Although all ECON courses are based on PowerPoints, she did a good job explaining, relating to real life events.  We used the textbook just for reading, but with PowerPoints, you don't really need to read.  She is now my boss, and she's so chill, laid back!
This man might be the Goat. whomever says he is bad is just coping and seething. Textbook has many practice problems to prepare you for the exam. Lock in twin.

Don't just "review" problems/hw. Do everything that they recommend to you ESPECIALLY EXTRA PRACTICE PROBLEMS AND EXAMS. REVIEW 1 WEEK AHEAD. DO THEM SEVERAL TIMES. Understand the HOW and the WHY. Although attendance isn't mandatory, GO. The participation + hw grade HELPS A LOT. DO ALL OF THE HW. READ CAREFULLY. LA's help but make sure YOU get it.

Before taking this class, have: 1) Know how to do CHEM 101/102 calculations, 2) Attention to detail, 3) A good, non-graphing calculator. Prof. Perks is really knowledgeable. As long as you do practice problems for the final and understand the experiment's main concepts, you'll be fine. Do your work, communicate, and SUBMIT IT ON TIME. A is possible
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I think that many people give Perks a bad score due to the fact that the class is simply just super difficult! Generally, I think that he is a good professor and will spend the time helping you during office hours if needed.
