Super specific with grading on the exam free responses though, so be extremely precise

The way Perks formats his lectures is that he expects you to understand the material somewhat coming into class through reading the book. If you don't take the proper time beforehand you will definitely be lost in lecture but when you come prepared his lectures help reinforce and patch holes from what you read. His exams aren't bad if you practice

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. I do not care if you have to extend your degree by a semester to avoid him. He is the only professor I have ever earned a C from and I have had him for both 102 and 351. He expects you to learn the content from pre-lecture assignments and the textbook without him teaching and is dismissive when you ask for help.

Dr.Perks is a great professor! He really does care about the students. PRE READ the textbook or you wouldn't understand the lectures( HE WOULD TELL YOU WHAT TO EXPECT ON THE EXAMS)Lectures are practice problems and very similar to the exam questions. Practice, Practice and it is not that hard. He really does help out in office hours as well.

Love Dr. Perks! I had him for 102 and he rocks 351. He is an enthusiastic and respectful chemist. There is so much to learn from him. Pay attention to every detail he says, do all the pre-lecture work, come to class with high understanding, ask questions and practice all the time until the exam. If you live in this course you have this!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's actually an average professor but organic chemistry is a difficult subject. I think he got too much hate for doing his job and it's more of a problem that the subject has too much material and is complex. The lectures were kind of useless if you didn't learn the material beforehand. It would have been nicer to learn in class imo. Lock in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's a good professor, that's about all I can say. His lectures and notes are accessible, he mainly just tells you what the textbook will, but in my opinion hearing him explain it is much better than reading the textbook. He cracks the occasional joke and he tries to immerse his students well in the class. Overall a good class experience.

Dr. Perks isn't the best professor, but he gives a lot of ways outside of tests to get good grades. I found the midterms to be representative of the materials covered in the book and online videos. Chem 102 is difficult if you aren't good at math or didn't fully understand 101, but that isn't the professor's fault.

Lectures focused on example problems with minimal content. Knowledgeable and experienced but had high expectations. Required videos were hard to follow, and he wasn't tech-savvy. Strong proficiency in prior material is essential. You must grasp concepts quickly, as falling behind can significantly impact your grade. HW/tests are intense and broad.

Didn't respond to my email about being sick before the final. I had to take it while sick. Failed the class because of it. 

Don't take perks.

This man DOES NOT TEACH. You will learn entirely from the textbook. His exams are horrible but not as horrible as his attitude and extremely strict personality. Let me emphasize that HE DOES NOT TEACH. He only goes over practice problems in class, no background no nothing. Organic chem isn't even that bad, it's just the prof

I wish I could have avoided him after 102....but here we are. He has all the same problems (if not more) as he did in 102, his exam questions are abs wild and isn't very helpful inside or outside of lecture. this class' only saving grace imo was gierasch was also teaching it and the textbook was actually useful. Perks, I am BEGGING you, pls retire.

Dr. Perks is a nice person and all, but his issue is with his exams. The exams are so hard, the material isn't that much of helping, and so is the univ's aid for learning. The extra credit is a joke and isn't helpful in any way except if you need few points for a letter change. There is a survey and students are blamed in it greatly.

Perks can be a bit quirky, but if you engage with his teaching methods, the class is manageable. Textbook is helpful, and Unstuck study is a great supplement for study prep. Stay focused, and you'll get through it.

Worst professor (if you can even call him that) to roam the earth. Doesn't teach in lecture, just does polling problems, expects you to learn and understand just from pre-reading (you learn more from the reading that this guy). Will belittle & single you out, minorities beware, will speak condescendingly. Explanations to questions are useless.

Throughout my entire school career, I've never had a professor I genuinely wished would quit. I'd rather be without a professor than have him. He doesn't teach; he expects you to learn beforehand, and we just do practice problems in class. I wish this guy would retire and go enjoy his life or something rather than torture us as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Belittles students for not understanding "simple" concepts but refuses to explain them differently. The class was at 9 am and over the semester, students would stop showing up to lecture. The class is consistently half full by mid-semester, so don't worry about not getting a seat. He is petty and will remember little things to bring up later.

It was really weird how he would approach you in lab in regards to not showing up to lecture or selecting the wrong poll answer. He questioned my validity in attendance because I selected a different poll answer and I offered to show him my notes as proof that I was in class. He has a way of making you feel small.

He's oddly confrontational. And I mean it in a respectful way. He goes up to you in ways that are questionable. And that's him personally. Viewing him as just a professor, I'd say he's got things to work on. I, myself, and a good amount of my peers discussed how much work we put in to prepare for his exams; and you can never be prepared. Womp womp
man only wants to see you fail. there's no such thing as success with him being the professor. class is very hard and his exams are undoable. beware and please drop the class!

The content for the class wasn't hard, in my opinion. I studied it as much as I could and understood what was going on in the class and for the most part, did well in the hw, poll during lecture, and discussion. The only problems were the exams and the prof. Exams didnt reflect what we learned and the prof was no help either in what 'help' he gave.

If you are taking CHEM102 with him - DONT. He made the class a lot harder than it was. He didn't answer any questions I had when in office hours (he'd be like, oh we covered that in class and then move on) and when I asked for other resources to learn, HE DIDNT HAV ANY. He felt like he was very unprepared to help students and it sucks.

Dr. Perks was a great professor for me. You may have to be flexible with your learning to understand his lecturing, but if you do that and can learn independently you are all good. Read everything given, do tons of practice problems, ask plenty of questions, and don't cram (the course is mainly tests). He is so sweet and hilarious. Be nice to him!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you're on your own, you're a person. Lectures consisted of AKTIV polling questions that were closed before you could even answer. This class covered 31 topics, and each was worse than the last. In class, polling is what you may need to save you're grade. The chemistry department needs help.
horrible professor. Instead of teaching the material in class, all he does is post poll questions and give minimal info about them. He's merciless when it comes to grades too

In 352L now and miss Perks from 351L. He gives you everything you need to succed. He provided videos from the years prior during COVID which set you up for an easy smoother procedure. He also made it very clear what he expects from you. The final was bizarre..but I like him. He's the type of guy that will roast you on spot but tough love.

Try not to be too intimidated by chem351, at the end of the day its just like any other class and the amount of time you put in will directly affect how well you do in the class. Textbook is a really great resource and try your best not to fall behind.

This is the worst professor ever. He came into lab and asked someone why they scored below average on an exam and everyone heard it. He is absurdly rude and mean. He makes exams so hard for no reason and lead offs were completely useless, he instead talks about random chemistry stuff he likes. He also doesn't know how technology works.

Lab manual is made just for UMBC so ask older students for their copy. Lab was pretty standard. Pre-lab quiz, in-lab quiz, and TA grade your work in the lab and write-up. "Lead off" is the Friday class before the labs, which was only sometimes helpful.

Heard from others that he was rude directly to students. Class lecture was okay. Made harder exam questions than the other professor. Okay overall, but was manageable because the class was split with another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took him for orgo and lab. He was pretty bad at the lab teachings, it seemed like he was just talking about random chemistry he found interesting. He also likes to stare at you in lab and is just weird. Overall seems friendly, but can be condescending. I was always annoyed when it was his turn to teach orgo lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One word describes this guy, awful. The way he talks in the lecture is as if you should already understand organic chemistry at the level he does. He is also very rude and dismissive.

Perks was nicer in lab than lecture, but is super dry either way. Takes attendance with clicker questions and only one is dropped so don't skip. Found his lectures a bit hard to understand and would have to go over material on my own, but he's available after class to answer questions. Final is good but make sure you remember/understand experiments

Perks isn't a hard professor, he just isn't too nice a person. Once the class was using the chat to ask about lab during his lecture and he left refusing to answer any questions. He often lectures too fast so it's hard to understand what he's teaching. He also had a lot of assignments, imo. Stuff due before class, after class + regular hw. 5/10
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Perks doesn't answer questions during class. He leaves that to his TAs. Sometimes he also confuses himself and takes a couple minutes to get situated again. Has easier exams compared to the other Ochem professor, but it takes more self study. Links a lot of good videos to watch, so you don't have to look yourself. Homework due once a week.

Didn't explain concepts clearly in class. The book explains it okay, as did the khan academy videos, but even with that, his class was hard to understand. He didn't pay attention to student questions in chat, didn't spend enough time on explaining the problems. If you didn't understand it & he moved on then you probably would have to find it alone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: It's a lab so you definitely need to show up to do well but he also taught 351 lecture and I really preferred Gierasch over him. He's nice in person but not the best teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Honestly he improved a lot from the fall sem. As long as you do your readings and reach out to LAs and listen to the ICAs he does in class (live), youll do well. Exams are tough since each question are worth 4 pts. Failed pretty much 3/4 of my exams but pulled As on ICA,HW, PCA and still got a B.

I had Perks for Lab and Lecture for organic CHEM. Overall, the lectures seem a little confusing because I was not used to his teaching style, however, he is the SWEETEST person ever and very understanding. He is fun to talk to and knows his information.
Extremely bad at explaining and teaching. He makes it much more confusing than it needs to be which makes learning hard. Can also be disorganized and gives unclear instructions.
Not a good professor. Very dry lecturer.

Mark is a very disorganized and disaster professor as he moves randomly through different topics. Homework assigned for lab is very vague & relies on the universal lab textbook that was made for all organic chemistry lab students across the nation. Sorting through the myriad of information in the textbook trying to prepare for lab is very tedious.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Perks is great. By now you should realize every science class at UMBC is a beast. The class in itself is hard but he breaks it down well. The key is to use the learning objectives to study (very important). Then solve a lot of questions and a bunch of practice exams. At least a B will be guaranteed. Also do your flash cards ASAP
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: very straightforward
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Hes a great guy and knows his stuff and can be funny sometimes. His exams are not bad at all they're just like the practice exams he provides. If you come to class, read before class and do the recommended problems you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: His exams are insane (average is usually around a 65), but there's a small curve at the end of the course. Take notes (textbook + lecture), go to office hours, SI/PASS, and CTC, and make flashcards ASAP when you start getting into mechanisms and synthesis. I'd definitely recommend covering every practice exam, too. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed the class. Dr. Perks' tests were straightforward and he clearly enjoys the material
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He co-taught CHEM351 with Gierasch in Fall 17 and I honestly don't understand why he gets such a bad rap. Very solid professor, teaches the material in a logical way, and will push you to the limit by requiring you to have understood the material and apply it in new scenarios. Exams might be a little rough, but nobody said Orgo was easy.

Clicker questions for 3/4 of lecture, meaning that you have to be there and you have to learn the material by yourself before going to lecture. There is online homework every class and they help you learn. For me, gap between 101 and 102 were huge, so I had to put so much effort on final exam(101 and 102 cumulative).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Boy, did Gierasch and Perks try to ruin Orgo 1 for a lot of people. The lectures were decent, but the exams were quite difficult, and by far the largest portion of the grade. The average for 3 out of 4 of the exams was 68-69%. That low an average does not speak well to the exams' fairness. My advice: take orgo elsewhere and transfer the credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's a pretty chill dude. He enjoys teaching and he cares about everyone's grade. he's a touch grader and the exams can be hard but as long as you keep up with the readings and aleks, attend every class and attend SI/Pass you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Perks cares so much, so really take advantage of all the opportunities given to ask questions because he'll really take the time to do it well. He is a tough grader, but he's super chill, and his lectures are great. I thought I wouldn't get an A in orgo, but i did by doing the recommended problems, going to SI/PASS, and having a tutor at the CTC.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Perks is a good professor. His lectures are okay. Sometimes, I get confused in class and his answers are not always helpful. He is approachable though. The class was not too bad. I felt that everything on the exams were pretty fair. There was nothing we had not seen before. The content for chem351 is harder than that of chem101 but exams are easier
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Perks is a good professor. If you actually talk to him and show him your concern, he will try to help. There are lots of opportunities for help on campus like SI Pass, Math Lab, Tutorial Center, etc. Do recommended textbook problems, the readings before every class, and go through practice exams and you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He is a bit difficult to understand him, but when you understand the material and concepts clearly, his reading quizzes and exams will be more or less straightforward. His exams are tough though and he will try to trick you, quite like the ACS. READ THE TEXT BOOK BEFORE EVERY CLASS. If you don't understand what you read, you wont be able to answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Clickers are used in every class so be there. He takes the time to learn your name even though there are more than 200 students. He's super anal about copying/cheating/etc.... so don't do it. His exams are next level in my opinion
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Perks is a great lecturer. He makes the topic easy to understand and the lectures are fun. He is not too approachable. Whenever I would see him for class-related questions I would always have the feeling that he is annoyed, and does not answer emails very quickly. He is an okay professor.

Dr Perks makes you work for your grade, no question. But its clear he cares about his students and puts a lot of effort into making the lab match up with 351 lecture. He makes a point of knowing students names. Even in a 200 plus lecture hall!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Decent lecturer. Exams were fair for organic chemistry 1. I'd recommend doing the Wiley practice problems to help with studying for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He is nice and has a passion for chemistry. He is not too difficult. a Lot thought chem 102 was easier than 101. If you got an A in 101, you will be fine. He curved the final. The final was super easy (90% chem 101 stuff).

ALEKS was rough this semester with a lot more knowledge checks. There was only a curve on the final, so even scoring way above the average may not get you an A. He tends to jump around a lot in the slides and skip a lot of the math so if you don't know how to do it don't expect to learn in class. I had it with Ms. Bass helping.

Dr. Perks is one of the best professors at UMBC! Yes, the material is difficult, but it's ORGO... it's very hard. He's clear cut with what he expects you to know (w/ learning objectives for the readings), and emphasized doing practice problems. He is a bit of a mess, but he's also very funny at times. If you work hard, your grade will reflect it.
Took him for lab and lecture and he is a nice person but he will put you on the spot to answer questions, is mainly trying to help you.

Dr Perks is a nice guy and really knows his stuff; also really helpful during office hours. Orgo itself is a nightmare. You are going to need to do practice problems outside of class if you want a good grade. Exams (multiple choice + free response) were tough as class averages were in the 60's70s. There was a giant curve at the end.

Really smart guy, you can tell he loves Orgo. He's really helpful during office hours. Lecture is only clicker questions so make sure you do the reading + hw before class. Exams were tough, but as long as you do the practice problems you'll be fine; exam is  multiple choice + free response. Giant curve at the end.

Extremely smart, almost too smart to teach students. He has high expectations of his students, but still makes an A achievable with hard work. Personally I fell behind in the beginning of the semester and never really recovered. DO NOT FALL BEHIND in the readings, you will be screwed by exam time if you do.

Dr. Perks is the best professor I have ever had.  He is passionate about organic chemistry and is brilliant intellectually, as well as being pretty funny.  The class isn't easy.  Its organic chemistry--tough is what you sign up for.  Its not his fault.  Ask for help.  Dont be intimidated.  If you fail, its on you.  He does his job.

Great guy. He's really nice and is genuinely interested in chemistry.  His lectures were a bit confusing, but he really tried. If you attend every lecture, and make sure you understand the labs you should be fine.

Dr. Perks is a professor who cares a lot about the subject he is teaching, and an intelligent man. His lectures are helpful, but only if you have done the assigned readings. He is very upfront about what an orgo student needs to do to succeed at the beginning of the semester. Be prepared to work and find a study group!

Very intelligent guy. Despite what others may have said, he pays attention to his students. In certain he enjoys teaching, but he will not sure that by making it easy for you. took his class in the summer from another university. He made enough of an impression for me to remember him years later and rate him. Study, pay attention, and ask questions
He knows the material, but does not have an effective way of teaching. He starts teaching something and jumps to a different thing so quickly.  He was not helpful when I visited him at his office.

Dr. Perks is brilliant!  Take the class seriously and ask questions. He teaches using the socratic method, so be ready to do a boat load of questions in class. The reading is a must to be able to do well in his class. Also he gives tough exams. They are do-able but give yourself ample time to study everything.

Not all smart people make great teachers. Very confusing guy. Stutters over himself alot. Does not post powerpoints prior to lecture, so you waste alot of time copying everything down and then try to play catchup to what hes talking about. Exams are rather difficult. If you can, get tutoring ASAP. Form study groups! TAs are better teachers than he.

Prepare to teach yourself orgo! Perks does not lecture at all. The entire class is full of clicker questions. Publisher used for online homework/quizzes is not the same publisher as the text that you will be required. GO OVER PREVIOUS EXAMS when studying for an exam. Clicker questions do NOT reflect exam material. Nothing does.

He knows every person - as in he was able to tell each (of 139) student their full names on the last day of lecture, and he truly is great at remembering who is what major etc. He's funny in class, knows A LOT, and loves orgo. He holds the class to high standards. It's HARD but he's a phenomenal teacher and is very smart, well-prepared, etc.
Knows all of students' names! Very cool and funny guy. Labs are definitely less interesting than 102L. Pre labs, post labs, and lab quizzes can be tricky so ask questions!

Perks is a strange teacher, I don't feel that he really likes teaching 102. He isn't very helpful if you ask him a question and his lectures are very haphazard. I don't think he knows what a conceptual framework is or any real methods to teaching, very smart guy though for what he does know. Pretty descent curve as well which surprised me.

Nice guy, but doesn't like teaching the class, so he just doesn't. Lecture consists of fast-paced clicker questions(5%) of your grade and him running through "examples" on his ipad with a projector. Get used to teaching yourself and always do the practice problems in the book. The exams are harder than they should be so ALWAYS do the old exams.
not helpful at all.

For 351L, Dr. Perks is very unorganized, and not very clear with assignments and class materials.  However, he is much better for lecture classes such as 102 or 351.  He's a really funny person and will pick on people who aren't paying attention and embarrass them (it's great).  He's also incredibly intelligent and sometimes forgets that you arent.

Doesn't present material in lecture. Assigns homework due day of exam on material that isn't on exam. Vindictively asks a ton of graded clicker questions on day of exam because he knows many students skip the class (on material not on the exam) in favor of preping for the exam. When connect was not working he told the class to "call McGraw-Hill"...

Doesn't present material in lecture. Assigns homework due day of exam on material that isn't on exam. Vindictively asks a ton of graded clicker questions on day of exam because he knows many students skip the class (on material not on the exam) in favor of preping for the exam. When connect was not working he told the class to "call McGraw-Hill"...

Great professor! I hated Orgo coming into it, but I've really grown to appreciate the subject. Kind of dorky, but he really spends time explaining the concepts you need to understand to move forward. Exams are, of course, tough, and homework + readings are pretty time-consuming, but if you work hard, you'll do well. Try to take Perks! :)

Dr Perks is great but he definitely is hard. His lectures are helpful IF you read the book first. They are not there to teach you the material, but to help you understand it. You are supposed to read before lecture, and then you go over it to conquer what was in the book. He knows who does well and who doesn't and is great with answering questions.

His exams do not relate in any way what so ever to the practice exams on blackboard.  Lectures are usless, discussion sucks, and he is by far a barking mad loon.  Looks like Larry Kings brother, and his only redeeming quality is that he swears when he makes mistakes and it provides a minor chuckle.  Don't take him for 102...don't do it.

I had Dr. Perks the second time I took 102 and for 352.  I LOVE THIS HIPPIE.  His mandals are the best.  But really, this man lives and breathes organic chemistry and was always very helpful.  I went in dreading organic chemistry and now I'm an organic chem grad student because of Dr. Perks.

Dr. Perks is a great teacher.  His exams are tough but fair.  Organic chemistry is hard; that's not his fault.  He cares about the chemistry and his students, and makes an effort to know you.  Knows organic chemistry like the back of his hand.  I thought his exams reflected the lectures; you don't have to teach yourself from the textbook alone.
Be prepared to teach yourself.

Go to class for clicker questions. Suffer through discussion. Lectures are boring but Perks is pretty good at making them a little interesting. He makes a lot of mistakes in the lecture notes. Also, teach yourself everything from the book. Tests cover all information in each chapter, not the stuff in the lectures. Tests are very difficult. Beware.

Boring, clicker points enforced. Go to lecture to help understand a bit of procedure. Uses TAs for labs. Pre and post labs are somewhat hard but mostly 3 questions long.Book is helpful for lab notebook. Follow lab notebook procedures.

Dr. Perks knows a ton about chemistry but his lectures are very poor. They are organized in a strange way and he messes up on 80% of the problems. The exams are extremely difficult with the average being around a 60%. Definitely read the book and do all of the recommended problems. Know every definition and concept from the book.

He seems to really like chem, but not as a teacher. It sometimes seems like he's not interested in teaching us. He does pretty cool demonstrations but he screws up his note ALL THE TIME. So confusing. He also stumbles over his words which also is confusing. Read the book, it helps. Or take another professor.

It seems that the professor is really interested in chemistry...but not chem 102. All he talks about is orgo. He screws up on a lot of problems in class and doesn't teach very well at all. For those who plan to do well in the class, read the textbook

Dr. Perks is a gifted Professor that truly loves Chemistry and has a true gift for teaching. He takes a lot of tough material and makes it really understandable. I would recommend him over any of the other Organic Chem Professors here.

Had him for chem lecture and lab. He's more at chill in lab then lecture. He sorta of impatient. Its helpful if you read the textbook before class because when he teaches I usually would not know what was going on.

he was not interested in teaching our class, he is a great lab teacher, but not lecturer.  the class is extremely curved, which is good because it is close to impossible to get an A without it.  when you take tests you will walk out thinking you did awesome, then you will see your grade, and your friend's grades, and be confused.

At first when I took Chem 102. It was definitely a bad experience with this teacher because it was his first time teaching it. However, when I took chem 352, he wasn't that bad of a teacher. At times it is hard to understand him. you are required to know material before class and do practice problems.

It really seems as though they could care less about the student. The professors really act like the class is a burden to them and they are not interested  the material. They could care less about your grade or class performance.

The class is definitely a weed out class despite what they claim. The material is not hard, but you go through it at really fast If you are involved with research and internships be prepared to do a lot of teaching yourself. I am really good at chem and do not get A's on all the exams they are really tricky, few questions, and nothing like lecture.

I was really scared of taking orgo 2 with him.However, he really changed my expectations in orgo 2. He is very knowledgeable and passionate about orgo, so he does his best to explain to students. The only problem is that he expects students to read the material before class, so he assumes you have some idea of what he's talking about.

This class if difficult no matter who is teaching it. To do well in the class, you must know nearly every single fact in the lecture notes, every fact in the textbook chapters, and EVERY formula. The tests had 25-28 questions, so you can only get two wrong to get an A. Don't expect many A's on exams. Go to office hours but don't walk in unprepared.
He was a very good professor and funny too. He is very helpful. Tied in organic with real life uses (made it interesting for me) and was very willing to help students.

Much better for orgo than he was for gen chem. The exams are difficult, but fair. He will answer your questions during class or office hours. He tries to give free points with clicker questions. Make sure you keep up with the reading, as he sometimes skips the details.
Awesome. Very knowledgeable about organic chemistry. Very charming personality.

It took a year to understand his teaching style. Dr.Perks is absolutely a fair professor. This is an orgo, of course it is hard. Don't expect the professor to tell you what to study. He just outlines the concepts so you study by yourself after class. Study the textbook, never get behind; then you can pull out "A" even w/out a curve. Use the textboo

Really nice guy and overall a great teacher. He is very smart and teaches assuming you already know what he is talking about, but if you read material b4 going to class you will be fine. His exams are not too difficult. Will curve them a lot.

Dr. Perks is so awesome! None of the classes that he teaches are easy, but it's chemistry. It's not going to be easy no matter who is teaching. But he's always willing to help if you ask for it, and he is genuinely a really good person!
he messes up on the example problems during class and doesnt realize it till he's finished a whole page of the problem and still not solved it. RELY ON TEXTBOOK

He is very excited about chemistry, but that doesn't always translate into being a good professor. His lectures were sometimes confusing. Reading the book is a necessity! Clickers count for accuracy, so try to really learn the subject.
Perks is a great teacher, and his exams were all fair. He really tries to get to know his students, which is rare in science classes.

Perks is crazy. He says not to memorize things or that words arn't important, but doesn't give formulas and asks for definitions on exams, so don't listen to him. He should be teaching organic. He tries to help but I get the feeling he judges. Curved just enough to get the B(.05%), so don't expect too much help.

If you're not good at chem like me, you shouldn't expect to get an A in his class instead of studying chem really hard. Study everyday and don't rely on his powerpoints for studying. Use the textbook, this is the only way you could survive this class. The exams are not that tricky if you STUDIED... he drops one exam..
He's a very nice person, but the class itself isn't. It starts out pretty easy and then just keeps going down from there. It goes down and down and down...and under. Good luck.

I love Perks! He's such a nice guy and he makes an effort to get to know his students. He's very willing to give help but you need to ask! Perks' lectures REQUIRE prior reading. Or else you're lost. Personally, the main use for his lecture notes was to follow along the examples to get the CPS questions right (they count for accuracy).

When it comes to teaching he expects that you know the concept before attending class. He provides lecture notes yet they are not congruent with his teaching method. In order to get an A you would have to study the textbook. He has a lot tricky questions on his exam.
exams are extremely hard

His exams start out really easy (especially during the beginning of the semester), and then get ridiculously hard. The lectures don't really do anything for you, but you have to go for attendence. Basically, you just have to teach yourself the entire course. If you can't, you're screwed.

Nice guy. His tests are easy, but only if you read the textbook. Otherwise, you're pretty much guaranteed to fail. He lectures as if it is a review, so read before lecture. If you learn well on your own, you'll do great. If not, I'd recommend someone else. He drops one exam. And he knows his stuff.

This guy has the uncanny ability to confuse himself. Every once in a while he'll post a clicker question and then realize that there's more than one answer, or the right answer's not on the screen. He uses notes a lot, but skips over ones he doesn't like, so you need to keep up. You may get by if you cram for tests 5 hours before, Just be careful.
Not a bad teacher, just can be hard. Is a very nice guy.

Scattered brain. Cannot stay on one topic to save his life or ours. His lecture notes are unorganized and are mostly pictures that come straight from the text book. Read the text book before/after lecture or else you'll be completely confused. Beware, he likes to throw in a little more "physics" than actually chemistry.
The worst professor I had in college....probably the only one I would ever speak bad about.  Just trust me, and avoid him at all costs.

Perks helps make the ACS practice finals. His tests are abnormally difficult. He is a poor lecturer, as he basically skims the book poorly. His notes are incomprehensible, and are mostly strange pictures. Smith apparently had easier tests and good notes. Only take Perks if you enjoy learning on your own and gaining nothing from lecture.
Not bad I guess.. pretty average.
Not a good prof. Lectures are hard to follow. I wish I took it with Dr. Smith instead.

Perks is a very nice man and he seems to be a good person. Still, he is a very difficult teacher. His notes are incomprehensible and it is very difficult to get anything out of class. In addition, his tests are incredibly difficult and well made, explicitly designed to trip you up and punish you for not knowing something entirely. Avoid.

He is a really good teacher, and if you actually come to class and do the work you will learn it.  He does explain things pretty clearly and is very helpful.  If you take the lab with him, he comes to all the labs and helps you if you need it.  He also does group work in lecture which is very helpful, and he knows everyone by name.

He honestly DOES try to teach, and if you go to his office hours he is extremely helpful and make you understand.  However, his tests don't reflect the material that you learned (or he stressed) in class.  Although he earns points for being very nice, I would suggest taking the class with another teacher.

I had him for Chem 351-352. Very articulate man who loves what he teaches. He is an amazing teacher for the material he has to teach, no one better so far. His only draw back is that he makes the exams very tough (but fair). Take him if you want to learn something, dont take him if you want an easy A (even though curve is ~80% = A).

Absolutely the worst Chemistry professor I have ever had. He takes a difficult subject and makes it near impossible to understand. Going off on tangents and already expecting his students to understand all the material doesn't help. He is also a complete arrogant jerk when you ask him questions. Take is with anyone else, except him!

This professor is great! If I had to choose between him and Hogsmane again, I would choose Perks. He teaches very by the book. As long as you read the book, do the problems, and do the homework, you will get an A. I'm not saying he is easy. The work is hard and time consuming, but it is not impossible. not for slackers.

I have taken CHEM102, 351, and 352 with him. For 102 DO NOT TAKE IT WITH HIM. He is terrible at teaching it. For organic he is great. He only tests on things he has covered in class. Read the book, do problems and you should be fine. He takes a significant amount of questions from the ACS Organic Chemistry Practice Guide, WORD FOR WORD.

This class was hard because the material is hard. I really think Perks could have done a better job helping students to understand. He is not a bad guy, but he belongs in Organic Chem. He wastes A LOT of class time with experiment that don't even work and going off on tangents about how the material relates to Organic Chem, which I didn't even need

If you're serious about chem, take professor perks. SLACKERS BEWARE. I didn't do much studying except a few days before the exam where I did ALL the probs in the chapters (about 400+ in 2 days) and pulled an A out of my ass. Do ALL the problems and you will do well in his class.

If you can help it, you shouldnt take him, he goes off subject all the time. He will do an example in class that will take 30 minutes and it will not even be right . You will know because a student will have to correct him. He also does NOT curve. If you have a 64.94 in his class and the passing grade is a 65, even if you are an active student he w

He is the worst chemistry teacher ever for 102, he cannot do any of the math problems and his tests are so hard. He does not teach worth crap and everything he tries to teach is already prepared on a slide for him. he cannot do the work so how do you learn-the answer is you learn on your own. His tests have nothing to do with what you do in class

perks really knows his stuff and is a nice guy. his curves are generous and he follows the textbook very well. I recommend him for serious chem. students who can dedicate the time to his problem solving oriented teaching style. also good to take for lab section

I could not adjust to his teaching style so fast- mainly he likes focusing on problem solving in order to understand the concepts (and not vice versa). If you like word problems then you will do fine, but if you are more of a conceptual person it might be a little bit difficult. Do a lot of practice problems and you could probably pass.

By far the WORST teacher I have EVER had. He doesn't use the book, hes arrogant and his demonstrations seldom work. Doesn't use a microphone in a large lecture hall, although it was a pain the first few weeks, it doesn't matter anymore because 1/8 of the class shows up. AGAIN, I CAN"T SAY THIS ENOUGH, HE IS THE WORST TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD!!!!!!

Dr. Perks will know your name, know how well you're doing in the class and will make himself available to help you as much as possible. His tests are harder than they seem but still not bad considering its organic

He's not that horrible. He doesn't go by the book so you really have to pay attention in class and take notes. Since u get 15% for just showing up, u can pull off a C in the class if u get aroud 40% on exams. 50+ is a C. Exams are REALLY hard but get ur hands on some old exams, he tends to repeat questions that are older than 2 years.
By the third exam, you will have a sevee case of learned helplessnes

He teaches material not from textbook. Therefore, exam score is so bad even though I read the textbook many times and understand the material. Also, he does not give time for taking note. He moves on to the next so so fast. He picks students up to answer the questions. Exams are worst that I've seen before.

The worst chemistry teacher I've had so far (they've really made an effort to get bad chemistry teachers) his exams are incredibly hard, and he doesn't teach AT ALL. All he does is put up examples on transparencies and tell you do to them in your groups. Then he picks on his favorite students to answer them, and moves on to the next question quick.

ACS anyway if you know what that is well guess what Perks is part of them , all perks does is give half free response and half multiple choice exams think easy > guess again go google ACS and u will know what horriable society i am talking about , 50 > is a C that was the only good thing and he makes you into groups for the whole semester

Horrible teacher. He never teaches ANY material and expects you to read the book instead, which would be OK if attendance wasn't graded. Basically he starts every lecture with "ER's" and "HAW's" and picks examples for you to do in groups. How am I supposed to do anything if you don't teach? Why am I paying you? To remind me to read the book?

One of the worst teachers ever...No structure to his classes. He just randomly rambles on the entire 50 min. a huge % of the class is retaking it. His tests are a killer.U can work every prob in the textbook correctly and still fail .Don't take this class, if you need good knowledge and grade in org chem. He will put you at a serious disadvantage.

Very helpful. One of few professors who know what he is talking about. Also very nice, will draw strucures and explain reasoing. Also he's on the ACS (American Chemical Society) board - they make the conprehensive test u take at end of 352 so he KNOWS his stuff well, talk to him as much as you want till u get it!

seems easy, but you really do gotta put in the work otherwise u'll end up with a B like me -__- study for the quizzes, they affect ur grade alot, and as long as u study for the quizzes you'll b fine for the final.

One of the best teachers Ive ever had.  Always helpful and friendly.  I had Dr. John Smith for Chem 101 and 102, and he was horrible.  Dr. Perks was great.  I wish I would have had him for all my Chem classes.
No Comments
No Comments
While extremely difficult and not the best, he's definitely better than any of the other professors who teach these courses.  must go to class in chem 102 tho for dumb group assignments each class.
Horrible Teacher ....Plz Dont take it ...Take Hosmane, or smith ...but neve never never never...Dr perks .... This is my request ...

Dr. Perks is an awesome professor. I took 352 the first time with Smith and he was horrible. Dr. Perks made his material very understandable and his group work reflects what you are to know for the exams. Sure, his exams are pretty hard, but UMBC has one of the top Chemistry programs--so the materia

I'm a straight A student, and this class has been VERY difficult. It's east to 'pass' the class because of a built in curve, but u really have to work ur ass off for an A or B. If u can't understand the material by reading it urself, ur screwed b/c Perks doesn't do a good job of teaching it at all.
C range from 50-70 B 75-85 A 85-100, 15% of grade for just coming to class and doing groupwork. Test average is around high 40's. Easy if you just need to pass it.

Perks was not a good teacher. He rushes through his lectures. Hes not good at explaining problemd to people in easy, understandable terms. He makes these groupwork problems that are redundant and stupid. He gets an attitude when asked for help outside of his office hours. Take Hosmane instead.

His group work and lectures are entirely relevent to the exams that he gives out, his explanations are well done, and he's always prepared for class. Points are given for attendence. And, in general, he's a nice guy.
I do not like his so-called group participation.  It does not make any sense.  I can learn everything from the book and without going to class. I did not like him as a teacher, but he is a nice guy.
Hard lectures, hard tests.  He comes well prepared for the lectures and usually has time after class - very good office hours.  Nice guy, but hard teacher.

Some people knock this dude, but I think he has a great way of teaching. He layed out a good fundamental track for the ACS final in 352. I liked his teaching style better than Smith's, but that's just me. Says hi and actually remembers my name.

ok, I know some people like hime, and some don't. This course will be very easy of you know his style (lecture, exam). So, first of all, try to find HIS STYLE, then you will have no problem. His lecture will be very clear only when you know how he teach.
Some people love his teaching style, some don't -- I was one of the ones who didn't. I couldn't follow his lectures, so I had to do it all myself from the textbook.

Perks seems like he is a very easy professor but when you take his exams, you will see how tough they are. The worst thing about this professor is the way he curves, it is the worst curve possible, believe me. He also teaches 102 & Orgo, great.

Words CANNOT express how horrible this teacher is. He says he doesnt "believe" in writing on the board so he just does experiments. Why doesnt he just tell the truth and say that he's lazy. Stay away from this guy.

Very organized lectures with lots of visuals and examples. Another good thing is his use of groupwork problems. Tests are inpossibly hard (class average was ~45%) and sometimes not approachable. Overall, is nice guy and cares whether or not youre learning

Biggest waste of my time ever. Even when I did go to class, I either couldnt follow  anything he said, or fell asleep. Good chemistry teachers should be able to make a boring, difficult topic fun and interesting, not MORE BORING
I know that this course is hard itself. However, he is well prepared for every lecture, and very helpful when you go his office to ask some problems. Very Good Teacher to prepare MCAT/PCAT/DAT.
Read the book and do all the HW problems, don't worry about lectures, its a waste of time and you only go over the stuff everyone gets anyways...if you happen to go over anything related that is.
Dr. Perks is the****!!!!...His exams are very easy! I like him so much I am taking him for Ogranic Chemistry next semester.
God, this guy is terrible. He acts like he doesnt want to teach the class because its a beginning class, he only really does experiments.  Don't go to lecture, just read the book.
No Comments
lectures suck dont bother going just study from the book.
No Comments
Lectures sometimes difficult to follow, but has best interests of students in mind...
Don't listen to these people, they're on crack. Great professor, clear lectures.
A total hardass, but still decent.
lectures are incredibly useless...very vague in his teaching...knows his stuff but doesn't know how to teach it
Lectures not helpful.
this guy sucks big time!!!!

His exams were tough, but more so because of the nature of this class rather than he himself. Study the slides and stay focused, start the projects early, and ask the TA's about any questions you have.

reviews.comment: Not sure why there's sm hate, he's a solid professor. Follows the slides, explains concepts clearly, and encourages questions. Slides were posted after lecture,emails answered quickly. He def cares! The class is just hard. Proj and hw match the course chair's. Straightforward, not flashy, but he helps you through. Exam format followed study guide.

The Course Material he writes on whiteboard would be your notes. Don't just rely on the exam reviews he provides because I have noticed the exam review he provided for final was actually a trap. Students including me prepared based on review and got screwed.
The worst professor/teacher I've had, Does not post anything on blackboard because it'd be convenient for students. He gives a little review before exam which has nothing to do with the exam itself.

Seems like a good guy, but I do not agree with his teaching style. Main thing is he teaches content that is not in line with the curriculum; I feel like I'm not learning what I need to. Spends too much time on SML and doesn't cover important topics that other classes do. Does not use blackboard and half the stuff he teaches is not in the textbook.

Mr. Woodcock is not an easy professor. Only 5 homeworks, so if you do bad your grade will drop. Very harsh grader, if you show a lot of work on the test, but the answer is wrong, 0 points. His prep questions for the tests only cover 1-2 problems of the 8/9 total on the exam. He makes tests so the average is 50% and grades on his calculated curve.

He teaches way differently than the other classes. Every other class was using C++ and he was using some random language. His exams are worded weirdly, even though I understood data structures well and did well on the projects his exams were horrifically awful. Seemed like a nice guy but just didn't learn anything from him.

He's a great lecturer, but you must make sure to take lots of notes. Always go over the practice exam questions (and answers that don't correspond) before the tests if you want to do well. The entire class is fitted to a bell curve. Overall, if you study and take notes you will do well. I have enjoyed this class.
Pay attention in class and take notes on everything and you can do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof Woodcock neither use power point nor a computer to compile his code. He use old school teaching style and he literally copy down codes from his notes to blackboard during class. Also, the material he covers in this class are different from other sections, which means piazza won't be useful for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Expected perfection and will take off for things that she has not stated that you were supposed to do.  Make sure you practice and keep up and memorize all spelling and grammar. Not very welcoming or inspiring.
Her lectures are basically built up on the homework/textbook, so as long as you stay up to date you should be good. Tests weren't too bad either, again just do the homework and attend lectures.

does not teach much, and you need to basically learn on your own or else you are cooked on all of the tests for the class (which i was, except the final), luckily grade is mostly determined by VHL assignments otherwise i would've failed
Not even worth it, just go take spanish.

Professor Tannan is a great professor. It was her first time at UMBC. She is kind, but a word of advice; I took high school french and had a gap year before college, I would suggest you know the basics of french before coming into 101. It is fast-paced. Make sure you do the homework on time, participate/attend class, and do the extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor King is very passionate about what she teaches. The class itself is easy, but it is discussion based, but participating is not difficult. There are no exams but there is a final project presentation based on a topic of your choice which was actually fun to do. There isn't a lot of homework but there are a lot of readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor King is amazing! Her class was kind of boring in the beginning but it really starts getting interesting once you start working on your personal project which counts as the final in this class. There is a lot of presentations, group work, and public speaking required so be prepared to share. She is super chill

I like Dr. Nicole King as a person but the course itself did not interest me and the only reason I took it was for a GEP credit. If you are not interested in public humanities I would not recommend. If you need to take this course for a GEP credit just be prepared to participate a lot.

the thing is a lot of students don't attend his lectures cuz they're a little hard to follow pace wise and with his accent. Other math professors also keep past quizzes and exams posted for study material while he didn't which I didn't really appreciate cuz it was pretty hard to know what to study. use resources posted on bb
very bad, watch professor Leonard instead if you want to pass and understand the material.

This teacher will withhold information from his students if they don't attend his lectures, which are impossible to understand. He changes his syllabus and the way exams are taken. The HW is mostly random times. He should be reported to the school and given an easier job that doesn't involve contact with students at all. He barely tries for his job

This professor doesn't deserve his job. The people rating him good only did bc they got a good grade in his class. I've done well in his class, and he is by far the worst teacher I've ever seen. I have taught myself everything bc you can't learn from him. He tries to make it as hard as possible for students to pass. He's one big emotional baby.
Worst grader
you cant understand him.

His lectures are completely pointless because you can't understand anything he says. His quizzes and exams are insanely hard; barely anyone passes. Don't take him if you do. He is a nice guy, though, but he's just not professor material. None of his study materials help either. I have had an A in every math class before him. DONT take his class

He is very lecture heavy. However, with homeworks, he cares more that you practice the material as opposed to submitting it on time. Beware though that final exam was bit tough. Still managed to get A on it though. His handwriting can be bit sloppy and talks very fast in lecture. Other than that, good prof and caring prof. Go to OH.

Dr. Rasika is kind, easy to talk to, and passionate about his subject, so attend office hours regardless of if you're struggling. His lectures were a bit difficult to follow, but it becomes easier if you go regularly. If you ask questions, he will slow down and re-explain. Just show up and try, and you'll be golden. I'm taking him again for 152.
His lecture are hard to understand but you can lowkey teach yourself everything with all the things he puts on BB. The HW is good to do, all the quizzes and exams are fair

He's not the greatest at lecturing. He cares more about the proof than showing us how to solve. You have to give up time to teach yourself. The online textbook helps, but to an extent. Extra credit is also a little, and the exam/quiz problems are more complex than those of other professors. I'd suggest considering another professor if available.

Save yourself the stress and take Calc with Dr. Dean. Dr. Rasika's teaching style is difficult to understand, and almost all of his quizzes/exams are more complex than Dr. Dean's. His lectures are not engaging either, and he doesn't give extra credit. I honestly learned more from YouTube. You need to really lock in if you want to pass with an A.

He goes over a lot of material pretty fast, usually uses the lectures to prove things to try to get people to understand why things are done a certain way. Has a pretty heavy accent and handwriting is really hard to read sometimes, but he's always willing to clarify anything. Genuinely kind and caring, generous with partial credit

I am currently taking Calculus I, and the professor puts 100% of his energy into teaching. He explains and proves most formulas very clearly and always checks if students understand (“Is it clear, guys?”). Some students may struggle if they don't speak up when confused, but having a solid foundation in previous math courses is very important.
Dont take this professor for calc 1, you will suffer!! He doesn't explain things clearly and just expects everyone to know what he's doing.

Builds student understanding of Calculus in a sensible, linear fashion by showing proofs behind equations. Things taught in this class always seem complex at first until he breaks them down through proofs. He answers questions when asked on the board, or will answer them after class. He will ask "Is it clear?" intermittently, be honest he explains

He is a great professor. I see people dislike him for absolutely no reason but he really gives his 100 percent in class. I got so many extra credit opportunities and his office hours were really helpful.

Rasika replaced Tighe in Calc1, had him for Calc2 also. He put 110% into the classes, w/ tons of office hours and really wants you to understand when you dont get it. Accent's a bit hard to understand. Not exactly a hard grader. He gave tons of practice work. He gave "hints" for quizes. He really does care man. Study more than you think in MATH152.

I had him for 152 this semester, not 151. I don't think he's a great lecturer, he moves way too fast and doesn't really explain concepts sufficiently imo. But in every other aspect, he's a good prof. He gives out a lot of practice that is very similar to exams. He's also nice and gives opportunities for extra credit. Doable if you actually study

It's a bit tough to warm up, but once his personality shows it's a nice experience both ways. He is very kind and wasn't strict about homework, allowing people extra time since he cared more about you getting the practice. His quizzes definitely test you. If you underestimate his exams, you will fail them; they are absolutely loaded. Nice guy!

Class was a bit disorganized and the final was way too hard. However, Prof. Mahwattege is an extremely lenient grader and his lectures are informative. Out of all the 225 profs, he's definitely one of the best and the class is definitely better-- especially since other profs (*cough cough*, Rostamian 👎) don't even bother grading homework.

Took him in the Fall of '24. I struggled a bit with this class. Just relying on the lectures to understand the material is not enough. You have to heavily study the material and textbooks outside of class as well. TA sessions are more useful. Gonna have to teach yourself, but if you're good at math, it isn't that bad. Lectures just aren't the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy and understanding too. Moves pretty quickly through lectures but he goes through many examples and practice problems. Might be a little hard to understand at times so I highly recommend going to office hours, he'll explain the concepts very well.

For resources you can go to office hours, your discussion section, read the online text book, look at the online notes, SI pass, access practice test for mid terms. Lectures cover main material that will be in the test and the reading checks are 4 questions, hw is around 16. If you failed it's your fault tbh he made it so easy.

Overall a decent professor. He speaks very quickly, but went through lots of practice during class and was relatively lenient with grading (he doesn't take off much for arithmetic errors.). It will definitely require a lot of outside work if you've never taken calculus, but he readily offers office hours and can be easily contacted by email.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Math 151 is already hard to begin with so workload will relatively be the same regardless of the professor. He is really fast with his lectures and has a noticeable accent but it wasnt too bad. His grading also seems to me very lenient. Highly suggest doing practice exams he gives out. He does not use technology. He a cool and funny dude though ngl

While people say he lectures fast (I wouldn't know legit watch every video in 2x speed), in my experience, if you read the textbook before lecture and take notes, there should be no problem. Outside of lecture, he is very responsive to emails and does want every student to succeed, just attend office hours and pay attention. Just read the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I'll cut him some slack since this prof had to unexpectedly take over in the middle of the semester while the old one quit. Very passionate and engaging when he teaches but is quite fast so pay attention. Also he purposely does not provide any resources/notes online which can be frustrating at times. Very friendly and understandable though.

Although I wouldn't recommend Mr. Rasika to students who are learning calc for the first time, he's a great professor for students like me, who have already taken calc. He's very fast during lectures but always encourages students to ask questions. He responds to emails quickly and has office hours twice a week. He's also friendly and approachable.

I thought he was pretty okay though his lecture style can be frustrating since he moves so fast. He's cool if you ask for help but you have to be very outspoken about needing it. This class requires a lot of work outside of going to lectures. His exams and quizzes were straightforward enough if you study

Do not take Rasika as your Calc 1 professor. While he seems decent, his teaching is tough to comprehend. There were quizzes every Thursday, and while the quizzes weren't as bad as the exams they were still a pain sometimes. The exams are challenging. If you do have Rasika make sure to know everything about calc before coming to class.

If your taking Math 151 DO NOT take Rasika as your professor. It's pretty hard to understand his lectures, the way he teaches is fast paced. But I can say he is a nice person to talk to but that doesn't mean he is a good professor.

Future calc 1 ppl, this class WILL be difficult for many regardless of the teacher. That being said, he is not a terrible teacher. Yes, he speaks quickly but you can ALWAYS interrupt him and ask him to slow down. GO TO OFFICE HOURS they are very helpful and you get to know him personally. Nag him for his own practice quizzes/exams you'll be peachy

He has a pretty strong accent in his lectures so he's pretty hard to understand and he moves fast. It's definitely a lot of self-teaching. But if you go to his office hours when you don't understand something and do all the homework, you'll do fine. He's an understanding dude too, so if you're a decent student dw

I would not recommend. He's nice and can be understanding but the way he lectures is so confusing. He will solve practice problems at an extremely fast pace, figuring them out as he goes, and does not give anyone time to process what he's doing. He will answer questions but most of the time the class is too confused to know what to ask

Do NOT take this class with him! He teaches as if you already know calc, making it extremely hard to follow. I go to class every day confused about past units and leave just as confused about the new ones. I spend 30 hours a week studying since you won't learn much in lecture. It's incredibly draining. Hard to understand and learn with him.

In his class right now and I hate it. He's hard to understand and just explains stuff like we already know it. 
His lectures just don't make sense to me, and I have to teach the topics
 in this class to myself by watching yt vids. So, if you're looking for a teacher that will explain the topics well and help you understand, then don't take him!

reviews.comment: He is nearly impossible to understand, lecture is used not to teach, but to do problems that he expects you to understand from reading the textbook. The class was very fast paced, he gave us at least 3 online quizzes a week, an in person quiz every Wednesday. Even one on one, it's hard to understand him. Tests are very hard to read. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is unresponsive to emails and seems difficult to reach.  Not very personable, and can even be rude or judgmental or condescending towards students.  Be prepared to complete every homework assignment, attend every class, and ace the exams (which are a mix of multiple choice and written, btw).  Overall, I would avoid this professor if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nkiru Nnawulezi is really strict and harsh, and her grading is quite arbitrary and difficult to understand.  She provides little to no feedback and does not allow students to look over exams with her.  She usually does not reply to emails either, so best to catch her right before or after class if you have a question.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Nnawulezi is the most unpredictable, harsh, and cold professor I have ever had. She seems uninterested in letting students connect with her or share personal experiences that are pertinent to the class. She is an incredibly tough grader and a lot of it seems arbitrary. Her tests are usually a mixture of short answers and multiple choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her class is quite easy material wise. I am not a great writer but I still got a 24/25 on every paper, however, she doesnt allow late work for any reason and if you miss one assignment you will not get an A. Her main issue is SHE DOES NOT REPLY TO EMAILS. It took her over a month to reply to one of my emails and multiple people have the same issue

I have never experienced so much stress before. DO NOT TAKE. Remove it from your cart I beg you. She is amazing, but her teaching methods are by far the worst that I have ever experienced. She takes at least 25 days to get back with grades, DOES NOT respond to emails, and is a harsh grader. She takes off points, and doesn't even explain why. RUN.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: DONT DO IT. She literally waited until the last week of class to grade everyones papers and its impossible to pass her class. Such a harsh grader. Ive NEVER received a D on paper until her class and Im a junior. This class was a huge mistake. Also she doesnt respond to emails.

Dr. Nnawulezi is the most unpredictable and juvenile professor Ive ever had. The course is 3 quizzes, and 4 papers, making the entire class 160 points. Each paper is 25 points, which gives you very little wiggle space for error. She grades extremely harsh for a course that is so little in points. The quizzes are easy-ish. DONT TAKE THIS CLASS.

Prof is incredibly split in my opinion; the lectures have been some of the most engaging and well-presented material I've seen in a classroom, but her policies are ruthless. If you miss an assignment, you will not get an A. Communication was really sparse as well. Unfortunately, a great professor with really frustrating practices.

Horrible professor. Boring and uninspiring, and doesn't know how to teach. Our entire grade was four exams which she never really told us what to expect. She had to tell the class to stop complaining to the TA about how awful she was. It was something she actually had to address. She's not easily accessible, she doesn't curve, she shouldn't teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This Professor is knowledgeable; however she makes students study too much just to pass any of the exans. She did NOT tell us what to expect on the exams and only gave us the questions on the next two exams after so many people failed the first two exams. She takes weeks to grade exams including the first one. Exams are the bulk of the grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the most useless classes I have ever taken. I learned nothing from this instructor. She is not a good professor. At all. Super rude. Intimidating. Totally disrespectful towards MOST of her students. 0/10, would NEVER take her again for anything. Ended up with a 89.7% and received a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Homework assigned EVERY class ontop of lengthy chapter readings. Vague powerpoints and tedious in-class assignments EVERY class. I ended the class with a 79.8% in which I asked in advance if I can improve an assignment to improve my final grade, she never replied to my email and of course would not round up. NOT WORTH IT!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: One of the best classes that I have taken. There was a lot of reading and a big group project that spans the entire semester. Great discussions. Tests are very specific to the reading. If you read, show up to class, and do well on the group project you should do well.

Very work heavy class, but the Professor N. will help you if needed. She will also take the time to schedule appointments with you and sit one-on-one to explain things. Hard class, but very good professor.
Hard class, requires a lot of reading. Sometimes the quiz questions were unclear or extremely specific, attempting to pull from up to 40 pages of text. Lot of work for what you get out of it.

Natalie Panfile is a hilarious and interesting professor who aims to provide her students with a true studio class experience. The drawing class is 4 hours long, and she gives excellent feedback to help her students improve. Her assignments leave a lot to interpretation, but she grades with this in mind. My art improved a lot in her class.

Natalia gives pretty vague guidelines for what she wants with her assignments, so it's a lot of trial and error in the brainstorming phase until she likes one of your ideas. But once you figure out something she likes, it's not too hard. A lot of the class is repetitive and I didn't learn too much, but it's overall not bad.

Natalia is hard to read, because you never know what she wants from you. Art itself is supposed to be subjective, and you're judged on everything. She also considers this a studio class, and expects multiple hours to be spent on pieces a day, even though its just an intro class. And don't even get me started on her online portfolio...

Dr. Ka is one of the nicest people I've met in my life. The material itself is somewhat difficult for all the Wolof courses, but he isn't a tough grader and is accommodating. There are a couple of presentations, homework is given somewhat often but is not difficult, and there are a few exams and speaking exams.

He's super nice and funny, but we almost never finished the content within the class period because he talked a lot and almost always showed up late to class. He also didn't put in a single grade until WEEKS into the semester. This class was not real. Pretty easy though, if you independently reinforce what you were trying to learn in class.

if you don't come to class, you're cooked. doesn't tell you when homework is due unless you come to class, gives random quizzes not outlined in the syllabus. if he yaps more abt a topic and pushes it to the next lecture, will push out the due dates for homework, but won't tell you unless you came to class that day (NEVER USES BLACKBOARD/EMAIL).

great prof! for this class, there were two group projects and he graded them easy since they were just summaries of a chapter in the book. the final paper wasnt bad either as it was based on a topic u chose. the only complaint i hav is that the tests werent in the og syllabus and he randomly announced them a week before (they were easy tho).
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fairly easy A (2 presentations, 3 tests, one ~10pg paper), but don't expect to learn a lot. Ka makes students do about half of the lecturing, and even if students don't know what they're talking about, he won't correct them. He also seems to hate technology; nothing is ever in Blackboard. Says attendance is mandatory but doesn't grade it.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this class online, but Professor Ka is the nicest professor I've ever had. You can tell he loves teaching Wolof. Although this class was an easy A I would say make sure you attend class. You miss one class and you've missed a WHOLE lot of material.
He is a tough grader. Using the study guide to prepare for the exam is useless.

Nicks legit a legend. He offers 2 buy coffee ' & has really insightful things 2 say bout the field as hes been in - videos hames, music, ads - u name it, hes done it! He has a unique way of explain concepts & is very theatrical w his movements-he'll dance around the classroom - its engaging, Plus, he sounds like Ryan Reynold! :)

Discussions were student-driven and Dr. Ka facilitated discussions, offering feedback and keeping the discussion on track. At first, I was dreading the two group presentations required, but the way they were assigned allowed students to be put into groups of people with shared interests and I thoroughly enjoyed preparing both presentations.
Great Professor!!! Take him!! There are group projects and presentations but overall the class was really interesting. Make sure you study for the tests!! Grades easy on the presentations.

Dr. Ka is a really great professor. He is very friendly and outgoing, very approachable. His class requires you to do group presentations and the final project is a 10-page paper, but it is not really that difficult. He is worth it!
This class was mostly led by students but his feedback is honest and knowledgeable. Seemed fair.

Ka loves the subject, and makes it easy for non-majors. This class is treated as a true "intro" to applied linguistics, but topics are interesting. He's sweet and funny, and genuinely caring. Slight senegalese accent, but not hard to understand. Talk to him 1-1, you'll have better conversations and he appreciates it. Great person overall.

I had Dr. Ka for LING 290, FREN 302, and FREN 315, and did a research assistantship with him for his Wolof Project. He is Senegalese, but knows a lot about the rest of the world as well. He is very intelligent and very helpful. There are times when he can be a bit dry when lecturing, but I still really enjoyed learning from him.

I decided to take Dr. Ka's class based on the other reviews about him on this website.  I was in the 6-week summer version of MLL-190 and really enjoyed the course.  Dr. Ka covered a lot of material during our class, but he made sure that important points were thoroughly explained before moving on to the next item.  He is a great instructor!

Two short powerpoint presentations based on textbook#1, two quizzes, two one-page homework assignments from textbook#2, final 10 page project double-spaced, all graded very magnanimously. Excellent professor with a genuine care for his students. Attendance sheet randomly distributed. Mild Kenyan accent. A very easy A with no linguistic interest.
OMG I LOVE DR. KA!!! All he wants is for his students to get what he's teaching and do well in class. He cares so much..he believes that all his students have the potential to do well....he is great!

Professor Ka is my FAVORITE professor at UMBC. I just love him. His MLL 210 class really raised my interest in Africa, and even though his 10-15 page annotated bibliography was a bit difficult to do, I actually enjoyed learning about my topic and got an A on it. Definitely an easy class, lots of videos. I recommend taking any class with him.

Probably the easiest class I've ever taken.  Dr. Ka is very enthusiastic about the material and always open to class discussions.  The material was interesting and varied.  Two presentations and one project that allow you to pursue your research interests.  No exams; easy to study for announced "pop" quizzes.  Very chill class and professor.

Dr Ka is incredibly nice. He didn't give any exams, just a couple quizzes that he graded very easily. We had to give two presentations (easy) and write a 10 page paper on basically any topic. Not a difficult class.

This class is complete B.S. and Ka knows it. He makes this class so easy. No exams. A couple of "pop" quizzes which don't require studying really. Other than that, 2 short presentations and one research paper. This class doesn't cover anything, but Ka enthusiastically talks about all kinds of stuff. Nice and very knowledgable.

Professor Ka is so enthusiastic, he can even make French phonetics interesting. He is a wonderful, likeable man, and I can't say enough good things about his personality. The course follows the syllabus, and heavy use is made of the text in class and at home. 1 hr. a week required at the IMC (hated that), but otherwise a very easy, reasonable class

If you're looking for an easy A... run away! Dr. Ka really makes you work for an A. Homework not required to do, but recommended. Exams are tricky because you don't know what to expect on them, and grades them pretty tough. If you want easy A, take McCray. Despite this, he is very friendly and like-able.

Unreasonable. I usually get A's, never struggled so hard in a class. I was told no and also you cannot have extra credit when I asked for a two day extension two weeks before the due date (I was out of state). Most of his assignments took me about 40 hours, so just don't have a life/job I guess. And he had a 5% assignment due before class day 1.

Took Olano in Graphics for Games, and he was honestly one of the best professors I've had at UMBC. While he was occasionally hard to follow in lectures, he cares deeply about the success of his students and is ALWAYS available on Discord with timely responses to ANY question about the projects.
