If you like video games I highly recommend 438/491.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, gives good feedback but doesn't really teach game development, it's mostly just a semester-long a group project where everyone is left to their own devices for the majority of the class. Grades very fairly, and takes note of individual effort of each group member, so make sure you contribute above and beyond to the group work.

This class is difficult but eye-opening especially if you want to get into game dev. Lectures consist of learning about UE5 and other computer graphics topics. Super smart guy who grades difficult projects leniently. Just put effort and utilize office hours and you will be okay :)

The 491 game development is a "tough" class that requires significant effort. But that shouldn't discourage anyone from taking it. The assignments are graded based on attempt, so as long as you put in time and effort, there should be no problem at all. Marc Olano is a very passionate professor, and taking his class is valuable for learning UE4.

Professor Olano is incredibly smart, but he knows way too much to be an effective teacher. Lectures consist of him scrolling through Unreal Engine code. Expect to put in 15 hours per assignment, they are INCREDIBLY difficult. Some easy grades are presentations (10%) and presentation feedback (15%), although this requires constant attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Excellent lecturer.  Gives a lot of examples/content that augments the slides.  I took advantage of his office hours and he was always very helpful.    You can't pass if you just listen to the class.  You need to read about the material outside of class and independently do the HW.

Olano made this class pretty fun. His tests were hard, but were always on topics discussed in lecture. He gives you a good chunk if his code for the projects, which makes some of the programming trivial.  Lectures were always exciting, full of graphics examples and demos. If you're going to take graphics, Olano is a great person to take it with.

Assignments were largely tedious (eg. ridiculously long strings of multiplying and adding things) that you have to be careful, not clever to complete. I thought the lecture was pretty uninspiring too. I had the impression that the professor didn't want to really be there teaching this class and it made me not want to be in the class too.
The architecture class was difficult, but there are also plenty of extra-credit questions in each homework. Helpful professor, treats everyone fairly. Exams are challenging. But I aced it anyway.
In general he's one of the better teachers in my opinion, but not the best.  He's tough but fair.  Knows his stuff, and has a good attitude 99% of the time, just watch out for that 1% :)

This guy loves two things, graphics and performance. He will twist and turn every architecture concept to a problem in graphics domain. His classes are boring and sleepy and assignments are all 'assumptions and justifications'.He will not teach anything but you will learn everything because of his hard assignments. His exams are very challenging.Av

Dr Olano is very intelligent but not capable of passing knowledge to students.  His explanations often include erroneous statements that he later realizes and corrects.  This is frustrating when the material covered is difficult and confusing to begin with.  He is unwilling to offer necessary help even during office hours.  Avoid this professor.

Very bright teacher.  Knows a lot about what he is doing.  Very helpful after class and during his office hours.  I didn't use the book too much, but I would have liked it near the end.  Like most comp sci classes, all the information is available on the internet.  Projects can be time consuming, but if you like graphics you will like this class.

I first came hoping to learn something new, and ended up learning that this is a class for people who knew prior the material to be covered. I would ask for help, and still be left in the dark as to how to complete the several insanely difficult projects he assigned. Office hours were during my other classes and the TA's accent was incomprehensible
Second class with professor, liked IS634 more. Class was good overall. Most assignments are writings. Wasn't too bad. Group project semester writing needed more instructions

This class was 60% group project, 40% individual assignments. It was a lot of work to do in the group project but it wasn't that bad cause the work was more "fun" for being school. The professor opens the content every week & the syllabus due dates are a little hard to understand but she puts the due dates on the actual assignments too. Not too bad
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great professor - accessible by email, she will take the time to explain any doubts. Work is fairly easy to complete with weekly assignments and only two major papers - one midterm and one group final paper. Only thing is instructions are sometimes unclear and she's also little bit of a picky grader. Pay attention to deadlines, but enjoyable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: To get an A in this class, you have to read a lot. You have to do good in your quiz, participate in weekly discussions and the final paper. Good professor, I would take it if she teaches a different course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is very passionate about teaching which makes his lectures more interesting and easy to listen to without getting bored. He is willing to work with students if they have issues, and exams can be difficult content wise but he tells you what to study to do well. He also allows a note sheet for every exam.

Dr. Omland was a great professor and I really enjoyed his section of the class. He was very easy to talk to and very personable so I did not feel intimidated going to his office hours. Really sweet guy, the key to getting A's on his exams (like I did) is simply just to write as much as you can from the slides onto your note sheet lol
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: shows bias and is rude. very unfair
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good professor. I did better on the exams with Dr. Omland, they were more conceptual or application based whereas Dr. Leips had some math which I wasn't great at(even if it was easy). For the most part I would agree that the material we learned during LECTURES were in the exams. Take advantage of the few extra credit opportunities you get!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: lectures were long but he makes a good job implementing practice problems during lectures to work on and gives full credit for participation as long as you come to class, tests problems were a bit tricky but overall easy class.

His lectures were very helpful and prepared me for the exams. But some of the exam questions were a little annoying for example a question asked about which reptiles are native to Maryland, which is irrelevant to my understanding of evolutionary biology. Besides questions like that exams weren't too hard.

Omland was an amazing professor. He was very understanding and easy to work with. He cares for his students and wants them to succeed. His lectures are amazing and he tries to make them entertaining and engaging. I would take him a million times over. One of the best bio professors I have ever seen. Pay attention to lectures and you will be set.

Dr. Omland's section is better organized than Leips's. The tests are not easy, but the reading quizzes and in-class questions prepare you for them, and most people in my class did better on his tests than Leips. He is very passionate about his work and easy to talk to! Would have gotten an A if he taught the entire course. Amazing Professor!

Go to lecture, tests will be easy. Go to office hours, get guaranteed As on tests. All lectures translates well into discussion. Reading quizzes before class are reasonable and can be done in under 20 mintues.

Professor Omland was great. Tests were super easy, since many of them used answers found in the reading quizzes, which we did before every class. If you do the reading quizzes and take note of the answers, you'll do fine. Lectures were engaging with polls and energy, although professor was technologically challenged at times. Overall, Great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: half the semester is omland, part 2 is leips. on omland: listen to the lectures & understand them. take note of the wordings and definitions. the tests were open note but timed, BUT you have to understand the minute details to really ace them. lectures were based on the textbook, so read the book. not everything was in the book; listen to lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Doctor Omland's tests are so bad. The questions are basically more "have you come to my lectures?" and not "do you understand the concepts of biology?" He will tell you you need to understand the fundamentals to pass, but in reality, you just need to memorize the massive Tree of Life and all the phylogenies, and record his lecture verbatim.

Dr. Omland is a very good professor. His tests arent that bad if you study and make sure to read before class like every other course. He is funny at times and passionate about his work and past research. The only thing that I wish he would do is provide more than one sample exam and be just a little more specific about exam content.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Omland is a great professor and the class is extremely easy as long as you are willing to both understand concepts and memorize some material. If you pay attention during the lectures and study the information he emphasizes, then the class should be an easy A.

He has minimal clicker questions and his exams aren't that bad. When I took the class, he taught the evolution portion which was very easy if you memorize content on his slides (misconceptions about evolution, phylogenies of chordates, amphibians, reptiles) and how to answer his questions - the man LOVES "all of the above/none of the above" choices

Dr. Omland explains concepts well and is enthusiastic about his subject. He is very opinionated about certain topics. He loves talking about his research and himself in general. He is extremely proud of his accomplishments and wants you to be too. Be prepared to memorize lectures and trees. The only required reading was a book chapter he wrote.

Do not get me wrong he is a good Professor, but him teaching with Professor Leips is complete hell. Do not take them together at all. Do yourself a favor and avoid this class if they teach it. And I am a biochemistry major and this class was too much and it could all be so simple.

Dr. Omland was THE BEST! He was very punctual about responding to emails and was so funny!! He really loves what he does and his enthusiasm is contagious! Go to lecture because not everything he says goes on the powerpoints. Nicest professor ever

He co-taught this class with Dr. Leips.  Dr. Omland taught the evolution part, which most of the time, was sheer memorization.  I didn't really care for the subject and I thought Dr. Omland was a bit narrow minded.  His class was fairly boring aside from him using strange emphasis which was funny.  That might be what I remember most from the class.

This class is less about learning and all about memorization. Even then, Dr. Omland makes memorizing information difficult. On several occasions he gave the class dates in lecture and on the test there would be completely different ones. Sometimes the right answer would be OVER A MILLION YEARS off of what he had told us before.

"Learning the process of biology" and "understanding the fundamental concepts" - no, his class is about memorization, and specifically memorizing phylogenetic trees. Has an obsession with "everyone's reading the trees wrong!" and will literally hammer trees into your skull until you want nothing to do with him, BIO 142, or biology in general.

My least favorite professor of the three. His lectures were dull and his huge ego and constantly bringing up his own papers/research made it worse. Annoying guy, but you can do well on his portion of the exams if you read and go over the relevant chapters and MEMORIZE THE TREES.

Loved him! Made evolution very easy. Understand the basic rules/facts/contradictions of evolution and you'll do well. Also, understanding phylogeny trees is important! Out of the 3 profs, he was the easiest & had the most straightforward exams. Study tip: Listen to ALL old lectures AGAIN & take notes to do well on the exam!!!!

boring and teaches difficult subjects. a lot of memorization and uses old fashioned projector when he wants to write notes or draw phylogenic trees rather than using the board. it is difficult to see what is being written and annoying.

Honestly, I hated learning about trees. I don't know if that makes this sound bias but he used the whiteboard a lot of the times so goto lecture (most likely not on powerpoint). Hard exams because you don't know what to  specifically study. You're on your own. Ask the TAs for help and pay attention in discussion for this part of the course.

Dr. Omland is the 2nd Eco/Evo prof. and he covers phylogentic trees. He is EXTREMELY intelligent and is the first bio prof. I have had who has gone into the philosophy of biology. I have great respect for him, but he is generally unapproachable, and very egotistical. 8% of the 2nd exam asked questions specifically on his research. Tests are hard.

Terrible. Really confusing and unorganized. Didn't make it clear what information would be on the exam, besides tons of confusing, overly detailed phylogeny trees. Ugh. And he's kind of a prick.. he thinks he's right about everything. I guess this part of the course is doable, but its everyone's least favorite.

Nerdy and knowledgeable. He's very interactive with the class, which is a plus. He expects you to know EVERYTHING he says + what's in the book. Tests are very hard, impossible to be prepared for them. Pay attention to his random bird facts, they'll show up again.

He's such a dork (with sense of humor)!  Before I took this class I didn't care for evolution or whatever, but the material he presented ended up being very interesting!  I admit some material made me go "wha...?" but he's pretty approachable if you got a question for him.
i thought it was an easy class. good professor, went over what skills we needed many times.... trees were cool!!

The 2nd teacher for the class. He is a bit crazy and expected you to know dates and all of the seemingly random relationships and trees that he draws. His exams are pretty much all trees. Does CPS early in the class so get there on time.

Dr. Omland's section of the course was my favorite. He is a rather goofy guy, but very nice and helpful. You really have to study the phylogeny trees and do all the readings, but for me, his section was so worth the work. Attendence is mandatory, though. He has CPS questions during the first five minutes of class. Pretty easy on the eyes, too.

He's very nice and knows a lot about his field of study, but his tests will screw up your grade in that class. Basically, you must know how to read those darn phylogeny trees; he bases almost his whole test on them. Also, he likes to do clickers as soon as class starts and if you miss it, he doesn't care.
Not a fan.
I liked dr.Omland alot. He is a little crazy but he gets his point accross and is very interesting. To study just write all the notes onto notecards and memorize them and you will be fine

Hard. Exams are hard. Avergaes are 20 to 30 out of 40. Expects you to memorize the deuterostomia ranks and others too; and his lectures tiny details. Don't procrastinate on the readings. Good at mimicking animal sounds. Kinda strange, but approachable. I disagree with the other ratings, no way he is the best teacher. The notes are def not easy
he was the 2nd teacher of this class , yes he is a gigantic nerd and needs to go do his bird watching --- exams sucked class average would be in the 30's / 20's

He is so ridiculously excited and positive about speciation. it's great. and his notes are very easy to take because there are so few. but don't get too confident about how easy everything may seem. you still need to study
What a gigantic nerd.  But he's cool as heck and if you show up and remain awake, you will do great in his class.
Good guy, OK teacher, passionate about what he is doing though, which is a good quality.

One of the best lecturers at UMBC. This subject could easily be tedious but he makes it fascinating. And he doesn't mind telling rude students to cut it out. His enthusiasm for the subject is contagious, I highly recommend this class!
No Comments

The Birdman will drive you coo coo with his tests.  Other than that, exams are off the notes which pretty much the class will make up as they answer questions as the class goes along.  Average professor since phylogenies are pretty boring in my mind.
Nerdy, dorky, cute in his own way. Birdman is on top of his game. fair man
His part of the class isn't as easy as Freeland's, but it isn't so bad.  Very approachable guy, though the material didn't interest me too much.
Pretty weird and quirky, and makes you participate. His exams will require you to study. He's alright.
very good teacher, explains very well, keeps you entertained and wanting to go to class, besides the notes are not all online and you'll need participation! funny guy!

Very interesting professor, can even make a bird brain understand evolution. I would recommend Omland anytime. Compared to all the other professors, Omland is very clear in what he is talking about. Tests are mostly from old exams.
He is V.E.R.Y. good at imitating animal and bird sounds, class was interesting aswell.

Memorize the notes and old exam questions you'll be fine. Has a tendency to break out into random frog, crow, oriole, and various other animals' mating calls. He is really good at them though! He'll throw stuff at people when they don't pay attention...mostly pens and occasionally a tennis ball.
Nice guy but tests are very hard. Grades completely based on tests. The lectures are rather interesting. He DOES offer a curve.

Has problems communicating clearly with students, but otherwise a good teacher. Will break out with a very loud, very accurate animal call at the drop of a hat - not just birds, either. Ask him about waking up in Borneo.
HIS EXAMS ARE HARD
boring, mean.

HORRIBLE! he's boring, doesn't know how to get the material across and tries to make jokes for the class to like him.  He's very rude to students, so if you are unclear about something...he's not the person to clarify it!

Does his best to teach, but utterly pretty disengaging in terms of the material.  Probably the more boring section of the course to be tested on and yes, his exams are a bag of fun, but not in the good way.
no direction to lectures, not very detailed.

Not a bad professor at all.  lectures are interesting, but make sure u take notes and study the past exams, cuz he takes stuff DIRECTLY from that (sometimes word for word).  dont have much choice with ecology professors, but hes a good one.

Great lecturer, but his exams were so damned confusing!!! He had some good stories and asked students to give examples.  It was at 9 in the morning, which made it sort of hard for me to get enthusiastic about the material.  The Statistics part is BORING.

Decent teacher but expects you to have your notes completely memorized word for word to do really good on his exams.  Like the last person wrote, hes a teacher that has a multiple choice test with 6-7 choices for each answer, so its hard to guess, lol

Some of the lectures left something to be desired.  But most of them were really interesting and engaging.  he loves nature.  he always talks about his trip to borneo, it gets old but some of the stories are funny. class is really easy if you study hard

Tests are confusing because he uses the whole A, A & B, A B & C, None of the above thing. I did a lot worse than I thought on tests. Knows his stuff, though. Don't come in late or leave your cell phone on or he'll single you out.
He never responds to e-mails/messages and is EXTREMELY unfriendly. If you write something he disagrees with he will penalize you for it. Avoid this teacher at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. O's lectures and stories about working in the field were my favorite parts about this course. Being an immigrant himself, and experienced working with immigrant communities, he has a great deal of insight and is the perfect person to teach this course. The main assignment of interviewing someone to hear their immigration story was great.

This is one of the best SOWK professors at UMBC. His class is easy and you learn a lot from the readings. Few quizzes, a mid term and a final and a final paper 10-12 pages long but definitely you will have time enough to complete it and is a great grader unlike some of the other professors in the same department.

Dr. O is super knowledgeable about social work and uses real-world examples to enhance your understanding of the subject matter. He responds to emails quickly and is very down to earth and understanding. I bought the textbook but didn't use it once and it didn't affect my grades at all.

I never even touched my textbook for this class and it didn't matter. All grading stuff was super easy, I almost feel like he gave everyone an A. I fought the urge to fall asleep every class. Despite this, I did enjoy taking the class because he gave good information about grad school and how to find success in my field. He was very knowledgeable.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. O is funny and carefree. Assignment due dates might get pushed back. He might get your class confused w/ another one. Technical problems may arise. Class may get canceled. Do the reading. Good review of Human Development class material. Tests are easy. Pay attention in class as he randomly calls on people. He's better w/ interaction than email.

Dr. O is a great professor that cares about his students and wants them to strive to do great things. He is accessible outside of class despite his busy schedule at times. He is a real gem and answers students questions if there are any. He also mentions in class background knowledge from being a therapist on different topics.

Great professor. Put good effort in and you will pass. He does lecturer by sitting in a chair and relaying his points verbally without demonstration. He knows how to explain information and answer questions in a way everyone understands. He encourages questions and gives reasonable assignments. You learn a lot in his classes.

The class overall was easy (exams and quizzes were online and open note/book) but Dr. O was always late and would ramble during lecture. I learned a lot but not from him specifically - more from the book.

Took 374 early this summer & it was great. Dr. O is a great professor and uses his own experiences and makes up scenarios to help his students understand. Attendance was mandatory because it was summer. Would have gotten an A, but didn't study as much as I should have. All in all, a great professor in the Social Work dept.

I had Dr. O for SOWK 388 & 374, he is very thorough, he offer's extra credit and his availability is always flexible if you need to see him. Everything he talks about in class he uploads to blackboard, gives great feedback on papers. The class is very enthusiast not boring at all. Just show up, pay attn & read you will get easy A. Best Prof ever!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I LOVE Dr. O!!! I will be taking his class next semester as well. A lot of students find him to be disorganized and don't like that he goes off on tangents. I happen to like his type of eccentricity, and I take to it well. The exams are easy as long as you read and have your notes and book by your side as you take them. Def recommend!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Okay so I am not the biggest fan of Dr. O but he isn't a difficult professor, I just don't like how disorganized he can be and how for every class we spend 20 or 30 minutes (in a 75 min class period) talking about random things... it's unnecessary! BUT exams are open book open note (Ctrl F is your friend)dont wait to do the papers-use the rubric
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Took 389 as a hybrid. Some online quizzes/exams & some in-class, but neither were very hard as he made them open note/book. Dr. O assigns two 10 pg. papers, but they're straightforward as long as you answer all questions, follow rubrics, and maintain page limits. Funny guy, very passionate, asked him to be my adviser I loved is classes that much!

He's alright. Nice enough. He does not use powerpoint, which is fine but his lectures can be very disorganized which is frustrating. He really overemphasizes spirituality and religion, making those who are non spiritual or religious uncomfortable. Class is easy, just a few assignments, lots of extra credit BUT he is really strict about attendance.

Nice,considerate professor who is ALWAYS willing to help& clarify.Impossible to fail;just attend class &he'll tell you EXACTLY what you need to know to pass the course&succeed in the field.Very knowledgable&prepares students for the future not just this one class. Definitely one of the best professors at UMBC!

Awful professor... He was frequently late and ill-prepared. His exams were full of obscure facts/statistics from the text. His lectures consisted of him reading from a study guide in the book. Nice guy, awful professor.

Interesting class material but did not have a clear structure for lectures. No powerpoints and over specific tests. Interesting guy but difficult to know if you are meeting his expectations on papers or on tests.

Dr. O really knows his stuff. He is also very personable and down to earth. I would say that it is sometimes hard to follow his lectures because he does not use powerpoint, but overall, I learned a lot in his class.
Great Teacher!

Dr. O is a great professor. He is very passionate about the profession and has experience in many different areas of social work. He comes from a more clinical/medical mindset which was helpful for those of us interested in medical/mental health/private practice.

The professor is very helpful to his students. His philosophy of class is to prepare students for practice (their career). The information he teaches is very practical. The professor does everything possible to help his student obtain excellent grades. His study guides are extremely helpful - study them for an A on his tests.

Great Professor. Instead of finding devious ways of tripping up his students, the professor finds ways to make the class material clear, practical, and applicable. One of the best teachers I have had.
Great teacher, really makes it interesting. I actually became a Social Work major because of on of his human behavior classes.
awesome, good class. love it
Class is fairly easy if you come to all classes and do all the assignments.. Very nice and funny guy.. I got a B but I could have gotten an A

One of the best professors I have ever had. Great personality, very easy to relate to, you can tell he cares and he makes learning fun. I would recommend anyone take a class with him. He is very insightful and just an overall great professor and person.
Awesome teacher, incredibly informative, helpful and understanding. Very fair grading, loved his class

Dr. O is a great professor! He is always willing to help students with papers, issues with the class, etc. There is a lot of psych in the class so brush up on your old psych notes. Awesome professor, cannot wait to have him for another class!
Very nice Professor.  Really wants you to do well.  Make sure to use the writing labs on papers, otherwise as long as you follow instructions you will do well.
He is a great professor. I really enjoyed his classes!
Awesome.

Dr. O is an awesome teacher and wants all of his students to do well. At first it was hard for me to understand him but after the 1st 2 classes I had pretty much picked up on his accent. He is very knowledgeable and has a lot of experience in the field.
GREAT!
Took him for 388 & 389. Great guy. Incredibly smart but teaching really isn't his forte. If you read and write decent papers you will receive a good grade.

This class was nearly identical to psych100, but even easier. His first exam was hard, but the second one was a breeze. He grades his papers very easily, so long as you follow the guidelines. At first he was frustrating, but he got better.
Dr. O is really funny...he tends to be a little unclear about exams and papers but overall its not a difficult class...i actually enjoyed it.

At first it was kind of annoying but he works with students. Compromises often, don't make annoy him. He is funny, cares about students. SOWK majors take this class with him. Best SOWK class I took thus far.
Dr O is very good I would recommend taking him if you can
Dr. O is great, once you get the rythem of his accent he is easy to understand.  He brings a ton of clinical and research exp. to his class discussion. Highly recommend him.

I took him for both human behavior classes! He is so much fun! I little boring at times because he lectures straight from the book but it makes it easy to follow along, he also cracks jokes every now and ok which are pretty funny, he also some how knows everything! very good guy highly recomendable

Very knowledgable man with good insights.  Class feels like an expanded PSYCH 101 class though.  They tried out a new text book (author: Schriver) that is ABSOLUTELY AWFUL. But Dr. O is very good, very accessible and (mostly) comprehesible.
He has a wonderful personality, very funny. He made the class very interesting. He was always willing to help me when I needed him to. His accent was not a problem for me at all. I enjoyed this class
He is a very helpful teacher.  This class is easy to take in because of his good personality.  He is funny.  His class is a class that I enjoyed.
Mr. Okundaye is a very nice teacher. Its a little hard to understand him sometimes due to his accent. But he's ok. He grades a little hard but he's very funny and keeps the class intresting.
Great teacher, make sure you pay attention though.

Dr. Oyen is very nice and clearly has a lot of passion for the field of Asian studies. Course was graded on in-class participation which could be made up online through discussion posts if you weren't in class, and 5 unit tests (no mid-term or final), along with a final project and a paper.

-Very few assignments: 10 in-class, midterm, final project (whole semester to write 6 pages), final
-Lenient grading, just need to show you understood general diasporic trends and events
-Primarily lectures, but I found them very engaging with interesting stories
-20 pages of reading per week, all provided on Blackboard

You can tell Dr. Oyen is really excited to talk about her area of study. The lectures were all very fun and concise, and there were many opportunities for us to chime in and discuss the topic at hand. There's a handful of quizzes and essays, but they are a piece of cake if you take notes during the lectures. Overall, loved the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Nice prof and enjoys what she teaches. Very knowledgeable and will help you through your papers. The first paper i wrote got a B but her notes made me realize what i had done wrong and the second paper i got a 97. There are group discussions and the class material was quite intriguing.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Oyen includes interesting informations on her slides, and it will be helpful to jot some notes during lectures. She will give out study guide for mid term and final, so make sure to prepare the outline for the essay portion. The class overall was not hard as long as you come to lecture; however, pay attention to the lessons, not your phone!!

She is a very nice person and truly passionate about her field however, her teaching structure wasn't good and she was a pretty harsh grader. As long as you go to class, and do well on the midterm and final you should be good.

She graded a level 100 class like a 400 level. I have taken level 600 classes at UMBC and got A's on essays fairly easily. However, I was shocked to see how tough she grades for a level 100 class. I wouldn't reccomend taking a class with her if you care about your GPA like I do. Kissing my 4.0 goodbye, I guess. Preparing for her final is hell.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: take any class you can with dr oyen! she uses clear rubrics, is pretty easy to reach via email or office hours, and gives helpful advice. she's open to students asking questions or challenging her lectures. not too much reading for a 400-level class. three papers, 'reading response' homework checks, and some in-class activities. phenomenal.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: clear rubrics and helpful advice. her passion for her subject is infectious; never thought i'd have so much fun learning historiography. as long as you genuinely apply yourself, you can succeed! the only class i've had where the lectures are informative AND involve memes and also the princess bride. looking forward to taking more classes with her!
She makes history fun to learn, and she's extremely helpful and willing to talk to you about any concerns you have. Just make sure you attend class on time and you're fine.

By far one of the worst classes I took at UMBC. I wrote the final paper & I did not get the grade I deserved. If I did not need this class for my major I would have never taken it. She is a very hard grader and won't tell you what you did wrong. Her lectures are nothing but a PowerPoint without any notes. Don't take this class if you don't have to.

Dr. Oyen is easily one of my favorite teachers at UMBC. She's  approachable and helpful, and her 201 class last semester shaped the way I write and study history. I hope I can take another class with her!

This course is an easy A.  The only required reading is online, you don't really need to use the textbook. Attendance is mandatory. A 15 page paper is required along with blackboard postings throughout the semester. Overall a great professor.

She just started teaching the class and she should stop after this year. She's uptight, passively condescending on a regular basis. Her mouth says one thing but her grading says another. She made a class that  basically is the 100 level in a history major a 400 level class. She made the paper more difficult that what it really needed to be
Great Professor

Asynchronous over winter semester. Homework was very similar to 103 which was fine. Had some other assignments each week (speaking, culture). On a speaking activity, prof got mad b/c everyone did it wrong (spoiler: his instructions were not clear at all). Reused questions from homework on quizzes/tests. Feedback was rare, and unhelpful when given.

Decent professor. Homework assignments primary way to learn content. In-class lectures review of homework. Sometimes felt like he was reaching for student participation too hard. Quizzes and tests not particularly difficult. Listen in class because sometimes he doesn't post details about projects, quizzes, etc. Clearly says what will be on quiz
Great prof.

had him again last semester. indeed one of the best prof on campus..I have a conflict with his course this semester but am looking forward to take his course next semester. I learned a lot from his last couple courses. Samir is an Excellent prof easy going and willing to explain and help.. he wants his students to learn PERIOD!

He isn't the best or most informative prof but he's really nice and an easy grader. He does tend to ramble and go a bit over time but it isn't too bad. You do a lot of work online and he tells you to do smaller textbook based assignments but he never collects them or grades them. He is very easy to please and nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--GROUP PROJECTS--Would take again

reviews.comment: He is a nice enough guy, but he will tell you things are due a few days before their due dates. Very unclear with directions. Lenient grader on tests. Expect to spend a lot of time (and money) on the online work for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's has a really nice personality and is lenient with grading tests but he is EXTREMELY unclear on assignments and only gives you details for huge assignments a week beforehand. A lot of the students were asking each other about the assignments afterwards and even then, everyone heard something different from him. Unclear & unorganized. See tags.
He is a fun professor and the tests are really fair and easy if you do homework. I enjoy his classes.
Professor Omari means well and has great intentions, but he is very disorganized and know it because he has too much on his plate. Fortunately he knows this and adjusts his grading accordingly.
one of the best I have had on campus

Although Samir is well-intentioned, his lack of clarity and plethora of assignments overshadow this trait. I often found myself not knowing what or when an assignment was due. Due to how many assignments were given, it felt like a 300 level course. Oftentimes, the large amount of assignments felt unnecessary. Despite this, he was a lenient grader.

Samir can be a little unclear at times, but he is more than willing to help you understand. He said something the other day like "I want you to learn; I'm not here to punish you." There is a TON of homework, but it is essential. Beware, he can get very distracted very quickly. Do the homework and come to class, and you will do well.
best professor i've ever had, well rounded and culturally rich. very approachable friendly and helpful

I LOVED Samir! He is a really nice guy. I was dreading taking a French course, but he made it bearable. The classes were pretty disorganized and I found that I had to do alot of learning independantly, but I think that is just the nature of the course. He had lots of funny stories and was very forgiving in his grading.
VERY GOOD
So nice! Great guy and really wants his students to do well! There is a lot of online work to do, but it is very easy. I highly recommend taking a class with him!
Hands down, the best professor at UMBC. One must take one of his French or Arabic classes at least once during their time at UMBC.
This class was easier than highschool french in my opinion. My lowest grade on anything in the class was a 79% Samir is a very very nice man! I highly recommend him!

Such a nice guy. Has a LOT on his plate; sometimes lectures can feel a bit rushed. If you don't do the workbook exercises on your own time, you'll fall behind easily. Don't leave the binder work til the last day. Everything on the tests is covered in class. Be prepared to move pretty fast 102-onwards. Love this man.

He has such a sweet & cute personality. He's always happy to answer questions and help. He's a busy guy teaching a lot of classes and he's also an academic adviser. He will always answer your questions during or after class. DO YOUR WORKBOOK work & all other homework and you will do great. Takes attendance but I'm not sure if it's part of the grade
Had Samir for French 103 and 202. Very sweet and helpful. EXCELLENT teacher despite the poor French curriculum. Moroccan, but knows a lot about many Francophone countries.

Samir is a very nice man and takes care to explain vocabulary and grammar that his students do not understand. He grades easily--do the C-Hour, homework, and tests, and you're guaranteed an A. Hampered by the inane 202 curriculum, but otherwise a great guy.
He's a nice guy. Pretty absent minded about the quizzes. Doesn't fllow the syllabus, gets sidtracked easily, is not clear about what homework is to be done. class is not very interactive.

A really sweet guy. He was very helpful, and took time to thoroughly explain a concept if the students were having trouble understanding it. He likes to learn from the students, too, regarding English idioms and expressions. It was a really fun class, and easy, too (at least I thought so, but then again I really love French).

Arabic. Samir is the best professor I've had at UMBC. He is incredibly helpful, and since his class sizes are small, he gets to know all his students, which may or may not help when the final grade is decided. His accent can get in the way sometimes, but  attend class, and do the homework, and you will surely get an A. Samir is an amazing professor

I love Samir. I wish I had been able to take 201 with him. He is one of the easiest professors to understand and very nice. He only canceled class when he had to leave the country because his father was sick and passed away.

A really nice person who goes out of his way to help his students. Relatively easy class, just a lot of homework. Sometimes unclear on explanation, but at least his exams are really easy. Had him for three consecutive semesters. I highly recommend him.

I really liked this professor, it is obvious that he cares about his students and really does what he can to help them. I took the class over summer and it was a lot of work, but I learned more than I ever thought I would. Definitely recommend him!!!

This guy is the best. If you have any questions, at all, he will explain it very well. Sometimes he explains so well he gives actual answers on exams. He gives a lot of extra work but they are very easy and helpful. I seriously reccomend him for every student especially those that are not that good in french. I guarentee you that you will have an A

Nice guy, but a little unclear. He expects very much from his Arabic students and moves extremely fast. I took his class during winter session, so it may not be accurate, but I found the class very hard and didn't learn much. Take his class if you must, but he is not ideal.
Great Professor!  He really wants you to learn the language.  His exams are fair and are graded fairly.  I love Samir...he really cares about each student.
He was very kind.  The class was easy.  He's almost too easy on exams.  I liked the compositions he gave us to do.  Good at explaining things and making you learn.
He is incredibly nice and hot in an odd, awkward, shy way. Really makes the class easy and is very approachable! SEKSAYYYY BEAST

This professor usually teaches french from what I hear but I had him for Arabic and he is without a doubt one of the most caring teachers I have ever met. He is extremely sensitive to students and his class is very easy to understand. If not, ask and he will make time to explain it to you.

Excellent lectures, explained things well and related them to things everyone would be able to understand. Very funny, ask him about his barber shop quartet. Does not allow formula sheets, firm that you should be able to "convince him you know what you're talking about" when taking exams. Do the homework without notes when possible for practice.

Explains things in depth and is reasonable with the difficulty. Lectures are recorded (audio only) and content is posted reliably. Plenty of homework to builds understanding. Exams are very fair. He also posts a plethora of other resources for practice, and does everything in his power to set everyone up for success. TAs are also awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nanes' lectures are cool. He's a chill guy and is willing to help. If you actually study, doing well in this class is super doable. Beware of the first quiz/exam and study more than you think you need to. Overall, Nanes makes it possible to do well if you put in effort.
The way I can't even read this guy's handwriting, and its suppose to be math, just pick another teacher. Does the absolute most for no reason(math 215)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Be ready to study, when he says you need to know something that means you have to spend 4 hours that night learning how to solve the problem in various ways. 

Quizzes are usually fair until they give you something you havent learned yet???

Grading is usually very fair but if you dont do well on exams then it will be a hard class

If you put in the work, you will do just fine. Dr. Nanes is an amazing professor. He actually made me enjoy calculus. Super funny and nice guy. He gives you all of the materials, advice, funny T-shirts, and anything else you would need to succeed in the class. It's a hard course, Dr. Nanes makes it doable. Also, he's a very lenient grader.

He's a fantastic prof who knows his stuff, he's a little dramatic and tends to exaggerate the difficulty of units but its because he truly wants his students to succeed and be prepared. He will work with you if you work with him. Talk to him, he's a complete nerd and if you're into video games he's the guy to talk to.

One of my favorite professors I've had so far on this campus. I highly recommend attending lectures, they are very worthwhile and better than just reading and taking notes on the textbook. Grading is pretty chill, always has 10 extra points in exams. He's just a cool guy all around.

Lenient grader, gives extra credit, but lectures aren't very helpful. Spends lectures reviewing reading quizzes and going on tangents. Explanations are wordy and vague. Focuses on doing problems wrong to prove how not to do things. Goes overtime often. Rude when approached with questions. Class isn't difficult, but not the best with Nanes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: For Introductory Real Analysis guaranteeing suffering, Dr. Nanes turned this once-torturous experience into a very digestible class. The homeworks are most valuable, which he gives guidance, his lecture notes are thorough and very valuable, and the pre-readings make lecture material easier. Dr. Nanes will always be your best choice for this class.
He very helpful when you need help and the lectures are very clear.

He's the best you've got. Exams/Quizzes may or may not be the same as past ones, but you can completely mess up some quizzes and still get an A. Same with exams, i left a question completely blank still got a B on it. He wants you to pass, just gotta practice math like he says. I'm not a math whiz but passed with an A. Take him if you can for 151

Godsend prof for difficult class, made hard topics very easy to understand and clearly seems like he cares about us and doesn't want to make us suffer. He warns you when class gets hard, so easy A if you stay on top of things. Best math prof at UMBC hands-down. if you need calc 3, take it with Nanes.

Dr. Nanes is a fantastic professor. Students from other math 151 classes would come to his lectures because they were much better than the lectures in their class. The grading was quite lenient, and Dr. Nanes was frequently available for homework help.

The things he tests you on (quizzes, exams) are studiable, but you just won't get by with using only past keys-- he actually switches up the questions to test your understanding. He is a no-BS type of person. Bad reviews are probably from people who tried bs-ing in some way and it didn't fly. He gives you everything you need to succeed-- "lock in".

I am absolutely horrible at math and I wholeheartedly think I would have failed with any other professor. Nanes gives insane amounts of partial credit on exams and he clearly knows what he's talking about. He makes concepts as simple as he can and gives lots of practice problems. If you have to take this class, take it with him.

Dr Nanes is a good professor when he wants to be. He missed class and arrived late a bunch and would glance over topics he decided were easy. The harder topics felt easier because he was really good when he  actually cared. Exams were fair but quizzes were sometimes based off barely covered material. If you have past 3D knowledge you should be good

Good extra credit opportunities, lenient grader. The lectures can be very longwinded at times but the practice problems are similar to homeworks, quizzes, and exams! That tough question you think "won't be on the exam" will 1000% be on the exam

I took this guys class a couple semesters ago. I just had a nightmare about it and thought I'd write a review. He is very demotivating and does not explain anything at all. He's pretty much in his own world when going through problems. He makes this class 10 times harder because he likes being funny and making “funny questions”.

Great techer for a difficult class, spent time going over and making sure a topic was in-depth covered. He makes the exams and prepares you correctly for them. Uploads his lectures and notes taken directly after the class which I depended on to pass. Made it so I could sleep in and cover the lectures myself. Godsend teacher for this class.

Professor Nanes is a really good professor. He's the only professor at umbc who makes linear algebra less of a nightmare (because the class is already hard) but he makes it so much easier to understand

Genuine guy who makes lectures effective to the extent that they're mandatory if you want to succeed in this class. As far as testing, he doesn't try to throw you off or trick you with a problem that is completely new. Everything will be similar to the old exams provided for practice. If you're taking Math151, or Math251, I highly recommend Nanes.

Nanes was a good prof when it comes to lectures and explaining topics. However, on some of the exams and quizzes, there are questions that he doesn't go over. Also, the pre lecture reading quizzes that are 10 percent of the grade are unnecessarily hard. He also shows up late like every day. Besides these things he is a good teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is one of those professor you have to take because the others aren't as good compared to him.
Great Prof, all I have to say.

Nanes comes to class every day in very silly shirts and is one of the best professors I've had in terms of their teaching ability, he breaks down and explains concepts very thoroughly. He did have a tendency to go over time for the first few weeks but got much better. His quizzes can be tricky but you'll do well if you understand the material

Professor Nanes is a very good math professor, he gives many extra credit opportunities and attending his lectures would make it easy to take the exams. He also posts his lectures for our reference. He does teach what the textbook contents are and it would help to use the text for prep. He is also easily accessible outside class.

Cares about all his students, a lot of homework and reading, but he always drops a couple in the final grading. Definitely go to his office hours, because not only will he explain things to you, but there are always other students there who are willing to help. Definitely gonna try to take another one of his courses again.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Nanes has so much personality in his lectures which keeps him engaging throughout. He also made Calculus easier to understand. Would highly recommend taking him for math classes

He shows up to lecture at least 5 minutes late almost every time. Cancelled lecture every other week and put up incomplete recordings of previous years lectures. one recording literally starts with him saying "Oops, I'm not recording" and just includes the second half of an example problem. He seems like a nice guy, and is a generous grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: amazing funny prof. he explains in a way that is comprehendible to the point you feel confident in what you doing. big preacher of practice makes perfect. his 3 exams are basically identically topic formatted like the previous semester's exams. my biggest tip is to look at your own notes and create practice questions rather than HW from WebAssign.

Linear Algebra gives you 20 definitions for the same thing. Dr. Nanes does a really good job of breaking these definitions down and connecting them to one another, and just making the lectures engaging and enjoyable. The tests are fair with extra credit built in. It is important to read before class, but that is b/c of the material, not Nanes.

Honestly, he's a good professor. For most of the lecture, he writes down the topics and explains them as he goes. He really encourages students to study, and he even has office hours and group discussions to explain very hard topics on calc. Also, he's very heavy with exams and quizzes, but that's to be expected for most math courses.
Generally good Professor, lectures were clear, work and grading mostly fair, but some grades were overwhelming and feedback discouraging.

Never had a professor thats been absent so many times! Literally was teaching myself throughout this semester because he decides to be absent every other week. There's weekly quizzes, and exams are pretty tough. I highly recommend any professor over him, as he likes to fly through lectures. If you do choose to take him all I can say is good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've encountered at this school so far. The only way to pass this course is if you teach yourself. He likes to rush through notes and rush through example problems. He's also quite insulting towards the class especially when exam averages aren't what he expects them to be. Better off with a different professor honestly.
The lectures he give really make the material super digestible when the textbook is overwhelming. He cares a lot, and makes lectures engaging and fun!

Worst prof i've taken by far. He's very demotivating and doesn't explain things well. He goes through problems super fast and doesn't really explain anything. He also assigns a lot of homework. I don't know why he has mostly 5 star ratings.
Great guy Really good at teaching calculus as he whips up equations from the top of his head, also funny that keeps lectures less boring 100% recommend.
Amazing professor which made the difficulty of the class seem a bit more manageable. Lectures are not required but are highly recommended as he is excellent at covering the most difficult topics.

At the start he seemed very intimidating, telling us how we needed to study for hours to pass. Yes, studying that amount is excessive, but doing it helps a lot. He tells exactly what material is covered on each quiz/exam, so there really isn't a surprise since the homework's are almost identical. GO TO LECTURE! He will really teach the material.
15 hours per week of hw, not worth

if you're a bio or non-stem major, take Nanes over Tighe for MATH 151. i took Tighe, then had to retake this semester. Nanes' exams and quizzes were MUCH easier than those of Tighe's. also after each exam you get 5 extra points just for showing up to the following discussion period. homework makes you suffer tho. nanes is a funny human in lecture

You have every opportunity to succeed in this class, from extra credit to an abundance of studying resources, so if you put in the work you will pass this class. Lectures are not mandatory, but if you do not go you will fall behind. Professor very clearly states what you need to know for the exam so you will never be blindsided by exam questions.

Nanes kept great notes on his iPad. Most of the time his notes are just walk-throughs of previous homework questions and reading quiz questions. Was good at emphasizing the imperative things to remember. Quizzes were incredibly fair. This course being online made it much easier, but Nanes provided enough help that outside sources weren't needed.

Prof Nanes was awesome, best prof at UMBC for Linear Algebra. He cares about his students, he's clear about what will be on exams and quizzes, and he's very helpful if you are having trouble. Its obvious that he wanted us to succeed, and most of us did.

Calc 3 is hard by itself, but he made it easier. Had to learn content on your own, but reviewed most of it in class. Don't take this class with a heavy workload. Weekly homework was not hard, but def needed more practice before quizzes/exams. Very funny and caring in class. Went through exam answers after the exam in discussion (always beneficial)

He is the best professor for Math 221 as of 2022. He grades fairly, cares for his students, and wants everyone to succeed, but you do have to put in a lot of work.  His feedback on quizzes and exams is fantastic, they may be mean sometimes, but I know where I lost points, and what to look back on.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: lecture consisted mostly around just reviewing reading quiz answers which I did not like, but when he actually taught it was really very good. Pretty average total workload. Material on exams/quizzes should not surprise you. Final exam was very generous. no questions are designed to trick, just test knowledge. Overall, very satisfied

He is probably the worst math professor I've ever had in all my years ofschooling. first of all the structure of his class is awful he has the class take a quiz on the stuff you learned 1-2 weeks ago while also having to do a reading quiz about different stuff. and his lectures are no help either when you ask for help he always has an arrogant ans

He was a great professor! Has syllabus with everything laid out with due dates and quiz and test days which is good for staying organized. The reading quizzes are due before classes, which is the same as for homework. Great Professor one of the best math professors at UMBC. Only thing is that it is a lot of individual studying and work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Nanes really wants students to learn. The course is very fast-paced and the homework takes an extremely long time and is just excessive. The TAs grade the homework harshly. The quizzes and exams were easy compared to the homework. He provides previous exams and quizzes from whence you can study which is extremely helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: The structure of this course is teach yourself. You are assigned reading quizzes BEFORE lecture (graded on accuracy). He explains stuff well but seldom is he actually teaching rather reviewing his quizzes. It just is not flexible to different learning styles. He has humor but that does not help you learn at the end of the day
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Get ready to learn by reading. If you don't do well learning out of a textbook, this class will be difficult. There is a quiz at the beginning of the semester based on your Calc 1 & 2 skills. Be prepared to take reading quizzes before he even goes over the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He truly wants you to succeed in Calc 3. He is extremely generous when it comes to extra credit (e.g. chance to get 120% on each exam, drops two quizzes, five hw's, etc.). Exams are a breeze for the most part if you have an understanding of the material and every practice exam question. The class is very manageable imo. Thanks Dr. Nanes!

It seems that online Nanes < in-person Nanes by a lot. I took this course during quarantine. 4 webassigns, 2 reading checks, 1 quiz almost every week. Nanes likes trick questions. Regarding his lectures, he just works through the reading checks which were graded prior to the lecture... so basically repeating what we had already taught ourselves.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class during quarantine. His lectures consisted of him going over the answers to the reading quiz we were required to complete before lecture. He didn't really teach us anything. We were expected to teach ourselves. Maybe he is better in person. His quizzes often had curve balls in them, which i felt was unnecessarily difficult.
Makes tests and quizzes fairly. Lectures tend to be confusing, but discussion sections make up for it.

Nanes is corny but hes cool. Read the book before class and take notes during. If he goes over an ex, pay attention, those and practice quizzes and exams are key. Nanes lets u know exactly what u do and dont need to know, take advantage of it. He was incredibly understanding about the online situation, he wants you to succeed. Best math prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: his class is pretty straightforward. I joined the class late due to issues for my major, so it was hard to catch up with so much work, but got thru it in the end. very helpful class and pretty easy to get an A if you work hard and know how to do the examples he goes ovr in class as well in discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Nanes! He is such an amazing Professor! He cares for his students and will try to help you pass the class if you are struggling. (Of course, you will have to attend CASTLE or office hours to receive help.) If you do not seek help from him, he will not care if you fail the class. Make sure to do all the hws and practice problems!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: He is a great person and tries to make class fun; moves very quickly on the material. I got a C but did P/F. Webassign is very annoying and there can be a lot so try and do it ahead of time. His class is lecture heavy so take good notes. He is very straight forward on the material so if you use all the resources given you should get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He's a really nice guy if you avoid doing the obvious disrespectful things like talking during class or using your phone. He's a great math teacher and ensures that students understand. If you have a problem with a concept, make it known to him after class or at office hours as soon as possible. He WILL help.

In person, Nanes is great. I enjoyed the classroom approach he takes even though it was weird at first. When we switched to an online setting, he posted lectures from the years before and had weekly office hours. Quizzes and exams were multiple choice. It felt like we were on our own and I wouldn't take this class online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Kalman Nanes is an amazing man with amazing lectures. Getting help from Nanes at castle on Fridays helped keep learn more than I ever have in a math class. He even messaged me to me to confirm I passed when I thought I failed! If you are bad at precalc, expect to work your butt off. He is brutally honest and will tell you you should retake precalc.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Nanes is a gem. He truly wants everyone to succeed in his class. Gave 20 extra credit points throughout the year. Quizzes are easy if you know what you are doing. Exams are tougher but manageable.

Dr. Nanes is a Sweetheart HE CARES ABOUT HIS STUDENTS. If you see him teaching math course I will greatly advice to take him. Math 301 is probably the hardest math class in the whole math main courses but Dr. breaks its downs and really makes it understandable. If you come with the intentions of not doing the work you should probably drop.

Nanes is the best math professor I have ever had! He puts hard stuff in funny and casual understandable terms. He totally made me get out of my "I am bad at math" mentality and I will probably get a B or A at the end of the semester. I legit cannot put into words how much Nanes has changed my outlook on math classes. Amazing professor.

Best 1 for calc3, loves to curse, DO THE PRACTICE EXAMS; he will call people out; you are placed in groups during lecture, for the entire semester; he randomly calls on people and shames them if they aren't correct, but this will force you to keep up; Do the readings (they suck); DO THE PRACTICE EXAMS; 2 quizzes weekly + 1 group quiz weekly
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Worst math professor ever! Lectures are useless. Most time is spent going those small hw quizzes. Has this group learning idea, where your classmates have to "rate you" at the end of the semester. Assing's 4 sets of hw's per week. Stay away!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Absolute worst. I tried to talk to him and was brought to tears to how horrible he is. I will never take his class again.

absolutely great professor. One of the best I've ever had. Very clear lectures and if you ever miss class notes and voice recording is online. previous quizzes are not really similar to one's you'll get. extra credit helps a lot

Dr. Nanes is one of the best professors I've ever had. His lectures are always interesting & he makes sure everyone understands. No surprises on quizzes/exams. He gives opportunities for extra credit and is always accessible for help outside of class. The online homework gets tiring but is an easy way to boost your grade. I'd take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I only rate when professors are either amazing/terrible. Best professor ever. Nanes really knows his stuff and actually wants to see his students succeed. He replies to emails on time and takes time on his lectures. He is always prepared for his materials to cover for lectures. His exams are moderately hard but manageable. Study & practice to pass.

The online assignments can get tiring but DO THEM, they're easy points! Exams are similar to the quizzes. Quizzes were kind of hard for me, but if you practice and pay attention you'll be fine. Look over the 3 exams for the final, it really helps.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: One of the most amazing professors I have ever attended a semester with. He would explain everything so clearly and appreciate your questions. His class is fun and clear. He would make the hardest equation a very simple one. I would absolutely tow his class again.

Dr. Nanes is one of my favorite professors at UMBC. His lectures are so clear and easy to follow. He does a great job at explaining concepts. His tests are very fair and are graded with an extra 10 points so you have the possibility of scoring a 110% on each exam. This class is a lot of group work,which sounds bad at first, but actually is helpful
Makes you work in groups. Fine other than that.

Nanes is amazing, he makes the lecture understandable and clear. In addition to that, he really really cares about his students. It is a pretty hard class because math is hard but if you listen to his advise and try hard you can 100% succeed. I recommend taking him if you have the chance! Also, attendance isn't mandatory but you should still go.

Dr. Nanes is amazing. If you show up to class, stay off your phone and be respectful he is extremely nice. His class is difficult, but he explains everything clearly and is very accessible out of class for extra help. He posts the notes from his lectures online, along with a voice recording of everything he says during lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is an amazing and nice professor but you have to work hard to get an A.

Dr. Nanes is an awesome professor. His grading criteria are hard but he really knows what he is teaching, so make sure to attend all his lectures. He posts all his lectures online and but it is much better to be in the lecture than to skip it. He is a fair professor and you can see he really cares about his students. 10/10
Nanes is a good professor. He teaches what you need to know and posts the audio of lectures online. He is funny, and quite blunt at times.

Nanes is a good professor. He makes Calc 3 more enjoyable. The tests were very fair and had extra credit on each. Homework and online quizzes can be tough to keep up with at times. Last time I took calculus was in high school, and I made it through this class fairly easily. Would recommend, definitely the best option for 251.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Nanes is awesome. He is very helpful and explains material really well. Lots of textbook reading and lots and lots of homework every week but the material is not that hard so Nanes makes the class fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Knowledgeable, nice, and humorous. Class uses Team-based learning and part of your grade is from that. Lots of prep work before class required but as a result you will be prepared when you come in. He's more than willing to put forth effort into helping you learn, so long as you put forth equal effort in learning the material. Take him!

Amazing guy, the math nerd that actually jokes with you and is cool! Only homework assignments are on WebAssign, but the real learning is in his class. You don't have to read the textbook if you just attend his class; teaching is clear, and precise. Don't be the statistic of kids who bomb the final, as long as you study regularly you'll get an A!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Nanes is a great professor, he explains concepts very well, and quiz material will mostly be closely related to examples given in lecture. As long as you don't get lazy you should be fine.

This was the hardest math class I've taken. Nanes mainly took everything in his lectures from the textbook, but still important to pay attention to the lectures. Provided practice quizzes/exams. I really appreciated the quiz drop and curve at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: This class was very difficult, and while I did poorly on some exams he assured the class that as long as you got close to the average score on the quizzes and tests you would pass the class. He ended up curving the grades in such a way that I passed when I thought I might not. So while his class was difficult, he is a good professor that cares.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Easily the best math teacher I've had in my life. Works very hard to make Calculus understandable while occasionally threading humor into his lessons. He truly cares that his students learn the material.

Nanes is the best! I failed calc 2, 3 times. I currently have a B in multivariable with Nanes! I have learned so much, but you have to be able to give this class a lot of time. I typically spend >1.5 hours every day on this class. It has been very rewarding. The class is set up in teams. You can rate teammates at the end and it affects their grades

Nanes is an excellent professor. His team-based learning style was definitely not for me. However, lots of pressure was put on the students through random participation. This made sure that you ACTUALLY knew and practiced the material. He offers practice exams/quizzes which are very similar to those you take during the semester. Go to him for help!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Heard great things about Nanes, but none of them showed in class. He taught directly from book, so there was no incentive to come to lecture. Examples were either easier or more complex than quiz and exam questions. You best hope for this class is webassign reading/homework grade scale, practice exams and quizzes, and the quality of your TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Nanes was the best professor that I have had so far. Group grading sounded like a terrible idea until I saw what it really meant. He holds everyone accountable and you will not be brought down by your group. TAKE HIM IF YOU GET THE CHANCE.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Best math professor I've ever had by far. Really cares about his students. This is the first math course I've ever genuinely enjoyed. It's hard, but if you put in the effort, you'll do fine. Nanes gives really helpful explanations and is really available outside class. It's a lot of group work, but that ends up helping you rather than hurting you.
Loved Dr. Nanes in my fall semester. He was a very hilarious lecturer, he would joke round a lot, and most of the material was very easy. His old quizzes were very helpful.

One of the best professors I have had explained difficult content in ways that made it easy to understand grade was made up partially of work done in groups which gave you the chance to do well even if you are not a good test taker. Would highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Great prof! As long as you do your homework and study for exams (which he often reuses exact problems from previous ones) you'll get an A. I really enjoyed the team component of it and he is a fair grader. Grades on understanding not arithmetic. Would most definitely take again for another class.

I heard he is good in other classes, not 152. Nanes did not teach us anything. You will need to learn all the material yourself and will be quizzed on it before even any examples are given in class. Watch his reading guides, they really do help. Very heavy group work. The online individual quizzes are the same as the in class team daily quizzes.

Nanes is a good professor, but the material isn't easy stuff. Since this was his first semester teaching it, all we did in lecture was go over the examples in the textbook. If you study the notes, do practice problems, and understand the definitions/theorems, it's not impossible to get a good grade.

Honestly, Nanes is a top notch professor. Easily breezing through exams and quizzes, Nanes prepares you for exactly what he's testing you for. Not only this, but he also has fun and hilarious lectures that actively engage the students in participating and understating the concept. His class is set up differently, you are put in teams for this class

I hated math for a long time, and I honestly dreaded this class. However, Professor Nanes is such a stellar teacher that not only did I pass with flying colors, I found myself loving the material. Attendance isn't mandatory per se, but he notices and will not hide his opinions of those who skip.

I've had Dr. Nanes for Calc 1, Calc 3, and Linear.  I always pick him if he's available since I find he is the best math professor I've ever had.  He like group work for larger classes since if keeps every group member accountable (ideally).  Book heavy with pre lecture quizzes, lots of other assignments as well but doesn't feel overwhelming.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: My all-time favorite professor.  Definitely the best professor in the department, in my opinion, and one of the best professors at UMBC.  I had him for both Linear and Math 301, and I enjoyed both classes with him.  He makes incredibly challenging subjects much easier to understand, and is very understanding himself.  Take a class with him!
Muhammad Ali of teaching math

I would consider Nanes to be the best professor within the Math department, if not in the entire school. His classes are hard, however he is exceptional at rephrasing the material for your particular level in math. This class was the third time I took nanes. this class was definitely more challenging but very doable. Expect to put in time.
He's the man. I got an easy A+ in the class, but I learned everything and he was very rigorous. Take him. He's one of the best lectures in UMBC math.

Awesome professor!  Made a very difficult subject understandable.  He understands that students have other classes, and won't be constantly perfect.  He structures his classes to give a lot of grace for bad test/quiz/homework days

At the beginning of the semester, he was a good professor. Everything was clear, I understood everything. Halfway through the semester, he kinda started rushing through the problems/lectures. Does judge you for not knowing some prior things about calculus. Always remember e^0 , ln(1) 0, cos(0)1. Exams same thing as practice tests, final: HARD
Best professor I've ever had. The class is hard, but it's easier with him than other professors, because he knows how to explain the material.
Nanes is the man

He is such a great professor! Best math professor since High School. He is very accommodating if students have conflicts about exams with other classes (I had to take 2 exams and the final at a different time). He is willingly to help his students as long as they show interest in learning and improving. Hilarious, great, totally awesome person!

Great professor! I would take him again in a heartbeat. I didn't think I would like the team based learning approach, but it was actually great. He knows his stuff. He records his nots and lectures and puts them online which is amazing.
Great professor!  Lots of work but if you do it you will succeed!

Dr. Nanes is a great teacher! Dont let team based learning scare you away! Hes the best teacher Ive had at UMBC so far. He explains concepts really well. Exams have extra points built in. If you have a good group, team based learning can be awesome! Study previous exams to prepare for exams.

Unclear sometimes and expected us to know things already. If you took Calc 1 in hs then this class will be easier i would think. Tests were pretty similar to practice tests. Hard final.
