truly the most caring prof. i accidentally missed a 100 point assignment, making my final grade a B, but she let me turn in the assignment a month after the semester ended, and changed my final grade to an A. because you have to take prac 096 with this course, she doesnt give too many assignments, with the most difficult being a presentation.

attendance is graded but classes are hybrid. we used class time to learn about education in baltimore & work on group projects. class always finished early & i usually used the time as a free period. she's a rlly easy grader, super easy to get an A.
She is so amazing and was really understanding I am definitely going to sign up for one of her other classes in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Williams, is an outstanding professor. She wants 's you to succeed in her classes. She does grade work late sometimes, and is very accommodating towards the students who missed the previous lectures! The course load can be very light depending on how you manage your time. Quizzes aren't complicated as long as you do the readings before class.

Professor Williams is amazing! I really enjoyed her FYS class and the assignments were not difficult as long as you do them ahead of time. There is a mandatory service requirement and another assignment where you have to attend one social justice event, but Dr. Williams provides you good resources to finish the assignments. She is also super sweet!

I took her in the Fall semester, she was amazing. You are graded by very few easy assignments. She gives a lot of extra credit. She would end class early, a lot. She's understanding, grades efficiently, and just overall very easy class to pass.

She is a wonderful professor. She does not give much homework and class goes by fast. She also likes to split the class into groups for small things, but it is never too challenging. Overall the class is one of the easiest classes I have taken, as long as you pay attention. You will be fine. She is accommodating and can help you if you need it.
Dr. Vickie Williams is very accommodating and caring.

The best professor i've ever had at UMBC. Dr. Williams is one of the most caring and kind professors that I have ever had. I've learned so much about child and education psychology. Our assignments were mostly discussion posts, the midterm was an easy MC test, and the final was a fun paper! TAKE HER!!! YOU'LL LOVE HER!!!

Wonderful Professor. She is everything one could look for in a good teacher. She groomed us to be sound professionals & made working w/her interesting & memorable experience. I will always be grateful for her support & kindness. She opened my eyes to new stages of opportunity & strength, & appreciate and treasure everything she taught me.

Her class was one of the easiest Ive ever taken. She almost is never clear with what you have to do but if you email or talk to her shes super understanding. The work is super easy and shes extremely sweet

reviews.comment: Dr. Williams is a very respectable and reasonable prof. She acknowledges not every student does well on tests and offers many extra credit opportunities. Syllabus is AWESOME! Explains everything clearly and includes syllabi for all assignments.

reviews.comment: Gives so much extra credit it is hard not to get an A+

She is my favorite person in this world. nice
SHE IS AMAZING! ALSO MY ADVISOR! i turned into more than 5 assignments late and still received an A you'll also learn alot! I WISH SHE TAUGHT ALL EDUCATION COURSES

Dr. Williams is a very sweet lady. She tries to make the course as easy and clear as possible and is one of the fairest and most lenient graders out there. Very nice teacher, reasonable guidelines. Final project was a group Powerpoint. As long as you try, you will get a good grade

She's friendly, knowledgeable about the subject and a very easy grader... but I personally found it kind of hard to be super interested in the class and sort of felt like it was a waste of my time and stuff I already learned. Great teacher! Very kind and helpful. She cares about her students, and it shows!

Excellent teacher who practices great teaching techniques in her classroom!  She cares about students' learning and wants to produce high quality teachers.  She is always available when students need her.  Would take her class again!

Oh Vickie! She is so taken advantage of and she knows it but she loves everyone. I loved this teacher she is such a spacey teacher. You can get away with not doing anything in her class and she will deliver an A. Totally a good class to take if you need to finish the dumb upper level requirements. Her laugh is very Fran Dresher.

Very easy teacher. Pretty much a review of PSYC 100 but with an education twist. If you take the night section, like I did, you get out of class by 6 usually and you have at least 3 classes that you do online instead of in class.

Dr. Williams is incredibly easy to get along with & makes it difficult to get anything other than an "A". Constructive criticism would be great (even on an A+ paper)

Dr. Williams puts everything you need to know for tests on powerpoints that she hands out to you.  Projects are easy, lots of groupwork. A good portion of the class is online, so you end up not going to class half the time.
Easy A...

Dr. Williams, formally a practicing psychologist, understands the process of education from the inside out. Besides, much of her class time is filled with our presentations, so if we don't learn from one another, what's that say about us as teachers?

VERY easy.  Actually told us that "you have to try very hard not to get an 'A' in my class."  A couple powerpoint presentations, but nothing too difficult.  Almost all work done in groups.  DEF a GPA booster
She is VERY nice, very easy (A's all through) and very interested in diverse points of view. Great progessor and if you have a hard semester, take her class(es) just to be able to chill.

EASY A!  Reads straight from power points.  Not too time spent in class.  No surprises about what you are being graded on.  Don't stress over her work...its not hard.  Annoying laugh & is a little obsessed with equality in the classroom between boys and girls.

If you want to learn something about Educational Psychology do not take this class.  If you want an easy A or B do. She seems very nice but her (very rare) lectures are directly read from PP.  She gives out clear rubrics but almost no other guidance for the projects, which are 100% of your grade.

She is definitely an easy teacher, and has a great personality- but don't expect to get much else from the class. I hate to say it, but I felt like it was a waste of my time and money. I have taken two classes with her and walked away feeling cheated. If your looking for an easy class this is it.
She is a good teacher.She uses the principles she teaches.

nice teacher, annoying laugh, but really nice. cares about her students and love what she does. you work in groups a lot and write a few easy papers. class does not always meet, but she always tells you in advance and gives online assignments instead.

Very saddening! Often fails to grade assignments on time. Some of the assignments were ungraded well after the semester ended. Barely replies to the emails, even though the course is completely online. The course is poorly designed. She blamed the wrong grade being displayed throughout the semester due to a Blackboard error, and did not fix it.

Ms. Caitlin is a caring and supportive instructor. While the Bio 233 textbook is a necessary requirement, the course itself is manageable for students who stay on top of their assignments and deadlines.

Prof. Varisco is an easy grader as long as you follow the syllabus. She does give extra credit opportunities and makeup assignments with proper documentation.

BIOL 101 not 233. Not sure what the other reviews are getting at—Professor Varisco is one of the best professors I've had at UMBC. She made students purchase a $75-$110 textboook and assigned only like 10 pages through the ENTIRE semester. Varisco relied on dense slides-reading directly from them with little explanation&made class feel overwhelming, w/ quiz/exam based on irrelevant info. Nutrition should be engaging,but wasn't.The course felt unproductive, with memorization over understanding.The groupproject was also weird-analyzing students' eating habits.

This professor is horrible; she doesn't care about the class or her students. Additionally, she takes forever to grade assignments. Everything is online, including the exams, which are on a lockdown browser, no camera though. Very nice, responds to emails fast, posts lectures on Blackboard, and honeslty no complaints about her teaching style.

Great professor who is easy to connect with, outlines clear expectations and is willing to help if you're confused. BIGGEST ADVICE: go to your TA's office hours!! (or hers!!) I was averaging a B/C on quizzes but after office hours I now avg A/B (and A's on exams!)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: She teaches calc as though everyone has already taken the course. She rushes through new concepts, but will spend 5 extra minutes reminding you how to find X and Y intercepts. The way she illustrates concepts often makes them more confusing. At one point she became irritated because people were asking her to go over something step-by-step.

She was a caring person, but not the best teacher for Calc. It was hard to understand her due to her accent, bad hand-writing, and speedy lectures. However, if you do the practice quizzes and exams provided you should be okay in her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Her class is easy if you study. She has lecture notes that you could print out which are very handy. She also give sometimes hints during the lecture of what questions will come up on the quizzes or exams. She is very nice and answers student questions. Her exams might be longer than the others but hers are way easier.

Shes a new prof, but she was okay overall. She sped through lectures, so if you don't have a Calculus background, you would probably have a hard time following her. Her handwriting isn't the best and her accent is a little heavy. Tests are long. But she is easily accessible outside of class. The discussion sections/ my TA saved me in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Not prepared when attends his lectures and very confusing. Better to read a textbook then come to class. Exams are terrible
Excellent professor.  Only a few times in the semester was he unclear.  Tough, good at getting students to participate.  You will learn a lot.

Wang's class consists of him reciting the book and if you're lucky, a few exercises not already worked out.  There is a significant disconnect between the weekly problem sets and the book/notes.  His exams are the sort where you think you know everything going in and then are frustrated when you get a C.  Has a very heavy accent.

well versed. He teaches exactly what you need to know and is willing to work with you. Stat 453 is a hard subject, but if you are willing to work and show him that you are working hard, you will get the grade you need.

I took Dr. Wang for Stat 451 & 453.  I would say that 451 is much harder than 453 (because there's going to be less students for 453).  He is very helpful.  However, you have to study really really hard for this class.  His homeworks and test are extremely hard! My advice is better know his office hours for help!
ok
He is good, nice,professional
i agree. the tests are also far from straightforward.
his english is not great, he reads off of slides which are taken straight from the book, and doesnt explain the concepts.

He's lowkey a good human being but when it comes to Calculus he breaks apart specifically due to his thick accent and he js reads word for word the slides. You gotta come into class knowing the concept or ur doomed. Your grade basically depends on quizzes and exams, study hard and you should get a B. Wisely choose your TA, connect with Anson
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: honestly a great guy and has a good personality just not very well at teaching. Has a thick accent and would get lost during his lectures. be prepared to do a lot of practice and studying on your own. lectures were always a week ahead of the quizzes. Oliver (TA) provided helpful videos, if you have the indian guy, good luck because he did nothing.

I genuinely believe that Professor Xuan is a cool guy. His personality is friendly, engaging, and he takes class participation in lectures seriously. However, where he completely falls apart is his teaching style. This man can not teach Calculus to save his life, and you will be completely lost if you do not already come in knowing every concept.

reviews.comment: Do not take his class, test averages are bad every time 56% average, nobody shows up to lecture because you cannot understand a word he says.

Lectures are useless but the quizzes and exams were not hard at all. The practice sets and practice exams were almost identical to the quizzes and exams. Just take like 2 hours a week to do practice problems and there is no reason you shouldn't get a high B or A. If you have that indian guy as your TA he is useless for any help.

pls save yourself. dont take his class 😭 he says attendance isn't mandatory but takes attendance. i stopped attending the lectures because they were just a big waste of time, i could never understand the topic he was trying to teach, his slides were kinda confusing too. Oliver is a great TA def reach out to him if you're struggling HES great.

Writing this review 2/3rds through the semester. 75% of the class skips lectures because they are impossible to understand (heavy accent) and not useful. Class average for Test 1 was ~56%. If you're gonna transfer to UMD, don't waste your time and GPA, because Math155 doesn't even transfer there. This class/prof is terrible!
Pick a god and start praying, you're cooked if you take him.
Pay attention & ask questions during lecture it will save you.
Prepare to do alot of practice on your own. Do all your homework, participate and seek tutoring, and you will be fine.

Lectures were a little confusing, homeworks didn't align with the tests and quizzes. I didn't perform well on a couple tests and the homework grade is what saved me. Make sure to pay attention and ask your TA questions during the discussion. Study and do all your work and you will be fine.

Absolute unit. The glare from his shiny forehead was a bright as the sun. The way he holds the marker and wrote on the board was just so tuff. He just so tuff! Thick accent. Can't always understand him. Good at math, cant really teach it. You have to be prepared to study hours and hours extra by yourself. Organic Chemistry Teacher gon be clutch.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS. Lectures are useless but he still checks for attendence even tho the syllabus says its not mandatory. Talks too fast. He doesn't post the lecture on BB until after its been given in class. It never matches the note shells posted BEFORE class. Hw/quizzes will never align w/ the most recent lecture. TA's are your best bet.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly he's not as bad as ppl make it seem. His accent may make it harder to understand but he's a really nice guy and unintentionally funny. Just do your hw on time and use the hw to study. Also study for the quizzes cus they're pretty easy. Also, use the lecture slides/textbook on your own time and you'll be good.

mr. xuan is a great person and he's unironically funny but he's not the best teacher. he doesn't go over everything we need to learn for the tests and quizes so you'd have to learn a lot of the material on your own using external sources. test reviews don't come with answers either which basically makes them useless for studying.

My lord and savior Xuan was always there when i needed him. His thick chinese accent sent shivers to my spine and made me ecstatic whenever I was in his lectures. Every time he wrote on the board, I was thrilled and memorized by his genius mind. He's an amazing person and even better professor. Truly a specimen.

this class is like a fever dream i swear. don't get me wrong he's a great guy but he jumps all over the place and will only really go over one problem per topic and you need to figure out the rest. you also have like 20-30 long problems for homework each week. he's funny and loves his students but he just can't teach math. love him tho he's my goat

I saw a post before taking his class about how cute he is. Thats not why I took his class but I realize exactly what that person meant. Professor Xuan is very funny and caring. He could sense when I was stuck and helped right away. He gave time in class to start on the hw and answered any question I had very well. 10/10 professor. i love him sm

Oh where would I be without my sweet loving Xuan. Such a kind soul and every lecture made me want to get up and have a one on one tutoring moment iykwim ;). His soft voices calms down the tightness of my soul and gives me shivers down my spine when he writes on the board. He graps the attention of every student by his voice that's as smooth as silk

Anson Xuan, my love, my life. What keeps me sane in this cruel corporeal realm is his sweet, soothing voice hidden behind a thick accent which puts me to sleep every night. I attend his office hours to see his cute face and smile. When he writes on the whiteboard in the massive lecture hall, his hands a beautiful representation of his masculinity.

Don't take him. you can't understand anything during the lecture. he is condescending. Not helpful. HW is easy, but the tests look completely different. absolute worst class I have ever taken, and the professor is terrible at teaching.

Good teacher imo. Knows what hes teaching and students just have issues with his accent. Pretty easy grade and rounded up my high B to an A after the final. Just follow the lectures to know what hes teaching even if you dont understand and work a little outside of class for the quizzes and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Mr. Xuan is a very good professor overall. Lectures were relatively clear and easy to understand. The only issue was that Xuan lectured to his tests but the final is made by a committee so some things were new. If you understand the prerequisites this class should be easy
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was an OK teacher. I didn't struggle with the course because I took calc in high school + math is my strong suit. However, he's not helpful to students who are weak at math. He doesn't also cover some topics in class that are on the quizzes and exams. He was funny though. I recommend doing more practice outside of class time and you'll be fine.

Prof.Xuan was... well I can't really speak on him because I stopped going to his lectures the second week into school. I would pop in occasionally and each time it was the same, I just couldn't follow what he was teaching and he's a little hard to understand, so I would just leave 5 minutes after popping in. Studying on your own time will help.

Would not recommend. Professor doesn't really explain topics thoroughly, just flips through slides as if we're in a English class or something. If it wasn't for an amazing TA I would've did worse. prof was nice, but being nice won't help my grade.

He's an ok professor but a nice person and is genuinely passionate about math. Lectures were boring at times and weekly quizzes were difficult. People give him poor ratings because of calc being their first "real" math class and expecting to pass without actually studying. If you have taken calc before or are willing to study you should be fine.
This professor is hilarious, he knows how to teach on a real note, I understand the content and he is good with grading which allows students to take opportunities to raise their grade

He can barely teach and the lecture mostly consist of him talking the whole time without any real engagement of the math that we are suppose to be doing in class. The whole time I was very confused and when asking for help he gets mad over the smallest things that aren't really important to how one may solve the problem

He is very hard to understand in most of his lectures. The course in and of itself is relatively easy if you stick to what information is provided in the online textbooks. 

He will rant about a mathematical concept for the majority of his lecture and then breeze over the rest of the lesson in the last 20 minutes.

Everyone is collectively lost and barely able to scrap by each quiz. He goes over quiz content the day of and rambles a lot during lecture. Concepts aren't explained very well, self studying is needed.

Professor Xuan is eh Professor, you will not learn anything from this class at all! He only read off slides and you will not have time to take notes, you are best to watch some topics on YouTube. Sometime he is very diffcult to listen to because of his accents. But, professor Xuan is the most cutest person ever, I have 5 posters in my room of him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Do not take this class if you don't have any knowledge otherwise you will struggle in this class. He goes way too fast and teaches sections an hour before a quiz. Some people don't show up because of how difficult it is to learn from him. I've learned more from my TA than him and that says a lot. No help at all.

Good luck to anyone whom had the displeasure to take him. He is a nice person and can be ironically funny, however, if you have never taken calculus before, or have done prep before hand, you are doing yourself a disservice. Doesn't prepare for quizzes, not really accessible, god help you
DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR, HE DOESN'T PROPERLY TEACH, AND NEVER PREPARES YOU FOR THE QUIZZES OR EXAMS.

reviews.comment: Terrible professor

Guys, Do NOT take this class with him. He has a very thick accent and does not explain concepts very well. Get ready to learn material of the quiz on the day of. Good luck to any who take this class with this professor

Seeing Prof. Xuan's bright face as soon I walk in every class always gives me butterflies. He always has this charming way of making me giggle like when he calls denominators "feet". I watch his video lectures before I go to bed just because his sweet voice puts me to sleep. Definitely take this class if you want to take math with some excitement.
if you want a good cry, this is the class to take :)

Honestly, this class is the easiest I've ever taken. The bad reviews are all trolls who don't listen to his lectures. They just don't understand calculus as he does; he is a phenomenal professor with a beautiful voice and an understanding of calculus. His voice is one of divine beauty and it gives me such ecstasy when hearing him talk.

I did very well in this class and I usually hate math. Lectures are easy to follow and he gives us time to take good notes. The people that wrote bad reviews were honestly people that didn't show up to class or just talked the entire lecture. If you want an A in math definitely take his class.

Honestly easiest A+ I have ever gotten. There was this one time where I had a detrimental question on one of the homework's and he enlightened me by instilling his intellect upon me by informing me, and I quote, "to find the pattern". These wise words have been engraved into my soul as UMBC student. Thank you Anson Xuan for THIS EZYYY A+!!!!!!

In most lectures, it is a miracle if Anson manages to not have a technological issue in which he requires help from a student. After 15 minutes of waiting, he begins. Mr. Xuan's first language was not English, and therefore he is not easy to understand behind his thick accent. All problems he does are on a white board on which nobody can see.
He does not know how to teach and is impossible to learn from. That being said I am just so brilliant that I get A's on all of the exams.

This professor is the worst to everr exist, if you want to learn math and you take him, just letting you know that you're failing. He's very hard to communicate with and is not willing to help you at all. I had so much difficulty listening to him. questions that show up on the exam are things we haven't even covered so avoid taking him.

Mr. Xuan is an amazing professor. At times, slightly hard to understand but he is very good at answering questions and explaining the reasons behind the math. If you pay attention and complete homework assignments the class is so easy
bad with technology, hard to communicate, kind of a silly goose

reviews.comment: he is bad professor

Cannot recommend Yang enough. I had him for 203 a few semesters ago and he was incredibly caring, friendly, and willing to work with me outside of class. I hated 203 lol but Yang really is a good guy, passionate, and always willing to help!

As of my current semester, I think I can say Prof. Yang is my favorite professor I have had for Computer Science. The exams are quite balanced as he gives you great practice exams to prepare you. Also very approachable and understanding. Overall, plenty of resources for you. If you have the option to, please try to get a spot in his class.

Professor Yang was awesome. It was very easy to tell that he cared that students actually understood the material, he frequently asked for feedback and made sure to answer every question. Homework was assigned once a week and was never too difficult. Final exam isn't cumulative. As long as you pay attention and take decent notes, you should be fine

Honestly one of the best Prof if not teachers I have had. He really cares about students and want everything for them to succeed. He gives big dad energy if you know what I mean. He's open to questions of any kind and will answer with sincerity and without condescension. As long as you do the work and practice you'll be good.

I believe Dr. Yang only teaches CMSC-203 and he is simply the best professor for CMSC-203. The class is weighed Homework 30%, Attendance 10%, Exam 1 20%, Exam 2 20% and the final exam 20%. The final isn't cumulative. Passing CMSC 203 with a B and above really depends on the professor and getting a B in Dr. Yang's class is doable.

Very caring about his students and thereby always asked for feedback to make the class better, incorporated recordings , ec , and very active office hours. He always was eager for class participation so don't be afraid to ask or answer questions during lecture.  Show up to class , do the HW on time, practice the study guide, and you will be fine !

Clearly one of the best profs ever at UMBC, he is not a tough grader, very open to student feedback, the only reason I did better on the second midterm was because he was recording the lectures, which were very helpful. If you go to him in office hours, he even allows students to work on the homework in the office hrs.

3 tests a semester, final not cumulative, graded leniently. Open to questions/helping, provides resources for learning, and seems to care about students. Only setbacks are his accent which becomes understandable as you go to class, and his lectures which can be tedious. Will call on you if he learns your name.

Strong teacher, albeit a bit dry at times. As long as you go to class, ask questions, and do your work you'll be fine. If you go to office hours he'll even help you with the homework. Even allows late homework submissions if you have a good track record. Couldn't ask for a better professor.

I liked his teaching style and it's clear he has a lot of experience in photography. There is a lot of homework, but not an impossible amount. It will be somewhat harder if you live on campus, since there's only so much you can photograph. As long as you don't procrastinate (seriously don't.) you will be okay!

the critiques. i genuinely cried during like 3 of them. he gives a lot of criticism that usually outweighs positive feedback. the assignments were long and torturous (between 100-1000) due every 2 weeks and it's hard to take good pics on campus. he grades pretty leniently as long as you follow the crtieria on the syllabus exactly.
Although I received a B in the class, I would not take him again. He is very strict with grading and missing a class brings your grade down tremendously.

The workload is excessive and unrealistic between 500 and 1,000 photos to complete within a two-week period. He rarely responds to emails. Grading takes an unreasonably long time. Attendance policies are also very strict. If a student is late or misses even one class, a significant number of points are deducted. Do not take this class

ART 211 with Professor Year is a lot of work. The class is split into around 6 assignments that range from 250-1,000 photos each. You only get about two weeks to complete each assignment so don't procrastinate. Grading is strict and missing a class can drag your grade down a lot. Professor Year cares a lot about photos and wants you to as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He gives like 5 huge photography assignments. Every assignment is like 250 pictures MINIMUM and the last few are like 500-1,000. You only have a two week span of time to do all of it. No cropping, all in manual and you have to edit your pictures. He doesn't answer email either
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took him in the winter thinking it would be easier but he makes the quizzes easy and the exams super hard. Furthermore an A is anything above 90.1 and a B is 75-90 so that was just awesome too. Take 102 with someone else if you can hit if he's your only option just do the work

'Twas the night before Christmas and I still don't have my final grade. He's nice, but the lectures weren't that helpful and were a bit boring. I recommend going anyway for the extra credit assignments. Everything is in the textbook, and the class is easy as long as you study.

Very nice and enthusiastic professor, and a simple class. He drops the lowest grade for each assignment in quizzes and finals/midterms. All quizzes are open notes, and he allows a note sheet for the midterms/finals. The lectures are a little boring, but he does practice problems and gives extra credit during class.

Very easy to approach, his lectures were sometimes hard to follow but he had notes online that were practically a baseline of the exams. He let's you bring a cheat sheet on exams, so they're never too hard. Make sure to go to lectures because he offers a ton of extra credit throughout the semester.

decent professor, kinda just reads off his notes and writes on the board. we do practice problems that are practically the same on exams. he is a nice guy and answers all questions well. there was an online quiz due every so often, dont forget to do those. just make sure to study and you will do well.

He knows what he's talking about, and he's pretty funny. Open to questions and is always positive. I liked the hybrid thing he did, and he didn't really give you many assignments besides quick quizzes and regular quizzes. His tests were pretty weird like some of the questions would be the first time hearing about it. But overall really solid class.

This class was treated as a joke. No one ever showed up, and everyone around me constantly failed the exams. Lectures were difficult to understand, and there was no curve. I would take it online if I could.

I took this Fall 2023. Professor Yuan was really good! I am not the brightest, but he was always willing to clarify concepts when asked. Just make sure to take notes during his lectures and ask if you're confused. There's one simple project and the exams. As long as you pay attention in class, you'll do good. The exams are the bulk of your grade.

I took him over the winter online so everything was condensed. Grade depended on quizzes, one assignment and two exams. The midterm was optional but that meant the final would be worth 65% of your grade. He also offered a 5% extra credit. Had good curves for Cs and Ds. For the one assignment we had, he upload a video on how to do it so it was easy.
Straightforward course, everything you need to succeed is provided, and if you don't understand he is open to answer questions. Good man, also is funny
Aside from small tests, literally no workload given. Very chill and laid back class

Professor is able to review and talk about the material very well and encourages me to ask questions if needed for clarification or help. Encourages to email the professor if there are any problems encountered and is lenient with grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great teacher, like a dad to me, taught me how to change my tire. Thank you Chunming.

He wasn't the best communicator, and there were some odd rules he enforced on tests and quizzes, such as not allowing students to return to previous questions they had answered. We also didn't cover very much material. I think it would be better taken in person.

A terrible professor. I learned absolutely nothing from him as this class was 100% self taught. He held no lectures. It was like he wasn't even there. I'm not sure how this is acceptable, it seems very lazy. Avoid at all costs - take a professor that will actually be present and put forth some sort of effort.

No lectures; he simply provides slides and notes, and asks you to read the textbook. You are on your own in this class. Class had two midterms, one final, a few quizzes, and one analytical assignment. He had review sessions before exams, but in my mind, no lectures means he did not care enough about the class to make an effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class over the winter. It is super easy over the winter. All I had to do was read the text book and take notes and I was all prepared. I don't remember there being any lectures so if you had a question, you would have to go to office hours. The quizzes were pretty easy and the final was a cake walk. TAKE DURING THE WINTER IF YOU CAN.
Very good professor. He is a fatherly figure to me. Great feedback.
Gives extra credit. Attendance not mandatory. Most test questions come from review chapter questions or online. Pretty fair grader. Not a lot of assignments. Tries to add humor.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Found the exams online, just memorize those. Nice prof though. Sometimes had extra credit as attendance.

Professor Yalew cares about students' success, however he is new to the department. He is a good lecturer, but it is hard to convert his lectures into usage/implementation without good homework preparation or study materials, which the course lacked in Fall '25. There are hiccups in the expectations and implementation of homework and exams.

I don't think he had the best approach for teaching this class. He would often go very fast, and it would be difficult to follow. While I went to every class, I do not think it is necessary as the lectures are recorded and posted to blackboard. There isn't a lot of homework, but it's 40% of your grade, with and the other 50% being the two exams.

This professor is literally THE best. He is one of my favorite lecturers that I will definitely remember for a long time. He's very understanding and is willing to work with you to help you get better in your subject. He was also understanding in terms of the finals and curved it for our class. Really loved this professor! 100% recommended.

respectful ,open to feedback, very helpful, few homework ,  test and the midterm are the hardest part (most important besides hw) which students should prepare by studying hw, guides , activity problems , and practice . Lectures are clear, handwriting is okay but could improve, heavy on note taking , but releases it online which is very helpful.

Lucky to have this professor. Was very understanding and generous when it came to asking for help. Also pretty lenient on partial credit (except for quizzes which are very little of the grade anyway). Also gave (though minimal) extra credit. Only small nitpick is that handwriting on the uploaded class notes was kind of hard to read sometimes.
Really nice professor and very understanding, quizzes were relatively easy. Midterm and final were difficult but he curved them generously. Overall a nice professor
The professor was amazing but the course itself was hard to follow and difficult. The class was difficult and many people scored low on the midterm and final.

Professor Zee is a great professor, but the class on the other hand is not so great. There's a lot about the class that is difficult to teach but I think professor Zee did a decent job at. I would definitely take this professor again, not for the same class. He also records lectures; put in the effort and I'm sure it will not be in vain.

Professor Zee relies heavily on printed notes and presentations, which may help some students but were hard for me to engage with. While the format didn't suit my learning style, office hours and asking questions during and after class were extremely helpful. His support, openness, and extra credit opportunities ultimately helped me earn an A.

Genuine buns.  Reads lecture notes and fills in a missing word and does absolutely no teaching.  Average on the midterm was like a 60.  Don't bother going to the classes it does you no good, but if you don't you also won't have anything to study so you're cooked either way. Good guy though.

Incoherent lectures, and when you inevitably cant understand the lectures and need to do some studying out of class, there are no resources available to you except the professors handwritten notes from the lectures, which are just as incoherent as his speaking. He's chill tho not a bad guy just not a good teacher. Avoid taking this guy for sure.

I took CMSC 331 w/ him, not 201. The class was extremely boring and useless. It's extremely theory-heavy. Every class was the same routine. He'd hand us a packet for note-taking and talk for the rest of the class. I could hardly understand his hand-writing. Extremely repetitive and stale lectures to point where I stopped showing up after 2 weeks.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Zee's lectures are okay and he's super nice in office hours and helpful. He might make mistakes on practice code in lecture but overall he's a nice prof who cares. This class is pretty hard at UMBC without python experience, so try to review some things beforehand. Exams are pretty hard ngl, but not in his control. Pray that you have a good TA

He taught really well with clear, step-by-step explanations and a good pace. His lectures were organized, and he used helpful examples that made tough ideas easier to understand. He encouraged questions, was patient, and made students feel comfortable asking for help.

Laziest prof ever. Only reads off slides and doesn't elaborate unless asked to. Does 0 live coding. Very hard to reach outside of class. Never gave back our exams. This guy runs the class based off of the leftovers he gets from the course coordinator prof. Unless you have some experience with data structures, don't risk taking this careless prof.
He reads off slides every class but his explanations are not bad. Good guy, answers questions to the best of his ability.

Cares about the class, engages with the students, explains any issues they might have, and is entertaining.

While he reads from the slides (and they sometimes aren't very clear), he does his best to explain and make sure the student understands.

Lectures are not mandatory/actual classwork (not projects/exams) is easy, would recommend.

Don't bother going to his lectures; he's a slide reader. He adds nothing of value to the course. Somehow, a computer science class about data structures does neither programming nor proofs. His entire teaching style is "proof by intimidation." The code works because he said so! The proof is true because he said so! Little to no explanation.

If I wanted someone to read the course coordinator's slides to me, I'd do it myself. I can count on one hand how many times he coded, or put something on the chalkboard.

All of the course material is prepared for him, the guy shows up with his job already done for him and yet he's the laziest faculty member I've ever seen.

Take anyone else.

reviews.comment: Mr. Ebrahimi cares for his students and makes sure that everyone understands the material. He will stop the entire class and make sure that you understand a certain concept so that you're prepared for exams. He was available outside of class and would update/fix the outdated slides (and add helpful information). Doesn't create exams/projects/labs.

Kifle's lectures are relatively straightforward. His slight accent makes him hard to understand sometimes. He is really approachable during his office hours, so do go! He sometimes has EC in his lectures. Quizzes are usually straightforward. I thought that discussions were not helpful, but they are 5% of your grade.
Very knowledgeable professor, and the class was interactive and interesting!
Very supportive and helpful professor!

I recommend studying the slides for the exams (likes to through trick questions for 1st exam). Quiz in lecture & are straight forward & weekly. Nice & approachable, but check Gritview of other professors before taking him. He likes to do EC in lectures, so do go! TA study sessions sometimes have similar exam problems. Discussions pointless.

reviews.comment: Great, Professor, really learnt a lot, and class was engaging. So yeah, man like Kifle.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are a bit boring and fast but he explains well and will answer your questions. His quizzes are extremely easy if you study and sometimes he'll give hints. Exams are harder, but still not that bad. Go to class because you will fall behind if you skip like me lol. The class starts easy but gets a lot harder at the end

Taking Stat 355 with Dr. Kifle was truly a privilege. I enrolled in his accelerated summer course, and even with three-hour sessions, he kept the class engaging from start to finish. If you need to take this course, I strongly recommend taking it with Dr. Kifle, even if it means waiting until next semester.

I had a great time taking this class with Prof. Kifle!  He made it fun and easy, with the same kinds of questions on exams as on quizzes and discussions.  He cared about individual students and was always ready to help.  He loves statistics and wants his students to love it, too!
Decent at lecturing. Great lecture slides. Exams and quizzes are easy if you go to the discussions.

Prof. Kifle is super nice, understanding, and makes sure the material is clear. Quizzes are copy-pasted from discussion worksheets—study those and you'll do great. Exams are a bit long but manageable. He gives bonus points too. One of the best classes I've taken—highly recommend STAT 355 with him!

Good professor. Quiz and exam questions are very similar to examples given in lecture slides with no curveballs. First exam was all MC w no partial credit, 2nd exam and final were mix of MC and short-answer. Overall Kifle makes the class fairly easy. Formula sheet given, just know how to apply formulas and use your stat tables.

I took him for winter and I liked it. He tought it well and sent the recordings before so you can watch whenever and however you want. He has a thick accent but not too bad. His online exams were multiple choice which had its pros and cons. in general hes a nice guy who enjoys answering questions which I think is important trait for prof.

Professor Kifle is really kind and great at teaching. He's good at summarizing lectures, explaining, and answering questions. He speaks slowly and clearly. He's transparent about what will and won't be on exams/quizzes, he offers lots of practice problems for preparation, he cuts out unimportant slides, and doesn't expect you to memorize formulas.

Dr. Kifle is a pretty straightforward professor. His quizzes and exams are directly from his slides. Usually in his 400-level classes, there is a final paper. The key to doing well is reading ahead of time and starting your final project early. Outside of class, Dr. Kifle is accessible via email and office hours and responds well to questions.

It was a mess all around for so many reasons. Was late on grading, didn't give much feedback, and bunched a lot of the class at the end. Intentionally made things unnecessarily difficult for most of the class. Avoid if you can

Middle of the road lectures, I didn't use his slides either. Fantastic homework's and tests tho. If you finish your weekly homework before the quizzes and understand it, you'll get an A. No curveballs. Sometimes gives hints in tests. Lots of multiple choice questions on midterms and the final. As long as your do your homework on time it's cake.

Pretty standard class. His slides are color coded well and contain many examples. No surprises on quizzes and exams; gives study guides for exams. He does have an accent, but it really isn't that bad. I understood everything he said.

First midterm was entirely multiple choice with no partial credit?? Second midterm was 20 MC with 2 free response. Odd format for a math class. Quizzes every week except exam weeks. Quiz problems usually come from slides which are pulled directly from the book. Lectures are boring as his slides are basically SS of the book. Formula sheet given.

Took summer online. No lectures, just watching his recorded lectures. Quiz every single week, sometimes a test a day after a quiz. After 1st day of class, was given a quiz. Quizzes/tests are reflective of practice problems in lectures. Majority of grade relies on quizzes and tests (6 quizzes, 2 tests, and 1 final). Ok class, get good at test taking
Difficult class but the class was well taught to the point that I was motivated to try actually learning about stats. Very good professor.

Very concise and clear lectures with examples that clearly reflect tests. Being in good attendance and checking work in discussion makes for easy A's. Gives a formula sheet, all you have to know is what each variable means. This is the easiest statistics can be made with the least work involved. Tests are simple. He's also just a really nice dude.

Winter Semester. Uses verbose online lectures to supplement in-person teaching. Online lectures are very bad due to his thick accent and lack of preparation - evident as his lectures fail to model either slides or textbook. Does not properly define variables and fails to show how where his formulas are derived from. Grade is padded by HW and Quiz.

Really good Professor tells you exactly what you need to know and what to expect during quizzes and exams. Lots of optional practice. Homework is WebAssign so if you like WebAssign that's a plus. One of the best stat professors at UMBC.

Accent so thick he needs to take classes to speak clearly. Forced students to use Lockdown Browser, which is well known as a unstable and destructive piece of corporate malware. Should not be allowed to continue teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Kifle is truly amazing. He tries to explain difficult concepts thoroughly with different examples and exercises. He's also very approachable outside of class, especially during office hours. If you come to class on time and pay attention to his lectures, you'll have a good understanding of the topics covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Kifle is a great professor who cares about his students. His lectures are easy to understand even though he does go fast. Make sure to study the material until you understand it, and you'll be fine. He'll even help with problems during the quiz and exams if a lot of students ask about the problem.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Kifle is a great all around professor for STAT 355. The lectures are engaging and the lecture slides he provides the class are amazing. There are weekly quizzes for this course when I took it during the fall semester, but they were all very straight forward. I would definitely recommend taking his class for STAT 355.

Kifle made the course material very easy to understand and was also very helpful in office hours. I wouldn't say his class is an easy A because you need to understand the material well enough to perform well in quizzes and exams, but studying the lecture slides is all you need to get good grades. If you're thinking about taking him for 355, do it!

Professor Kifle is really good but you must want to learn the material. He gives you everything you need to be successful and literally tells you exactly how. You must work in this class. If you do, you will learn a lot!

Very thick accent! I do not understand a word out of him. He also assumes everyone should know everything already and does not understand that people have zero knowledge about what he is teaching. 0/10. Save yourself. Do not take class with him.

The power point slides can be slightly confusing, but they are very thorough and explain everything necessary for the course. Rough presenter; honestly this class works well with me skipping class and just reading the lecture slides. Quizzes and exams are consistent with what was given on the homework. Attendance was mandatory only for discussion.

The meta-analysis course was only offered to graduate students before Spring 22. Kifle made a graduate student course seem really easy. Detailed PowerPoints that were extremely helpful to look back on, working through problems in class, easily reachable through email for help on code. Kifle is a harsh person though. He's snappy. Not the nicest!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: STAT 418 is pretty difficult. But Kifle is a great teacher.
Very good professor. Goes over lengthy proofs in class, but he mainly tests on the concepts and applications. Clear notes which are posted online. One of the best professors in STAT department!

Dr. Kifle is a good professor. His class notes are helpful and clear to follow, he posts them online too. We had 2 quizzes and a few homework assignments, some in R. He did a few random in-class attendance checks that counted as points. We had a midterm and a final group project/presentation. Definitely have to understand the material but doable.

Prof. Kifle is a good teacher, the class is just SO EASY. like read the slide/pay attention during lecture, do the HW (solution are posted before you turn it in), and you will do fine at both quizzes and exam. Discussion are the worst use of my time ever i don't even bother going its not worth the 2% participation points.

He lets you know what the class consists of and with two classes a week, one is for quizzes and the other is only a lecture, however every once in a while he will have an in-class assignment so you should show up. He is a fairly strict professor and isn't the nicest guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He emphasizes the important topics in lecture and provided good examples to further help me understand. For quizzes, focus on the ppt qs, and the homework and you will ace them! As for the midterms, be thorough with all the ppt questions, quizzes and HW. He does leave a few qs blank in his ppt so make sure to come to class to get those answers!

The class consists of three exams (including the final), 12 quizzes, 12 homeworks, and 2 (extremely easy) excel projects. The exams weren't that hard, but sometimes getting a single question wrong would cost so many points. He allows you to have your own formula sheet for the final. Show up to class because sometimes he gives extra points for that.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Really good professor. He lectures a lot and participation isn't very important. His criteria for what he's testing/quizzing you on is clear. Test questions were from class examples and homework. He wants you to succeed. If you like structure and traditional lectures, he's your guy. One of the best statistics professors along with Dr. Stanwyck
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I had a hybrid course where you only go to class to take quizzes and exams. We had two midterms, three projects, and one final. Homework and quizzes every week. It was pretty easy in my opinion but you definitely need to dedicate some effort to studying. Nothing too crazy. I mostly talked to the TA since he managed the quizzes. Rarely saw the prof

I took this class for the first summer session and it was the biggest mistake. This class is no joke. It is intense! She does not teach you anything in the lectures and 90% of the class is teach yourself/ read a confusing textbook and do a rediculous amout of workload. Understandibly this was a summer course but good god...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The content itself is not too hard especially if you already have basic statistics background. Huang doesn't really teach or explain concepts well. Everything is graded by the TA, who might or might not be helpful depending on the TA. You have to self-study for most of the class.

I needed an 8% on the final to get an A with solid quiz scores. Studied way harder for the class than I needed to. Lot of extra credit. She does count attendance via extra credit so get someone to send you a code. Copying down the homework solutions is really helpful for studying for quizzes. Don't expect to actually learn any statistics though.

Dr. Huang has easily been one of the worst professors I have had at UMBC in regards to actually teaching the material. A TA teaches during the lecture portion before giving a quiz, every class, and the TA also does all the grading. You have to teach yourself everything in this course, with little to no help in class. Inconsistent grading as well.

Class was very disorganized and communication about assignments was often unclear. She makes a lot of mistakes in class and it's your job to notice them and correct them. That being said, the hybrid coursework was fine. If you put the time into the class you will get an A. 5 hwmk, 5 online quizzes, 5 class quizzes with lowest dropped each. 2 exams.

Her course is fantastic in terms of layout. She has lots of extra credit opportunities to cushion your grade, and is overall a very nice teacher. The only complaint I have is that the TA does most of the teaching, but I suppose with the limited time she has during lecture she can't do much about that. I'd definitely recommend taking this course!!

Easy A. No need to read the textbook, the slides cover everything you need to know. She lets you make your own / use a formula sheet for every quiz and exam, a normal piece of paper, double sided. Offers up to 6% in extra credit. She is a nice person and although the TA does the majority of the grading, is always willing to help. Highly recommend!

Prof. did none of the work and the T.A. did everything (making exams, grading, etc.). She required people to come in to pick up quizzes but then lectured about irrelevant material. Definitely use the math lab tutor bc that's the best place to learn. The material itself is easy, you just need to get the right formulas. The other professor is better.

Really easy class, professor taught well for a hybrid course. Easy 2 projects + extra cred project, 4 quizzes/homework, midterm, and final. A breeze. Take this teacher if you can. Quizzes can be found online and were reused from previous classes taught.

The worst professor I've ever had. TA did all the teaching, graded everything, & was way more reliable. All she had to do was grade the final, & apparently she can't even do that because the whole class has NG for a final grade. Her teaching style is lazy and she's a joke for a teacher. The class is an easy A, but she's awful.

Took the winter session and it's pretty easy to get through, although prepare yourself for a lot of work: 5 homework assignments, two exams are cumulative, 3 in-class quizzes, two projects (one is optional, 50 points for extra credit) and 5 online quizzes. Material isn't hard, read the textbook to supplement the ppt slides.

If you understand her powerpoints and examples, you'll have an easy time in her class. She's extremely generous with extra credit. She posts the solutions to homework prior to when the homework is due. The textbook was basically useless because everything you need to know is on her powerpoints. She allows students to bring a one page formula sheet.

She puts her powerpoints online--and you can get through the class without cracking open the book(except for HWs). The class isn't that rigorous--you get to have a formula sheet for quizzes and exams. The professor tries her best--but it's difficult when she only spends 50 mins a week teaching us--the other 50 mins is a quiz.

The class is easy if you read the book, just learn from there and her lectures will all make sense. Her quizzes and exams are pretty straightforward, knw the material from the book and then her teaching methods won't really even matter. It was an online course so we only met once a week for weekly quizzes and 3 exams.
She needs to learn how to use a whiteboard for teaching. Also, she needs go back to school and learn how to teach. Unless you can teach yourself stat find a different teacher

This is the easiet class that I've never had before. The professor is very nice, but the class is pretty boring. You don't really have to go to class, and all lectures come out directly from the textbook. There are a lot of extra credits. Just do the assinged hws, do average on quizzies and exams, then you'll be fine. This class is a breeze..
Honestly one of the best professors in the CS department. Not an ego grader or tester, genuinely wants you to learn and does everything to make sure everyone understands the concepts.

Very dense lectures, and he's not a very interesting presenter. Only two tests, a project, and 4 homeworks. Tests were very hard, but there was a curve. He's not an outright bad professor and this wasn't the hardest class I've taken, but he wasn't an amazing teacher and it wasn't an easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very hard class I think almost everyone was lost. He is a very caring guy, but I think he just has too high expectations. There was a very hard project and he at least gave us a week extension. I found it hard to pay attention to his lectures. The problem was he taught on one side of the class and slides were filled to the brim with words.

I took CMPE 212:  There was no option for CMPE212, so I chose CMSC 684 as the title.

Younis is an amazing guy.  Please don't be afraid to pester him to go over something again in lecture.  It is inevitable that you don't understand him sometimes.  His classes are difficult.  He is funny and caring and knows his students by name.
The classes were boring. His slides have a huge amount of material packed in them. Sometimes it can get very hard to follow what he is teaching. The project is very hard and complicated.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I took computer architecture  with prof Younis in the summer 2017. If your looking for an easy summer class then he is not the prof for you. Even though he may expect a lot out of his students he goes to great lengths to make sure you have a through understanding of the material by the end of the class.  It was a great class and I learned a lot.

Great professor, but its a lot of work.   I wanted to get more of a high level understanding of computer architecture and he made us go reeeallly in depth into the mechanics of pipelining and calculations of how anything affects a processors execution time.  You wont need it, just take the class with someone easier.

Classes are boring. Most of the students slept during the class.  Project was very hard and unnecessary for real life. There were always some confusions in assignment and project. I didn't like the class that much.

Took class spring 2013, project was hard but interesting, make sure you give yourself enough time to complete it! It will take a lot of time to run down edge cases. Very great presentation style and understood when problems came up. Show that you are working, and he will spend the time to help you out however he can.

Very understanding professor, will always work with you, as long as you show you are putting in the effort. Understands the subject well and presents his lectures clearly. Homework prepares you very well for tests. Course was done somewhat in a seminar style, with students presenting, he made sure to fill in gaps when students did not do well.
Younis is very helpful so long as you put in the effort. The project is pretty tough. I would recommend starting on it early. I learned a lot in this class and was glad to have taken it.

Very nice and helpful professor. Computer Architecture is a bit difficult to grasp but Professor Younis instills confidence in all his students. Home works were the most difficult part of class but grading was very lenient.
awesome person but he has really high expectations. tough project. mid-term is kind of hard but final is easier. HWs are not bad. awesome lectures. expect to spend a lot of time on his projects...

very dry lectures had trouble staying focused every day. teacher runs class like a high school. mandatory attendance and must not do anything else except paying attention to lectures or you will be in danger of failing. assignments and exams are laughably easy though.

I have taken two classes with Dr. Zhang so far, and they have both been great! She makes the density and amount of material (still a lot) for 300 and 400 level history courses easy to understand and creates interesting assignments/in-class activities. Looking forward to taking more courses with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class was *ok*. Tests were open book/note with study guides, so very easy. Everyone did poorly on the pop quizzes (multiple choice), but this is her first semester here, so the course is still a work in progress. She's very nice, was open to feedback + gave extra credit opportunities. If you need a 100 lvl history class, this is a good option!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Does not respond to emails, doesn't enter grades, reads off slides and does not explain stuff in depth enough to prepare you for the style of exams. Tests are hard and the "helpful" study guide she claims is useful is actually just a really long list of subtopics in each chapter. I had to teach myself everything. Choose another prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's not mean or anything but shes just not good at teaching and is very disorganized. She read from slides and just doesn't explain well stuff well. Doesn't respond to emails and exams are hard with a very unhelpful study guide. If you're fine teaching yourself everything its ok but you're better ofzaf with a more engaging teacher who cares more.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She was very nice but her organization was not great. Assignments and quizzes were released late so the schedule didn't even matter. She released less quizzes then the syllabus claimed we were supposed to do. Her exams were difficult. Her study guides were somewhat helpful but her exams didn't correlate with the study guide.

Although the course says no coding experience is needed, I think CMSC 201 or an intro programming class with Python should be a prerequisite. If you've worked with code before, you'll be fine. The projects were interesting, but most lectures felt boring. Most grading was done by TAs, though the professor was very approachable and easy to talk to.

If you talk with her one-on-one, she's very down-to-earth and friendly. As a professor, I found her to be highly unorganized and difficult to learn from. She would often forget to post assignments, so her syllabus was pointless by week three. Study guides weren't helpful and lectures were mostly her reading slides, so I had to self-teach a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The course itself was not very beginner-friendly, especially with no coding experience. The workload was not too bad. She pushes students towards the TA rather than herself. I would not take her again as a beginner is coding, would go for someone who aims to have more connection with their students.

The course demands significant time commitment. Homework assignments typically require 1-2 hours or more each. The course includes a group project with deliverables due every week. The professor's expectations are borderline unrealistic given students have multiple courses. There were three exams that were in-person. Avoid if possible.

This was a gateway class, and the workload wasn't too demanding. She takes extremely long to enter grades, so you never know where your grade is at. The assignments aren't too bad, but the exams are hard. She doesn't provide any in depth study guide for the mini tests. She just reads off the slides the entire lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great class!  I recommend
This professor is genuinely not okay. I believe she is on something because her eyes are always red and talk extra slow.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Subpar professor, lousy course. Takes centuries to grade anything. Timeframes for group proj deliverables are absurd. Mandatory attendance also sucks; her lectures are dry and last the full 2.5 hours. Unfortunately, 436 is required so there is no avoiding it. You'll have to just thug it out; get a good group for the project.

Personally, she was rude to me. I took from 4:30pm to 7pm so If I HAD TO, I would take her twice a week like a normal class. She is slick at the mouth, once I fell asleep in class (due to it being damn near 2hrs+ and I'm a commuter), instead of asking if I was okay. She said "if you want to sleep get out of class". As if she could throw me out.

AVOID this class with her. She rarely responds to emails and her instructions are vague. The course itself isn't too hard, but she makes it difficult. Grading is done only at the end, and the exam was very tough with little time. She's nice personally but not effective as an IS professor. No grade curve either. My bf had the same issue in IS 448.

Considering the fact that IS 310 is a gateway class, she makes the class pretty simple. We had mini tests, 9 assignments, a couple quizzes that are open textbook, and 2 exams. It's not too difficult, and she gives study guides for each exam and mini test, so study those. Good professor, but she does take a long time to enter grades.

Assignments from first few weeks of class still not graded months in.
Group project deliverables due every week. Most requirements in the group project she just tells you to read the book and figure it out.
Lecture is not that useful she just reads from slides.

She's a decent professor, the material isn't difficult but it does feel rushed since the project is coded from scratch as you learn. Homework can be demanding. She is willing to help if you reach out response times do take a little long and so do grades. It is a passable class but I felt like I really had to work hard to maintain a B.

Prof Zaidi is an excellent teacher! One of the best I've had. you will learn so much about front end development. We had to code from scratch for our group project which was quite interesting, and she is willing to help. It was 3 Homeworks, 2 exams and 1 project...but slow grader. Looking forward to take her IS436 next semester. Good Luck!

She explains things clearly in class - which is extremely helpful for coding. 448 is a lot of concepts at a fast-pace though, so get help from her early if you need it. She's pretty lenient with grading as long as you try. Her exams are straightforward (and she gives a study guide). The group project takes WORK though - so get a good group!

She makes this course hard to fail, easily the best professor for IS310, if she is available please take her. Gives multiple opportunities to keep your grade either at or above the B you need to pass this class, excellently done. She will get you through the gateways as long as you do your work and pay attention in lecture.

Professor Zaidi is excellent; she wants her students to learn and gives an appropriate amount of assignments. The best thing is she makes study guides which you can fill out and are extremely helpful for her quizzes and exams. So show up to class, do the assignments and study guides, and you'll get the 'A' you deserve.

Professor Zaidi is a pretty good professor, she has a deep understanding of course materials and does a great job and explaining to students. Don't skip lectures, take notes in class, study for exams and you will probably get an A.

Easily one of my favorite professors at UMBC and I wish I had taken this class sooner. The content is all very interesting, but there is a lot of material covered during the semester, so missing even one lecture could hurt. She grades very fairly and is very approachable if you have questions or need help. Highly recommend taking her class!

She is a great professor we only had quiz and homework which was very simple. If you read the study guide you will get 100% on quiz. She takes quiz and exam in class though but they were not hard since she provided the study guide.

Professor Zaidi is very helpful and gives you real world knowledge and experience.  She has helped me on work projects as well outside of class, and has so much real world experience, which isn't the case with a lot of professors who are more "book smart" with little to no real world, hands on experience.  You have to do the work!

She has on her syllabus that she will take 14 business days to grade an assignment. She means that for her email as well. Took her class cause she had 4/5 at first but things went down hill. Content isn't very difficult but with the type of professor she is, it doesn't take much to make it "rough" BE AWARE and BE CAREFUL !
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not what I expected slow grader you dont know what you have in the class. Lectures have nothing to do with exams, rather worded difficult . Assignments were almost impossible to seek help for
i picked the teacher based on the good reviews but she had difficult exams and isnt always available for help. if you want a heavy schedule take someone else.

Tests weighed a lot and be prepared to study. Class became very difficult when transitioned to online and will take up most of your time. Doesn't ever respond to emails so if your group is not helpful for the project, good luck. Doesn't grade until the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Semester long project along with quizzes and at most 2 homework assignments. Find reliable group-mates and the semester will be smooth sailing. Doesn't respond back to emails and is a slow grader. However, is reasonable with extending deadlines.

She's easy on the eyes for sure!  If she is available for IS436 take her. I'm not saying she is the best teacher in the world or anything but she has a lot of real world systems analyst experience so she tells you what is important. Tests, HW, Group Project is graded very easily and relaxed. You should get an A if you are competent.

Probably one of the best professors I encountered within the IS major at Umbc. was a student here before so understands the course load of students and makes her exams and assignments doable. Study slides for exams, and use slides for homework assignments as well.

She is slow to post grades and the homework assignments are wordy and confusing. She also provides about 20 files for each chapter and you only use 1 or 2, which is confusing when she makes you download the whole thing. But overall she seems like she is familiar with the material and her lectures are pretty straightforward. Not too much homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Outstanding professor! Loved her class, she's very knowledgeable and loves to get to know her students. My only negative is that it takes forever for her to grade anything, and she's not good at organization. With so few assignments that factor into your grade, she did a really bad job at giving students a heads up.

The only thing I did not like about this professor is, most days she is late to class. She getting into our daily lives and asking about personnel stuff. Other than that, she is a wonderful professor!
Professor Taj is great. She assigns a reasonable amount of work, is not too demanding, and is very accommodating and willing to help students.

Easy course. Went on a field trip to an NGO and gave us breakfast twice throughout the semester. The course consists of 3 reflections, a midterm, and a Case Study paper/presentation. The course was hybrid, Mondays were lectures, and Wednesdays were online with speakers in the field. We sometimes didn't have class on Wednesdays. Would take again!

Shes a good professor, the class is very discussion based, and would talk alot if people dont participate. Very easy class. Graded by 8 or 9 weekly assignments, midterm, and presentation. Would take again.

Zareen Taj is an extremely interesting professor and I never lacked to pay attention in class, BUT she is just as happy to talk you to death if you don't participate. So do the reading, come to class knowledgeable in the subject material, and it will go by much more quickly for you as she is beneficially responsive to high participation.

Easy class, interesting topics/videos. There are 5 quizzes, 2 Unit Tests, and 5 assignments. Overall, good Professor, but group discussions in class was okay. Depending on the class, some weeks you will meet twice a week; others you will meet once a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class contained a decent amount of reading and homework assignments, but the structure of the class was well done. Once you figure out the proper criteria for grading, everything goes smoothly. She is also a very fair grader.

Midterm scores were very low, but the grading seemed heavily curved at the end. You MUST read the text for acronyms, he tests strict definitions, not the lecture stories. CPSA HW is confusing until it clicks. Final reused tough quiz Qs. Recovery is possible, but you must study his specific terminology to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: You have to read dense chapters every week and remember everything. Lectures are way too in-depth and do not really help on projects, assignments, or quizzes. Frequent quizzes that cover chapter content in minute detail. Low class averages across the board. Don't take this class if you don't already know your stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: DONT TAKE 487 WITHOUT 481 AND 426. Content of the class is just hard and theres a lot.  He gives quizzes on chapters but won't announce it over email or ahead of time (you get used to it but it sucks). reviews.comment: was prepared for a nightmare after reading the other reviews on here, but Ziegler turned out to be a very reasonable prof. very knowledgeable and genuinely wants to help students understand the material (though his bedside manner isnt the fuzziest). you learn a lot! READ THE TEXTBOOK LIKE A BIBLE. projects are tough but grading is very generous
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ziegler is incredibly smart and is very knowledgeable about the subject. However, he lets you know he's smarter than you and that there are definitely stupid questions. He's incredibly condescending and does not promote an atmosphere for positive learning. He grades fairly and provides good feedback, but is honestly scary to approach.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Zieglar is too smart for his own good. Asks for participation but will laugh at even slightly incorrect answers. Projects requirements are somewhat ambiguous, and use software with almost no online resources. Projects take months to grade. Weekly quizzes pull directly from textbook. Very smart man, but a below average professor.

The professor is awesome. Attendance should be taken seriously given lots of exam questions could be included from things discussed in class that might not be explicitly mentioned in the text book. The course is somewhat challenging but broadens student's understanding of cryptographic algorithms and network protocols.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The course consists of reading and memorizing 350 pages of dense net sec specs. The projects are in an obscure language Dr. Z wrote. He is rude.
