Still, he is very knowledgeable and responds quickly to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Ziegler was comically bad. Only teacher I've ever had that required a textbook at UMBC and despite making us read the entire thing, he would routinely say that the textbook was incorrect. Homeworks were confusing, extremely time consuming, and unreasonably difficult. This class was a literal bruh moment the whole way through.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Zieglar is by far the worst professor I've had at UMBC. If you read all required material before the lectures & take good notes, you should do well on quizzes. He doesn't make it comfortable to answer questions in class; if any part of your response is incorrect, he will laugh and say "no" 6 times/second. Great material, arrogant professor. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Brutal. Dude is way too smart for his own good, when to MIT and works in NSA. Incredibly RUDE, wants people to participate, puts their opinion on BLAST. Could talk all class about any networking topic. Read the book. Assignments are super vague, hard. Read the assignment thoroughly before going for help. Curved midterm because people failed.

Brutal but highly informative class taught by someone whose been in industry (NSA) for more than double the time I've been alive. That being said, I think he sometimes forgets that we're undergrads (and the only prereq for networks is 341!), and the homeworks are obscene, esp. the BBS project. Take if and only if you really want to learn.

Could be better, but he's okay I guess, and there are definitely worse professors than him. If you attend all classes and take notes vigorously, you should be able to pass the class with at least a B. The textbook homework is a little excessive and obnoxious IMO though, just a heads up.

reviews.comment: I took him Spring 2020. He was really accommodating during the online environment and we had fun projects where you learned a lot. Some say the exams are on the harder side, but as long as you read the book and pay attention in class you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Okay so the semester with him was crazy. 100 slide power points. Theres a project but you can get x3 for your grade. The homework, project, and assignments are worth 55% ! Literally the answers can be found online and the questions come from the textbook directly. Now he does give quizzes at the end of each chapter and they are difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great class, lots of protocols to cover. Requires you read each chapter, then goes through the book slides. Enjoyed the lectures, always gives good answers to questions, ie if you ask something he just explained, he will remind you he just answered that, then rephrase it. HW, quizes and exams right from the book, its theory,if you read, you pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Doesn't describe concepts well, and conflicting explanations in different classes Take a chunk of your assignment and project points for something minor

Terrible lecturer. He says to read the book, and class is just for asking questions. He does not post a hw/test schedule online to force people to go to class. Tests and quizzes are impossible. Average quiz grades are 10-20%, and midterm average was 50%. He asks that we read 150+ page chapters in a week, then tests on some very small detail.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Exams are hard but this is by design, he only wants you to read the material and participate in class discussions. I am by no means a genius and I managed to get an A. I would rate this class somewhere under Algorithms, OS and AI. The material ties in well with Algo and OS. Take his class if you want a solid foundation to grow on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Although he knows a lot about Networks, he definitely does not know how to teach AT ALL. Terrible lectures. Completely unhelpful when asking questions. Everyone failed all the exams, I'm pretty sure the class was curved 99%. He scans the room every day in the beginning like a robot to see who's missing. Got a 1% and passed with a C. AVOID.

reviews.comment: Read ahead and participate in lecture, projects are interesting and fun. Exams are extremely hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She was really funny and I really enjoyed taking her. If you take this class over the summer, it's almost impossible to get an a because 60% of your grade is the final and she does give a pretty tough final, but besides that she was very fun to take she explained the material well and she was very caring teacher.

Excellent professor
Be ready to put the work in
It was hard to understand the lectures. Even with open book and open notes in exams, her grading did not make sense. I wish I had taken the class with someone else.
She'll raise her voice and even scream at you if you ask too many questions!
This professor has no patience with students, and if you ask questions she'll cut you off in the middle of a sentence. Stay away from this one.
Not open to discuss or explaining anything outside of class. Has no patience.

Dr. Zhu is so funny and really cares about her students. The lectures were very informative and easy to follow, and she posts good notes online for you to access later. The material she tells you to study is exactly what shows up on her exams. Overall great professor, and I wish the UMBC engineering dept had more faculty like her.

Professor Zhu is always available in her office and is always willing to help you on your HW. She is always making jokes in class to keep your attention. She is definitely a tough grader but a 60% is a C so there is really no one to blame but yourself if you don't pass the class.

Shes the best professor at UMBC. Genuienly cares for her students and presents the material pretty well. If you dont get it in lecture, she is ALWAYS available and will work with you until you get it. Shes also hilarious.
Go to her office.  She is the most helpful and accessible professor I have ever taken.  You have to work for your grade, but she is very fair in her assessments.

She cares about students and wants you to succeed. She's energetic and her lectures are funny sometimes. Exams are open book and based on homework, so as long as you understand the concepts, you are good to go. She's always in her office and ready to help you.

Dr. Zhu is extremely helpful but her lectures are confusing and won't support the material. Also her accent takes a while to get used to. However she is almost always at her office and will usually drop what she is doing to help you. She will flat out tell you what you need to do to get an A on your reports if you JUST ASK.

Dr. Zhu is very helpful and friendly during office hours. She is very passionate about heat transfer (it's one of her research areas). Her lectures can be a little tricky to follow at times, especially because she has a bit of an accent. Once you get used to it, it's not too bad, though.

There are six labs throughout the semester that make up 84% of your final grade.  They are incredibly time-consuming, but they aren't graded too harshly.  The final exam is short answer and multiple choice (only worth 10%), and there is an ethical analysis paper that was worth 6%.  It's only 2 credits, but you put work into it as if it's 4.

The material its self can be difficult, which is only why I rated 'Easiness' a 3. Posts her own notes, for you to print out. She is very helpful both during class and at office hours. Tests are hard, but very fair and they are open book. Looking forward to taking her other classes.
By far one of the best professors in the mechanical engineering department.  I highly recommend taking a class with her.
Prepares notes for you so you dont have to take any in class. Open book/note final. sometimes hard to understand.
Gives you the notes. Pretty straight-forward class.  Final exam was tough but  was open notes/book.  Overall, pretty good teacher.

Zhu is a great professor! The labs are very organized and she explains exactly how to lab the reports. As long as you follow her report you should do well in the class. She will revise your report if you give it to her before it's due. I've heard that Eggleton is extremely difficult in this course.

Do the homework, and you'll do fine on exams, which were always open book/open notes. If you find yourself confused, definitely visit her during office hours because her explanations have helped clarify a lot of concepts.
Good Teacher will help you out. Her accent is very thick so be ready

Unlike the older reviews I never found his lectures dry. He's not the type to jump up and down but he gives some really interesting/passionate lectures and never read off the screen. Lots of cool content to make you think. BUT his las few lectures need polishing. Music lectures very unclear and days where we read from text together were mindnumbing
Dr. Fatih is so nice! The VHL assignments do get very tedious, but they are very helpful if you put full effort into them.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 3 days into French 102 for the Winter session and I'm hating it.  I understand it's condensed and extremely fast-paced, but this is insane.  I've taken winter courses in the past and haven't seen anything like this. 20-35 VHL assignments every day except for Sunday, quizzes on Saturdays.  Tried to ask a question two days ago, still no response.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I regret taking French 102 online and async. the class is done entirely through VHL, and it's just not enough to learn off of. Prof didn't go back through the VHL work to give partial credit. he had lectures on Blackboard, but the time was not announced before I registered and I could never attend, and the recordings weren't very helpful.

This teacher was chill. He makes his zoom sessions optional for students. All assignments are done in VHL (Vista Higher Learning) which you have to pay for. Your grade is really dependent on how well you do on quizzes and tests. Go through the modules and you should do fine on the tests. The teacher is also always available to answer questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Friendly but very unorganized and overall confusing class. Literally you can tell he's just winging it sometimes. A bit inconsiderate of student's times and the fact that some students have other classes. One of my least favorite french profs

Overall for a 4 week course, this class is very intensive. This professor does a good job explaining grammar and what we need to know if the optional live lectures and was generally accessible by email at any point in time. Only complaint was he continuously released quizzes and his study guides like 12 hours before they were due.
He's really understanding and patient. He gives wonderful and detailed feedback, would definitely take him again.
I took him for 102 and 201 online and it was pretty easy. Got an A in both. Learned a lot. Take him.
He is a very tough grader but would give you good feedback for what you got wrong. I think he is a great professor for French. I took him over the summer for the 201 sess to meet my grad requirement.

Professor Faith is one of those professor that goes the extra mile to help his students understand the subject. He is very kind, patient and encourages people to ask questions. I took him during the 4 week summer session so although it was all accelerated, it wasn't all that difficult. Just practice using his study guide and you will do fine.

One of the worst professor's I've had at UMBC and definitely the worst in MLLI. Super disorganized and takes off so many points for tiny things. Everything is based off his lectures, which make no sense. Avoid if at all possible!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took this during the four-week session in the summer. It was quick, and all online. We did have to buy a book, but it's relatively cheap if you rent it. We had four quizzes, and three tests, and homework. You don't get feedback on how you did, just your grade. I would advise people to take this class during the summer, online, SUPER EASY.

While the lectures were a bit dry and he read directly from the power point, he made sure we understood the content and appreciated participation to help solidify the concept. He also makes sure students know that he is available for questions outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I had him for an online class, so I don't know what he was like in person, but what I do know is he was great at teaching it. So far he has been the only professor at UMBC that actually emails me back and gives great feedback on homework and tests and such.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Great professor and go deeply into details and he makes sure that you understand him. Easy grader, no attendance required but he gives points if you always show up. Just a lot of reading (3 big books) with 40 pages between each class

If you have a strong background in French, he's a good professor to take. He teaches as if all the students in the class are French majors or minors. He's very strict about grammar. He's also an extremely picky grader and will knock off a lot of points over minor errors. Make sure you attend class b/c he goes over a lot of examples.
He is the best Prof you will see at UMBC!
I also took MLL 301 and beg to differ with the previous comment; actually I learned a lot from the course and knowing Dr. Fatih personally I know he taught this course many times before!

Highly disorganized. He openly said he had never taught this class before and had no idea what he was doing. The material was not particularly difficult, but trying to navigate what he wanted was annoying

I enjoyed learning about the psychological aspects of the revolutions in Tunisia and the Maghreb, not just learning facts and current events but trying to understand the deeper motivations and analyzing the situation from that perspective. Combination of lecture, documentaries and news footage was very helpful. Overall, great class, great prof.
The course topic was fascinating and allowed me a different point of view to a contemporary topic. He found lots of good videos that really enhanced the material.
I took 2 french courses at umbc; this one is a French wizard. he goes the extra mile. I got an A but still was annoyed by the attitude of some students.
Terrible. Quizzes and assignments never pertained to what we were supposed to actually learning in class. So awful, I'm avoiding at all costs in the future
Interesting lectures. No nonsense prof, but with a great sense of humor. You really learn something about France's cultures and literature.

This class was very easy. He's super boring which makes the class boring but he's not that bad. The quizzes are easy and I think he let's you drop one. Gives you simple homework from the book but it's mostly for practice. Goes over everything from the book on the board to make sure you understand.

I can't believe what some guys on here said about prof. Fatih. He's one of the best teacher of French at UMBC. He really cares about students. Befre I signed up 4 his class, I checked his UMBC evaluations online; they're outstanding. I took two courses with him and I have been impressed with his skills. I would def. recommend him.

very distracted and neglectful of the class. canceled class once but never made up the quiz we missed. his tests are 10 questions and worth 200 points with 5 MC and 5 short answer. only gave us one quiz when we should have had 4. read straight from the text, and sometimes seemed to interact with certain students only. very frustrating class overall

I thought he was a terrible teacher. I learned almost nothing except a few grammar things. He's also incredibly unorganized. The movie the class was based on was from the 60s, so we virtually learned a ton of ancient vocabulary that isn't even used in France (my French friends could not believe what I was learning). Avoid getting him if you can.

prof fatih can be a bit confusing at times with what he expects from you, however he really tries to cater to the class so he began emailing us what he expected each week to make it easier. he also really tries to make sure we do well on the tests, he's funny and kind, and also relatively flexible abt taking stuff late

A semi-strict prof that moves pretty fast. Usually only went over new stuff once, then a quick review next class. He is pretty lax about the C-hour work and mostly assigns activities from out of the book. A good prof to take if you have had french before or have the basics down well.

He really seems to love his job. Very enthusiastic about litterature and culture. Made me enjoy lit too.The workload was just right. Perfect balance between readings (novels and scholarly articles) and written assignments. I recommend his graduate classes!
Selfish and Bad teacher.
Wonderful and highly interesting lectures; very dynamic and never misses a class.

Goods: had him for an 8oclock class but was ok with people coming late, skipping a few classes, late assignments, easy exams etc. Bads: really overqualified and knows this. Not the best teacher, basically only teaches grammar, not enthusiastic, thinks students are stupid. I forgot most french from even 101 but got an A by memorizing grammar.
I think he is pretty good. He is very helpful and the class is short and sweet.
Amazing professor.  Very accommodating and understanding. His lectures are very clear as well as the discussions. Attend them and you'll know everything you need to.

You will perform well on the assignments and tests if you pay attention during the lectures. Fair grading was applied, and the feedback was very beneficial. The professor answers emails promptly and is readily available for any questions. Anyone interested in taking the course should take because you will learn, and he allows cheat sheet.

Very bland professor. Class is basically 410 pt2. Skip lectures (slides are posted online), and discussions (mandatory attendance) teach you what you need to know. Exams are VERY easy bc A) you can bring a cheat sheet and B) exam problems are based off of the HW. HW problems are based off the discussion examples. Easy class if you put in the work.

The saving grace of 420 with Chen is he lets you bring cheat sheets for the in-person exams. His exams are also pretty straightforward. However, felt the lab sessions were more helpful than the actual lectures, but overall, he teaches decently. Group project takes a decent amount of time - so just stay on top of it.

reviews.comment:
If you pay attention in the lectures, you will do great in the assignments and the exams. 
Grading was fair and the feedback was really helpful.
The professor is very much available on emails for all doubts and responds quickly. Would definitely recommend him if you want to learn the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The professor is great. teaches good, learned a lot from him.

The homework assignments, exams, and in-class project are all reasonable. Dr. Chen is a good lecturer and it's not at all nerve-wrecking to ask him questions. You're allowed to use two double-sided pages of cheat sheets during the exam. Take anything with Chen!

Awesome professor! He pretty much reads directly off the slides. The homework he assigns are super easy and he actually made databases fun and interesting.  He makes SQL seem like a breeze and he let's you bring 2 pages (double sided) cheat sheets to his exams and his exams aren't hard at all. Highly recommend.

This professor is pretty straightforward.  If you pay a decent amount of attention in class and have a brief SQL background you should have no problem getting an A.  (I took this class as an undergrad, btw.)  You are allowed 2 cheat sheets on each of the exams.
great professor, no doubt... he will let u to bring a 2 page cheet sheet for exams. even though know what u atleast wrote  in the cheet sheet otherwise ...will be in trouble
very easy!! take him for 410 and you dont even need the textbook at all. Everything is posted on blackboard. SQL was a nice addition.
This class is really easy. Sometimes I felt like he thought we were all stupid and he was laughing at our stupidity. However, I definitely recommend taking him.

Take 410 w/ Chen!  His class is extremely easy and he will even let you use a 2 pg. note sheet in exams.  There is a group project that you work on throughout the year but it's nothing very time consuming.  His class can be boring at times so make sure you bring your laptop.  Great prof. overall!

His tests are incredibly easy: allows 2 double-sided pages of notes + a sheet of diagrams. HW is simple too. On top of that his grading is incredibly lenient. Semester long project is quick, easy 100%. Learned some SQL which was nice. Covered most of the text, so I guess i learned some stuff

Fun Class, Learned a lot of SQL. Dr. Chen is really lenient in his grading. If you pay attention in class, everything will be easy. The exams are really easy! All you have to do is study the in-class discussions, and that will be on the exams. There is one big project that may be the hardest part of the class.

Wonderful Spanish teacher ! I was sad to find out that she wasn't teaching Spanish 102 for spring 2016. She really made Spanish easy and fun to learn. She is compassionate about teaching and the homeworks will help you pass the test . Study everything and you are sure to pass her class. She is very friendly and helpful ! She made Spanish fun!
Nicest Teacher Ever!
No Comments
Great professor! would take class with her again!
Very very easy tests. Very nice lady.  Don't think you can get away without doing homework though..she likes to give pop quizzes to check up on that.

The class was great, as long as you do well on the exams you will be fine, i struggled. The quizzes and exams are great when you have the materials to prepare. his lectures were amazing and so helpful. i wish more professors were like him.

Although lectures are long, Dr. Smith does a great job explaining concepts with detail and gives plenty of practice problems during class. I enjoyed how he is enthusiastic about the material and tries to make it engaging.  The think about its and Mini quizzes were very helpful tools for studying for quizzes and exam.

reviews.comment: My favorite professor from UMBC, his lectures were interesting and he offered so much help learning the material. His exams arent quite as difficult as Dr. Tracys but youll still learn a ton! I wish I could take him for every chemistry class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith taught the second half of online CHEM 437. His pre-recorded lectures were very long and had lots of extra information. He used the book for his lectures, so reading the book was helpful to find which information was important. The class time was used as optional problem sessions because the practice was not covered in the lectures.

I went into his half of the class with virtually no chance for an A. Only missed one point on all his assignments and learned so much about Biochem in the process. First half was HELL while he was super clear and an amazing lecturer. Take this man for anything he teaches and you will not regret your decision. Also, talk to him during office hours.

Dr. Smith is one of THE best professors in the chemistry department. I almost failed this class, the first exam I got a 10/30. The second exam, which is the final exam, I got a 29/30. If Dr. Smith had not taken over the second semester, I would have failed. Please go to his lectures, study what he points out on the slides, look over old quizzes!

I really enjoyed taking Biochemistry with Dr. Smith. He made it clear what we will be tested on, taking exam questions straight from in class problems and past exams. He was always accessible outside of class, and really cared about his students doing well. Although he is a new professor, he was very knowledgeable about the course content
Super great professor!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Aaron Smith was an amazing professor--really taught the course well, was very engaging, made difficult topics very easy to understand, and progressed through material in a logical, methodical manner that made sense. Exams were very easy (straight from slides/practice exams) and he was a godsend for a good grade in the class. Strongly recommend.
He is a great professor. This class was a little difficult for me, but Dr. Smith made the material as easy to understand as possible. Plus there was a ton of extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very few grades in this class and the homework is worth 45% of your grade. For the homework you are given the choice of a 4000 word essay or an extremely difficult coding assignment. My CS major roommate who is in his last semester looked at it and stated that it is something that he would do in a 400 level CS class. I do not recommend this class.
The class has a lot of reading involved. Majority of the classes will need you to go back to understand what was said. In-person classes are way better here compared to online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 2 Exams, 2 Assignments, 1 Project. Exams are combination of: T/F, MC, Analysis, and Conceptualizing. Assignments: Paper & Coding, Project: Coding or 4k paper. He knows his stuff, slow on grading, doesn't post grades on bb, can be hard to reach outside of class.

1 project, 2 HW assignments, midterm & final. His lectures are engaging. Won't give you the grades back, Doesn't post the grade on BB. You won't know if you are passing or failing until the semester ends. Tests are mostly applying problems to real issues, not that bad. Project and HW are tough, code like a pro or write a 4000-word essay.

Here's the breakdown. The class met once a week, he read off the powerpoint but made it very engaging. He is a very slow grader, very annoying how the semester ends in a few weeks and I don't know if i'm passing. His tests are not conceptual but application. His project is horrible, either you know how to code like a pro or write a 4000 word essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Massey was a good teacher and had reasonable grading standards. Lecture should not be skipped, attendance is very important. His grading was pretty thorough, but if you read through his slides and the accompanying textbook chapters it wasn't all that bad. This class may be difficult for those that cannot write well. Somewhat writing intensive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Good and cool professor. Nice teaching of subject.

Makes you work alot for no purpose. This professor needs to know the meaning of teaching. If you want an A for this course , go ahead. But he is torturous and makes you work a lot! It would be a suggestion not to go for this course under him if you have taken some tough course because all you will doing the whole semester is just writing. A big NO!
So kind; he really care about his students and the class is really engaging.

He was a wonderful teacher and understood that this was a beginner entrepreneurship class, so he didn't go out of his way to make our lives harder. The only thing that was annoying was that we had to supplement every presentation with a paper or two, regurgitating our presentations . Otherwise, I can say I learned and had a good time.

The guy really cares about his class and if you pay attention to him and listen to his lectures, you will learn a good bit. The problem is its a 2+ hr class once a week and most students aren't enthusiastic by the time it comes. He is a good professor and he knows his stuff. He is chill and wants you to be interested in entrepreneurship and succeed

He knows a lot about the business world and how to get a company started and gives great tips . The class was pretty easy you just sit there and can be on your laptop. Only homework is a presentation, a paper, and the final project. Definitely take this class with him

He's nice to look at. I'll give him that. But he was extremely lazy when it came to the class. It's obviously not his top priority. Most of the class time was spent with students giving pointless current event presentations and boring guest speakers. He barely taught us anything. Also the grading system was VERY unclear. Take him because he's hot.

I would take again.  Nice, funny, friendly, you learn as much as you would like.  You can blow it off or not.  Do the questions before class and you can get all of the answers you need for the test.  Test are easy if you just read over the answers to the questions regularly.
Difficult class, test formats change, plenty of reading, need to read material several times to do well, do ALL questions when assigned them.

If you go to class and do the guiding questions you should do fine. I didn't like that he kept "testing" new exam formats on my class so our final exam was impossible. I would've probably gotten an A if it hadn't been for his inconsistency in testing formats.

AWESOME.Professor Smith is one of the greatest I've ever had. He is interesting, charming, funny, conversational, and very helpful. He tells you which questions from your notes will be on the tests and goes over them. You can't do poorly unless you don't study or ask for help when needed. He made me want to take a phil minor. Class is fun, take it

A good professor, no doubt about it. Made me want to change majors. Discussion was very stimulating and he kept you interested in the material. You need to be able to write a lot and want to discuss. He also provided all the reading materials in electronic format so the students didn't have to buy anything. Good class.

Great professor, one of the best I've had. Very interested in the subject matter, and always helpful and funny. Tests are written so your wrist may hurt after, but there's only 3 total and no other assignments, including papers. Easy A as long as you attend class and listen to what he says. Loved his class and taking another by him in Spring :)

For basic philosophy:Understand that many students are there for basic requirements however he also encourages, engages and challenges the logic of the most interested students. He gave a list of possible essay questions that would be on the exam. He gets distracted and off topic often but only temporarily. Very nice and open to opposing views.

omy lord!

Good Teacher
he is good

hes good, attend the class, he cares a lot abt group participation

Actually nice and cares abt his students!!! 3 reviews on scholar articles, 1 debate and 1 group project (with the same group) and 4 exams. He gives really good study guides and answers to any questions. 100% recommend him

chill prof that doesnt tolerate bs. he gives study guides that are the exam. ngl ur gonna have to grind for the lockdown + camera exams, the concepts take a bit to understand and its a lot of memorizing but i promise, hold that study guide near and dear to ur heart and ur guaranteed an 80+ on it. ps take a shot everytime he strokes his beard

PLEASE AVOID AT ALL COSTS IF YOU ACTUALLY WANT TO LEARN!!!!

reviews.comment: Dr. Abrams was a funny and great teacher. If you do all the assignments and complete all the study guides before the exam, you really shouldn't have a problem getting an A.

If you study her slides, use her study guides, and pay attention to her jeopardy, you'll pass her exams. She knows 311 can get very boring but she still manages to make it as interesting as she can. You can tell she's very passionate about what she does which is inspiring. OLAs can get hard but she does have good extra credit via SONA, etc.

Professor Abrams is amazing. It was a group version of 311 she still lectured each unit for you to properly understand the course material. Her personality is infectious and makes you want to smile. Extremely sweet, caring, and wants everyone to do well. Lots of extra credit, exams are fair-just read the book, and she's easy on the eyes (jus sayin)

Abrams was probably one of the nicest and most accommodating profs I've had at UMBC. She knew 311's content was dry, but she pulled examples from her own research exp and I felt like that made the class all the more bearable. I learned things about psych research I otherwise wouldn't have known by just learning content from the textbook.

Dr. Abrams is a down to earth professor that makes learning the material bearable. She is accessible during her office hours and she's goes in-depth with explaining things. The exams are tough, but if you study the powerpoints and her study guides you'll get an A. She lets you earn up to 50 points of extra credit through SONA and events.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The best professor at UMBC. HANDS DOWN.

Dr. Abrams is great. She cares about her students, she's good about giving examples to explain concepts, especially for such dry material. She's willing to make an appointment with you and is big on explaining how things are in the real word, which makes her a great resource.

Her exams are pretty tough and are not always from the study guide. She is extremely friendly and funny, although her class wasn't very organized. Groups are assigned and she gives group work randomly, which are a large portion of your grade. No cumulative final, 4 exams, and a group project. Extra credit opportunity through SONA, which helps a lot

This professor always seems to be in a world of her own. The exams are quite hard, with the true and false questions being extremely ambiguous. The group work she assigns every so often is pretty important because there aren't that many grades in the course, but they are very sporadic and I don't think she even knows when they will be.

The subject material is incredibly tedious and dull, but she made it worth it! She explains concepts by talking about actual research to get you connected. Breaks the umbc official class format and lectures for you--god bless because the class format is AWFUL and her lectures are amazing. Show up, skim the reading, do the homework, do just fine.

PSYC 311 is incredibly boring, and sometimes Dr. Abrams legitimately just reads off the slides and you question if it's worth it to descend into the void. It's not a difficult class by any means(she sometimes repeats questions from the group quizzes onto exams) at all though. Get the EC though(50 pts max!)- you won't be sure if your group is stupid
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: PSYC 311 is boring, dry, tedious, and dense.. but Professor Abrams saved us all from a slow and boring semester by bringing her cheery humor and lighthearted nature to class every day. She's young, fun, uses relevant and poignant examples,  demonstrates applications of 311, & inspires us to work hard. She does not dumb it down, just brings us up.
EASY EASY A. Show up and get A. Two exams which are 100% from the study guide she gives 2 days before exam. Group presentations are super easy.
Very easy class; In-class assignments add up so make sure to attend every class; Great and understanding professor; There are no exams, just applied work
Easy class, just make sure you show up for the in-class assignments.

He is a good instructor and explains math concepts very clearly. He makes it so you never need to read the textbook. If you attend the lectures and do practice problems regularly, the course should be straightforward.

All around, Reddan is a great instructor. The class doesn't feel boring and he engages the classroom well. The biggest downside to him is his tangents. One time, he started talking about the Simpsons and how it's the best show for mathematicians. It was interesting to hear but took away time from instruction. He only teaches in the summer.

Prof. Adali was very effective in teaching the theoretical foundations of the relevant concepts and made clear connections with the applications. The assignments were beneficial for understanding the concepts and prepared us well for the exams.

Not an effective teaching professor. She can laugh or show frustration when students cannot answer questions, which some may find discouraging. Classroom interactions can feel tense. 
Core courses may be better with another professor, and non-core classes often include mostly/only her research lab students.

Dr. Adali is not qualified to be a professor. She may be qualified to work as a research professor but that is all. She gets frustrated or laughs at student's questions. She gives bare minimum material so you have to heavily study the book to prepare for exams. She may ignore you if she feels you are not doing well in class. Very disappointing
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Hard tests, but she teaches all of what you will need from the test in class. She is very knowledgeable, you just have to study her class notes and do the homework many times. Excellent teacher, the best in the department
Woohoo best prof
She knows the subject very well.if you ask a question,she will make sure you undrestand.
She knows the subject very well.

Not very eager to help students with comprehension. Laughed at several students for answering incorrectly in class. Assumes that students have same prior knowledge as she. Gives difficult tests that are not easily finished in time allotted. Does not give take home tests.

Did not teach some of what was in the course description. Test items were fair, but grading was not (i.e. deducted points for x^H = x^T, x = real). Refused to provide notes for days that I had to miss class, and that material was on the test. Changed assignment for a month's work, claimed lack of convergence.  When confonted, admitted convergence.

Took ENME 110 during the summer. Although it was a very fast paced for a 8 week course. Prof B did a very good job at explaining every concept with detail and many different approaches. He genuinely cares for his students to do well. Homework was very similar to the exams. Def recommend.
Took him for ENME 464, not 204. Professor Bridandolph has a long way to go when it comes to teaching, but he's chill fr.

I had a really good experience taking this class. Prof. Bridendolph often correlates some of the course material with personal work and designs he did in the industry which made the lectures extremely engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It's very obvious he cares a lot about teaching engineering, as he always seemed very interested in everyone's projects. That being said, lecutres were very mundane in my opinion. He tried to spice them up but I could tell they were just recycled. The work for that class isn't super hard if you know CAD, there's just a lot of it.
Great Professor. Extremely personable and always make a point of utilizing office hours for any question related to the course.

Not great lecturer. Just 2 quizzes covered lecture material. Useful stuff (e.g. CAD) learned in the Labs w/ TAs. The group project and reverse engineering project is the majority of the work. Some dates/grading criteria were not clear in the class . Lecture material didn't matter except for lecture quizzes and (scarce) relevance to projects.

Overall a really fun class. Showing up and paying attention makes the class makes it super easy and he's also really approachable and friendly plus he's funny. He gives good feedback to help you grasp foundational concepts, he's also very flexible with assignments. The assignments are super fun too.
I love him

Honestly, if you show up and do the work it's an A you don't even need to be a good photographer you just need to attempt it. The only thing I didn't like was that since we turned things in on a Google Drive that he has access to there were no grades in bb he'd tell you verbally what your grade is but it would've been nice to have it written down.

The issue with this course was the messy and non-negotiable environment. The worst part was the perfectionist expectations that the professor held for the students. Students would receive low scores, even when their work was highly detailed. Her standards for what qualifies as perfect are unusually high, almost impossible to reach.

She is uniquely terrible at her job among UMBC's art professors. She is uninterested in teaching more than the bare minimum, directing us to tutorial videos that don't help. She doesnt teach important tools like program shortcuts, yet expects them from us. These are long projects, but she admits to not viewing them fully before giving an F.

She is self obsessed and disorganized. She calls peoples work disturbing, for minor issues and awful at giving people authentic feedback just saying that it looks wong or needs to be changed without any explanation. Her Syllabus is confusing and doesn't match to what she says during class. I dropped out due to her disrespectful attitude.

A good professor and is very knowledgeable about Graphic Design. I have learned a lot about Design that I didn't know before. I think most of the negative reviews are people that would argue just to prove they are right. I will say, her communication is not very good but she still cares about your work, you as a student just need to be respectful.

If this was my first introduction to graphic design, I would've switched majors. Drags lessons on longer than necessary, gives conflicting advice, will not let students record or take notes during lectures, and the designs she teaches are just confusing. If she edits part of your work, she'll critique it the next day not knowing SHE made it. Avoid!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: heavy on attendance, disrespectful, dont get sick because you wont have an excused absence, contradicts her own rubrics, directions, and crits. Will edit your work and then hate it the next day, and then get defensive when you say she did it. Would recommend taking this class with a different professor.
Changes her feedback depending on her mood, refuses to acknowledge when she's wrong, and does not give clear instructions

By far my favorite design prof at UMBC. She can be a tough cookie but intends to better you as a designer. She has plenty of design knowledge to share and brings the heat to critiques. Don't take her words to heart, she means no harm. You'll see your work grow throughout projects and the feedback will pay off!

She is not the best teacher. She gives tough criticism and is sometimes rude about it. She often contradicts herself in the feedback she gives students. Also not very understanding in my own experience of certain situations. She made me feel terrible and hopeless about my work and discouraged my interest in graphic design.

Great designer... Awful professor. She will tear down your design and your soul. While she gives a lot of feedback on how to correct your design, she will also insult your performance (ex: "If I was a design company, I would've fired you by now"). Took away my interest in book design and made me fearful of each critique session I have with her.
I attended her class last year. I had a hard time communicating with her, and the feedback she gave me was not very helpful. She is qualified as an artist, but not a professor.

Gives a ton of feedback but you have to learn how to understand her because she doesn't communicate very well. Impossible to reach outside of class and gives no feedback on submitted assignments. She's an amazing graphic designer but a terrible teacher. I learned nothing about the technical side of graphic design and only background and history.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's a designer first and teacher last. Shes very knowledgeable but a terrible explainer. Frequently goes on tangents and if youre not one of her favorites expect little remarks as to what you did right. Contradicts her own critiques and has her own tastes where if you dont meet them expect your grade to drop. She's a good person, but a bad prof
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: MY FAVORITE PROFESSOR! She knows everything there is about graphic design and she really helps you improve your skills. The class is not really hard. She grades based on if you listen to her feedback and fix what needs to be changed. A lot of her criteria is unclear so you should go over it with her to make sure.

Long overdue review, for context I had my class with her during Fall 2019. It was one of my worst experiences at UMBC. I was criticized for every action I did although it was the same as my peers which was approved. Got my first panic attack then. Felt pretty much worthless. She did end class with "Oh, I was a bit hard on you" with a laugh
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Grading criteria and assignment directions are often UNCLEAR. Make sure to ask for clarification or examples if you're confused. Hours of work go down the drain with one misunderstanding. Otherwise, I think she gives honest, direct feedback. She is understanding and often times gives us extra time if we express concerns on a deadline. Good class.

Professor Abraham is very kind and flexible, it was a difficult and busy year but she was very committed to her class despite all the hardships. Take notes on her feedback and participate in lectures, she'll appreciate it. This class breaks down design principles and builds makes you reconsider your process, there's room for failure, & fun projects
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She clearly has experience in the graphic design field but makes this lower level class more difficult than it should be with unclear directions and critiques. Her critiques can come off quite harshly or rude even though she is trying to help. Though I have never had her in person, online is not the best option for this class or this professor.

Horrible professor, did not like her. Her grading criteria was not clear AT ALL. Show to students once on how she graded but yet did not even follow it. Unclear on how she graded any students assignment. She will grade you on how enthusiastic you are in the course. If you are not then she will give you a bad grade. Worst professor ever. DONT TAKE

Professor Abraham is a highly talented graphic designer and has a strong grasp on the principles of good design. You will learn the most from her feedback, so I recommend you really listen and understand what she is telling you. If you are humble and willing to take her feedback, you will find this an easy class!

-No individual work in the class (no lab), she want everything to be done at home.  -every class, she gives lecture (usually showing other students work) and critique work that you did at home.  - very subjective -Will take your computer to rearrange your designs - instructions are not clear - she doesn't respect students option or work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This professor is so knowledgeable about the field. It's refreshing to have a professor who gives real life examples and assigns projects that you can actually put in your portfolio! I loved this teacher. She at times gives directions that are hard to understand and contradictory, but overall she was great. She gives great feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Guenet is a Graphic Designer, not a teacher. Until she learns how to differentiate, you might as well find a random client on the street to teach the class for you because it will practically be the same thing.

She does contradict herself often and really pushes her students which is why she has the poor reputation she does. However she is completely understanding and there to help you if you take the time to get to know her and ask for help. Respect and participation go extremely far and she is known for giving students several design opportunities

Professor Abraham really cares about her students and wants to see you pass the class, but she's really terrible to work with. She is very confusing and clear with what she wants, and flips back and forth of her opinion. Although she has great feedback, she's very picky of what she wants, and she's very criticizing, and gives you C's for no reason.

Guenet is a great professor, however she is a lot of design students first experience with a 'client' so she gets a bad rep. She is honest with her critiques which really pushes you to improve. Despite her flip-flopping, she is extremely helpful and you'll love your work in the end. If you don't, that's not her fault.
So bad! This professor shouldn't be teaching. Anyone  half-decent graphic design teacher giving you the same assignment would do an equal or better job. Nothing special here.
GD 1 as a class was generally easy but she is a horrible professor. You won't learn as much from this professor compared to others in the department. Avoid Guenet if possible.
Learnt alot from her one on one. She is ver frustrating to work with and is very wishy washy with what she wants. She has great knowledge of design and type. If you make an effort she will too.
She has a lot of experience and is knowledgeable about graphic design but she is a terrible professor. She doesn't really teach anything, but rather critiques based on her style preference.

She is horrible! you will pretty much have to take her as a GD Major here at UMBC, but she is so scatterbrained, always flip flops on what she wants you to do, she will tell you to change something, then decided she dosent like it that way.  There are no deadlines until the final crit.

She is an extremely caring and understanding person. She is not clear often and some of her projects seem like busy work rather then something that will actually help you develop your skills. Overall she cares about her students learning and she wants them to be happy. Not a bad teacher at all

Guenet is awesome! Definelty one of my favorite professors at UMBC. She is extremely helpful to anyone who truly wants to learn. She is honest with your work and has tons of experience to back up her opinions. If you don't get a lot out of this class it's because you didn't put enough in it. I can't wait to have her in the future!
Probably the most sincerely nice professor I've ever had at UMBC. She is always willing to help and is always perfectly honest with your work.
she is not very clear with her assignments and also never responds to emails. her homework are not hard but the directions are very vague.

She chooses favorites, forgets who you are if you are not a favorite, and grades arbitrarily. She's also always late. She forgets to mention details about the assignments. She's a nice person and GD majors pretty much have to have her as a teacher, but she's not a very good teacher.

She has a lot of real world experience and knowledge. She's not ridiculous and anal about stupid things either, and doesn't baby-sit. If you do good work, you get a good grade. No stupid gimmicky crap to pointlessly stress you out. I really liked her, and I'm taking her next class next semester.
She's too scatterbrained and has too many other responsibilities to be a good teacher. It was an easy class but I learned nothing.
Very nice, easy going atmosphere in the class, not the easiest grader unless you spend the big bucks printing... don't fall behind cuz she doesn't have weekly deadlines.
Love Guenet! Hard but worth it, You learn a lot and she gets really involved. You should try to learn as much from her as possible.
Great professor, relaxed classes, no deadlines until final crit, helps you improve your work, just really a great sincere person outside of class too.

Took Dr. B for CMSC 441. He will be the first to admit that he isn't the right prof for everyone, but I loved the class. Algorithms is interesting topic and Dr. B wants you actually learn how to critically think. The lectures are fun and he brings good energy to class. Just make sure to stop him and ask questions because he does talk quickly.

Professor Bargteil is an excellent professor. The only downside is that he has nothing to do with the projects. If you start the projects early and go to office hours the projects aren't too bad. As for lecturing, all you need to do is pay attention and take notes. His tests are the homeworks, but with the numbers changed. Anyone can pass him

He teaches material very fast, just ask him to slow down. His lecture doesn't use power point slides (so if you're used to that, choose a different professor). The homework he assigns is basically the exams, so just keep practicing those. Lastly, his writing can be difficult to read, so ask him/clarify what he wrote.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: AVOID! writes tiny unreadable gibberish on the board. he has never actually coded in front of us and only writes it in his terrible handwriting with 30 errors. he didn't know which proj we were on! and he forgets to assign the hw on time and doesnt change the due date. he doesnt teach the material assigned in the projects so good luck not failing.

Super chill and easygoing. A bit disorganized and bases lectures on what the class wants to focus on. But they are pretty engaging; he'll give advice and tell interesting stories from time to time. Exams are very similar to homeworks so it's easy to do well if you understand those.

Bargteil is a very lax grader with 15% of the grading going towards homework assignments you get full credit on if you turn literally anything in (blank pdf included). Tests were easy as they were based on the homework assignments. However, his lectures were unorganized and I couldn't learn much from him. Easy teacher but not a good one.

Class was very straight-forward. Professor Bargteil was very knowledgeable and, although boring sometimes, lectures were very helpful. Homeworks were basically graded for completion and exams were based off homeworks, so it wasn't too difficult. Very enjoyable semester

Professor Bargteil was a good professor although sometimes lectures were a bit dry. There are 6 projects, midterm and a final, the class was pretty difficult but is manageable and there is lots of extra credit so it's not too hard to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Bargteil found a way to make the class enjoyable. He added lots of humor into his lectures as well as fun facts about important people who came up with the different algorithms covered in class. He was not always prepared for class with examples, but clearly knew the material he was talking about. Lots of fun, best CMSC prof at UMBC.

Bargteil was clearly not excited about teaching 341, he was seldom prepared for class and often made mistakes when drawing trees on the board. On the plus side, he was extremely clear about expectations on exams to the point of giving basically the same exam as a practice exam. Nice guy, I feel bad that he was forced to teach 341.

Clearly knows what he's talking about, works in the field and is generally very knowledgeable and intelligent. He heavily focuses on students actually learning and understanding the material. The course mostly follows the book and the book is pretty good. First projects are pretty difficult but they get easier and there's a lot of extra credit.

There are 6 projects worth 60% total. They are difficult and time-consuming. Partial credit is very generous, just get something running. This class covers a lot of difficult material. He is not good at explaining it, but does not expect you to learn all of it. Tests are hard, but curved as much as 40-50%. Work hard and you can get a B.

great prof 
made it easy to understand material

I took his Math 215 class this past summer (Summer 09') because I heard all the bad reviews about Kapoor. Only Kapoor teaches Math 215 during the regular school year, so I definitely wanted to take Vancea, from the good reviews he got. Let me tell you, go to class, pay attention, act like you want 2 learn, and you will pass.  Test are not that hard

I only had Adrian as a TA for my Calculus I class. He was very clear though, and I sure as hell learned a hell of alot more from him than I did from my professor (Wilson). Adrian is a good teacher, and knows what he is talking about.
i thought i was  getting a D in the class but i ended up with a B. just make sure you go to class and look like ur trying. do the homework and participate in class
Def. take this guy, he's the best one teaching this course. Easy A+

BAD teacher, I dont understand whats going on in the class along with the rest of the class.  Unfortunately he was the only professor teaching this class.  The material he goes over in class is not clear at all.
He's friendly and helpful to students if you ask for help but his lectures are mediocre at best.
I am not sure why he has such low ratings, his classes are really easy to get A's in if you read the material and do work.
just rattles off code, does take questions or explain anything!!
He just reads the slides and says um a lot. His quizzes are hard as hell and are focused on small details in comparison to the full chapter. DO NOT TAKE HIM!

reviews.comment: By far, worst professor ever. The class is very dry and tough. He lectures straight out of the textbook by showing you it and reading it. Even then, he says "um" every 2 words which drove me crazy after one lecture that I never attend them because of it. His quizzes are tough and fast paced and focus on minute details relative to the entire chapter
Ta? A joke. His lectures? A joke. This class was so unnecessarily hard. He never gives a clear grading criteria and will find anything to take point off of.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Doesn't teach that well.. No friendly interaction with students .. Gives out tests suddenly out of nowhere.. Just not motivated to teach
Uses R and teaches quantitative methods. Highly recommended.
Organized course. You know what to expect. Grades on time and answer questions accurately. Sharp guy.

The huge group project dominates the class. Groups are assigned by him, and the project will be difficult if your group members aren't up to it. It's a lot of work. He can be snarky to students who ask questions or answer them incorrectly during class, even though he encourages participation. Tests and quizzes are easy, open book, & taken online.

Dr. Koru is a nice guy.   However I'm not a fan of the timed online quizzes and exams.  On two occasions for quizzes my connection failed which affected my grade.  Luckily he allowed me to take those two quizzes over.   Make sure your group for the project has strong programmers.
Professor is very professional and "clean cut". Class has a ton of work, but isn't really difficult. I found it extremely boring but others may disagree. Overall, good professor.
The course is among the most difficult courses I have ever taken. Having said that, the professor is helpful and he is an expert.

This class was pretty heavy workload-wise. There were weekly readings and online quizzes (open book). Your grade relies primarily on a semester-long group project. Dr. Koru actually provides useful feedback in a timely manner, though he may not seem to be the most approachable person. Ask plenty of questions.
Answered questions to clarify any issues in a timely manner.  Available via email.

Not easy but gives a lot of insight. I was working full time while taking this course. Course project is a real project which is difficult so teamwork is important. Examples given in the class were helpful.

The course was well organized. Weekly readings and project were useful. We learned Ruby programming and I am looking forward to learning Ruby on Rails. The professor is an expert and he has been helpful in programming tasks
gives good guidelines and grades on time.. he knows a lot. he is nice, the course is hard but useful... pleasant experience overall

Such a useful course for my current and future jobs. He is a very helpful, warm, and wonderful person but make no mistake; when it comes to academics he is also an expert and he'll make you work hard. Quizzes are useful and they keep you on track. The project is tough but gives insight.

Course material is interesting  and very useful.  Your grade is based off of online quizzes , an online midterm, participation, and a project.  Project is very time consuming  so don't make your scope too large.  The professor's grading style is strange so you may get low deliverable scores even though you met all of the requirements. Nice but dull

Very professional appearance and presentation, but a normal underneath (don't let the 20pg syllabus fool you). Be professional with your project deliverables.  Reading quizzes every week, but they're easy.  Project deliverables are tough, involved, and the core of your grade, so be prepared.  Compared to the other teachers, he's the one you want.

I am taking the systems analysis and design from him. The expectations are crystal clear. The project is extremely useful. The best organized class among I've taken so far. The professor is very knowledgeable.

Directions for class assignments are vague or contradictory.  He doesn't explain why he considers answers to problems to be correct or not.  His sylabus is innacurrate with regard to project due dates.  Expects 100% class attendance even though he often isn't there when projects are due, so TA's from OTHER CLASSES end up grading your work.

Tied for worst teacher ever.  Very little help on projects. sub/ta gave exams, hard to understand, boring as hell and reads from slides. TA grades all documents after converting them to chinese.  Had class grade quizzes and made up answers as he went and couldn't explain why certain answers were right. would not explain grades when asked

She breaks all the material down into simplistic and realistic concepts, only teaching students what they need for a foundational understanding of STATs. She is a kind person and a generous grader. Show up to lectures for hints on what material will be heavy/important on the next quiz/exam. For Kifle, he is a tough grader & has hard lectures.

Probably one of the best professors here but if you like self-studying on your own and skipping some lectures/discussions you will definitely lose some meaningful points. Outside of that , accessible outside of class(including discord) , tries to know everyone's names, and definitely cares!

Class itself was difficult, many different things to remember, but no matter who you take it with it would be tough. Professor is super nice and she takes the time to learn everyone's names and is super lenient if you can't make a class or so. Overall she was really nice, and cares about making her students understand the material.

reviews.comment: Very well structured classes and lectures. Grading wise: she gives 2 quizes off and 1 homework for free, exams aren't hard and most of the quizes are based on discussion. Slides are helpful as well. In a class of like 100+ kids she will know all of you by name. She is lowkey chill and has great office hours; would definetely recommend.

reviews.comment: Overall good professor no complaints, she's nice and makes a boring class not so boring. Very lenient and friendly.

reviews.comment:
100/100 RECOMMENDED !!
Just go through her lectures and the study guides she provides before the exam. SHE WILL even go thru the study guide with the whole class well that's what you will be seeing on EXAM ;).And if you don't understand any QA from the Study guide, She probably will upload videos for those QA on YouTube. And it's an STRAIGHT A  :)
Very access outside of class, really cares about student's success. she gives out prior exams that are super helpful to study before exams.

reviews.comment: Her class is pretty easy. It is exam heavy but they are almost the same as the study guides. Other than that, her lectures are kind of boring and don't make sense until the last 15 minutes

reviews.comment: An overall great professor! Attendance is mandatory and readings from the night before are discussed in class so be prepared for that. She was very understanding of extenuating circumstances and cares about students succeeding!

lots of reading but really easy. assignments were all simple, really lenient grader and very approachable. attendance was mandatory, lectures were easy and she likes participation. had us write a paper on a piece of media of our choice which was fun. open note/open book exams were great. great zero stress class.

Professor Novistskaya cares a lot about what she is teaching, and it's a pretty informative class. Homework after class through Perusall with readings, it's a simple 3 annotations, a few pop quizzes, sometimes she tells you beforehand. One midterm and final (study guide can be used during them) with some group discussion.

reviews.comment: Dr. Novitskaya is so incredibly kind and her genuine passion for GWST makes the course engaging and inspiring. Highly recommend her class.

Never take this class if you are in your right mind. She would never listen to any requests or anything. It would be like hell for finals. Very careless and I would say not at all worthy for credit. You will suffer her classes. DO NOT TAKE THIS FOR CREDIT.

reviews.comment: Great teacher in every aspect.

Loved her! She was sweet, caring, and very knowledgable. She also was very open to different opinions. Most of the class is graded on very easy pop quizzes and class activities. She is understanding and a very easy grader.

Professor Novitskaya is one of the sweetest professors at UMBC. She is very passionate and makes her lectures very interesting and engaging. The class is fairly easy with annotations on an assigned reading due before class, 2 papers, and 1 midterm/final. She also brought snacks for us on the last week. I would def recommend taking her class:)

She's really sweet and passionate about her work, which is evident from her detailed lectures. She's very easy to engage with during class and allows for interactive discussions among students at allocated times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Novitskaya is very sweet and soft spoken. The way she teaches her lessons makes it clear she is very passionate about her work. Before class we read/annotated a couple articles and there were two papers and one midterm in total. Very simple and interesting course. I would def take her class again!

She's a really kind, caring, and helpful person, you can tell she is passionate about the topics, her job, and what not, along with the topics being interesting and relevant to our time. Definitely recommend taking a class with her, I had her my first semester and am taking a class with her this Spring semester 2025.

I loved being in Dr. Novitskaya's class this semester. She is very passionate about GWST and makes lectures fun and engaging. In every class before the lecture, we had annotations due from our readings (most of them super interesting) and two papers in the semester. I would recommend her class if you want a fun and interesting GEP.

Prof. Novitskaya is very sweet and well-spoken; it is clear that she is passionate about GWST and really cares about her students. Her lectures are very entertaining. She asks a lot of thought-provoking questions and she really appreciates when her students respond. That being said, if you don't like to discuss, this is not the class for you.

go. to. office. hours! If you go to office hours you will get the easiest A of your academic career. If you don't, best of luck passing. Aside from this, Dr. Tokay is super friendly and geniunely fun to spend time with in office hours.

Every assignment also has a built in curve of 30-40 points.

reviews.comment: I took ges 311 in spring 2019 and I would highly recommend his class! He is very passionate about the subjects and if you pay attention and do the homework, you will do just fine! Be attentive during lectures because everything that is on the tests in directly from the lectures and homeworks. Great class! Learned so much!

It's very homework heavy, and the homework is really hard, but he is very helpful and available outside of class. Personally, I wouldn't recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Tokay is a great professor. He is very understanding of personal issues and helps you to do well in the class. He realizes that his class is tough, so he gives A LOT of extra credit and holds long office hours. You can get an A if you focus of accumulating the extra credit points and go to office hours for everything (especially homework)!

If you're not extremely interested in meteorology, DO NOT take this class. There is a lot of complicated math involved that is explained very poorly. The professor is very enthusiastic, but his slides just consist of paragraphs he reads verbatim during lecture.
The tests are not that difficult. There is plenty of extra credit on both the tests and the hw. The professor is very willing to help.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROF! His voice seems to elevate during the most insignificant points in the lecture and he snaps his fingers frequently to wake you up.  Lecture material is incomprehensible and tests are extraordinarily difficult.

Impossible course. Posted the lectures online, which were the exact same thing as what he went over in class. Except they make no sense whatsoever. If you think you're just learning about weather, then forget it. There is math involved and it's not easy. Not recommended. Take P/F if you have to.
Syllabus included a 5% discretionary grade where he reserved the right to change your grade by 5%.  He didn't like me falling asleep in his class and he changed my final grade from 94% to 89%

Rude to students. Not given enough time for exams. Exam grading based on answers, NOT work (have to do work for points though), so if you mess up algebra, you lose points, and answers feed into one another, so the mistakes compound. Mandatory attendance for grades. Ineffective teaching. Avoid Khan at all costs if you value your GPA and sanity.

Barely, if at all, explains theory and skips directly to the example problems. Concepts and examples no sense without understanding the theory. Exams and quizzes often range in the 40-70% with no curve. Often rude to students, Encourages questions only to tell you that its too simple and you need to reread past notes/textbook ask the TA.

Participate for "brownie points" by asking questions, but half answers question, skips steps with algebra for the sake on time, but then complains when you ask a question. Not very tech savvy - nothing posted on blackboard, all homework sent in emails. Very harsh grader.
khan is the worst teacher everrrrrr. His grading is so unclear. He does not help at all. We could make up an exam with the final but he didn't choose the best one so it was a gamble.
Awfeul
Just overall not a nice guy. Is not understanding.

literally avoid like the plague. so many things are messed up with him, ask ANYONE in the department about him and they will have plenty, PLENTY of horror stories to share with you.
Probably the worst professor ive ever had. He is rude and racist. Dont bother asking a question because he will make fun of you. If you dont understand the TA is very nice and welcoming.

He's great

Terrible teacher. I have never heard any teacher asked to give him good evaluation grades except this creation. Avoid him as much as you could.

Terrible teacher. Avoid. I received an A, but I had to teach myself everything. His lectures are useless, and asking him questions doesn't help because he gets confused and never actually answers the questions that students ask him. Stay away from him.

Even the Pharaoh of Egypt would be considered humble compare this monster. The sheer frustration of dealing with his wishy washy guidelines and random grading system is enough to brand him a bad egg. Yet he also manages to be incredibly unclear, mean and immune to reason. The text book is almost never used, dont buy it.

he's a nice guy but sometimes could be a little obnoxious, overall a good professor, grades you nicely and work isn't that hard you just gotta study a few hours a week for math 106, I would only recommend him for ANY math classes, but I think he only teaches math 106.

Alex cares about his students and tries to make hard material understandable, I really like his style. He's great! Grading on online ALEKS HW (hate!), quizzes, and exams (not bad). reviews.comment: Professor Sheranko was spectacular. He's one of those professors who actually tries at his job and it shows. He's very sympathetic with students who don't get the material (like me) and is extremely flexible and willing to help at any point. Be warned though, the class itself is tough (especially because it uses the ALEKS program for homework)

Professor Sheranko is great! He's super funny and time to explain problems. Attendance was not mandatory but definitely do attend them. He posts blank and annotated slides. There were weekly quizzes and Aleks which were a bit annoying.
He was the type of grader when I would take the exam or quiz instead of leaving the grade blank he would input a 0% as if I didn't take it so I didn't know my grade until grades were due.

Professor Sheranko is definitely one of the best professors at UMBC. The content is challenging at times, but he made it bearable. He would joke around in class and was great at making connections with students. The ALEKS homework is tedious and there are quizzes every week, but going to office hours was always helpful with studying. 10/10!

The weekly quizzes were a bit much, but he provides study guides with multiple examples of each question and the answers. He's very open to questions and provides thorough lectures. Make sure you study for the quizzes/exams! The weekly homework on ALEKS wasn't too bad either. Also, make sure to go to the lectures! You won't do well otherwise.

Super cool teacher that advocates for everyone's success and will help you as long as you put in the effort back. Make sure to ask questions if you need to, his explanations are very clear, concise and thoughtful. Also MAKE SURE TO ATTEND LECTURES EVEN IF THEY ARE OPTIONAL they are very very helpful. Prof Sheranko is also v funny and genuine.

Sheranko is super chill and wants you to succeed. The homework on ALEKS gets a bit tedious (why I didn't get an A), but if you go to lectures and ask questions, you'll be great. The reviews are very similar to what you'll see on the tests, and he is always open to questions. If you don't understand something, office hours are a lifesaver trust me.

reviews.comment: Shares his projects with prof Mironov, his lectures are pretty boring and I basically stopped going to them altogether as the class discord with the TAs from mironovs section is a way better resource. Prof. Allgood seemed unprepared for CMSC 313. His lectures involved copying problems to the board, but these often contained errors he struggled to fix and students frequently had to correct him. reviews.comment: Not the best lecturer, especially for a class like 421 where there's not many resources. I had to rely on the TAs a lot. Tests were also like long.

Most of these reviews do not align with anything I have seen in his courses and are most likely written by students who are not locked in.

1. Fair exams: no cheat sheets, short essay style, completely fair.
2. Projects: assigned & graded by other profs. (not great)
3. Lectures: boring, lowkey impossible to listen, can skip, review slides alone.
4. Grading: 3 exams, 30% homework (practically a curve), 4 projects.

Overall: not a bad prof!

Prof taught using other profs slides and did not know the content. Gave a single midterm with 17 pages of work in a 70 min class. Projects were interesting, but rubrics were vague. Very nice person, connects to students well, however prone to frequent tangents about unrelated content.

His lectures and slides are basically the same. Lectures are skippable, and exams are on the easier side. Not a good lecturer. Start projects early since he doesn't do in class coding for topics related to the projects. Besides the projects, it's not that hard to get an A, just study for exams, do homeworks, and start projects early.

I had professor Nick Allgood for Software Engineering I, but my only options on this site were only 341 and 201.
