The experience you get in diagrams, Jira, problem solving, documentation, testing, etc. are all important

Lectures are snoozers; distracted easily, reads off the slides, and barely does in-class coding. Projects are difficult but manageable. Exams were nasty but were curved/graded lightly. He also changed the final exam date without announcing it until the day before exams started. Avoid Allgood if you want to learn and avoid tearing your hair out.

Allgood talks in a monotone voice and is impossible to focus on. At some point I stopped attending his class completely and my grade was the same. One time at the end of a lecture he said "Okay, now who wants to watch me play Dark Souls 3?" so definitely a kind and cool guy but not a great teacher unfortunately, I wish him well with his PhD program

Professor Allgood's lectures are monotone and extremely boring. I often tried to ask questions in class and he was unable to answer. Went to his office hours and he turned to the internet to explain one of the more important topics to me. His explanations both in and outside of class are unclear, so be prepared to teach yourself the content.

I would compare Nick Allgood to Ben Johnson. He's like the first form of a Pokemon while Ben Johnson is the final evolution. Except Nick Allgood is like Ash's pikachu who refuses to evolve. Metaphors aside, you'll be teaching yourself this entire semester. He has not been useful what so ever. He can't convey material well to save his life.

Truly "all good," but could be "all great." My main gripe is that he gives out pre-written notes that he also uses as his lecture material, so I never really felt the need to take notes myself, which often led to getting distracted in class. Once I got some TA help, I did good. The exams can be unexpectedly difficult, so be sure to reread your code

He is very knowledgeable on the subject, but his lectures are hard to pay attention. If you don't understand something, I recommend asking him for help. He's a very nice and caring professor always looking to help. Projects are the same for everyone taking the course and they're very hard. Exams are individual to professors. Not easy but not hard.

Allgood just did not teach the content in a way that students could understand. He frequently second guessed his own material and left his class out of luck for the several rigorous projects. Nice guy, not a great professor.

reviews.comment: you will 100% pass this class, don't even sweat it. I had her for both CHEM 123 & CHEM 124 and she made gen chem / orgo chem so easy, it felt like breathing. exams/quizzes are all multiple choice, and if you have any questions she is very approachable. won't make you feel dumb if you don't understand a subject. she is a soft and wholesome prof.

Dr. Tracy is one of the best professors at UMBC. She is so incredibly kind and clearly wants all her students to succeed. She is easily accessible outside of class and she offers simple explanations for complex concepts. She makes chemistry feel approachable and manageable.

Dr. Tracy is one of the best professors at UMBC. She is incredibly kind and always available outside of class for additional questions. She genuinely wants every student to succeed and her passion for the topic makes the course interesting and engaging. She simplifies complex topics and makes chemistry feel approachable for every skill level.
Difficult class for me personally, but incredible professor. She's always willing to help.

lecture are prerecorded online but some test questions are from in person lectures sometimes. very kind prof and accessible outside of class. creates good energy for her lectures and shes chill. class isnt too hard with just watching lectures, you'll easily pass with an A. theyre like a cheat code to the class

Mrs. Tracy is an amazing professor and she needs to be given her flowers. So caring and just wants you to grasp the material and pass. She is truly a breath of fresh air. Her exams are online and open book (during normal class time) and classes are in the morning, which is also a lifesaver. I really haven't had a better science professor.

Alison Tracy is amazing. Exams are online and they're open book. She spends time outside of class and there's also tutoring for this class. She entertains the class very well. I highly recommend her for chemistry and she teaches it in the morning which is better than Chem 101 and 102.

Tracy is such a nice professor and was my favorite professor as a freshman. She explains problems and questions very well. You should definitely go to the lectures, it helped me a lot to understand the unit and what to prepare for an exam. Exams are open note and are online not in class too. Easy class as long as you go to lectures youll be good.

shes so amazing and kind. her lectures make eveything make sense and having the class time reserved for the problem sessions is so smart. she's a good teacher but her kindness makes up for it. she really wants you to pass and she's always free for office hours to help you out.

Professor Tracy is hands down one of the best teachers I have had in my whole academic career. She is extremely straight forward and will break down any "hard" topic to make it easier for her students. I really like the way this class is set up, kinda like a hybrid approach. Anyway I would take her again!

Tracy is such an amazing professor to have, the class is very straight forward in what you have to do. She post the lectures online and you are to watch them before coming into class. Tracy Allison is the BEST chem prof you'll ever have at UMBC. She's passionate about what she teaches. The way is super engaging and if you don't get the material she is more than happy to explain it thoroughly.
The teacher was really sweet.

Dr. Allison is a caring professor and she makes her classes interesting and it is very easy to do well and understand what is going on in the class. Chem 123 is in a hybrid format where the lecture videos are posted ahead of time and then problem sets are posted and are gone over during class time. Take this class especially if you are able to.

She is an amazing teacher and makes the class so manageable. Heavily encourage watching the online video lectures and going to in-person lectures when you can. She makes it so that you can easily get help from her or SI pass. In person, she is great at teaching new information as well. Very funny and cares for students like her own children.

Shes a great professor, very understanding, and replies to emails quickly. Do the exams and problem sets and you're good to go. She posts the lectures online and you just need to come to class having listened to it already. All exams are taken online outside of class and you can use your notes.

Very sweet lady but oh my god are the in-person problem-solving sessions a snoozefest. The asynchronous lectures are great but the problem-solving sessions arent worth it unless you're REALLY struggling.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Tracy is an amazing professor and I love the way her class is organized. She makes sure you understand the material and never tests you on something she didn't teach. Professor Tracy is by far the best professor I've had during my freshmen year. She is very passionate about chemistry and makes learning easy. Although attendance isn't mandatory I recommend going as she provides a lot more insight on the content you're learning. As long as you watch the lectures and do the work the class is relatively easy.

I absolutely loved Dr. Tracy! Her lectures were online and prerecorded. Overall, amazing professor and made life easy and the class stress free!

Professor Tracy is literally the best professor, I was so nervous for this class but she makes it so much easier to understand. Love love her energy and she is so caring. Such an amazing professor to have for a difficult topic like chem. She's very caring and wants you to understand as much as you can. so good at explaining everything and she gives so many practice problems that you will understand everything, only had to meet once a week, lectures were online, lecture videos are two hours along bc she gives so many practice problems, only have problem sets and exams, problem sets are easy and open note, final is easy if you study
Such an amazing professor, really down to earth and very easy to

Dr. Tracy is very kind and speaks about biochemistry in a way that is easy to understand. If you show up to lab, do you work (and actually try) you'll do great. If I could have her for every class, no lie, I would.

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Tracy! She teaches very well and helps students to actually LEARN the material. She is very enthusiastic about chem and I believe that that's why the class was one of my favorites. Participation is not necessarily required but we had to turn in work in class.

One of the best professors in UMBC definitely. Easy to email and ask questions, please do not hesitate to reach out to her if you are having issues with deadlines or with the work in general. She is an absolute angel when interacted with. The work is extremely specific and be prepared to write essays for your post-labs. However, still recommend.

She is the sweetest person ever. I am not a chemistry person at all but she explained everything so clearly and thoroughly that it was easy to learn. She is always willing to help, and will answer any questions you have. The tests are very challenging but if you stay on top of studying and take detailed notes you'll be fine.

Love this women. She is so kind and always comes to lectures happy to teach and cares about ALL her students. She is an absolute angel <3 I would take this class a million times just to keep her as a teacher fr. periodt.

Tracy is a very understanding and thorough lecturer! I received a 96% in this class through effort and her support. In order to do well, I recommend going to all the lectures and doing the additional textbook problems. Exams were decent, make sure you really go over the lecture notes(and take the practice exams!) she is very helpful in office hours

Dr Tracy is just amazing. She is the best professor at umbc. She is so understanding and caring. I wish all my professors at umbc were like her. She loves interacting with students. She knows each and every student by the name. She is just amazing.

Words cannot describe how incredible Dr. Tracy is. She's beyond a professor. She is always there for you, day or night, to answer any questions. Gladly see you anytime outside of office hours, spend time talking you through a problem, or even just to talk about nonsense. She'll email even late at night to help u finish a lab report on time. Amazing

Dr. Tracy is truly amazing. She's very patient and helps you a lot during exams. She's also very good at making the class material easy to understand and doesn't ever judge any student. Also! She's super funny and sweet. Def. the best professor I've ever had.

She is such a fantastic professor. She makes the student's understanding her top priority. reviews.comment: She is an absolute angel. Always willing to help. However, her exams are harder then you may think, so study hard!! Don't let her kindness fool you lol. Use SI pass sessions if available
Dr. Tracy is amazing. She cares therefore her students care as well. She is an amazing lecturer who manages to make chemistry fun. Very understanding and always willing to help students. Lover her

Dr. Tracy's Chem 123/124 class is lecture heavy, if you don't attend class and take notes, you will have a hard time with the exams. Complete all the problem sets on time, they will help boost your grade. She is very caring and will do whatever she can to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is absolutely amazing! Shes caring and understanding towards first year students and only tests on material covered in class. She is clear about the content and is willing to help anyone who needs it. Ill be taking her for chem 124 this spring and I am so excited!

AMAZING professor. Loved her. I gave it a 4 on difficulty because I find chemistry easy, however, some do not. One of the best teachers at UMBC! If you show up to class, take good notes and understand the lectures, you are set for an easy grade!

Real good instructor. Cares a lot about her students. Tests are tough, so studying is a must. Fair grader.  Accessible outside of class. Didn't use the textbook at all, you could probably get away without it.  SI Pass sessions are extremely helpful. Dropped  from a B  in 123 to a C in 124  when SI was  not offered.
Best teacher I have had at UMBC and I am saying this a senior.  There aren't enough words to describe how awesome she is.
She somehow makes the content more understandable and is extremely flexible about meeting with students.

Dr. Tracy is the sweetest! she is smart, caring, and funny! I loved taking 102 with her, she needs to teach 101 and 102 all the time, carpenters' method is not working... Dr. Tracy's exams were challenging but she was always so helpful and never moved on until you understood everything.

Dr. Tracy is a really great professor! Put a 3 on easiness only because CHEM 124 is not easy but she makes it as understandable as possible and she is very approachable if you ever have questions. I'm very glad i had her!! Would definitely recommend! Only teacher to take if you need to take Chem 123 and 124. She is clear about grading and exams
Dr. Tracy was amazing and very sweet. She explains things very clearly and makes chemistry seem soo easy. Take her!

Dr. Tracy is very clear cut and makes the material of CHEM102 seem easier than it is. No clicker questions so lecture is not mandatory. I got away with skipping a few times in the semester but she always has at least one lecture-related question on her exams (which are easier than carpenter's). She loves to answer questions during class.

Great class! I felt like I learned tons, but you have to be willing to put a lot of work to receive a high grade. She's very nice and fair so if you do the work, she will reward you. What's interesting is that you do watch films but you also learn about the history of the LGBT community in America, which was eye-opening for me.

This class was fairly easy, with readings being optional because she creates powerpoints that you go over in class that outline the main points of the articles. As long as you show up for a majority of the classes and take notes, you should do well. Prof. Householder is approachable and helpful.
Cute teacher. Hot topic. But disorganized.

There is WAY too much work demanded of this class given the fact that it is a 300 level class.  You don't realize going in that you have to see like 20 films on your own time, and the exams are certainly not easy. Didn't like a final project AND exam.
Great class. I felt like I learned a lot without having a ton of work.

I have taken a lot of women's studies and film classes, and learned a lot of the same stuff, but I actually learned a lot of new material in this class. The exams are easy if you pay attention, and the film discussions are open forum and really fun. If you love to study film and you want an engaging professor, I highly recommend this class.

this class was neat but she never really tells you how important the readings are. I think like everyone in the class did poorly on the only exam but she knows her stuff and the exam was not weighted to high so i still ended up with a B.

this class was pretty good. you have to do the readings and pay attention to lecture, but you'll learn a lot. she doesn't really give feedback on your weekly postings, but she does comment heavily on papers. and she's adorable
Im singing Hot. Hot Hot! and a great teacher. Beautiful Gorgeous and Sexy
All I can say is ha-ha-Hot! Hot professor, at first I thought she was a student until she went up in front of the class. Anyways, she has great knowledge in graphic design and very  helpful.
Hot as a beast indeed. Great professor, understanding, knowlegeable, and has a great eye for design.
Shes hot as a beast, and class was so much fun

I read all of the bad reviews on here before taking this class, but it was the only section I could fit in my schedule. If you have any choice at all, do NOT take this class. The amount of homework assigned is ridiculous, and most of it is not  even graded until finals week. I wish I would have just waited and taken it with another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: This class would have been one of the most useful classes in my professional career and she ruined it. She was unprofessional, a horrible communicator, she looked down her nose at everyone, and she was incredibly boring.
Awful professor
Yes, there are assignments.  You're in school.  Do the work.  I appreciated the work we had to do in class and I feel like I write better because of it.  I would absolutely take her class again.

She takes attendance, so if you skip three classes.. you fail. She gives so much unnecessary, long assignments, but she doesn't grade any of it. Her "lectures" are so long, boring and pointless. You don't learn anything in the class or out of class. I've never taken a class where so much unneeded work was assigned.  This class sucks.

The material learned is pretty easy and useless at the same time. WAY too many useless assignments that takes her forever to grade. Going to class is pretty much a waste of time, but attendance is mandatory and if you miss 3 classes your grade drops 1 letter. Would NOT recommend taking her!

This class was disappointing. You learn and discuss the obvious, redundantly, and she gives so much work and never grades any of it. I spent the most of my time on this class, and learned the least from. Hard to follow what is due when because there is just so much of it, and you have to coordinate with team members. do not take!
Very easy, must show up but very easy grader and lots of extra credit. Just do your work and get an A.

Although this class was somewhat of an easy "A," it was a very annoying class. I did not learn much at all. She is horrible at returning grades to us in a timely manner and gives us no feedback on repetitive assignments, so we have no idea if we are completing it correctly. It is the last day of class and we do not have most major assignments back.
Gives a lot of work, sometimes seems to be unnecessary amounts.

Assignments all felt like busy work and were too easy. On one hand it was hardly any work, but on the other I learned nothing. Lectures were prodigiously pointless. Once we just watched a Ted talk on success and that was the whole class. We didn't even discuss the video or anything.

Cannot recommend her.  She relies almost completely on handouts, and tidbits from the internet, without any concrete teaching.  There were a few helpful exercises in class, but they were overwhelmed and stifled by her indirect, enigmatic style. On top of that, she assigns far too much busywork to make the class worthwhile.  Avoid at all costs.

Stay away! She gives a crazy amount of busy work and it's difficult to follow and understand her. Her style is all over the place and so is her personality. If have to wait a semester to take this class just to avoid her, it's worth waiting.

Avoid at all costs. She assigns way too much work, including two different sets of recurring journals, and does not teach anything. Not very organized. She does however, provide helpful feedback on assignments.

Redundant class and a time waster. She's not clear about her assignments and can be strict in grading. She deducts a point leaving out a letter in a word! She teaches as if she's never taught in her life. She gives too many assignments, mainly group assignments, which take up too much time when there are more important classes to worry about.
I feel like I haven't learned anything this semester.  :-(

You will be sorry if you take this class. She gives a billion handouts which are all confusing and incomprehensible!! Her assignments are time-wasters and teach us NOTHING.  I rather take a W than try and continue in this class. It was the worst college experience of my LIFE.

This professor does provide a lot of busy work, but the material that she teaches is very applicable and useful to the assignments.  She is very helpful and always available during office hours.  She is a vice nice and understanding professor.  It is not hard to do well in this class, just do the assignments posted on BB and submit them on time.
She has a bunch of completion things due. Very sweet and wanting to help, should be an easy A

Probably the worst professor I have ever encountered. Her blackboard is terrible and it is almost impossible to follow her throughout the class. Had to take a W for the course because I never knew when anything was du. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS

Unclear and confusing presentation of material, useless busy work and assignments, unnecessarily long assignments, bombards us with handouts. I highly recommend checking out another professor for this course.

Extremely disorganized, hard to tell what is due when, assignments feel like high school.  Then again i never turned in one assignment on time, didnt submit the final paper, and still got a B so i guess shes ok...
Never responded to my e-mails. Blackboard was the messiest thing I've ever seen so it becomes very easy to miss assignments. Do not take this class with her.

Definitely one of, if not the worst Professor's I've ever had. No one ever knows what's going on in the class & I don't think she does either. She is extremely unorganized and her handouts and Blackboard site are extremely lengthy. This is the first class I've really felt totally lost in & I am a senior. Good luck!!!!
She assigns so much work and does not stick to the syllabus. She does not have clear directions and does not specify things. I was extremely frustrated throughout this whole entire class.

She made me feel like I was in first grade again. Nothing was graded until the week before the semester ended, so nobody had any idea of what their grades were. There were way too many group projects/assignments. The class was, however, incredibly easy, and since it was held in a lab, everyone was on the computers messing around all class.

Not the best teacher. Assigns NUMEROUS assignments. Doesn't grade on time. Attendance is mandatory. A lot of lecture in class. Be prepared to for help because you need to ask her A LOT of questions.Definitely go to the writing center. Be prepared to do numerous writing assignments.My writing seemed to improve because of all the writing assignments.

Great professor.  I dreaded this class because I hate writing but it has taught me to be a much better writer.  I gave it 100% effort and I really benefited from it.  She wants the students to do well.  She is tough (but fair) and you are in college so you should be putting in all of your effort anyways.  Don't be lazy and you will do well.
not the most helpful teacher and there is a lot of writing but if you follow her directions you'll get an A

I've had her for 101 and 393 and got A's for both classes.  She may take a while to grade papers but she does give very thorough feedback.  She is a fair grader if you put the time in and she notices.  Class is mandatory and she usually tries to engage the class a lot -> miss class = -grade. Overall a great teacher, don't understand the bad reviews

horrible prof. rude, and off the wall comments all the time. Never gave feedback, didnt help students. Talked about students behind their back in a negative way. I got an A, but it took alot of kissing butt. Other people did more work than I did and got Bs.

Took a summer tech writing and while there is a lot of work it seems reasonable the problem is this professor doesn't provide any feedback.  You can't learn without graded feedback throughout.  I got a B in the class and have no idea why.  Nothing is learned from this class making it a huge waste of time.

I think the comments on this site about Professor Walters are a little too harsh. If you have any problems with her grading and think that you deserve better, you can always go to her and ask her for help. Also, she lets you re-do tons of assignments. If you're still having trouble, use the WRITING CENTER. She's also extremely nice.

Show up in class, do most of the work, the "huge essay" isn't hard, and you don't even have to do 25,000 words.  READ THE SYLLABUS CAREFULLY and that assignment is a breeze.  She isn't good at returning stuff though, so it's hard to tell where you are at through the semester.
this lady made us write a 25,000 word essay....if you enjoy english please spare yourself disappointment...
No grading done. She hasn't gotten back to us on any assignment we've done. She hasn't helped us become better writers, at all.

Really guys, she was not that bad of a professor. I've actually learned a lot from her. She focuses more on the conceptual part of writing, which other ENGL100 professors tend to ignore. Yes, she does have a lot of writing assignments--it's still a college-level english class--but they are easy, and the topics are very broad.

She is by far the most inconsistent teacher on the planet. She never gives the papers back on time, her midterm was an exercise in futility the research paper forces you to write 2500 words on something you do not want to do even a little bit. Anyone who is facing her as a professor i suggest you put English off a semester.

I don't understand why everyone thinks she's so difficult. She's probably the easiest professor I've had. I mean it's an English class so you have to expect to write. She's not helpful and she's boring, but her class is a piece of cake compared to my high school English classes.

I don't even know where to begin to describe how bad this class was.  Best advice you will ever receive: DO NOT TAKE THIS TEACHER. Even if it's your last chance. Wait until next semester.  There's a good 8 or more papers to write, with all these extra pointless assignments added to them.  Seriously, if you want to pass, do not take.

While she, as a teacher, can be bearable the amount of work assigned a week is unbelievable. I write more in this 100 class than any of my 300 level writing intense classes. She may be okay but the work is not.
By far one of the worst teachers i've ever had.. nothing special about her, i HIGHLY recommend you stay away from this one...

We had about seven or eight papers in this class and by the end of the semester we got back like two of them. There was an extreme assignment during the end of the semester where we had to write 23,000 words of anything. I didn't see the point to that because she wasn't going to read it because she takes forever to grade. I hated this class.

I think I received two useful pieces of information from this professor during the entire semester. She wasted time reading over material that students could clearly read for themselves, rather than simply asking for questions.

This class by far is a nightmare.  I dread dragging myself to class and sitting there.  The WHOLE class feels this way.  She isn't helpful much at all.  You don't get your papers back before the next one is due which makes it hard for you to improve your writing skills.  Do NOT take her class unless it's the last one you can possibly take.
She should seriously consider finding a new career. By far, she is THE most irresponsible and unprofessional teacher I've had the misfortune of taking a class from.

Although attendance is apart of your grade, she doesn't ask questions.  Her email was messed up with SPAM this semester, but she is definitely helpful!  Don't read too many books, just more writing.  I HATE English, but she has definitely helped me become a better writer!
Great teacher! She understands that writing is a learning process that takes more than one class to perfect.
Tough teacher but pushes you to beyond what you think you can do.  I'm going to be writing much longer thesis papers later and I think she was trying to help prepare us for that.

This Teacher is terrible, half the time you don't even know what's going on. Does not follow syllabus, late and sometimes no show..Does not ever return you papers, or give you guidelines to what she wants...I think she is a****2....Will give 10 page papers for homework...and expect them to be turned in with no problems..huh? Just Avoid Her!
aweful teacher and should quit immediately. doesnt even understanding what she is teaching and cant grade for crap

Professor goes over slides with little to no words on them. His explanations are very vague and don't have any actual substance or information. He expects you to be paying attention at all times as well as he will call on students randomly. He clearly does not have enough experience as a teacher and it is a big gamble to stay.

I was there when my classmates made these reviews.I gave him a 4/5 because from the beginning of the class, it seemed pretty boring and hard (ONLY because he's new at UMBC). Just save yourself the stress and don't take him currently. His inexperience shows and it was just a gamble for me staying in the class. His explanations are vague, his slides are either too many words or pictures with little to no words. His exam structure is vague, can't take constructive criticism and left good fake reviews for himself.

reviews.comment: This class was super lecture-heavy, and the professor didn't explain things well. The syllabus didn't match how the class was actually graded, which was confusing. He was slow to grade and hard to reach, but he is a pretty easy grader. The class did get a bit better toward the end, but overall it was hard to stay engaged.

This Professor is horrible, he doesn't respond to emails, can't teach (his explanations are vague) his slides are either completely overly verbose or pictures with little to no words. His exam structure is vague and can't take constructive criticism, leaves good fake reviews for himself. This class is truly a gamble please save yourself the stress.

reviews.comment: Some of the ratings about this professor are completely wrong. Take a different professor. He will confuse you throughout the whole semester, and when you email him, he will take weeks to respond to simple questions. The class was in complete confusion learning from this professor.

Worse professor. I usually nvr post on here.  But this professor is posting fake 5 star ratings on here for himself. Please save yourself and take another professor if you care about understanding material.
One of the best Professors I have had in my tenure at UMBC. I truly wish he teaches other high level courses so I can take him again!

reviews.comment: Best IS professor at umbc. Responds to emails on time and for exams you are given a cheat sheet. 100% would retake this course again if I could even if it didn't count for credit.
This class was so good I almost failed on purpose so I could take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This man is the best lecturer ever to exist. Im graduating, but I don't want to cause I want to take this class again.

Good professor, made IS310 easy, doesn't teach much and is slide heavy. He also takes a while on grading. However, he will help you and he's new to UMBC, so cut him some slack as a beginner professor. Ending with an A because the class work was easy, and the exams shouldn't be hard as long as you study.
such a good professor -- really understands the students esp since its a night lecture course. would take him again since he's chill.
made IS310 much better/easier and got an A in this class which was supposed to be pretty hard. W PROF !!!!
This is the best IS310 professor ever. Amit for life.

I'm going to just put this here as an early warning. Currently taking his 425 class and he really does not teach, does not follow the syllabus, and is very very vague of what content is on the exam. It got so bad that the midterm was delayed because all the students did not know what we were suppose to study. Avoid him like the plague.

reviews.comment: Beyond amazing as a professor. Really helps build passion into photography!

A very fun and engaging class. If you remotely like any bit of photography, you will enjoy this class. Most of the assignments are enjoyable and let you get creative your own way, and isn't tough at all. Also very lenient with due dates and is very helpful when you have trouble with assignments!

Professor Voos is an amazing professor. She helped me a lot when I was struggling with personal issues during the semester. She was very flexible with due dates and always willing to help. She is very kind to her students. This class is an easy A as long as you do your work.

Easily the best teacher I ever had! Very flexible with disabilities and assignment deadlines, super kind and understanding, and allows maximum creativity for students. As someone who dislikes videography she made this class interesting and enjoyable! 10/10, favorite professor

she was very nice, understanding, supportive, resourceful, and easy to get in contact with. she showed respect for our individual submissions and projects, even personally complimenting me on one of my projects, saying she was very proud of my work. she brings great energy to the class and made me want to pursue photography more. highly recommend!!

Kindest, most laid back prof I've ever had! She's very communicative & clear on her directions. She wants the best for all her students. She offers valuable help when needed. We really only had class on days when a new project was introduced & crit day, giving us ample time to film & edit our videos! She'd host editing workshops if need be. Easy A!

Amelia is one of the best professors I have had. I didn't know much about photography but she makes the concept easy to grasp. She doesn't care about attendance or extending deadlines as long as you talk to her or email her. If I see her as a professor in any class id lady take it with her.
get ready to really have to earn those 4 credits. 47+ homework assignments, 2 written exams, 1 oral exam, several quizzes, and a final project. grades with less leniency than the military.

Didich is an excellent prof who cares about her class and students. Arabic is difficult to learn, but there's no one better to learn it with. 
Participation matters, so go to class! She'll engage e/o in Arabic, forcing you to practice what you learned. This is the only way to learn a language, so try your best and don't be afraid to make mistakes!

Professor Didich is a great professor and it would be hard to fail this class even if you're not good at picking up languages. Lectures provide a good context of French words, and homework is often, but very doable. People who do not show up to class will miss out on a lot of material, so make sure to go. Go to lectures, participate, and do HW.
Took MLL424 with her. The class is easy. She responded to questions via email quite quickly. Overall, nice professor.
She's silly. Makes you really learn the language and participate everyday. She's responsible and follows the syllabus very closely.
Great Professor, took over the summer and has clear instructions on all the assignments and tests. Very helpful would recommend
waste of a class bc of her
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! This class moves faster than 101 so studying the topics by yourself is important. She offers extra credit and cares about her students understanding what she teaches. Come to class prepared!!

French is a hard subject at UMBC, but Professor Didich is the best option. She is a fair grader (except pronunciation). If you stay on top of the VHL homework and study the lesson packets, it's manageable. She may not seem approachable at first, but if you get to know her, she is caring and wants her students to succeed. There is also extra credit!

Very friendly and informative, also passionate about the class. She does give a good amount of work but most assignments take less than 5 minutes. Very patient but will not tolerate disrespect towards herself or other students. Makes sure everyone gets a turn to speak. She is particular about wring formatting with assignments and will remove points
Great professor. She is very patient and takes time to explain the topics. Her quizzes are easy.

Most caring professor!! She cares about her students so much and truly wants everyone to pass. Participation is a big part of the class, but as long as you put in the effort, you'll get the points. She's also an easy grader and gives a lot of extra credit. It's an easy A if you do the homework and attend class!

She is a good professor but is definitely tough on people. She knows people take language credits for reqs but still expects you to respect her and the content. Lots of HW with multiple things due a week but this is the nature of language learning. DW as the HW is pretty easy. IMO if you do the work and turn everything in you will have no problems.

she was very mean and condescending. took her twice and I couldn't finish my 201 with her because I hated being around her. She definitely expects you to learn everything on your own. If you don't know something she'll keep pressing, and embarrasses you. a lot of homework. She wants you to prioritize her classes as if its the only class you have...
Took arabic 101 last year and 2 its pretty easy in the beganning but gets harder towards the end. She usually caters more to the arab students for obvious reasons

I am going to be straightforward
She expects you to be a person who already should know things
She expects you to give this class as much importance as your MAJOR!
She is a very terrible and unfair grader 
She doesn't consider hard work and effort 
She would give you questions in the exam that she never taught in class
SHE LOVES GIVING LOW SCORES!

TAKE ARABIC WITH HER!!! I guarantee you will not be bored in her class. If you are a active learner, she is the professor for you. Weekly HW packet due, but it is not a stress. Super kind and funny. Also engages everyone in class (everyone participates in class). She takes the time to make sure you understand. Not many like her at UMBC.

Had her for French 201, and it was hard. Moved quickly, easy to get left behind if you don't lock in. "You-get-it-or-you-don't" grading. Can't say she's nice, but can't say she's mean either. Tests every other week, LOTS of HW on VHL (may differ in future). Take a lower French class first if you haven't done any since ~junior year high school, fr.

She is a great professor. The class is structured well so you always can expect when an assignment is due each week. Although there is a good amount of homework, it is very useful especially when preparing for tests. Finally, she is very nice and gets to know each individual student.

I could not stand this woman as she made it so incredibly difficult to learn. She didn't like to repeat herself and doesn't like it if someone doesn't know off of the first try. She teaches based off of the textbook and expects you to come prepared with the knowledge from the text book.

As a professor she wasn't the worst. Although the workload was very heavy it was manageable and she taught it well. However, she repeatedly would mix up the black students in class with one another and dismiss it as if it was nothing. Showed no regard towards that issue, as a teacher you should try and remember students name.
She got frustrated quick with my class but the class is easy if you keep up and participate. And do accept late work but will have points off.

Learning the Arabic alphabet is no joke whoever you take it with, doubly so if you're cramming a 4-credit course into 4 weeks. Take this demanding skill seriously, really invest in the homework and SPEAK in the professor's lectures, and you can land an A [if by a hairsbreadth]. She really makes entry into the language possible, very encouraging.

reviews.comment: Participation matters. You have to talk to get credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Though there were times Prof Didich came across as rude, what shes truly doing is shaping you into someone who will be able to learn a new language. Accept the amazing criticisms and feedback and don't fret if she laughs a little. Learning a new language can be a little silly. I credit her foundation building skills for getting me through in one go
This class does not seem like an intro class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class is taught so backwards. You have to learn the material before class then fully know it by class. You get called on a billion times a class. There were so many vhl assignments. Tests and quizzes aren't to bad. The professor is overall nice but does not like repeating herself and gets irritated if you dont know something.
Had her for Fren101, very easy A as long as you go to class and participate. Make sure to practice and write down her examples. She does not like to repeat herself so be attentive.

reviews.comment: She's terrible. By far one of the worst professors I've had. She teaches backwards in the sense that she expects you to read the text book first and show your mastery of the subject in the class where it should be the opposite. She is also incredibly rude, Ive learned nothing thus far.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Shes not nice. She isn't helpful either. Expects you to know everything about the language and doesn't give proper feed back. She has anger issues and can be extremely rude at times. Also she gives A LOT of work. So forget about all your other classes when taking her. She thinks this is everyones major.

Absolutely love Amina. Took her for ARBC 102, 201. A complete sweetheart and she genuinely wants you to learn the language. She doesn't take crap though and doesn't like it when you're distracted during class. She's helpful and hospitable but firm. Make sure you do all your work and pay attention to due dates and emails!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I absolutely love Amina. Shes everything youd ever want in a professor. Kindhearted, caring and genuinely wants you to succeed. She loves her students and will do whatever she can to make the language easier for you to learn. Just dont use your phone in class haha! Highly recommend. If you have her as an option dont hesitate. SHES AMAZING
Amina Didich is such a great professor! She really cares about her students, and is really helpful. She is funny, and loves her students. Definitely would recommend taking a class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Solid Arabic professor for 101 overall, and even plan to take her again for 102. learning the language itself is about as hard as I expect, but her tests and homework assignments are very simple and a lot of the content is gone over multiple times in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I'm in awe of this woman. She is so loving and kind. As boring a a french class can be, she made it fun and interesting. Everyone loved her and basically didn't want the class to end! she's one of a kind! her grading system is easy and she goes through everything before quizzes or exams.

Prof B is extremely approachable outside of class and does his best to answer questions in as much detail as possible. He drew examples of ADTs whenever possible which I found very helpful. Exams and projects were straight to the point and not too bad as long as you pay attention during class. Probably one of the best CS profs at this school!

Simply not a good professor for this course.  Either late to every lecture, or flat out cancels it.  Does not explain concepts all that well, his exams are poorly written, is not in control of the projects, and is overall very disorganized.  It is still possible to do well in this class, but your best bet is to teach yourself the content.

awful paced class. too much time was spent on specificalities so we were unprepared for projects. wasn't in touch with the main professor so couldn't answer questions about the projects beyond general info. was tardy to every class. exam questions had ridiculous point weighting and since he didn't proctor exams he couldn't answer exam questions.

He was friendly and explained the concepts, but he was wishy-washy. He often canceled class or switched the meeting format with same-day warning. He tried to punish the whole class because some students weren't there. He wasn't familiar enough with the projects to be helpful with them. He covered only ~75% of the material we should have learned.

He cares about his students and goes above to present material to help make you understand. This is a hard class, you need to do outside research on your own to have a deeper understanding of these concepts that will repeat again. Attend office hours, he will explain concepts in detail.he is not in charge of projects so cant blame him.

He is a kind professor who can be flexible with due dates if you plan in advance and communicate. But he tried to cancel half of the classes for the semester. Spent 30 minutes on project structures (SPLAY), but 3 days on miscellaneous things. Doesn't know about projects at all. Does not plan for class. I did not learn a single thing this semester.

I am sorry but the reviewer  that said he a good professor is living in a delusion . he is awful , he tries to cut corners and only "teach" us stuff just for exams and reads from the slides instead of giving us practical problems and break it down step by step. he just talks and acts like a TA or tutor instead of a professor. I learn all myself.

I have never had a worse professor. I did very well with the concepts and had no major problems with the projects, but I still struggled on the exams. The second exam, no one finished and he would not take feedback on the length of the exams, instead arguing with us the next class about why we should have been able to finish. DO NOT TAKE PROFESSOR.

I took CMSC 341 over the summer with Prof B. The class was hectic, due to being a 15 week course crammed into an 8 week course.

Prof B was very approachable and personable on discord, which served as a main means of communication. Seemed to be a fair grader, and was open to criticism about poor wording on assignments, often issuing corrections.

All the bad reviews are probably people that either did not understand the class or expected the professor to handhold them through the semester. Very chill professor and is understanding to situations and is very lenient with some due dates. 341 is a tough class and he made the experience easier compared to what I heard from other friends.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly one of the best professors. All the bad grades are from the class being hard, it is very hard but this professor makes it so much easier than it needs to be with how lenient he is. He is also very quick at responding on discord. I would take again!

Everything from the tests was from or derived from the slides. The projects were common for all sections, and they gave 2 weeks per project for a reason. It wasn't particularly hard. People who didn't get a B or higher didn't manage their time on projects or didn't pay attention / attend class.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Do NOT take this professor. The class itself is challenging, but he made it 10x harder because he is so disorganized. Never responds to email, only communicates on discord. Takes FOREVER to post exam scores. Didn't know barely any of our grades going into the final. Had to curve a bunch just for people to pass. Would recommend anyone but him.

Middle of the road lecture wise, answers project questions during class. His lectures are fine, nothing special. Homework is participation and he gives a 3% "attendance" grade to mainly just boosts your final grade. Exams are a mixed bag, but he will curve them if everybody does terrible. Do well on the projects and study regularly and its EZ.

I would not take this professor. Take ANY other professor. Grading is very unclear and he is impossible to get ahold of. The class itself is not a 5/5 difficulty but dealing with this professor is. All email correspondence was bordering on aggressive or rude. Take anyone else but not him. 5/5 do NOT recommend

Unorganized professor, had to teach myself or go to the TA's for help. Attendance was mandatory but it was pointless going in person. Grades weren't put in until very late so I had no idea what my grade would be which was very misleading. Also, we randomly switched to online lessons which was how it should've been from the start. Disappointing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture pptx are not made by him, they are made by Donyaee (same as projects). Lectures are worthless, better off self-learning. Exams are hard, there are 2 of them and a final. Nobody finished the second exam, and even though he is NOW potentially doing a curve, it does not excuse an impossible exam. He is nice on occassion, but that is about it.

Professor resists student feedback and seems uninterested in improving. Lectures are unengaging, relying heavily on reading slides. Whiteboard explanations are often confusing and disorganized. I was disappointed, as I initially had high hopes for this class.

This is above all a mandatory class for computer science majors and every option is difficult.
Know going into it that lectures are mandatory, but not his. If you take his class you can still do Dixon's lectures. That is really the only role that the professor has. Because it's the TA's who do the real work, the instructor matters little.

Rambles a lot and live coding in class was rare but it was his first semester teaching. He does care about students and would spend lots of time clarifying project/exam questions and had exam prep outside of class. He's a former student and provides useful info for future classes and topics. Ok for 201 but would not take for more advanced classes.

I didn't learn much from him and most of my studying came from past knowledge and working with TAs. His lectures are essentially useless, he rambles way too much, and wastes half the lecture going over the project? However, you're not out of luck if you get stuck with him; you can always attend another professor's lecture.

His lectures are rambly. He doesn't grade anything in a decent amount of time. Two TAs and he just graded everything on the deadline Jan 2th. Rushed assignments and projects last minute. Assigned a project after the final exam and made it due right before Christmas. Really passive-aggressive and condescending to students asking questions.

Adjunk professor. Seriously the most unprofessional "teacher" at this school. Somehow takes him two months to grade a simple assignment when he has 2 TA's, constantly cancels classes and wont go over material, and attempted to teach python after the final exam because he procrastinated doing his 1 job. Don't take this class with him ever.

To be honest, for this class office hours matter more than anything since all professors used the same course material. I will say though he is really chill for a professor and you can come up to him after class about pretty much anything related to the course. He was late for a couple of lectures but outside of that, he was pretty solid.

Lectures were disorganized rambling, instructions were unclear, grading took forever with little or no productive feedback. Totally unreliable with schedule. Despised communication. Wouldn't provide material online or helpful resources. Barely learned anything for three months then went at 2x speed for the actual topics promised. Worst Ive ever had
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's a good professor. Seems very caring and understanding, but such a tough grader on discussion posts. Definitely not an "easy" class, but it's bearable. Graded by participation, weekly discussion posts & reflections, with a fun midterm and final! Midterm was creating your own medieval story, final was cooking a recipe from Middle Ages!

This was my second class with Froide and I loved it.  The readings she chose were really interesting and Froide always leads amazing lectures.  The coursework was minimal.  We didn't have any tests or massively difficult assignments.  Our final was baking something based on historic recipes!  10/10, would take again.

Amazing class and an amazing professor! If you're interested in European history you'll have a good time in her class. Lectures are engaging and she comes up with very fun assignments. She was also very kind to students and was accessible outside of class. If you're a history major or just looking for something fun I would recommend this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Tudor/Stuart history was a great class. Prof. Froide is really passionate about the subject and knows a lot. She also made it easy to understand and joked around a lot. Lectures are pretty vital to understanding the subject, so make sure you don't sleep on them. Also, get ready to read, write, and do thorough analysis of assigned readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: passionate about the subject and very knowledgeable. open to conversation with students within lectures. not too much reading for a 400-level. tough but fair grader - really expects a lot from papers and test responses (blue books!). we had a feast day at the end of the semester for extra credit. kind, cares about students. clear syllabus/policies.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is a decent Professor and knows the subject. However, she is a tough grader and the class was boring to be honest. She also has political leanings that can get frustrating.  Attendance is mandatory and your grade will reflect. If your're going to to be out of town she needs written proof in advance. I've had better at UMBC.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The course was meh, but Prof. Froide is a good professor.   Three papers and two assignments.  Attendance is "mandatory"-it won't ding your grade too bad for missing more than the 2 "allowed" absences.  The grading is fairly tough for a 200-level course.  Lots of reading, but that's to be expected for a history course.

As a person, Froide is very friendly and helpful. But she is a tough grader. Her two TA's are EXTREMELY tough. There were 2 tests and 3 papers. The papers were difficult to write because the content was tedious and boring.

Prof. Froide could make Mortuary Science seem like a fun subject. Her lectures are upbeat and energetic. She doesn't read verbatim off the PowerPoint or constantly stop to consult her notes.  Despite having almost 100 students, we frequently had class discussions which really made you think. Froide has been my favorite professor at UMBC.
Professor froide is great, but she is a tough grader. You will read 4-5 books since its a history class, but only the chapter that is assigned to you by your last name. No test and one final project.
Professor Froide is one of the best in the History department! She's so helpful and nice and lets you know just what she's looking for on papers and tests. I'd take another class with her for sure.

This teacher was amazing. She provided many resources that you could use during your research. She is very approachable and will help you with anything and everything. She really wants you to be successful. Also, you can write about any topic as long as you can link it to 18th century London. This class was amazing. Definitely take her!

She is one of the best professors in the department. As long as you come to class, take notes, and read you'll do fine. If you do what is listen above you will have no problem getting an A. She is very helpful and entertaining. She is also the nicest person in the department.

Class could be interesting, but it could also be supremely boring and sometimes droned on forever. Although it was a topic I was interested in, she just couldn't seem to grab my attention. The books were very boring and she didn't like my writing style. In general, a good prof, knows her stuff, but not good for a non hist major who needs electives

I'm not a history major and I was real intimidated by the amount of books we were required for this class, but I really enjoyed it. You write a short paper for each book, discuss them in class, and have two longer papers to write on subjects you choose. Participation and attendance count for 25% of your grade, but it's easy if you try. Great prof!

Dr. Froide is AMAZING! Her lectures are like one-on-one conversations! She makes complicated British history seem accessible and understandable. I don't know how she does it, but I get it now! Attendance is optional, but go to EVERY class & you won't regret it! The books and research are interesting too! Uses visuals,discussions and group work.

She is a great teacher! She is very helpful!! This class is quite reading and writing intensive, but is still fun. One of the two research papers is about crime in 18th Century London, and the research you conduct about these criminals is so interesting and enlivens the past!

You don't learn too much general European women's history.  Instead you read books on specific topics.  2 papers and "discussion questions" on the books & no exams.  The class is based around the books & discussing them.  You should probably take a class before this to put everything into context.  There is no real lecture.  The course is lacking.

SHe is a good teacher. She assigned two papers and discussion questions which made up the majority of your grade. She also assigned points for attending class. She made helpful comments on your paper to let you know what you had done wrong. Only bad part was you were graded on your classroom participation so expect to talk alot

HIST 497 this semester was on 18th century London. The class involved researching any aspect of London's history with 18th century English newspapers.  Dr. Froide was truly helpfull in recommending books, answering questions, and commenting on the rough draft for improvements. Overall, an amazing professor!!

Best teacher of the Western Civ teachers.  Classes are lecture based.  Fun, smart, and effective.  3 non-cumulative tests are essay based which turned out to be a great way to be tested on the material.  There's 2 short papers on museum trips, which are easy.  Great teacher, I recommend taking her.

Dr. Froide made learning about European Women's history a fun and enlightening experience. She assigned interesting readings and the class discussions were never dull. This course had 3 male students and 20 female students... as a male student I can say the class was a positive experience and would recommend it to anyone.

Excellent professor! She is really knowledgeable about early modern England. Also, Froide assigns interesting readings about topics like witches and Britain's path to becoming a world power. A fair grader and writes a lot of comments on papers to show what was done well or not so well.

Professor Anushka Aqil's class is a very easy and light course to take. There was only one homework assignment and the exams were online. The presentations are the "big" assignment but the instructions were very clear and it is hard to not do well on them. Overall this was a great class!

The class material was easy and interesting, but Prof. Anuska often came off as awkward and snarky when students participated, which discouraged engagement. Her questions before each class began were loaded and random. Her Blackboard setup is very disorganized, especially the project sector. There's only one paper but it's not even worth much (5%).

I love the course and everything MINUS the prof and group projects no one would even try to do something unless forced, plz grow up. Her attitude the heck she always has to one-up someone and it's annoying, was very passive-aggressive.Whenever we did presentations/group work, it was very chaotic and messy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: She's very nice and understanding! I took 202 with her. Most work is online, but you do student cases in class, usually in groups. Each case is done differently—some are presentations, some are done individually. She's helpful, but you do have to teach yourself a lot. Overall, it's manageable if you stay on top of things.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Shes great, such an easy teacher, we only did 6 case studies with 3 exams and that was it and they were very easy. you should definitely take her! Attendance is only needed when ur doing a case study, but exams were take home.

Really loved 380 with her, it was pretty easy and the class was actually interesting. Especially after having to deal with all the bad HAPP professors (andrea), I defiantly wouldn't take her for granted. She is a harsh grader when it comes to writing, but it helped me improve my writing for the other upper levels so its better I heard it from her.

She was a bad professor. Extremely opinionated and if you had a differing view on something then you were wrong no mater what. Very condescending and will not take you seriously. Never take her class and avoid this professor at all costs.
She is very opinionated and her "lectures" are answering questions on the readings in class. Very tough professor and would never recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While the topics taught in the class are interesting, Anushka is so heavily opinionated that it makes any open discussion awkward and forced. Also, participation will make or break your grade, so despite the fact you will be belittled by her for anything you say, you have to do it anyway even though you will feel like an idiot for trying.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
She somehow expected three original thoughts per student in a 20 person class that met for 75 minutes every week. Agree with the other person, her tone was extremely condescending which makes people nervous to participate. If your answer wasn't perfect you wouldn't get a participation point.

Takes FOREVER to grade as well. Would avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: her style of teaching was just very lazy to me. discussion oriented class but she makes it hard to participate because her tone is very condescending. she does not assign any assignments, you are only graded from discussions, 2 group projects, midterm and final which makes it hard to improve your grade if need be. she is a very slow grader as well.

While she is incredibly nice, she is a very harsh grader. Better to overcite everything because she will knock you 10% for having one sentence uncited. Theres a group Policy brief which sucks if you have a bad group because it's a lot of work especially the second part. The tests are not too bad. Quizzes don't count as a grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is a good prof. I don't like the fact that she doesn't grade the assignment on time which can be frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Qualitative Cross-Cultural Research. ** If you wish to learn qualitative research processes, then Mrs. Acquavita is a fabulous professor. She has pretty high expectations of her students but is available for assistance along the way, like no other Professor I have had at UMB. If you dread group projects, this is not the class for you.
She seems like a nice person, but is a very unpredictable grader. On the plus side, I will say that I did learn a lot about the history of social work in her class.

Not the most interesting class, but once you get used to her teaching style, you learn a lot. She tries to keep class interesting by utilizing different learning techniques. Is a tough grader, but if you follow the rubrics, you'll do fine. Also, she gives phenomenal reviews for the exam, so if you study what she gives you, you'll pass.
Just don't do it.
No Comments

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!! She is a PhD Candidate and feels like she has something to prove and so she grades ridiculously. She was so boring and I learned NOTHING. She assigned so many projects: 4 papers (one 25 pager) and some other "homework assignments." It was ridiculous. If you value your money spent in graduate school--don't take her.

This was my second course with her, and I love her so much. She really cares about her students and wants them to understand what they are learning. Her lectures were easy to understand and follow along with, and they were always enhanced with humor. She's definitely one of my favorite professors I've had here.

Amazing class and professor. This is a late review, as I had her Winter 21, this was also my first class at UMBC as a transfer after getting my AA. I could not have asked for a better introduction into the university. The material was thought provoking and promoted self awareness. I recommend this course and this professor to everyone.
Professor Arevalo was so kind and understanding to everyone this semester, the class was easy and the material was interesting.
Best Professor Ive ever met at UMBC so far. She is extremely helpful and patient. As long as you go to class every day youll pass. (Also gives out loads of extra credit)

You will learn everything about Spain and it's history and culture from the way beginning of time. Her study guides are helpful for the exams. Make sure you pay attention to everything you read. You will have projects, blogs, and an essay. Homework's are related to the readings you do. Attendance is a must you will miss a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Arevalo-Guerrero was at all times caring and very supportive. SPAN 307 is an intense course because it is about Spain's history but it is definitely an interesting course.

Definitely a good professor, she is very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject matter, especially SPAN 307 as she is a Spaniard! She does give a lot of written work, but she is a fair grader and as long as you are enthusiastic and committed to learning she will always work with you.

Senora Arevalo-Guerrero is one of the best Spanish professors I've ever had... she is extremely helpful and very flexible.. in short, she understands that you are human and that Spanish is not your first language.
She is a good professor, pretty easy on the grading, and very flexible with turning things in.

Prof. Arevalo-Guerrero is a good teacher and very nice. She's got a different style of classroom, mainly focused on discussion and increasing "Intercultural Competency". Still i find myself learnign a lot even though we don't do much grammar review. There's some writing involved. If you need more of a language learning based class she's not for you

Knows all to know about CS & Math. HWs are 15%, the 3 exams are the rest of the grade. Kinda crazy BUT the exam questions are softballs. He hints to what is on the exams. The math is unlike anything I've taken before. He answers any question and makes sure you get it. He is strict on grading, however he cares for students. YOU. MUST. STUDY. PROOFS.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You HAVE to read the textbook because he provides 0 notes and lectures will not be comprehensible at all if you haven't read it beforehand. 85% of your grade is 3 exams while the rest of it are frustrating homeworks that'll be up to 25 questions long - other teachers will only have you do like 5 questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: if u have a choice take any other professor. your grade is basically what u get on the 3 exams. the avg for my class mightve been a D and he didnt curve. lectures were poorly paced and in my opinion you fare better by learning straight from the textbook. if i could give a 0 i would, disclaimer i am a  4.0 student this guy was not good
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good lecturer. You have to work for it but you can earn it if you try hard enough.

I really liked him! Tries to connect what we learn in lectures to things that he's done in industry and give "real life" examples. His PhD is in math so he's fairly strict in terms of making sure the proofs are logical and structured the way they should be, so he's a tough grader. That being said I learned a lot. Redo HW problems to review for exam
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hard, but fair. If you work for it, you should get the grade. He knows what he's talking about and does it well. A+

He's a really good teacher, and keeps class interesting enough. If you take notes and pay attention you'll be fine. Exams can be more difficult and there is a decent amount of homework, however, he's not unreasonable.

He's a nice guy, but he grades like his life depends on it. You don't write the proof the way he wants it.. he'll deduct 10 points. There are 3 exams including the final and they're all really difficult. Half the class failed the first two exams, and I don't know if he's gonna curve the class. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HIM. TAKE IT IN SUMMER.

Honestly, he is a good teacher but he grades as if we are flawless humans who cannot possibly make error in life. Will possibly end up gives you a two letter grade curve. Doesn't really care too much about the class.

Although Professor Horta is a lenient grader, his lectures are a nightmare. He wastes your time rambling and giving advanced examples without much explanation. His expectations are incredibly unclear, and each exam is worth 25% of your grade which makes the lack of clarity even more stressful. To succeed with him, you need to be your own teacher.
Class wasn't too difficult, but this was my second time taking it. Not recommended for first time students. Takes a long time to return tests, doesn't have office hours or use Blackboard.
Very annoying. Lectures are boring, incomprehensible, and tests are hard. Don't take.
Boring, unhelpful, and hard. Lectures are very boring, did not learn anything, and tests are very confusing. AVOID.
301 is a hard class. But if you must take it, take it with Arnie. Very good professor and is always willing to help out. Presents the material clearly and makes it clear what you need to know.
Very intelligent and helpful.  It all comes down to your effort.

You have got to be kidding. I walked into the final with a B average and after studying for 2 weeks, I still failed the final which was so hard that 2 people actually got up and left once they saw it.  Not a bad teacher but his final submarined 5 people that I knew in the class including myself. I ended with a D and never retook it.
The best! Best! Best! professor I ever had!  He made  linear algebra really easy and fun!  Instead of hating the homeworks I really enjoy doing them!  A really great professor.  Everyone loves him^_^

Dr. Elisabeth genuinely care about her students. She encourage us to learn from one another and to build bridges that will help us have better communication and to learn problem solving skills that will impact not only our careers but also our personal lives. Easy grading. Course is well organize and she is easy to reach and helpful.

She's very willing to help students, and passionate about what she teaches. She interacts with the class and encourages us to interact with each other. She explains confusing concepts without translating, so we understand the ideas in the context of the language, encouraging us to think in Spanish rather than constantly translating everything.

Fun, engaging, thought-provoking... a great class and teacher! I took the class online in Summer 2024, and she was fast in responding and giving feedback. I learned a lot about the topic, myself and my culture. She is understanding with students and really wants you to succeed. I highly recommend taking the class with her.

Love her! So sweet, incredibly knowledgeable, very fun to be around and always willing to learn. One of my favorite classes I've taken thus far: thought-provoking, useful, and taught super well. It can be a lot (multiple assignments a week) but all very interesting and a great opportunity to learn from other people.
While Dra. Arevalo is very knowledgable, I could hardly understand anything she said. She is hard to understand-- even in English.  She makes her lectures entertaining but the class itself is boring.

Dr. Guerrero is a wonderful professor and the class is fun. You have discussion board posts and blog entries once a week, a presentation where you present something from your culture, and 2 exams that aren't hard. At the end of the semester there is a multi cultural potluck that is lots of fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: The professor did make us read many chapters for the Espana y Sus Culturas class, however, I learned so much! She only has two exams and a paper. She gives study guides for each exam which help whilst studying. A true understanding of the material is needed and in lecture, she clears is up. Lectures seem long and boring if you don't do the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Although she is very friendly in person, I found this class to be very disorganized. I went to her office hours many times during the semester for feedback on my essays and made the changes but she still took points off of random things. Didn't do anything in class besides talk about irrelevant and random things; doesn't teach spanish. bad prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: very reasonable workload and grading system. participation and attendance are important

I am taking her class right now and I love it. She is so nice and helpful and I LOVE that she is from Spain so you can learn the correct way to use vosotros. A lot of other professors don't know it or refuse to teach it. I highly recommend.

He's blatantly biased towards certain students. In fact, it's known by many that one student got an exam grade in the 60's on the 1st midterm and online he changed to the 70's. He gives up on ALL the students just because they don't get the grades he expects on exams. He needs to take responsibility for this! Awful professor!!

Exams make up 90% of the final grade so if you mess up on just one of the midterms there's a lot of catching up to do. The grading on the exams have an unclear criteria/rubric and it is very easy to lose points if you don't write exactly what he wants to see. Lectures made the content more confusing than just reading the textbook.

He's constantly making fun of students and blocks the board so students cannot see what he is writing. If you go to ask questions he really doesn't want to help as he thinks he covered it well enough in class. He will laugh at the students and say "it's easy". Unfortunately, you can't take it with anyone else as he's the only choice.

Being a biochemistry major and taking the chem required PCHEM was scary enough, mainly because I had not done calculus is 3 years as well as how hard I heard this class to be. Dr.Arnold however made the subject very approachable and made it easier to understand. He can be a bit passive aggressive but, is a very great professor. GO TO PCHEM CLUB!!

Prof Arnold is not a mean prof (though I wouldn't call him nice). He is however precieved as mean to many students. The course was hard to learn from to the point that going to lecture left people more confused than staying and listening. When 50% of the class is failing exams he points out the one student who got an 98. An anomaly not the standard

Dr. Arnold is a rockstar lecturer, but a bit old school. His lectures are very engaging, if fast-paced, and he takes a lot of time to go through the more complex parts of pchem in "gorey detail," but he also often glosses over whole branches of mathematics that he assumes we're all familar with, but aren't prerequisites (diff eq, lin alg).

Excellent teaching style, but he doesn't stick to the order of the textbook. Write down every example in class - he probably just gave you some great hints for the homework. For more help, go to PChem club. Again, he will help you solve the homework, clarify material, and prepare you for the exams in the most efficient way possible: problem solving

Go to class, go to P. Chem club, and hold on for the wild ride. Dr. Arnold is THE best professor that I've had, and he makes P-chem tolerable. He's helpful and always has answers when you approach him with intelligent questions regarding HW and concepts. You get out what you put into this course.  "P-chem isn't difficult, it's just complicated."

Attend Class, Take notes, Do Homework, Check keys to HW posted, Finals  has atleast 3 HW q's. Doesn't exactly follow the textbook but insists on reading. 4 q's on mid-term exams. Gives an eqn sheet for exam, so no need to memorize the formulae. Overall, one of the best professors in the Uni and trust me I've encountered a lot in the past 3-4 years

Great Professor. very helpful. really cares about student learning. P-chem is a very difficult class. Homework is extremely challenging and time consuming. Exams are almost as difficult. He sets up a "PChem club" each semester. highly recommend participating  or forming your own study group. Course material is almost impossible to grasp without it
extremely good, wish I had professors like him in every class. A tough topic like Pchem is made very interesting and most importantly I've never felt bored during his lecture

Good teacher. Hard subject so it wouldn't matter who teaches it. He tends to make tests questions from homeworks which he doesn't grade at all. He is a fair grader. Tests are 4 questions and generally reflect whatever he has taught. Good teacher.

His class is definitely not easy, but he's straight forward in what he expects of you and students have ample opportunity to learn the material. He is a good lecturer and eager to help students outside of class.
