The sweetest and best professor I've ever had in my three years of college. She's clearly very passionate about her job and she tries to relate to students. She's very understanding and flexible with due dates and I wish I could take all my HAPP courses with her. She deserves a raise. The type of professor they all should aspire to be.

Honestly is one of my favorite professors on campus, she is the reason I decided to switch to a HAPP major. Just do your study guide and youll pass her exam everytime, her final is a retake of one of your exams ( i had her pre covid though)
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This was the worst class that I have ever taken if your are not planning on going into the health field don't take this it is way too much to work for an elective all these people that give a good rating to this class are try hards who trying to get into the health field do not take this as an elective you will fail.

A lot of professors at UMBC won't budge their grading policies, even in the wake of a pandemic that's forced us to drastically change the way we live and learn. But Katie really understands and cares. Deadlines were not strictly enforced at all and she was always willing to give feedback if you needed it. I'd definitely take her again if I could.

Katie is the best HAPP prof at UMBC. She really cares about our success and comfort. HAPP100 content is easy, but sometimes questions on exams. can be tricky. HAPP340 has no textbook, and assignments are super easy. I had both these during corona, and she was so understanding, never gave us strict due dates, and sometimes extended exam time. BEST!!

honestly my favorite HAPP teacher so far. Class is extremely easy, the reading quizzes dont count as a grade , the writing you unlock from getting a 80% or higher on the reading quizzes is what counts for a grade. unit test is amazingly easy, final is choose one of the 3 to retake. boring lecture but extremely easy, take notes in class, very nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is the best HAPP professor at UMBC. She assigns fair and helpful work. Her lectures are engaging and you actually learn. I took HAPP 300 and 411 with her, loved her both times!

Professor Birger is one of THE best HAPP professors at UMBC. I wish she taught all of the HAPP courses because then I would actually learn. In all of her classes her lecture slides are information heavy and are very helpful for her exams without necessarily having to read the book. She gives amazing information on not just her class but life.

She's super chill. She definitely talks a lot during her lecture, but she posts them online so if you couldn't keep up in class you can still work at your own pace. She lets people redo assignments if you didn't like the grade you received.

Literally this is the best professor to take this class with. I showed up to class for the first month before I realized that a literal high school drop out who knows that the mitochondria is the powerhouse of the cell can pass this class.

Professor Birger teaches one of the harder classes that HAPP majors have to take and she makes the info heavy class easier to understand. The content is still a bit difficult but she is very easy to talk to whenever you have an issue. Would deff recommend her to anyone since she is one of the more down to earth profs I've had at this school.

Professor Birger is one of my favorite professors in the HAPP department. Although the assigned book for this class was hard to follow, Birger make it so easy to understand. Her lectures are clear and she keeps you engaged. Two exams; Mid-Term and Final, 1 group debate, a couple reading responses, and quizzes each week. I recommend taking her!

She's a pretty good professor. She seems interested in her subject and her students. However, the attendance is nowhere near mandatory. All assignments (tests included) are online. She posts her slides, and it's really easy to complete your assignments using only the slides she posts. I'd recommend taking HAPP 200 with her, it was pretty good.
She is such a great professor, she makes lectures interesting and fun, one of my favorite classes. Quite a bit of writing but just keep track of what is due and she grades fairly. Take her class!!!

I truly enjoyed this class. Mrs. Birger is professional, peppy, courteous and a great teacher. She somehow manages to make the mundane, boring topic of health regulation interesting. I enjoy her lectures and actually learn about the material. Exams are easy if you pay attention in class and take good notes.

Not sure why others say it's hard, but I got 100% on both the midterm and the final and ended with a 99% in the class. It's ridiculously easy if you show up to class and read over the slides once or twice.  Her exams are a joke, as long as you went to class you can easily get 100%. You don't even need to read the book.
She's the best HAPP professor!

Her lectures were always interesting and I picked up a lot of valuable knowledge. Her class is different from other HAPP classes as it does not reiterate the exact same points. You will definitely pick up new information from this class. She is also not an A producing factory. She is tough but fair. If you study, you will do well in the class.

Professor Birger is one of those rare  and enthusiastic professors who is extraordinarily passionate about teaching. It is always apparent from the powerpoint discussions that she is highly knowledgeable about health policy and health care in general.   she is also very attractive!

Had him this past fall for 115 at Towson, class wasn't too difficult as long as you pay attention. The tests and exams aren't difficult as long as you do the homework and do the study guides posted. Allowed a note card for every exam and did a great job of teaching the material in the class. Even cracked a joke or two during most classes.

Although he was sometimes disorganized, I think he was an overall good professor. I had a lot of fun in his class and I found him very funny. Just make sure to do the homework and study for the tests! He was also a very quick grader. His class was very welcoming, and everyone would participate and work together. I would take him again!

Had him for Math 106. He has a rlly hard accent & rlly hard to know what he's saying most of the time. He was alright with teaching math but sometimes idk how I understood what he was saying. theres a lot of hw on a website we did i forgot but omg it was annoying. you basically have teach urself in this class, so beaware its not fun. idk how i pass

He's a pretty chill professor, and allows a note card on exams with anything on them. His lectures are always on time and organized. He posts the lecture notes after class. Overall pretty good math professor.

I don't think I have ever experienced a professor like him... He could be very scatter-brained, indecisive and his lectures were very messy. I want to be fair to him seeing as he is a new professor and I am hopeful that he is knowledgable in his profession; I could not understand him at all, the whole class would have to correct him often.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Her lecture explanations were poor & not engaging. When doing in class activities, she wouldn't give much time to digest and solve them. She deliberately made attendance a grade because she noticed low engagement(which I find petty). You get multiple attempts on homework & 3 online exams. Overall, her class is manageable but not an easy A.

Good, but a little overrated. She's a standout in the lecture department and is very good at teaching, but when it comes to grade transparency and assignment breadth, there's a lot to be desired. It's impossible to see how your final grade was calculated, and exams take up, if I'm not mistaken, 75% of the grade.
Reads a lot from the textbook so I personally didn't get much from the lectures, found myself needing to teach myself a lot of the content, but overall, she is a nice professor

Exams take up most of your grade. She was very nice, but I could not learn in her lecture. She was not very clear in her explanations and gave little time to complete in class work. Homework was weekly, but again has litte impact on your overall grade. It did not prepare me to move forward. All exams done online at home. Doesnt enter grades at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Homework only once a week, she truly does care about teaching and makes lectures interactive ,exams were take home. My favorite professor right now. Is also very understanding
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is so lovely and nice, just pay attention to her lectures and ask questions, participation matters, I am thinking of picking up an economics minor because of her

Really nice professor for the classes I did attend. As others have pointed out, it's a 101 course, and attendance is optional. Really just do the online homework and exams, and you're golden. She does offer help and is super approachable. I'm sure the experience is tougher for the higher level course, but it was really chilled for the 101 class.

nice lady, boring lectures, skipped a lot of the classes because you could do everything online. there was one or two classes i had to show up to for attendance/participation credit. calm class just disengaging
Easiest A of my life, i took it as a filler class and set aside on average 15 minutes max per week to get HW/exams done. Don't bother going to class, its too easy to waste your time like that.
attendance isnt mandatory; her class is so easy its just homework with 3 exams and ur done.

Took the class online and it was pretty easy. Had to learn a lot of material in a short amount of time but it is definitely doable. Everything was online and the only interaction we had was the reminder emails she would send about the 2 exams we took. Super easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
3 online exams with no lockdown browser each 27% (no final), 1 in class activity 3%, 10 homeworks 16% (drops lowest 2).

Exams are exactly like homeworks, sometimes there were even the same questions. In class activity was 1 front and back WS on 2 units. LOTS of textbook reading but her classes are lowkey word for word from the textbook.

Her lectures are verbatim what is in the textbook. I wasn't aware how this class was run so that's on me but the online model is not very aligned with her lectures. Granted if you're willing to do loads of practise on the website itself she's great. 3 heavily weighted exams rlly drag you down if you do badly on one. She's not bad not great.

Lecture was good, she talks A LOT. Also in a huge room she writing on the whiteboard. By the end of the lecture the board was randomly covered in the tiniest writing and graphs that I am pretty sure no one could actually read. The class only had 3 grades, exams, homework, and a single in class activity. Online exams, no quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Bing Ma is incredibly sweet and as an introductory microeconomics class, the material in and of itself is not difficult. HOWEVER: if you're used to getting good grades without really studying or waiting until the last minute to study, get over that behavior quickly! 84% of your grade is comprised of exams, so don't wing it if you want an A!

Prof Ma is great professor. Class was not mandatory I showed up for 2 lectures since I was retaking the course. There was one class a week on Tuesdays, 10 hws online, and 3 exams online no final. Prof Ma was definitely a better professor then my other one highly recommend for econ 101.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was very sweet, and very passionate which made lectures easy to follow. Gave a bunch of examples, and all the homework, quizzes, and exams were online. When asked a question, she'd answer very clearly. Definitely would take her again for another econ course.

Easy A. We had class once a week and attendance was optional. Exams were online, no FINAL. Homeworks were so easy and almost everything was online. If you're looking for an easy A gen ed, take this class.

Took her for ECON 101. Attending lectures will benefit you greatly. Understanding her is a bit hard because she doesn't speak as loud even with a mic on but will answer questions when asked. One BIG problem is she does not give any exceptions, even if there is a system error or you're sick which caused me to get a B

The class was easy. Do the weekly hw (multiple attempts) and then three exams. Redoing the hw will help you prepare for the exams. Didn't go to class after the 2nd week, the lecture room was on the exact opposite side of campus and I wasn't about to walk that much in the morning. I still passed with a B. Easy 100% on hw and low B average for exams.

Professor Ma is a highly engaging professor. Lectures are based on the textbook and clarify the concepts wonderfully. Weekly homework assignments are useful as they allow infinite attempts, which helps with understanding. 3 exams with no final. Exams are fair, consisting of multiple choice and graphing problems. Wonderful intro micro course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Bing Ma is an easy A. All exams are online. Attendance is not mandatory. I would recommend her.

Professor Bing Ma is an alright  Professor, it seems like she only read off the slides and didn't really teach. I didn't really learn anything due to that. Some of her explanations weren't clear in my view, they were a bit hard to understand. Exams are extremely weighted.
The only interaction with the professor was emails from her. The course was online, everything was online, literally everything. Easiest A ever.

Took her online and easy A! She gives 3 exams and weekly homework. She provides you with all the notes and powerpoints for each chapter. Only downside to her is that she doesn't post grades on blackboard so you pretty much have to keep track of your grades on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Great professor to take if u want an easy A in economics. Just do the homework and make sure you know the terms for the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great prof. COVID season was especially easy. Lectures were clear. Take this class if you want the credit.

Professor Ma decided last minute to teach this course asynchronously despite it being an in-person class. Lectures were unnecessary and I self taught the class. The exams were heavily weighted for your grade. Online program can be hard to graph on which can affect your grade but, you can keep retaking it until you get them right but this takes time

Really easy class with this professor, especially asynch/online. She posts lectures and TA notes, which explained the material well. She also gives exam study guides/reviews before tests. Homework (unlimited attempts were a plus) and the tests were all on Pearson, which were fairly easy and short to complete. I would 100% take ECON 101 with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: no lectures with this asynch course. weekly hws were due and had 3 exams every couple chapters. this class was very easy online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 10 total homeworks (almost 1 weekly + one dropped), and 3 *heavily-weighted* exams. asynchronous + prerecorded lectures. the hws are fairly easy but the exams are tough. it felt like the class was computer generated. do the practice problems outside of the hw, and take notes. this isn't a passive class, so do as much practice as you possibly can.

for online classes it was not synchronized classes and it was an easy A if you read the textbook. However, if youre looking for an engaging econ class that will challenge you, this is not the class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Pretty easy class. A 89 is an A. Entire grade is 3 exams and a few practice problems a week. Easy GEP, take her
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was taught asynchronously and was pretty easy. I recommend reading the text in addition to watching her lecture videos, because the tests ask questions that require understanding, not just memorization. Also use myeconlab's practice quizzes to study (ones with green background) because a lot of the questions there, show up on the tests!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: During COVID, this prof was asynchronous. All exams and homework were online thru MyEconLab and pretty simple. Lectures were just her reading from slides, you won't really need the textbook.

Econ 101 during COVID: This class is the definition of easy. If you need an easy online class here it is. All homework and exam questions are online. The exam was given through Pearson with no webcam or respondus lockdown browser. Not good for people who want to learn the material but great for people who want an A

Prof. Bing Ma's tests are fairly easy. However, if you actually want to learn from a lecture, do not take her class. All she does is reading off of her PowerPoint and using her old examples over and over. So, if you are not an independent learner and want a fun class, you should avoid this class. Also, she is not often available to her students.
Super easy class. Online, but the professor always sends out emails before the exams on exactly what needs to be covered. Not an overwhelming amount of work either.

Professor Ma's class is incredibly straightforward. Pay attention in lecture or read the textbook (you likely won't need to do both), do the homework, lightly review, and the tests should be relatively easy. By the way, she doesn't post *any* grades on Blackboard, so make sure to keep track of your scores!

Shes good at teaching so there's no complaints. She said you should read the book but don't do that. Go to class and write down literally everything and do the practice problems she gives out. Solid experience. You def gotta work though
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her lecture is very clear. She doesnt take attendance every time, but sometimes she give students class work for attendance. There are only three exams in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very easy, unlimited hw attempts and easy topic.

Professor Ma's style of ECON 101 is perfect. Lectures on Thursdays, TA sessions that end early on Tuesdays. Weekly online questions and three big tests. Multiple choices are definitions or quick math. Free response questions are exactly like examples in class. There's plenty of time for questions and she makes it clear what content is covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Ma is a great professor! She clearly states what you will be tested on and gives review days before the exam. She also gives out study guides which consist of key words that you need to know for the exam which were also very helpful. She also does a lot of examples in class which was very helpful for the exams. Just study her lectures slides!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr Ma is one of the best professors I have ever had. Her lectures are crystal clear and she clearly explains what she will be testing you on. Day before exams are review days and she tells you exactly what to study. However, the entire grade is 3 exams, and she is a bit hard to reach outside of class. Made a very difficult class interesting.
Wonderful teacher!! One of the best I've ever had. She also talks about the difficulties that she had learning certain concepts and this has shaped the way she teaches others.

Best professor for Econ 311. Goes at a pace where you actually understand stuff. Go to her review sessions, she tells you what's on the exam basically. Go home and redo the problems you did in class (study set questions) because they will show up on the exam but just in a different format.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She's a decent professor. Good with explaining topics but horrible with going over graph examples and connecting concepts because she rushes through em, reviews aren't in-depth, no study guide samples,She'll tell you the topics and the rest is up to you. Another downside is she doesnt post grades. Keep her 1st survey, final exam get 10pt to redo.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She's a professor that actually cares about how you learn. Brings up modern topics, encourages thinking, explains the content well and on time, helps students with questions, and it's an overall easy course with simple exam questions. Only downside is that she doesn't post grades online. Regardless, I highly recommend taking her.
She is very nice and clear with explaining things but none of the grades are accessible online and our final grade was not posted until the last possible day.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Ma is a great professor. She encouraged class collaborations as well as group work to solidify each lesson. She hand back each exams in class so you will know what grade you got and why you got the grade. The effective teaching methods really helped and got me to have interest and enjoy a subject I had always felt remorse.

She doesn't post grades online which is very annoying. Showing up to her class is not mandatory. If you show up on the days of the review and keep up with the homework, you'll be fine. She reads from the slides usually.

She does not post any grades online at all, which is very frustrating if you want to know how you're doing in the class. Her lectures are also pretty useless since the notes are sparse and she just reads off the slides verbatim. But no cumulative final and you can learn all the material by doing the hw and in-class examples.
Best teacher for ECON 101. Really well taught

Her style of teaching changed my entire attitude towards her class. Her lectures are a MUST because the examinations are based on the class materials she covers in class. The class has fairly tough exams, but you'll find that the homework and extra credit can level out for a decent grade boost.

She's very patient and nice professor, but her class is tough if you don't show up every time and take notes of the lectures. Following the slides and go over the problem sets you will pass this class.

ECON311 is a tough course. However, she really taught well and she was as clear as possible while still making sure you learned all of the information. The exams, although difficult as it supposed to be for ECON 311, were always fair. Highly recommend.

If you do bad in this class, it's not her, it's you. Her lectures are crystal clear and she makes the exams as straightforward as possible. This is definitely a less theory, more math type of class but it's really easy if you put in the time to study. Best professor for 311.
One of the best teachers at UMBC. She genuinely cares about students grades and will try to clarify everything. Exams are exactly like her study questions.

Just use her lecture notes. Material is pretty easy. First two exams were just about what you would expect, but final exam had a lot of stuff not covered on her review, so be careful about that. Decent professor.

Don't buy the book. I didn't touch it. Use her lecture notes (posted online) as your notes and you'll be fine. The first 3rd of the class was review of STAT 351, the rest was intro to Econometrics. Pretty simply if you follow her lectures. She tests somewhat based on her Problem Sets, so get those down. Listen to her when she reviews  too.

Econ421 is really a statistics course and therefore tougher than most econ courses. Fortunately she waters the material down somewhat. Overall nice lady and cares for her students. Occasionally she can be moody or difficult to understand. However, she teaches using ppt slides that are pretty clear. Study them/do problems. Book is super confusing.
Three tests each 30% of grade. Last 10% is attendance and involvement. She hands over the material very well and is very organized.
Very organized and clear. Great teacher highly recommend.
Not at all theoretical. Makes us write papers instead of taking exams and goes really easy on the grading. Allowed me to correct a huge error with my final paper days after I gave it in.

Seriously hard to understand, heavy accent. But she writes a lot of what she says on the board, so its not impossible to understand. No need to buy the book. Make sure you go to the review session before the tests, she pretty much gives out the essay questions there

Also for 467. Frequent attendance=extra credit. Don't need book unless you skip class, lecture is very good. 467 way easier than 421. She is very nice and even funny once you get to know her, but it won't seem that way at first. Just answer her questions, go to class, and she will like you. Plus these habits tend to yield high grades.

Most interesting class of the semester! Very little reading, clear idea of what was going to be on tests, no papers, no homework. Easy and fun! Even though attendance isn't counted - Ma offers extra credit to students who are in class via pop quizzes.

Professor Ma is great - a very nice lady with a unique (cute) sense of humor. The class examines the U.S. Health Care system from an economic perspective. There are three exams, which I aced by taking good notes and putting in a couple hours study time. No papers, no final, no need to buy the text, interesting material... this was my kind of class!
pretty easy teacher. not as boring as others. grading is pretty hard tho. If I had a choice, I would've choosen C.Yuan(who's her husband i believe)cuz he is a easy grader...
There's not much econ in it, no real math, not tons of graphs. Go to class, write what's on the board, study. 3 tests total. You will only be tested on whats on the board. Go to class!

She is a good professor. I got a C on the first exam. I did not do any extra credit work because I got flu (there are like 2 chances to get extra credit. I missed both). However, she still did not let me submit the extra credit after deadline. I got an A on the class project and got an A on the final exam. So I ended up getting an A in the class.
Easy teacher, but hard class. She  goes over what's on the exam, but it is still hard. Have to attend lecture to do well. Dont need to buy the book. Final was HARD. Easy to get a B or a C...
Pretty easy class, just copy what she writes on the board and you'll get an easy a.

Don't let her scare you off on the first day... she gets better. She really cares and wants students to understand the material. First two tests were fairly easy; just do the study questions. Watch out for the final. It was tough worth and 50% of your grade.
Very fair professor. Grade based on 3 exams. If you go to class and pay attention during the review sessions, it's very easy to get an A in the class.

Bing Ma is a great professor. She seemed irritated the first few weeks, but since then has gotten so much better. She teaches the material so that  you can understand it. Do her practice problems and the exams will be very simple for you. Her "exam review" classes are really helpful too. Her lectures are online but def. still always go to class!

She really tries to make the class understandable.  She goes through exactly what will be on the test and they aren't tricky. If you pay attention and go to class, she's very willing to help you out.  If you don't, she'll ridicule you in class ;P

OK that person had her for one day before making that review. She has gotten better but still pretty condescending. She expects a bit much which is weird cuz she used to teach at UCLA and I thought they were dumb.

Never have I EVER taken a class like this. The exams are designed to make you second-guess what you know, the lectures fast paced, and the homework barely matches the learning objectives. Even with a final grade curve and an exam drop, people still struggle to earn a good grade—take that as a sign!!
Solid biology professor for UMBC. He's a cool guy, but you can tell he likes to hear himself talk. Pretty good at lecturing and is nice one-on-one as well.

I loved his lectures; he puts a lot of effort into what he teaches, and cracks the occasional joke. People don't give him the same effort he gives them. All his lecture slides are available on Blackboard, so reviewing and studying is easy. Overall a great class.

Passionate professor who taught hard to understand content in a pretty understandable way! I felt like he was rushing a lot of the time, but to be fair there was a lot of content in each lecture and his slides were thorough enough to go back through and read and understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures were passionless and boring unless he was lecturing about cancer. His content wasn't challenging, but there was so much in each lecture, making it hard to remember it all. His exam style was tricky; discussions and homework assignments were hard. The class is curved, so it's not hard to get a B or an A with a little more effort!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams based on lectures so make sure to study those well and probably make flashcards and prepare for discussions. I didnt touch the textbook unless it was for some difficult HW problems. Kind of condescending and tough grader. HWs were long, difficult, and unhelpful and no drops. Barely any time to answer clickers and only drops one of those.

Dr. B is knowledgeable about the material, especially the topics on cancer. His lectures dominated the final exam so make sure to study his slides. Overall clear lectures but somewhat boring, and the material he teaches is heavily memorization-based. Everything on the exams is on the slides so just memorize from those.
Okay at explaining lecture slides but the slides are really heavy. There's homework once a week and discussion is very confusing if you didn't review everything beforehand

Can drop 1 exam (including the final). Homework was difficult and not useful. One time, I mentioned to him that the homework included content we hadn't reviewed yet, and he told me to "read ahead". Felt like he does research and teaches minimally. Lectures were stale and difficult to follow at times. Not the most friendly. Overall grade is curved.

Exams are based on lectures only, not textbook. Dr. Bieberich has very concise lectures, and his slides are easy to study from. He does participation questions at the start of class, meaning if you are late a couple minutes, chances are you already missed the questions. A little condescending but overall not a bad professor. HW due once a week.

Gave a curve where 85 was an A. His exams were tricky and tough but everything from his slides. Covers a lot of info in lectures and tests on details. Explains concepts fairly well. Not lenient at all. If you don't do things according to instructions, you get penalized. I worked very hard and still got a B. Final was brutal.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bieberich is much less engaging than Dr. Eisenmann. He has more material to get through since he covers all the memorization heavy parts of genetics, but he is slow and gets behind due to taking to many questions. Take this class with him and Eisenmann and you'll be fine. His exams are easy since it's just brute memorizing.

Terrible lectures. He never explains concepts. He literally just reads off the slides in a very monotone voice. He also takes too many questions during lecture so we lose time and fall behind. Genetics is super detail-oriented and Biebs does not make class interesting or engaging at all.
Nice guy, knows his stuff, but he has a lot of information crammed onto his slides, and I found myself falling asleep during his lectures. However he does get the information across. TAKE NOTES.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is amazing. Make sure you go through all his slides and understands almost everything. Exams are straight from slides. Memorize if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. B was amazing and so inspirational. He knows all of his stuff, makes exams fairly tricky, you can tell his questions apart from Eisenmann's questions. Had to study a lot harder for Dr. B exams but he tells you what you'll need to know for the exams so  I always got a high B on his exams. one thing, HE NEVER RESPONDS TO EMAILS!!!!

Professor knows A LOT about the field and is able to answer almost any question. That being said, he doesn't go by the syllabus (attendance is graded on scale with lateabsence and he gives everyone e.c, dont need seminars), also he will find just about anything to pick at with your papers/exam. However, if you show up its easy enough to pass.

I was in the combined section of eisenman and Bieberich for 302. It's a tough class. Exam averages were usually in the 60 somethings. I liked him over the other professor because he has a funny way about him and he puts things into jokes so you remember things better. You get 5 exams and they take the 4 highest for your grade.
Amazing and inspirational professor!
I LOVE HIM!!! He's one of the best professors I've ever had.
His lectures are awesome and he is so nice and friendly!!! One of the best professors I've ever had. I would love to take his classes again.

He is so clear on what to study. He posts all the lecture slides and emphesizes on what we should study more. He makes biology easier for me and he is also inspirational. Definitely love to take more of his biology classes.

I have mixed feelings about Dr. Bieberich.  He wasn't incredibly organized in class and often rushed through the material to get it done on time.  Also, like most bio professors, his exams were fairly tricky.  That being said, there are definitely worse professors here in the bio department, so don't stress too much if you're stuck with Biebs.

Great professor!  Very helpful and cares a lot about his students.  His tests are very tricky.  Just work really hard, go over each question AT LEAST twice, and you should be able to come out with the grade that you want.  He's VERY specific so you can't just memorize the big picture stuff... I got an A by memorizing every little detail I could.
Good professor. Hard class

The best class I took at UMBC. Amazing teacher. Best Ever. He rocks ! Never enjoyed classes this much (even though it was at 8 AM !). He is super cool and an extremely nice and helpful person. If you are not interested in science, take this class and you will start loving it ! Highly recommended.

One of the best biology professors out there. Very clear explanations, and while material can be challenging, goes above and beyond to make sure everyone is caught up. Does not patronize you for being wrong or not understanding something. Outstanding knowledge of biological field of research. Would highly recommend any of his classes.
Really good professor. Puts powerpoints online after lectures. Very clear, and good at answering questions.

Must go to lectures as the questions he asks in class appears on the exams.  Only professor to wear American Eagle and still look hot.  Knows Bio really well, will answer questions, is very nice.  Exams are based strongly on the lecture but reading the book will help signifigantly.  Very nice, smart and helpful.  Take this class with him.

Good Professor!  Explicates the material well and only lectures on things you need to know for the exam.  However, you need to take good notes because there are stuff not on his outlines that are most likely on the exam.  His exams are similar to previous exams.  Take  it with him IF you have to...in general the course is difficult

His exams weren't as hard as Eisenmann's and he was very approachable. Must go to class though, because pdf notes aren't specific enough and textbook is too descriptive and will make you learn things you dont need to know. You will do well in the class if you go to it regularly
awesome professor He knows what he is talking about and very cool when it comes to grading. As long as you do your work you should be fine. A guy is nice!
Great teacher... hard class but Dr. Bieberich is very clear and helpful.
Good course
No Comments
Pretty good teacher.. writes everything out.. but can be a freaking hardass..

309 has more or less the same coursework for any professor or section however Billingsley does not prepare you for the assignments that are given. Attendance is mandatory and is graded. The lectures are so boring. The course would've been better off online/asynchronous. Heavy work load that's not too difficult but very time consuming

Dr. Billingsley is an amazing professor! She lays out everything clearly, with class only one day a week for the course. One quiz and assignment due weekly with weekly readings. 2 final papers, and a final exam. Love her teaching style and the way she was so energetic at 8 in the morning!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Billingsley is a great professor and is super nice! This class is a little hard to get through because of how long the class is but I would take this class again with her. The assignments feel like busy work but are very helpful.

She is cool, but her lectures are super boring, and it's difficult to pay attention. She is big on group activities. Her assignments are annoying, too. Lots of essays in the class. If you can keep up with the assignments, the class is easy. Participating in class is the worst part.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Blair is a great professor! I took her HIST 301 class and she is a very nice person that enjoy the topics she teaches. Classes are discussion heavy so attendance is mandatory. Essays and the Mid-Term and Final are based on class discussions as well. I highly recommend taking this course it was very interesting

Prof. Blair is one of the sweetest teachers and I loved her MD History class. Be prepared to write. There are 2 small papers and one big one/ research project. But she does help walk you through the project, which makes it easier. Doing the readings and attending lectures is also vital to passing her midterm/finals.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very good professor in terms of grading. In my 2 Essays and a Research Paper, even though I'm not a History major she straight up gave me B's. The Midterm and Final is based on the class readings that she assigns, there are study guides for both the exams. Very straightforward and easy-to approach professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is really sweet and caring to her students. Her love of the subject matter carries her classes. Like most UMBC professors, she is far left politically, but unlike most UMBC professors, she doesn't beat you over the head with her politics. Great professor for public history classes. I had her as my adviser and I genuinely miss her!

His lectures are extremely good. I was suprised every time because he taught them like it was the first time teaching them. He was always so excited teaching the class. Finally a professor who loves his job and cares for students.

One of the coolest professors at UMBC by far. Always fills his class with anecdotes relating to the course material making it fun to learn. Semester long group project was a drag but as a professor he did everything else as well as possible. Definitely take if you get the chance.

Sweet guy, he really wants everyone to do well in his class. Attendance is mandatory, but he is very reasonable if you do not come a few times. This class is an easy A/B so you could skip at least half the classes and be fine, but I recommend going because his lectures are awesome and you should give him the respect he deserves.
Actually a very easy class. Semester long group project broken down into 4 papers. Expect about an hour or 2 of work a weel very enjoyable class.

Dr. Birrane took this class way too seriously. We are CMSC majors, not English majors. He is a super harsh grader and your grade relies heavily on the group you're assigned. Weekly quizzes were over the top with what he expected us to remember from class (mostly things he just brushed over).

His work consists of a quiz per lecture, a glorified homework assignment, phases/group projects, lengthy homeworks, the midterm and final were online for this semester. We also had the option to attend class in person or online. Feedback can be harsh but I personally didn't mind. I think Birrane is a cool and funny dude.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: He's a VERY tough grader and will leave harsh feedback. If you are one to take feedback to heart, do not take this class with him. There is a semester long group project, weekly lecture quizzes, two exams, and homework that are of essay lengths. If you want an easy A, look for another professor, cause this class is a lot of work for an A.
Extremely tough grader specifically when it comes to the papers you write. Don't let him be your first choice.

Edward is an okay teacher. His exams had many silly questions and his semester long project was a mess. If you get stuck with 2 group mates who don't care about their grade it's gonna be hard to get an A. He uses a "multiplier" to help boost grades but his algorithm for determining it is ridiculous and many times hurts your grade. Don't recommend.

This professor teaches you HOW to think as opposed to WHAT to think. He teaches not only ethics but critical thinking and writing skills. His lectures are really interesting, He's sort of tough on grading but it's always in the interest of molding students into better thinkers. Be prepared to write a lot, that project is no joke.

Edward has done an amazing job teaching 304 online. He records YouTube videos explaining the PowerPoints. There are 11 weekly quizzes based off entirely from the PowerPoints; 5 homework's; 2 exams on LockDown but without webcam tho! and 1 semester long group project. Would definitely recommend him if you need an easy A and want to up your GPA

First of, the course is labeled as writing intensive so do expect the group essay to take a good chunk of time. Each stage of the group essay was graded individually and the feedback Birrane gave was extensive and thorough which helped immensely with the following stages. Lectures are interesting and solid. Quizzes and exams are more than fair.
Hands down most enjoyable class of my semester

He is an nice and interesting professor but not necessarily an easy A. Expect to do a lot of writing. Tests are also medium difficulty and not a complete joke like others. Also only professor for ethics to give a final. If the schedule is convenient hes not the worst option but think twice if you're taking a tough courseload.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Cool professor, really smart in his field, great lecturer, and very decent on grading. Pay attention at least 75% in class and you'll do great on the quizzes. Put a couple hours of work in on the project and you'll do well. Material is a little tougher than expected, but for a CS class it's definitely a break.

Prof. is really passionate about this class, but it's a slog. Group projects with 7 people yet he wants "one person feel" from papers. Class discussions are painful to those who hate philosophy type nothing discussions. Makes you write and study a lot for a required writing class. Prof. isn't a jerk or bad at his job but take someone else for 304.

He has been doing this for years and he is GOOD. A lot of the grading options is up to you (er... the earlier class) you can show up to either of his lectures. He's a really smart nerd with a glorious sense of humour. This is the big one: HE MAKES YOU CARE! His lectures are so good/engaging and so interesting you dont want to leave.

Lots of short quizzes, but theyre easy and dont count for much. Very up front about whats on the tests. Semester long project is essentially just a big paper. Graded pretty harshly, but if you pay attention to his feedback and incorporate that into later phases, youll get good grades moving forward. Great lecturer

Lectures were informative and not super boring. Treats the class as an equal. Has short quizzes every week that were previous lecture content. Exam content are never surprises. Tries to spice up the class with class votes, videos, and memes. The quizzes cover lecture, and exams cover the quizzes. Long term group writing project as final

The best professor for 304. Weekly quizzes, so make sure to go to class. Tells you what exactly to study for exam, which have quiz short answers on them potentially. He is a tough grader, but he grades you as an equal, as a professional in the field. His lectures are amazing, he's hysterical, and you're missing out if you don't take this professor.

Memes. This professor truly connects with the students. You will really enjoy his lectures and assignments. He is a bit of a tough grader, but he grades you like he would any other professional in the field.
If there was an award for the Best Professor at UMBC, it would definitely be him  Spring 2018

He presents the material in such a way that you learn something without busting your hump. The tests and quizzes are easy but the semester group project can be involved ( a lot of writing). The peer evaluation for the project are good and he helps with the group members that don't pull their weight.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Great professor with a sense of humor! Exams and quizzes are easy and he tries his best to make sure the whole class passes. Semester-long group project is a pain and the grading was ambiguous at times. He grades them harshly at times. Definitely makes you work for it, but his lectures are worth going to.
Good professor, the year long group project kind of blows (averaged around 75%), but if you do well on the exams and quizzes and homework you can still get an A.

This class has a semester-long group project; your team must find a professor with a project for you. You fill out a lot of documentation, while working on your code. The class material is easy and the reviews tell you everything you need to know. Birrane is a very laid back professor and you'll enjoy his class.

Do not listen to any negative reviews about Professor Blake, I grew to really love this class and enjoy his teaching style. It is easy to succeed in this class but you must be committed and take it seriously. Do the homework, go to every lecture, and study right before the quiz. If you don't like studying or reading, this is not the class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I like the fact he curves tests and has engaging lectures. There's also only one major essay you have to do throughout the semester, other than that its just Perusals. I did not like the fact that we had lock down browser the exams weren't too bad.

Class is 70% self-taught. Required online videos & readings (Perusall) so you're expected to understand the material before class. Disappointing bcs class time serves solely as a review session. Paper on Lochner v. New York—expectations and instructions were barely discussed in class when it is 30% of our grade. Struggles to explain concept clearly
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's strict about many things, the assignments are very clear and demanding in my opinion, and he DOES NOT CARE about the students! He reiterates everything said in the slides on Persuall but then makes attendance mandatory-we don't even review! I suppose it is a good preparation for law school if all the professors there are prudes.
do not listen to these other reviews. this prof is evil. his lectures are so boring and he does nothing but target students b/c he has nothing better to do. avoid taking his class if u can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This course is like an undergrad version of law school. There are a lot of readings, and many things we need to know are discussed in class. It's difficult to keep up with the class discussion since he talks about it fast, but he always asks if we need to spend more time on a topic. Not a lot of assignments, but memorizing concepts takes a while.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Blake for POLI230 and he was incredible! So kind and genuinely wants his students to succeed. The study questions at the end of the lecture videos are very helpful on the quizzes. He even offered to read our essay drafts and give comments before we submit to get the best grade possible. 100% would take a class with him again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Blake is a fantastic teacher! Sometimes goes on tangents, but mostly sticks to the material and is willing to humor the class answering random questions. Decent amount of reading, but if you enjoy legal jargon this class is for you! Definitely not an easy A, but he is willing to work with you if you go to office hours and put in the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class is pretty straight forward with weekly readings and three quizzes. The quizzes are online but they are lockdown browser which makes it a little more difficult. Prof Blake is very intimidating and very patronizing I won't be taking another class with him here. Attendance is mandatory. He doesn't offer a lot of help for reviewing for quizzes

Definitely recommend! He's a little intimidating because he speaks quite fast and has an encyclopedic knowledge about the subject, so really listen during his lectures. Do the assigned readings early, because they are dense and otherwise you will feel lost in class. This is a hard class, but he really presents you with every opportunity to succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Blake is a great professor and is really passionate about what he teaches but talks really fast. There a lot of readings that need to be done before classes. I recommend watching youtube summaries of the cases before actually reading and going to class or you'll be lost. He provides study questions which come on the test which is helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best professors you'll ever meet. Super passionate about the course material and gives the class an easygoing feel despite all the legalese. Also runs Moot Court!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great instructor, engaging lectures. Lots of reading, with graded annotations (easy to score high if you actually read and try). Curves the exams (in your favor) depending on the grade distribution. Gave great feedback on the rough draft for the final paper, which helped me score high on that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Blake really knows the ins and outs of constitutional law. He checks attendance so make sure you show up to class. Some of the readings are long but the content fits the class. Lectures are pretty straight forward, hes pretty funny and makes the tests pretty easy overall.

Even tho it's in person, he records lectures and has the slides available. Def pay attention to what he's saying. Make sure to do the readings well before the due date cuz these r actual court cases so some can be v long. also if you don't read them thoroughly, make sure to google what these cases r abt so that you can be prepared for the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The best thing about his class was that I figured out that I wasn't interested in polisci, so that's a plus. Anyways, there are 2 readings every week that u need to annotate due 5pm before lecture the next day, 3 quizzes, one of which acts as a 'final' but is the same as other quizzes and one essay. It's all p doable as long as ur willing to do it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Blake is awesome and makes easy for students to succeed. There was a big paper at the end, but he helps you with sources and ideas beforehand. Just make sure you take notes in his lectures and study before his quizzes.
Hands down the best professor I have ever had, balances a healthy workload with amazing discussion and a genuinely funny approach to content. Take every class he offers!!!

First Amendment Freedoms was excellent. Each week we were assigned 3 cases to read in full. You can skim and look for summaries online to help. However, it is important to know all the key arguments made during the case. Attendance and participation mandatory, but it's super fun. Assignments/papers 2 case briefs, 2 case opinions, and 1 moot court.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Blake was my favorite professor for the semester. His class isn't super easy, but if you put in the work you get great results. Loved the debates! Most cases can be found online, but the book is so helpful. He prefers students to bring the text, but I didn't have it half the time. Prof. Blake didn't care. Awesome class and teacher. 10/10
Great Professor!

Prof. Blake is  always willing to answer questions/go over something in more detail so students feel comfortable with the material. As long as you put in effort- do the readings, participate in class and take notes- passing is easy.
Participation matters in his class, so try your best to be engaged because it's graded. Also, try to read the texts given before class; they're really helpful, so you aren't confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: came back to say these reviews are true.

Prof. Bloom is my favorite professor! He's hilarious and speaks his mind. Lots of reading in this class and lots of summaries, the workload is heavy. Your biggest grade is a creative story worth 100 points and there will be discussions on everyone's stories. He HATES computers, almost everything is on paper. No final exam, no quizzes. Just homework

He flip flops so much on the grading of essays. Obviously grading literature is subjective, but he seems to love taking points off for stupid stuff and then contradicts the feedback hell give in previous assignments. Terrible teacher, seems nice enough though, but nice isnt good enough when youre making a mockery out of a class students paid for
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: prof bloom really helped my writing skills, the textbook was called they say i say and was free and really helpful. if you write to the style he likes you'll get an easy A. he really gave good feedback and only had 4 synchronous classes for the whole entire semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of my favorite teachers in my experience here at UMBC. He's funny, he's nice, and he cares a lot about what he's teaching and that comes through in the class and its structure. If you have to take a class, do it with him! I don't think you'll regret it.

Took class as an AH elective. Bloom is a really good teacher and the class was fun, but expect a large amount of work. Journal due every class which mostly consisted of summarizing the book. Make sure you have the time to complete all the busy work if you're going to take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Unless you want to read 300 pages a night and write summaries until your fingers fall off, don't take this class. There are easier ways to satisfy your ENG requirement, trust me. Just don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He is definitely my favorite English professor I've ever taken and I've taken quite a few. You do have to read for hw and do a journal on each of the readings, and take a quiz on the readings every day. But I did feel, as a writer, he helped me improved tremendously, and I am definitely wanting to take another class with him soon!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Bloom is a good guy, and I found him to be respectful and open--we even had some annoying people, but he was still patient. There were journals due each class for the reading as well as a mini-quiz, which was a lot of work and he insisted on printing, so that kind of sucked. Otherwise I enjoyed the socratic-style discussions of the class.

I think he is the best English professor here. He does give a lot of homework in the first part of the semester then later he focuses mostly on essays. There are only 3 essays with 2 revisions. Honestly do as he says and revise your papers and you will get a good grade.

Most of the time he is really energetic and encourages the class to feel comfortable to raise their hands and provide their thoughts from readings.  Even though there was a book required for us to get at the beginning of the semester, he was careful to choose a book which he knew would be affordable and not expensive. & He likes to speak his mind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Bloom is a shining example of professionalism and passion that very few teachers achieve. He intensely polite and insightful, and genuinely cares about helping each and every one of his students improve their writing. Will remain objective at all times, and expresses criticism without being disparaging, even went talking one-on-one.

He is really good at letting you know your faults and helps you improve upon your skills. He is very nice but can be strict at the same time. Has a lot of passion for the subject and expects everyone to participate in discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Ryan Bloom is a great professor! He's a tough grader but is always willing and happy to help you with papers, understanding readings, etc. He is so energetic and passionate about what he does, and I feel like I am learning so much in his class! While he only assigns 3 papers, he assigns a lot of readings and participation is essential to success.

Although I only received a B in his class, he was the most fun and inspiring teacher. He was always kind and would offer assistance if needed. He grades very hard but if you do your best and ask for help he will guide you. I feel like I actually learned a TON in his class and would take again!

His class is pretty easy. He only gives you 3 papers the entire semester, while other teachers give you 4 to 5 papers. He also does not give you an assignment on the freshman summer reading. He gives you the chance to do revisions on your papers so you can improve your grade on them as well. Do the assigned readings, show up, and participate.

Ryan bloom his a tough grader,  if you work closely with him you can achieve a lot. My english skills were poor when I took the class but with hard work and dedication you can easily pass the class. If you want to take English 100  with Ryan Bloom  Make sure you attend all his lectures and show up in time.

Very hard on grading. Takes a lot of points off from workshop if you do not meet his requirement perfectly. Essays have to be exactly the way he wants. Avoid if possible. Unless you love English do not take.

Professor Bloom certainly knows fiction, and certainly has a passion for it.  He is an easy professor to talk to before, during, and after class about writing and literature.  Grades are based on participation and turning in your assignments on time.  It's a fun class if you're interested and willing to do the work.

Extremely tough class. Unless you genuinely love english and appreciate the course, do not take. He treats it more than what a 100 level class should be treated as. Do essays exactly how he wants or you will fail. I went to the writing center to edit my essay and still received a 72% even though the writing center said it was perfectly fine.

This is a grueling class. You won't have fun, it won't be easy, and Bloom will be very strict. Writing essays isn't just a matter of time and diligence; you need a stroke of brilliance and inspiration to even have a topic. Bloom tries to be cool and that's where all the other positive reviews come from, but the class is very difficult.

I really enjoyed this class. Participate in discussions and come to class (on time) he takes attendance. No final, just three papers and a presentation on your third paper. Grades hard but you can turn in papers twice for a better grade. Extremely helpful if you let him know you need it.

He is a very hard professor. Gives 3 essays, does not give tests if the class does well in discussion. Very tough grader. If you are not a strong writer, I would recommend finding a different professor. This semester isn't over but I think I got a C, when I am normally an A/B student.

The class is challenging, but helps you to become a better writer. Some of the books were interesting, others not so much. Reading the books for discussions, and writing the essays were the most time-consuming. Take this class if you have a strong foundation in English and it should be a breeze.
This guy is awesome, just ask him questions and do all the small assignments and remember the LARGER CULTURE THESIS in all of your essays. Definitely one of my favorite professors.

This guy is extremely boring, the essays don't make sense and he gives incredibly dull clarity, I would not suggest this professor at all unless you are a very good writer.  Also, MAKE SURE YOU READ THE BOOK, I didn't my grade hurt on one of the Essays, the grading format was way too unclear.

He is a decent (in that you'll probably learn a lot) but slightly difficult professor (challenging grader); even above average students will struggle to get an A.  His class moves at quite a clip, and it can be a challenge to meet all the minute requirements he has, all of which affect your grade; coming to class on time, little assignments, etc.

I recommend taking his class if you consider yourself to be a moderately strong writer, as he is a tough grader; the difficulty of the class slightly exceeds that of a typical 100 level course. That aside, the books he assigns are interesting and his assignments are easy. The Group work can be a bit aggravating. Attendance is mandatory.

Compared to other English professors, he is well liked. He gives one less essay than other professors but one extra book to read. This saves a lot of time. He has a class discussion after you read each book rather than a test. You can ask him for help, but be sure to delete a paragraph if he says so. Emphasize the "larger culture" in all essays.

Too much time spent on group work. It's fine if your group is motivated, but if you get stuck with people who don't care, you're really wasting time and learn very little. The discussion of the texts we read were brief and ill focused.

I really enjoyed his class, looking back at it. Somewhat of a hard grader on the papers, so go to his office hours and to the writing center. Other than that, most assignments are easy and take no more than 5 to 10 minutes. Makes class enjoyable and fun to attend

Great teacher, it's not an easy class by any means. He's hardcore about MLA formatting so make sure you know that. He's a tough grader all around. Grades are determined by some papers, showing up to class, and participating.

great teacher. caring, approachable, involved, and dedicated. he also responds to e-mail very quickly. his reading choices are great and he is very knowledgeable. show up for class and participate in discussion and it should be easy for you. recommended!
A pretty good professor though a hard grader.
He's a pretty nice guy. The amount of books you read and essays you write are reasonable. He's a hard grader on the essays though, and I didn't like some of the essay topics.
Bad to below-average teacher who thinks he's "hip" and "with it". Avoid if possible.

An overall catch; great guy, great teacher.  He obviously is passionate about what he teaches, and makes sure everyone's on the same page.  Never hard to reach, always willing to help.  Genuinely wants students to do well, grades on self-improvement.

Even though it's only a 100 level class, there's a lot of work involved. The essays are graded really hard, so you've got to know what you're doing when writing. But class was always interesting and fun and interactive. You only read a few novels and discuss them. Just go to class and participate and you'll be fine.

I've had this professor before and he's pretty clear on how his class is structured. For ENG 233, we had to read a book a week, write 2 major papers, do a presentation, and have 5 reading responses and 5 discussion questions. It sounds like a lot but is not. The readings were really fun and interesting. Great professor!I Definitely recommend him.

Professor Bloom is a really great Professor. In this class there is a lot of reading and I wouldn't call it an easy class but he always kept it fun. I never dreaded going to his class. He generally picks pretty good books too, although you have to read a book a week. I definitely recommend him.
best professor i've had. real laid back. take this class especially if you're a soccer fan. he loves soccer
He is Horrible!! and definately NOT hot!! that's insanity! He might try to sound nice..but infact he is very cruel...I would recommend avoiding his class if possible! P.S. NOT HOT!!!
Almost everyone else who rated him thought he was absolutely perfect, but I think he's just okay. His lectures are okay and I personally think he looks just so-so, lol.

I tried really hard and spent more hours on the class then all my other classes combined. Keep in mind this is English 100!!! Miss 2 classes or be late for 4 classes and he will either fail you or give you a non passing grade. DO NOT BE FOOLED BY NICE COMMENTS!!! He  acts very nice but is in reality an ENG 100 professor who does not teach ENG 100.

He's awesome!! Definitely one of the better English profs, based on what I've heard. Most books are fairly interesting, and he is fun to talk to. He's big on participation, and sort of a tough grader, but I enjoyed his class.
Chill teacher, you can tell he's passionate about his work.  Very helpful when it comes time to write essays.  Pretty average amount of work for an english class.  Would reccomend.
Worth taking. Reasonable essay topics. Fair grader. And he's pretty sexy...I wish he taught more classes
No Comments
he's a pretty chill profesor.. not too difficult if you try on the essays and understand what he expects from them. show up for class! 3 absenses is possible grounds for failure.
A really good professor.  Essay topics are different but not too hard once you get a hold on what he wants.  I thought he was pretty cute too actually
Ryan Bloom is definitely a great teacher. He cares about his students and wants them to do well! He also throws some humor and excitement in there to keep us interested :)

I am so glad I got Professor Bloom my freshman year! If you can get him---take him! He is incredibly HOTT! and I want to marry him! Class was easy, he was great and funny---never boring at all! Great class, will definitely take him again if I can!

definitely the cutest professor. Grades fairly, not easy or hard. Only 4 essays, about 2 weeks to do each of them. His essay topics are a little difficult though. No exams, just discussions on the books. The books are actually pretty interesting and you have plenty of time to read them
No Comments

Very nice and helpful to students. Holds discussions for the novels and texts we read in class which are always fun. Fair in teaching, helps with essays and tells you how you can improve them.  Participate, show up to every class and you will do fine!

Enthusiastic about teaching; willing to help students with any problems. Great guy, nice to look at, good sense of humor. The class is basically a few essays, each progressively harder, along with novels and handouts to read and discuss (never any quizzes, unless he suspects no one has read the material). Definitely take Engl100 with him.
Sincerely tries to get the concept across clearly to each student.  A side note, Dawn is very pretty too.
Dawn Block is very knowledgeable, and her lectures we fun. I certainly learned a lot.
The lecture slides are online and the exams are based off of the study guides. Easy A. Attend class to participate in group work.

Had her for 104 and 201. She really made it easy to learn basic programming concepts. Tests were basically the study guides and were much easier than the homeworks (which weren't too difficult, but challenging sometimes). I definitely would recommend her if you need to take either course.
Having had her for 104 and 201, I will say that if you don't get to have a class with her you are missing out.  Just an all around great prof.

The class can be a little boring if you go everyday and understand everything. The labs are very helpful in practicing each concept and I would definitely at least flip through the book from time to time. It proved very helpful. Ms. Block and the TAs were very helpful through email. They won't give you the answer but will send you in the right way

Mrs. Block is one of my favorite professors. She is very helpful through email and in just talking to her. The TAs were also very helpful and the homeworks weren't very hard. Exams are made up of questions from the study guide so just do that before the exam. Grades very generously.

One of the best teachers at UMBC. Quite funny and brings candy to class once in a while. She's young and always smiling so you can associate with her easily. If you haven't taken programming before, she should be your pick! Also for CMSC 201!
She's prompt with responding to emails, lectures clearly, and is overall very reasonable with workload. She also brings candy to class!
Clear lectures, posts the slides. Available for questions via email anytime. What more could you want?
Amazing, one of the best teachers I've had my freshman year
She is one the most helpful and passionate teachers I've ever had. She not only is willing to help you succeed in her class, she will also help you outside of class with advising type issues.

Professor Block is absolutely Beautiful.  She should be a news anchor or something.  Honestly, attendance is not mandatory but I did go to all classes.  Who wouldn't!  She's cool AND hot AND knows computers.

The best teacher at UMBC. I had her for 201 back in the Spring of 2008 and even to this day passing in the hall she will address me by name and inquire after my studies. Very good teacher. Cares for the students.

Extremely clear professor. I went into 104 having had no prior programming experience and am now in 313 and 331 and having no trouble. This is thanks to her! She made the class so fun and enjoyable but also made sure that everyone was learning what they needed to in order to be successful in 201... and beyond!
Great teacher, very clear and helpful. tests are not that hard, really easy if you study. computer programs are time consuming. great class to see if you want to major in computer science

The Best Professor at UMBC. If you graduate without taking her easy CMSC 104 class, you are really missing out. She is HOT!! Not just the guys but even the girls think so! She is sweet and goes out of her way to help her students. You get chocolate if you go visit her in her office. She will take time out for you. Take her! She is Fantabulous!!

Ms.Block is extremely helpful if she sees that you are trying to your full potential. Brings in candies on holidays & exam days!! Easy to understand and easy to approach. She is not there to intimidate you rather to help you. Take advantage of her office hours if you need help!  Definitely recommend her for 104, 201 and other classes she teaches.

One of the best professors i've had at UMBC. Def worth taking a class with her! Midterm & final is fairly easy if you complete the study questions she gives out a week prior to the exam. Very helpful, funny, friendly & makes the course much more interesting than it really is. Brings in candy on exam days; this semester, she even brought ice cream:)

Ms. Block is great. i have nothing but respect for her. I have her as both my teacher and advisor for the last year and she's extremely helpful. She's a very happy person (smiles all the time). she will always help you with your code and everything and clear on what each project is suppose to do. you should def. take her. my fav. teacher ever.
Awesome teacher, very helpful, and very clear in lecture.

The best teacher Ive had. Discussion is mandatory, but helpful if you dont have much programming experience. I also had her for 104 and she is a very good teacher and makes an effort to learn everyones name. Shes even starting to sway me in CMSC minoring.
my favorite teacher ever! smart, nice, and funny. i think i have a crush on her ;)
She's very clear with her teaching
She is a good teacher.  I had a lot of previous programming experience, so the class seemed slow.  Otherwise I'm sure it would be fine, and she's a cool, fun person too.

Programming is fun. She makes it easy to understand. Explains materials very clearly. Very approachable if you need help. Highly recommend this class/professor if you want to learn to program but have no prior experience.
No Comments

she is hot! i like how she teaches the class with her easy to follow powerpoint slides. she is willing to help out all the time. she is a nice person to have for a teacher. take comp sci with her if you can
She is a great person.  Very easy to get along with and more than willing to help.  I would recommend over anyone else.
Very good teacher, she explain very well.

Ms. Block is extremely helpful when teaching and understands the structure of how to help others learn the material.  She publishes all the lectures on a web site and most of the homework is sent through the computer.  She teaches the basics of programming and you only need to read the book for the first portion of the course-for computer history.
No Comments
The class is hard and boring no matter who is the teacher, but she makes it a better class to go to, and plus she is very hot!

Well, she isn't teaching 201 next semester, but I can say she is a good professor.  Don't get me wrong, the lectures will be boring no matter who you  take it with, but she tries hard, and is a lot easier on the eyes than most.

I also had her as a grader for 201, and I found her grading to be very fair... no one I knew ever got anything under a 90 for a working project (with the exception of one person: global variables are bad!) when she graded... always nice and very clear about what was wrong or bad with your project :)

I enjoyed her class.  She gave out candy on the first day, special days, and any day there was a test which was only the midterm and final.  She also makes herself extremely avalible if you need help and is nice.  Highly recomend her.  She is very easy to understand and has interesting storyies.
great teacher, very helpful, and very easy on the eyes.  can't beat it.

She is VERY clear in her teaching and gives good explanations if you don't understand something.  She is kind and helpful.  Her programs and tests start out easy, but gradually get harder, but that is expected, but they are always fair.  I would absolutely take her class again!
Take it
Yeah, take her class.  Check out office hours and stay up with class (if you have difficulty) and it'll be fine.

I can't say she's a great teacher beacuse this class is taught completely off lecture notes and isnt really all that hard. The only semi-difficult part of the class is when it comes to pointers and she handled that well.

Hot as****.. her **** alone will give you incentive to go to class. And shes smart as**** and could program your ass off any day of the week, so definitely take Block. (P.S. She loves Belvedere Vodka)
Shes good, hott too! just dont sleep in her class or u wont know how to do the prog projects
I had her as a "grader" for CMSC201 projects. Very unclear about grading decisions. With questions, she either does not respond, responds in a rude manner, or gives an irrelevant response.
She seems to have no real world coding experience, which might not work in your favor.
