reviews.comment: Honestly the best professor I have had at UMBC. He is so caring about his students and really wants you to learn and to have the best experience possible. His lectures are really interesting and you learn a lot about the intricacies of the Spanish language as well as culture. There is a lot of hw but as long as you do the work you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Felix is a solid dude. He is easy going, pretty funny, and engaging. He gets side tracked pretty easily if you talk about Colombia. If you are thinking about taking 201 over the winter, do it. The class is easy if you put in the work. I do not recommend taking this class without doing 102 or 103, or without prior experience, you won't do well.

Prof. Burgos is the real deal!! Younger professor. Took him over winter and was expecting to struggle. He did a good job pacing the class and is very approachable and helpful. He made the class interesting and I left the class clearly understanding concepts that I struggled with earlier. Go to class, do the homework and assignments n youll be ok.

I had Professor Burgos over the winter session and I went into this course dreading Spanish.  Having not taken Spanish since 4-5 years, I was worried that I would not get back on track.  But the class was enjoyable and the material was easy to grasp if you read and do the HW.  If you take his course you will surely enjoy it.
He is a very nice guy and funny. Makes class enjoyable. However, he is disorganized and is not good at making sure everyone understands the material.

He is a funny guy and makes class enjoyable. However, he is not a great teacher. He is disorganized and does not adequately teach you what he expects you to know on quizzes, etc. He is a harsh grader as well.

He made the class more enjoyable to sit through, and he has a good sense of humor.  The class was pretty easy, and he explains everything clearly.  In my opinion, he should've collected homework because people complained about not understanding anything (they didn't do the homework...)

One of the best Spanish professors I've had. He understands what it's like being a student and doesn't overload the required work. He may seem unclear and difficult to understand. However, when he's teaching a comment if you're 100% honest with him and tell him you don't understand he'll slow it down and go over it until you do! Great professor!

I think he has good intentions, but overall he is not that great of a professor. I you want to actually learn something, look somewhere else. Not very good at explaining things and was not very helpful at office hours.

He is a sweet guy and always tries to keep the class fun an entertaining. Attendance is mandatory and oral participation for in-class activities is required but the exams are based mostly on those activities so they help you. Just remember to do your homework/online assignments and you shouldn?t get lower than a B. Recommended!

Very nice guy and a good teacher but if you're bad at Spanish I would stay away from his class. He wants to help you if you're struggling but does not know how and will fail you if he thinks you're not ready for 201.

Felix was an awesome professor. I learned so much in that class. He was very patient with students' questions and his exams were easy if you followed his study guides. Definitely take spanish with him if you can.
You have to go to class, but it's worth it great teacher lots of work with other students. One of the best teacher's I've had here.
Professor Burgos is a very fair teacher who is willing to help students. Prior to taking this class, I dreaded Spanish, but this man helped me a lot. I will always respect him for that.
Great teacher! Native Spanish Speaker makes the class go by very quick. He grades fair and makes class entertaining. I didn't like spanish before I took this class and now I love it.
Amazing teacher!! really cool and fun. class goes by way too fast with this guy. He's really chill because he's still a student himself. 100% helpful and clear.
DO NOT TAKE HIM. you won't learn anything much. Class activites are hard. Too much work. Exams are also hard. There are 10 quizes weekly, and they are fairly ok.
Nice guy. He wants his students to succeed. He's not a hard grader.
Great teacher. He keeps class entertaining. Exams are based on class activities. Take him!! Do all the work, then you'll be fine!
I enjoyed his class very much! He's very helpful and willing to help

Took him for winter session which I was NOT looking forward to-but he made it not so painful. I was disappointed to see the negative comments about him b/c he is very passionate about teaching & always willing to clarify. My experience w/ him was positive, he is fairly easy on the grading but really wants you to understand the material. Funny too.
Professor Burgos is a wonderful teacher, very committed and does his best to help the students. I made a lot of progress with him. Go Felix! you rock!
Stay away. He his not a good teacher at all.  He is boring and you will not learn anything about spanish.  You will be screwed for spanish 201.  Find another teacher.

He is not a good professor.  He rambles on and on about things that have nothing to do with anything to with the class.  His quizzes are pretty.  If you plan on continuing your spanish career do not take him for 102. You will be screwed.  His accent doesnt make things any easier to learn and his blackboard and online chats are useless.  Stay away.
chabite!
No Comments

She is a phenomenal teacher that just helped me fall in love with the field of psychology even more.  I didn't know what CP was before taking the class, and even now that it is over, I am actually going back to some of the readings. I keep applying CP to almost everything I see.  It is a lot of work but a really great class.

I would recommend taking a different class then hers. She seems to forget you have other classes and assigned like 150 pages or more to read a week. Assigned long papers. Group project were just awful with no support from her.

Ms. Buckingham is a fantastic teacher! She's pretty funny, definitely knows what she's talking about, and is super clear. Lectures follow the book but don't cover everything. You definitely need to read for this class to get an A.

i got an A, so it's not impossible!  yeah, you have to study hard, but i actually thought her lectures were interesting and review sessions were pretty helpful.  i also went to her office hours, which helped me.  id recommend you take this class, but i think too many people take it thinking it is an easy A - i worked for my A but learned a lot.

Lectures are pointless as she just regurgitates everything from the textbook. You better be there, only for the sparse clicker questions that add up. She does not prepare you for her exams, which are somehow difficult even if you've read the textbook. You probably won't get an A in this class. Just find someone else.
interesting class, nice professor, and fun group work. Just do the labs and study with peer mentors and you'll be fine.

I loved this class!  It was really interesting!  I actually decided to double major in psych (I'm also a bio major) because of it.  Professor Buckingham was really nice and upbeat.  She made lectures interesting and fun.  I hope to take other classes with her in the future.

Class was difficult but professor cared about students. Always willing to answer questions in lecture and wanted us to participate. I went to her office hours and emailed when I had questions and she was always helpful. Class was interesting. Yes, a lot information was in labs, book, and lecture, but that is what made me learn. You need to study.

The class wasn't difficult, it's just that there was alot of reading and online labs. Going to class was mandatory because there were clicker questions and group work during each lecture. This class definitely isn't an easy A, therefore, you should read over the textbook and review notes before every exam.
would rather play tetris
good

Dry lectures, not good at explaining things, is combative with questions, may or may not address questions from homework.  Lenient grader -- will give credit if you mix up signs or if you were close to the answer thru your work shown. Seems like a nice person but not a good teacher if you are not math-minded already. I got a tutor for all tests.

Took her for 152 and didn't pass, mostly because of the weird team structure and group quizzes were not a good set-up for Calc 2. Just took her for Calc 3 and it was a lot better without the teams. She would be better if she explained things a little more thoroughly instead of just writing definitions but she did show a lot of diagrams.
Made a tough topic more clear. Highly recommended.
She is nice and sweet, I would love to take a class with her again. Has an accent but she is understandable,  I do not think anyone would have trouble with that.

If you took BC Calculus in high school and never had to study, this class will probably be easy for you. She is not very clear in her lectures, especially in the first unit on vectors. She shows steps but doesn't explain them. I went to lectures, but I found the textbook more useful. It is not required for class. She is helpful only if you ask.

After reading these reviews, I reluctantly signed up for two classes with Dr. Budimirovic for this semester. Much to my surprise, I found both classes pleasant, with requirements and expectations clearly outlined. Although the lectures aren't incredibly inspiring (it's math after all), I have to say that I definitely enjoyed classes with her.

I appreciate her in that she tends to be a lenient grader. She also hand-grades homeworks and (most) assesments by herself, so I appreciate that. But overall she is a terrible lecturer. Going to class makes you develop a hate for Linear Algebra because she is just way too boring.
Hard to hear, but she teaches through examples (which are usually helpful). Reading the textbook is extremely useful for quizzes and tests.

I took Linear Algebra and Calc III with her.  Obviously, she was not the best at explaining certain concepts but if you read the book before class, it was easier to follow along.  Quizzes and exams are manageable, especially because she gives practice exams.  It also helps to come to class because occasionally you get some helpful tips from her.

This was by far the worst class I've ever taken. The professor does not speak to the class and the lectures, if you can call them that, are not relevant to the course material. She is helpful for office hours, but you are better off taking it with another professor or just waiting another semester if possible.
I took math 151,221, and 251 with tatjana. i think she is a good professor, but her exams are harder than other professors'. She gives extra points for every exam.

Lectures are useless, but you have to show up to get credit. Tests are difficult in relation the amount of instruction we are given. She is a very nice lady, but unfortunately just an awful teacher. Nearly impossible to understand.

Doesn't know how to teach. Tells her students to attend another professors lectures rather than helping. If you haven't taken calc 1 before you will struggle in her class. I would not take calc 2 when I was supposed to just because I would have this professor again. It's better to not take this class, than to take it with this professor.

She's a nice person, but you have to teach yourself a lot of the material. Definitely definitely read the book. Quizzes can be tricky but her exams are easy and she gives a lot of extra credit on them. It can be hard to understand her explanations because she doesn't teach well; also she speaks really softly so it can be hard to hear her.

good stuff first: on test review day we would get some helpful information out of her. she also knows her stuff. bad part: she speaks quietly and doesn't say much. i was unclear about what she was saying half the time. the book helped, linear algebra was new  and i struggled to understand it. help from the book my team mates and coming to class
The professor doesn't use a microphone. Skips around in steps. Everything about this class is ridiculously hard like we're expected to be math majors. Don't even bother with this person.

She's a perfectly nice person. However, her lectures are useless. She halfway solves problems on the board without lecturing, speaks in a soft voice and overall is no help. Most people don't attend class. Not a horrific experience, but I self-taught myself everything.

Worst professor I've ever had. She expects you to already 100% understand the material before class, and skips steps constantly with no explanation. If you have to take this course, avoid this professor at all cost.

kind person but a bad professor. She skips steps when solving a problem and her voice is low. After the 2nd week of classes 80% of people in the class stopped coming. TA's grade most of the tests and were lenient with grading. But you will be teaching yours CALC 2. Professor Leonard Youtube  I passed all my tests bc of him look him up.

Basically, everything that's already been said here. If I could give the money spent on this class to this youtube guy "Evans Lawrence" I would. His series of youtube lectures follow the stewart textbook we use and are the only reason did well in this class and learned anything. If you find yourself in this class, check him out.

Her speaking abilities are poor and she is difficult to understand at times. Apparently she is just a lecturer and doesn't hold the experience of an actual professor. I recommend asking you TA's for help and reading the book.
She is a good professor.

She's a nice enough person, but a terrible professor. Class is always spent with her sort of doing examples on the board with no one paying any attention. Class wasn't unreasonably hard, but plan on teaching yourself. She never explains material and is generally useless for anything other than answering questions.

She is very quiet in her lectures. It is very hard to understand because of her accent (which isn't her fault). I took Calculus BC, in high school, so the class was pretty straightforward. But if you are coming just from pre-calculus, you will most likely struggle a lot. Do the homework, it helps.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. If you have taken Calc AB or BC in highschool, you might be fine. But if you've just taken Precalc or Calc with Apps in HS, withdraw ASAP or switch to a better professor like Nanes. Tatjana does not clearly explain what's gonna be on the test and skips around different problems in her lectures

Here's a warning to all students of this school: do not take this professor unless your school career depends on it.  Lectures are beyond useless; they will confuse you. She's impossible to hear and refuses to change her lecturing style.  Exams are very, very tough but doable.  If you take this class, YOU will be teaching YOURSELF calculus.

Can't hear anything!! Doesn't clarify what she's writing on the board!! Learn from your teaching assistants and/or fellow classmates!! Jeez I knew calc 2 was hard to teach but I didn't know it was this bad!!
She is very confusing. she can't even speak with clarity. DONT take her class

Her lectures are very difficult to understand, and she does not always lecture or assign homework covering what ends up on the exams.  For me, the TA and Khan Academy got me through this class.  I would say her only plus side is she does offer some extra credit on some quizzes and other random things.  Maybe six cumulative points by end of term.
Could use to be more clear as to whats on the exams.

I dont know if she tries or not, and I feel bad just bad mouthing her incase she is trying but she isnt a good professor. She uploads her notes online which is nice but I never understand anything during lecture, let alone hear her and i sit in the 3rd row. She solves problems without much explanation, as if we have math degrees already.

Super quiet and doesn't use a microphone, so sit in the first row if you want to hear. Accent makes it impossible to understand as well. Rushes through material and does not explain it, though sometimes gives a half assed explanation. I had to withdraw from the course. I had just taken precalc and got a B so it wasn't because I was rusty.
I think she is a pretty good teacher.

I am extremely dissatisfied with the quality of education this teacher was providing to her students.  For one, she was not clear.  By this I mean that she constantly provided wrong answers to her lecture examples and did not speak up.  I did not feel comfortable learning from a teacher that could not make the most basic efforts to teach correctly.

She was an incredible professor and I enjoyed being challenged in class. She kept me engaged in class. Excited to step into class and discuss the reading as a class. I highly recommend her if you want a good challenge.

Gives very unclear directions on assignments. Never prepared for lectures despite course being lecture heavy. Extremely unresponsive to questions from students and even if she does answer, her responses are dismissive: either giving a vague answer or say "we'll talk about that in next class" only to never talk about it. DO NOT take her classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor is fair and thorough and gives helpful feedback. She has made me love policy, which I had not idea I'd like.

Professor Harmon-Darrow is pretty strict and organized. She expects a lot of her students (nothing unreasonable) but the positive is that you'll learn a lot. Lectures were sooo boring, though. Multiple hours of sitting and listening to her speak with little emphasis or excitement. Great teacher, just needs to work on lectures!
Had a great experience in this class! Knowledgeable of the material and passionate about the field of Social Work! Would definitely take a class again!

One girl in my class STILL didn't have her midterm graded even by the time of the final. Read straight off the powerpoint, rarely answered emails about questions on the material. ALSO doesn't believe in study guides. I got As on the paper, would've had an A in the class if she had provided some form of a study guide.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Gave us a list of content to study for exams, but none of it was on the exam. After being confronted about it by multiple students, it did not change. Unclear grading criteria and difficult material. Reads word for word from the powerpoints. Boring
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I took the thermo class with Prof. Romero over a year ago and enjoyed it. There is a lot to keep up with, but it got me ready for my first internship, and now on my way to my first job. I wish I could have taken the energy course as well.

I took this class last year and really enjoyed it. Some of the concepts were a bit hard to get, but really enjoyed learning about nuclear energy. Knowing about the topics discussed in class helped me get my first job.
The class was a lot of work but Prof. Talamas was fine teaching it.
I loved this class and totally recommend it to anyone that wants to learn about nuclear energy. The visit to the nuclear reactors was awesome!

I loved taking the energy class with Prof. Talamas, particularly the discussions of nuclear fission and fusion. I would recommend this class to anyone who wants to learn about different types of energy, in particular nuclear fusion. I applied to graduate school after taking this class.

I recently took this class and is one of the best classes I've ever taken. Prof. Talamas was very good at explaining the material, and I was always able to meet with him after class. I'm hoping to take the more advanced classes he teaches, and would recommend this professor to anyone that really wants to learn.

This professor is awful. He doesn't answer emails, grades harshly, and takes off points for anything. He rambles in lectures instead of teaching and doesn't tell you what you need to know for exams. Anyone praising has to get an internship with him. You will literally be teaching yourself thermodynamics. Most of the class was unsatisfied

As a whole, this professor wasn't that good at administering information. He does not follow the syllabus and would be chapters ahead of students during class, leaving them perplexed. His exams themselves weren't hard, but grading was very tough. He would give out pop quizzes which we were not forewarned about at the beginning of the semester.

Lectures can be confusing, but he more than makes up for it with how friendly the exams are. Questions are usually more conceptual. Although the syllabus said we had pop quizzes in class, that never happened, and you could realistically skip all the lectures and be just fine. The textbook will be your best friend for learning the material anyway.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr.  Romero-Talamas has been the most difficult professor I've had at UMBC. His grading was extremely harsh, and the expectations for assignments and exams were unclear. The graduate TA often came off as rude and dismissive when students asked questions. Overall, the course felt more like an obstacle than a learning experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The class is fine and the prof is understanding. He helped me find my first internship. More than other professors for sure!

Dr. Romero is not a good professor. He attacks the character of his students if they come to him for help or with concerns about the class. He is not very accessible outside of class and will not answer his emails. He rushes through all of the content.. He is not good about answering questions in class and will not look up from his tablet.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very ~okay~ professor. Weekly homework that isn't too hard and pretty short. Decent amount of studying. Exams and final make up 85% of your grade. Lectures are pretty easy to follow but get boring, consist of him answering problems or covering concepts from textbook, but does't upload notes. Gives lots of real world examples of content
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was super interesting and has helped me a lot, including during my first job interview (and helped me get a foot in the door!) I wish I could take it again, as I know the discussions are always updated. I definitely recommend it!

I would not recommend taking Dr. Romero. He is not very accessible outside of class and won't respond to emails. He is only here for his research and teaching seems to take a backseat for him. Doesn't provide resources whether that be lecture notes or other important resources. All example problems are from the answer key that he copies exactly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He does give partial credit in exams. The class and homework are pretty doable if you follow from the beginning. Going to office hours is always helpful if you're stuck.

This class is what I always thought a university level class should be. With proper lectures and assignments that actually teach something useful. If all you want is to get an easy grade without actually putting time in this class, then you should wait for someone else to teach the class.

The discussion lectures and extra sessions have been very helpful. They almost gave away the first two exams, which were easy, yet Prof. Talamas and the teaching assistants keep the class interesting and are always willing to help.

This prof was understanding when I needed a break due to a medical condition. I've enjoyed the lectures and have been to his office plenty of times. He's always very patient explaining the material. Those who complain about the lectures are usually the ones that never even attend the lectures or care to follow the material!

He's clearly not happy to be teaching, that's for sure. As a student who only really needs the bare minimum out of a teacher to learn effectively: clear instruction and explanation of the material, as well as correlation to the tests, he struggles to even do that. His passion for the subject lies within research, and he should've stuck to that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is actually pretty easy if you actually go to class and follow the material. The exams and assignment are also pretty easy if you spend a normal amount of time on them. The prof knows the material well. You just need to keep up and you'll be fine.

WORST PROFESSOR EVER!!! Gives no partial credit whatsoever on exams, even if there is one miniscule mistake. He doesn't know how to teach. Doesn't go into any detail while teaching and just assumes that the class knows everything. He has no respect for his students and doesn't care for their success. You have to learn from outside sources.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This professor was understanding when I was not able to attend the first exam. So far the lectures have been interesting, and he's accessible after class to answer questions.

This is one of the worst professors I have ever had. He does not know how to teach. He is not organized whatsoever. He does not go into any detail with any of his lectures. He comes late to class every day. I haven't been able to learn anything from him, all of what I have learned has been from youtube. No one in the class has learned anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you really want to learn thermodynamics, you definitely want to take this class. Makes class interesting and has plenty of real examples to use in the class.

I enjoyed this class and the discussions we had every day. I had to be absent for several days because of health reasons. The prof helped me catch up with the class and gave me the chance to submit overdue homework. He was always available to meet and he was very patient with me. I recommend this class to anyone that wants to learn about energy.

I enjoyed taking this elective with Prof. Talamas. We had to read and discuss articles everyday, and we covered a lot of material of different energy sources. The assignments were constant but not too hard. Nuclear energy was new for me, but I feel that I learned a lot about the issues and the technology.
Best class in my senior year! Classes are super interesting. I wish I had taken more classes with this prof!
A lot of material covered in this class, and sometimes hard to keep up with it. Much better to meet in person with this prof if you have questions, he knows his stuff.
Talamas is always willing to help inside and outside the classroom. You just need to reach out for help. Lots of assignments and quizzes, but not hard.

If you really want to learn thermo, take the class with Prof. Romero. If you do all the assignments and go to all discussion sessions, you will be fine. The exams are actually pretty easy if you did all the problems in class and discussion sessions. The quizzes sometimes are pretty random but they're not worth much.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I've enjoyed this class from the beginning. If you keep up with the reading and homework you'll be fine with this class. If you ask the prof. about thermo problems outside class, he'll work out the problems with you even if they are not the assigned problems (ask him about spacecraft!). The teaching assistants have also been super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: This is the best engineering class I've taken. Prof. Talamas really knows the material, and shows real life applications and examples. Grading is fair, but tons of reading and quizzes.
I mean he is a good person but suck at teaching. Just take Maria whenever you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Better to talk to 1-on-1 and is very nice, but during lectures he seems to read and draw diagrams word for word directly out of the book. If you write down the examples and study from that, you should be fine. He enjoys telling real life applications of concepts which is interesting but makes a hard class even harder reading directly from the book.
The lectures definitely need improvement, this teacher is a research guy and that is probably what he loves. Overall not horrible but without a curve you won't pass

Dr. Talamas is very accessible, you just need to ask for help! If you keep up with the class and assignments, the exams are pretty fair. There are quizzes every class but they're easy and not worth much, so if you miss one is not a big deal.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: One line, Don't do it gang. Take Sanchez, Carlos does a quiz everyday of class with no definitive understanding of what on, no study guides for quizzes or exams, structure of the lecture is clear but he USED CHALK in a lecture hall in 2022 so most of the class walks out after the mandatory test at the begin, that should tell you all for real.
if you ask him questions about your exams he will literally deduct points from questions you got correct.
Thermo is a required course and Prof. Romero-Talamas was great teaching it. Will definitely take another class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The professor is clearly interested in the material and cares about engaging the students with the material. Attending lectures isn't mandatory however if you do not go to them you will find it fairly difficult to interpret the text. Pacing of the class is fair, lots of reading with very few assignments. Lectures at times can be lengthy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: great professor! her personality is very chill, & the lectures are very thorough and if you pay attention, she made me really interested in learning philosophy and as an introduction to many interesting topics! most of the grades are based on the exams, grading can be sometimes strict but just takes notes, read, and go to class, you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her ~300 logic class was unsatisfying compared to what i took for computer science. Frankly, I wasn't moved by her lectures. Somewhat dubious grading. Accessible by email. The textbook is uninspiring, yet everything's straight out of it. When I took it, 4 homeworks, 4 midterm exams: Final (optional) is a redo exam of choice. Attendance mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I was scared to take her because of these reviews, but she wasn't bad. Nice professor, but a bit unorganized at times. Helpful and answered emails quickly. I didn't read the textbook like she said to, but I was able to get an A by attending the lectures and completing the practice problems. The tests were hard, but the textbook had harder problems.

PHIL 150: The absolute worst professor I've had at this university. Grading criteria is nonexistent, grades based on her own opinion. Compared answers with other students, had the exact same thing written, one loses half points while the other doesn't. Lectures are mandatory yapathons. Will tank your grade and gpa over the slightest loss of points.

She is a super nice person, but the lectures feel awkward and not engaging. I find many other students not even paying attention but attendance is mandatory. Attendance is like the only grade for the longest time too.

Probably the most boring professor amongst all at UMBC. Everything about her is boring:the way she speaks, the way she presents her lectures, the way she does literally anything, and the worst part is that she makes attendance mandatory. Basically only graded on 3 exams the entire semester, to which she grades them with no rubric ?? Don't take her.

I can see why students do not like her teaching ethic but I personally did I struggled in the beginning but progressively improved as the course went on. You really have to pay attention to understand this content and it adds on to each other kind of like math. Think of it like math but with language.

We were tested on 3 exams, attendance, and discussion posts. Exams are 90% of our grade. Class is an hour and fifteen minutes of boring lecture, and for the first 4 classes, she did not allow us to use laptops because she wanted us more in touch with the "regular" way to take notes. Bad professor, makes all content boring, and horrible grading
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Cassell somehow makes an insanely boring and convoluted topic even more difficult to follow. She hardly explains topics during class, instead opting to fly through slides. Homeworks are graded on "effort" and are graded out of 2 points, so if you don't "try" enough, you'll just get a 50%. The textbook does a better teaching job.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Cassel is not a good Professor at all!! First of all the class grade is soley based on 3 exams and the weight of each goes up every-time. Second she does not even grade them in a timely manner. Told to use the feedback from the past exam to do the next one, how can we do that if we cant even know what we did wrong.

reviews.comment: Nice professor and very knowledgeable. Interesting class, we read articles related to scientific reasoning. There were 3 take home exams which included essay type questions. Gave good feedback on exams. I would recommend taking this professor for this course.

reviews.comment: Interesting topics, lots of papers to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Caruso definitely comes off as a little intimidating to approach at first. He's pretty blunt with his input, but all of his advice was invaluable when there was a problem with our experiment and he was very encouraging as well! Exams weren't too hard, but don't underestimate them! There's only two and can make or break an A or B.

Can't tell who I hated more - this class or the professor. This man is so grumpy and the class is so difficult. Makes you do pointless presentations every week, completely useful and angry, and the exams are so difficult they don't even cover what he teaches during lecture. He's gives such bad explanation, and prep for exams

The instructor was funny in the lecture and helpful in the lab. The phage class was a lot of work, but most of the class got an A and almost everyone else got a B, so I don't think he's a tough grader. It was fun doing experiments, so if you want to do that kind of thing, it's a good choice. If you don't like research at all, maybe not for you.

Very passive aggressive both talking to him in person and via email, professor was funny during lecture, but was very rude in one on one conversations. Class was taught with Tracy Smith: There were no clear grading criteria on lab reports, exams were extremely difficult, and lab reports made up the most of the grade and were graded extremely late.

reviews.comment: Good class to take if you like wet lab type of stuff. Professor gets grumpy sometimes and comes off as rude. Tough grader but not the worst professor ever. I recommend the course and the prof isn't terrible. I took him again for the spring semester and it was fine. Attendance is mandatory. Participation in art is also mandatory, but that's expected
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He's a good professor and very accommodating but he has a short temper. DO NOT take phage hunters (unless you're good with lab) as it's very disorganized & takes a lot of work outside class. 1 TA is extremely helpful. Exams are based on lecture slides & paper but u need to remember details. I highly recommended taking regular lab
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I do not like this professor at all. He is very micro aggressive and rude. I barely even passed this course and the whole phage format was hell on earth. Please take the spring version of the lab but just not with this prof

I would not retake a class with this professor. He is rude and I do have a weird micro aggressive exchanges with him. The exams are tough and detailed so make sure you don't study at the last minute. Too much reading and the lectures aren't helpful one bit

I had a terrible time taking this class. TA's were awful and no help at all. The professor was nice but hard to reach out to sometimes. The exams were very difficult and had no idea how to prepare for them. Also need to take a bunch of outside time in class to prepare for things. Very work heavy and should be higher than 2 credits.

Labs required LOTS of outside scheduled lab time so be prepared for that. Quizzes are easy and I love my TA's! It was draining at first because my phage keeps failing but eventually it got better. Midterm was not bad at all, but the final exam is something else so be prepared for that also! Lots of T/F questions, questions about readings, etc.

I thought he was pretty okay. In comparison to other professors in bio, 10/10. He can be a little rude though. the class has a lot of paper you have to read and KNOW. Our midterm and final were mainly about the papers we read in INCREDIBLE DETAIL. it kicked our behinds. The TAs grade most of the stuff but for exams its hard to be fully prepared
I do not like this professor. I can't ask him anything he's so unapproachable and rude. The tests are hard and his grading is annoying. He barely also curves

The class is all over the place and he does not prepare you for exams at all. I didn't even know what to study and the study guide he gives is only somewhat useful. He forced  weekly presentations and forces you to come outside lab. He's unapproachable and the ta are useless  so you're pretty much screwed if you need help

This professor made the lab so engaging and enjoyable! The exams required real understanding, not memorization, and TAs did the gradings. The presentations, though kind of made me anxious, built my confidence and made me feel like a scientist. Stay on top of tasks, and an A is achievable!
There are plenty of ways to earn points, just get them done!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The ta does all the grading which tends to be pretty easy grader. You must look over syllabus for the quizzes which aren't easy and exams are VERY difficult so you have to use the study guide and memorize every topic. He is in fact unapproachable and has an attitude from time to time but generally is a nice guy.

Exams were harder than predicted. Cares a lot and is passionate about this topic. Can be sassy sometimes. Overall funny guy, but can go on and on during lectures. Most of the grading is done by TA. Prepare to come into lab outside of scheduled time OFTEN.

This class has sparked genuine scientific curiosity, thanks to Dr, Caruso's chill vibe and infectious enthusiasm. 

Lab is online via Labster. Take this class instead of the water class!!

Great professor. He might seem tough at first, but if you talk to him, he's pretty understanding and sensible.  The class was really interesting, though his lectures go on a little long.  There's a lot of major deadlines in and out of lab, but if you pay attention in lecture, you'll be fine.  Be prepared to come to lab outside of scheduled time.
His lectures were honestly very interesting and he was always very helpful during the labs.

Prof.Caruso restored my faith in UMBC's Biology department. After taking BIOL141 w/ Feeser, I was ready to drop Biology as my major. He was helpful & clear when answering questions, lectures were organized and easy to follow. He cares about individual students and wants everyone to succeed. He's passionate about the topic & grades work quickly.

The professor was friendly and approachable to help students. Whoever said his exams were fair they definitely were not. They are very tough and hard to study for. You need to pay very close attention to details in lectures and labs to get a good grade. Quizzes although tough are easier than the exams
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Caruso is a professor who is very passionate about his work, which in turn made you feel passionate about the class. This class was adjusted into a bioinformatics format (more like 316L) for the pandemic. As long as you went to class, you would be fine. A lot of work outside of class though. The final was difficult, but it was curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: The lab was adjusted so it is more bioinformatics. I understand the pandemic made labs different, but at least let us know before signing up for a bioinformatics lab instead of genetics. Final was the absolute worst. I had an A all semester and caruso tested us on the SMALLEST details of the semester. TAKE AFTER THE PANDEMIC ENDS, NOT WORTH IT.

He has a very different personality in class and during his office hours. He's very engaging and clear in class. If your the type of student who plans on coming to his office, do not take any of his classes. He is very disrespectful and annoyed when students come in for help.

He's a good guy. Taking BIOL 109 as a winter course is definitely more fun than Science of Water, but the content can be a bit more difficult if you're not STEM-oriented/experienced. The class content isn't hard and he makes things easy to understand. Bonus points if you're into bears I guess.

Dr. Caruso is a good Professor. In this class, he teaches students how to do scientific research independently. To me, this was amazing because I could work at my own pace and be responsible for my own experiments. Also, be prepared to write a scientific research paper over the entire semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dr. Caruso makes this class as close to a real life lab experience as it can get. You do have to come to class outside of regular class hours, but its likely you wont have to stay the whole time during your class. You also have to buy a poster at the end of the class, but you don't have to buy a text book. One of the best classes I've taken.

Dr. Caruso gives very engaging lectures for lead-offs. He is very funny! However, he can do a better job at explaining the rationale behind protocols in lab. His exams are tough! Make sure you know EVERYTHING. Although hes overall a nice guy, he can have his moments where he isnt too friendly and is intimidating to approach for questions.

Really nice, hilarious and knowledgable. Labs weren't bad and you often leave early. Have to come into lab outside of lab time to check on plates.  It's imperative you read the articles he assigns-key points will appear on quizzes and exams. Exams are all free response and T/F based on data analysis, protocol rationale, and the assigned readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Caruso is an awesome professor and he even gave us the PDF for the lab manual. Yes, you have to come in outside of lab time to succeed, but he doesn't ask you to spend an unreasonable amount of time there. He is a fair grader, funny man, and very knowledgable about any errors you may run into!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr Caruso is very helpful and organized . He is very clear on what you have to do . He is willing to answer your question . I think he is on of the best instructor in the Bio department at umbc

Dr. Caruso is very clear and informative. If you want to pass, you should attend every lecture and lab and TAKE LOTS OF NOTES. His lectures are engaging- he answers student questions & will re-explain if you don't understand a concept. Overall, an excellent professor! (he also has a sense of humor- he made a Game of Thrones reference in our final)

Show up to lecture and pay attention and you may not even have to read the book. I slacked off towards the end of the course but Still got a B. Reading the book helps clarify and reinforce whats said in lecture or vice versa. Easiest Bio class ive taken at umbc hands down

Dr. Caruso makes you earn your grade. His tests are hard, but not unreasonable. If you understand all the labs really well, either by reading them before lecture, or going into office hours, and not skipping labs, you will get a B for sure. Monday lab couldn't get as much help as the other labs, because lecture is Friday.

Dr. Caruso is a nice guy and is pretty approachable.  If you need help from him, it's your responsibility to get it.  His exams were difficult but fair.  The lab (Phage Hunters) requires you to make time outside of class to come in but it's pretty rewarding to see one experiment come to fruition.  I got an A, but I didn't skimp at all.
Great lecturer but writes frustrating tests like the others said. He told us there would be no curve so people dropped but THEN gave a 7% curve! Take his class but be prepared to fight on his tests.

He is seriously one of the best biology professor at UMBC. He actually teaches and you learn a lot from him. I admire him a lot and I know i would of gotten a better grade if I had studied a little better for the exams.

WARNING!let me tell you, he was ridiculous.If you want to play logic games,I recommend you take his class.his tests get harder each time like different levels in a game. they are extremely tricky and he wasn't very helpful.I have a name for him "trick master".on the exam, all his options are the same but if you pick the wrong answer, its GAME OVER.
Approachable and helpful. Difficult material, but uses an inexpensive lab manual (~$7) instead of an expensive textbook.

Not helpful when I visited him in his office plus he is disrespectful. I guess you do not have any choice since he is the only 302L teacher at UMBC. He made 302L hard. Ask TA questions that you don't understand, but not him. Do not seek help from him.
Great teacher! First biology teacher I've had at umbc that was willing to teach and chat during class. He lectured from powerpoint slides that he posted and he was as clear as could be.
I should have known better, you should know better also. Run away.

A full-time lecturer, and it shows! The best professor I've ever had. Actually enjoys answering questions. Take advantage of his helpfulness, especially if you have him in your actual lab section (usually Monday). A midterm and final are the only exams, but there are weekly quizzes, which are not hard. Make sure to prepare for lab ahead of time.

The "textbook" is a cheap lab manual that has crucial information for how to do the labs. It's also available as a pdf. A lot of the stuff is very intuitive. The Arabinose lab is extremely complicated. Out of the 6 or so you do, that's the hardest. The fruit fly simulations are all theory--and done with pen, paper and computer. Very stimulating.

I took a couple of classes from him for Bio. He is very helpful, fair and nice. I think he is better as a higher level class teacher though, because he wants you to ask informed questions, of course, as freshmen, we always expect the teacher to say what we want to know before looking in the book :) He is a good person who loves what he does.

Good professor but didnt like the teaching technique with the team based learning. It was hard  though. Have to work hard over all and do alot on your own. Exams were also very hard after the first one.

He's very cheerful and really knows his stuff. He's helpful and intelligent and presents everything you need to know very clearly. I only did poorly because I got a stomach virus and missed a key section of the class. So, when you get into the gene sequencing, don't miss any related classes or labs at any cost!

I had him for bio109 and we learned pointless crap and did pointless labs the class reminded me once again why non major lab science classes were pointless to take... Half the class hated him half got along with him he i personally hated him

Very good teacher. Respects students that come to learn and put effort forward. Was always willing to help during his office hours, never made you feel bad for misunderstanding material. Overall A grade teacher!
Upstandish when I visited in office hours last year. Not very clear either.
His interest in the subject makes him a really great lecturer.

Good lecturer. Poor exam maker. Ask questions if there is a problem on the exam that confuses you, and he'll try to steer you to the right answer. The book was useless so I wouldn't buy it. Overall the class was fine and there was a really nice curve.

Professor over simplifies lecture material and then asks complicated exam questions. Asks questions like 'one of the above, two of the above, all, none'. The tests increase in difficulty after each time. THe book is completely useless. Overall, I got a C, but I really had to struggle and study hard!

the class is very difficult. memorize the lecture slides because a lot of his questions are straight recall. Read the book as it will have info on his exams that arentfrom lecture notes. Stressful but there is a nice curve at the end. 84 for an A, 71 for a b, 54 for a C in my year. Each exam is harder than the one before so do well in the beginning

He is a very funny lecturer and does his best to keep the class's interest because it is 2 hours long. Approachable and has videos/pictures to demonstrate difficult concepts. Only downside is the exams get harder every  single time and quite tricky.
He's ok. Decent lecturer but his tests are really difficult. You need to study your ass off just to get a B or C.

really great professor. his exams are difficult, but if you argue your point, he sometimes changes the answer key. very helpful, and very funny, i would highly suggest taking him.  dont need the book, just memorize his slides and you'll do good on his exams...

AMAZING professor! very clear and has a good sense of humor. Shows old exams which helps alot. Only thing is, that he one time went on a rant about how there was so much evidence against intelligent design. It was apparent what his opinion was about creation vs. evolution and i think that it shouldnt have been brought up at all.

he explains things clearly. He know's how to teach very well and knows the material extremely well. I had a good learning experience in his class. I'd take him again. I think he's better than most of the biology professors here.

Dr. Caruso is very arrogant.  He takes pride of having his Phd in Genetics.  He thinks that he knows everything.  His tests are very hard, he called his test "Lecture Test," that means you dont have to read the text but in actuality you do.  His lectures are extremely boring.  He writes his notes for 2 hours everday. He makes Genetics boring.
Ugh.

Very good professor! Made genetics fun and interesting. Don't need to read the book at all, just go to his lectures and take good notes and you will pass. All exams are based on what he says in class! Def. take Genetics with Caruso!

Okay teacher. Can get off topic.  At the beginning of the semester was very helpful, but towards the end wasn't as helpful. He never answered my emails, or if he did, it is a week or two later. He doesn't thoroughly explain what course material is going to be on the exams.

Took a 30-45 min lecture and made it last 75 mins every week. He knows no matter how many times he says something people will still mess it up so he repeats things again and again, which is lousy for the people who get it the first time. Other than that the labs are straightforward and easy. Take the quizzes seriously - you'll really help yourself

I dont know what the first two people are talking about. I am AWFUL when it comes to science and I was so nervous about taking a science class but I ended up getting a B in the class and that too after I slacked off for a bit. My exam grades weren't all that but I did well in the EASY labs. TAKE THIS CLASS FOR YOUR GFR
Good teacher. Much better than the Water course.

Bad teacher. Me and my roomate honestly had everything we ever did in lecture totally covered and got C's on the exam. His exam did not belong in our class. My TA even told me they thought the exam was "BS" thankfully the TA did their best to make up for his unfairness with kind lab grades. Caruso you are a JOKE.

Its a fair amount of material covered in a short period of time but he does it well. I can handle science courses fairly well so I may be bias to the other non-majors. This class is a good pick but dont expect an easy A. Show up, and for your own sake study a little every week for the quizes. The exams are pretty tough but you'll manage.
hilarious guy and friendly.  easy teaching style and is comprehensive.  MUCH friendlier and easier to talk to, and overall, a better teacher than Sandoz.  definitely a high priority guy to take

Before taking this class, I heard great things about Caruso. Naturally, the class got increasingly more difficult, but at an insane extent. We were doing 300 level work (cloning) even though we weren't bio majors. Despite being a 100 level course, the class avg was 57% on the final. Take sci 100. Your graed will thank you.

Caruso is a professor I would take again. He has a sense of humor, is laid back, doesn't kill on exams, and makes lectures bearable, if not enjoyable. My only critique is that sometimes he talked as though he was talking down to us. A professor worth taking! You'll probably enjoy him!

Very good teacher. Does a good job explaining hard concepts. Makes lectures engaging and interesting. Very approachable, and always willing to help. You should take him instead of Sandoz for lab, because he is a better teacher, even though his class is harder and you do twice as much.
Great teacher, tough grader.

Funny, engaging in lectures, and made difficult concepts seem simple. A bit hard to approach one on one, as he seemed always busy with so many people in his class. I actually found the labs confusing, but this had more to do with the incoherency of the TA

Very good teacher! Very helpful when I had questions outside of class. Also gave very good lectures that made genetics a lot easier to understand. Also ver interested about subject and knows a lot. Very easy to get in touch with (around alot) and leniant.
funny guy, tries his hardest to make concepts clear. willing to help at all times, but sometimes can get a little moody. still very approachable. says hi to me on campus outside of lab

material was easy enough, sometimes quizzes were kind of tough. easy labs and he gave interesting lectures. he could be kind of abrupt when you asked questions one on one. great for nonmajors needing a lab.
Good teacher, interesting class.
The material is somewhat hard but he makes a good effort.  Very student Oriented
Cool guy.  Material is kinda hard but he's a good teacher.

This professor wasn't difficult by any means. The main assignments in this class at 4 exams and quizzes. I would say to be on top of quizzes due to their grade importance. The professor was fine and she did try her best I'd like to say. If anything I believe more discussions would be beneficial instead of simple slide show lectures.

This course was not easy and you need to study to do well. However if you find the right study methods you will be able to earn an A. She also offers many extra credit assignments and test retakes so you are set up for success.
The class is really easy if you do all the work on time - Read the chapters and you will come to lectures prepared. Her lectures aren't that exciting but she is nice as a prof.

The course is okay, the professor/TA isn't that helpful. If you miss even 2 out of the 11 quizzes, your grade suffers tremendously- no exceptions or excuses. She has guided notes that you can teach yourself from. Should do great as long as you stay on top of the quizzes and spend as much time as you can studying

I found the professors teaching method ineffective, if I didn't already have a background in ABA I would've failed this class because the lectures are unhelpful and I don't have time to teach myself so much material in such little time. 
The exams are tricky, but luckily the tests are open note. 2-3 extra credit opportunities

Lectures don't really give you anything that reading the textbook doesn't and she posts the slides anyways. The class is really easy overall, but if you miss a quiz or two your grade is basically irrecoverable unless you do the small extra credit opportunities given which only help on the brink of a letter grade. very nice prof and lab opportunity

Had her for the Fall semester. Very boring lectures, literally could teach myself. You can have multiple attempts on the quizzes. She offers you guided notes if you ask. Overall easy class, but very boring to go to.
She isn't flexible at all with her deadlines, no matter what the reason may be. Droning lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She gives you the chance to get the easiest A because she takes the quiz questions out of the textbook and exam questions out of the lectures. She lectures by guided notes and emphasizes the exam being based on such. The only downside is either her or the TA, who make multiple mistakes on the answer key for some exams. Overall an easy class.

GREAT professor for Spanish 201. He cares about students and wants them to try their best. He gives lots of opportunities for students to succeed: homework, in-class participation, small projects, and exams. Together, as long as you try, these lead to a fun finish to your language requirement. He has realistic expectations for students.

Carmody is very understanding, a great professor overall. However, make sure you stay on top of your work. Once you miss something it is closed so be sure you know how to navigate the course work, textbooks and always communicate with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: extremely unbearable workload and poor communication skills

Professor Carmody was an excellent professor for SPAN 201! He was very lenient with grading and always made sure you understood the content well. He understood that I was juggling a lot for my senior year spring semester. I would recommend him to anyone needing to take SPAN201 for a required GEP. Especially all bio majors!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: i literally suck at spanish so bad and was so scared to take this class but he makes it a breeze, its literally hard to fail. such a sweet and considerate person overall too. u wont regret taking his class

Took this in Spring 2024. Prof. is a very nice man and explains all the concepts in class as best as he can. He is always willing to help and listen to questions. The class itself has a ton of homework and quizzes, so make sure to stay on top of your work. Start it as early as possible! Besides that, he's great. If you can take his class, do it!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Carmody is such a sweet guy. He's accessable outside office hours and through email. Lots of assignments online, with a writing paper and written final (only on chapters 4-6). There's an oral exam, which he provides questions for and makes it very comfortable. He's super sweet overall!

One of my favorite professors at this school. He does a lot of group work and wants the class to get involved. The only down side of this class is the amount of homework assigned. However, he will grant you extensions within reason.

He was a great professor - my favorite at UMBC. You could tell he really cared about his students and was more interested in making sure you learned versus getting everything right. He gave extensions to any student who needed them and was very funny and charismatic.

Prof. Carmody is a very down to earth guy. His class is homework heavy, but he's always willing to give extensions when needed. He's a non-native speaker, which made learning easier imo. He helps students thoroughly prepare for exams in class. He made this course, which I was dreading, actually tolerable and kinda fun. Would def recommend him.

Professor is amazing - he teaches Spanish in such a stress-free way. He's very lenient in class and very understanding as a person - you can tell he wants you to enjoy learning Spanish. 10/10 experience. The only con is 201 has lots of material, so the workload is decently heavy, and the automatic grading system is a pain (not his fault).
I had a great experience taking Prof. Carmody's course. The lectures were extremely engaging and really helped me process the material.
Gave good feedback, and a balanced amount of assignments.

He's an amazing Professor. I love his lectures. He is very understanding and gives extensions on assignments. Also is willing to reopen a past-due assignment. The amount of hw is a lot, but bearable. Time manage. Make sure to study. Would take it again!

Prof. Carmody is probably the best bet for a Spanish prof at UMBC as he's a non-native speaker. However, he's extremely difficult to get in touch with, which is super annoying. He is very understanding and flexible if you need extra time. This class is just a lot of work and will suck regardless of whose teaching thanks to the Spanish department.

Professor Carmody was one of the best professors I have had here at UMBC. He is very charismatic and interesting to listen to. His course work is decently heavy, but he is very understanding if you need an extension or help. His lectures are laid back and fun. He helped grow my interest in Spanish which I am now pursuing as a secondary study.

Professor Carmody's Spanish 201 class was very heavy on homework, but it slows down towards the end of the semester. He understands that he puts a lot on his students and is always willing to extend student deadlines. His lectures really allow students to ask questions and prepare for written/vocal exams. He is a great professor!

Prof. Carmody is a very good professor, Attendance is mandatory but going to class is very important because if he sees that you are there every class and participating he's willing to give you better grades in his class. He's a very lenient and understanding professor so if you work with him he'll work with you.

Prof. Carmody was a great professor and an overall great person. Learning another language is difficult but he did his very best to make it bearable. The class is homework heavy and tests are hard but if you participate and complete all the assignments you should be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I had Prof. Carmody Fall 2022 semester. He made this class as painless as he possibly could. He's clear, understanding, and pretty funny. There are two big exams, worth 18% of your grade but if you do well on homework it will even things out. I failed every quiz and still passed. Heavy workload! There are also two easy speaking exams. Take Carmody!

Professor Carmody was extremely accessible and helpful throughout the course, though there was a pretty solid chunk of online homework, it helped prepare for class. The in-class activities were always enjoyable and I never felt like going to class was a chore. Great prof
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The subject matter was difficult to digest in a short period of time but he did a great job explaining it and trying to help you understand. Homework assignments had unlimited attempts so you could find the right answer and writing feedback was clear.
Professor Carmody makes the tough subject matter involved in this course easy. He works with his students so that they can succeed. I highly recommend taking him.
He was the best part about an otherwise difficult class. Very nice and approachable, and always willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a funny professor and allows a hard course to feel easy even though there is a lot of homework but if you manage your time you can get it done. The tests and quizzes are hard and you need to memorize a lot of concepts. Overall it is not bad.

Carmody is the best Spanish professor at UMBC. 201 is not an easy class, but somehow he made it bearable. The workload is heavy in the 1st half of the semester, but it slows down in the 2nd half. Just show up, participate, and do the work, and he'll grade leniently. If you fail his class, it's because you're lazy. He's also a genuinely nice person.

Loved taking spanish with Carmody. I literally do not know any Spanish and i was pissed umbc makes it a requirement. He made it as painless as possible. 2 oral exams. 1 final. Modules every week, HW, and a group project. I took winter session

I was barely able to get into his Spanish 201 course and I am so glad I switched to his class. He is a great teacher. If you have a chance to take him for any Spanish course then I would pick him over everyone else. For any Spanish course, the workload is going to be a lot. He makes it more doable and is very understanding if you ever need help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Taking SPAN201 was A LOT of work. Me and a majority of students considered dropping the course because of the work load Professor Carmody gave. But, I managed to pass with an A. I advise everyone to complete homework on time. He is a great professor and I learned a lot from his course. I recommend taking him but beware of the workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He was honestly the most understanding and caring professor I've ever had. While there is a lot of homework, he does release it early and you can get it done ahead of time. Most of the grades are for projects and oral examinations and he's super understanding so you won't fail the class at all! Absolutely loved having prof. Carmody!!

I was really worried about taking SPAN 201, as I hadn't taken a Spanish class in 5 years beforehand, but Professor Carmody made it as painless as possible. He was a very generous grader and a really nice person. Some people complain about the Homework, but that's out of his control, and is part of the curriculum he has to abide by.

Carmody is a great professor that tries his best to make an insanely difficult class bearable. If you show up, ask questions, do your homework, and just generally TRY, you'll do fine, and he'll be lenient when grading your quizzes and exams. if you don't, you'll fail and deserve it. He's very understanding, flexible, and a genuinely nice person.

I think the professor is great at teaching Spanish. His lectures are informative and he does a good job making sure we absorb the information. I wasn't a fan of the class itself. The workload is heavy even for a summer class, the tests are VERY hard and require a lot of memorization and they require Proctorio, which is an instant negative to me.
Carmody requires Proctorio. Offers no alternatives. Take SPAN 201 with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I was dreading SPAN201, but somehow Prof Carmody made it bearable. He's a non-native speaker and a grad student, so he really understands his students and is always willing to help and answer questions. Tons of homework and group projects, but his lectures are helpful and the assignments are clearly explained.

The class consists of quizzes, a midterm and final, compositions, group projects and homework assignments. The homework assignments are easy if you use the vocabulary from the book to help you. The grammar homework assignments are not hard if you pay attention in class and to the videos.

Prof. Carmody is a great professor! Took his class Spring 2020 and he handled the transition to online classes very well! Always is happy to answer any questions that you have. Makes assignment guidelines clear the majority of the time. Also since he is not a native Spanish speaker, I felt like he was very understanding if you were struggling!

Awesome dude. He really cares about his students and will help you succeed as long as your willing to put in the work. He's a REAL teacher - meaning he has the ability to teach someone a language instead of just lecturing. Extra credit opportunities are available if you struggle on exams/homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: It was a hard class but professor Carmody is a very nice and caring professor. he is great at teaching. You just have to study hard and complete all the homework assignments. He is also very lenient!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you are taking Spanish at UMBC, make sure you enroll in his class. He is a very reasonable person and is a student himself so he is very lenient about things! I wish I took him in Spanish 101 & 102. I always got a B in those classes because the professors wanted perfection. Sean Carmody understands you're learning so he's not harsh at grading!

I only rate when Profs. are either amazing or terrible. Carmody is by far the best 201 Prof. A language course is intimidating, but he is a non-native Spanish Prof. who is very lenient throughout the course. Lots of online homework, but do all of them & you will pass. 2 major exams but he prepares you well. 3-4 Group Projects to keep your grade up.
Prof, Carmody is very patient with everyone, easy to reach. The textbook and homework is online, I hated that part, but Prof. Carmody offers opportunities for extra credit.

The best foreign language teacher on campus, bar none. Professor Carmody really cares about his students and will do everything in his power to make sure you at least get a 'C'. Three easy group projects, homework that has a check work function, two tests but many extra credit opportunities. He's always available for office hours if you need help.
The most annoying thing about this class is that we had four group projects. Sean Carmody is a super lax grader though. As long as you do all the homework assignments youll be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Take Professor Carmody's class if you want to pass Spanish 201 with a good grade. The best Spanish professor at UMBC. He is very understanding and can actually teach Spanish. English is his first language so he knows how to teach Spanish. Makes sure you do all of your work and you will pass this class.
He has no organization what so ever... kinda seems like he's winging it. His due dates are a little everywhere and are really hard to keep track of. Not a fan.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I do not like speaking Spanish, but it seems like the most relevant language to learn so I took Spanish 101 and 201 with Professor Carmody (who is VERY cute). He is very fair with tests and grades. Make sure to participate in class and always have your textbook.

Professor Carmody is great. He's always there to answer questions and to help you along the course. He is also forgiving. If you weren't able to submit an assignment online by the due date, he usually is very lenient about it. However, obviously, do not make it a habit. He is very approachable, patient, never gets angry, so please take him.

Prof. Carmody is a good teacher. 201 was the first Spanish class I've taken since my sophomore year of high school and I didn't have much of a problem. Pay attention in class and do the activities he gives out, and you'll learn fairly quickly. Lots of homework, but it's pretty easy overall. Tests were fair, he makes it clear what will be on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Prof. Carmody is a great teacher. He likes to make jokes and makes it easy to learn. If you miss class, he's good about letting you make up work. The calendar of assignments can be confusing, just make sure to remember your grade depends on the group work. He is a bit disorganized with due dates so just ask him if he's not clear.

He does not design this course and is therefore not responsible for that mess. However, does a good job with what the department makes him teach. You basically teach yourself Spanish from a book in this class which can be super challenging.  Wish UMBC would use the communicative approach to Spanish.

Super nice guy. Lots of good stories. He knows the language well. Isn't the best teacher.. he'll answer specific questions when you ask, but teaches straight out of the book with no further elaboration. Doesn't respond to e-mails, seems too busy to teach. REALLY easy on the eyes.

Carmody is super cool! Fun guy and very into Spanish. He isn't very good at reminding you about due dates so be sure to stay on top of everything. He is a little fast paced. I think sometimes he forgets we don't speak Spanish, but he is very helpful when you ask questions.

Friendly professor and easy to talk to but he does not explain anything or actually teach you. Everything you learn is right out of the book. Never remembers due dates and hardly responds to emails.  Cool professor but not a great teacher

You read straight for the book, and do all the activities from the book. He is funny and entertaining, but not as helpful as I wish he could have been. he gets confused about his own assignments. 2 online homeworks a week, 2 oral exams, tests/quizzes weren't too difficult,  2 chats that were easy. Good amount of work, not hard, just time consuming

His classwork/homework outline is very confusing and when you ask him questions about due date or details he never knows. He does not explain things in class or teach really. All we do is all of the book work with partners and he does not elaborate on the answers when we go over them. He's always lost or confused about his own classwork/homework
The class was always fun because of the way he interacted with the students, he is easy to approach and tries his best to help you stay on track. His tests and  exams were easy.

Very good professor! He is very flexible and is aware that not everyone is a professional when it comes to speaking spanish. As long as your try he pretty much passes you. His exams and quizes are not a surprise. Everything he teaches you are on them. I would def recommend taking him. Easy passing grade. I am not good at spanish so glad i took him.
I took this class about two years ago, best professor there so far. Chill, upbeat, and knowledgeable of Spanish language and culture (his wife is hispanic/latina. Great prof, would highly recommend!

Wow. Only way to describe, if not the best teacher here, definitely one of them. Outlines what's going to be on quizzes/exams. Let's you ask translations during exams if it's not directly related to material. ONLY complaint is the grading. His lack of TA makes you get things back very late. Other than that, couldn't be better. TAKE HIS CLASS!!!!!!!

More work than I was expecting but a fairly easy A. Easy to focus in class, he's upbeat and relatable. Very helpful. Work consists of 5 quias, 3 chats, and 2 responses online (all outside class) and 6 quizes, 2 writing exams, 2 oral exams, and 2 cummalitive exams (all in class)
Great teacher. Easy going,nice, interested in students learning.  I would take him again.
Please take this guy, he is so chill and down to earth, an excellent instructor, and an all around excellent teacher!
Sean is the best

He is very helpful and nice. His class isn't hard and his test are okay. The hardest part of the exams are the listening section but he replays them as much as you need. Very approachable and understanding. One of my favorite professors.

He is very helpful and easy going. The 1st few weeks he will speak in english, after that its str8 spanish and he has no problems explaining or answering Q's, so dont hesitate. All in all, he's very approachable, easy going, and very helpful if you ask. His assignments are fairly ez as well. Great Spanish teacher!
Really nice guy and great teacher. Not strict at all and is understanding if you say things wrong or give incorrect responses.

Awesome professor. He's really friendly and approachable--one of the best in the department. He's an overall nice guy who has a great sense of humor and loves to teach. Prof. Carmody's youth is definitely an asset because he relates well to the students. Take his class! You won't regret it!
This guy is a boss. He will help students and give extra credit, even though he says he won't at the beginning of class. A teacher you MUST take if your learning spanish.
Awesome and friendly. Best Spanish teacher I had.

One of the best professors I've ever had. He speaks fluent Spanish and does a great job in teaching it. He relates to the students and will not hesitate to help anyone that doesn't understand the material. An effective teacher that is easy to talk to. Highly recommended.

An awesome professor. He's super laid back but effective, though it's an introductory class he uses spanish 98% of the time. But he always makes sure that we understand, and tries to help us. He's also pretty funny and easy on the eyes. I definitely recommend him. One thing; he's strict about no phones.

He made learning Spanish seem effortless. After the first couple of chapters he will stop using English all together, but if you don't understand and ask what he's saying, he'll draw on the board or make gestures to try and help you understand.  Awesome teacher, definitely recommend.

Great proff.  he loves spanish and trys to make it fun in every class. the only problem is that on quiz/test he will give u points off if u spell stuff wrong. so make sure u practice spelling the words. and study vocab. rest is easy.

I love Dr. Cella. She means super well and always wants what is best for her students. If needed, she will extend deadlines if you communicate with her. She values effort and honesty and wants what is best for her students. She's the best!
Dr. Cella is friendly, flexible, and funny. She wants to see you succeed, and her musicianship classes are relaxed and semi-informal.
