reviews.comment: I see all these rating and unfortunately its TRUE, I've had a Terrible experience. Doesn't reply to emails, gets irritated when you ask questions, and talks down to students. He is very very RUDE, One of the worst instructors I've had, Idk who hired this man as a Prof. Paul shud b FIRED tbh. Pls avoid this man if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Paul.C, is very unresponsive to emails and does'nt handle student questions well. When students ask for help or clarification, he often reacts with frustration or sarcasm, which creates an uncomfortable learning environment. It felt very unprofessional, and it made it hard to succeed in the class. I would recommend avoiding this course if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was hybrid but we never met in person until the final exam. The group project rubric was so unclear and vague, then he started to take off points because we didn't put comments in the right places. Mind you, we added comments when suitable. I barely learned anything from his lectures. Shout out to Udemy fr.

self-taught class cuz you meet every other week. expects you to code what he barely taught. Very few things in the grade: hws, 3 discussions, 2 exams, and a group project; not much room to struggle. project rubric was unclear. revealed the final date just a week before it occurred. don't have a strong java foundation? expect to struggle
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is essentially self taught unless you are extremely proficient in Java I would not recommend this class. Homeworks can take hours, exam are extremely difficult and he is incredibly boring to listen to during the lectures. The final project is also extremely unclear and difficult. Likely one of the worst professors in the entire IS dept.

This class should basically count as a self taught course considering while you do meet virtually he expects a lot from the assignments even if you have barely gone over it in class. I tried to set up an office hours with him because I needed help and he never responded. I went to IS147 tutoring for hw and he still marks it as wrong. Don't take.

tldr: RUN

if yall are struggling and are weak coders, don't take this prof. the set up for this class is alternating asynch and online. he goes through a billion slides, doesnt really teach, makes u code, and expects u to learn. if yall cant learn by yourself (and be honest), look elsewhere

Worst Java Prof. He never reviews anything before a quiz. He piles topics on top of topics and then expects you to do assignments on topics he has not taught. This is not an introductory class, especially with the way this professor teaches. We felt like we were teaching ourselves Java. He takes points for anything! Extremely confusing!

save yourself - passing this class will be a labor of love. Prof seems like a good guy but he's a meh professor because he's hard to get a hold of outside of class and the assignments can be confusing. He's specific about grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's nice inside class but he is verrryyyy rigid when it comes to grading. Expect a chunk points off on your assignment over miniscule errors or details. It is hard to succeed in his class, but possible if you grind. He will also randomly cancel lecture or do async with little to no update sometimes, but it is to be expected as an older gentleman.
His grading policy isn't clear. he doesn't take attendance but being in class is important. he is okay but  VERY TOUGH GRADER.
The class was okay.

The class and concept are hard if you have no experience in coding but he tries his best to make it understandable. He is very nice and encouraging to have you participate. He is also good at explaining and giving real-life examples. Half of your grade is weekly HWs, the other half is 4 (online and open note) quizzes and one group project.

Great professor for IS 147. I was not familiar with Java before, but he taught this as a great Intro class. Homework was not difficult to complete and hes a lenient grader. Quizzes were short, open book/open note, and fairly easy if you review the material. One final project, but it is not too bad if you have an idea of what you're doing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The class is challenging and you get to hands-on learn Python and PHP, but the professor is an absolute jerk. If you miss one assignment (during a pandemic!), you will be criticized as having a poor approach to graduate school, along with a bunch of other unprofessional "advice." He then makes errors and recycles old material. Nice approach...

Terrible professor for an online class. You learn everything from w3schools and the rest of the internet. Also makes you do a group project despite it being an online class so get used to working with random strangers who will work on a completely different schedule than you since this is an online class and they're traveling.

Weekly assignments are practical and instructive. Course materials are all online and a bit disorganized. It's easy to miss something important. Keep in mind that the two exams (a midterm and a final) account for a large portion of your grade, are very terminology-heavy and don't directly relate to the weekly assignments.

If you're just starting to learn how to code, take this professor. All his quizzes are open note and the project is with a partner. If you need help, he will assist you until you understand. He's an amazing professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is the best Java instructor at UMBC. If you have the option, take it with him.

Comitz is one of my favorite profs of all time! He really knows his Java and as long as you complete the homeworks, show up to class and put forth decent effort you will get an A. Exams are online, open book, and pretty short.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Even though the class is really long, Dr. Comitz doesn't usually use up all the time. He teaches all the material thoroughly without feeling like he's rushing it. You can tell how passionate he is about Java and coding in general through his lectures. He is a lenient grader and you will get an A if you show him that you're trying.

Dr. Comitz knows his Java. You will be ahead of other IS 147 students if you take him. If you stay after class to talk to him, he will help you with whatever you are struggling with. As long as you are trying and doing the homework, he will give you credit for it.

He is a great IS147 professor.  Your grade consists of homework assignments, 4 quizzes, and a project. There is no final. Also, all quizzes are open note. He is very knowledgeable and will help you understand concepts if you're struggling. He also emphasizes team work and so you work on all of the homework assignments and the project with a partner

Java intro course. Professor was condescending. Treated less skilled students as if they were wasting his time. Hardly welcoming for a major that accepts undergrads without experience in CS or IS. Felt disrespected at times. Grading was based off of one major project and about 5 or so quizzes. If you can't code, learn quickly.

Prof. Comitz was very knowledgable. The material being taught was also very interesting. However, he is quick to make assumptions and judgments of students and will talk down to them even if it is not deserved.

There are 4 quizzes, weekly homework assignments, & a final project. All are very reasonable. He's a nice guy and a clear lecturer, but he can be kind of boring. There are no surprises on quizzes which are open note & open Internet. This is an interesting class, but if you're not a good programmer, do NOT take it.

He is a good professor. There is no textbook, you learn as you do work on hws. He is very knowledgeable. His exams are short (10 questions) and each question is 1% of your grade. Don't worry though, you are allowed to look at the internet/your notes during exams. I did the hw, attended class, I passed easily that way.

Great professor, very experienced and personable. He actually wants to teach students and have them be successful.  There's no final exam, instead a final project that you work on during the semester.  As long as you don't procrastinate on the project, you will do fine, assuming you have the programming background required for the course.

Nice guy. The class will be hard if you and your partner don't know Java very well. He's a lenient grader, but the assignments will be hard for those who haven't coded in a while or aren't confident in their abilities. Don't overthink the quizzes, because most questions aren't tricky.

Worst teachers I ever had. There are 4 quizzes, homework, and then a final project. Quizzes are a big part of your grade. The quizzes can be hard and tricky even with open book. He knows his java but can not teach very well. If you already know java then go ahead an take it otherwise use a different class for your programing requirement

Great professor, he's a very experienced java programmer and knows his material well.  Attendance is mandatory (graded), the homework assignments aren't bad and the project is reasonable provided you start early.  You do a lot of programming, while the concepts are basic, this is not an intro to java course  (reconsider if you have zero java exp.)

Comitz is such a knowledgeable Java programmer that he fails to realize that his 147 students, for the most part, have never written a line of code in their life. I came into the class with no prior knowledge and I felt like he moved too quickly. He grades fairly, although he said I would get a B, and he gave me a C.

Also you do need to spend 3-4 hours outside of class working on projects every week. You don't have to get them perfect to get full credit, though. You MUST read the chapters before class or the slides and the projects might seem somewhat confusing. Don't let the easy first projects lull you into a false sense of security. Keep reading!

Last poster apparently didn't take into account tests and quizzes. Paul's grading system is weird, but if you show him you're actually trying and stay after class to talk with him about homework, he'll be lenient with grading. Quizzes are open book. He sometimes comes off as cocky, but overall a nice guy and good teacher. Knows his Java.

I worked my butt off in this class. He grades using checks, check pluses and check minuses. I got decent grades on the quizes, and "check pluses" on all the programming projects, which to me is at least a B. I checked my grades when they were posted, and I got a C in the class. I guess a "check plus" means a C and that projects mean NOTHING
The exams can be challenging and a fair amount of work outside the classroom is required. I learned a great deal - but I worked for it.

I took his 310 class a few semesters ago. His tests were hard, you need to read the book and study hard or you're not getting past a C. He assigns a project you need to present in class. Its anoying but it can help your grade. Again, it's not hard to get a C, but you need to work for that B.
Good teacher.  The mid term and final were open note and open book.  The hw is assigned weekly and graded.  It was an easy way to get points.  Group project is assigned and was fairly easy.
Comitz is a good professor and great person. Tests are challenging, but Comitz's interest, knowledge and enthusiasm of the subject make the class worth it.  I def recommend him.
No Comments
This is basically a teach yourself class. Test are hard with multiple answer per problem. I suggest passing him by.

You definitely have to read the book & teach yourself the material if you don't already know this stuff.  The definitions & explanations in the book make a whole lot more sense than his.  He works for Boeing & he knows his stuff, but not that great of a teacher.  However, he doesn't require alot of work (2 tests, 1 paper) & he's better than Redding

If you have the opportunity to pass this guy by, I would do so.  He tests Grad-School style with any number of multiple choice answers being right answers.  This makes easy material relatively difficult.  Class is hideously boring, and he is terribly dorky.  He teaches all 2.5 hours while 1.5 hours is review.  Just don't take anything with this guy

This class was one of the easiest i have ever taken...anyone with a fair amount of computer knowledge will do just fine with a little studying...i have an above average computer knowledge base and i got A's on all of the tests with zero studying done
This is a challenging course. The professor puts his heart and soul into it - this comes through in the lectures. They are enthusiastic and high energy.
This professor is a confuesd man and bit to dramatic and agreek (which he's proud to be) exams are frustrating and class is boring

Paul Comitz has his ups and downs, but overall is a good professor.  He teaches 1 day per week, and goes the entire 3 hours.  He is extremily thorough, and quite knowledgable...but he will force you to participate...it gets old after a while.  Only real bad thing about him is he doesn't give a structured syll. and doesn't respond to e-mails.

Very easy class, don't even need the textbook. Just return it and keep doing the assignments until you get a 100. I finished the whole class by the end of spring break so make sure you don't miss any assignments and you're good for the whole semester.
Somehow takes her forever to upload our final grades when the entire class is automated and she doesnt have to grade anything. Don't email her cuz she doesn't want to hear it

This class is very easy, the professor essentially doesn't exist. Unlimited attempts for every assignment. No actual learning is required. The textbook contains all the assignments and are directly from text. Copy and paste in textbook search bar.

The professor does not want you to contact or email her, but she was very understanding when I had a mid-semester injury. I enjoyed this class because it was entirely online. Everything was super easy. Just take the quizzes and tests until you get a perfect score.  I got this class done by October, and it opened up early in August.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Just pretend she doesnt exist because she repeats 20 times in the syllabus to not contact her. The class is very easy. You can easily do any assignment without looking at the notes at all.
This professor really does not want you emailing her. Luckily, you don't really need to. Class is super easy and you get unlimited attempts on most stuff. You get out of it what you put into it.

I loved this class because it was all online & you just read the book and grades automatically pull from Cengage (you can do multiple attempts to get a 100). No interaction with the professor, you just learn on your own at your own pace but everything was pretty straightforward.

There will be no interaction with the professor for this class. I found out the name of the professor on the last week of the semester just to leave this rate for her class here... Easy credits and not much learning.

Not much of a professor. Since this class is online, she basically sets it up as asynchronous and gives no extensions whatsoever. She does not seem to care about her students because she directs them to Cenage support if we had any questions at all and basically makes it clear in the syllabus she doesn't want you emailing her.

don't take late work but class was easy and the book is expensive but if you have the book you don't need the lecture but if you don't have the book watch the lectures because she literally paraphrase the book.

It was taught online. If you had any questions about the topic (such as wondering why you got a question wrong), she would tell you to contact Cengage support, and wouldn't answer much. Despite this, the topics were relatively easy, and several assignments had unlimited attempts. Everything is in the textbook, so read that before doing assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very easy class, just a bunch of busy work, but prof. is passive aggressive. On the first day (and multiple other times) she sent out an email basically saying don't ask her for help on anything bc she doesn't know how to fix it. I don't know why she got paid. There were no lectures and all homework was done through Cengage which was auto-graded.
Literally the easiest A ever. Its all online and all the chapters are very easy. Take this.

Dr. Cronin is an amazing professor. He is passionate in what he does and is an awesome lecturer. Couple small papers and 1 very long review paper. Exams were fully written and really tough. No textbook though, so everything is from his lectures. If you're up for the challenge, take his class!

I want to be like Dr Cronin when I grow up. He's brilliant in his preferred field of research, sharp and enthusiastic even when stepping outside of it. Every lesson with him was engaging and in-depth, less like a class and more like a field trip even though we never left our seats. Discussions always came with a wonderfully dry sense of humor.

Dr. Cronin is a real G. He's so freaking funny and chill. But exams are LONG and very detail oriented but definitely straightforward and easy to get partial credit. If you don't come to class, don't expect to pass. 10000/100 would recommend him for Neurobiology.
dude, TC is the man!  His expectations are fair even though he can be tough.  He knows so much! He's brilliant!
Not an easy one, but fair and a real pro in his field

Currently taking Professor Crabtree. He is a very knowledgable and an amazing professor. I am doing good in his class so far, but he is just condescending and very inconsiderate to students. I love his teaching style and his lectures are very energetic and passionate. I would take him again for any future IS surprisingly because he can teach.

He may come off as strict at first but he's really chill. Doesn't accept late work but gives reminders and details. Everything is in the syllabus so make sure you read it. If you read the book and go to lecture you will get an A or a B. Overall good professor

He is a passionate lecturer, though classes can feel dull at times. Project makes up 25% of the grade, 5 Tests make up 75% and are based on slides and key points (read slides for the A). While there's little extra credit, He's disciplined but understanding and shares advice from his professional experience to help students become system analysts.

He takes some getting used to, as he comes off pretty strict about everything. The tests make up most of your grade - so make sure you study the slides really well. The capstone project can be a beast - but he does give great feedback and lets you revise deliverables to earn points back.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The Professor explains how this class is one of those classes where you have to take it serious and study. He is 100% right, now I'm a lazy student so I should have every reason to hate the class, yet the professor balances his strict class with probably the best compliments you'll hear from a professor ever. If your schedule is light take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very knowledgeable. He pushes his students to be the best, AND he expects his students to know everything he teaches. I found his quizzes hard- you get like 30 mins and 25-27 questions per quiz. Overall, I think you will learn a lot in this class, and you will get the grade you deserve. When someone works hard, he sees it and appreciates it.

This professor will always try to push you to give your best. From the very first class, you sense that you need to prepare yourself to grasp a great amount of knowledge. He will prepare you to think like a Manager or an executive of an organization. Once you READ (mind it) rubrics, every dot will connect. Pros and cons: be ready for your best.

Crabtree grew on me a lot. His personality is something to get used to at first, but he's a great prof to have. He may sound harsh at times but he's always constructive & specific, and his praise is as intense as his criticism. Always lets you improve deliverables after for full credit back! He doesn't leave anyone behind especially when COVID hit
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is a very understanding professor, he cares about his students but if he sees you lacking he'll make sure you understand the importance of coming to class. If you don't take notes or read the book you will not pass this class, the material is heavy and exams are purely based on the material taught in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Crabtree is a good at teaching FYS102. There are a lot of assignments, but it was fairly easy. I recommend taking him if you are planning to take FYS102. The class is easy itself and not that much assignments. There is this one big project at the end of the semester that basically determines your grade and it was easy. Easy A!

Crabtree goes in depth into the topics that are gone over in IS310. This is confusing for those that are new to the topics, but won't affect your grade. His assignments are easy to get As on if you follow his strict rubrics. His tests are really annoying and specific though, so you should STUDY THE POWERPOINTS! He does not round, I had an 89.2.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: If you would like to be disrespected in class the go ahead be my guest. He is by far the most disrespectful professor in my 4 years of school. He is condescending and believe me he does not care about you or your performance. He will make you feel like a failure and is never available through email and you won't even feel comfortable talking to him
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: 5 exams made up of 75% of your grade, and 25% from the project. Exams follow his slides, but the project is a beast, make sure you do what he tells you to do and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Crabtree is a cool dude. He's basically a robot but if you complete the requirements for assignments expect a 100%. Honestly nothing negative I could say about this guy. 10/10 would recommend
Professor Crabtree is a great professor. He may be strict at times but if you follow all directions and read instructions very carefully, you will not have any problems.

I got a 95% in his class this past semester. He doesn't give busy work and there's only 5-6 assignments and 2 Exams. 1 Group Debate 2 one-page response assignments 1 two to three page paper 1 annotated bibliograpy Note: he will not change dates or accept late work, just deal with it. Go to every class, study, participate, not hard to get A or B.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Crabtree started out as condescending teacher with a strict agenda. His lectures were vary passionate but fly through the material. Rubric is essentially the bible and must be followed strictly without any deviation. I'm a little biased because I did not pass the class however, his attitude and flexibility made the class miserable. Study hard.

Dr. Crabtree is awesome! He can be a bit quirky and has a specific style you'll have to adapt to in order to succeed. He works extremely hard to make requirements clear and accessible, constantly communicating due dates through email and announcements. He might seem unapproachable, but he is very caring and puts student success at the forefront.

He's very disrespectful! He literally does not care if you have an emergency he will straight up give you a zero if you do not turn in an assignment. He isn't understanding and will tell students they are failures if they fail to turn in an assignment or miss class. Do all assignments and really study for exams!! He makes the questions confusing.

His test dont match his power points and he doesnt use the textbook at all. Hes pretty great with other assignments just if you arent a good test taker/a person who loves to use the book to learn, forget this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class itself is easy and there's not a lot of work. The professor however is very condescending and disrespectful directly and indirectly to students. He emphasizes that you can't pass unless you to show up to class, but that is definitely not the case. It is an easy upper level IS class though.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor, he truly cares about his students and the subjects he teaches. He does not read off slides and often stops if the class has questions, his grading is fair. Best IS300 professor out there

Professor Crabtree can come off to be rude and not so approachable. He is very clear on his rubric and syllabus and if you ask any questions about an assignment he will call you out and say look at the syllabus. Otherwise the assignments in class are easy but long. Do not buy the textbook, just find the PDF online. It is used for 2 assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Crabtree is an awesome lecturer. He explains everything needed to know for exams and assignments. There is 2 exams, a annotated bibliography of 10 articles(easy), 2 case studies, article review, and debate. He is strict with due dates. The material is easy to understand. Go to class, read the book,study review slides and you get at least a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Crabtree motivates and encourage students to do their best. I can see that he puts a lot effort/time/energy into the class. Although he can be intimidating at times, he is only doing it for our own good. In the real workforce, people are more brutal. Think of Dr. Crabtree as preparing you for the real world.

I recommend him for IS300 to all my friends. Reason being: he is very clear about exams, weekly quizzes ensure you learn the material as you go, and he is VERY good at actually conveying his knowledge and teaching it. He doesnt just talk thru slides- he actually teaches. He can be very intimidating and condescending- and he hates "stupid" questions

I took IS300 with Professor Crabtree during the summer session, and I would definitely recommend him. He encourages active googling during lecture in case one may not fully understand a term or concept, and urges his students type up notes in class. If you're looking for an organized clear and concise professor... take him you will not regret it!
Fair grader and nice teacher. His exams are exactly what was taught in class.

Much respect goes to this professor. He immediately got to the point the first class and laid out what is required to pass this course. While yes it may come off as intimidating, he is simply preparing you for the next course. Coming to every class is MANDATORY if you want to pass the course. If he sees a problem, he will candid and state it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This guy is an intimidating individual but he knows what he is talking about. He is one of the better professors to take IS300 with! The textbook was extremely useless because his lectures were good enough. The textbook is only needed for one case study. TAKE HIM IF YOU WANT A BRIGHT FUTURE IN INFORMATION SYSTEMS!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Dr. Crabtree is a great professor. He is very organized and makes sure that you do not miss any deadlines. He doesn't believe in busy work, rather he focuses on making sure that you learn the material. His lectures are engaging as he brings his experiences from the field.
Dr. Crabtree is a kind and fair instructor.

FYS102: Social Issues in Business is an easy A class. Lectures were brutal especially for 2.5 hour classes. The concepts learned in this class are all easy but he makes them sound super difficult. Crabtree is kind of rude and unclear when answering questions. If you need an A class to raise your gpa, then take this class. If not, save the trouble.

He's a very entertaining professor. He'll send out lovely reminders of assignment due dates and he's very specific so if you don't get something, it's probably because you weren't paying attention.  That said, the textbook was utterly useless -_-, I regret renting it. It was necessary for one assignment but if you have a friend, I suggest sharing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Crabtree is a very nice person and a good teacher. He is clear in his requirements and is very reasonable. I definetley recommend him for IS 300.
Professor is just and considerate in rating you efforts in participation towards the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Connects with students and values participation. He's a good speaker, knows his stuff, and lecture is pretty engaging and wasn't boring to me. Class required a good amount of group work and three group presentations in front of class. Grading was fair as long as you put in effort and try your best. In my opinion one of the top IS professors.
He's such a nice guy. He cares about his students and doesn't pile up too much work on you. His exams are from exactly what he's taught in class .

He seems like a nice guy and the class isn't too hard. But he micro manages EVERYTHING. He so organized about everything to the point its kind of annoying. But other than that just your average class. 2 group projects ( 1 debate and 1 paper),  relatively easy pop quizzes, and 2 exams.

Really good professor. He'll do things to get on your nerves sometimes, but the fact that he is so professional in the way he organizes his class makes it really worth it.   Grades things quickly, unambiguously, and providing specific citation to lecture notes or textbook for every question.  He wont accept anything past due  Need2read
Good professor with a cordial nature. Not very hectic course.
A very good speaker, so attending his lectures aren't too boring. Not much to say. Attend class, take some notes, study slides and you will likely pass with a B.

He's probably one of the best lecturers. Class consisted of 3 group assignments that are chosen at random in the first week. Participation is graded and only 2 exams (both non cumulative). He's a very syllabus oriented so MAKE SURE TO READ IT. Other than that its an overall easy class and exams aren't really tough. Focus on the group projects....
Great professor, he cares about his students.

Incredibly monotone which is painful for two and a half hours. Seminars are supposed to be discussion-based, but the main component of this class was lecture. Somewhat patronizing; most of the topics were pretty easy to understand but he treated them as if they were extremely difficult. There was a lot that the course could have explored but didn't
Very dedicated Professor, one of the best at UMBC. The class projects which are in a group are demanding but very interesting.

Don't know if he'll teach this class again, but he was one of the best professors I have had at UMBC. Very passionate, really wants you to succeed. Be sure to attend, pay attention, and participate. I always looked forward to going to his class.

he's nice but sometimes annoying. class consisted of 2 exams, 2 projects. cant have the same group for both projects. the 2nd project is the longest one with upto 15 pages (single space). tests are straight forward from the ppts. well u gotta come to class. he hates students who skip class.  participation needed ( 10 points for the whole sem total)

Easy class. He puts a lot of emphasis on group work - you're stuck with the same group for the entire semester (3 projects) & they're picked randomly. Even though the projects aren't difficult, the group work will be a pain if you don't get a good group. No tests, and a couple of easy but maybe time consuming assignments near the end.

funny lady, very kind. I was always tired but her class was very fun, super interesting too. She makes me want to continue taking socy after having her fall 2019, even complimented my anime t-shirt haha. I took lots of notes in class and did the study guide so i always passed the test. very easy class, easy homework and helpful department. miss her
Professor Crane is awesome. She is enthusiastic and energetic every single class. She covers the material very well and uses tons of examples to help you remember. I definitely recommend her.

She's amazing! Her lectures are great and organized. The class is very well organized. Do the work and you'll do well. Tests can be a bit tricky but if you read the textbook and pay attention you'll be fine.

took her at UMCP and she was the most friendly/caring/funny prof I've ever had. very passionate about sociology & really cares about her students. lots of extra credit opportunities, easy hw. relates the material back to the real world/current things to help us understand. learned a lot from her, amazing person and professor. highly recommend.

Professor Crane is by far one of the best teachers I have taken this semester! The groupwork is fairly easy as long as students read, do the quiz, and, do the assignment. The tests are on 3 chapters at a time which is easy to manage as long as you understand the concepts. The peer mentors and the teacher assistant were also very helpful!

GO TO HER CLASS! It'll make the material some much easier to study and I am not great at sociology. If you go to her office hour, she would help you. There are many group assignments that are kind of hard even though you get to work in groups because the TAs grade them hard.
Best professor at UMBC hand down!!!!! She is very caring and understanding. her lectures are very interesting.

I really enjoyed her class. It was easy for me, but I still read the textbook and studied for exams. She made the class interesting and informative. One of the best professors I have had. You will get an A if you can memorize definitions and apply concepts.

Crane is super engaging and makes the subjects, which can sometimes be tough topics to talk about, more fun. The homework is easy and so is the reading. The groupwork is graded harshly sometimes, but this is because of the TAs. I found that the review sessions before each exam, which were ran by the TAs, were not helpful.

She is a really nice person and teacher. The lectures are interesting as well. The only problem is that the TI grades harder than her and the group works were always graded hard which has a lot of impact on your final grade

I would recommend taking her for this class, she's a great professor and it's honestly not that hard. There's homework due once a week, easy group assignments, mandatory review class before test day (which is so convenient). The content is very interesting and easy to enjoy & understand.

Prof. Crane is truly passionate about Sociology and it shows during lectures. There are 3 exams, weekly assignments, and group work. Tests were fairly easy as long as you thoroughly review material. Content can be considered "common sense" but was still interesting nonetheless. Highly recommend this course if you need it to satisfy an GEP.

Amazing person with a great personality. But she is no way lenient about her grading. There are weekly assignments(not difficult),& TA nitpicks small details about it & it can make or break your grade. Her lectures are interesting & engaging, & I really learnt a lot of things in her class. But she doesn't give opportunities to raise your grade.

Rachel Crane was probably one of the best professors I've had so far, but Sociology is not my most favorite subject. She is energetic and super funny, but lectures can be boring at times, but she tries her best to make it better. Exams are somewhat hard because they are half MC and half written. In-class group work is also annoying.

Professor Crane really is an enthusiastic professor when it comes to sociology. The class schedules is divided between lecture days and group work days. Her lectures are very in depth with lots of real-world examples, helping us students to connect. The group work was another way to study up on sociology. The textbook was barely used.
Great personality. Study for the exams, but they aren't too hard. The videos she plays are sometimes weird or kind of pointless, but besides that it's fine.

She seems to actually care about you and how you do. The textbook is useful, but she basically just repeats the textbook during lectures. No computers are allowed in most of her classes. Lectures can get boring, especially if you read the textbook before, but I'd rather boring than confusing. If you try, you will succeed.

She really cares about her students and if I could I would definitely take this class again. If you have the chance to take her I say completely go for it!! She gives our weekly individual assignments but theyre mainly straightforward. She also gives a concept guide w the main topics that will be on the exam which is also extremely helpful. 10/10!

Professor Crane is a real gem. I took this class freshman year and I'm so glad I did. Her lectures are long but she tries to make it fun by putting funny jokes and awesome content. She is really caring. She addresses everyone with their first name when there are over 100 students. Very nice and caring professor. Make sure to take notes!

I only come on here if my professor was GREAT or the total opposite. Prof Crane cares about her students grades and takes her time to teach material. I was in her lecture hall class, she would address me by my name after only one instance of speaking to her (which is unrelated but so genuine) and gave me an extension. Very recommended!

He made political science fun. He taught like six different courses and I took every one of them. Loved his presidential impressions! He inspired me to choose a career I wouldn't have otherwise pursued.

I had Croatti for State and Local Politics. He is very aware of what happens with the Maryland legislature since he writes for a magazine. We did a lot of things in Annapolis like take capitol tours and learn about state history. He is not easy to write papers for, he has a lot of rules and is a stickler for format issues, but I loved the class.

Professor Croatti made a difference with "mini" internships to volunteer a few hours to build our resume, guest speakers, and extra credit events. I took many courses with him at Catonsville campus and Shady Grove. My presidency class went to the White House where we spoke with Bush's speech writer. He made politics interesting, not easy to do.

A lot of students in this class texted the entire time and you could tell it got on Croatti?s nerves. He?ll eventually call you out on it so my advice is to put the phones away. If you're not prepared for your oral report, God help you. Otherwise, great lectures and lots of fun outside-the-classroom experiences.

Although Proffesor Croatti is strict, he puts forth a lot of effort in preparing for his lecture, and his assignments and field trips are very interesting. I did enjoy his class very much. Professor Croatti A+ teacher

he's actually a good professor. His class is extremely informative, and you actually walk out pretty smart about the topic taught;) do the extra credit! -not only will it boost your grade, but its actually fun!
No Comments

Do the extra credit field trips all of them and you will do great in the class and they're alot of fun. He loves the Native Americans and can work them into any class and will. He likes to pick on students to so just keep your head low and you will be fine. The class isn't easy but do all the extra credit and you'll get an A.

A very interesting and engaging class; very insightful prof. His lectures are amazing and teach you things you only learn in class, not the book. You'll get an A if you go to the lectures, do the readings, the internship, and do a couple of the extra credit assignments.
This professor is very caring and genuinely sincere. He cares about the well-being of his students. He is kind and will do just about anything to help, if asked.

Prof. Croati is a great lecturer and very knowledgeable of the subject matter. He is great at teaching topics with an independant point of view. I enjoyed the extra credit field trips to the embassies in D.C. However,he can be arrogant and unapproachable. He onced harrassed a student because her cell phone went off in class and she cried.

Croatti teaches similar topics (Native Americans, Kurds, etc.) in each class he teaches but tailors them to specific courses. He once took a week in 2003 (the 40th anniversary) to address JFK from all angles. He was voted Teacher of the Year by poli sci majors in 2006 because he provides extra credit and places students into internships in DC.

He makes the subjects interesting and you will want to learn more. His tests are straight out of the book and are easy if you study. He challenges students' assumptions often but not entirely without reason. EXCELLENT professor.
Croati is the best professer I've had. He isn't easy, but HE allows chances for extra credit. His class is incredably worth it, a wonderful experience. And he looks like George Clooney.
Be prepared to write a very long paper. Exams fairly easy essays. Lots of extra credit possibilities. Classes are very entertaining.

He’s a very intelligent man who knows what he’s talking about. He does pick sides of arguments, but presents the material with a very none bias approach. Goes a little bit off topic sometimes, but always is very interesting. Never a boring moment in his class. Take him, he’s very good. Lots of extra credit, which can boost you a letter grade.

AMAZING professor. Tests are somewhat confusing because the multiple choice is a bit ambiguous...but he gives plenty of extra credit. Although he is very liberal, he sheds light on both views. Funny. Interesting. Must take his class!!
This professor is not willing to work with his students at all and seems to think that what he says is law. Don't take his class, it will be a lot of work for nothing in the end.

Yeah, he has a heart attack if a cell phone goes off and takes students aside to chastise them, but definitely worth attending, even if it's mandatory, and he's quite helpful with internships, jobs and application letters. Embassy visits are great. He runs a tight ship, more like a cruise ship with stops at foreign ports.

Croatti is a great prof for most people. He is liberal and opinionated & can be abrasive. I've taken 2 of his classes & loved both. He knows everything & is so passionate about world politics. This class was on Iraq & presented from a worldly (not American) pov. Embassy visits in DC (with the actual ambassadors from Iraq & Syria) were a highlight.

by far my favorite polisci teacher...he loves what he does and it shows.  i took three classes with him and loved each one.  lots of extra credit...read the books and attend class. you won't regret his seemingly endless well of knowledge.

The way Professor Croatti comes across about the problems the nation is facing can be seen by some as abrasive, but I think he's just trying to drive the point home and make you think. He has a passion for problem-solving but he realizes that problems only get solved if people care.
Absolutely is a jerk for requiring attendance! Coolege is optional, dude! Wake up, man.
He is VERY intelligent, however he is a true Jerk !

He really is a wonderful teacher and he doesn't have a ego or thinks he knows everything. He's there to teach and that's his job. He is very inspiring and wants you to make a difference in your world. I think he cares about all of his students and is one of the sweetest people at UMBC- besides Robin.

This class was on Iraq, and it was extremely interesting. It was 3hrs long but Croatti made time fly.  Exams were easy as long as you came to class.  His analysis of Israel was right on the money. The only ones complaining about it are Zionists.

Croatti is great!!..loved his stance on political issues and agreed about 99% of the time......but dont forget to to read all the assigned chapters before taking a test. He does't go over the test material in class....and usually lectures are not related to the textbook. Take advantage of the extra credit events.

Great class, lots of embassy visits, an off-campus  dinner at the end that was very interesting, and the food was good. Makes points in lectures that relate to the book but only if you're paying attention

Very interesting class. Loves to get off topic and rather carried away with current events. Lectures may not help much, but the book is your friend, and the tests are not hard at all. However, be ready to talk a lot about the JFK assassination. The group project is an easy way to get points in this class, so use it to your advantage.

I truly enjoyed this class; he was very interested and knowledgeable. He leans to the left, so be prepared for that. Lots of extra credit opportunities, easy tests, easy final project, easy A. As long as you go to class, you will ace his tests. I went into the class apathetic, and came out educated and enthusiastic about the topics we discussed.
Easy going and interesting. Doesn't assign massive essay exams--he uses multiple choice.
A lot about the Native peoples, so if you're into what happened to the "orginial Americans", then this is the course for you.

Awful. If you want to learn what Croatti thinks and considers reality - take his class. The lectures don't cover the syllabus at all. 70% of the test questions were never covered in class. Readings have nothing to do with "lectures". Better name for class: "Croatti's viewpoint on Israel conflicts". If you make him feel important, may help you grade
An exciting class during a campaign season. Lots of guest speakers and elected officials.
Embassy visits are cool.  Tests can be hard but extra credit helps. A lot on Iraq but at least it's interesting.
Oh my god--if Croatti didn't throw in his own material, I would have screamed in the middle of class.  The book is way too long. Buy it used! But the class overall is definitely worth taking.
A fun class--but don't expect normal assignments. Lots of outside stuff, like community lectures. Good for extra credit--take advantage of it!

By far, the worst teacher in the history of humanity.  How anyone could find this guy interesting or a good teacher is beyond me.  This is not a Political Sciene class, in fact, the major itself ceases to exist upon entering his class.  Any bum off the street could teach better than this man, granted, that's really what they got in him.  Stay away!
clarity and hepfulness

Prof Croatti manages to make what could be mind numbingly boring material fairly interesting. He also offers service learning mini-internships for this course if you like that kind of hands on experience. Some of his policies are strict (ie attenance) but overall I would recommend him.

interesting class but pretty hard.  He does not teach from book but you need the material.  He is obsessed with the JFK assasination.  We spent 5 weeks watching movies and talking about it but we were not tested on it. ALWAYS TURN OFF YOUR CELL PHONE
Too hard.

I decided to take public administration and expected to learn about bureaucracy but unfortunately this fellow (who seems to regard himself as the new messiah of education) teaches rumors that I could just as well have learned on the internet.  Save yourself some time, don't take his class, spend more time online and you'll be just as well.
No Comments

Croatti is one of the best teacher that i have ever had. He is very smart and i will recommed every poli sci major to have him.... i never got bore in his class.. and like every student i also enjoy his lectures tooo.
Although I don't agree with Prf. Croatti on Israel, he's a great teacher. I definitely reccomend him.

i took both his 260 & 409B classes, he's a nice guy, the lectures are interesting if you take him for the first time, but he teaches you the same material no mater what the suject of the course is.  The exams are super hard, he tests you on dates (wtf????), if you wanna get an A, avoid him! never taking him again!

Good class.  Whoever thought that the class was too hard or material too irrelevant needs to work on their critical reading. I have taken several classes with this professor, and material is repeated, but this is inevitable when teaching courses on the middle-east.  He provides ample extra credit which are always enriching. You do fine if u read.

absolutely horrid. his teaching skills and dynamic speaking are ruined by the fact he lacks any substantial personality as an individual. Which makes it hard to get help. HOWEVER, Croatti's insight and genius shows when asked to analyze ANYTHING BUT ISRAEL in the mid-east. Give him a shot, you will learn alot. Just know none of it is on your exam.

Absolutely awful.  Never take a class with him.  Lecture topics not pertinent to exam material at all.  You are tested on random tidbits of info he says in lecture that you think are not related.  If you have to take his class, expect low test grades, and spending your whole semester doing Extra Credit to make up for it.  Do the internship.

I just hated it. He rambles non-coherently about the same subject matter over and over. His militant liberalism oozes with every lecture. He offers tons of extra credit and really makes an effort to help the student. I hated his class. With a passion.

I've taken POLI240/260/409B with Croatti. You learn a lot of facts that do not pertain to the course. He teaches the same material to all classes.  However, the material is fairly interesting. His classes only consist of 3 m/c exams...very easy and a paper.  You could probably get C's on all the tests & get an A if you did enough extra credit.

Loved his class, didn't just teach straight from a book but made his lectures interesting. He did start to repeat a lot of what he taught in other classes, Zappruder film/JFK, Lincoln's Assination, etc. Basically a conspiracy theorist in a lot of senses. But he is a very intelligent man, able to recite a lot of facts/legislation on the spot.
Very knowledgeable, and interesting.  He does get on a bit of an ego trip from time to time, but i liked his class quite a bit overall.
Pretty easy class, definitely do the internship. Very interesting class, make sure to do the reading...tests M/C, pretty easy. Pretty intelligent guy as well.

He is an awesome professor. He definitely makes the class fun and the extra credits are also helpful. My only problem was that he was really harsh while grading the paper. He does give you the option of an internship as well...I would go with that.

This guy was awsome. He gave the facts w/o wearing his own political beliefs on his sleeve and gave tons of extra credit opportunities also. I loved his class and never missed a day. Plus, he was DROP DEAD SEXY!!!!!!!!!!!

He cares about his students,lectures on things you can't get out of a textbook, brings facts up that most people don't know and adds jokes to his lectures. Group presentations took a lot of class time up. He seems a little intimidating, but once you get to know him he's great and is willing to talk to you one on one. Definately take a class w/him!!

A conspiracy theorist and idiot who believes everything in the world is caused by cabals of powerful people trying to rule the world. Intellectually dishonest, tossing out bits and pieces of "facts" that fit his argument, distorting history in the process. Not liberal or conservative, but stupid.

Fairly easy, lots of extra credit offered, internship or paper (be careful on biblio + citations, lets you rewrite for additional grade), exams multiple choice - make sure you read and study the book.  His lectures are interesting, but not quite on the topic at hand.

You will learn a lot in any Croatti class. His quizzes are a little difficult but are multiple choice. You have to do the reading to do well. Lots of extra credit. There was a group paper/presentation that was a bit tedious. Class will be reworked before it is offered again.

Wonderful teacher who obviously cares about what he teaches.  He encourages his classes to be involved...do the internship instead of the paper!  Exams are easy if you read the book and come to class. Tons of extra credit.

He made the three+ hours lecture go by quickly.  He's very interesting and adds some jokes to his lectures.  Tries to give the facts w/o bias.  As long as you do the reading and pay attention you'll do fine.
No Comments

Love this guy! His lectures are very interesting and he makes you think about a lot of issues.  Do the internship, tests are M.C., and if you go to events you can get a lot of extra credit. He does a good job of presenting unbiased info, and there is something attractive about him.

Note that the person who hated him didn't understand how course numbers work! He was really interesting. Tests not hard, special project was a bit of a pain. I would take a class with him again, even though he is a wee bit off at times.
I had this professor for POLI 240 and not only are his lectures super-engrossing and interesting, he's really really ridiculously attractive....love it

easy polisci class, lectures are very engrossing, lots of speakers/ex credit field trips; got 100pts excred. exams are super easy- 30 q's MC, no essays.  he grades term paper harshly. work on it ahead of time& be esp. careful writing citations and biblio.
hated him, was a complete jerk that has NO CLUE how to teach.  he is miserable.  if you can, advoid like the plague!
Although he is entertaining, he's a hard grader. He gives no leeway. I worked very hard on an essay...he completely slaughtered it! Good news: tests are REALLY easy

A charismatic, humorous professor whose lectures often have a theatrical bent and never fail to be engrossing. A class that's hard to fall asleep in because he's so engaging. Easy exams, term paper easy compared to other poli-classes, great 100-lvl course

Completely lost it by the end of the semester Yelled at students for really odd things, accused others of taking too much advantage of the extra credit, would not allow one student to take the final because his project was not done "in the right spir

My class with Professor Croatti is shaping up to me a lot more interesting than I thought an intro poli-sci course would be!  He has a lot of thought-provoking things to say, and shares them without excluding other points of view.

Be prepared to either write a very long paper or serve a 20-hr mini-internship and write a short paper. Exams fairly easy with no essays. Lots of speakers and extra credit trips. Classes are very entertaining.

Doesn't post anything to blackboard, including powerpoints and grades. Makes it hard to understand what will be on exams, considering some exams include almost 10 chapters of material. He is very picky about the way he grades, and wants you to answer questions a certain way but expects you to learn from reading directly from the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Analytical is a difficult and time consuming class. Attending lecture is critical. Doesnt post slides online and only covers select material from the text. If you do the assigned homework, attend class and keep up with the lab reports you should pull at least a B. Nice guy, but he expects you to put in the work and there are no shortcuts.
Terrible professor. Didn't prepare us for the final (ACS) exam at all
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lectures are monotonous. He wants you to understand the concepts. If you need help, go to his office hours. The book covers a lot that he does not and will not test you on, though the practice problems are essential.
challenging professor.  Need to do all HW problems well before exams, this will help.

you literally need to press your ear up against his mouth to hear him lecture. powerpoints required binoculars to read. never had a satisfying answer to a question. if you are considering taking him for any class, just wait and hope that the next semester will have a better professor.

Powerpoint reader. Asks questions that students don't know during lectures so we sit there for about 5 minutes just blankly staring at him until we keep guessing and guessing until we accidentally get it right. Exams are hard as balls. No curve. Showed up to class everyday. Studied my ass off. Pretty sure I failed. Lab was easy tho.

He is the best professor I have ever had.  Here at UMBC or CCBC.  The only people who could possibly complain about his teaching are the ones who do nothing but expect a good grade for paying and showing up.

not helpful at all! i think this is the only  class he teaches, doenst really make the effort to TEACH you, rather reads the powerpoint which is exactly the book..exams were HARD, he made the second one slightly easier, since people got 30% the first time. he says he wants to help you...i dont know how that would even be possible.

Cullum is a professor doing his best to teach a mandatorily tough class, and maybe inspire students while he's at it. He brings humor to class, but this class is no joke: work as many problems as possible! - or you won't survive. Much better than some of the other profs teaching this class.
class wasnt too hard, labs took a lot of time but they were basically free points. do the textbook problems and go over the notes and youll get at least a B on the exams.

Cullum teaches from powerpoint. Usually in a rush to copy down notes to absorb material. Does not use blackboard. Exams are extremely hard, does not give enough time. 90+ A, 80+ B, etc. Means well, very nice and approachable, but tough professor.

"There is no such thing as bad art. Only effective, and less effective" and he meant it.  Always gave meaningful critiques.  Pushed students to go out of their comfort zones.  Showing that you care about your work is what he looks for.
Great class, got to print what you wanted to. Very helpful & knows his stuff. Definitely take him for a print class!

He's fantastic! He's very helpful and understanding. There were times when I was worried and felt really stupid because I couldn't grasp a process in class, but he helped me through it even when it was rough. One of the best professors I've had.

Prof. Custen is very laid back and definitely makes the effort to keep the class environment as low stress as possible. He looks to see that you learn the processes more than anything else and as long as you do the work and put forth the effort you will do fine. :)
Very good studio art teacher
Very willing to explain and help out so long as you pay attention when he is initially explaining the topic. Dont be late or miss the critique days. Do your work and get an A
Intro to print... easy grader. Helpful and relaxed about grading/projects... take him if you can for any of his classes whether it's graphic design or not!!

Very cool, laid back guy. Critique atmosphere is fun and NOT intimidating like some other classes. Just go to class, do the projects, and get an A. He is an easy grader but does not like lateness on critique days! Be on time and have your work complete on time. I had a lot of fun in that class. Make friends in class, it'll help!
Awesome teacher, just come to class and do the work, easy A. Always there to help the students.

Pretty awesome teacher. Hadn't taken Spanish in years before taking her class, was definitely worried beforehand, however Natalie erased all the fears I had going into this class. She made her exams crystal clear and laid out for us what we needed to study for each part of the exam. Also a very lenient grader. Very cool professor!

Young professor, so she relates to her students quite well.  She expects a lot of thought and interpretation about the novels but also allows students to debate amongst themselves.  Two big papers and two exams plus homework make up your grade.

She is soo nice tests crazy easy She understands what you are going through because shes young herself. Very fair grader basically no homework and if there is she goes over it in class only collected one assignment the whole semester and adjusts hw level knowing you will have more in other classes(b4 spring break.

Personally, I think Natalia is a great Spanish 201 professor. She is very understanding, willing to work witht he students, and there is not a ton of homework. The test are easy as long as you look at the material ahead of time and she tells you what is going to be on the exams. There is no reason anyone should fail her class unless they are lazy.
I personally LOVED Natalia. Sure she was a little disorganized, but I feel like she went out of her way to make sure we understood the material. She mad this a very enjoyable class.
Nice teacher, but very disorganized. Hard to tell what her grading policy is. Also, mid-Term and Final a week apart!? Procrastinate, much? Although she is nice, I would look at other teachers first.
Being in class with her is very fun, you learn a lot of things about spain. Good cultural ressource... a little grumpy sometimes :)

This teacher is extremely slow at returning grades. She is the only one who has not sent in grade for my transcript and she never responds to emails. Several times, she has not shown up to class. Flakey and ignorant. Avoid at all costs!

You will enjoy this class if you go to lectures, do your work honestly, and go to office hours when you dont understand something. If you don't do these, this class will be exceptionally hard. Second time taking the class and slacked heavy the first time now doing what I advised and have A+ on all exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Might not apply for everyone's study styles but using only her posted lecture slides were enough to earn an A on each exam. Try not to get lazy and fall behind, but even if you do each exam can honestly be studied for the night before. Very willing to help everyone and has a good sense of humor. Mostly went to lecture to listen to her jokes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lili is the sweetest and one of the best professors I've ever had! Explained concepts extremely clearly and caused my fear of Physics to dissipate. She is VERY clear on what she expects for exams and as long as you pay attention in class and do all the homework you should succeed in her class. She's also amazing at motivating her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor Cui's class is very straightforward. There are weekly friday quizzes which can be done with the people around you, but they are very helpful in preparing for the test since most of the questions on the quiz are put on the test. Her lectures are very helpful as well, and reading the textbook is useful as well to do practice problems

Good professor! Took PHYS121 in her class. Have to say, it is a hard class. Tons of work. I passed it, therefore can't complain. I would take her for another class also, she is a nice person and solid professor. Only minus she sometimes speaks to fast and is not very clear. Otherwise, she is great. Make sure to attend and read the textbook.

Good professor? Yes or No? Yes okay Dr Lili has very good lectures and if you don't skip or pay attention, you will learn basically everything you need to succeed in the course (although I still highly recommend reading the textbook!)

Lili is clear from the beginning about what she expects and how you can succeed in her class. The most important thing is to show up to lectures and discussions, and you shouldn't have to put too much independent effort into understanding the material. She is extremely accessible and cares about her students' performance.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Lili Cui was an amazing professor. If you keep on top of the homework and pre-lectures you will do fine. She really helps people understand the concepts and uses plenty of examples. Her accent can be a little difficult, but overall it's not too hard to understand once you get used to it. She also really cares about her students.

I was afraid to take physics, but Lili made this class so enjoyable. If you pay attention in lecture, you will do well in the class. Homework is hard, but is great test prep. Expectations were clear, tests were fair, and even the workload wasn't too bad. Great professor for a difficult course
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Had her for the Physics 122L. Was nice, and could explain concepts across, although she was often difficult to understand and fairly strict with participation and due dates.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Terrible professor. Her accent is way too heavy to overcome and she flies through the lectures as if you've already taken the class before. The homework are very hard, but it's what you need to fully understand the course. Exams are straightforward. I recommend the book and LOTS of practice on your own.
She made it so confusing.  I just took it in the summer and it is so much better.

Very nice and friendly, but unrealistic expectations for students.  Her lectures were hard to follow, the homework was MUCH harder than anything covered in class, and her tests could be very hard (over half the class got an F on one test) She sometimes tests on things barely covered in class and homework. No curve.
I liked her a lot! She's very helpful during office hours and she grades exams really fast. I didn't really care for physics before but I like it now because of this class.

Great professor! Her lectures are clear. The tests are very straight forward and are very similar to the past exams that she makes available. She's very approachable so go to her office hours if you don't really understand something gone over in class. Taking the class seriously and preparing for each lecture is the key to success.

Class consists of exams, online homework, labs and lab homework, and weekly clicker quizzes. Exams can throw you off due to a question or two not really covered thoroughly in class or in lab. It's very important to practice your timing while working through old exams as the actual exams tend to be much longer and trickier.

Amazing! Lots of points to be earned! Clicker quiz every Friday, you can use your neighbors for the quiz. Really helpful. Easy exams. I hated physics before but loved it with her! She completely changed my mind about it! She has a cute accent which makes her a bit more attractive ;) Enjoy!

Lili is a very inspiring, dedicated, and helpful professor. If one does the work she requires and/or recommends, then the course is easy. I found her lectures to be a good reinforcement of the material. Making use of her office hours will also help one succeed in the class. She is very willing to answer student questions.

Dr. Cui was awesome. She has an accent, but it's not too hard to understand. She's a morning person, so she'll try to wake you up, and she's funny. Homeworks are difficult, but you get many tries. Tests are very easy. I always worried about getting hard questions, but HW was ALWAYS harder than the test.

Dr. Cui is without a doubt one of my favorite professors at UMBC! She's very enthusiastic, extremely approachable, kind, and even funny! I had her for 121, and although her class was hard, it was very doable. Dr. Cui is a great person and an amazing professor! I would wholeheartedly recommend her to prospective students!
She is a good teacher, and her exams are pretty straightforward. However lectures are useless, and there is no curve at all.

She's not at all helpful when you ask a question; she never answered a single email of mine. This is a college class, yet she'll walk around bugging people who don't take notes. I got an A, and I didn't need to take notes. Though lecture is useful, her voice irritated me. All of her shortcomings are made-up for by the ridiculously easy tests.
Nice teacher.

She's a REALLY good teacher for you if this is your first foray into physics. I see that after a few pages, the reviews go sour, but I think she was younger and less experienced then. Tests were graded usually within 12 hours, homework was put up promptly, and there were practice tests galore. Overall, this is an incredibly easy class if you study.

Lili is a sweatheart that will always take time to explain things to her students. To succeed in her class, don't be afraid to raise your hand and voice your concerns; she will always answer you to the best of her abilities. Also, go to the tutorial center, it makes the HW MUCH more reasonable :)

Great teacher, very approachable and explains content very well. As long as you understand the equations the work is fairly simple. Tests were easier than expected. Vpython use is very engaging and makes learning much easier. Teacher takes input and adjusts teaching style through semester.

I honestly have no idea why her rating is so low. If you didn't do well in the class it's probably your fault, not hers. She's always available to help and genuinely wants students to do well. The exams are completely fair and if you follow along in class/discussion you should be able to pull off a B easily. But you do have to the work.

Lili is really sweet - she wants students to learn and does her best to ensure that they do. Lectures are good and clear, but Mastering Physics homework is REALLY hard. Use her office hours, she's very helpful there. Good teacher for a difficult subject.

I'm not Chinese & can't speak any, & I thought her accent was easy to understand. Discussion questions were hardest, then homework, then exams. Exams are reasonable, provided you study. I was scared of going into PHYS 121 because of the reviews I had read here, but it turned out fairly well. I earned an A, and I'm not even that good at Physics.

I can barely understand anything she says. She doesn't teach very well. She spends most of her time on conceptual questions. When she does do actual problems. she starts off real easy and then all of a sudden the problems get really hard so there's no real learning curve. Her tests are a lot easier than her hw problems and problems in discussion.

I can not understand her. Overall, she spends 2/3 of the class talking about the conceptual part and the 1/3 on actual problems. She breezes by the questions and I learned most of the stuff  in her class by myself. Avoid her if possible.

Wow her exams are the easiest exams ever! Take the honors section. I'm retaking after withdrawing with Takacs (sp?) who was horrible and this is a breath of fresh air. The exams and homework are actually related to the lectures and what we've been taught, unlike Takacs'.

Honestly, I don't understand why she is getting negative reviews. If you don't do as well as you'd like, it is probably your fault not hers. She is a great teacher. Her lecture notes are good and her exams are completely fair. Don't be prejudice due to the other reviews. She is great!

First of all her english is horrible. The concepts are hard enough without here enormous accent. Btw she is here on a work visa...get the idea. This will ruin physics for you and the discussion session is 2 hours of hell and you dont get anything out of it except a headache.
if you do the homework(understand everything) and redo the problems done in class, you'll ace the class. as far as curving goes she curves hw grades only.

Overall, really not a hard class.  Some of the material is hard, and she doesn't explain it very well sometimes, but most who take it only need it for gen ed.  Grades are basically curved (if you get at least 80% on class/homework, you get full points), so the only possible way to lose points are tests.  Like any class, you have to put time in.

i had her for 121 and 122. i've always hated physics, but i don't think anyones given her fair ratings. physics isn't something someone can just learn from someone else. it requires a lot of practice. her exams are fair and so is her grading. i'm have a C but i'm not gonna blame her when i don't spend much time trying. she really does care.

She explains the basic concepts decently, but doesn't explain how to actually solve a problem. She usually gets behind in lecture, so at the end, she writes like 5 equations on the board with no explanation. She can be more helpful during office hours, but only if she understands what you're asking. I strongly suggest just reading the book.

A professor that is interested in what she is teaching but not easily understood.  The accent is not what makes it hard to understand the material.  The lack of explanation and rushed problems are what confuse the entire class.  Overall this class put me into a state of depression.  Try to avoid this professor if possible.

Was not the greatest experience ever....she's really into physics and all but clarity of these advance concepts doesnt come easy in the class.  My opinion, if you dont seek outside resources for help, you'll fail

She is definitely not one of UMBC's finer teachers.  I attribute her lack of clarity more to her lack of understanding than to her accent.  Overall you are not likely to come out of either of these two classes with more interest than you went in with, and regardless of your grade a little piece of your soul die in that class.  Take it with Anderson

I agree with the previous poster. The best 2 weeks of class ever. Mastering Physics is not fun at all. We don't learn enough beforehand, especially now that we're behind. I hate this class and I used to love physics.

Absolutely fantastic professor! Although she may seem a bit curt, she is incredibly caring about her students. All you need to do is attend office hours and she will make your life so much better. Definitely one of the best professors I have ever had and she made genetics doable.
I took her with team based learning and they expect you to know things that aren't even the book. She seems nice but sometimes makes you feel stupid.

she teaches at a non-bio major level, most of the time. However, she does assume you've had high school bio within that last year, which means there's a lot of details she doesn't explain. I have never had a teacher who never acknowledge my 2 emails I attempted to send (eventually just emailed Miller) and spoke with such arrogance. awesome lab. a little too unorganized for my taste but i loved Wagner. she is so silly!

Team based learning was terrible...did not learn anything from the professors; we had to learn by ourselves...take the lecture course that is offered!

Do NOT take "Team-Based Learning" with Wagner for Genetics!!!! Its basically a class where 300 kids sit in lecture and teach each other or themselves. The professors DO NOT really teach. So save yourself while you can :'(
One of my favorite professors! Quizzes were not that bad always fair. The notebook checks were fair as well. The group project was hard but extremely fun! This was probably my favorite lab

Class was good. Quizzes we're hard so studying is a must. Make sure notebook is neat and organized. There was a final group project in the class it was ok. She might not do it again after this semester thought.TA was okay but can be rude at times
