Annoying political preaching that does nothing to contribute to class.  Grading and scoring methods, often extremely unclear. TAs exacerbated this problem.  Insane amount of reading required.

Dr. Hody is a great teacher and her lectures are very interesting most of  the time.  However, you've gotta watch out for her TA Gavin.  No really, he does most of the grading and he's not fair about it at All.  It's a shame because I think I could've really enjoyed the class if I didn't have to contest every grade I got.
I like her class discussions.. beware she is very democratic but that wasn't a problem for me. She's a cool lady.
She is an amazing teacher! One of the best at UMBC!

One of the greatest teachers at UMBC.  Extremely intelligent, engaging, witty, FUNNY and makes the subject soooo interesting.  Gives lots of chances to improve work.  Always there to talk to for help or questions.  Fun course.  Definitely recommend.
great professor.  kinda hard and you definitely have to study, but has a great sense of humor and is always willing to help out...

Callenging class.  3 quizzes (25%) and 3 papers (75%), allows re-writes and averages 1st with 2nd for final grade. LONG lectures that are sometimes interesting but rarely address information that is being graded.  Honors requirement is weekly discussion section with a 1-2 page paper for each (we had 8 honors papers total). Essay grading is odd.

One of my favorite classes. If you like the subject you will love this. ALWAYS DO THE READING and come prepared for class.  She does not take crap from students.  But if you participate and are prepared you will get so much out of the class, and she will always help you out in the future.

Hody seems to be a nice prof. she is but to certain people. She doesn't talk to everyone the same. She does talk alot. The work isn't bad that she gives. But what kind of concept is this!? She believes essays are an "A" or a "D"!
evryone else who made comments are morons.  Dr. Hody is the best teacher I have ever had at UMBC.

I agree with the last post. I have heard that this class has changed drastically from previous semesters, and right now it sucks. She said the department is changing the class. Completely unreasonable,even if it was a 400-level class.
Vague, rambling, gives 4 days to complete a research project, obscure test questions, massive reading assignments. I am an excellent student with a high GPA, and I hate this class.
Dr. Hody is incredibly knowledgable. She works without notes, and doesn't need them due to her vast reservoir of knowledge. She encourages open discussion and debate thus making her a great teacher.
No Comments
No Comments

Joan is problematic. She yelled and belittled students them in the front of the entire class, and has been known to do the same with faculty, too. While that doesn't meet the school's values of respect, there's been a lack of accountability (another value that's not upheld). Different race, different standards.

Shes definitely a challenging professor, but if you attend lecture and read the text you will mostly likely do well. She is an amazing lecturer, who is funny and incredibly caring. Como Tips: Study the case maps & clinical process sheets!!

Prof Davenport seems very nice in class, but her lectures do not prepare you for the exams at all! It seemed like no matter how hard you study, the exams felt impossible and it almost discouraged me from studying because studying didn't seem to help. She is a very harsh grader, and you will basically need to teach yourself the content. Not good

NURS310 was revised this semester and it seems to be more of a mess than it used to be. Lectures, PowerPoint slides and assigned textbook readings don't prepare even the smartest students for the exams. The lectures can feel like storytime rather than exam prep. Grades may have been lowest in this class compared to any other
She's awesome.  We only had her as a guest lecturer, but based on that I would totally sign up for anything she was teaching.

Dr. Davenport will appear to be "too cool for school" as the last rater described her, but she is definitely not out to help students succeed. Especially, CERTAIN students. I will just leave that to your imagination. Read the book, do the lab book, and pray you get a good clinical instructor, who can give you the practical experience to learn.
JDAV is too cool for school. She rocks.
Awesome....Makes class fun
the only time i read the book was for lab and i did fine on the test. If you take lab seriously then it will make the tests easy. A lot of lab is just like studying for the tests.

Shes pretty entertaining but like everyone else said, you HAVE to read the book. Attending class isnt important (as long as you read), but it isnt super painful either - she's interesting. Focus on LAB! You can really learn a lot there that is helpful for the tests if you don't just mess around the whole time.

Yes very lively lecturer but can also be very unprofessional/rough 2 students by embarrassing them in front of class if they say something stupid. She picks on people in the front row 2 do assessement on in front of whole class. Lectures do not cover what's on tests. Use book & wkbk. Prep for Val #4 from Day 1 & it will help prep 4 exams 2.

Yes very lively lecturer but can also be very unprofessional/rough to students by embarrassing them in front of class if they say something stupid. She picks on people in the front row to do assessement on in front of the whole class.

Health Assessment was a very entertaining class. She is an enthusiastic speaker makes class lively and has a good presentation but she doesn;t really go over technique and breezes over the lecture.  You will have to READ the book because you cant just go by lecture alone.  Most of the questions are from the book-- focus on the ABNORMALS

Lively lecturer.  Lecture does not cover entire book where exam questions come from so you have to read.  Some blanks in her notes so you have to attend her lecture.  She knows her stuff, but she wings her lectures on assessment techniques.
She is the cat's meow. She should be America's Top Model. I could not have passed gas without this class and her as my instructor.
I disagree. She is not cold at all. She just has a rough personality... actually, I enjoy dealing with her one-on-one. Very intelligent and competent. One of the best professors I have every had.
entertaining, definately knows her stuff. Engages class in discussion and makes you think. I agree woth other user, cold personality when dealing with one-on-one
Entertaining lectures.  Comes accross as very nice but one-on-one can be cold.

You could go either way with her. If she is in a good mood, you will like her. But catch her on a bad day and look out. She is however one of the most intelligent people I know and has a way of lecturing that actually kept my attention. Be warned Med/Surg is one of the most intense courses in our program.

Great professor. Davenport knows her stuff and wants you to learn, be a good nurse and most of all succeed. The rapport she builds with her students is very good and makes each person feel like she genuinely cares about them.

You get out what you put into this class.  Read the powerpoints and as much of the text as you can stomach to prepare for tests.  If you get a B, you're a genius. Start the hemo and analysis paper as soon as you can. Trust me. Davenport's a good help if you just go to her. She loves questions.

307/308 is a difficult course, it is expected in nursing...it is NOT impossible though. Be prepared and study and you will be okay. All professors in this course are incredibly knowledgeable and want you to do well!
Hard tests, but a great teacher!  Very easy to go to w/problems & questions.  Be prepared to learn lots.
No Comments
she is a great person, but her tests are a killer.

Tests are impossible to pass.  Directions are vague and unclear.  She doesn't explain herself and she is disorganized. She wants you to fail.  At least she tells jokes during lectures. That's what really matters.
Tests are extremely hard and sometimes are  impossible to do well on. She can be helpful at times, but expects you to know and understand every concept from the hurried-through lectures.
Very educated.  Tests are hard, and clinicals are hard, but expected in nursing.  If you have a problem you can go to her, but don't make her mad.  She is understanding and helps the best she can.
He really just wants to discuss during the lecture. As long as you read and memorize people's life stories, you should be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was one of my favorite professors at UMBC because he's very nice, he grades late work, and you can still earn an A for the late work he grades. His class was always fun and always makes you genuinely want to learn more. He is an understanding teacher especially if you're sick or missed class, he won't rush to give you a bad grade or attendance.

Honestly, he is very chill. Overall, he is really nice and gives all of the exams and assignments in advance so you can prepare for them. If you go to class and turn in the work you will do fine. Sometimes his power points can be long but otherwise I have no complaints
He is a funny guy, but he can really talk for such a long time. We had a midterm and a final and a long like 10 page paper and slideshow due at the end of the semester.

You might have to buy the books for class if you can't find the pdf online. He's a cool professor, cool lectures and he likes to make conversation. If you don't have the best memory or studying method, I suggest taking the online class because the exams are written in person. He's only a tough grader on the exams, but that's reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: My class this semester was in person and required 8 book reviews, 8 page research paper, midterm and final. The hardest part of this class was the exams because they were in person, on paper, all writing. He was very lenient with deadlines and grading on these exams though. He is funny and just wants students to learn. The book reviews were easy.

5 book reviews, midterm, final, and 8 page research paper. Lots of busy work but everything can be done through google. Easy grader, very lenient with due dates. A lot of writing tho, the lecture was ok. Easy elective but lots of easy busy work.

the amazing lectures i would take that with a grain of salt .he is really easy take late work and not as many book reports as i thought. understandable but didn't like some of the things he said there were rude and partition matter. easy to keep up with.

I had Professor Turner in Fall 2021. I'm just now writing my reviews. One of the best professors I have ever had. The class was really easy, fun, and had interesting lectures. Only downside is if you do not like reading, don't take this class. The class requires reading, but it's not that bad. Prof is very accommodating. Highly recommend this class

There is a lot of writing in this class, specifically, there is a book review about once a week and a final research paper. Professor Turner is cool and has a good sense of humor but he tends to be argumentative. He will play devil's advocate and challenge students' ideas when they participate.
His class easy if you keep up.
A lot of writing. Over 20+ pages of writing including the research paper. Very easy class but be prepared to write a lot.

Professor Turner is a really good teacher and if you like learning about problems in the black community or even why black people are so vocal on some issues you will definitely enjoy this class. There are book reviews however he's not a tough grader he just wants to know you read or understand them. Would definitely recommend!
Very good professor about 6 book reviews which can be done without reading. The midterm and final is easy can be done via google help.
He is the best. There are a lot of book review essays but he is not hard when he grades

I only rate when professors are either amazing/terrible. Turner is amazing. One of my favorite professors. He knows his stuff and is very friendly. He will lecture a lot but will engage you in the lectures. He likes participation and hearing different viewpoints. He gives out practice exams that look just like the real exams. Very easy A. 10/10.
Very good prof, you can tell he cares a lot about his students. The class was a lot of work at times but as long as you do the work and listen to grading feedback it's not that hard to get an A.

One of my favorite professors in the physics department! He cares deeply about his students and is ALWAYS there for help. I found the lectures were extremely useful for completing the lab reports. Also, even though lab is 3 hours, it never actually takes that long. You can tell he genuinely enjoys what he does and wants to see his students thrive.

He is very understanding to students and clearly loves what he does. He enables you to succeed and is very accessible & approachable. As with all lab classes, the lab reports take time, and it's never something to procrastinate on as you will not have enough time otherwise. But he gives the most digestible & pleasant experience for such a class.
Solid professor. There is a ton of writing associated with his class. However, I am sure that the skills I have gained in his class will be extremely handy some day.

Lectures are skippable if you know your statistics and physics 2. Labs are pretty interesting and usually we finished with 2 hours to spare, you must do a report for every lab but you get two weeks to do them. Very lenient grader on the final project and he brought snacks on presentation day. He's awesome and I love him. Makes a lab class fun.

One of the best professors in UMBC. I've been in this university for quite a while and can with confidence say that Dr. Gonzales is one of the most kind, caring, and smart professors out there. He always listens to student feedback and gladly helps with things unrelated to his class, be it other homework or life advice. Everyone I know loves him:)

A kind guy who wants you to learn physics. Be prepared for a lab report/analysis each week with difficult questions. There is an independent lab at the end where you work with 2-3 people. If you reach out to him, he is always willing to help. Gives extra credit sometimes.

Great professor! Took this course completely asynchronously and had no trouble at all, he's a proficient grader as well. As a freshman in my first semester, the course was interesting and easy to follow, definitely recommend taking it with him!

He's a decent lecturer, but he doesn't use slides so reviewing for exams is a bit tedious and it's hard to know what exactly his grading criteria is. Not all readings are used in exams or even discussed in class, and there are 7+ readings per week, so keeping up sometimes feels like a waste of time. Interesting content though!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 3 fairly hard (open note) exams but had the option of averaging first 2 for a grade on the 3rd. 1 paper. Attendance is mandatory and there are a lot of readings, but I think the discussions and lectures are worthwhile for learning the material. He is pretty funny as well and tells stories about his experiences which he ties back into the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Jenkins is a true student of philosophy. He promotes conversation that relates to all majors to connect with the lecture topics. Anyone looking for a philosophy elective would benefit greatly from his classes, no matter what major you may be pursuing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! As long as you read the books assigned you will be fine. Reading is really important, majority of his questions are from the lecture notes and the book so it's not like he makes this class hard to pass. He gives you everything and the rest is on you. Reply to 4 discussion posts (weekly quizzes). Everything is straight forward.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: I do not understand philosophy at all so this class was not fun for me, but if you like philosophy hopefully you'll enjoy it more. You have one quiz a week and sometimes a discussion where you have to respond to 4 times. There is a midterm and a final paper, and the midterm is 20 short answer questions for 2 hours which is a little difficult.

I loved Prof. Jenkins. I struggled a lot at the beginning of the semester, but I was able to get a B at the end. His lectures were a bit boring (I was falling asleep a lot) but they were interesting. He really helped me in the end with our final paper. I went to his office hours and he explained all the concepts for me and made sure I understood.

Professor Jenkins makes the class very engaging. It is important to take notes and pay attention for exams and the final paper. He is very helpful and accessible outside of class and connects with his students. He made lectures very fun and interesting.

Prof. Jenkins is a great professor. Most of the notes and info you need for essays are discussed orally in class, so attendance and participation is a must. He posts transcripts of his lectures on BB (super helpful). He's a fair grader, but should incorporate more reading checks on the topics discussed in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was a great professor, and I really enjoyed his lectures. The only problem I had was that your grade is solely based on three exams, attendance, and a final paper. Since I didn't do super well on one of the exams, I lost my ability to earn an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He comes off arrogant and lacking empathy. He claims that take-home exams can be completed in 75 minutes but requires so much detail that you end up spending many hours. If you leave out a detail that was not even asked in the question the whole question is marked wrong. He laughs at vegans/vegetarians and propagandizes capitalism whenever he can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is online and was taught asynchronously even though it has set meeting times. You watch a lecture every week, complete the corresponding quiz, and there are 6 discussions you have to complete throughout the semester as well. Everything is very easy and straightforward. Highly recommend this class for art and humanity credits.
Very easy class if you literally just do the work every week, professor Jenkins is really accessible outside of class.

Hands-down one of the best professors at UMBC. I took Philosophy 150 online, and he was available to help each time I had questions. His lectures were in PowerPoints. All you have to do is read the PowerPoint, read the textbook (even though I didn't), and take notes. As long as you go through the material provided, you should be fine!

Professor Jenkins is absolutely amazing and I would take his class again any day. The lectures are easy to understand and he really makes them fun and interactive. He is friendly and always helps with test preparations.  I never thought I would enjoy philosophy as much as I did. He is very fair with grading and does not want his students to fail.

Class was supposed to be discussion-based, and then he got annoyed with side conversations. So it turned into a lecture. Textbook was "required" but never used. Few really short group assignments, 1 exam, and a final paper. Easy A as long as you are engaged in class. Canceled class sometimes too. Sometimes funny. Knows what he's talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You would have to be self-motivated and super interested in ethics in order to stay awake in this class. The course itself is not challenging though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He seems really nice but he's the worst prof. He made me get a B just for .1 point. He promises you that he will bump high grades at the , all capppp.

It looks like Prof Jenkins is a good Prof for other classes, but for PHIL 346 he is pretty bad. Extremely snarky and pretentious attitude, boring lectures, and when you ask for help he just repeats the same thing that didnt make sense already. Not the worst Prof. Ive had, but definitely the most pretentious. Granted this was also a winter class.

Really great guy. For my class the only grades were for exams and attendance. Although there is some reading involved his class is not difficult and his lectures were great. Very funny and makes lecture fun.
had about 8 quizes with 55 extra credit and exam was easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really great guy and very laid back. All the material is presented to you early and he is very set on expectations. The assignments werent too much and I actually learned a lot without being overwhelmed.

Jenkins is an absolute awesome prof. Wish more mechanical engineering prof were like him. He genuine, promotes discussion and debate, and makes what could be the most boring 2 hours an enjoyable class. Show up, pay attention and take some notes, read the assigned textbook sections and you'll get an A. Anyone that's salty about their grade didnt try

Jenkins is a fantastic prof. he is aware that mech e's have to take this ethics course so he tries to make it as interactive and applicable as possible. students will say he is not receptive to other's opinions but he doesn't validate when people say things because that is not the point of philosophy discussions in general. best prof to take 251 w/
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is the best teacher to ever teach philosophy at UMBC. He explains everything in class very clearly. He uses many examples to help you understand the different philosophers and their theories because lets be honest philosophy is a very dull but he makes it very interesting! This is my second time taking philosophy AND I have never laughed as much

Don't skip class because attendance is a part of your grade. He is hilarious and his lectures are not hard to follow at all. If you pay attention in this class, take notes, and show up, it is an easy A.

Professor Jenkins is an amazing professor. For some philosophy can get boring real quick especially a 2 hour class but he found ways to make us laugh and keeps us engaged. The discussions were amazing and he was always open to other viewpoints. He understands you have other harder classes and doesn't stress you with too much work. Very fair grader!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He is a really good professor. PHIL 152 was super easy. He makes a study guide for all exams and goes over it in class. He averaged the first two exams and if you had a passing grade you did not have to take the 3rd exam if you did not want to- you just automatically receive the average grade of the first 2 exams for your third exam grade.

Cool professor  Logic is a very difficult class if you are not a math major. That said, he made the class bearable. Very clear grading criteria 3 online quizzes 3 exams (last one is optional) and a final. He has a lot of interesting stories and often will get carried away. Attendance is mandatory so you will need to show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Took Phil 100 over the winter semester. It was very short and there was 1 in class exam and the final was online, got As on both. Didn't need to buy the textbook or Platonic dialogues. Just listen and take notes in class and you will do fine. He also posts his own notes online which is helpful for weekly online quiz. Easy class and short.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I had a hard time but he seemed to grade fairly until the final exam. It was all proofs (the hardest thing we learned all year) and if you did something wrong on 1 line (the average was 6 or 7 lines per problem), it was all wrong. Half the class got below a C. My grade went from a high C to a D. Avoid Logic w/him if you can, esp. if you hate math.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great guy - very funny and makes what I consider to be a dry subject very interesting. Lots of reading but don't worry, he goes over everything in class (so if you don't read or didn't understand you won't miss much). Only exams and a final paper (plus attendance grade), but if you do his study guides and ask questions the exams aren't bad at all
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Jenkins is super funny and a great professor. He's really straightforward with what he wants, and grades pretty easily since he knows you're only in this class because its required. If you study for exams and pay attention in class, you're golden
Funny professor. I liked him. Gives an easy A if you show up to every class and take notes. Its more important what he lectures on in class than what you read, but he tests on some of both.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor! Clear and quick when it comes to grading. Promotes in class discussion. The class is broken down into attendance/participation, online quizzes, and exams. The exams were short answer and mainly focus on material discussed in class and in the notes. Notes are posted online. If you show up and pay attention its an easy A.

As a professor Mr. Jenkins was okay. His exams and quizzes were very difficult. Deductive logic is a difficult class but he did not go out of his way to make the class easy. He tried his best at teaching the material though, I don't think that is what he usually teaches. He is probably better at teaching other classes. Also, he is a hard grader
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Really funny guy, I really enjoyed the way he taught. Always making jokes, trying to keep the class engaged. There are 3 tests, 1 final paper, and attendance. Even though I showed up to every class, I still struggled heavily with all 3 tests and the paper. If you're looking for an EASY A&H class, I'd look elsewhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Always had a humorous story to tie together the lesson, and made the class interesting and engaging. Willing to go off on tangents, but ultimately taught the necessary material in a clear, concise way. Perfect introduction to the field of philosophy, or just to fulfill a credit. 3 written answer tests, a final paper, and participation required.

If you like ethics, you will LOVE this class.  Readings are tied to real-world questions and thoroughly discussed. Tests are both comprehensive and fair. Jenkins is a great instructor, will take another class with him.

Show up, pay attention, take notes, and study. Do those things and you will be fine. I personally did not like his teaching style. His choice of language in explaining things is a bit... messy and difficult to follow.

Professor Jenkins is an amazing professor! His lectures are interesting and makes philosophy very enjoyable. He always told us what was to be expected on an exam so we could study efficiently. Make sure you go to class everyday or you won't get all of the material, but also because he is hilarious! I would highly recommend this class to anyone!

Jenkins is very engaging and interesting when giving lectures; that being said, he rarely writes anything down, so pay attention in class and write down everything. Exams are fair, assuming you took good notes and studied them. One paper at the end of the semester. You get points for attendance, so show up. Overall good guy and entertaining.

Her lectures were comprehensive for the topics, she will answer questions if any students have any. The class projects are not made by her however and tend to be very difficult to code. Her exams are easier than the other professors and doesn't assign homework. Don't let this fool you as there is no point buffer because of no homework. Study!!!

Overall chill professor, would recommend attending lectures in person because notes are handwritten and difficult to understand. Exams are relatively easy if you pay attention during lecture. Is very engaging and encourages students to ask questions. Responds to emails very quickly and is accessible outside of class.

She writes on a chalkboard, which makes it easy to take notes. She grades leniently; I thought I failed an exam once only to get a B. Projects not by her. Lectures are important or you'll get lost; Notes aren't the clearest. Very understanding and gave me project extension when I had family emergency. +4% extra credit overall. Only teaches in fall.

Def. take her for CMSC 341 her explanations are spot on! Uses chalk to draw examples on board and knows the content and wants the student to actually learn. Attendance was not mandatory but i still attended each class b/c of how the amount of content she covered in each class with thorough explanations. Responds pretty quickly too on emails. Chill

She's a lenient grader, cheat sheets are allowed for exams, and gives very few homework's. Now, if you don't like professors that just talk and write on the board, you will not like her. I however, prefer this method of teaching so I quite enjoyed this class.

Prof Dey gets a bad rep but in all honesty she does the best she can. All 341 Profs will suck bc the class is hard. She tries to be understanding and has extra credit opportunities, she doesn't swarm you with HW bc projects are already hard. Her tests are not difficult as long as you either study well or go to class. She's a great prof just try.
Really not great.

Lectures are monotonous and boring, hard not to fall asleep during class. Exams are extremely difficult and often nothing like the lectures or even what the professor says is on the exam. Other sections got much easier exams. Random pop quizzes during class. Very frustrating class, especially when prof states X,Y,Z will be on exam and it isn't.

Shes knowledgeable, but I cannot recommend anyone take her for 341. Monotonous, boring lectures. Often doesnt have the presentation written ahead of time. If you have her in room 102 in the engr. building, get ready to kill your eyes as you attempt to read her scribblings on the dirty whiteboard. Put up review slides at 2am the day of the midterm

Newish prof. Dey taught 491-crowd computing. There's no final, but a semester group project. Make sure you get good teammates for your group project, and stick with a topic that is achievable (less work) within the scope of a 3-credit course. The midterm is lecture-based, so take good notes. Overall interesting material, but lots of reading papers.

Dey is not bad, she was a new prof F2020 semester. 3 ethical analyses which the criteria was really vague but they were graded very leniently. You have groups for debates and the final paper. Class was alright, not great but not the worst. Her quizzes are straight from the book which has the answers in it so they were easy.
So sweet and caring, genuinely cares about her students. Grading is super generous compared to other professors in the department. Getting an A in this class is very realistic in this class
Generous grading, caring and friendly prof
Great proffessor. Can sometimes be very repetitive, but she knows her stuff. Also a fashionista at heart.

Professor Madan will straight up tell you exactly what you need to know for the exams. there is never any surprises. She has taught this class many times and knows the concepts students often don't understand. So she will sometimes spend 30 minutes explaining something that you didn't even realize you didn't understand.

Poor lecturer, does not explain things into detail. Wants students to succeed so exams are not very hard but again very poor at explaining the material. Also has a thick accent which makes things harder to understand.

Prof Madan is fairly good. She was just okay at explaining new things and used class time to just go over a bunch of examples. The best part of the class was what you were expected to understand. Deadlines were clear and the tests were very representative of the material studied. TA was pretty bad. Took partially online during COVID crisis
Incredibly nice. She is very approachable and is of great help in office hours. If you understand all of the homework and lecture slides, you will do well in this class.

Prof. Sidhu has many slides. Very monotonous and boring lecture. Reads off of slides and his accent is hard and because he is old so sometimes he just mumbles when he does not want to explain. Half the class stopped coming to class in the 1st week. Easy grading of assignments though. 

Exams Qs are from Hw / study guide problems.

Sidhu changes the assignment with days left until its due. Homework assignments are vague, and you need to be a mind reader to understand the expectations/requirements. Want to actually learn something? Be prepared from Sidhu to pass the buck and tell the students read about key concepts. The mid-term was 4 questions worth 40 points.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors at UMBC. Never took a single class during an entire semester and only asked for presentations from students. Never uploaded grades or feedback on time and directly gave a grade on C+. Never responds to emails, never helps students, and has not given any feedback about the grades either. AVOID any class under him.

STAY AWAY FROM PROF IF YOU CAN. Changed proj requirements days before it was due, put a student on blast for asking questions, implies proj requirements, grading is ruthless, dodges questions, hardly answers email, gives 1 day for assignment questions, brags about tenure so does what he wants. S21 reached out to higher-ups with little to no results

Professor Sidhu had no idea how to run a class. The lectures were worthless so you basically need to teach yourself using Google. Horrible professor, it'll cause you lots of unnecessary headaches, just don't take a class with him!

This professor is clueless. Doesn't even answer questions during lecture even though we could see them popping up on his screen.

What was evident to me after two weeks in CMSC681 was that Dr. Deepinder Sidhu has little to no interest in teaching. "Oh you didn't draw a diagram, -1"

This professor is one of the worst professor's I have seen at UMBC. First, he only have 6 powerpoints uploaded during the whole semester. There are about 160 slides in each lecture. One of the worst instructors I've ever had at UMBC. Do not take any course under him.

Absolutely horrible. Generally just puts zero effort into the class. Would recommend just not taking this class, no matter how much you like networks, as you'll learn much more from a book than from this man.
worst class ever. How such course and professor exist, on the master's level is a great riddle to solve.

This was the worst class in my whole academic career. The Professor is totally unaware of advancement in the field he was teaching. There was no proper structure to the class. Honestly, my high school classes were more articulated than this class and made more sense.

This class isn't as hard as many people are saying. I assume it depends on how good you are at studying off of powerpoints and cramming for tests. By far worst prof taken at UMBC bar none in cs dept. This class is very easy in terms of hw (only 5 short ones) but the tests were graded very hard by TA's. Not terrible but you won't learn much. He speaks in a quiet monotone so be sure you listen up. Exams directly from slides and are super easy if you listen and brush up on the slides. His attendance at his own office hours is variable but he is a nice person, especially one-on-one. Recommend as a GPA boost. Take him over other options for CMSC 481.

Probably the worst class I've taken at UMBC. His lectures are extremely boring and the content is dated. reviews.comment: I think Prof. Sidhu was quite knowledgeable but his lectures were really boring; he speaks in a monotone. If you pay attention in class then the class is an easy A. We had 3 simple homeworks and 2 slightly difficult projects. The exams were hard because he does not provide review guides.

I'm not sure why people are complaining in this class. His exams are fair and straightforward.  I was scared at first because of all the information we have to learn but the exams so far are more general.  No complaints here!

Absolutely horrible. Gives long uninformative lectures, and generally just puts zero effort into the class. Would recommend just not taking this class, no matter how much you like networks, as you'll learn much more from a book than from this man.

One of the worst instructors I've ever had at UMBC. Cancels class often, lectures are useless as he just reads the slides to you, and he starts counting attendance once people stop showing up (which doesn't take long). Exams have no study guides and will ask you a few specific questions on random info out of 100s of slides to parse.

Sidhu doesn't care, at all. The entire class is just your team working on a semester long project, which is anything of your choosing. He won't teach you anything, and showed up only half the time, maybe less.

Worst professor I have ever had by far! Not easy to understand, speaks in a monotone, incredibly boring material being presented by a incredibly boring professor. No textbook so the only way to learn is to listen to him. Terrible. Just awful. Booooooo!

Absolutely one of the worst professors I've had. Lecture is pointless, all he does is read the slides right to you. Exams are terrible, after 1000+ slides of material they were 8 questions and 3 questions on specific, mostly unimportant information. Grade was 90% two exams and 10% two projects.

Laziest professor at UMBC. No textbook. No slides. Leaves immediately after class. I felt like I had no resources to learn. Sidhu is good at teaching and the TA is decent, but I need a text or slides or something. He goes way to fast to write it all down. Lenient grader. This class is 80% memorization. Helpful to record lecture. Wiki is your bff.
great teacher
great teacher, he did teach from his writing but it was very beneficial. i learned a lot from his class!
He mostly teaches from his own, outdated papers for the first month of class.  Overall for a graduate course he taught nothing of use and the class was a complete waste of time.  Awful.

I think Dr.Sidhu is a articulate professor. Dr. Sidhu expresses himself easily in clear and very effective language. And also, tries to comprehend with other students. OVERALL I THINK HE IS A VERY INTELLIGENT and KNOWLEDGEABLE PROFESSER.
I am currently taking him for computer networking.  His tests are straightforward concept definitions.  The programming projects are fairly simple.
he is very sweet and his lectures were good, he tends to ramble though so you might get lost. lectures are helpful to come to. expecations on quizzes and exams are very clear

Dr. Koirala is extremely kind and caring and is very willing to help other students outside of class. The lectures are very clear and he gives practice problems that very closely resemble the quizzes/exams. Extra credit questions on quizzes were also very easy. Lectures can be a bit boring at times cause he can overexplain things.

His lectures were mostly him reading off the slides which made it useless to attend lectures. He was not engaging in presenting the information. He did have a lot of practice in between the slides which were helpful, especially since the quizzes and exams were exactly like the practice.

Take this bichem class with him and Aaron smith! His first half was really good he made things very understandable and you can always email him if you didnt understand a topic. He is a little monotone so lectures can be boring sometimes esp for the 2 hours of class, but his exams are not hard if you study and he made biochem easy to remember.10/10

Professor is nice and has a sense of humor. Lectures are pretty boring but they're not for a grade. His lectures can be confusing sometimes but overall not bad. Quizzes and exams are easy if you study.

He is one of the best professors in the Chemistry department! He made the information easily digestible and was very clear in his expectations. I'm not a big fan of chemistry but he made me love the class. The topic is not easy but honestly, put some effort in and you will be fine. He's very understanding and he wants us to succeed!

BESTIES Dr. Koirala actually made me like Biochemistry and I hate chemistry. He was a really enjoyable professor to have, and everything was really straight forward. All the information on exams came from HW and ppt lectures. He tends to over explain certain topics, but I'd rather that than someone who doesn't explain at all. He's great!
Professor Dillon is probably the best lecturer I have ever encountered in UMBC so far; hes also very nice and comfortable to talk to.

Professor Dillon is a pretty decent lecturer. Everything made sense the first time he explained it, and he puts a lot of effort into making sure students understand the material presented. Mr. In That Regard Himself! In all seriousness Professor Dillon is an amazing teacher and honestly cool dude. "In that regard"

Dr. Dillon is a great professor and a nice guy. he might go a little fast at times, but he's really understanding and will slow down and explain things again if you ask. there was a tuesday lecture and a thursday quiz, and a few exams, all in person. the best thing about his class is that he records every lecture and posts it in a timely manner.

Quizzes are hard and you need to go to lecture to do remotely good on them, lecture will make you sleepy.
Harsh grader for midterm and final, but does build in extra credit(30 points extra on 250) and you only need an 85% for an A

Hes an honest teacher, very good in my opinion. Just a nice man who knows the material very well and is very patient with the whole thing going online.

He's super stingy with the points that's the reason for the curve

If you suck at notetaking (as I do) run away from him. fast.  Though he is a pretty nice guy.  Just hard to learn from.

Just go to class and you will be fine. No textbook. You only need an 82% for an A, and he adds extra credit to each test. He goes over in class exactly what will be on the test and provides old tests which he sometimes uses the same questions and just changes the numbers. Good professor.

Great professor! He's pretty hard but very clear on what he expects from exams. Don't buy the textbook. Take good notes and go to the review sessions before the test and just do the review problems he gives out and you'll get an A. He also curves a lot.

Prof. Coates is probably one of the hardest and worst out of all. He grades on a bell curve and there is no extra credit. Very poor professor.  He failed 75% of the students on the midterm and there was only one A. After speaking to many students we believe that he is worth reporting; certainly on grounds for discrimination. Poor professor, leader and mentor. Save your money and take a different class.

He blabs about a bunch of stuff that isn't in the textbook (save yourself the money and don't buy it) and that you type it in Wiki and it doesn't exist. This teacher is terrible...when u go to office hours and ask him question , u get more confused than what u already are....its seem that he doesnt really know to explain the material from his class.....he looks nice but what does it matter if he doesnt explain and get u to know the stuff that u r suppose to know....

this teacher is so bad..... beside of being a hard a class already...he makes it more hard , he doesnt curve and if u get 69% , he will still give a D....u must no take a class with a him.....for the senior who are planning to take econ 475 financial investment....dont even bother.....
He is hard teacher.  Don't take his class.  He grades hard too.

Lecture is unclear and boring, the material is hard if you don't have a good enough background. The only things I learned from are from the book by myself. a word of advice, dont take his class

Kind of boring, but you can learn quite a bit from him if you can pay attention.  The online problem sets are almost 'gimmie' points.  There's no curve, but there are almost always mroe points available than the max on the sylabus (ex: max grade can be 575 / 500)

One of the best professors i have ever had!!!! always willing to answer questions and review old exams. class is a little boring. need to know a few formula....knowing econ 374 will help soooo much! there is a book review,4-5 multi. choice problem sets, 2 midterms and a final. he give lots of chances for extra credit.Take notes, READ the text!!!

I dont think it is a hard class, lectures are boring its true, but if you study just a little you will be fine.(B)If you ask question, he will explain the material. He is not a great professor, but not a worst either.

his class is the WORST CLASS i have ever taken ..dosent knows what he is teaching just writing on the board and people sitting with blank faces dont bother him. thinks it is his PHD level class and boosts about his work..HE IS NUMBER 1 IN DISCHOURAGING PEOPLE.

Very good professor, you can tell that she wants each student to succeed. She goes through the slides very fast, but she gives a lot of extra resources that help with studying for tests. There is one small quiz each week, 2 midterms, and a final. Do the homework each week because she uses a lot of the questions on her tests.

"Professor" tries to "teach" by reading and going through slideshows as fast as possible without giving any time to process what is happening then expects you to be able to memorize 3-4 ginormous chapters before the exam. Everything that she would go over and had uploaded on blackboard would be not even close to whats on the exam or weekly quizzes

ECON101 is not an easy credit when you consider how much memorization & HW you need to do. However, Dickson tells you what to expect to be on tests, quizzes are given on a schedule. Her lectures are alright. She's helpful with questions in class. The top grade on a quiz/test becomes 100% and lower grades go up by the difference (95->100, 70->75)

One of the nicest teachers, but the quizzes for a 101 class were a little bit rough. She explains topics well and is more than willing to answer questions. If your looking for a easy credit, do NOT take this class.

She's a great teacher! Show up to class and do your part, you can get an A in the class. She curves all the exams and quizzes and homework. There is a lot of homework! About 48 questions each week but also you get unlimited try's on the homework. Just be prepared to study a lot. Also i recommend going to office hours! It's very helpful!

reviews.comment: She was an absolute sweetheart.  Her quizzes were pretty simple and as long as you read the textbook and pay attention during the lecture, you're sure to get an 80-100% on your quiz.  The exams are little tricky though, but she is super understanding and sweet.

Prof. Dickson is a great professor. She's passionate about economics and tries her best to make it interesting. The homework is on Pearson with unlimited tries, the quizzes are easy, just do the homework and read your notes. She goes over past topics a lot and makes the topics easy to understand. Attendance isn't required but it's suggested.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr.Dickson is a good professor and is a really nice person. She gives out weekly quizzes but they are mainly to encourage people to come to class. She goes over material multiple times and is very accessible through office hours. She makes a pretty uninteresting course such as intro econ interesting with real life applications and funny stories.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is so sweet as a woman but a lot of her lectures consisted of her just reading off of her powerpoint. There are weekly quizzes that consist of about 7 questions, super easy if you just watch a youtube video on what the topic is right before the class. The tests are weighted a lot but she curves so it's okay.

reviews.comment: she is a kind person to meet with, but the lectures are pretty slow. the quizzes can be worded oddly and tricky. just read the textbook. She does give curves for exams. extra credit doesn't exist here.
She is very sweet, but the lectures are not very informative. The homework was not difficult. However, her questions on quizzes and exams are quite tricky.
Just read off the powerpoints and kind of sounds like she is always about to cry....coughs into her mic too...

She's very nice, but she just reads the powerpoint so I stopped going to lecture. material itself isn't that hard to understand, but the few chapters especially the graphs were kind of hard. Homework is easy and simple, but the tests and quizzes are tricky and hard. If she didn't curve the grades, I would've failed.

She makes understanding material easier as she repeats information a lot and reviews for quizzes and tests. The homework is very helpful for learning and studying. Drops the lowest quiz grade and curves grades. Gives lots of opportunities to raise grade. Not the most interesting class, but helpful and informative.

Unless this class is mandatory for your degree, this is not a class you should take for GEPs. She expects in depth knowledge of all course material, which is understandable. However, for a 101 class the content, what is expected of students, and homework load is unreasonable. I had 400 level courses this semester that I've found much easier.

She's very friendly and wants her students to succeed. Will help you out with any conceptual misunderstanding. Unfortunately, perhaps due to the online format, she did not engage her students very well. Classes were redundant if you did the reading and homework. Quizzes and tests had problems exactly like the homeworks, and she did curve grades.
Her lectures are ppt heavy, but it was easy. Her tests are from past homework and previous tests just memorize them. If you ask her for feedback, she will help you.

reviews.comment: Nobody listens to her because everyone will get confused. Just read by yourself or get a group of friends and learn it by yourself.
the teacher is really bad. she does not know how to teach. do it by yourself and youll get an A.

She isn't great. The lectures aren't worth attending since you'll need to teach yourself the material anyway. Just read the textbook and go to her office hours if you need help since she is extremely helpful there (but not in lectures).

It was a horrible class, her test are hard, she does not know how to teach.

reviews.comment: Pay attention in lecture and its an easy A. You have one easy paper to write and occasional my econlab hw. There are really easy quizzes in class that are a few multiple choice questions. The lectures are interesting but it is heavily based on the PowerPoints

She curves the quizzes and tests, drops the lowest hw and quiz so don't worry TOO much
