reviews.comment: She writes out the important concepts on the board and reviews the book during class. Theres one quiz a week and one homework due a week. Usually the homework is about 50 questions or less. I recommend to sit in front so you can hear her. Shes also very helpful one on one. She wants you to succeed so shell help as much as she can.

Covers a lot of material in her class, you will basically study the whole book. Make sure to take notes, but also to read the chapters, because some questions in the exams are from the book. She explains pretty well and is very accessible during office hours.
hard to hear her. her is laugh is unbearable. its like a annoying evil laugh. she is not understanding at all. talks about her husband a lot. she makes an easy class super hard.

Lisa is a nice person and is approachable if you need help. However, her teaching style is pretty bad for microeconomics. She rushes through material and doesn't explain concepts well. Had 3 tests during semester and she makes up all questions so be ready to teach yourself the material alot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Alright class. Managed to get an A fairly easily, but she gives out a ton (more than I've ever seen) of different readings which you're expected to understand for the exams. Not hard, but a good bit of material. She doesn't give great feedback and takes forever to grade things. It's an alright class as long as you take notes and study a bit.
pretty terrible. it takes FOREVER to get grades back. her lectures can be confusing, they arent very well prepared and she makes mistakes often.
Most helpful of all my professors, very straight forward about information on the test, takes questions before tests and quizzes, goes over information clearly and uses tons of examples.
overall great professor. Would recommend to anyone taking economics. Very easy to understand and if you show up to class then you will definitely pass with an A.

Most annoying laugh ever.  Takes a class that should be easy and makes it unnecessarily difficult.  Hands out at minimum 5 packets a day and expects you to memorize each one.  Seems to know the material well but does a poor job of teaching it.  Poor explanations to the problem sets.  Hope you like teaching yourself from the textbook.

She's very nice and willing to help you if you need it. If you attend her class, take notes, and do your myeconlab hw, you should be able to get a good grade. She's pretty lenient on grading, gives curves on the exams and drops quizzes. Great professor. I recommend her.

Do not take her! she is not really good at teaching. she is messy and speaks too softly for a large class. Her test are hard. The book that she requires id REALLY expensive for a 101 class and is not really helpful. She curves because she knows that her class is hard.
Awkward laugh. Try sitting in the front of a large class because it can be hard to hear her. Make sure to take good notes since she doesn't use powerpoints. Tests are not too bad. She does curve.

First off, her laugh is almost unbearable. Take her class and you will soon learn what I mean. She cannot compute simple math equations and often would ask the class to help her or the class would have to correct her work (uh, aren't you the one with the PhD?). The class is not hard, and she curves, but aside from that she is a hassle to deal with.

I'm taking her this semester. Come to class. She gives study guides that are helpful and be sure to go over quizes and old mid terms because she uses them on her exams. Curves everything. Her laugh is hilarious and she tries to make sure everyone passes. She's not that bad!! Just study and come to office hours
She definitely is not the best teacher I have ever had, but for sure not the worst.  I would describe her as an average level professor.  Just go to class and pay attention, you should be fine.

Overall very good, can get tripped up by questions sometimes and can come off unclear, but dont be afraid to ask for clarification. Gives you a review packet for the exams with everything you need to know and has plenty of office hours, very helpful.  Homework every few weeks is easy and extremely helpful.  Very informative for a 101 class.
Great teacher. Explained everything in concise, plain language that was easy to follow. She made sure to answer questions and was very helpful during her office hours.
If you take good notes and come to class it should be easy.  Fortunately she is usually pretty entertaining in class so it is easy to follow.  She usually will curve a test so those are not hard.

Try to avoid this professor at all cost, horrible teacher. She never grades in time. She never answered any three of my emails. Her whiny voice and annoying laugh makes it hard to listen to speak. She gives big curve since people usually don't do so well as a result of her horrible teaching. DON'T BUY THE BOOK -- EVERYTHING IS ON MYECONLAB!!!

She's really a great teacher. She writes everything she says up on a white board, so there is no way you can't get all of the information. If you have a question, she'll stop and re-explain for you. She gives handouts that are helpful and a good way to study. And she gives good curves on tests. 1 midterm, 1 final, quizzes and an easy essay.
An outstanding, clear, thoughtful professor who knew how to engage the class.  Went a bit slow on Unit 1 so that we didn't fully cover unit 3, but otherwise knows how to present material well.

She's a really nice person (and even brought in candy,) but she tends to get scattered in all of her thoughts. Her tests are extremely difficult because they focus on application whereas we only learn broad concepts in class. I wouldn't recommend her; she's just an average teacher who gets through the material.
shes pregnant. and balls to wall about econ!!!!!!
She KNOWS HER ECON!  Very good teacher.  I will remember Microeconomics for the rest of my life because of her, GREAT TEACHER.  I will recommend her to anyone!

She never answers anyone questions properly, only talks around the subject for a bit and always seems to be dazed. Although what she says may be true, she doesn't deliver it in a comprehensible manner. She makes awkward jokes and doesn't really discuss the details of exams, quizzes or assignments. Teaching's not her thing.

Prof. ****son is very bubbly and always smiling. She goes through all of the material in detail and will stop to answer questions and explain concepts along the way. Her quizzes are OK, you will do well if you study the material. Her tests are HARD, but once again, study and you will at least get a C. I would recommend her to anyone taking any econ
Teaches super well and easy to learn material. No exams but projects instead and attendance matters.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Very outgoing and caring. She gives very detailed feedback on your papers/projects and even if you have major mistakes, she doesn't take off many points for it as long as you show effort. She'll ask you to get 2 books, one about printing and leaves of grass. Only get leaves of grass. Lot of the readings you can skip

Great professor, very understanding and social towards her students. She didn't give out large amounts of work and is very lenient on her grading. She gives great advice so if you apply it for your next paper/project you will surely receive a better grade

This class was very easy and honestly you can get by without doing some of the readings as long as there's no work to go with it. There are some papers but very little of them can't be done within an hour. Professor DiCuirci is great and passionate about what she does and I would love to be in another one of her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I've been in college for almost 10 years and Prof. DiCuirci is one of the smartest, loveliest profs. I've had three of her classes. She really cares about her students and the things she teaches. She never assigns an unreasonable amount of work, and it never feels like busy work. Her projects are usually a lot of fun to do. All around a solid prof.

Amazing teacher. The texts can be daunting and boring, but she really enjoys them and makes it interesting. Her class is theory-based and research heavy, and her assignments can be vague. However, just engage with her and ask her questions and you'll be fine because she does not grade harshly at all. Highly recommended. She is a lovely person.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Dicuirci is really fun! Her lectures were really engaging and easy to follow (and she posts them online!). You have to write a lot of small papers for this class which can get easy to lose track of! But overall she was really fun! Also, she has great fashion. She appreciates people who participate, so please do the reading!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Though ENGL 302 s a dry class due to the subject material, Professor DiCuirci is a great teacher that genuinely cares about her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Stimulate, direct, and pace interaction with the class, encourages independent thought/criticism, uses wit and humor effectively, superior public speaker, knows whether or not the class is following the material/students motivation, more than fair, approachable and a valuable source of advice. Strongly recommend.

Explains clearly, well prepared, makes difficult topics easy to understand and memorable, energetic and dynamic person, enjoys teaching, conveys a love of the field, and has an aura of self-confidence, gives the student a sense of the field: its past, present, and future directions, the origins of ideas and concepts. Highly recommend.

Great, personable, engaging professor. Sometimes her writing assignments are a little bit vague and youre not 100% sure what shes looking for, but once you get the hang of her grading, its easy. Extremely accessible outside of class and very willing to help in anyway.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Professor DiCuirci was one of the only literature professors I enjoyed as an English major on the CT track. She is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about her work. She is always willing to provide feedback and is fairly available outside of class. Her free writes can be fairly challenging but often produce true and meaningful lit. analysis .

This is a tough theory based class but she makes a very boring subject matter more interesting. She is super helpful & understanding. Its not an easy A but there are opportunities to get points. Only negative is sometimes you don't go over what is assigned. But allows you to get away with not necessarily doing the reading on the day it is assigned.
She''s a very kind professor and is willing to help you when you''re confused about something. Really enjoyed this class and learning about colonial history with her.

She's great. She's nice, intelligent, and kept my attention the entire class: even if it got a little stale. Typical two papers, midterm, final, some quizzes and a participation grade. She loves participation too. Take her and you won't regret it.

She was an excellent well-organized teacher. It could get boring sometimes, but she's very likeable, so you'll get through it. I loved her as a person, and she really smart, knows her subject matter, and is excited about it. She can only become a better teacher with more experience so definitely take her class. She's great!

She is very understanding and enthusiastic about the material, however she can be overwhelming and not always clear with her wording or assignments. She also grades based on her opinion not based on a rubric which can be frustrating. She loves participation however if you do well on the writing assignments you'll still do well.
Dr. DiCuirci is an incredible professor. Very interested in the material and her students' responses to said material. Very concise syllabus and interesting course!
I had her for two classes, and enjoyed both. Her class can be challenging but if you keep up with the reading and free-writes you'll do fine. I highly recommend in-class participation...she loves it!
Very passionate about the material. A lot of reading, but it's rewarding. Two papers, two exams, plus easy reading quizzes and free-writes.

We're given prequizzes to watch before units like Phys, Bio, etc. Next, with group, do a protocol sheet where you hypothesis & write how you will do your experiment. Then, do experiment. Lastly, you record results. You're given HW too. Extremely easy class (HS lab course).

Only bad side is professor talks alot, which hinders from doing expriments.

Dr. Cambraia is one of the best teachers I've ever had! She's very sweet and is always willing to help anyone! Felt like I learned more from her than my intro chem lab. Wish she taught more classes! Assigned lab reports, but gave extensions if you asked. Genuinely wants students to learn and succeed! Definitely take her is you have the opportunity!

Microbiology is a class you have to study for. She makes it bit bearable and it is possible to get an A if you put in the work. We work with groups a lot in this class but as someone that hates group work, it is definitely not bad. She is funny and helps outside of class if you ask. Definitely love her class! 100% recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: i love prof munoz!!! literally the best professor at UMBC, so sweet and caring. she is very understanding that you have other obligations outside her class she is very lenient. her class consist of reading the assigned readings and talking about them, a few quizzes and a group and solo project. if you know spanish you will get an A. def reccomend!
Great professor. was amazing at teaching and kept thing clear simple and fun. If you know Spanish already easy A

She is a very nice teacher if something is happening with you, she will help you out and even give you more time if you are overwhelmed. Tip for quizzes the day before a quiz ask her what to study sometimes the quizzes are questions, we have done in class.

Just about that sweetest professor I've ever had. She's so caring and forgiving and really understands the state of the world atm. She takes a lot of interest in her students and I wish all my professors could be like her.

If you want to progress in Spanish, are serious about your degree and doing the assignments then you want this professor and you will have no complaints. She is very earnest and sincere and works hard for the class and the students. It is clear that she is devoted to teaching  and giving each of her students respect and a chance to succeed.
Great teacher! She made the semester worth it. She does expect you to do the work, but it isn't that bad. I wish I had her for all my classes.

Muñoz is new, but amazing. She is extremely helpful and wants the students to do well. Very fair grader. She's extremely intelligent and assigns some difficult readings, but isn't pretentious or patronizing. She is overall an amazing professor and made the semester a lot better. Oh yeah, she's beautiful, too!

There was plenty of work but it was nothing crazy and she was very flexible about due dates if you talked to her. She gives great feedback on essays and other work, and wants to make sure you know the topic before quizzes or exams. She was really a wonderful professor.

She is new at UMBC. Discussions in the classroom are a great way to clear up any questions you have about the readings, and this has been my favorite part about this course. The readings had been great so far. If you go to class , you will be fine.

Professor Dixon is a good choice to take CMSC201 if you already have coding experience. If you don't then it will seem overwhelming and you will need to take time to learn it outside the lecture. Pretty good professor, I recommend it.

This class is easy if you already had coding experience before taking the class, if not then it will seemed overwhelming and pretty difficult but professor Dixon makes the class enjoyable and makes it "easier" to understand when you're learning programming for the first time if you go to his lectures.

I didn't really attend the lectures because I already knew the course material, and it was never worth my time. Taking from the class discord, it looks like if you aren't already fully prepared with the course material beforehand, this class is quite hard. The time that I did go to his lecture, he was pretty charismatic and funny. A decent guy.

Good lecturer stuck in a badly designed course. Exams written by other professors did not match what was taught. Writing code on paper in 2025 is outdated and unfair. Email responses were slow or nonexistent. The teaching was solid. The system around it failed.

Class went well for the most part but the biggest issue is that he couldn't care less about how his students do individually. I had multiple occurrences where I wasn't able to turn something in for a legitimate reason and the response was "tough luck". If you want to do well in this class, pray you don't have any issues in your personal life.

Lectures were great, some were fast paced, but much better than average. Live coding examples very insightful. Online content was invaluable. He's very caring/empathetic but understandably has to assert his boundaries. Projects were cool (criteria too vague) and exams fair, but answers really should go on same page as questions. Overall: 9.2/10

I failed my first time. 202 is brutal by design. Class is in C++. Dixon is a good lecturer, great at answering questions. Very wise with C++. I do believe he cares about his students in a tough love sort of way. 5 projects back to back, 2 weeks per. 2 midterms on paper. If you can legitimately pass this class, you're meant for this stuff. If not...

Fast lectures, if you go to office hours often then you will be fine. You need a B for CMSC majors, and I recommend to not underestimate the exam difficulty, study for the exam a week ahead and get ahead on the projects because they aren't easy either. Stay in office hours constantly and ask any question during lectures, he will answer.

P.S. I took CMSC 462, but it's not an option in the drop-down menu. He is good at giving lectures, but has little empathy for students. You cannot ask for extra credit, extensions, or any flexibility with him, or he will get immediately suspicious and blunt (speaking for myself and others). Tests are confusing, but he is lenient with grading.

He's THE BEST professor to go with for 202. His in-person lectures were fast-paced and difficult to keep up with, but I found going over his prerecorded lectures and code videos helped reinforce topics. Exams were brutal (class average was next to failing), so start proj early and do well. Take advantage of extra credit and office hours.

Absolute GOAT. He made CMSC202 super fun. He makes all the project, and every project was so intuitive. He teaches so well and answers every question so fluently. I have just finished my 2nd semester and I can confidently say that he is the best professor I have encountered at UMBC so far.

This is the "weed-out" class of CMSC, so expect it to be difficult. Dixon is effective and fair. BB course is very organized, has video lectures, slides, and live coding for each topic. He explains concepts well. Just don't procrastinate projects, and start studying for exams a week in advance.
Explains things too quickly and doesn't always check if the class is keeping up. Office hours were helpful, but the lectures could be clearer.
He was so passive-aggressive in class, and the one time I interacted with him, he was rude for no reason. You will have to learn everything yourself. avoid him at all costs
This guy is just not a nice understanding person at all

Dixon is great. The class itself was never too bad and he was a very good lecturer. The projects are hard at first (or at least were when I took the class) bc you have to implement dozens of test cases later on. Obv every cs major has to take this class, i wouldn't worry too much if you get dixon

very hard class if you don't have experience in C++. Exams are a nightmare though, but if you do well on the projects, you can pass with a B at least. Professor is good, very helpful and understanding in OH. Most of the T/A's I went to for help weren't helpful, so recommend computing success center and Dixon's OH if you need help on projects.

Office hours were held in discord during Calc3 time, which many people could not make. Besides that the class is dependent on you understanding what you did on the projects, even then you will get a C on the exam unless you somehow are a goat in C++. The exams are very rough and you will need to start the projects early. A true test of independece.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: hard class great professor.  lectures aren't mandatory he posts everything including code along videos but still worth going to.  most of the work is projects but if you start on time i never struggled to get it done on time.

Overall, a very interesting course. There are two exams, three projects in a six week semester. Dr Dixon gave us a gnarly group project at the end of the fast semester which was really fun to work on but we didn't have much time to complete. You should be fine to take this class over the summer, just try your best.

He's very condescending. He will talk about how his students always complain that there isn't enough time to finish exams. He won't listen and instead says we just need to "try our best", then proceeds to grade harshly. We were given an entire software engineering project to do in 1.5 weeks, with no leniency to compensate. Honestly was ridiculous.

Condescending and can't make exams. The average for 1st exam was 68% and 60% for the final. Project 4 was convoluted; other than that, the projects were great. The labs helped cement concepts, but some labs were harder than others. Practically no partial credit for questions on exams. Take all assignments seriously. My programming ability improved.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: HORRIBLE PROFESSOR. literally had PROOF of not working on a file after the submission and didnt submit because the submission instruction was WRONGG!!!!!!!! AND NOW CANT EVEN GET CREDIT FOR THE WORK????? THERES EVIDENCE AND THIS PROFESSOR CANT ADMIT HIS MISTAKES AND JUST BE FAIR FOR HIS OWN ERROR. Guys stay away, PLS FOR YOUR SANITY.

Prof had good lectures to understand the material, but it can go a bit fast in the coding section of them, so the projects and labs is likely where you will learn the most. The projects were created by him, and were interesting to make! Project rubric could be vague or conflicting w/ test case sometimes, but is fixed after first few days of proj.
Literally a discord moderator
lol

The 202 reviews are applicable even in this 400-level class. Passive aggressive/condescending, and grades very annoyingly. Expect to often lose points on dumb things that were not discussed in project/exam directions. Content is very easy though, same content listed in the first 433 review. Exam 1 time is too short, exam 2 is easy

Professor's lectures were mostly easy to clearly understand, except in some of the more esoteric content, which just became confusing. Professor was extremely helpful, understanding, and friendly in office hours when asked for help. Assignments are extremely crushing, however.

Prof I mean DR. Dixon! The overall course was not too bad until the last Project which was literally a Software Engineering I project due in a week! He was extremely passive aggressive to the point of stop responding to emails. He will give you ZEROS. In a summary, he is a keyboard warrior online and in person he is a moderate person.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very condescending when he speaks and does not seem to care about his students at all. would recommend taking class with anyone else.

Since I didn't rlly go to lecture, i can't rlly comment on him or his teaching style, but i'll say this: best way to pass is to probably learn a little c++ b4 the sem starts and then during the sem, go to OH for projects (the TAs who helped me were pretty good!), and study the slides + wrksheets for exams and you should be good to go! you got this!

His powerpoints and lectures are good, but his interactions with students are horrendous. When helping students, he is very condescending and patronizing. The project guidelines are oftentimes misleading and confusing, but professor Dixon's attitude towards students discourages them from asking questions and actively seeking help.

One of the best professors I've ever attended a class for. Well experienced in the coding industry, professional and concise in his explanations, and regularly helps out many who have questions at the end of lectures. Even designs the projects himself for us to make. Genuinely would recommend Dixon when going into 202.

Fantastic lecturer, which in a fully coordinated course, is the only thing that really matters. Projects are challenging but not excessively hard. You can take him with confidence for any courses he is teaching.

The class is hard, the course setup is the same old strategy. Any student can easily cheat on labs and exams. The lecture is boring and students are falling asleep in that class, slide or lectures don't help with coding the project but help with exams. In class, code helps, but he is a way fast talker, and lots of things just go over the head.

Cool dude, hard class but not his fault, will be hard no matter who you take but his lecture videos helped a ton and actually knows the curriculum and topics in and out. a vet in c++ and makes all the projects and exams so he can help you off the rip with those, also curves a good amount end of the year

Solid professor.  This is a tough class to teach, its hard to grasp all of the concepts he teaches, and most of the learning and understanding comes from figuring it out on your own.  The lectures can help, but it either doesn't spend the time, or they are not enough to understand everything you need to know.

He is ok compared to other CS professors tbh, but the office hour isn't that helpful on discord, TA's are bad. If you had coding experience in C++ and you are good at coding then it is maybe a perfect class for you, otherwise, it is really difficult, you will work hard but might get a C.

Dixon is the best 202 professor.  His lectures are engaging and he has passion for what he teaches.  The things that are wrong with this course are that the projects are not very well structured and are often not easily understood and that he is quite rude in his personal office hours.  Study for exams with worksheet + powerpoints, and OH for projs

This class was project-based. There was no clear rubric, & you never knew what you would lose points on. If you understood a project, great! Otherwise office hours were the only way you could get help (but it wasn't very helpful if you were confused). He granted extensions a few times. He's not helpful if you don't already know the material.

Prof Dixon is a man, Helpful and his projects aren't too bad, Lots of people don't like him but don't want to actually put an effort into learning stuff. Cares about students, though he can be passive-aggressive that's just him being him and is a super dope guy, his youtube videos are good all you need to study for exams.

Attendance not taken.Lecture helpful/organized,explains concept->codes it out.Labs short+easy.Projs long,dont procrastinate(offers extension+EC).Exams hard,use practice guide+PPTs(gives points back if TA grades wrong).TAs/prof accessible via discord office hrs.Try to ignore bad/bias reviews.Pretty sure ill get an A.Take him if u can,i recommend.

I took Dr. Dixon's ethics course and it was really fun. We had a lot of stimulating group discussions about ethical topics in computing. The course ended with a final paper (1500 words) on a topic of our choosing. He allowed a degree of flexibility on topic choice and I was able to write about something that really interested me. Excellent course.

I took his scripting languages course to pick up credits over the summer. We did group exercises and projects in perl, python, awk, javascript, and other languages. More than any course, 433 with Dr. Dixon emphasized practical skills that are directly applicable in the workplace. He gives insightful, direct and meaningful feedback on work.

Dr. Dixon gives really good lectures and slide shows to study. The projects are pretty well designed and do a lot of the teaching themselves. I never really needed any help so I can't comment on how office hours are. Parts of the exams didn't really test understanding but aside from that the class was great.

Prof. Dixion overall is a "good" professor.
There are a few things that were a little unprofessional but considering the number of students in 202
and how busy OH can get, it's sort of understandable.
However, it is not okay for him to somewhat make jabs at students about their code.
He has great lectures, but OH might be a bit of a struggle.

I had Dr. Dixon for CMSC202 and thought he was really great. He's a really smart, funny guy and clearly cares about the success of his students. 202 has a negative reputation because I think it's when a lot of students realize the computer science major isn't what they expected, but Dr. Dixon is as accommodating as he can be for a course like that.

For people reading these reviews, they are slightly valid.  He's generally very good but the couple of times I have gone to office hours and he helped me he was slightly condescending.  I usually get help from the TAs because of that.  He is good at explaining, he tends to get frustrated if you don't understand it right away in his office hours :/
Professor dixon did hands on coding while in class that had to to donwith upcoming projects and hws and would send students the code for reference in you own assignments. Great experience

Dixon isn't bad at teaching lectures but the project guidelines and comments are horrendously misleading. His bad attitude towards his students are seriously dehumanizing. He will also try to find reasons to ban you on the class Discord server, cutting you off from office hours. There are better profs to take 202 with and Dixon is not one of them.

Out of touch, disrepectful, and unhelpful. Really bad experience, even though I passed, I would rather end everything than take him again, considering our interactions almost led to that anyway. There are hard classes, hard classes because of professor, and then there is both. This class is both and he loves to make a jab if you are struggling

Somehow managed to pass this hell but hearing about similar experiences from current students in his class. He’ll constantly say he will do anything to help you learn. DO NOT BE FOOLED!!! I have rarely been incensed when communicating with professors. Degrading and honestly made me feel like changing majors, despite my good grades. Just appalling

Trash assignment instructions and grading on tests is absurd. For projects, the ‘instructions’ provide no clarity and dr. dixon only gives bits of info mixed with passive aggressive remarks which is frustrating. For tests, the number/type of questions is only viable in given time if you write perfect programs on first attempt or else it is zero
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Since CMSC 202 is a gateway class, it means to be hard. Prof Dixon really cares about his students, he also tries his best to help. He would love to answer questions during the lecture, and he explains the concepts well. Start the projects ASAP. Dont wait until last days to start it bc OH is always full on the last two days.

Professor Dixon is by far one of the best cs profs i've had. When teaching, Dixon would make difficult topics so much easier to understand. His projects were hard but doable and fair b/c he'd teach the right material to prepare us for the projects. TAKE HIM!! Although 202 is generally a hard class, Dixon makes it easier! Hope I have him again.

expect to succeed despite prof dixon, not because of him. the TAs and library tutors might as well teach the course. im considering changing majors or schools because apparently he is one of the best CS professors here which is pathetic. the project documents are written poorly for no reason other than incompetence

terrible assignment instructions and trash attitude, expect to be talked down to unless youre a genius. and he wonders why people reviewing him dont like him. he had a public pity party in the groupchat for the class today, never saw something so sad. take literally anyone else or transfer, hes that bad.

Wasnt going to leave a review but since he made a huge ordeal about students not appreciating him enough Ill keep it real. Pretty good at teaching itself in lectures, but he is a complete negative in office hours help and assignment instructions. Maybe he should put as much effort into being a professor as he expects us to put into course work. L

Pros: solid lectures, friendly, light-hearted discussion, pretty good slides. Cons: Terrible assignment instructions are legitimately vague, super dismissive if youre struggling on something, pretty rude one-on-one honestly PS: if you write a review, dont identify yourself, he saw previous negative reviews and started complaining in class chat
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE!!!!!!!! Decent lectures but super unhelpful 1 on 1, he starts tripping if you email him about any questions if you arent asking worthy questions or something. I guess he has seen some of these reviews because he was complaining about reviews in a class Discord chat. I did well only due to the extra tutoring in the library, 100% not him
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Dixon is an ok professor. His lectures are engaging for the most part. He is nice in person but very passive aggressive when you talk to him online. Projects were tough even if I started them early and he acted like it was a chore when you asked him for help online. You need to study very hard for tests and tests are done on paper.

Dr. Dixon is a good professor. It's fairly simple to get a good grade as the class is out of 1000 points with the breakdown being 50/50 test and project. As long as you start the projects with adequate time, he is willing to help you through the project. The tests are slightly finicky, you have to know how to code and not have an IDE tell you how.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! He is very knowledgeable on C++ and is very dedicated to helping his students. If you are struggling to understand he will help you! Responds to emails quickly. I learned a lot in this course.

Writes horrible assignment instructions then either gets mad, gets condescending, or ignores you if youre struggling. Fairly amicable during lectures but the worst office hours I have attended from any class. If you already are an expert on everything in this class feel free to take his class. Otherwise, be ready to be spoken down to often by him
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Start Projects EARLY. Office Hour lines build up as you get closer to the due-date. The Professor is great when presenting lectures, and seems amicable. Major caveat: Completely opposite one-on-one. It's like he's wasting his time if you struggle with concepts and content. Exams will hurt if you don't put in considerable time beforehand.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not good professor, doesnt teach clearly. Ignores emails, office hours require you to wait around 2-4 hours even if you join first thing at 7 am. Every assignment is supposed to have late submission option for 15% off according to syllabus, but last project he decided to remove it without telling anyone. He belittles people who need concept help
Professor Dixon goes out of his way to help students succeed. His lectures are well organized and he explains things very well.

Ignores emails you send him. We were required to submit multiple files for our second project, and I had an issue/question with one file to submit. Rather than clearly respond to the emails I sent, he eventually passively said he will think of a way to help with that issue when he feels like it and to stop contacting him for any issue. Very rude
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not helpful at all, not nearly as nice as 201 professors, office hours are a minimum of a 3 hour wait each and every single day for 10 minutes of help
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Tight, well-structured class. Watch lectures on own time, labs in class (2.5 hours to do 6 problems with groupmates) on material. Projects are relatively interesting, 1+2 are basically problem sets, 3 is group game dev w/ db + web framework. Exams are basically solo labs and brutal, but doable. If you have time + money to take, more than worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was taken during COVID. The class was completely asynchronous but the recorded lectures were excellent. This class is a lot of work but it's spaced out well. Dr. Dixon really wants students to learn how to code in this class and cares about the students' learning.

Dixon is the best choice for 202. He's the course chair and gives great help on projects (and the TAs) if he's available. He teaches in a way that is really easy to understand fairly difficult concepts. And with the move to online, he's been super accommodating. He's great but the class is not easy, start projects early and take good notes!
he didn't have any live classes during COVID, which came across as lazy to me but i guess that could be a positive to you if you don't want to interact with your instructor. grades took forever

Jeremy's lectures are extremely well managed and presented giving you an easy reference to any topic you learn in class. Projects take considerable time but extensions are given 2-3 times per semester. Make sure you study for the exams as you will need more than what you code for the projects. Also go to the online office hours they help a ton.
I loved this class because of how easy he made it to understand and get help. Uploaded lectures to youtube and used discord for students to ask questions and get help quickly. TAKE HIM

This is a very fair professor. He makes sure that plenty of help is available for every student. The lectures are understandable and helpful. He provides PowerPoint slides for every topic. Exams are difficult but doable. Projects are easy if you put the time in. This course requires a LOT of work. Overall, would highly recommend.

Prof. Dixon's lectures were always helpful, most of the time, necessary for you to know what to do on the projects. The class is HW and Project heavy but he tends to really help you out. I went to him outside of class and I honestly though he was helpful, but he was just too intimidating. I preferred going to the TA's for help in that class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Excellent Professor. Class is very organized. Fun projects that reinforce important concepts. If you put in the time to understand the concepts, this class is an easy A.

He isn't a bad teacher, he knows what he is talking about but if you don't spend time outside of class practicing the programming language you aren't likely to pass. If you are doing this class don't take other classes that would take your time away from this. Start projects early, DO NOT rely on a curve. Even with the pandemic they curved 7 pts.

Professor Dixon is a nice person! You can always talk to him, and he does care about helping his students. This class is super tough. Incredibly difficult material and this class assume you know C++ quite well! This is by no means a beginner's class. You need to be experienced at C++ do even get a B, and a lot of outside help will be needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: It's a writing-intensive course so def get help from the writing center. there's mandatory peer review but if you're not a strong writer you'll need help. 4 papers, the last one should be 15 pages. the discussions are really interesting and you get points to participate. one midterm and it was based on discussion topics so pay attention!

Dixon may be someone to hang out on a Saturday with, but other than being funny, hes not a good prof. There are many things he tells you how to use and not what they actually mean, he copies examples off the internet, and recycles projects from the year before, making them so confusing because he screws up the documentation and doesn't care to fix.

Prof. Dixon is a really great choice for 202, he gives engaging lectures that provide a foundation for learning key concepts to computer science and helps visualize them with live-coding examples, giving you all you need to know. Very open to questions and gives thorough explanations to help you understand the content better.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Im talking about Dr. Dixon outside of his courses. He knows the computer science undergraduate program like the back of his hand. If you have a sub-par advisor, go to Dixon. If you have a bad professor go learn from Dixon. If you dont know which movie to see this weekend, go to Dixon (Honestly, i dont know if im joking on that last one). He is bae.
Difficult class, but Dixon is fair and is knowledgeable. Tests/Final are weighted heavily so be sure to study hard for them. Go to office hours for the projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Dixon was solid. His class was hard but he tried to explain things. The projects were kinda hard but do-able. Again, office hours were more helpful but not a bad professor overall. His lectures were funny and not dull.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Projects/labs are difficult & requires a lot of work but its do-able. prof Dixon is funny and tries to make lecture interesting. Pay attention in class because it will help when doing projects and labs. The TA's who write the exams are ridiculous and they are harder than they should be. But the prof overall is good at explaining concepts & is funny
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is an OK professor teaching a really difficult class. 202 is designed to weed students out but if you put in work you will be ok. He really cares about students
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Dixon was a great professor. His lectures were good, and he would always show live-coding examples to demonstrate the use of what he's teaching. The projects were fair and really help reinforce the important topics from class. His lectures were very interesting. Exams are fair, some information isn't on study guide, but they aren't bad.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Dixon is funny and makes the lectures entertaining and relatable. The class is difficult if you are not experienced with programming, but he does a great job of teaching what you need to know.

Amazing lectures feel like great conversation w/ a guy who truly loves this stuff. Easy labs, avg exams. Easy projects but for 1-2 hard parts each. Earlier you get to those parts the earlier you can ask for help. He's accessible, chill, & WILL help you short of doing it himself. Made me feel like I can succeed & I need more of that right about now.
He unnecessary makes projects very difficult and tells us to use functions that we haven't covered in lecture yet. Doesn't show all sample outputs on project handouts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: I received a C in CMSC 202, though I was 4 points off getting a B in this course. I reviewed any wrongful grading from any of his TAs, and I requested if he could give me 4 of those points back. However, he said that I have to retake this course this Fall. This shows that he actually cares about you since CMSC 341 is a continuation of C++ language.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I didn't know an ethics course could be this good. He gives engaging lectures with humor but doesn't try too hard to be funny. He does demand a lot as there are 4 sizeable papers due throughout the course and in-class participation is worth a significant amount of your grade, however, as this is standard across ethics courses, take it with Dixon.

I had him for 201, which is a pretty easy class in general if you know even the bare basics of programming. I would recommend that if you program already you take the class anyway because it is an easy A.  Class aside, Dixon is a really good professor. His lectures are engaging and the grading system is extremely clear.

Dixon is a good lecturer and provides a lot of examples in class. Be warned though, 202 is much harder than 201. His slides included less coding examples compared to 201 and projects include materials that you aren't taught in class. He's prepping you for 341, so expect projects to be harder. Project grading by TAs vary due to subjectivity

He teaches you Everything you need to Know. He is very patient with his students, Always ready and willing to help. I can't think of any reason why I won't want him as my professor ever. Professor Dixon is Greatttttttt

Professor Dixon a pretty good lecturer, always answers questions even if that means explaining it different ways. He keeps the mood of lectures pretty light, with a joke here and there. Very helpful outside of class, definitely go to office hours if you are having trouble with anything. Especially with projects, he'll help clear up any concerns.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lectures not helpful, not understanding about grades, exams based off slides so reading the book doesn't really help. Would not recommend.

Dixon is the man. He teaches what you need yo kno and goes over coding examples during lecture  for further practice. Weekly homework are a little challenging but him and the TA's are very helpful if you go to their office hours (there are many). The midterm should be fairly easy if you pay attentio in class and practice with the HW's.

He actually cares about helping his students. If you don't understand something and express that, then he will go out of his way to help you understand it. He encourages students to go to his office hours if they need help. Will give coding examples in class for further explanation. He is clear in his explanations. We didn't use the textbook.
Very good lecturer! A very discussion-oriented lecturer. He's also very understanding when it comes to grading.
Always open to questions and teaches lectures with a cheery mood. Makes jokes along the way to keep students interested.

IS 450: class was a nice 450 experience. HW every week, not too hard. 3 exams, non-cumulative final. She reviews your study guide and gives suggestions if you send it early enough. Lectures are pretty boring. Wireshark labs weren't too hard. In-class exercise every once in a while, that is graded, so don't skip too many lectures. She's very nice.

Pretty fun class. You get to configure Windows servers and create an Active Directory domain. The labs are pretty straightforward, but they can sometimes be weird. Exams are the only downside. You are allowed one double-sided cheat sheet, but the questions are pretty tough. I still think its worth taking though.

Very engaging lecture and she gives great examples. 9 homeworks that total 40% of your grade but the lowest one is dropped (online and mc). 3 exams that total 60% of your grade, they are straight forward with no trick questions. It is a lot of content but as long as you pay attention you will do fine.

Solid prof. 3 non-cumulative in-person tests, ~9 HWs (on blackboard & timed, 1 dropped). Lectures are ok, slides posted online with some extra readings. HWs are straightforward as long as you review the slides/readings. Exams are so-so; can easily catch you off guard if you don't prep; lets you send in your study guide and will give feedback on it.

On her class there are 3 exams and 9 homework's she drops the lowest 1. She is passionate about teaching, the tests are from lectures. The exam is very hard you need to memorize the concept from the reading. Missing class affect the grades since she go over important stuff on class that actually not on the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is straightforward. As long as you read the materials she shares and review weekly, you will be fine in this class.
One of the best professors I've ever had, great material prepared for the class and really good explanations of tough concepts. She will work to make sure you get it if you show effort

She knows what she is talking about but you have to take lots of notes during class. The slides don't have much information on them, but she explains them during class. Lots of labs in mindtap that can be tedious and time consuming, but straightforward instructions.

Is451M was easy with Professor Glazer, she did amazing explaining the slides. The only thing is the Exams were tough because they were scenarios. buts the exams didn't weight a lot the labs did. the labs aren't tough but the labs Virtual Machines kept freezing. also if you did bad on the labs you can re-do them for full credit. she is very GREAT.

She is an awesome professor, who really knows her stuff. They are 3 exams and I think 15 homework's She drops the lowest homework. she is really caring and does really well explain her slides, the tests are from articles and from lecture so make sure to read them and pay attention in class and you will be fine.

Not sure why her ratings aren't higher. Her class is relatively straightforward. Grade is mostly based on weekly HW quizzes and exams. Content is not too hard to understand, and she does a good job at lecturing and responding to emails. Lectures are not mandatory and she records them. She's also a very nice person. Overall, a solid choice.

Ms. Glazer is hands down one my best prof. at UMBX, took 451 with her also. This class is set up easier compare to 451. 3 exams, pretty straightforward if you are attending lecture and reading, and rest are lab which are all completed in class. Don't miss labs, read her slides/book, do review questions, you'll be solid. Again, She is awesome.

One of the hardest class I have ever taken at UMBC. There are three exams, 4 quizzes, and one case study. The exams are 75% of the grade while quizzes are only 5 % each, and 10% for case study. The lowest quiz grade gets dropped. She is a very tough grader and sometimes rude to students. She relates networking to real life. Would not recommend her!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Exams are extremely hard, nothing from her notes help. Boring lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Entire grade is exams

A lot of material is covered. There are quizzes between the tests, so you get an idea of what you are expected to know. Lecture ends early most days but feels like it went the distance. Not the most exciting delivery from a professor, but I learned a lot. The "OIT" tour was fun.

No textbook, all material publicly accessible online (articles). All powerpoint lectures are based off those materials, you will do much much better if you actually read them. Great lecturer, wants you to ask questions and succeed. Material isn't even difficult... Class does not require any actual networking... Just broad concepts...

Study and do the required readings and you will do well. I am surprised to see the poor ratings, the professor is more than willing to help after class and the networking knowledge (mainly concepts in 451)  is very valuable. The IS people who complain the technology classes are too hard (We have it easy compared to comp sci) should switch to BTA.

Worst class you'll ever take. Terrible lecturer, difficult tests, and tough grader. The lecture is dry, boring, and not at all engaging. The tests are out of 35 (take no less than 32 for an A) and the quizzes are out of 15 (take no less than 14 for an A). If you want to excel, you need to be dreaming and eating networking. The material is huge

One of the Worst Professors in UMBC. She teaches , but she is really mean when coming to exams. She would talk all through the class which makes boring. Her exams are tough as hell only people who know networking can easily handle it. She would on purpose make it harder for students to pass. Also, she will take points off for no purpose. DONT TAKE

Horrible Professor- If you do not have a background in Networking her tests are impossible. She will not help you study for material that is going to be on it. She is not helpful when you ask outside of class. DO NOT TAKE THIS UNLESS YOU HAVE A STRONG NETWORKING BACKGROUND.
good professor

Very Clear! 3 exams and 5 pop quizzes, so you need to make sure you do well in all of those. Quizzes are all multiple choice; However, the exams have multiple choice and short answers. She grades the multiple choice very easy tho. Make sure you know the section that you have not been quizzed on before the exam Last exam will be 80 percent caching.
Overall great professor. She is very clear and straight-forward. Her lectures slides outline everything you need to know for the exams.

Easily best networking professor I've ever had. 3 pop quizzes, 3 exams, no cumulative. We don't even have homework. Just make sure you go to all the classes, she gives you hints about when the pop qizzes are (she pretty much tells you). She uses relevant articles and Cisco webpages to teach, no textbook usage! She's super nice and really clear

Great instructor, one of the best in IS department. She likes what she does and she does it right. Lectures are straight forward and exams are easy if you know the material. She seams like a really nice person and she cute too. Great professor!
She is an amazing teacher! Loves what she teaches, responds promptly to emails, and super cute. DEFINITELY TAKE HER! EASY A!!

All of Glazer's classes are great.  She's very familiar with all of the topics and makes it fairly easy for students to understand.  This class was lab based using the textbook, and exams were easily studied for by taking notes in class and by using class slides, available on BlackBoard.  Grade is solely based participation, three exams and a quiz.

GREAT professor, horrible lecturer. Class isn't mandatory so don't worry about skipping now and then. She gives pop quizzes at random (but you can kinda guess when to expect them). Wording on exams is tricky in places so you MUST read carefully. 3 exams = 90% of the grade. 10% = quizzes. Do not underestimate the exams it is very easy to lose an A.

The best advice I can give you is to take the hw seriously since it's worth 40% of your grade.  The exams come from her lectures and online readings so if you pay attention you should be able to get an A no problem.  The professor is really nice and knows her stuff!

You have 3 exams, 10 HW assignments and thats it.  Exams (25 multiple choice) are based off of HW assignments (10-20 multiple choice), so study those questions and related topics.  HW questions are a bit tricky, so the slides and wikipedia will be your friends.  Class attendance is optional.  Half is online (free day) and half is in class lecture.

great teacher.. beautiful too..try to do good in home works all the time.. if u do that u will be fine in exam as well as in overall grade.. do not compare 450 and 451 451 is way too easy for people who took martens
No textbook required, everything on blackboard....only meets once per week. Although her wordings on exams/quizzes are pretty much  close to impossible to understand....
Great teacher, really easy course. Class only meets once a week. Online quizzes are pretty hard but exams are pretty easy. I didn't try very hard and I got a B.

I think she is easy, but try to do good on all h.w on blackboard because it will help you out in the end of class.  Other then that she is cool.  Test are comes from h.w assignments SAVED ALL OF THEM.  BEST OF LUCK

She's a nice person and seems interested with the course material. Class is once a week, mostly (unless it is a "study for exam Thursday"). There are Blackboard assignments each week, and while these are easy, they  are at least 4-5 questions that are so vague that the "best" possible answer is a mystery. She's too stubborn to make them clearer.

This was a very easy class.  We were assigned weekly HW that she answered nearly all the questions during the weekly lecture.  Although the schedule says the class meets twice a week we only met once a week.
She's very knowledgable, fair & teaches well.  This class gave us a lot of good info with enough hands-on activities to keep it interesting.  I would take any IS class with her.
class was easy. very thorough in her lectures and everything taught in class was on the test. the end of chapter multiple choice really helps on the pop quizzes.

I felt this class was very straight forward.  Glazer was very helpful and as long as you studied the questions at the end of each chapter you can easily pull a B on all her quizes and exams. I got an A without much difficulty. HINT: Use the books website for answers to the end of chapter questions.
No Comments

She was an incredibly sweet and understanding professor! Overall, she made the course incredibly interesting and was easy to reach out to. Her grading criteria made sense as well and there were multiple opportunities to do better.

I actually really liked professor Johnson! she was a great teacher; she provided direct feedback and was really engaging with her students. There are weekly discussions and quizzes that are lockdown browser, but if you read the material it should be very easy. But this course is heavy writing with multiple papers as it is a writing intensive course

It's pretty difficult as it is a writing intensive course. As long as you review the content, have a foundational understanding of the chapters and watch her PowerPoint lectures, and give yourself time to complete tasks you'll be fine. She sets clear expectations to follow if you take a day to read it out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Be prepared to have a C for the first 1/4-1/2 of the semester. The content wasn't hard, but weekly quizzes made me cry as the questions were EXTREMELY unclear. However, easy writing assignments make up for it, and if you go to the writing center, +10% each. I stopped reading textbook for quizzes halfway and just read the articles. Overall, not bad.
Good professor, be ready for quizzes that have almost nothing to do with the reading though
She has a nice personality! But she is a bad grader! She is gonna make you suffer for 200 level class! Im taking biology writing intensive and its a 400 class and much much easier

This professor is very nice, but for 200 level class, she is a very TOUGH grader! That was her only problem. She has so many good reviews and all are right about her. you can get A in this class but you have to work hard she is a very very TOUGH grader. Literally, for a small mistake, she is going to take away 10 or 20 points.

He teaches with overheads, which are hard to read, and he talks very quietly, so make sure you sit in the front if you want to hear/see. Workload is 2 exams, 2 projects (easy, on financial data), and you have to read this book and take 2 quizzes (only worth 10 pts)
Easy if you're good at following directions, exams are just like practice exams (MC).  Highly recommend for many economics courses.

Exams are tough so you have to know your terms, ratios, and equations-which is a hassle since he races through them as if you should already know them. He gives you previous exams to study from which helps a good amount. Be 100% attentive and copy down all notes..
material is ok, just don't like him personally.

Three test one project, test are multiple choice.  Can be tricky, make sure you can do the problems, by front to back back to front.  Will on occasion throw a curve ball or two.  Would definently take him again! Got an A in the class!

Prof. Lamdin breaks down what can be very confusing topics into dumb language.  His exams are fair which consist of 20 multiple choice questions however they are not that easy.  He does give out practice exams with solutions from previous semesters which help ALOT.  I will be looking forward to taking him next semester in his investments class.

Lamdin is pretty easy. If u've had him before u know exactly what 2 expect, no surprises. Quizes on the readings r very easy! Questions straight from text & r MC, T/F, fill in blank. Haven't had a test yet but he gives previous exams from other semesters so u can study from those. He's a great prof I had him for ECON374 so I wanted 2 take him again
flat out sucks and is of no help.  Flys through the material like a nuclear bomb just dropped. If you have even the smallest trouble with math, forget this guy.

Lamdin is cool but his lecture isn't really about teaching as much as it is about copying down what he puts in the over head becaue all he does is read the over head notes. He could just put it on black board and you would be just as well off. Exams are multiple choice but still not easy so study. Nice guy.

There is alot of material to cover so it makes studying for the exams a little more difficult however, he gives you exams from previous semesters which REALLY helps with studying.  Majority of the questions are the same just with different numbers plugged in.  Ur grade consists of 2 exams 1 project and 1 final.  I think Prf Lamdin makes Econ374 fun

The material covered in this class is hard, but he explains everything very clearly. Just follow his notes, you don't even need to buy the book. The exams (2 mid-terms and final)are not bad, learn from old exams. Project(just one) is easy, just follow his instructions. You don't need to show up for class, but it would be better if you did.
He was very nice and helpful. If you use the exams as study tools, you will do well.

his class is supposed to be pretty easy cuz he gives u the old exams but they are never the same as the old exams he changes it up like crazy but if u get an A on the easy project and do good on the final, u will get at least a B in the class

I like Lamdin...he knows his stuff...you can't afford to slack in his class...but if you follow his past exams and stuff...you should be ok...I learned at alot...thats something I can't say for all professors...:(
boring but very easy class. just study the review tests and project is a piece of cake!
Really easy!  Just go to class and study the exam reviews
He sucks big time and very rude too!
Great teacher.  Really easy!!  Project is a joke it is so easy.  Great exam reviews
No Comments

The professor was very genuine and caring. He always explained us things and engaged us during lectures with discussion. There were some surprise activities and extra credit opportunities during lecture as well!

Though quizzes and test were closed notes, they were take home. And the professor let us retake a quiz if we explained why we missed.

Honestly, I showed up to maybe 2 lectures the entire semester. You really don't have to go. Professor Dopico seems nice and genuine. The class is a free A. You don't need to do anything. Every week you'll have a test that's take home and open note, same when it comes to exams. I don't understand his low rating, maybe in other classes he isn't great
The professor brought a fresh look to a verybstaightforwd couese on etymology and medical terms with some activities and group work. Very passionate about the material.
Fun class with different activities. Be sure to attend lectures, might get extra credit in doing so
Very nice class try to show up and do well on the weekly tests and exams and you should do well.

I had a great time in the course. The lectures were cool and the teacher taught using his student interests and a down to earth style.

Also the homework was not too bad. 20-30 pages assigned per week for a class that meets once a week is very doable!

heavy, HEAVY reading HW. lectures are not very engaging and hella dense in information. if you have a genuine passion in mythology you can get along with him and will probably enjoy this class but if you are planning to take this class as a free easy credit do not. 

major plus is test are online and can be done on your own time.

He does explain things a bit too fast, however once you communicate with him during after-school hours, he does help in breaking down projects and assignments into smaller and more simplified chunks. Provides good extra credit opportunities, and will extend assignments for students if necessary. Very passionate about the material he teaches.

reviews.comment: Professor was fairly pleasant and seemed to be passionate on the subject. Homework was straight from the textbook and quizzes weren't too far off what was talked about in lecture. All quizzes and both midterm and final have a small amount of extra credit. Should be an easy A.

reviews.comment: Boring class but was pretty easy. He was a nice guy, but the syllabus and his idea of the class felt different.
Inconsistent grading and expectations, unclear rubrics, HEAVY weekly homework readings, sent me the wrong final exam and went MIA for the rest of the day

reviews.comment: +1 for rounding up overall grades of 79/89 & being generous with extensions, but the amount you'll NEED to ask for them is just cruel. DO NOT TAKE HIM.

reviews.comment: Dopico was one of the most unpleasant professors I have taken. I feel he had way too high of expectations for the students for a 200 level class. reviews.comment: lol. class is ancs210. check gritview to see how had his grade distribution is. unless you have 50h/wk to devote to this class and a deep love of the subject, avoid this prof at all costs. comes across as a good human being tho so dont be too mean to him.
