reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: i heard that rlst 210 and ancs 201 had different experiences but i took ancs and he was a tough grader and assigned hard papers. he "didnt believe in rubrics" but that led to the papers being confusing as to what he expected and then us getting low grades. he gave too little time on the exams, overall not a mean person but not a good professor

Tests you on material he barely covers, if at all. Doesn't hold office hours. Rubrics have no real distinctions between scores. Some grades take MONTHS to show up, and if you think he'll give you truly constructive feedback on the bad ones... tough luck. Also accused my whole class of cheating on the midterm without evidence. DO NOT TAKE HIM. EVER.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Do not take this class with him. LOTS of long homework and quizzes. Unclear grading criteria that take weeks for results. Do not trust those two good reviews. If an elective's coursework is laid out to where you have to constantly ask for extensions and reach out - it's the professor, not the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: While he isn't an easy grader, he is absolutely a fair one. His lectures are interesting and energetic, he clearly cares about the subject. He is very willing to give extensions, work with you, and explain things provided you actually communicate with him, something I am inclined to believe many of the negative reviewers did not do.

While there was a lot of work, all the due dates and assignments were well laid out. I emailed this professor many times about missing assignments and needing extensions, and he was open-minded and understanding every time. As long as you do the work and communicate with him, he is an amazing professor with a great sense of humor.

Frustrating. In my semester, he told us there isn't a textbook for the class, but I just found out his lectures (disjointed, rushed) are based primarily off of one. If he does that in your semester, the textbook is Ancient Greece A Political, Social, and Cultural History (4th edition) by Sarah B. Pomeroy, Stanley M Burstein. Oxford Press.

Pros: This class is VERY good exposure therapy to research papers, if you're able to put in the time and energy. IMO, if you come to him with questions about the material (like I often did), he's really nice and receptive to feedback. There is extra credit.

Cons: VERY inconsistent grading, and rushed over-condensed lectures.

I should have followed my gut and dropped the class in the first week when I felt like this isn't gonna end well, for somebody who claimed this class didn't need initial knowledge, he expects you to know everything, only if I found reviews on him before we signed up but he totally ruined the idea of this class being easy, take it with phin pls.

For an intro arts and humanities class this professor assigns too much work. Students are expected to read 100-200 page myths each week with a reading journal to complete. He often criticizes the class for not understanding the myth and having incorrect interpretations. Mythology can be interpreted in DIFFERENT WAYS.

He berates the whole class for our poor writing skills and when asked how to do better or explain the feedback, he just says that getting bad grades is what will help us in our writing for the future. Assignments often have incorrect descriptions that are not updated making it confusing on what we are writing about.

Though at first it appeared like the class was going to be fun & entertaining, he expects the class to know everything (even though he assured it was just an introductory class.) His attitude during the lectures feels sarcastic to those that are confused. Tough grader with no clear feedback other than berating you for not knowing. Long assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Worst prof Ive had in my 4 years. So much wrong with how he set up the course, but worst part was his attitude. he saw himself as a "good prof" just because he didnt act like his old college profs. He accused of us not knowing how to write, but when we asked how to analyze the text we were to write on, his response was: you'll just have to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dopico is the worst professor I have ever had in my four years of college. This is an intro course, but he expected us to have strong knowledge of Greek history from day 1. He is nitpicky when it comes to grading. He gave papers to do every other week with no rubric and no feedback. He berated the class for not being smart. Don't take his class.

This class was incredibly difficult. I took a 200 level on classical mythology, and he had us reading about 200 pages per week. The instructions for the paper were incredibly vague. Basically every class started with him angrily ranting about everything he disliked in the reading journals. I took it as an elective, and had to drop it from stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awesome professor. She's very kind and has a great passion for biology. Had no complaints about any part of this class.
Dr. Donohue is extremely helpful. Her enthusiasm for biology was evident and she wanted everyone to succeed
The only reason I even passed this course is because she let me redo an assignment. Great prof!

She was the other prof teaching with Dr. Leupen for this class. She was okay? Like the labs were fine and she explained what she wanted clearly but her in-lab quizzes were a lot harder simply because they just weren't as to the point as Leupen's (imo). When she said anything from the protocol would be tested, she meant it.
Took Unruly Bodies in the summer. Interesting class for culture gep!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took this class online in the winter session and loved it!! Dr. Kate is my favorite professor by far and I found the readings for this course were really interesting and engaging. She's very accessible outside of class and super understanding about accommodations and deadlines and really makes the class enjoyable. She is also very passionate. :)

Dr. Kate is the best instructor I've ever had. She's amazing to her students, and you can tell she cares about them individually. The class was an easy A, you just have to do the weekly discussion boards. Attendance isn't mandatory, but I always hate to miss her class because it's so enjoyable. She's truly an amazing professor.
Attendance is not counted for, basically one assignment due per week. She is super flexible and super nice!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Kate is probably one of the best professors in the Gender, Women, and Sexuality Studies department, maybe one of the best at the school. She is very understanding and is willing to give you time to make sure your work is the best it can be. Her lectures are engaging and interesting and she makes you care about the class.

Dr. Kate is a real gem and a great professor! She is so funny and gives amazing lectures! There is a lot of reading assigned for each class but it's definitely not necessary that you read *all* of it because it will be discussed in class, but make sure to take notes. This was by far my favorite class this semester, maybe my favorite class at UMBC!

Dr. Kate is a great professor! Her class is so fun to go to. If you need a culture credit for GEP at UMBC, this one is the way to go! Lots of reading, but if you don't do every page no need to sweat, just understand the main points and you will be okay. Exams are written and you have plenty of time to do them, attendance is important, fair grader.

Dr. Kate is an amazing professor! Feminist Activism is a great class too. No tests, one major project, one group project, 4 discussion questions. Her classes are heavily discussion based, super chill and open. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: A wonderful course that I really enjoyed taking with Dr. Drabinski.  She is very understanding when there are any circumstances related to the exams or grading and the grading criteria is very clear.  This course involves essays and BB discussions related to the material and it is straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Kate is by far my favorite professor at UMBC. She makes lectures interesting and they are almost always hilarious. She makes learning very easy as she does not give standard exams but has you do essays instead. She's very understanding when life happens and is there to help students with matters even outside of the class.

Taking a Dr. Kate course is one of those invaluable experiences UMBC has to offer.  She engages you with the material through stories of her own life and an extensive knowledge bank and understanding of the world.  I've had her for both GWST 200 and 310 and she was fantastic for both.  Willing to work with students.  Read in order to participate.

Dr. Kate is by far my favorite professor at UMBC. She makes lecture relevant to what's going on today and really knows her stuff. She was the highlight of my Mondays and Wednesdays. Definitely take one of her classes!
She is an amazing teacher. So willing to help, very understanding. Incredibly interesting, loved going to class. Projects were fairly easy and fun to do.
Awesome lady, awesome teacher. Definitely would recommend!
I love her. she's the best!
Best prof I've ever had.

Easily one of the best professors I've ever had. Friendly, knowledgeable, engaging and hilarious. The course material was interesting enough, but having her as a teacher made it just that much better. I highly recommend her.

By far my favorite professor in college so far. Don't blow her class off because it appears to be easy, you'll learn so much if you pay attention, go to class, and do the readings. This class made me pick up a GWST minor.

took this class over the winter. 2 easy group presentations. 1 presentation at the end. a few films. Keep up with the readings. Take notes, this makes the (3)take-home exams easier on you. if you type notes, make sure you reference your notes on what pages your notes come from.

I loved taking Professor Holladay! I took him during Spring 2024, and even though attendance was optional, I still attended nearly every class, because he has a great demeanor and is very intelligent in his content area. The only thing I'd say is that you need to be open to reading a good amount per week, and the material will likely be quite new.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the best professors at UMBC. Have taken multiple classes with him and plan to continue taking them with him. Very intelligent about everything he teaches. Super understanding and happy to give extensions, especially if you are vocal in class and generally do your work. Seriously, take ENGL 300 with him!!!

[ENGL 387] - Very easy class but never responds to emails during the semester. He grades very late, so you do not know if you are passing or failing the class until the last day grades are put in. Instructions are misleading at times, and in-person classes aren't informative sometimes.

He is really understanding when it comes to extensions and makes himself available for additional help. Probably the nicest professor at UMBC, he seems to enjoy what he teaches and genuinely wants to help students succeed. 2 discussion posts and readings per week with 3 essays and 1 project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A very very sweet professor. I learned much from him for class where we discussed disabilities and how people can be treated unfairly because of them. I was in a pretty small class, 7 people including me. But Prof made it easy to hold a discussion. Readings were interesting and relatable. Deadlines were flexible. He was very understanding.

reviews.comment: As a grader and a one-on-one reviewer, he's fine. But he's an awful lecturer. He sounds constantly nervous and his voice puts me to sleep.

reviews.comment: There is a lot of work for this class but Im rating him as a professor. Hes very caring and sweet and is always willing to help or grant an extension. Hes always available on his email and gives wonderful feedback. I would take him again in a heartbeat
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Holladay is a great professor. The material is not as boring as people on here make it out to be if you are actually interested in communications. He really is such a sweet guy and seems like he loves teaching and what he teaches but unfortunately the material is extremely boring. Never takes attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's a young professor. The course content is extremely boring. Attendance is supposedly mandatory but I never saw him take it. He makes students do a lot of discussion posts on blackboard instead of teaching us the material. Most of class is spent sitting around, but he never releases class early. Hardly any assignments from him and no grades.

Professor Holladay is by far the coolest and nicest professors I've had in awhile. He cares about his students and is willing to listen to reason if any trouble should befall you. I highly recommend taking his class, if you show up, participate, and take notes you'll do fine. Study for midterm, the projects are easy if you put in the effort + time

Dr.Pan undoubtedly has more knowledge in her field, But her way of teaching is totally worst. Most of her classes are just a presentation and you will get boared of it. Apart from very few topics, i dont remember any thing useful from her lectures.

The lectures were lengthy to follow, making it difficult to absorb the information. Additionally, no accommodation regarding missed exams, unless you go to the hospital when sick. While polls were used, only a small percentage of the material covered in class appeared on the quizzes, which were still challenging, even slides were mostly useless.

reviews.comment: Great Professor, She cares and Easy grader
Great professor, super clear on what is expected for exams and the project. Gave reviews for each test so you knew what was coming. Highly recommend.

Overall, pretty good. Grading for the projects is a bit ambiguous, with different TAs giving different advice, leading to point deductions at times, since project requirements aren't straightforward. Takes a lot of time to do the projects, concepts aren't that hard, just tedious implementation.

He has live coding in lectures which can help solidify the basics of each concept, but beyond that the lectures are standard. TA's grade your projects and exams, which can make or break your semester, there are some serious differences from grader to grader. Professor wasn't very friendly or accessible when I needed help & didn't respond to emails.

Donyaee is very nice and is pretty thorough with his lectures. The majority of your grades is from homeworks and tests. The quizzes were mostly based off lecture notes, focusing on terminology mostly. He's very nice so don't be afraid to ask for help. There was also a curve at the end of the semester.

The resources he posts on Blackboard are practically unintelligible. Everything I have learnt thus far was either from Youtube or other professors' slides I got from my friends. Even those are poorly explained but at least a few things are sensible.
This professor is great. He's always willing to help you out and he actually cares about your learning. Absolutely recommend this class for the summer too!

He's a good professor, you might have to geekforgeeks for some clarifications on some concepts. Projects and homeworks weren't crazy, you should be fine as long as you start as early as possible. More importantly, he's a great person who's willing to help out students when in need, and fun to talk to in general.

I think he's the best prof for data structure he explained things very easily and class is not boring, he likes when student ask question and help you understand what you're confused about. He's very knowledgable.

He's a very knowledgeable professor, but this course I feel wasn't the best organized. His lectures can be quite confusing, and leave us not fully prepared for homeworks or quizzes. Plus, it's hard to prepare for exams. We're given a mock exam, but it's like 50% representative of the actual. Not an easy A or B. Homeworks were graded harshly too.

reviews.comment: Great, interesting class, but demands a lot of time. The lectures help a lot and the supplementary videos he provides is essentially broken down portions of the lectures. Be prepared to Google A LOT for this class. Many items and troubleshooting tips will need to be Googled as they aren't covered very well in the lectures/notes.

Lectures were bland. Projects were long and involved, but there wasn't much other homework. Tests were difficult but curved. Solidly middle-of-the-road professor- I don't have anything particularly bad to write about, but also nothing particularly great to write about either.

Donyaee is one of the better teachers in the cmsc department. He takes time in class for students to practice concepts and his quizzes reflect material covered. He is also very gracious with extensions and looking over grades done by the TA
It's easy to pass his class if you put in the effort. Curves the final grade which is amazing.

reviews.comment: bestie. he is such an amazing prof!

reviews.comment: Donyaee is a good professor to some extent. I say to some extent because if a professor depends on curves they really aren't that great. His exams are very difficult and will get curved no matter what.
Ver caring professor just pay attention in class

Overall a really lackluster professor. Lectures are extremely hard to follow and do not help with homeworks and exams. The only other option he offers is his overpriced textbook that barely gives a surface level understanding of the content. Prepare to have lots of outside resources and make sure to take the it online if you can.

Nice guy, lenient grading, and flexible on request. He provided very limited context so it was difficult to want to understand the material as opposed to just memorizing steps to pass. The homeworks were easy (40%), activities were for completion (5%), quizzes were a little challenging (5%), midterm and final exams were not easy, study! (50%).

In charge of 341 projects, and they can be pretty difficult. Also a lot of errors and things missing when projects are initially released. Honestly, you'll only be relying on the TA's for help, they're your best bet :)

A decent professor. Lectures were pretty hard to follow but he posts lots of resources on blackboard so you can catch up if you're lost. There's a textbook for this class but you really didn't need it.

He's an okay professor. He says to buy his textbook for $90. I didn't buy it, nor did I need it. If online, watch the lectures at 1.5x speed. Homework was graded for accuracy and activities for completion. Quizzes and exams are fairly straightforward and have similar questions like previous assignments, occasionally weird questions with no guidance

reviews.comment: Due to videos just being posted as a lecture for half the semester it was hard to connect and understand. Easily accessible outside of class, TA's helped a lot. Projects are challenging and difficult.
He is an understanding professor and tries his best to help the students.

He's a very supportive teacher. I got extension in two different projects. I explained my situation to him, and he was very understanding. Everything is pre-recoded and it was a bit tough to get through (2 hours per week), but it was useful. And same for his powerpoints.

His pre-recorded lectures are lifeless. Other than that and having to buy the textbook he wrote for $90 extra instead of the book every class uses, it wasn't terrible. Textbook was pretty useless too. Exams were okay since lots of the problems were from quizzes. Wouldn't take him again though.

I believe Donyaee has really improved since he was first teaching a few semesters ago. Although the homeworks are worth a lot (40%) and there's only 6 of them, he's really quick with responding to emails and helping. He also randomly decides to push dates so that was a plus. His exams are easy if you do well on the quizzes (5% of grade).
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Great professor. Puts effort in explaining content

He makes you buy his own book for a minimum of $90. Don't take him for CMSC331 since you can find the other professors textbook for no charge. He prerecords his lectures, which is the only positive. Dry and boring tone when lecturing. Weekly homework, activities, and quizzes.
Pro tip: if you're taking 331 online, watch the videos at 1.5x speed. It helped me a lot with staying focused. Good professor overall.

Took this class over the summer and it was a breeze. Also prof. is very helpful. He held office hours twice a week and was able to clear up any questions I had. Also homework was 40% of the grade; if you do well on those and actually know your stuff, you'll get a good grade. Very generous grader also :)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: For CMSC 202, Professor Donyaee was very interactive with students, but I found myself struggling to understand him and was bored in some lectures. The class definitely makes you work for your grade, though.

His lectures are from his book. His book got some wrong answers. The book is not clear how to solve the problem. The solution is not consistent. Thus, no way to know where your point would be taken off. He (or his TA) grades very harsh.

This guy sucks. Hard. He is unclear about what exactly he is trying to teach, grades things far too harshly, and basis his "class participation" grade on things he says multiple times are not graded. Horrible. Avoid.

Dr. Donyaee is a great person! Very open, understanding, and reachable. The curriculum in class is hard, and to find that information online is hard. Nevertheless, as long as you try to do homework, and try, you should pass!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took him over the summer and he's really improved. He's a good teacher and the material makes sense, just practice it. He wants you to do well. Definitely curved the class.
Dr. Donayaee is an awesome teacher, he really cares about whether his students understand the lessons. He has improved very much from his first semester.

This was Dr. Donyaee's second semester teaching and he has tremendously improved. The class is very heavy regarding how much material you are responsible for, but you will learn a lot. He gave a hard final, but also curved it very fairly. The hw and midterm were also fair. He is also a very nice person and is nice about helping students.

Most of the very low reviews below were posted before final grades when most people expected to fail. Homework is kind of difficult, but if you go to office hours he helps a lot. The tests are very hard. Overall it is a difficult course, but he curved generously to make up for it. As a professor he's very nice and helpful.

The homework was painful and the tests were quite difficult, but ultimately I received an A when I was expecting a C. So you'll have to work, but the final grades are more generous than you'd expect. More importantly, Donyaee posted better review materials as the semester went by. So future semesters should go better for students.

A very nice and caring professor, this was his first semester teaching so he may have been a bit rough around the edges, but I'm sure he will improve in the future. His midterm was impossibly difficult, but he showed the desire to improve and although difficult, the final was more fair.

The course was not hard but this professor made it way harder then expected. The exams are very tough and his grading are very unfair. I would not recommend anyone to take this professor. He will not provide you anything like past exams etc for the help. The exam guide is useless. Lecture notes are just scanned copy of the book.

I don't understand all the iffy ratings people have given him. I'd say it's one of the harder courses I've taken, but comp sci courses aren't supposed to be easy A's. Homework isn't bad & seems to be graded pretty fair and not too harsh. The exam was tough, but he gives you literally the notes for everything we've gone over in class so study those
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Really nice guy but horrible at teaching. No lecture slides in class, only blackboard notes in paragraphs copied directed from the textbook. Lectures are done on the chalkboard with no clear objective of what hes teaching, not good at explanations. 6 hws with unclear directions, grading is inconsistent. Many students are hoping to pass.

He is an incredibly nice person, but that is about it. He decided to make a course that is supposed to be easy incredibly difficult. The coding HW is worth almost nothing compared to the writing HW. The midterm was one the worst experiences I've ever had, he provided no study guide and was surprised when a lot of people failed.
Awful professor. He writes on the board but never connects each lecture with each other and his exams do not test the material that we learned in class. I would NOT recommend.

Professor Donyaee is a nice guy. However, he assigns lots of homework and the exams are hard and long. He gives heavy lectures and expects you to know everything. Homework is not always from the book. You have to code in python, C, C++, etc. He thinks everyone is proficient coding. Try taking another instructor unless you're great coding.

Professor Draganescu did nothing to prepare you for exams, and never uploaded any material for you to practice, and the tests were significantly harder than ANY other class. Avoid for math 300 as you will not get a good understanding of proofs at all.

I saw the reviews here and thought Draganescu would be pretty horrible, but he is not bad. He is pretty funny when lecturing, and the worked examples done during class are relevant to the homework. The only problem is the way he explains the abstract: 3Blue1Brown's Essence of Linear Algebra series on Youtube can help you with that though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is a nice person and does try very hard to teach the class. However, he teaches too abstractly and is really hard to follow. His quizzes are from the book but his exams are really theoretical.

He's a nice person, but he is bad at explaining mathematical concepts in terms that students can understand. He also writes proof-based exams that are not in line with what the homework has you practice. In addition, the first exam was graded too late for me to drop the class and save my GPA. There are FAR better options for MATH 221.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Try to take a different professor if possible!! He gives computational homework, but the tests are almost entirely theory based. His lectures make little to no sense (go to the lectures anyway - not graded but used to boost your grade if you showed up). Read the book and memorize language/theories. It's not impossible, but it's not fun either.

He is a good teacher, no doubt. He will challenge you to the max with the problems he assigns and tests on. 80% of your grade  comes from 3 tests all of which will be the hardest 3 tests you will ever take. If you are a math person and you know for sure you will pass then sure take him and learn the most. For the average person, take someone else.

He puts the entire burden  on  tests. Its a hard class and many of the other teachers give quizzes and a lot more HW  which help with understand as well as grades. it feels like he does the bare minimum.
hes ok

The people below me sound like people who usually don't get A's in math classes, and are giving him a good rating because they did well. I also received an A, but I usually do so my view is more objective. He isn't hard by any means, but hes certainly not "the man". He is hard to follow in class. Unless your self -taught, lectures will be useless

Dr. Draganescu was friendly and very fair.  Like others said, he likes to prove things,  explain theory, and do hard problems in class.  However, homework (quizzes) and tests covered the core concepts of the course and were not very difficult.  If you read the book, take good notes, do the homework, and pay attention, there is no reason to do bad.

Draganescu is the man, best math professor ive had at UMBC. Grade is made up of quizes exams and final. Quizes are based on HW. Exams somewhat challenging but questions focus on core concepts. He wants his students to succeed and makes that possible with some announcements at the end of the semester. You wont be disappointed,take the class with him

Great Professor.  As long as you did the homework, and came to class and put in a little effort, you will get a good grade.  He explains things very well, and his classes are completely related to the topic.

Sometimes goes above what is necessary in class scaring students.  However, he is very helpful, gives exams that give many to do well.  Homeworks can sometimes be a little difficult but the exams will bring up your grade.
He is a bad teacher, make me start scared math. I don't think he knows how to teach. The things he wrote on blackboard was mass. Terrible
He is not very easy to understand in the lecture but he is very fair in all aspects of teaching. His grading methods allow you to recover even if you don't do well in the  beginning.

One of the better professors at UMBC.  He's new, and I hope more people discover him.  He's willing to work with you as much as you need it.  Tends to do a lot of proofs in class, gears it more towards math majors than engineering students. Sample Exam may or may not strongly resemble the actual exam.  Take him if you want to learn something.

Teaches an intro class the way it should be taught; tests focus on problem solving and not a ton of theory...he tells you what to expect on each test and gives plenty of partial credit.  The project is a pain but most people got good grades.  If you do the homework and practice his sample exams, a B is almost guaranteed and an A is very possible.

Very good professor. Detailed, easy to understand lectures. Although the class is quiz/exam heavy there are many drops and good TAs to help you prepare. Some exams may be difficult but Prof. Listorti is considerate in grading.

Super great professor. Posts notes for each lecture online and lectures are easy to follow. The exams, and quizzes are pretty decent, and he posts tests from previous years which are really helpful when reviewing. He also offers drops for assignments and quizzes, so it's okay if you don't do well on some of them. TAs are also very good.

I couldn't recommend Professor Listorti more. He makes notes available before every lecture, he makes difficult concepts easier to understand, he offers drops for assignments, and he's open to go over concepts before exams if you have any questions! On top of that, he's a high school math teacher, which further shows his passion beyond lectures.
holy she is so boring in her lectures. Then shes a really tough grader on essays, she doesnt even say what u did wrong.

If you ever encounter situations or difficulties just reach out! Dr. Dunn-Gallier is super understanding if you explain your situation, and is willing to accommodate if needed. She reached out to me regarding my disability accommodations early on in the semester so she could better understand and accommodate my needs, not just what was on paper.

I don't know why she has low ratings; this class is such an easy A. She is a great professor, communicates well, and is very understanding. You just have to attend class and do the assignments, you don't even really need to read the entire textbook. Lock in guys!!

She's a good professor! Her lectures can be a bit boring sometimes, and some of her lecture points are personalized as we watched a Destiny Child's music video and a scene from Wicked, I know for some it might not be enjoyable in their interests (for me it was great!). She has strict deadlines, homework each week, three papers, and a final project
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Do not take her unless you wanna be failed over the wrong citation format 😒
She'll fail you for the littlest mistake in your essay

DO NOT TAKE!!!
She's a tough grader she WILL fail your paper if you miss one of the littlest requirements (like the formatting even if you did everything else right), she takes her job way too seriously.

Overall, Dr. Dunn-Gallier is a really great professor. However, her strict deadlines, and weekly assignments serve little motivation to actually do work in the class. There are weekly group work assignments assigned in class that take about 20 minutes to complete, but a lot of the time we would have five or ten minutes as lecture ran over.
Such a nice professor! I loved this class, she is super understanding about missing class if you have a valid excuse.

If you're a senior STEM major like I am, don't take this class. Mandatory attendance and lots of busy work. This class is clearly for freshmen. Her lectures are also very boring, and chalked lack of participation up to “you guys must be stressed with the current political climate”, instead of recognizing none of us want to watch Wicked in class.

The assignment load is very manageable and she is very understanding if you give her a heads up. Class is reading heavy and its hard to follow along without reading before hand. She puts you into groups that don't change the whole semester. Final project was easy and open ended.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was a great take and she's really awesome to talk to. Theres a decent amount of reading and you will be put in a group. The final was really open ended and the assignments could be pretty flexible. High recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Idk why she is rated poorly, this class is a easy A. Async assignments every week and 3 papers/1 final project (no late assignments). She is also so interesting to talk to! go to her office hours. Downside is that lectures are kinda boring/mandatory but is just an hour ONCE a week so it isn't that bad. Overall easy A take her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class would be sm better if the attendance wasn't mandatory and you didn't have to come in and waste your life away during an unnecessarily long lecture about perhaps the most boring subjects imaginable, while she slips in her own political agenda throughout. Other then that, easy A class. If you dont mind sitting in some lectures, take it!

She knows her stuff and is kind one-on-one. However, I didn't like her class for a few reasons. She assigned groups for us to sit + complete assignments with, which seemed silly b/c it was a large lecture hall. Her lectures were boring. Also, she accepts no late work. This can hurt you later on, especially b/c papers are a large part of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Dunn-Gallier is a fantastic teacher. She is well read and knows her stuff. She is engaging and knows how to give lectures without them feeling boring. She uses a flipped classroom model, so be sure to do your reading before class. She is a stickler about no late work though, so make sure you do all your assignments on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall a decent professor. Super super lecture heavy and mainly just goes over stuff that's in the textbook. Extra credit is engrained in participation in the class through Poll Everywhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Miller is retiring this semester. Good professor who is clearly passionate, and if that helps you to be passionate than you will love his class. He changes as it goes depending on the semester (my class had a paper where we had to disprove chatGPT). It's a tough class due to all the concepts you're likely to hear about for the first time
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Miller says everything you need to pass the class in his lectures. A little hard to consistently pay attention, but i passed without doing any of the readings.

My favourite professor at UMBC. Very lecture heavy, but he always makes them fun and interesting to listen to. The exams are super straight forward (just a bunch of multiple-choice questions), he always tells you exactly what's going to be on them, and he has practice tests for you to study.

He's okay. But more importantly, he releases practice quizzes that are not graded, BUT they helped me more than anything to do better on the tests. I wouldn't have gotten a B without those practice quizzes.

I took geomorph and then fluvial with Dr. Miller. He goes above and beyond to make sure that you really understand the information. The course definitely requires you to work, but fluvial was my favorite class in GES. He's accessible outside of class and also willing to help with things outside of the course. I 100% recommend taking this.

Dr. Miller is a great professor, had him for 310 and then again for 400. He is lecture heavy and his classes are a bit harder, but I ended up learning the most from his classes. Def take fluvial morphology if you can, one of the best classes I've ever taken. Dr. Miller really cares about his students and does everything he can to help.

This class has intensely heavy exams, this past semester, for a whopping 75% of your grade. Studying for this class is straightforwards but just dense with information, so prepare to allocate plenty of hours outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's very intelligent, and I absolutely loved his Geomorphology class, but for some reason, Hydrology didn't really hold my interest. He did far too many derivations on the board and messed up halfway through, yet expected us to have a perfect grasp of the concepts. I wish he had made it more fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Great class. Learned a lot.

Professor Miller is very friendly and cares a ton about the subject. He uses clickers so come to class. If you pay attention or just read the textbook and study you will pass. Pay attention to the clicker questions, they will most likely show up on the exam. He moves very fast and gives lots of examples, but the slides are posted after every class

Class is very lecture heavy and class participation is a big portion of final grade. The class overall is more work heavy but it is all EASY. The online quizzes do not count towards your grade but DO THEM, most questions on tests will be pulled directly from them. Prof. Miller is amazing and really does what he can to help you succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is very smart but teaches the class like it's a 300 level instead of 100. The class moves very fast and has at minimum 100 slides a day. There was a lot of information given quickly. Online, non-graded quizzes help to prepare for tests. Clicker questions every day also help. Learning modules are hard but interesting. Grades are straightforward.

He knows what hes talking about. He's not a bad professor but his lectures can be a little dull to that point that it's hard to pay attention. During class he has clicker questions but once he uploads the slides the answers are not on the slides so it makes it hard when you do the online quizzes which are super long. exams are similar to the quiz.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Class works well with Science of Water if you take one after the other. Daily quizzes on clickers count for large portion of grade and serve as attendance tracker. Textbook is required but if you take notes at all lectures and do the optional study guides on blackboard you'll pass the daily quizzes and 3 tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Go to class, clicker points are a good percentage of your grade. Do the modules and get A's on them. They are tedious and time consuming but not difficult. The quizzes are your best friend, study them, every question, most of them will be on the exam. Read the textbook material for the clicker questions. If you do all of these, its an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very responsible, knowledgeable, and carrying. The quizzes are very similar to the test. Lectures heavy but if you just study the slides, pay attention in class, it'll be easy.  The material is interesting so it won't be hard. Will have to work harder for an A and not very hard for a B. I'd def recommend him.

Professor Miller is an extremely knowledgeable and passionate professor. His lectures are pretty rapid fire but the practice quizzes he posts online are essentially the tests. There are clicker questions that you get graded on every class so attendance is necessary. Show up, pay a little attention, and do the practice quizzes and you'll pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a good professor. He helps you if you ask for the help since its a huge class. His online quizzes look a lot like the exams so make sure you study the quizzes, they aren't for credit but help study for his exams. The class itself is pretty boring unless your really into geographical sciences. His class isn't hard as long as you put work in.

Dr. Miller is passionate about what he does, but he doesn't seem to understand that not everyone in his 100-level classes are as interested in the subject as he is. He zooms through the lectures, so it's better to save your hand and just print the lectures off once he puts them on Blackboard. Take the practice tests; they don't hurt your grade.

A good professor that was clear in his lectures that were sometimes boring, sometimes interesting. Have to come to class, because lectures have clicker questions and are major part of your grade. No homework, except like 5 learning modules that can be done in 10 minutes. 3 Exams that are like the non-graded online quizzes he posts.

Dr. Miller is great! Make sure you go to class because he does incorporate clicker questions, that will impact your grade. He is very helpful and answers questions throughout class. If you go to class, take the online quizzes, and review the the course material theres no way you should get a grade less than a B!

Patient, clear, helpful, approachable, and a passionate professor. Many people found this class boring, but that is because they had no interest in the subjects of matter. The exams are based upon ungraded practice quizzes. Easy to get an A, yet you can learn a lot. Miller is one of my favorite professors at UMBC thus far. Highly recommend.

Textbook will reinforce learning but not essential. Lectures can be boring but there are clicker questions for points so you can't skip that often. Learning Modules are often easy but take A LOT of time. Exams are based off of the online quizzes (which don't count). If your confused ask questions and TAKE THE PRACTICE QUIZZES.

If you have a serious interest in hydrology, you will learn a great deal from this class.  Be prepared for lengthy and challenging assignments and exams that will make you want to chop your hand off.  That being said, this class is very fulfilling and Dr. Miller will ensure that you learn as much as possible.

He is very passionate, but boring and dull. It is hard not to sleep and goof off in class. What you need to do to get an A in this class is take all the online practice quizzes for good exam grades, and do all the learning modules. Textbook not necessary.

Great professor! Dr. Miller offers a ton of reading material, videos, websites, etc. online for students interested in geography. I've never had a professor who takes the time to put together so much extra material! Fast grader and good with keeping students updated through e-mail. Exams are practically identical to online practice quizzes.

Just show up for class for clicker questions which are based on reading the textbook. Do learning modules. Study off of optional online quizzes. Lots of quiz questions, so start them early. You'll end up using your textbook and lecture slides so that's how you study.

He's very passionate about this subject, but the class is boring. His exams are not all that hard, just study the quizes bkuz the same questions will b on the exam. He gives quizes every week, and gives 3 attempts. Nething over 80% is passing. Its not that much of a hard class just extremely boring. Use ur quizes as a study guide.

I had Dr. Miller for Physical Geography this past semester- I thought he was fantastic! His tests are fair, and he makes class worth going to by using powerpoints and animations to help explain harder to grasp concepts. He posts all materials on blackboard. There are 3 exams, about 12 online quizzes, and 4 learning modules. Highly recommended!

Be warned: his classes are notoriously difficult; but you will learn a great deal. You must do the reading and you must attend lectures. The classes are a lot of work, but he's very helpful and will go out of his way to make sure that you understand the concepts explained. Attend study groups for the exams.

His exams are all essay, but you don't have to write in paragraph form. You will need to remember a lot of information, but you'll learn a great deal. Make sure you start all his assignments more than the night before, since they'll take you a while. Overall, a pretty good teacher.
Reading the textbook and taking notes from it helps a lot with the lectures. Taking the exams are extremely difficult because it's mostly conceptual information.

Hes a good professor, If your a student who can assume to know the material as much as he does. I respect him as a man I respect his determination. But any time when kids in the class still pass and miss days and still pass because test are 90% of the grade? its a joke and just not worth it. avoid.

To be frank, Dr. Miller is no joke.  Taking a course with him will be a true experience.  He is very smart and speaks fast.  It is truly on you as a student to grab information that you feel is important to take note of.  Exams are full essay and require you to have definitely learned the information.  Its hard, but I approve of his teaching

This was an awesome class.  The material was rather challenging at times.  Some of the projects can be a little tedious (no project will take "20 minutes"!).  But Dr.  Miller is an excellent professor.  Lectures are well prepared.  Nah the exams aren't That bad.  Join study groups- will help tremendously.

Class was tough and very broad, but Dr. Miller makes it worth it.  He speaks very quickly, but will go out of his way to accommodate his availability with yours if you need to meet with him outside of his office hours for help.  STUDY HARD for exams, they are long and tedious.  LOTS OF WRITING!

I'm not shocked that i didnt do to well in this class. he assumes you get off the bus knowing this material.too much information with nothing to put it in.no quizes just months between test in which your supposed to remember somehow. bless those who do. for others? cost me my gpa. advice? quit this class if you enter. its just not worth it.

class is boring and hard to understand, especially considering it's entry level...but Miller is obviously passionate about the material and is very willing to help anyone that asks for it. Usually curves grades because the material is hard. Good guy and decent professor...if you go to class and read the book you should be okay.

He is truly passionate about the subject, and will go to great lengths to answer any questions and make sure you comprehend the material. He does expect a fair amount of work from you, so don't think you can just skate through the class.

Andy Miller is pretty much the man. He teaches an interesting subject and his lectures are well prepared. You won't like or understand the class if you haven't the slightest care for the sciences. If you have trouble in the class he will go to great lengths to help you out.

Class consists of 3 exams, they are not cumulative. Provides good study guides for exams. Lectures can be a bit boring, but he tries his best to get the class involved. He is more than willing to help his students if they put in the effort.
I have not been to class in 3 weeks and still plan on getting an A in this class. Three total test and the final isn't cumulative. Easy as anything.

I expected this class to be fun but it wasn't. Very boring lectures. I eventually stopped going to class but I ended up with a B in the class thanks to the book and CD-ROM. Much better teacher than he was.
Very hard for an introuductory course. He will help you if you need it. Lectures are too difficult to understand. AVOID TAKING THIS CLASS!!!!

DO NOT TAKE MILLER! HE IS PURE EVIL!  Boring lectures, too complicated for an intro level course, practice questions w/ no answers.  Usually HAS to curve exam grades b/c most people dont pass them.  HE SUCKS! Lectures based off text book though. Chem knowledge required...not fair!
Challenging class,but worth it. Pay attention and take good notes, you will make it. DONT SLACK ON NOTES!!!

knows his stuff!!!, lecture are pretty interesting, and the tests arent too bad if you actually study.  Usually curves.  Dont have to attend class, everything you need for tests is in the book.   very willing to help any student outside class

Tests are kind of hard, but really knows stuff.  lectures are uninteresting though and although he tries hard to get the class involved in the topic.  seems to be willing to help students as much as possible though
I enjoyed this class

Killer tests, very picky grader, drones on and on about boring or irrelevant topics. Not helpful at all. I thought this class was going to be about the entire Chesapeake Bay, but instead it was 90% about microbes and tidal patterns. AVOID AT ALL COST.
Not a hard course but you have to know your information, teacher knows his stuff

She is amazing!!! the best professor i've taken at umbc and extremely caring, after having a bad experience with another professor ghosting me for my letter of rec she  wrote one for me in 2 days and submitted right away on such short notice please take her she's the best !!!

Professor Ducat is amazing, and she is so passionate about her job and what she is teaching. There are some readings you must complete, but they are fairly easy. The homework is easy, and the quiz is open note. The final project is so fun (you do a case study on a fictional character of your choosing). Take her class, you won't regret it.

I'm taking Community Psychology with Prof. Ducat now and she's super nice. 

We have 3 assignments per week, no final, just a Town Hall. I have an A in the class so far and it's not too hard. If you show up and participate in class she gives you extra credit. She also lets you resubmit late assignments and assignments you want a better grade on.

Dr. Duffy is a great professor who the students can really relate to. He is easy to speak with and very approachable. Standard book hw, exams based on them, and group design project with a presentation at end of sem. Material could be dull at times, but the project was very open ended and good practice for rising engineers. Very positive experience
Duffy is one of the best professors I have had, highly recommend taking any class with him.

A fantastic professor that lets his personality shine through into his lectures. Easy to get a hold of and is very down to earth. Have taken 3 classes with him and not a single one was confusing or unenjoyable.

He is a very considerate and funny dude and the lectures were very engaging and helpful. The homeworks are kinda confusing to navigate, but once you get used to it it'll make sense. Make sure to get started with the assignments early because some of them take some time to do. Overall an amazing guy and a moderately easy class.
Only a week and a half in but he seems like a pretty cool guy, ngl
Took the course over the summer session and had a blast. The material was well explained and Prof is understanding enough to give you assistance when you need it. Also a great conversationalist.

Great experience! Handled remote learning exceptionally well and assigned reasonable amounts of work per week. The quality of the group members you select at the beginning of the semester will determine your grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great teacher highly recommended. He jokes around making it more fun and interesting to learn. He teaches the material in a clear and easy way. He gives a clear grading rubric of the homework, which can cause it to take longer, but it teaches you the thought process for solving problems. He responds quickly and is very easy to access out of class.

Homework problems are few, but take a long time. He is not the best at teaching undergrads because he is used to teaching grad students, so his lectures can be confusing since he doesn't always know what we do or don't know. It doesn't seem like he reviews his slides beforehand, so he will often be trying to figure out his own diagrams in lecture
Absolutely hilarious, and the content was always so interesting. Every lecture was like a podcast, and I learned so many cool things throughout the semester.

Terrific teacher and class, he cares very much about what he teaches as he follows a presentation with no words. Knocking knowledge off his dome and not missing a beat. A 2hr 30min class once a week and a dim lit theatre room made perfect for relaxation and chill time. It was wonderful, 3 papers is all this class grades, and they'll be A's.
Easiest class ever. Attendance is mandatory and graded along with only 3 papers that consisted of 1000 words each. His lectures were interesting and the films he showed felt like fever dreams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the most amazing professors I've had! Super knowledgeable and engaging in lectures- never boring. Workload was also super minimal, and he was a very easy grader. I'd say it's an easy A and a super interesting class. Lectures can be long, but he is respectful of students' time. Loved ART215!
Such a nice professor! Graded by attendance and 3 easy papers. Really passionate about art. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's nice, knows what he's talking about, and is genuinely enthusiastic about the subjects. His grading is simple as well; he takes attendance but does not use it to determine the final grade. His course only has three big papers, and it was rather simple and achievable if you took your time.

Lectures were incredible, I learned a lot from his course without any stress. Lectures are long but interesting--great time to draw and introduces many artists that he is very knowledgeable about. Only had three essays, all of which were graded very easily. Highly recommend to anyone needing an art credit or a chill class :)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The easiest class you could possibly take. Graded by 3 papers, no exams whatsoever. Class is just him showing us movies and videos while passionately lecturing on some other cool art stuff. He can be funny depending on your sense of humor. Really easy grader as well, follow the prompts & you'll be fine. Show up to class though he marks attendance

Easy class! You can tell he is passionate about what he teaches. The lectures are long, so I highly recommend bringing a sketchbook with you and sitting next to a friend. Don't bother bringing a laptop since he will call you out. I received A's for all three papers. Not easy assignments, but they could be done in a single night.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great class- interesting and super easy!

This class was super easy. There are no exams. The class is graded on attendance and 3 essays, which were only around 1000 words each. You can easily sign in for other people. We mainly just watched movies and looked at artwork during class, but participation doesn't matter so you can go to sleep or go on your phone.
Was really nice and understanding. We basically watched a lot of movies and there were a total of three papers and no final. This was a class that I looked forward to.

Definitely an easy A class. Would've liked some warning about content of some videos- some of us have migraines triggered by flashing lights -but otherwise pretty solid. Mostly just hid in the back and played minecraft when the movies were too much for my head. Tip for papers- he likes big words only if you use them right. You should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Took ART215 and ART329 with Mark - very caring and kind professor! Always understanding and genuinely wants to get to know students. Extremely knowledgable and passionate about photography and art in general. Shows a lot of movies and film clips in class and always leads great discussions afterward. Highly recommend!
Easy Art class. Show up for attendance and do the three papers and you'll pass the class, no problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's honestly awesome. The grade is dependent on 3 papers and attendance. The lectures don't have much to do with what you write about most of the time, but either way, its a really interesting class (and I'm a STEM major, highly recommend). If you need an art GEP covered, take this
east A class. come to the class and submit 3 papers to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Mark Durant cares deeply about the subjects, and gives amazing lectures.  Most of the content is exclusive, attending lecture is a treat.  The only downside is that the class is very long, but if you pay attention it's more like entertainment than class.  The only grades other than attendance are 3 papers, which are short and easy to complete.

Art 215 is a great sampler of contemporary art, and a very easy class! You have 4 essays, but there are no tests or quizzes based on the lectures. Just show upit's mandatoryand enjoy yourself! You're sure to see some new stuff, and it's mandatory for most of ya'll anyway. (P.s. non art majors looking for an easy, interesting classthis is it.)

Class was VERY interesting- I loved all the topics he discussed in this class. The only killer is that the lecture is 2 1/2 hours.....you can get away with falling asleep. Lectures are great to listen to, but not completely mandatory to pay attention. Essays are easy and have nothing to do with the lectures. Pretty easy A class.

Pretty easy class to begin with, but he's fun to listen to. It's hard to lecture on intro to art stuff, and intro to photography, but I think he does it better than anyone else could.  He's enthusiastic about it too.

Wonderful teacher! He's very passionate about the subject. If you're an art major the content is interesting and his personality makes it even better. He does take attendance even though it's a lecture hall class, so it's important to go, but since it's a fun class, that's not hard! The only down side is that it's such a long class at 2 1/2 hours.

This class was incredibly boring, but he at least seemed interested in it. It was annoying that he taught in a bigger than usual lecture hall and refused to use a microphone, and because his voice is soft, it was hard to hear him. He's not very good at grading papers, and it seems his top priority is focusing on how many words it has. Average.

Best professor EVER. The man is funny, relatable, approachable, helpful, and if you take a few classes with him, he certainly becomes a friend. His grading method is awesome. If you try, you will get an A, no doubt about it. Despite knowing I'd get an A in his classes, I actually did the most work in them. I couldn't recommend this professor more!!

There's really nothing to lecture about in intro to art and media studies. There are many photos to look at and many videos to watch, most will put you to sleep. I really don't know if I can say much about the class. Attendance isn't mandatory. Just do the three essays and you're basically in the clear. Reading the graphic novels is fun though.

Not a very good teacher...actually, he doesn't teach much at all, he just shows movies and such most of the time.  The essays appear to be graded purely on whether he likes them or not, so if he doesn't like how you write, you're sunk.

Truly fantastic professor. Has become a mentor and friend. Don't be afraid to speak to him after class, he is very relaxed and humorous, and just wants people to discuss during his classes. If you're not interested in the material you're probably not listening well enough. Take advantage of an interested professor!
His upper level classes are not a breeze like the intro class talked about below, but he is still a fun, and very intelligent.

Really easy class... all you do is watch movies--seriously. He is really easy but doesn't do a very good job introducing or explaining the films we watch. Either way, there's practically no way you can fail. The textbooks are comic books.

really easy class, all you have to do is go and watch movies, read a couple of comic books and write short (3page) papers about them. he's really nice and very into everything covered in the class. guest speakers are also pretty interesting.

Loved his Intro to Art and Media class. He's smart and sharp and has good taste, and the class is more of a viewing session with a couple of papers (I got all A's) than a lecture. It was a great break from schedule, even though it's 3 hours. Cool teacher, and his wife, Bea Bufrahi, is also an awesome teacher at the Baltimore School for the Arts.

He was awesome and fair. Just know beforehand that if you want an A on a paper he wants "original thinking". I made a B on the first paper because I was expecting him to be like all other teachers who just want to hear what's been said before. His class was very good and I learned a lot.

Mark is the best! He is the only teacher that has both feet on the ground. He honestly critiques everyone fairly but doesn't beat around the bush he will tell you that you are doing well or not. Show up for his class everyday and do the work and show progress and he will give you an A. Some of his stories he tells in class are so worth the trip.
Extremely easy. Guaranteed A if you attempt everything. I even skipped a lot of classes.

this class was very boring, ur grade is base on 3 papers. we had a sign up sheet, so if u were taking this class w/ a bunch of ppl u could take turns going to class just to get ur named signed. the 1st 2 papers were base off 2 books and the last is about some an artist, so basical u don't need to go to class. No notes, no tests.

very opinionated and doesn't hesitate to snap at ur comments during open discussions.  this class was a waste. all we did was watch videos and write 3 papers. when disagreeing w/ him he will simply brush u off.

Dr. Dusman is one of the best teachers I have ever had. She treats each student with so much respect and thoughtfulness. She is supportive what you want to do with your composition, and is there to help guide and help you get to your best!

Difficulty is more like a 3.5.  If you indicate that you have a drive and desire to work hard, Dr. Dusman will help you achieve things you never thought possible. This is not an exaggeration. She is a phenomenal educator, probably one of the best in the country right now. If you have any opportunity to take one of her classes, jump at it!
Very good professor. Took instrumentation. Geared towards music education majors, not composers. Was an easy class as long as you tried and followed what the book/professor said to do.

One of the best professors at UMBC. Hands down. I adore her and she has been a great help to be as a Music student. She's very approachable and makes concise and creative decisions whenever you have concerns. The class is easy if you are willing to do the work. Be prepared to do a lot of composing for class and always PARTICIPATE in discussions!

She is one of the best professors I've had. ALWAYS DO YOUR WORK, it will help you understand composition better. She is a very talented composer, too. In her administrative aspect, she is very decisive and very creative with solutions to problems. She has helped me out in all of my years here as a Music student.

A very challenging but EXCELLENT professor. He pushed us to our limits, and really encouraged us to invest a lot of thought and research into making our best work. Has good insight. His feedback is excellent and spot-on, and meets students at their level. He doesn't coddle but is kind and cares for students. Be ready to be stretched and grow a lot.

I rather have my schedule changed all the way if there is another type 2 professor. Aviod him at all cost, I am so god dam glad is the last day of his class. SO SICK his BS. He is not teaching next semester so I am so glad for the future type 2 students. But if any of y'all see the name Dugan please RUN!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I do not like him AT ALL. He just make the class so stressful, I like the projects but his way of running the class made it very hard. He wants us to print constantly and very unclear. I have never been so stress in my life. HE REALLY IS A WORK OF ART. whoever thinks that he is a good professor , you must be really crazy . I give him 0 star
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Awful class & very very expensive. He grades your work as if you should already have 20 years experience under your belt. Doesnt explain how to do things. Expects you to have work printed every class & doesnt care about the expense. Save up a few hundred $ before taking this class, youll need it. He doesnt like cheap paper either
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I like him , however he is very strict with critique and I am not being sensitive but I feel like he has like 6 faces. One 1 min he like what you are doing and tells you to keep going and when the final is due he throws you under the bus.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Dugan has good info about the intricacies of design, but seldom shares it. Grading is arbitrary at best, syllabus is useless. You don't learn how become a good designer in his class. You just make a design, change it to how he wants it to look, then hope he doesn't contradict himself in the next crit. You don't keep your projects, either.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you want to learn skip this professor. He is confusing at best and doesn't believe in feedback or guidance.  I wish I knew beforehand. Wasted my hard earned money.

Take her if you want an easy A. 2 exams and 1 final. 1 easy group project. She gives a couple of HW which really help with the exams. Very quick and lenient grader. Gives a lot of partial credits. Her lectures are kinda boring as she reads from the slides. She gives practice assignments at the end of the lectures which helps. Cares for her students
Lectures are boring. She wants to help everyone. She replies to emails in 3 minutes. She gives a ton of partial credit on tests. She is always available to help her students.

Her lectures can be boring sometimes as she reads from the slides but she let you ask questions and there are exercises after each lecture. One semester-long group project, there are hw every week which help you with the project and exams. Get back to your email quickly. Overall a good professor who cares about her students.

Professor Dvorak is a good professor. I loved his energy, and he always told interesting stories. My only complaint is his disorganization. His blackboard is a mess, and the tests are easy but unpredictable. The study guides aren't great, and his wording can be difficult to read. However, the class is not a hard class and the topic is interesting.

Love this guy! Very down to earth and cares about people, esp the homeless population he works with. Good sense of humor and passionate about his field. Addictions of any kind are so relevant and this class hits all of them to some degree. I highly recommend him. He also cares about what's going on in your own life unlike some professors.

The class was late at night, but he did his best to engage students. Great guy, straight up, funny, sarcastic, flexible. Go to class, take notes, book isn't exactly necessary but it was helpful. Posts p-points before exams. Had to attend NA/AA/etc. meeting, but the paper for that was straightforward. Highly recommend his class!! Learned a LOT!

I am a drug counselor and took this class for an easy A (which it was). However, the info Dvorak gives is his opinion, unsubstantiated by research, and follows a long line of myths that plague the substance abuse field. Please do your own search for knowledge in this field and do not believe the outdated beliefs that Dvorak portrays as fact.

This class was late at night, and it was difficult to stay awake and focused on his lectures. He does not stay on topic and he has the worst powerpoints I've ever seen. I thought it was difficult for me because I basically didn't know what was going on. Read your book, and go to class and he won't fail you.

He is extremely engaging.  This class is very interesting and you will learn a lot from Professor D.  He has a lot of experience and shares stories with about past and current clients to add to lecture material. Lecture slides are online.

Definitely recommend this teacher. And considering he only teaches this one course at umbc, don't miss the chance! Brings great knowledge from years of experience in field, and is incredibly funny, all around great person.  This is one of the few college courses I have taken that I looked forward to coming to class. If SW major, plz take this class

This professor seemed ok at first, but when it came down to the grade at the end of the semester,he tells you one thing on the syllabus and then grades you completely different, even if u attend all the classes and participate. I agree with another poster, he plays favorites. Avoid!

This was my favorite class this semester, and Dr. D made it that way. He's funny and down to earth. As long as you go to class and listen to what he has to say, you'll do just fine on the exams. While the papers may seem intimidating at first, they really arent that bad if you follow the directions. Take this class!!

Worst Professor I have ever had. He's a nice guy, but when it comes to grading the paper (which is worth 30% of the grade) he is HORRIBLE. If he likes you, he will give you a decent grade. Otherwise, you will get a C or if you are lucky (like I was) you will get a low B. It was my lowest grade that I ever got on a paper in college.

This guy is great! He's a MSW C.L. and brings a lot of 'real' knowledge from his work experiences in the field. The class is titled "Addictive Behavior Patterns," but most of the course focused on Substance Abuse. Overall, a very informative course and a must for anyone considering working with the Substance Abusing population. Easy exams too!

Took this course online with one in person lecture. Eric seems very knowledgeable and definitely enjoys the arts, but otherwise I can't say much about him. Video lectures are straightforward and cover the content of the readings, and also include the films being discussed. Units are at your own pace with a generous deadline. Tests are very simple.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Spent the entire class as slave labor for his pet project instead of learning anything. I understand that the school wants to keep him on, but they really need to stop letting him teach at this point.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Even before the pandemic Eric Dyer was constantly and consistently disorganized and unprepared for class, When we had physical classes we would spend a abhorrent amount of time trying to get his presentations to work. His presentations were just a word-for-word recanting of the textbook that we were required to read for random pop-quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable in his field and brings that perspective to the class, he also provided great feedback and insight during work in progress days, and kept projects interesting. His class was by far my favorite of my college career. However, he can be a bit slow to reply to emails and is pretty hard to track down if you need him outside of class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Not sure about personality. Doesn't reply to emails, doesn't post grades, but does give you excellent feedback if you know to ask for it. A little too hands-off, kinda unclear with grading criteria, but otherwise pretty okay. If you have a bad group in one of his group projects, he won't do anything about it, and that's what boils my crayfish.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: You won't know your grades on assignments as he does not post them. When changes to the syllabus were made & to what the final project would be, it was such a hassle to get him to give us enough time to complete it. On top of that he wanted the final due 2 weeks before final's week, & was unable to give a reason as to why the due date was pushed up
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Well versed and very approachable in the subject in animation. He always finds time to discuss classwork. He is a keeper.
Good professor has experience with working as a successful independent artist.  Good crit just a bit slow on grades.  Does use blackboard and you have the ability to retry on projects

Really great guy, appreciates if you're serious and always willing to work with you and give you a better grade if you redo a project.  He's there to help you learn and provides honest and helpful criticism. He does not appreciate (of course) if you blow off his assignments.  If you've never taken 341 be prepared DO NOT UNDERESTIMATE projects!!!!

Great class, you'll learn a lot. Very approachable professor. Nice. He encourages you to create the best, high quality work you can produce. A little late with e-mail responses, though, but he is a busy guy. AWESOME! You will improve in animating if you put in the effort! 2 thumbs up.
Good teacher. Smart, funny, approachable. I thoroughly enjoyed the course material as well.

An awesome professor, as long as you get your work done and make the effort. Can be seem somewhat rude at times if you are frequently late or fall short on assignments, but if you try hard, you'll do fine in the class.
Does not respond to email, condescending.

He lectures better than any other professor in the department.  There is a final project where you have to build a toy (yes, another toy project) that is run off of elastic or potential energy.  There are also labs where you use a milling machine and a lathe.  Take lots of notes, but still you'll need a miracle to get a B on any of his exams.

Very interesting class. He is an excellent lecturer. You have 50 minutes to take the midterm, but you really need about 3 hours. The lab reports use up most of the time you need to study for other classes, and nobody does well on them. They are graded incredibly harshly. TAKE NOTES IN CLASS! The exams are open notes, and trust me, you need them.

I?ve never seen anyone who can give a well organized lecture from memory. HW grading is fair. Tests are meant to destroy your spirit. Practice lots of problems. Labs are interesting, but the reports are graded harshly and inconsistently. Overall, an intense and interesting class taught by a very knowledgeable professor.

Very high expectations.  Very good at teaching and very interested in the subjects he teaches.  You will learn a lot from him.  Do not try to BS through his class, you will do poorly if you do.  Come to class and always write notes

Very well prepared instructor.  Took over a 6 week summer session so it went very fast but he was very clear and easy to understand.  Not many instructors can teach a summer class.  He is one of them.

Very knowledgeable on a subject, never had a lecture prepared on a sheet of paper, derived every formula from memory and all lectures were organized as though he were reading from a script. Talks and writes at the same time, bring a recording device and write at the same time. Ruthless taskmaster, be warned. He will insult your intelligence.
Best teacher I have had at UMBC.  Requires a lot of work, but very fair.  Lectures off the top of his head, and damn good at it.  Makes material enjoyable.

Smart. Extrmly tgh grdr. You could spnd 12 hrs on a reprt, it's perfct, you get a 90 b/c he didn't lik th ordr or choice of wrds in 1 sent.  He goes vry fst, somtims dsn't use exmpls when nec.  Exms are hard and some ?s arnt taught, & not in txt, reqr resrch or extrpltn of fcts. lern lots thogh. Smtmes it's hard to c how infrmtn is going 2 b used
This is a sneak
