Only bad students would give him a bad rating.  Grading is clearly explained and exam topics are outlined prior to exam. This professor is one of the best you will have in ME at UMBC.  Highly recommended.

This guy rocks.  My hand still trembles at the thought of this class.  Harded ME course so far... and I'm almost done.  I learned so much my head hurts.  He is very knowledgeable and always eager to share it with you (as long as it's during office hours... "teaching is a job!").  Don't fear, just man up.  You'll be a stronger person if you survive.
Definitely an awful professor. Try to get Zupan if you can. Arola's lectures are clear but the labs and exams aren't. This class is extremely time consuming and he's a plain jerk!

Avoid this professor if possible. His exams are setup so students will perform poorly eventhough the material isn't difficult. The grading isn't clear and the whole class is curved at the end. The curve isn't explained so good luck trying to calculate your grade. Avoid this pompous jerk and find a helpful professor ;)
This class is difficult and time consuming.  Dr. Arola's lectures are very clear.  I learned alot!
The class is very time consuming and semi-difficult. Some of the labs are confusing so the TA comes in handy. Zupan is the best professor for this course.

absolutely great, i can honestly say one of the best professors i have had.  He is extremely organized and intelligent. It shows in the presentation of his lectures.  I have found him to be very helpful when you go for help.

Dr. Arola is God's son.  And don't ever forget it...not that he'll let you.  He extreamly well prepared and presented lectures, and he is very fair. but don't misunderstand him...teaching is a JOB.  He is onr of the best profs you will ever have at UMBC.
The easiest A ever!

The class structure under her supervision is easy because most of the material was kinda common sense so class lecture is very boring, I fell asleep a few times but still got an A because last minute reading is sufficient. Exams were online for this semester and open note so the course is a breeze. She reads off the laptop so its all book stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Shelter Dziya is a very compassionate lecturer, she truly does care about student well being, i was going through a tough time with some family matters and she took the time to email and check in on me. The lectures are clear, enjoyable and i feel that i have managed to get alot of of them.

Professor Shelter Is passionate and dedicated. She's consistent in her expectations and clear in her requirements. If you engage and put in work she'll work with. No chance of coasting and passing, she won't make last minute exceptions if you've not engaged throughout. Good sense of humour and inspirational. Her motivation motivates!

She's very specific about what she wants on open ended questions. She can be very sarcastic and unprofessional in emails to the class. She's got a great energy for lecturing but if she's in a mood it's a terrible time. Start her assignments early, some of them WILL take 10 hours to complete.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She. Drives. Me . Inane. Will TEXT (Remind 101) you at inappropriate times about unimportant things. Full of herself. Treats you like you're in second grade but then expects a lot. Cancels class a lot. RIDICULOUS time consuming assignments.

Treats us like high schoolers: interrupts lecture to tell off a single student and micromanages by only allowing laptops in the first 3 rows in a huge hall. She just reads off the slides but has in-class group activities randomly. All you have to do is show up, read the book, and do the labs for an easy A. Exams are based off the book and labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's horrible. Although she pretends to know everything, you can watch her google and research questions she is asked in class. None of the material is her own. Be sure to attend and pay attention as she obviously has a chip on her shoulder about attendance and phone usage while in class.

She tried to fail me because I missed a test, for which I was in the hospital at the time. I've seen her google the answers to questions she is asked during the middle of class. To top it off, none of the study material she gives out is actually her own work. One of the most asinine professors I've ever had. Astounded that she is employed at UMBC.

Did none of her own work, got PowerPoints and in-class activities from other sources. Didn't know answers to large numbers of questions asked, then would proceed to Google answers. If you want to actually learn the material, read the book because she won't teach it to you. It's a shame that attendance is required, although the class is very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Easy, most of the work is online. If you do the online work and get 100%, tests are no problem.

She hates people being on their phones during lecture (which is understandable), but she will stop teaching just to call you out or kick you out. Lots of clicker questions which count towards your grade so come to class. If you do the homework and quizzes online you should get at least a B in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I expected this to be an easy class because its a 100 level. I am also a junior so I didn't expect the class to have such strict participation and attendance rules. Aside from that the professor was really fun and engaging. Some topics were better than others but for the most part I really enjoyed this course. Just wish attendance wasn't mandatory.
Amazing person and professor. Take her classes.
She's the man
One of the best profs i've had. Shes very nice and helpful. She even helped me do a project for another class. Very interesting subject matter.
Interesting lectures, but TAs grade unfairly
Really interesting class and professor. She loves philosophy and tries hard to explain it. Posts notes on blackboard and assignments are fairly easy.

Interesting topics but honestly little point in going to class. She puts all notes on blackboard and after the first exam she gave us a list of all the questions on the test. I failed first exam, aced other two. the difference? I stopped going to class. TAs grade INSANELY hard. Honestly, MEMORIZE THE READINGS because that is what they grade on.

The class was really good! She lets you get into debates with your classmates which I found really helpful when it came time to write my final schema analysis. She expresses her own view a lot...but if you can get beyond that, she's a lot of fun!!

She's a great teacher.  She's so funny and makes the class interesting -- and her Australian accent is so cute!  I had a death in my family when the final paper was due and she was so understanding and really helped me out.  She's always willing to talk or help you out if you stop by her office after class.  The class is a challenge but very fun!

Dr. Dwyer is a sweet lady and youcan tell she loves what she's teaching.  Grading scale is nice, but her TA's grade unbelieveably hard for a 100 level class.  All tests are essay, so it leaves answers open to interpretation. Enjoyable class, but tests and papers are more difficult than they should be.

The class and the readings are rather boring. If you do not agree with Dwyer, she will basically humiliate you in class. She is very narrow and even makes**** boring. Additionally, her TAs are neither interesting or well informed. Don't take this class, it is simply not worth the effort or frustration.
Readings for the class were well-picked, but Dwyer is very narrow, not particularly interesting, and as a whole uncompelling.  I would not recommend.

She is an awesome teacher. Even if ur major does not require this class, take it. you will be very inspired. her tests are very easy thanks to her review questions. the papers are also very easy and she will look at as many drafts as you want her to. she will go out of her way to help you any way she can. she rocks!!!
this was the most interesting class i have taken so far. her lectures are very funny and she allows a lot of time for class discussion, plus the tests are ridiculously easy.
I love her Contemporary Moral Issues class.  I've never been so interested in a class before.  The content is so relevant and captivating.  Dwyer really inspires you to think and analyze.
not hard, but philosophically narrow

She was a very detailed teacher. She helped me understand a lot about philosophy. Her classes aren't boring, they're interesting. Tests are easy... you get review questions that pretty much outline the test. She gives her free time to help and talk to you

Liked listening to her Australian accent. Great woman. Fun classes-brought her dog. Papers aren't bad if you prepare and GO TO CLASS. Exams are easy, get questions ahead of time. I had no prior experience in philosophy and loved the class, got an A.
If you actually get to know her, she's a really interesting and helpful person who deserves more credit than given.
She is a very analytical philosopher, which is nice, but she has little knowledge of and love for non-analytic philosophy.
awesome teacher for seminars, good grader, brought her dog ramsey to class
Hope you like writing papers . . .

Was a little entertaining in class, but super arrogant. I emailed him that I was sick a day in advance, and gives me a zero for it. I go talk to him about it, and he fails to mention there being a pop quiz or anything and refuses to change the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lots of simple, busy work! Three papers that can be completed with last-minute research, weekly blogs, and three-question quizzes every week. It's not necessary to be present. Overall, a simple elective.
A lot of easy busy work! 3 papers which can be done by last min research, weekly 3 questions quizzes, and weekly blogs. Attendance is not required. Easy elective overall.

He was a great professor and made his classes super engaging. The only issue if anything was that grades took forever to come in but he provides opportunities to improve your grades by the end of the semester and provides extensions. Although there were three papers and weekly quizzes, there is no final so it cancels out.

First off, there are no pop quizzes and he grades fast, so I think he's taken his past criticism to heart. Ealick is an amazing lecturer. I thought I would hate the class but its my favorite. Its not a lot of work and its not a big deal to miss a class, the readings he assigns cover the lectures well.

Do NOT take this class. Almost the end of the semester and I currently have 3 grades in. The feeling of genuinely not knowing the outcome of this class is one that no one deserves to have. Anything that I need to improve on, I won't know until the end of the semester. It's quite annoying too, considering he has a TA.

Expects students to be understanding when he doesn't grade anything on time. Harsh grader as well, so if you are unhappy with your grades (when he finally returns them) there is no time to correct anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Best professor Tom take during the summer. He is always so chill. Tough grader. But assignments are simple. Easy to get. Good grade.

Ealick is the best. He's open about his expectations, grading criteria (not a pushover), and really knows his stuff. He'll clarify, answer questions, listen if there is an issue, and cares if you care. Attendance is not mandatory but recommended; take good notes. Top notch lectures and discussion is encouraged. I'll never forget this class.

This professor was my first encounter with philosophy and he made sure to make it an awesome one. His lectures were never boring and I found them really interesting, plus the were easy to follow which is nice. We only had 2 short papers and one 5-page paper, and they were both easy. If you need to take a philosophy class, make it this one.
By far the best teacher that I've had so far.  An engergetic teacher who makes the lessons interesting and comprehensible.  Highly recommended.
Had him for Modern PR. Nice and a relatively easy grader. Group project at the end of the semester that is presented to judges.

Super kind, 
Super chill,
Super interactive.
If you just show up and do the bare minimum you'll get an A.
You could probably do neither of those and still get an A. 
But he's cool and his class is worth attending. 
Highly recommend.
Honestly one of the kindest professors I've ever had. He is so calm and patient with students. The material is not hard if you really pay attention. He's a real professional.

Professor Eagle was a great PR professor. As a current professional, he was able to give the class an insider view of what it is like to work in Public Relations. He brought in great guest speakers, and helped us stay current with media trends, something someone in the industry would likely do. Great professor!

A pretty easy class. you learn a lot of interesting things, but the book isn't necessary to get a good grade. 10 short news stories, a news release, a midterm, then a final project is all you really do. However, make sure you get a good project group or your grade will suffer. Overall a really good professor, very kind and open minded!

Eagle is still an active PR professional, so he is able to really teach about the field with current trends in mind. You turn in 10 "Sharing Stories" over the course of the semester, take a relatively easy mid-term, and then pitch a PR plan with a group for your final. If you're interested in PR, this is a must-take class with a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: A really sweet guy. He was extremely laid back and so understandable. His class is a public relations class, so he has you bring in a typed paper about a news story you found interesting and has you talk about it in class. One, REALLY easy midterm, which he gives a study guide for and a final group project. Take this if you're an MCS major.

Dr. Brooks runs his classes on the premise that students are adults who are responsible for their own education. If you put in the effort, you will learn so much. He is always ready to help with and discuss anything, from his own coursework, to outside projects, to future plans. Don't waste his time if you want to just coast through school:)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good professor, but can come off unprepared or underwhelming at times. He will start the semester off very tough-sounding, saying that you can't make up work that you miss, but that will change by the end of the semester. Lots of videos, lots of reading. He does not grade ANYTHING until after the semester is over, except attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Brooks was encouraging, he wants best for his students. In class discussions he is considerate in his responses in a refreshing and engaging way. Grades are slow to come back on assignments (mostly of reading responses, essays, and small quizzes) but he gives feedback & is accommodating and willing to help & explain.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Kind of disorganized and confusing. A very nice professor and the content was interesting, but nothing was graded until after the semester, and I felt like my time and effort wasn't being respected. In class, we mostly just read from his PowerPoints and watched documentaries. Lots of writing, which was good for understanding but exhausting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great discussions. Interesting documentaries. Flexible deadlines. Caring personality. Creative and safe space. I finally found books I enjoy reading through this class.

I learned SO much in this course. Dr. Brooks is an absolutely amazing instructor and really works with you wherever you are. He assigns a lot of reading (15 books in my class), but all of them are very up to date and you will learn a ton if you read everything. If you don't think you can handle that, I would suggest taking someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: NO idea why rating is so lowwork smart, not hard ppl! Take this class with expectation to get an A, not learn (sadbuttrue). He assigns like 53 books, but you don't ACTUALLY hv to read them all  just get quotes for the reading responses & ur good. Papers never correlate to the booksjust show up to every class, do assignments, and you'll get an A.

There is a lot of reading required for class but he gives you everything you need to be successful. As long as you do the reading and assignments on time, and attend class there is no reason why you should not get an A. He did post some assignments late but always gives extra time when he does. Lots of good insightful group discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--So many papers

reviews.comment: The reading material teaches you nothing about actually analyzing arguments but rather is an excuse to talk about subject matter close to him. Way too much reading to actually get any depth out of anything and by the end of the class I wasn't doing it at all and still passed because it isn't necessary. Group work every class that was pointless.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Great professor, you learn a lot even beyond the scope of rhetoric and English in this class. The group project is tricky, but if you ask him questions, you'll be just fine. The paper gets broken up into chunks which helps. Challenging, but super rewarding and fun. MUST do the reading
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Brooks makes you work for your grade but is accessible by email and office hours if you need clarification on any instructions that seem vague. The inclusion of African American rhetoric as the core of the class is an amazing opportunity to learn about texts and contexts outside the white canon. Open communication and try your best
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I'm stunned that no one has mentioned the absolute worst part of his class: the 30-page paper that you work on all semester, on which he gives no guidance or feedback whatsoever. Also, there is a reading response due every class and missing even one nets you a B, per his ridiculous "grading" contract. Avoid this course at all costs.

Professor Brooks is a nice guy, but this class was incredibly poor. He used a vague contract and didn't grade anything until the end. His online syllabus is poorly laid out, and he changes it without explicitly telling you. The worst part is he runs this class like an African American studies class, not like an English class as advertised. :(
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Enjoyable man. Not an enjoyable class. It felt like he taught the class to only teach African-American studies, not English. I did not learn anything useful related to rhetoric, which the course was supposed to be focused on. The content was boring and unrelated to what I thought it would be. He also uses a grading contract. Avoid if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy but I haven't learned anything English related. He is obsessed with African-American oppression and lets his fascination with the topic corrupt the subject matter of the class. It feels like he only took the job to spread awareness to a topic close to him as opposed to actually teaching English. It is deliberate and he knows it.

His lectured are extremely boring. He barely teaches anything in class and will allow so much time to go by while you discuss with your peers. Plays very boring videos and podcasts. Terrible class! (He is a nice, intelligent professor) I dislike his teaching style though.

Professor Brooks himself is friendly and intelligent. However, the structure of his class is vague and different, the readings thick and unstimulating, and the projects/assignments unique but unsatisfying. The class teaches one another and interacting with your peers is mandatory. Try your best and use your resources and you should be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Brooks is really cool and so nice, but this is one of those classes that doesn't have set grades and you constantly worry about what's being counted because there's no way of knowing. It does involve a lot of interaction with peers. I wouldn't say the class was very difficult, but it does get really boring at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Classes are lead by the students, so I never knew if I was getting the info that the prof wanted us to understand. A lot of reading and some of it was redundant. SSRs were a pain more than helpful, but they are a way to prove that we read. He did give a pop quiz. The projects were vague, but that gave me the freedom to learn new programs and info.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Such a nice guy and really cares about what you're saying when you speak up in class. Is very welcoming to all students creative ideas and never makes you feel dumb. The assignments aren't difficult and very enlightening. I love it!
He is so disorganized. His instructions are unclear and indirect. I cannot stand his teaching style. I would never take another class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Nice enough but not very passionate. Leaves us to our own devices and pretty much has us teach the class so I haven't really learned anything from him. The projects are easy enough once you get past the vagueness. A lot of reading and the readings are sometimes redundant. Don't skip more than 2 classes because he doesnt take drs. notes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He is very good. Ask for anything and he will help. Projects every week. Even your midterm and final is a project. Do work and you will get an Easy A in this class.

class: programming languages. all group work. different language every time, couldn't use c++, java, or python so had to learn new stuff. new project every week. Went above and beyond, explaining everything from how to write a resume, functional programming, chomsky grammars,  and other great theory stuff. also very entertaining.

He's a nice teacher and has a lot of knowledge about many different languages. You have to work hard in this class but he gives you many chances to get extra points(group work).  I'm glad I took this class with him.

Larkey is just not a reliable or dependable professor. He doesnt explain assignments well, and the assignments he gives are incredibly convoluted so explanations are very important. He is slow to email back, if he even responds. And he is always unprepared, his lectures are very repetitive and overall pointless. The textbook isnt used at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Larkey is just winging it the whole time. His lectures go long, and he often repeats his video examples multiple times. The textbook is mostly unrelated to the course in its entirety. He gave one massive quiz that was a solid L. He often goes off syllabus to assign something huge and extensive. The class is interesting, but he's bad at running it.

His lectures are dull. The weekend before spring break he decided to assign a 20 page paper and an accompanying project to be done the week of break in lieu of the scheduled midterm on the posted syllabus "for our benefit."
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Spent a whole class counting his "um"s. It was a 1hr 15 min class and he said "um" 189 times. Went off syllabus first class. Makes up assignments and doesn't give specifics (compare these two shows. that's it). Drones on and on. classes are spent watching the same scene of a show in different languages. Never gives assignments or grades back.

Loves to hear himself talk. Takes attendance when no one is paying attention. Expects you to do the readings when he rarely brings them up in class. There was 1 quiz. Never updates Blackboard. LOTS OF GROUP PAPERS! The premise of the class is awesome but he ruins it with ill-prepared and long lectures. Doesn't stick to syllabus at all. Can't teach.

When walking into this course I thought that the class would be easy. Which in fact the course was. He rarely went off the syllabus or used the books he said to purchas. However, at the end once grades were out the grade DID NOT reflect the other grades that were given during the course of the semester.
Impossibly absentminded. Went off the syllabus after the first class. Expectations never made clear. Class structure was clearly not well thought out.

Will go on long tangents in German that the students can't understand. Assignments are not always made clear, but same format as 101/102 make it relatively easy. Fair but strict grader. Opinions on the language differ from the native German Frau Sutton, makes things confusing. Very knowledgeable but more suited for higher-level classes.

He could not teach his way out of a Kindergarten class. He doesn't know what he is doing. He was meant to teach upper level classes and not meant to teach German 201. He spent the last ten minutes of his class teaching the grammar portion and spent most of the class working with a partner.

This professor knows what he is talking about and is a very intelligent man. If you do the work, you are almost guaranteed and A. He teaches directly from the textbook and tests directly from the textbook.

A little tough--but you learn the language if you do all the work. Resigned about current status of MLL dept. but loves students who care. Very helpful outside of classroom. Very cool personal interests, plays German rock in class. A bit forgetful.

Really nice guy. First part of the class is boring- lewis and Clark. But at the end we got into the environmental movement and was a lot better. Gives study guides but grades a little hard. Not an easy A but if you work a little hard you'll get one.

You know, he is a really nice man. His class is required for the major and he really is NOT a difficult grader. He hands out study guides before each quiz and paper and the guides HAVE THE QUIZ QUESTIONS ON IT. If you are too lazy to pick up a book, change your major.  The only negative thing about him is he rambles and is VERY boring.
This guy is a really tough grader. You MUST read all the assignments. Overall, he is a nice guy and you walk away with a new perspective on things.
One og the greatst professors ever!! Such a nice little man!

Dr. Orser, though sometimes difficult in personality and grading, is really interested in the progress of his students as well as the quality of your work.  He's also filled with a wealth of useful knowledge and if you make the effort you will learn a LOT from him.

FYS on "Sense of Place", had to read a few fiction novels and write papers on them and on "field trips" we went on for the class. It made my days more interesting, at least. Teacher is a sweet old man, he remembers me now and boosted my self esteem concerning my writing. I'd recommend him.

Great, nice guy, but a horrendously difficult grader.  His grading policy is devastatingly unclear and costs the student the most.  Good for the lectures, but be aware that the papers are killer and plentiful!
Dr. Orser is a sweet, sweet old man.  He grades kind of tough, but fair.  Definitely one of the very best professors I've ever had.  He changed my life, I mean it.
Dr. Eggleton is a sweetheart and an excellent professor. Fluids is one of the hardest classes so you still need to put in a lot of work to pass.

He was nice, we barely met because it was online but he was easy going and a good teacher. He knew the material well and knew how to teach it. He wasnt so tech savy which was annoying but it was bearable. His exams were hard but he was a fair grader.

320 is a tough class and he taught it well. I was very confused at one point and i went to his office hours and he retaught the topic in a different way until I understood it. Overall he tries very hard to teach the material well and to be helpful when you ask. Showing up to class is a must because we run though very helpful practice problems.

Took him and Sanchez during summer. Always draw a free body diagram and write your assumptions even if it seems pointless because points will be deducted. Very nice professor though. If you don't like monotones or slow talking professors, grow up
He's an alright teacher and he does want people to pass, but thermo is not an easy class. Write down every stupid assumption and sketch every diagram, or else you can lose quite a few points
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: Take ENME320 with this professor, you won't regret it. His grading style is fair so that nobody won't fail his class unless you don't understand a single equation.

he s a very nice professor. he ll explain things clearly if you ask him questions. quizzes and exams are mostly from homework, so make sure you study every problem. he curves your grade by giving you a chance to use final exam grade to replace your worst midterm grade. it saved most ppl.

Most irritating teacher I've ever had. His monotone voice and repeated use off the word "right?" every two seconds drove me up the wall. Horrible instructor, does not like to teach. Uses a reversed classroom, which means that you teach yourself and he stares blankly at you while you do problems in class.

He is really busy, so don't assume that office hours will available all the time. The exams are not too difficult, but the final exam is by far the hardest and is worth the most. Make sure you do well on the final because it will probably decide your grade for the class.
excellent professor

Word of advice when taking this class: learn how to do Kline-McClintock error analysis, and show ALL of your formulas in the Appendix section, or else he'll brutalize your papers. Also, he lies about giving necessary equations on the final exam, so memorize them in advance.

Prof Rudow is the best! Our class had a few people but it was very exiting to join in and have conversations. We had weekly hw in which we presented to the class and had big discussions. He gives alot of insight in the psychology field and teaches us as well from personal experience. He is a very caring and enjoyable prof, I loved this course!

Dr. Rudow has a lot of experience in the field, which is evident in his lectures. He shares a lot of personal stories, but they are almost always related to the course. He is a fair grader, and posts grades promptly. He occasionally forgets due dates, so keep an eye on the syllabus. His laid back, frank attitude makes him a great professor overall.

Dr. Rudo is very engaging in his lectures. His years of experience in the field make for great stories that are always appreciated since they show how to apply the topic to real life. He is also a great person who clearly cares for his students and is very understanding. Make sure to sign up for his classes if they are available.

Professor Rudow was good. His lectures were long and a bit rambly; however, he was a fair grader and he really encouraged us to contribute to the class. This was especially helpful since it was the first semester back in-person after nearly a year and a half or so of lockdowns and virtual classes.

Rudow was an easy going professor. His class can get boring but when he'd talk about other things to relate to the lecture it was better. We only had a midterm and final. Attendance is a big part of your grade and there are not many things so make sure to show up! Easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Rudow was a great professor! His class was a bit boring at time but when he'd get off topic he'd have some interesting stories to share. We had weekly short 1 page paper, as well as a midterm and final. Attendance plays a big role also, so show up to get marked as present or grade will be affected. Otherwise pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Rudow is a fantastic professor. He is a true expert in his field, and his knowledge is very valuable in class. He is also truly invested in his students' success. If you attend the lectures and do the work assigned, you will get a good grade. He also has a fantastic sense of humor. I highly recommend his class.

He definitely gets very off-topic. The lectures were unbearable for me. He reads directly from the slides interjecting with his own opinions. I learned everything about the topic just from reading the textbook. Sexist/misogynistic undertones that several other females in class picked up on in. Easy A. Very flexible, which was nice.

took him in fall 2020- sweet guy, funny, replies fast to emails, class can get off topic (especially election time). weekly assignments(easy), midterm and final- midterm and final solely on the book(mc)- DON'T RELEY ON PPs - contains little material, most of its not on tests, read the book over and over to get those tricky qs. Overall good class

Im confused by other reviews. I dont get the hype. Dr. Rudow gets very off topic during lectures to a point where its annoying. Hes extremely political and expresses his views frequently. PPT are not prepared by him and do not help. The book is outdated. Exams have many issues and content not covered in lectures/PPT/book.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easiest A you'll ever get! I've taken two classes now with Professor Rudow and he's great! There are no weekly assignments just readings, a midterm and final!
Dr. Rudow is great! I recommend taking his classes. He's really nice. A+ professor I've already taken 324 and 360 with him.
Go to class, read the textbook, do your work  A
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Rudow is one of the best professors I've had at UMBC. You do need to show up, make sure you do the online quizzes, and you will need the textbook as the quiz questions come from the book and lecture slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: WoW, Dr. Rudow is one of the best in the whole state of Maryland. He has a great attitude and I can always ask him a question. How he dealt with me and saying that I have questions truly he was one of the best. I was praying for him to be happy and healthy. He is a real person and I got an A and a B and telling you you can do it by doing your work!
Great Conversations

Amazing professor, so understanding and treats students like HUMANS who have other priorities and understands that sometimes life happens. You learn alot from his class. Not just about the curriculum, but also about life.

Everyone told me to take his courses. He isn't difficult per se, but he has a policy that you have to get a 94% or above to get an A in his course. I earned a 92% because I missed one class (4 points per class attendance). I don't think missing 1 class earns a B. I got A's on the mid term and final (only other grades in his course). Bye bye 4.0....
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Someone at UMBC recommended me some of the professors to take and Dr. Rudow was 1 of them and I see why. He speaks on real life experiences and he is not here to fail any of the students because he provides open notes exam yay . I have no idea why 1 student gave him a poor review and still rated him as easy to me that is weird. Dr. Rudow is nice

I've taken like 3 classes with him and its a guaranteed A. He does just go over the powerpoint and talks all class which makes it super boring so bring work to do in class because your do get points for attendance (show up & pass). Other than being boring the class is super easy and he is "a real gem" :)
Amazing professor

He is the best Dr. and Professor because he is very educated and smart and his brain is the best. He knows what to do and he also has the best attitude you can find. If you do your reading and you listen and come to class you can get a good grade but you have to read. Have fun! I prayed for this teacher because he really cares about everybody!

This man is a gem in the broken world of academia. His class was exceptionally easy, but I still learned more from him than any other professor. Other sections had a 20+ page final; we had a 2 page final. Take him because if he taught every class in the program, I would take him over anyone else, any day of the week.
He is a really kind professor. You will learn about things that don't necessarily pertain to the class but to real world situations. Overall my favorite professor!
Funny guy and a "real gem'!

Grading was based on attendance, a midterm & final. Both take-home, but very difficult. Get the textbook for them. Around 50+ questions each. His class was primarily lectures (30%) and him sharing stories (70%). I couldn't get pass his sexist comments and anecdotes. If you want an A, he's your man. If you want to learn, try a different route.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's so chill but reads off PPT slides. He's basically reiterating what's in the book. You will complete several assessments on your personality, etc. and write a paper on your findings about yourself. Pretty fun.  Midterm  3 ppg. take home, cover 3 units/chaps. on most important things you learned. There's a presentation (1-3 people) and a paper.

Easy, but very annoying. Spent about 20 minutes each class unnecessarily sharing his political opinions. He subscribed us to his son's newsletter without asking us for permission. Attendance is a big part of the grade, and attending his class was unbearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Rudow is great and really funny! He didn't assign any homework which was amazing and we only had two tests, the Midterm and the Final and both were take home open book exams.

Dr Rudow is great. Class discussions are engaging & helpful in understanding concepts.  Exams are take home, for someone who suffers from exam anxiety, extremely grateful! I learned a lot minus the anxiety that surrounds exams. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!
Had him for HR (MPS IO Psychology).  Fantastic teacher... very, very down-to-earth and fair grader.  Hands down the best teacher I've ever had

No papers, no assignments, no quizzes. Just two take-home tests (midterm & final). Rambles on and on in class, but you should have a computer to waste time on while he does so. Easiest A at the campus. Also, buy the e-book for his classes if available. Makes it easier to find the answers for the tests. Attendance is mandatory though, get the points

Literally the most boring class I have ever taken. I took it during the summer and it was a struggle to come to class and sit and listen to him ramble for 3 hours. I learned nothing that I didn't know already. However, he gives take home exams and he is easy. DO NOT recommend.
Super easy professor. Final grade was based off 3 exams (that you take home!) and 14 quizzes (that you do online and have unlimited chances to make it 100%). Would recommend!!!
BEST professor everrr. His test are take home, and he argues the answers when you "turn them in," which means you hand your test to your friend and they grade it. He's so chill and funny. LOVE HIM!
Easy professor. All tests are take homes and you grade them in class..you can argue for you answers! He is boring but you get an A!

Dr. Eisenmann is a great professor. Although his lectures can get a little boring and it can be hard to pay attention, he still presents the material well. He is pretty approachable and also gives learning objectives unlike some of his colleagues in the biology department. If he is teaching genetics or biochem, take it with him!

He did a great job for a hard class like biochem. He's very clear when he teaches and has such a great personaity. he's always helpful to students and he curves the class real good. 55%-70=C, 71%-84%=B, 85-100=A. Reading quizzes and homeworks(online) = 15%, in-class poll questions=15%, exams(5 exams 1 drop)=70%. If he teaches biochem take him!

His lectures are def tough so are his exams so be prepared to study. However he is lenient when it comes to curves and grading. He def has a lot of generosity and unnecessarily curved just to be generous

Reposted w/ correct class code. Great professor, difficult content. Take notes before class, pay attention at lecture, stay on top of studying. Exams are hard (avg mid 60s, my avg was 98), follow the objectives. You can drop the final, course curve 85%+ = A. You will learn so much if you put effort in! I recommend BIOL430 for any premeds.

dr. eisenmann is an amazing professor! im just a bad student lol! i think its just the class content thats hard but he provides everything you need to know in lectures in a very easy way and his lecture style is very engaging! the exams also reflect the content accurately, which is nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Love Dr. E such an amazing person/professor! Lectures were entertaining/informative, giving you everything needed to understand and do well. I recommend reading the textbook, but it's not required. Go to class, take notes, engage with the content, and do all the work on time, and Dr. E will ensure you understand everything. This class was the best!

Out of all the Biology proffessors I have taken, Dr.Eisenmann is the best one. In the beginning of classes, We generally take ICQ's based on previous class lectures. That is an easy way to get point toward your grade as they are 15% of your grade. If you attend the lectures and actually put an effort into learning the material, it is easy to pass.
Really good professor and an amazing lecturer!!

2nd half of course is harder than 1st (had Dr. Lu). Dr. E is funny and good at lecturing, but you must take notes BEFORE and study hard for exams. He said exam 3 was the hardest, but I got 100% lol, however exam 4 was difficult. Serious weed out class, course exam average was 63%. Some extra credit and final curve applied at end (~87%+ is an A).

he is a strong lecturer but only taught half semester. dr.e does clickers at beginning of next class and emphasizes studying his underlines notes on lecture. exams are 50% of the grade (5 total, lowest dropped), 20% discussion, 15% clicker, 15% homework.
Great professor, he teaches and explains things very well. Always is open about receiving questions and will thoroughly explain everything. If you read and do the work youll do well
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's way too clicker happy and will spend upwards of 40 minutes just grilling us on obscure facts. Him and Lu also would talk during our exams on the mic and giggle with each other which is very distracting and annoying. Not the worst prof here by any means, him and Lu are actually the best ones at umbc. Not sympathetic to technological issues

Good professor, just a lot of material. Exams are tough, understand material well. You can skip finals with a good grade and pretty good curve at the end of semester. Just prepare to understand details because exams are more application wise.

BIOL 302 is a hard class with hard exams. Luckily, Dr. Eisenmann is a great lecturer and helps great with understanding genetic concepts. He is very approachable for questions. My only gripe with this class is graded clicker questions. The anxiety of that was traumatic.

Eisenmann expects a big-time commitment with the pre-class videos which are basically the only traditional lecture we received during the online class. The test averages were very low but there was a significant end-of-semester curve and he dropped an exam. Overall I think he knows what he's talking about but felt very disorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Horrible, is the simplest way to put it. Took this course during spring semester of 2021 and was not satisfied at all. His "discussions" were not used as time for students to discuss material. Instead they were mandatory quizzes each week. Literally no empathy whatsoever for students. Avoid at all costs definitely not a good professor online.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: AVOID HIM AT ALL COST!!!

Student teacher interaction is awful. Professor Eisenmann doesn't listen to his students or make any effort to communicate effectively. Has ignored every legitimate concern brought to him. Mastering bio doesn't allow multiple attempts or instant grading. Average exam scores are D's. Constantly makes mistakes and fixes them by reducing student score

Dr. Eisenmann quizzes on lecture videos that are more than an hour long, which you are supposed to watch BEFORE lecture. His quizes and exam are extremely memory based, so if you are more of a full picture thinker you will struggle. Multiple students have given feedback, asked for changes in any degree in the class and he has not been receptive.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Eisenmann is a tough grader. His exams are hard. Actually, this class is hard in general, but Dr. Eisenmann's lecture videos are informative. He explains things well and he clearly knows what he's talking about. Exams are now in LockDown browser because of the people who cheated on the first two exams.

Chose inspirational because he inspired me to change my bio major to something else. Don't take him. Honestly, just avoid this whole school if you can bc there's a lot of bad professors like him here. If you take him, expect to be laughed at when you're down, for your emails to be ignored and for your privacy to be invaded via lockdown browser.

Wait till the summer to take this class with another professor. Practice exams are NOTHING like the actual exam. Have to use lockdown with webcam. Discussion doesn't teach you much of anything, it's just another way for him to give you another quiz, besides ICA he gives during lecture every week. My mental health is low, and my grade is lower.

I struggle with this class. I'm coming here after taking exam 2 so things may change. But currently, I don't like the structure of exams. It did not reflect the practice exams. They are so long and dense with info. And sometimes the answer choices are very similar, you have to know the specific details. Plus, hw and ICAs are one attempt. This sucks

Dr. Eisenmann is a wonderful professor. His lecture slides are very thorough and he only tests on things from lectures and discussions. Discussions are easy if you prepare for them. There are 7 exams but only 6 of them are used in the final grade calculation. Studying is necessary but can definitely get an A on the exams if you prepare.

The tests are difficult, but he said he does an overall curve at the end of the semester (previous years, 85 curved to an A). Make sure you read the textbook and pay attention to lectures. Also it's important to read through the powerpoints for discussion if you want to get a good quiz grade (so far gotten all As on discussion quizzes)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very smart professor, however: 1. His class is set up to where your grade is made up of in-class quizzes, exams, and horrible discussion quizzes. 2. The exams problems are way too long to read, and some have an insane number of answer options. 3. When we make a suggestion, he shuts us down.
Tests are unclear and, the practice exams are NOTHING like the actual exams. The exams ask things that aren't in the lectures. Please do yourself a favor and take another class.

His exams are the worst. You have 28-29 questions that are nothing like the lecture slides. Seriously, one answer choice had 12+ options. Can't learn from hw cuz it won't explain why you got it wrong. Discussion is crack. Your basically quizzed on everything with no room for error. I will just simply pass away.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Just took the most recent exam, and I'm honestly losing hope in this class. The practice exams and clickers are NOTHING like the exams. No learning objectives except to practically inhale all of his slides but then on the exam you realize the slides were useless because reading through his exam will take half the time. Discussion is the worst.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Boring lecturer but after going to SI Pass and understanding each of his powerpoints, I was able to do well on his tests. HIs exams are application heavy but I could tell with each test he made it more fair to raise the test average. He did a big curve at the end of this semester so I can tell he tries to make sure students learn but also not fail

Dr. E is a great lecturer. He makes things as clear as possible and makes sure that everyone is successful in his class if they put the effort. He is a true gentleman, very approachable, and caring. I do recommend taking his classes.

Eisenmann is an incredible lecturer! I felt this class was incredibly easy and could grasp onto every word he said. His exams tend to be harder since they are more application based rather than memorization, but they're very doable. Take him for Genetics and you will love the class!

He does a really great job explaining concepts that may be hard to grasp. I think he does a really great job keeping the class engaged. There is a ton of material to cover so you need to go to lecture. He can also be pretty funny and has a more laid back attitude.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very engaging, able to keep your attention during lectures, though I sometimes found the slides hard to follow. There is A LOT of information to cover but he does a decent job at getting it across, plus he makes the slides accessible to look back on, along with extra articles and videos to look at for extra help.

Dr. E was a great prof but he doesn't really care and his attitude makes him unapproachable but outside of lecture he is a GREAT GUY. This class is very difficult but its not as bad as team based in the fall. Take it in the spring with Dr. E and be prepared to read the textbook all the time. The curve is pretty generous.

I took the class with Dr. B and E. The class is very difficult. The first few weeks may be review, but after that there are a lot of small details. He speaks very fast and does not post the slides in full online. I just listened to his lectures again because he spoke so fast. I pretty much barely got an A with the curve(I got lucky).

He goes by the lecture too fast. Doesn't put up all the slides. Try to find old exams. He reuses questions a lot, he even reuses questions from other teachers. After a while I stopped taking notes in class because he was going to fast. HATE THE TEXTBOOK! It confuses you more than helps you. Try do well on the four exams bc the final is harder

Let me start by saying you can tell dude man is smart and knows his area well. But as a student starting that class I don't. 302 is hard enough already without him flying through lectures and leaving his PowerPoint slides blank so you constantly have to look and see if you have to snap a picture or not. Not gonna say avoid him but hes not easy
Super HOT!!!!  Amazing professor, fun lectures, exams are a bit tough but oh well I got A overall because of 7% curve! I would really love to take his other classes.
I just love him, he's sooooooooooooooo hot!!

Okay, he's awfully pretty to look at and lacks any awkwardness at all. But Bieberich was actually more responsive to communications. He lectures well, is engaging, has slides and audio available which I really appreciate in any class for study. Tests multiple choice, but the challenging variety.

Never opened my book--just go through his lectures and the audio after class and you should have no problem getting an A in the course. All his exams are straight out of the powerpoint. He does a great job explaining it clearly. He's one of the best professors I've had. The last exam was quite difficult, but other than that it's not too bad.

Literally fell asleep in every single class. If you can learn from people just reading powerpoints, Eisenmann is your guy. Discussions aren't awful. Exams are a b%tch if you aren't an expert at the concepts. Some powerpoints are omitted when posted onto blackboard. Do your best on the HW and come to class. SI sessions are hit/miss in effectiveness.

Just print out the lecture slides and go through his lecture audio. Class is a breeze. Exams are either you know it or you don't type of affair; straight from class slides. Great Professor with more than a generous curve. Although Discussion was a bit hard.

I dont understand why people hype him. He literally just reads straight from his powerpoints. His exams are fair, some tricky questions - study hard to avoid accumulative final. Used textbook a lot. DEF review old exams. Very generous curve. Gotta give it to him though... has great hair. I thought he wasnt approachable, said unnecessary comments.

The best you can have. He's very helpful and clear. Exams are extremely easy if you pay attention to lectures and review them. Tells stories instead of lecturing and very engaging. Awesome hair and voice. He's just the best.

He made me love genetics.  He's enthusiastic, an awesome teacher, and has great hair (seriously I love his hair). You don't need the textbook except to do optional practice problems, I got along fine with Google and an outdated text from high school. Study hard, re-listen to audio of his lectures, ask questions. Tests are tricky but not impossible.

He's a fantastic professor. So clear. He explicitly states that everything that will be on the exam was covered in lecture, and he is telling the truth. The exams are so fair. Like the average grade on his exams are a 70! That's when you know you have a great proessor.
He is sooo helpful! So much better than miller, wagner, sokolove etc. He is also really good looking lol

Great professor, definitely passionate about what he does. Very fair, drops the lowest test and curves like a mad man; don't get ahead of yourself though, this class is incredibly difficult. There's a lot of material to remember. He goes through lectures very quickly, but his lectures are interesting and informative.

Flies through his lectures like he's the Flash. Bring a laptop to take notes or listen to lecture audio. Don't waste your time trying to write notes/printing out lecture slides. Exams are really hard. Drops your lowest exam, but get all the points you can. Study discussion material, it is on the exams. Have fun... not.

Dr. Eisenmann is one of the best biology professors I've had so far at UMBC. If you have any questions he's extremely helpful and very good with explaining topics that are sometimes hard to get your head around. This course isn't very easy though, you do have to put in some work. :) Amazing professor, highly recommend!

Overall, I really enjoyed Biol 302. Dr. E is awesome. His lectures are clear for the most part and he usually throws in a laugh or two during class. Get all clicker questions, attend all discussion sections, and don't miss any online assignments! It will either make you or break you and they actually help! I got a B in his class if it helps any.
Great professor for this class! Highly recommended. Very helpful and clear on subject material.
very good teacher...one of the best bio teacher and he is very clear and explains the materials very well...
he is such an excellent proffessor, very clear, knows what he says, and OMG he is such a hottie. i seriously drool over him every class. but seriously getting back on topic, i highly recommend him!

I'm about to graduate, and Eisenmann is probably the best teacher I've had here. Very organized, articulate and knowledgeable. People in that class asked some pretty dumb questions, and he was always calm and helpful. Not bad looking either. He gave out practice exams that really helped on the actual exams.

the class wasnt too hard, at least his tests reflected the material he taught. was able to pull off an A w/o the curve just reading the book and going over the power points a few nights before the exams. i found that i stayed awake for eisenmann's lectures more often than lindahl's.

The class is difficult, yes, but he is better than his counterparts.  His exams are a little easier than Lindahl, and he makes class interesting.  Very little use of the book, but it's still helpful.  Very easy to understand and very helpful

One of the better bio professors at UMBC. Gives coherent (but speedy) explanations in class using figures from the book which are later posted online. No lecture transcripts available, so you need to take your own notes. The tests are hard, but not impossible. He covers everything tested in class, but too fast to understand without extra reading.
Avoid this class at all costs. Exams are impossible. You have to memorize his EVERY word AND the textbook. Doesn't answer questions clearly and makes you even more confused.

He rocks. He is awesome to listen to, easy to understand, and very helpful when you ask him questions. Be prepared though; the tests are much more difficult than you would expect, with a pretty low class averages. I will take any class ever taught by him. Certainly do take him if you get the chance!
hes pretty much the man. clear, to the point, asks only stuff hes covered in class on tests- just awesome

He is a good teacher who writes out notes in outline format and puts up powerpoints, but his exams are impossible. You must go to class regularly to pass this class. He didnt seem very approachable, although I didnt try to at all during the semester. Much better alternative to Blumberg

Exams are hard....but it's because UMBC professors are using "medical school" format exams.   You have to take really good notes (word for word) and read the book AND somehow memorize the figures of his outline to achieve a good score on this exams.   Overall not a bad professor.

I had Dr. Eisenmann for developmental bio a few years okay. Sure, a decent teacher but overrated in my opinion-- it may have something to do with the fact that all the girls in the lecture thought he was cute. Developmental is one of those subjects that you end up teaching yourself (at least in my experience) and Eisenmann was an average prof.
Best biology teacher there imo.  Great lectures, fair tests, very clear.  Notes available online before each lecture, complete with pictures.  Very organized and very intellegent.
Eisenmann is HOT! and his exam questions are easier than Bieberich's
No Comments
Super clear lectures and is willing to engage with students during them! The homework and clickers can be difficult but the tests are pretty clearly based on lecture material.

Eisenmann is definitely an expert in his field. He is very knowledgeable in his lectures so definitely pay attention. Genetics is not an easy class but he tries his best to help you. The clickers are the KEY to his exams. Very understanding and empathetic with his students.

One of the best professors in UMBC! Knows the subject very well, answers questions clearly, helpful and welcoming during office hours. Exams are fair nothing tricky. CPS questions and the questions from the back of the book Dr. Eisenmann suggests at the beginning of each lecture very helpful for exams! Go to class, understand cps questions study!
Excellent Professor! Really known his stuff and wants everyone to do well. Goes a little fast buts posts lectures on Itunes. Would definitely take him again

Great professor. Excellent, detailed slides, relevant cps questions (very similar to exam questions). Very good speaker and answers questions precisely (not like certain other professors also teaching 302 who never answer the darn question).
No Comments
He goes over stuff really fast in class. So be sure to go to class, otherwise you will do bad. Don't buy the book...you don't use it very often.
Nice teacher, brings insight from outside experiences to class, reviews tests and cares about his students.
Great Teacher. Best at UMBC. come to class pay attention and do your part and get an A.Very helpful teacher. One of a Kind
Very easily teacher. very easy class, always willing to change the class aroudn to accomdate to the student as long as they show up to class

Easy class. Good Professor! A day before the exam he will go over what will be on it. If you study from that you'll be fine. Learn a lot from this class. WOrk load: 4-5 exams (easy), 1 project, 1 oral presentation. Very good Professor.
Yeah I already knew some accounting coming in and he had no idea what he's talking about. Read the book and you'll be fine. Nice guy, just doesnt prepare at all for class lol.

Read the book, you'll need it for this class. People say this is easy class, if might if you actually do the work and read the text. It's not easy as it looks, as half of our class drop. Anyway, great professor.

The class is very easy. Just show up, listen to him go over the slides, and then leave.  Even though he moves at a very fast pace (a chapter a class), it's very basic and general.  If you have basic accounting knowledge, you'll be fine.  Ask for take-home tests and open-note tests, he'll more than likely will give it to you.

This is one of the most ridiculously easy classes I have ever had!  The teacher is a nice guy, but he doesn't teach anything.  I don't think he does any preparation work for the class at all (I don't think he has even read the book).  He makes up for this by giving open note exams, which, again, makes this class a total joke.
Professor Khan is so kind and caring. She gives valuable feedback and the class is pretty easy as long as you do the work and participate! Love her, I wish I could have all my classes taught by her.

Professor Ellia is new, she has a lot of good traits, she was slowly settling in to a consistent teaching style.The textbook is informative. Attendance is mandatory no matter what she says! The group project was poorly organized. The lectures are informative, but don't go if you are not engaged because she will call you out. in-class notes only
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Ellia is great. I learned a lot; her work experience provided great examples and insight! The few shortcomings I noticed that became an issue for others: fluctuating lecture style, mandatory attendance; in-class activities that cannot be made up (big chunk of your grade), NO study guides for exams, no extensions (better luck in-person)

Professor Hernandez was very caring. There is a lot of homework, but if you do them little by little over time it becomes more manageable. She is very understanding that most students haven't taken Spanish in a long time. She is very kind and helpful, she tells you exactly what will be on written/oral exams so you can prepare. Def take her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There are assignments every class. You can access them online, but she will not accept submissions unless you were in class. I already speak spanish, but this class is not really beginner friendly. Since day one, she was adding spanish into her vocab. A classmate of mine struggled a lot and decided to drop out. Way too many assignments tbh.

Huge workload and many quizzes. Quizzes are in person, and mostly fill in the blank with zero partial credit. However the amount of other busy work you are graded on means you can basically fail all the quizzes and get a B if you do all the other work. But this class was def tedious. She does call on people randomly and we did get a pop quiz once
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: horrible horrible teacher she does not answers emails or messages and gives missing assignments in your grade book even thought they are turned in.

Check blackboard religiously. There are a lot of assignments that are hard to keep track of. You'll have weekly homework in the chapter folder, there are two projects that you have to do something for weekly, and there's this thing called "Quest" that you will absolutely forget about until the day it's due (or after if you're me)

took her at loyola. I rlly dont like learning languages. however, she was a very pleasant teacher. class wasnt bad at all. class is easy to follow and prepares you well for tests/quizzes. decent amount of hw but you online resources speed it up.  nice lady and good teacher. learned a lot actually. never thought id positively review a spanish class

honestly went into her class expecting the absolute worst last Spanish class i took was in 10th grade during covid so i was barely present but let me tell u, if u attend class, do all ur home work projects and quests on time  (they are all online) heck u can even get cs on all ur quizzes and u can get an F on the final and  still pass with a high B

Hernandez is a good choice for Span 201. Even after 3 years without Spanish, I was able to pass 201. She makes it clear what to study for quizzes/exams, & genuinely wants her students to get their foreign lang credit. Span 201 course is heavy in general, so you honestly need to put in the work and participate. I'd recommend Hernandez for Span 201.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Mary Ely is a pretty good professor but I would recommend that you take Spanish 101 before 201 because a lot of the material was not taught to me on the HS level and she expects you to know it already. She can get frustrated with the class when they aren't understanding and isn't the nicest about it. 4-7 HW assignments every week, but few quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lots and lots of homework, so be ready for that. Overall, she's a good professor and is clear about what will be on exams and the oral assessment. If you stay on top of the due dates and study vocab, you'll be fine but it is definitely NOT an easy A. She might also randomly call on you.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Just a horrible teacher who moves wayyyy too fast and gives a crap ton of bs connect assignments as if her class is as important as a STEM class.

I recently had to repeat Spanish 201 because I failed last semester, I took Katherine Solano last semester and decided to take Professor Hernandez this semester. When comparing the two I found Professor Hernandez to be more easygoing to her students and more lenient when comes to grading.

Lot's of homework but that's mostly the department's doing. Participate in her class, show up, and try your best and she'll be your favorite professor. If she knows you, then you'll do great in her class, but if you skip constantly then you won't get any slack from her.

Honestly, I dont like her. She seems to have favorites and i think influences her grading on some papers. There is alot of writing, and all exams were taken paper/pencil. She gives you a "study guide" a day before the exam! Non-resposive to emails. But, she is willing to open up assignments if you missed it. Get ready to get randomly called on!

Things started out okay. Seemed nice, but disorganized. Due dates not clear, nor were homework assignments or projects discussed much in class.  Lots of online homework with various due dates. Main issue was lack of communication/no or long email response times. She was very confrontational when I had an issue with the syllabus/course organization.

Professor Hernandez really cares about her students. She does a good job at engaging the classroom, and is passionate about teaching. She is a fair grader, and is willing to go over and explain things when you don't understand. I looked forward to going to her class every week.

We always got called on randomly which I hated. Profe would not be very good at explaining and she would not give clear examples; she would use other conjugations in her examples. I feel like we moved so fast. Let me tell you we always had Connect homework (the online textbook). Group quizzes were nice. She was kind.

I love Mary Ely Hernandez. She's a truly a gem of a professor, and really does care about her students. I surprised myself, and ended up really enjoyed learning Spanish with her when I took it over the summer

Definitely use her class as a way of practicing your Spanish because she will help guide you all the way, and answer all of your questions.

Class is fairly easy if you put in the effort. Felt like she assigned a lot in the beginning of the course, but as the semester flew by, it was pretty easy to adjust and the course load was decreased a lot. Doing homework is important for grade and attendance is mandatory. We had to do two oral exams, one midterm, one final, and one group project.

Awesome professor. She is caring and wants all of her students to succeed; she gives everyone the resources and opportunities they need to do well. Power points are extremely helpful for studying. She gives clear instructions on all exams and quizzes. Responds very quickly. If you study and put in the effort, you'll get a good grade. No complaints.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I would advise everyone who needs to take an language course with her to take it over the summer/winter. Good professor, tries hard to help students understand the material. Easy tests/quizzes if you study. Take notes and read the textbook. Do your part, submit your work on time and you'll pass. Attendance and participation is really important

She is very nice and down-to-earth with a relaxed but very involved way of teaching. Participation is your ticket to success with class exercises. There is a good amount of homework weekly, but most are simple with the very occasional writing assignment. As long as you actually do the work, you will get an A. She is very helpful with her feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She can be kind in the beginning but becomes more brash over time, especially when students aren't understanding concepts. The number of due dates were horrid and random by the week: Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday, Sunday. Sometimes all 4 in the same week. 9am due dates for some homework and then 11:59pm for others. Speaking grading isnt always clear.

For a class that is only taken by the majority of students for the requirement, this prof grades pretty harsh. Not consistent with grading and will call on you out of nowhere so be ready in class. She invites questions but only in the chat where it's hard to get your thoughts across, especially in a foreign language course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Its difficult due to a language barrier and comparing english to spanish. If you send an email sometimes she wont respond until 2 days after it. Which is difficult due to if you have a question on an assignment.

This was an okay class. Only took it to finish out a Language requirement. Her classes are a bit annoying. Only had it once a week but still assignments are due throughout the week. Unlimited attempts on online submitting. Quizzes i didn't like due to proctoring. Only annoying part was her saying "chicos" 24/7 every statement.

Prof Hernandez cares about her students, and does her best to ensure that students are actually understanding the language rather than simply memorizing it. Participation is very important as that's a large part of the way she teaches. However, being in her class was not intimidating because she is very understanding and clarifies mistakes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is a really nice caring teacher. If you are worried about Spanish 201 I would definitely recommend taking it with her. Even though it is tough she wont let you fail if you try. Go to office hours and ask questions. She wants you to pass. Very organized and on top of things. Goes above and beyond to help students.

Thanks to her, SPAN 201 was my favorite class during my first semester of freshman year. She's so sweet and thoroughly explains something when a student is confused. Also, she speaks a good balance of Spanish and English. Online homework assignments aren't bad if you pay attention during lecture and study the vocabulary in the textbook.

Mary Ely is so sweet and cares so much about her students. Participation is important, but she fosters a forgiving classroom. She's very encouraging and super helpful, and while there's homework at least a couple times a week, as long as you actually try, you can't fail. She's the best Spanish teacher here and she actually wants you to learn.

She is honestly one of the best professors here, cares a lot about her students and is always open to help. There's a fair amount of work, but she is very reasonable about what she assigns. As a person she is very active and personable, and makes coming to class a pleasure. There are a lot of options for 201 professors, make sure you choose her.

Instead of participating by raising hands, she will call on a random person meaning you can get called on 0 times or 10 times in a class, and if she doesn't call on you, she will give you a poor participation score. What she says and what the rubric says don't match up a lot and if you don't understand something she will tell you to just study more
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Spanish class can be intimidating when you do not know the language well and if you do not participate she will not like that. She is a very strict grader and if you miss class she will not help you make up work. The online work is very tedious and is not helpful with the lectures she gives. On top of online work there are a lot of written work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is honestly an amazing teacher! I had her for SPAN101 and then a different teacher for SPAN102 and the differences in their teaching styles were insane. Prof Hernandez is very patient and understanding when it comes to questions. She is a big fan of class participation, which actually helps with her conversational style of teaching.

She is amazing with helping students understand Spanish. Very participation-oriented but she makes sure the discussion is fun and engaging. Assignments are completed online, and while they're a bit tedious they're not difficult. Exams can be tricky. Overall Prof Hernandez challenges her classes but makes sure they succeed if they try.

Elaine is an incredible professor. College is meant to push us to grow and she creates a warm space to learn and experiment with ideas. She won't force you to learn, that's your own responsibility and why you're in college, but if you put in the effort you'll become a more fully formed human:)
I took a class with her back in 2013 and I still remember how great of a professor she was for ENGL100 Composition. Definitely take her class if you get the chance!

Professor MacDougall is such a kind and lovely person. The course was an honors seminar, so it was discussion based and there were projects included but there were no exams. She is so understanding and so genuine, she made the course engaging. I would 100% recommend you take her class!

Elaine is my favorite professor ever. She is so caring and understanding towards students, and doesn't make her classes more difficult than they need to be. If you have the chance to take a class with Elaine, absolutely take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Not difficult class that helped students understand the course.
Elaine made English digestible.  Is very understanding which made English a breeze with her.  Take English with you if you can, as long as you do everything you will get an A.

Professor MacDougall may the only time in my life where I enjoyed an English class. She had us sign a contract that said if we turned all 5 essays in, participated in class and showed up every week, we would automatically get an A. She cares about her students and is very flexible with due dates. She values student inputs and opinions.

Professor MacDougall is great, she is a caring person and will make sure you succeed. As of Spring 2022, her FYS101 is labor based so as long as you do the work (which isn't even a lot to being with) then you will be fine in her class.

Took the FYS - Truth and Technology, and it was super chill and actually pretty fun! She was a really good professor and very understanding. The assignments we had were all easy and she wasn't too bad about deadlines either. Definitely the easiest A for me for the semester. If I was able to take english with I would've! She's an amazing prof!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: elaine is an absolute gem

One of the nicest professors I've had! She cares about her students and is understanding. The work is not difficult, with minimal homework, and for a writing intensive class, there was not too much work. The longest paper we had was two pages. I would highly recommend

I had Elaine MacDougall for ENGL 101 with my cohort of Sondheim Scholars. Such a gem, very fun and helpful. If you're a Sondheim then you're in for a treat, if not then you should definitely take her class!

The FYS was mainly discussion based, but there are a few short papers that essentially give your thoughts on in class discussions. Watched lots of movies and videos.
