Not a bad teacher, but he co-teaches with Tatareweicz, who grades extremely terribly and arbitrarily. This is a 100 level class. I have taken 300 and 400 level English classes and earned A's easily. I got a C on the 1st paper. That being said, Brown is a much better professor and grades much more fairly. Knows his stuff but is sometimes unprepared.

It's a pretty easy class and he's a nice guy but it can get boring sometimes. It wasn't bad for a writing intensive class. 4 essays and a few other SMALL assignments. There are a lot of long readings. You don't have to read every single one in depth but at least skim over them because essays are based on readings. No exams, final, or note-taking :)

Frustrating class- Assignments graded weeks/months after turned in, bribed w/candy & extra credit for this. Lots of LONG required readings posted on blackboard only, lots of printing. Lectures not prepared well. Lots of work in last few weeks because he kept pushing things back. Interesting subject though, just a LOT of work for a 100 level class!

Class material was interesting and Professor Brown definitely knows his stuff, but he's really unprepared.  There's a lot of down time in class while he's trying to figure out what he wants to say.  Tests are easy, but he takes FOREVER to grade things.

Awesome professor. Very interested in what he is teaching. The essays are easy and not too long. Offers several chances for extra credit. Very committed to making his students better writers. The class is interesting. It made me think a lot about how science is done.
SO easy an easy A. Just do your short 3 pg papers well.

History of Science Since 1700. Allows you to take exam within a 48 hour period. Not too tough of a grader on exams, you don't really need to come to class if you read, but never gives work back. EVER. Never graded our final paper (which was worth 60% of the grade). Avoid if you can.

Easy prof, is his last semester teaching at UMBC (Spring 2025), gave us all A's on quizzes bc of course evaluations, Was easy and fair when it comes to grading. However, he is strict with electronics, found this bit frustrating.

I DO NOTTT reccomend him if your looking to take an easy GEP.

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

Quite literally the best teacher I've ever had at any university. Succinct about expectations and thorough in feedback. Provides extensive notes on lectures. A professor who seems to actually want students to benefit from the course. Encourages/seems to enjoy open-minded discussion in class. Lectures are intelligently humorous and engaging. 17/10.

Dr. Campbell delivers clear lectures and provides notes online so you can pay closer attention to what he is saying in class rather than having to worry about taking extensive notes. If at any point you find something to be unclear, he is there to answer questions. His lectures and reading assignments are engaging and he gives helpful feedback.

Professor Campbell is definitely one of the best professors I've hat at UMBC. Your grade in this class comes only from papers (8 pages max)  and class participation (10%) so you should definitely go to class. Took in winter 2025. Easy class

I enjoyed being in his class so much that it did not even feel like schoolwork. He is available to help and simplifies the class for you to enjoy. His projects are reasonable and will help in improving your knowledge.

Professor Stokan was an amazing professor. very good teacher.

AND his lectures DO correspond with the exam? you just need to read the book and listen to what he says obviously correlating with the book. Nice guy he's my academic advisor approachable to me

BIGGEST ****. don't take it with him, find another class with a different professor if you absolutely have to. It's all common sense but he makes everything much  more difficult than it really is. heartless and shows no remorse for any situation, even if you're practically dying.
The class is made harder than it should be; it's very important to read the book.

Pretty average teacher. Exams are a bit hard though, you will need to study. Never any homework except to read. I usually waited till a few days before the Exam to read everything i was supposed to and still did fine. Very friendly guy.

dogwater professor, in order to get a good grade you need to come to every single class which shouldnt even matter for some easy A credit class. made way harder than it needed to be. nobody cares about archaelogy

I did not get a lot out of this class. It was just tedious and very memorization heavy for the quizzes.
Loved taking this professors course. She is being hated on way to hard by these people. Its a hard class, but that's what college is dummies. Would take again I had fun :3

reviews.comment: Do not take her class. She makes the lectures super boring and the way she conducts herself makes it clear that she does not want to be there. Does not respond to student's concerns or emails.

Her lectures felt like it was put together very last minute and she doesn't seem enthusiastic when giving lectures. It was made unnecessarily difficult despite it being also meant for non-majors. She did not stick to the dates in the syllabus, does not respond to her emails and takes forever to grade. Worst professor I've had in four years at UMBC

This class is so boring. She gives study guides, but a lot of times the material on the guide doesn't match up with the content of the test. If you can take something else I would suggest it unless you are very interested in rocks and past civilizations.

I had her online for ARCH 120 and ARCH 350. If you aren't sure you are interested in archaeology PLEASE take her course. She is very passionate about what she teaches and tells you all about her own experiences as well as the course material. If ARCH 350 Museum Studies pops up to take again do NOT walk RUN to register, it is so inspiring.

Easy A, 3 Exams, the lowest one is dropped, a few quizzes, the lowest quiz grade is dropped, and two homework. Attendance counts as a grade. A lot of extra credit opportunities, no need to purchase any books.

Esther Doyle Read is very chill. Yes, she does read mostly off the powerpoint slides, but it's a history course, so what do you expect? And since it's a history course, there are a lot of readings! So do your readings, (including study guides!) show up to class, try to participate, and turn in your stuff on time, and this should be an easy A.

reviews.comment: Super easy to get an A. Gives a ton of extra credits(In the exam and for the whole class). I mean what could be easier than just showing up to the class, not taking a single note and only listing to the lecture( more like listening to a story). Don't study anything until you get the study guide(You don't have to). Sticking to study guide  A.

Lecture subject matter is good, but she reads straight from pp and barely strays from it. Doesn't answer emails, but does answer questions in class. Class was not very challenging since everything on the test is on a study guide. Assigns a lot of reading, but you don't need it to get an A. Also, constantly lectures about plagiarism.

She is very rude about not responding to emails. She does not acknowledge you in class or apologize for not repsonding to any of 6-7 emails sent. Most unprofessioanl professor. She expects us to know as much as she does even though we are not acheologists. I would highly recomend not taking a class with her. It is supposed to be an easy A, but no.

There is no point going to class when she reads word from word the lecture slides and then she posts them. We are not kids.  Not professional when it comes to be organizing and on time with commitments.

She is a horrible professor. I emailed her a total of 10 times about things she was not clear about in class and did not receive ONE reply. Her quizzes and tests require too much memorization and she says not to take notes in class because she uploads the lecture slides yet those are not enough to comprehend the info.

The class was really easy to get an A on.  The class consists of three exams and lowest one is dropped. So it is wise to study for the first two exams and get it over with. There were six quizes of which two lowest were dropped. The class was very boring but was really easy to get an A. Attendance is mandatory.

I did not like taking this class with Hamilton. His lectures didn't make much sense. If you have background in Python, sure you're good. If you rely on his teaching to learn, you'll probably have difficulty. His exams aren't bad. He's just okay. He's very unhelpful during office hours.

Definitely attend the lectures, he does a great job explaining the topics. Do not procrastinate especially on the projects. Start learning python before you take the course because he moves pretty fast, and go to his office hours!

Class is all lectures hearing him geek out about the class content(highly recommend), covers concepts in the form of "how does this algorithm/proof operate, be able to write some psuedocode or result so you can show you understand". Very smart guy, good course.

Hamilton is both a thorough and fun lecturer (downside is he is confusing at times, and fast). The class is hard if you're not used to coding so if you're like me don't expect to get everything the first time. Projects and homework are hard. Do not procrastinate it is painful. Exams are straightforward if you know the content and he's very lenient
Great professor! Explains complex topics clearly and makes class engaging. Super helpful during office hours.
the goattttt
hes so helpful and explains stuff so well!
Such an amazing professor! All the people complaining are just lazy, and 201 is the easiest it'll get if you're a comp sci major.

You can tell Professor Hamilton truly loves teaching. Their passion for computer science makes lectures engaging and fun, even when the topic is like recursion. They're great at breaking down difficult material and making it feel manageable. Highly recommend their classes if you get the chance!
This is a good class. good prof
Without question this is the best comp sci professor at UMBC, its not an easy class, but its worth it
Pretty simple class for beginners
Not sure about these negative ratings, this is for sure who you want to take this class with
Go to lecture and your good.  no textbook needed
This is a very good prof. I took 201 with him a couple semesters ago and he was great. he needs to teach more upper level classes
Very good prof. I went in with little to no coding experience and he really helped
If you go to class, you should be fine. The practice exams are almost identical to the actual exams

For a CS Prof, he's decent. HE TYPES EXSTREAMLY FAST! You actually have to put effort into the class, it's not an easy class. Its frustrating when he'd go through previous exams and there'd be mistakes or he would run out of time or could say that the problem was extremely hard and why did he put it on the exam. Go to the lectures, or you'll fail.

The class was easy for the most part. I would recommend learning the basics of Python before starting to make the class even more easier to the point where you don't need to show up to any lecture. He does try to trick you on the exams sometimes so be careful about that. Overall, easy class.

He likes to go off on random tangents. His lectures are pretty dry, but 201 is so easy you don't need to go unless you want to relearn or have him go over the basics. I would say to go to his class right before the midterms as he gives you the answers for the multiple-choice section and tells you what you need to focus on.

His lectures and dry, confusing, and overall not helpful. He frequently goes on tangents about pop culture, such as spending large amounts of class time talking about Portal 2 or The Fifth Element. Luckily, CMSC201 is extremely easy, so you probably don't need to go to class to pass.

You either like him or you don't. He doesn't bore you with slides and does in-class programming almost 99% of the time. Projects are definitely more difficult than they should be for a introductory class but they are all doable. Tests are difficult-ish.
The man!!! Office hours he is very helpful. Projects are very clear and the rubric is put out for projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Entertaining and self deprecating. 202 is rough with anyone and your experience won't be too different between sections, but Hamilton kept class time engaging, at least compared to Dixon

Professor Hamilton is amazing! He's very committed to his students' success, explains difficult concepts well, accessible outside class, and genuinely cares about his students. Lectures can be fast-paced due to extensive material of the course itself. Consider taking 104 first, regardless of professor. Very underrated and deserves more recognition.

As someone who has both been taught by and worked for Professor Hamilton, I can say he is by far the best professor I've ever had. If you're willing to do the work with integrity, you'll have no trouble succeeding in this class. He genuinely cares about his students and he's very approachable in office hours.

Only enroll in Hamilton's 201 class if you have coding experience. His rapid pace requires extensive outside work. I secured an A with prior knowledge but still struggled on projects, but tests are easy if you practice with example tests. Beware: strict policy against code sharing; sharing results in class failure. I would avoid him if you can.

Great professor, just pay attention in lectures and practice what he teaches in class and go over his github slides. Exams are easy. Best to reach out to him via email with screenshots of your code and explain the issue you are having. 6 HW, 10 Labs and 3 Projects. Exams were pretty easy, simple concepts covered MCQs, debugging and 2 coding.
Mr. Hamilton is special, so it's no wonder he spends so much time talking about star wars instead of teaching us how to code. You have to self-teach yourself almost everything.

Good lectures that were easy to understand, textbook referenced but not required to read. He doesn't post any content online so it is definitely required to come to lecture, but he is funny and engaging so it never felt like a slog. All tests and homework graded leniently. As others have said, he is more of a math guy.
They are super nice, make all the assignments clear, and go over some processes with similar questions in class. Super easy class.

really accessible and helpful during office hours and responds to emails within 5 hours or less. he is truly a math dude and many of his examples are math-related. he does go sometimes a bit too fast but dw he posts his notes on Git Hub. attendance isn't mandatory but I suggest you come to class to hear the explanations.

idk wth was going on in his 201 class, but he does seem to be more of a math guy. For 441 I didn't really pay attention in class, but it was like discrete math so it was never too bad and for once in my CMSC life there were actually online sources for the stuff we were learning. the class was easy and the final was optional (for our class at least)

Eric literally bestieeee. Class was hard bc no prior experience. He is knowledgeable about Python, so his personal office hours were more helpful than TAs. Sometimes hes too fast/sidetracks during lectures, but he gave us exam extra credit + would give project hints. Get ready to invest a lot of time into the weekly HW (6) and projects (3)!

Eric's lectures are very useful and everything he demonstrates has a purpose. I can't speak for the 201 students, but I would say that he's a math guy, so 441 is probably his strong suit. Highly recommend.

Not a CS major, but I took this because it was a recommended class for me to know. I hadn't done a bit of python before this class and I felt like it was pretty easy. If you miss a lecture he has an entire semester of lectures from COVID up on his youtube channel which made the in-class lectures not as stressful. His lectures helped a lot. Spring22

reviews.comment: Prof Hamilton teaches the class by explaining and using whatever he taught in pyCharm w/ energy. I like the unusual information he would share while discussing coding. The worst aspect of his teaching method is that his hands move too quickly, making it difficult to keep up with him later in the semester, although he publishes his notes on GitHub.

Pretty nice professor. Heavy on lecturing with no materials posted online, so you need to go to class to get the information. Lectures are pretty clear though and if you take notes you can get through them. You can tell he's really passionate about computer science though and he'll sidetrack into more complicated stuff as he lectures.

I have never hated a professor more. I had 2 years of coding experience going into the class and still fell behind and was told it was my fault for not doing enough to catch up when I asked for help. He basically refused to clarify any questions I had on projects because 'all the info was in the rubric'

Coming into this class with hardly any solid programming experience was quite difficult at the beginning. Over time it got easier although the homework and projects got harder. The best tip I could give to a student prior to taking this course is to look over the lecture slides before class and to start the homework as soon as possible.

CMSC 201 is an intro to programming but he teaches as if you already know the basics. Hamilton is understanding when asking for extensions. Teaches and codes too fast, I couldn't keep up. As someone who has no coding experience, hws and projects were very difficult and one hw problem took me days to do even with the help of tutors and my TA.

Codes in class, but doesn't properly explain what the code means or why he's writing it. Even though the class is meant for people with no programming experience, there's no way anyone could learn without previous experience with his pacing and poor explanations.

It's like he's trying to put the whole class to sleep every lecture. Doesn't let students help each other or discuss how they solved a certain problem, considers it cheating. Had a book but would be unclear on due dates for assignments on it. Doesn't put the grades in Blackboard, you have to create a whole new account just to see exam grades.

This dude goes so damn fast you cannot even keep up. You know he is bad when everyone is staring at their screen confused in his lecture not even trying to take notes or even attempting to but the dude just goes way too fast. His homeworks and projects are obscene and its so called "beginner" programmer with "no" prior coding experience is terrible

Wonerfully funny and online-savvy guy, but this was the most disorganized and hard to learn class I've ever had. Super easy grader though!

He is a terrible professor who not only doesnt used the text book at all, but his lectures are really useless. His lectures are cringeworthy and are not worth going to. Dont take his class, please. Id rather go to a community college than learn from "Mr Hamilton". Btw, star trek sucks dork

Overall, Professor Hamilton's course on Intro to CompSci 1 was challenging, but rewarding. The assignments in this class are project-based, meaning you use the code you learn over time. If you have taken Comp sci in HS(or prior computer science courses), you should be fine, but if not this will be very hard for you. The Homework's take a while to do / typing, formatting and submitting and that's not including time spent thinking about it. His lectures are all over the place and goes off topic often. Most TAs are also really good.

I took this in fall 2020. The lectures are extremely disorganized, but somewhere within that mess, there's stuff you're gonna depend on for projects and hw. He does not care about the class and it shows. He spent no time writing projects; multiple times he had to rewrite the assignment or the solution to make sense, throwing off the entire schedule. Lectures are complete nonsense ramblings with no prep on his part. If you are on SDS; he is uncooperative about accommodations and will say it's unfair.
Hamilton is excellent. Really smart guy and delivers lectures in an entertaining way.

Eric Hamilton is a really great professor. His lectures were a lot of fun. Professor Hamilton was always very engaging. The lectures can get kind of math-heavy when he goes off on math tangents at the chalk board, but it's fun seeing him get into it. Quizzes and exams aren't too difficult if you follow along with all of the lectures.

Hamilton is just not it. His lectures have little-to-basically nothing to do with the homework and other assignments that he assigns; so there really is no point in going. The assignments are endless, so unless you have an incomprehensible amount of free time, good luck trying to finish on time. This is a weed-out class, but he just makes it hell.

reviews.comment: Unless you have endless time on your hands, this class might not be for you. the amount of time needed to complete the hw and projects is a lot. They aren't crazy difficult, but its basically just trial and error because you are trying to learn the concepts while having to code semi complex projects/homework.
Want even my teaches but he's the only reason I survived my class because my teacher was very incompetent. A cool dude who teaches quite well.

His entirely class structure during COVID college was intensely impersonal and a slog to get through. From youtube livestreams that werent good teaching/review tools, to projects that were always harder & more time consuming than he planned, to just having a condescending attitude throughout it all-- he made sure the class wasnt student friendly

Unusually mean and not very understanding of the online environment. He completely got rid of a lecture time because he didn't feel like repeating himself, so a lot of students couldn't ask questions during lectures and had to just watch a recording. When students would ask questions in class, he would read them outloud, pause and not even answer??

This class ruined by self esteem and my first semester at college. The professor was never available. The TA's had to teach. The TA's are abundant but your chance of getting one that is actually willing to help you is low. Try to get A's on the projects because they will be a big influence on your grade. And it's 100% not a beginner class.

Aside from late homeworks, exams, and slow grading, Prof. Hamilton made this class with several horror stories quite enjoyable imo. His lectures were super helpful as he mostly draws out the concepts and does live coding on those topics. He is super helpful with the projects especially early on, so don't sleep on the projects and ask too late.

CMSC201 for majors with Professor Hamilton was initially easy but became incredibly difficult, even with my prior coding experience. Hamilton handled this online semester poorly, making assignments more difficult than necessary (he acknowledged this himself) and was not helpful at all. He is smart and knows his stuff, but isn't a good professor.

Hamilton is a nice guy, but the class is god awful. During his lectures he goes off on random topics that have nothing to do with the lesson or the upcoming assignments. Tried to set a meeting up to talk about hws/etc but he never showed up. If you dont have background knowledge, dont even bother. TAs are nice but quite harsh and not specific.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 201 was beyond difficult; nowhere near considered an "introductory course." If you have no prior background in Python, you're going to be spending an immense amount of time and energy on the homeworks/assignments. Hamilton was "nice" and knows his stuff, but goes on random tangents about stuff that doesn't relate to anything. Not recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Hamilton is great 201, but fell apart in 341. He was always late on the release of homeworks and exams, always late on the grading of said assignments, one time changed a question on the midterm half way through us taking it, and doesn't read the project documentation before helping students thus breaking code. We felt neglected as a class.

Prof. Hamilton offers extension on projects and homework, is very accessible outside of class, gives extra credit on projects and likes to crack a joke or two in lectures and on assignments but he expects a lot for an intro course and made me question whether I wanted to continue CMSC. Hamilton knows his stuff, but I wouldn't recommend him to start

If you think you will, or currently struggle with entry level coding, try turtle programming on CodeHS. This level of coding is below what a college level class is, but will help w/ fundamentals. Prof E does a great job explaining concepts and makes it to where its not just some boring thing where you watch a dude type for an hour.

A lot of bad reviews that I don't think he deserves. This class is obviously a weed-out class. If you can't take the heat, don't be mad at prof E. His lectures are helpful and he is pretty accommodating regarding extensions and all. especially online. This class was probably the most difficult I've taken but I can give credit where it's due.

Eric Hamilton is one of the worst professors at UMBC I have ever taken. Not only are his lectures intensely concept/course heavy, but he does not explain them in a manner in which you as an introductory student, would understand. Unless you have prior background knowledge in Python, you are going to fail. He knows his stuff, but is not a good prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Eric is a math whiz, and that routinely shows up in his lectures. He's also funny and likes to crack nerdy jokes when teaching.

Hamilton made sure to keep the class interesting. The best thing to see in a professor is to see them actually caring about students really learning the material. He taught so that people understood, not so they would just do well on the exam. He super available outside of class, and I only went to him for help with code instead of TA office hours.

Since most people are signing up for classes soon, ill write a review. As the other reviews have said, the class is extremely difficult for an introductory class. I've never coded before and I find myself spending hours outside of class trying to understand. Hamilton knows his stuff, but as intro level students, he holds a very high standard.

If you're looking to get into Computer Science, do not start your journey with Hamilton. The class is homework heavy and assignments take between 20-25 hours a week to get a low B. It disappoints me to say that I was really looking forward to my major because of Python, however, it is just ruined for me.

Fantastic guy! Really likes to teach you things. Very easy grader, during one exam he literally helped people on the exam sheet. His lectures were very fun, and I enjoyed being in them. 10/10 would recommend
terrible with lectures. Acts like he actually cares, but in reality, he doesn't. gives the stupidest programs for he and bad exam questions. lots of grammatical errors in his problem sets.

I took comp201 with prior experience, and I would absolutely NOT recommend Mr. Hamilton to anyone who really wants to learn. His assignments forbid students from using the built in features of Python for no reason other than to increase the difficulty. If I hadn't worked as a developer before this class, I would have failed.

I had him for 201 in the Fall 2019. He had very specific slides which helped me better understand the material covered. His live coding does tend to go fast. But he was always happy to help during his office hours when it came to projects and exams. He helps guide you on the projects which is very helpful. Would definitely take him again!

Makes an intro class, which students with no prior programming knowledge should be able to take impossibly difficult. In class, he gives the most basic examples but in the homework & tests, expects you to solve difficult problems even those with programming experience struggle with. He is also cold and aloof when you approach him during office hour

Even before class went online due to Covid-19, his teaching was the most unprofessional, disorganized, and lazy I have EVER encountered in all my years of schooling. When asked about a course plan or help outside of class, he responded with "lol, I don't even know what I am going to be teaching when I walk into class!". Do not take with Hamilton!!!

I am so happy I took Eric for 341. Hes very knowledgeable on the subject and always kept the class interesting. He helped me and others a lot on projects for hours after office hours were supposed to end. He made difficult exams but graded them very leniently. He chose to make our final optional which took a lot of stress off of finals week.

Nice guy but I didnt learn anything from his lectures. UMBC claims you dont need programming experience to pass the class but even people with programming experience struggled the second half of the semester. I withdrew from the class because I was failing.

Professor Hamilton is a decent professor. He def knows the subject and cares about teaching. The class is a little disorganized with the grading but this is an irregular semester. I had no experience with coding before the semester and this class was pretty easy. Just play around with python and you'll do fine.

Hamilton knows his stuff and has been coding for a long time. However, homeworks and projects are way to hard for an introductory course and the expectations are way too high. Do not expect to receive many grades for this course even though you will have assignments weekly.

A lot of the bad reviews here are surprising. Erics lectures are easy to follow and well paced. He goes off on tangents sometimes but it keeps the class fun. I had no experience coding and found that if you just attend the lectures and start the work early, its an easy course. The biggest downside is grading is slow but its a giant class.

Eric Hamilton is by far the worst professor I've had at UMBC. Has a horrible attitude, and acts like he's doing you a favor answering your questions. He ignores emails, grades extremely tough, and takes months to grade assignments.. DO NOT take this class with Eric Hamilton unless you want to suffer for an entire semester. Horrible Prof/Person.

Bruh this professor is trash. He got a cocky attitude and he seem like he don't want to help you or something. He makes the projects and assignments way too hard. TAKES FOREVER TO GRADE. THAT OTHER REVIEW THAT SAYS he explained project 3 very carefully is a burner because proj3 was released 2 weeks after April 13, 2020. DONT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!!!!

He definitely knows his stuff and is helpful. However, he makes an intro class impossibly difficult, especially the homeworks . Grading is tough and strict as well. I think he is in charge of the material for this semester and I heard from those that took 201 previously said that this current semester's material seems way more difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you do not have people who you can study with or already know the material, be prepared to study individually. When asked for additional help, he uses the "I have other students to worry about" attitude. Takes several weeks to get back returned assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I retook the class with Hamilton and I found his lectures to be really engaging, he can get a little off topic, which I didn't mind, and actually found very interesting, but for first time learners of the material, it might be a little confusing. For proj3, he gave a very helpful walkthrough, when other profs will avoid talking about projs at all.

DO NOT TAKE HIS COURSE! He doesnt not go by syllabus at all for grading. He changes it mid-semester (50/50)to where youre screwed. You dont get feedback on turned in work like weeks after. He often cancels his office hours and ignores your help emails. One lecture he spent 45 minutes on a topic to then have realized he taught it wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Eric is a great guy, and banters with the class a lot which is very cool and funny. I had him for CMSC 201 and have him now for 203, and my advice would be that while he's a good teacher for 201, he's not great for 203. It may be because this is his first time teaching this class, but the structure is very messy. He's easy for 203, less for 201.
Hamilton is a really good guy, but just goes off on random tangents about math almost every 5 minutes. Hes a mathematician at heart, and it really shows.

Professor Hamilton was by far my favorite professor so far. He kept the lectures entertaining and overall was just very knowledgable. I felt that the Projects were a little on the tougher side, but regardless CMSC 201 was great.

He was poor. I did ASL 101 with him online, and he rarely responded to emails & waited until JAN 5TH to grade 25 assignments from weeks prior. He will ignore you during Zooms and doesn't seem to really care about students. I'm thinking about taking ASL at my local community college & transferring the credit instead of letting ASL drag down my GPA.

Do not take this professor if you want to be happy. He is SO condescending and has kicked someone from our zoom for yawning. He doesn't answer emails and grades everything within the last week of the semester. Group assignments are done each class- if your partner doesn't know what's happening, tough luck- he does NOT care and will call you out.

This professor does not respond to emails or questions via Zoom. I have repeatedly reached out to him, and he has not replied to a single thing. He only bothers responding to you if he thinks you aren't paying attention. The class is fairly easy. He does not grade anything until the last minute, though. I would not recommend him as a professor.

The single worst professor at UMBC. This man will ignore you the entire semester because he doesn't care about his students at all. Grading is completely arbitrary and most of the assignments weren't graded until after the last day of class. Do not take his class under any circumstances, it's crazy to me that this man still has a JOB.

For ASL 101 - Do NOT take this professor if you genuinely want to learn ASL. He does not respond to emails, very disrespectful towards students, instructions on assignments are very unclear, accuses you of using your phone of you're just zoning out, and kicks you from the mandatory Google meet classes without telling you.

This professor does not enter any grades until the day before grades are due to the university, you will never know how you are doing in the class the entire semester. He doesn't bother to respond to emails either, he's extremely unhelpful. The entire class you're paired up with a random person to practice signing you barely know, it's unhelpful

He only sometimes responds to emails, also didn't grade until the class was completed. Nice guy and I think his lectures are helpful in learning ASL but the structure of the class was lacking. His syllabus changed but he never posted the updated version so nobody knew due dates. He also forgot to post lots of stuff, so many students got confused.
Grading was too tough and there's lots of make up opportunities, interesting content
Interesting, fair and give extra credit for participating

reviews.comment: She will give extra points if you participate in class.

Toughest Professor for Ethics. The class was very challenging and interactive. Although the grading isn't very good plus their are lot of written assignments which makes this course more of a Theorotical. Again, its very difficult to achieve good grades in this subject. Professor has an amazing knowledge base and skillset. DON'T
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Craig is super nice and a excellent professor. She made the subject of inclusivity in education fun and super informative. I will definitely be a better teacher thanks to the lesson she taught.
Everything everyone is saying is true. She is an amazing teacher. She does everything in her power for you to learn and have fun. TAKE HER!
I LOVE HER AND THE CLASS! SHE MADE NIGHT CLASS WORTH GOING TO

I wish I had her for all my EDU classes. She is one of the more organized EDU teachers. She makes class fun with all sorts of activities. More than willing to help and always on task. Great personality too. Definitely recommend taking her class!
Amazing teacher! You will have such a good time in her class! I learned so much from her! I wish she would teach more education classes!!

Everything that the previous commentator said was true.Really sweet teacher. She is an elementary school teacher and it shows in the way she approaches group work and other activities that we had to do in class. Very easy course, always out early, highly recommended!

I loved this professor! She gives you all your points as long as you do your work. Always let us out of class early, since it was late at night. Very understanding and sweet. Made me interested in Special Ed.

By far one of my favorite professors at UMBC. He was very good at connecting the material we learned in class to real world scenarios, and is great at getting you interested in the material. Lectures are great, and they go by pretty fast. If you have the chance to take him, do it! :)

He is a great professor and the class can be easy. As long as you go to the SI sessions and pay attention in class you will easily pass this class. Make sure to take great notes too. You don't need the book at all.

Dr. Parker is a wonderful professor... definitely the best I've had at UMBC. He is interesting and a genuinely nice person. However, this does not mean his upper level courses are easy. Do all assigned readings and get ready to do ALOT of writing. GES 326 was one of the most eye opening and intriguing courses I've ever taken. Highly recommend!

Go to class, take notes, study those notes, then take the exam. Simple. Maybe it's hard for freshmen to get used to, but I wish more courses were just this simple. No need for the textbook because the exams are based on the lectures/notes.

Professor Parker is great! If you go to class, write down the notes and try to understand everything he's very easy.  He is willing to help you out as much as possible if you show an interest and actually try to learn.  Take his class if you get a chance.  Very interesting guy

Sandy is wonderful professor! He gives very in-depth notes and is very into the subject. He gives 3 exams, which are moderately difficult, but if you attend every class and take great notes, you'll be fine! Oh and don't even bother buying the book, you are assigned readings but they don't really help, it's just kind of an overview of the subject.
Really enjoyed the class, exams are based on notes only. highly enthusiastic. spent half of his life in Brazil. knows his stuff. very fun and easy going
Take good notes to do wellgood in the class. Exams are basically the grade. Prof. knows his stuff, very enthusiastic about it.
Great professor! Had him for environmental science, really knows his stuff. Only thing is he talks really fast and a lot of note-taking during class. Take good notes to get good grades on the exams!

Wonderful professor. The professor gives you a good base on which to start regarding the subject. When the professor arrived at the institution, one could sense how the animation department became more alive with more chances to talk to people in the industry.
Absolutely love Eva! I had her for Intro to Animation as well. She is amazing to work with, very understanding, and knows her stuff. I would recommend her to everyone!

I took Professor Grandoni's Intro to Animation class and she has been one of my favorite professors. She is extremely passionate about animation, creates a fun and lively environment in the classroom, and is always supportive of her students. She also has a lot of knowledge and gives clear and specific feedback that helps each student improve.

Took her for Intro to 2D Animation and she was such a great professor.  Constantly supportive of students and was understanding of any issues with meeting deadlines or completing assignments. Gave in-depth feedback through video format and was very helpful throughout the artistic process. Very passionate and brings humor to her lectures!
One of my favorite professors I've ever had, shows great enthusiasm, goes the extra mile for students, classes are fun and engaging. Can't recommend enough, wish more professors were like her!

Hands down the best professor I've ever had, took both her intro animation class ART341 & motion graphics ART447, and her positive classroom atmosphere and enthusiasm make learning animation an enjoyable experience. She helps her students through roadblocks and offers great feedback to create portfolio-ready pieces, you won't want to miss a class.

Really interesting class, focused on the cultural framework surrounding groundbreaking legal cases! Fairly easy A if you put effort into your writing. Ever is super flexible with deadlines and gives great feedback.
Prof. Hanna was great! This class was so easy, I wish that they taught more POLI classes. They were quite unorganized through material and grading but overall this class is an easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Hanna is a very kind and clearly competent professor who never fails to make their lectures engaging and fun. Professor Hanna clearly had a lot going on in their personal life, and was somewhat disorganized in terms of posting class materials or letting students know in advance if class was canceled, but overall great professor!

Prof. Hanna is the best out there! They have a lot of passion for their job and they always make sure to check on their students wellbeing (mental and physical). They are very understanding and they assign real life case readings and podcasts which will be discussed in class. Assignments are straight forward and easy if you pay great attention.
Very tough grader will note every single little mistake, the class is a writing-intensive class.
I do not suggest to take her at all if you want to be stressed out.

Definitely a challenging course. Felt like my first "college course". At first I was not a fan of Dr. Evans. It almost seemed like she took the class too seriously. But boy was I wrong. What an amazing class and teacher. I went from dreading the class to loving it. The papers are intense though and she grades pretty harshly, but she is the best!!!
Eve really made me feel secure about my major. She educated me and inspired me. I would highly recommend her.

Eve is the worst professor. Her lectures and assignment are never clear. She is very arrogant and picky. She thinks that she is the best and no one is better than her. She is a control freak and doesn't care about any of student. She is very bossy, her way or no another way. She doesn't smile. I don't recommend anyone takes her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Eve is among the best prof's I've ever had. She's to the point and isn't afraid to hit you where it hurts. But it's for such a good cause. I love her.

Eve is like the combination of Ellen Degeneres, Naom Chompsky, Maggie Smith, and a distracted and disoriented terrier dog rolled into one fantastic person. If you put in the work, she will do anything for you. If you are in THTR202, just read the damn plays. You'll be a better person for it.
EVE IS THE BEST

Eyal is a great teacher, both caring and knowledgeable, I couldn't possibly fit all my praise into 350 characters. He cares very much about his students and puts their needs before any due date or assignment. He assigned challenging readings but they never felt stressful. The discussions for ENGL 2599 were always interesting and thought-provoking.

Likely one of the more manageable ENWR classes at UVA. Eyal prioritized his students well-being over any specific class requirements, and I really appreciated that. I also have an entirely new perspective on social inequity in America
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The Spanish at UMBC is nearly impossible, so the grading distribution/amount of work is out of his hands. But he's probably the best professor for Spanish because he's extremely helpful and cares for his students. He understands how tough and demanding the course is. Come to class, ask him questions and he'll help! I would definitely recommend him
There is a lot of work but the Spanish department controls this. He is helpful explaining what you got wrong on the exam. Sometimes doing lecture he's unclear on the rule or confuses things.

Rude when talking to students. Never thinks she is wrong. Lectures are all ChatGPT, so are emails and announcements. Easily impressed. Doesn't know what she is teaching. Has no qualifications for this class. Won't put grades in if you question her grading. Grading doesn't make any sense. Expects everyone to participate in every class. Never on time

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. She has no clue what she is teaching. All her lectures are AI and her Final's are actually impossible to complete on time. She grades items at the last moment, some of which are time crucial as its feedback for future assignments.

Dr. Nibbs is by far one of the worst professors I have ever had at UMBC. I am a paramedic cohort senior member and have taken both EDHS 301 and EDHS 423 with her. I somehow earned a B in these pointless, repetitive and poorly designed courses. She cannot use blackboard, nor can she accept feedback. Every lesson and slideshow is chatted with CHATGPT

reviews.comment: AVOID, It is obvious that she has barely any understanding of the class, grades are almost random, after comparing grades with other students I do not believe she has ever read any submissions, and must grade using a crystal ball. She has been incredibly rude to students voicing concerns. The least professional teacher I have had ever by far.

Professor Nibbs is extremely vague with her directions and provides no clear due dates for anything. When asked for clarifying questions regarding exams or papers she is rude. She clearly has no understanding of how to teach and just reads straight from slides. Avoid taking her classes at all costs unless you are required to.

Extremely unhelpful when asked for clarification. The class was relatively easy but she made it so much more confusing and difficult than it had to be. Also the exams were absolutely ridiculous. I was excited for this class, but I wouldn't recommend it to anyone, even though it's online.
She makes the class more difficult than it needs to be and provides no type of insight into the material. Also, she is extremely vague when asked for clarification.

reviews.comment: Get ready to teach yourself everything. She's unclear about what we're supposed to do, and she deducts points almost randomly. However, if you simply read the texts, you'll manage to do okay.

reviews.comment: Great professor! Assignments were intentional and concise. Appreciated that the class texts used had an audio version available. I wish all PSYC classes were structured similarly.
I took professor Falligant's class a few semesters back. I wish I could take another course with him. Very funny during lecture, and the lectures are very interesting. He's not a hard grader either.
Extremely interesting lectures. I'm not a psychology major, but this is still one of the most fun classes I have ever taken. It's also pretty easy on the grading.

i loved her, she's very passionate about what she does & that inspired me. but i hated how many topics were in each section bc that jus made it even harder on the exams. her study guides only hold a portion of what will be on the test but i passed!

Farnsworth was a good teacher for GES 110. Your grade is determined by 3 exams and an optional final, plus some videos with easy quizzes. The exams are content-dense, but as long as you study, you should be good.

reviews.comment: She is alright and is very passionate about what she does but the chunk of your grade is purely based on how well you do on the exams, which can get kind of difficult because they are very dense at around 65-ish.

GES 110. Overall great professor. But her lecture slides tend to be about 30-45 slides. Very caring. The downside about her lectures is that her lectures can be very boring. But she really cares about her students, and she wants you to excel in her course. She is also very accessible outside of class.

Professor Yang's class was very interesting and captivating and I did love the class. she engages with many different materials and she uses so many sources to keep explaining her overall theme for the theorists. work-wise, there are reading journals to be done for each reading nearly, 3 papers, and a big final that does take a lot of time to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class was a TON of difficult readings but once you learned how to take notes on them it was more time consuming than hard. She was a great professor and made learning the materials fun. She was also very political and a lot of what we learned was very one sided and political.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof Yang's class is so simple: Do the readings with the guided questions that she provides Show up to class and participate. *The days she gives the reading quizzes are at random, but with the questions, she gives you it is so simple to pass! Just make sure you are taking good notes because you will need them for the two main papers she assigns.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The readings at the beginning of the class were super annoying, but once you get over those, Yang is a great professor to have for the senior seminar. She is great with making sure you are not overwhelmed and breaks everything down into small, manageable tasks. She really makes you delve into your topic too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Really insightful and leads great discussions. Definitely learned a lot in this class and feel more passionate about MCS as a result. Papers are graded fairly easily - she seems to just wants students to understand the material and grasp ideas taught in lectures and throughout readings. Very kind and understanding professor.

Professor Yang is amazing! She is a great lecturer who really wants her students to understand the material and be able to use the different theories in real life. There is A LOT of reading, but if you do that and make sure you do the reading journals, the class is easy.

Dr. Yang is one the best professors I've had at the university. Her syllabus, which details how she grades are very clear. She gives about 8-10 responses and drops the lowest two. Expect to do a mapping project, a reflective essay, a topic proposal and eventually a research paper. Loved learning about media and how it affects the global sphere.

Yang is a sweet lady but the class is a bit tough. She is a tough grader in that it's not easy to get an A on your papers. She gives about 8 little critical response quizzes on the readings, but thankfully drops 2 of the lowest graded ones. The readings are definitely boring and long, but skim the first couple of pages, and you get the jist of it.

Nice lady, but her perspective is SO obvious in this class. If you talk about how something is not "americanization," she hushes the thought. Boring readings and lots of them. Assignments are pretty straight-forward for the most part. Typical grader, not too tough and drops two of your lowest in-class writing grades.

Lectures and graded assignments are so oddly specific about one particular thing, like Nollywood or Korean Cinema. The class is basically, things are spread across the world and everything is turning into a multinational production, and yet, she makes it so hard to understand. The concept is simple. She makes it confusing for no reasonable purpose

I have had Dr. Yang for two classes and I would recommend her classes to anyone who likes to critical analysis of visual culture and loves class discussion. There are plenty of opportunities to share in her class and the subject matter is thought provoking. Though her classes aren't easy, it is worth taking. She is very committed to the subject.

Although the class seems interesting on paper it is such a drag to sit through. Some of the themes and topics she touched on in class were interesting but she never focused on them for long. Really LONG BORING readings that you will read in their entirety only to get one sentence worth of information. She seems nice enough though.

Go to class often, even though attendance is not mandatory. Required Readings. 12 reading quizzes with 2-3 grades dropped. Have Midterm, Presentation and Final. The professor is approachable. This class helps improve writing skills and understanding with readings. A is possible, but require effort and attendance.

COME TO CLASS! READ THE BOOK! because she will give reading quizzes. this is not a bs easy A class bc it requires work. I thought it would be an easy A but it's most def. not. B is manageable. if you're a good writer awesome, you'll fly by this class, but unlike me I suck at writing so it was kinda hard. Class itself is really interesting.

She is very nice but pretty unclear in her grading policies and is not very helpful. The course has 1 project that is making a movie and she has someone else come in and show you ONCE how to do that. The reading journals are pretty easy to google and find summaries of and comprehend well enough to get good grades on those. TURN BACK NOW
useless and time consuming, complicated homework with lots of readings.
Awesome teacher. Very easy to talk to and if you show interest in the subject you will pass easy. A little hard to understand but more than willing to work with students. BEST TEACHER I"VE EVER HAD
Talks way too slow and treats students like they are in middle school

Dr. Farahati is incredibly passionate about health economics and is able to extend that passion into teaching the material which makes it much easier to learn. Makes a strong effort to know her students and is very reasonable and will accommodate you if you reach out and communicate your circumstances. All in all a great professor!!!

Very disorganized and unclear with expectations for the class. Exams had typos and some MC questions were missing the correct answer. To be fair, my class had a change in professors and she started teaching our class about 3 weeks after the start of the semester, but she did not make the transition easy at all.

Professor Farahati is amazing and really cares about each of her students. She was always quick with replying to emails and was very helpful when discussing the course material. Her exams are tough but the textbook is your best friend. She is a great econ professor and I recommend her 1000000%
Professor Farahati loves teaching and her students. She goes above and beyond her way and her time to help the students to understand the real application of economics in healthcare.
Very knowledgable, fair and inspirational!

Really would not recommend this professor. The content she teaches is not hard at all, but she's extremely disorganized and not good at explaining things. The course Blackboard is confusing and she doesn't explain what she wants on the paper so its very hard to write well. She's friendly, but you won't learn anything more than 101 level stuff.

Professor Farahati is probably the best professor in the school, there is a reason why there is always a wait list to get in her class. She is very caring, a lenient grader and her discussion boards are a great study guide for incoming exams. She drops your lowest exam, homework and discussion score and she is always asking for feed back. Easy A.

reviews.comment: Would definitely take her again

reviews.comment: Professor Farah is the best online teacher for econ 101 she actually cares about her students. She lets you makeup assignments and she also gives a lot of extra credit. She also responds to emails efficiently. She is an amazing professor!!!!!
I took her class online so don't really know her lecture style, but I can say that she was organized, responsive, and a fair grader. Solid Econ professor.

She seems nice enough, but she is definitely disorganized. She will sometimes change grading criteria on the day that an assignment's due, which is very frustrating. On the other hand, she isn't a hard grader. I'm sure she'd be better in-person.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She is one of the sweetest professor i've ever had by far. She is willing to help you with your work, and very understandable. Come to class, do your homework and weekly assignments, One midterm and final exam, EASY A.  I would definitely take her again if i have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I took her ECON102 Hybrid class. Just about everything was done online, we only met in person around 3-4 times. Most of the tests were online and very easy. There's a final paper at the end of the semester that's worth 20% of your grade, but if you've participated throughout the semester, she won't grade it hard.

Professor Farahati is the sweetest! I loved her! She was one of my favorite HAPP professors. It was her first time teaching 412, so she basically designed the class to fit our needs. Points are given for attendance and we had a take home midterm and final. We has two group presentations that were based off our weekly assignments.

Honestly, She isn't bad at all! I would say come to class, do her homeworks and exams and its an easy A. We had one midterm and Final and both were take home. A final research paper at the end and Yes, she was a bit unorganized with the online stuff but seriously loved her.  She is an amazing teacher and is willing to help you in any way!
Wonderful professor, always willing to help out her students. Very Knowledgeable. Will recommend her to anyone who wants to take Health Economic.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Very disorganized. directions and grading criteria were NOT clear. One paper at the end that basically determines your grade. You don't even know your grade most of the semester. Don't take her under any circumstances, you'll probably get away with an A but it will be VERY frustrating along the way.
Chill prof, easy A class, had her for Macroeconomics
Thoughtful and respectful. Prof Shaya is very knowledgeable and takes her time explaining difficult concepts
Respected professor, really wants you to succeed
Excellent mentor
The best role model and inspirational professor at the  University of Maryland School of Pharmacy
favorite professor
Best mentor
excellent
Dr Shaya is inspiring and she has excellent command of the material. She is an excellent role model and her students and advisees thrive under her mentorship.
One of the best
Professor Shaya is very articulate and comprehensive, she masters the content and gives many examples. One of the best!
No Comments

Do NOT take this class with this professor. He rushes through 80–90 slides, reads straight from them, never explains, and ignores the textbook. Practice exams DO NOT match real exams, which test random niche details. Class averages were failing (highest was a 64%, with over 200 students). He sets students up for failure—take someone else.

Never have I EVER taken a class like this. The exams are designed to make you second-guess what you know, the lectures fast paced, and the homework barely matches the learning objectives. Even with a final grade curve and an exam drop, people still struggle to earn a good grade—take that as a sign!!

Nice guy but terrible prof. Very unorganized and scattered slides which makes it really hard to study. His lectures consist of heavy breathing and just reading the slides at x2 speed. Took the class with him and Bierberich, who was a really good professor with super neat and easy to follow slides and good lectures in contrast to this dude.

Dr. Vonhoff is very knowledgeable and passionate about teaching and wants his students to succeed. He provides resources to do well on exams. it is a tough class in general so you have to study on your own and put in the effort, but if you have any questions or concerns about the material or class he is happy to discuss with you in his office hours

He is a nice man. But his exams are all on slide material but he goes through 90 slides in such a short time every lecture so you have to make time outside of class to understand the material. He goes too quick and the exams are worded weird.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. V is very approachable. Accessible outside of class and willing to meet with students to discuss lecture or test material. Genetics is a hard course so obviously the lectures are heavy, but he includes several visuals to help convey the info. Study lecture slides before and after lectures and the class won't be as bad as people say it is.
The Professor rushed through the slides during lecture so it was very hard to understand. The textbook wasn't really helpful and the exams were based on the slides. The curve is high though

Can drop 1 exam. Lecture powerpoints were difficult to follow during class at times. A caring and kind person when you ask for help. Exams could be tough as lecture content was not the most dynamic all the time. Definitely tried to make the class more engaging.

Professor Vonhoff is one of the nicest I've had at UMBC. His powerpoints have a lot of information on them but that is helpful when you need to review for exams. His exams did require a good bit of studying, which is typical for an upper-level BIO course. It's clear he cares about students and he is always happy to answer any questions you have.

I am taking BIO302 this semester with Prof. Vonhoff and I would not recommend any other student to take this class with him because he spends more times reading information off the slides instead of actually explaining them. The exams are heavily based on his slides and each of his lecture consists of 90-100 slides.

For someone who teaches genetics, he should be able to explain the topics clearly and slowly. Dr. Vonhoffs lectures are too much and he only spends a very small amount of time explaining something that needs a deep explanation. Other than that he's chill

Vonhoff as a lecturer was just all over the place. I don't think he should have taught the classical genetics portion of the course since the textbook questions were not really reflective of what would be on the test and lectures were very dense. Do well on the first 4 exams so you can drop the final. The final was 73 questions (as a reference).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Probably his first semester teaching genetics. Very sweet but lecture slides were repetitive and not well organized. Tests are difficult so you have to study a lot to even get an 80. Class exam average was around 62. There are not enough practice problems provided that appear on exams. Some exam problems even the Professor couldnt explain well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class under Professor Vonhoff was intense. Each Lecture covered around 80-130 slides and his exams were brutal. Poorly written, and sometimes based on 1 specific detail on a single slide. He's a great person, but a bad lecturer. Exams are worth 60% of the final grade and with his bad lecturing and difficult exams, earning a high grade is tough.

I think he is a new teacher for genetics this semester. He has a lot of slides and some of them are filler. He does not go into depth on certain topics he teaches. However, I can see he tries his best in engaging with his students. I believe he will get better as time goes on. However, for the class, make sure to use outside resources to study.

You will have weekly tests in class about the reading of the week. He has a lot of focus on the applications of you GLBL degree after college and cements ideas and concepts that will set you up for success outside of the academic sphere. will take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Filomeno is a great professor. He will critique your paper hard! But it makes you a better writer. The course has 11 weekly reading quizzes (3 lowest drop),  2 Essay Papers, and 2 Global Engagement research papers. The course isn't easy, but it's not too hard. Definitely became a better writer after his course.

This class was so chill. Mostly it was reading ~30 page chapter each week and two online lectures. 3 tests total and a few other projects, but nothing too hard. Tests were graded a bit harshly imo but they are open-book. Technically attendance isn't mandatory, but participation is a grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good instructor. But didn't really take much effort himself to make the lecture material (which was all theory) that interesting. The public policy dialogues were fun though. Weekly one question multiple choice quizzes that are worth 2% of your grade each. Still worth taking if you want a social science credit.
